Branch: dev1/fix/usage-preset-timezone
Base: d0caf24a0f37
At: 2026-10-29T06:17:49Z

## Summary

The usage page decides which calendar day an invocation belongs to in two different zones on the same screen, so the date presets and the filter disagree about "today".

- The presets (`Today`, `Last 7 days`, `Last 30 days`) build their range from the **browser's local date**.
- The filter compares each invocation's day against that range after bucketing the invocation in the **server's reporting time zone** (`Asia/Shanghai` by default, also reported back as `analytics.filters.timeZone`).

For any browser whose local date differs from that zone's date, clicking `Today` drops the invocations of the last hours — the freshest usage is exactly what disappears.

## Where

`apps/web/src/UsagePage.tsx` (main `d0caf24a`, blob `96ecb2bce2` — unchanged from `1e886583`):

- `:316-327` — `localDateBucket()` / `localDateBucketDaysAgo()` read `getFullYear()/getMonth()/getDate()`, i.e. the browser's local calendar day.
- `:482-483` — `applyPreset(days)` puts those local dates into `filters.from` / `filters.to`.
- `:963-964` — `filterGlobalUsageSummary(summary, filters, analytics?.filters.timeZone)`; the default is `Asia/Shanghai` (`:256`).
- `:192-197`, `:199-207` — each invocation is bucketed with `usageSummaryDateBucket(startedAt, timeZone)` and compared to `filters.from` / `filters.to` as strings.

So the preset boundary and the comparison boundary are not the same boundary.

## Reproduction

The filter is exported, so this runs against the shipped function. Build a one-invocation summary (the fixture shape is the one already used in `apps/web/tests/UsagePage.test.tsx`), give the invocation a `startedAt` ten minutes before the given instant, and call the real `filterGlobalUsageSummary` with the range the preset would produce:

```js
const today = localDateBucket();                       // UsagePage.tsx:316-321, copied verbatim
const kept = count(filterGlobalUsageSummary(summary,
  { from: today, to: today }, "Asia/Shanghai"));
console.log(today, kept);
```

```
TZ=America/New_York node --import tsx probe.mjs 2026-10-29T13:00:00-04:00
```

```
TZ                       = America/New_York
invocation startedAt     = 2026-10-29T16:50:00.000Z
preset 'today' (local)   = 2026-10-29 | 'last 7 days' from 2026-10-23
filter bucket (server)   = 2026-10-30 (Asia/Shanghai)
filter, preset range     = { from: '2026-10-29', to: '2026-10-29' } -> invocations kept: 0
filter, server-zone range= { from: '2026-10-30', to: '2026-10-30' } -> invocations kept: 1
```

Second run at the current instant, with a browser zone on the other side of the date line, no clock injection:

```
TZ=Pacific/Pago_Pago node --import tsx probe.mjs
preset 'today' (local)   = 2026-10-28
filter bucket (server)   = 2026-10-29 (Asia/Shanghai)
filter, preset range     -> invocations kept: 0
filter, server-zone range-> invocations kept: 1
```

## Actual vs expected

- Actual: an invocation from ten minutes ago is filtered out by `Today`, and the whole surface reports no usage, whenever the browser's local date and the server's reporting-zone date differ (for `America/New_York` that is 12:00–24:00 local every day; the window follows the browser's offset).
- Expected: `Today` means the current day of the zone the page is already using to bucket invocations, so it includes every invocation of the current day in that zone — and the range and the comparison never disagree.

A second, smaller instance of the same root cause: `analytics.filters.timeZone` is what the API reports, so a deployment configured to another zone shows the same drift for a browser in `Asia/Shanghai`.

## Fix

Give the presets the same zone the filter uses: have `localDateBucket` / `localDateBucketDaysAgo` take a `timeZone` and format with the `Intl.DateTimeFormat` instance already built at `:183-190`, and pass `analytics?.filters.timeZone` from `applyPreset`. One file, ~20-40 lines, no API change. A regression test fits beside the existing `filterGlobalUsageSummary(summary, { from: "2026-08-04", to: "2026-08-04" }, "UTC")` assertion in `apps/web/tests/UsagePage.test.tsx:392`.

## Duplicate check

Searched issues and pull requests (open and closed) for `usage timeZone`, `Asia/Shanghai`, `today usage filter` and `usage preset last 7 days`: no matching report. `#447` (per-message send time) and `#544`/`#118` are unrelated.

issue:692.body:
## Summary

Model setup is the first-run gate: with no provider configured, **Settings → Model registry** opens the *Connect model* wizard automatically (`apps/web/src/ProviderModelSettings.tsx:617-618`). The screen is meant to answer one question — "which model will my runs use?" — but it currently asks it in six different places, uses one label for two different actions, and commits some answers with a Save button while committing others the moment they are clicked. This report is about that flow, not about how any single control looks.

## What the screen offers today

| # | Control | Where | What it writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Connect model` → `Save & connect` | registry heading (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:897-904`) | creates the provider **and** registers every model the vendor lists, immediately |
| 2 | `Fetch model list` → tick rows → `Save & connect` | wizard footer (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:828-841`) | same, narrowed to the ticked models |
| 3 | `Advanced configuration` → `Manual entries` / `Model identifier` | a fold inside the wizard (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:745-794`) | same, for models the listing does not return |
| 4 | `Refresh list` → per-row `Add` | expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:346-348`) | one model, immediately |
| 5 | `Add model` (toggle) → manual form | bottom of the expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:505-515`) | one model, immediately |
| 6 | `Global default task model` select | registry heading (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:879-896`) | `globalSettings.modelId`, immediately |
| 7 | `Edit` provider → `Save` / `Cancel` | expanded provider (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:703-749`) | provider fields, staged until Save |

Above all of that sits a separate `Model catalog` strip with its own refresh (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:386-400`).

## Problems

### 1. `Add model` means two different things, one above the other

Inside the same expanded provider, the per-model row action uses `t("providers.models.add")` (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:348`) and the toggle that opens the manual form uses the *same* string (`:506`). So the row of a listed model offers "Add" (register this model) and a few pixels below the table another "Add model" opens a form. The wizard reuses the label a third time for its manual-entry toggle, but submits with a different one, `Add to list` (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:779, 791`). A user cannot predict what any of these three controls will do from its label.

### 2. Two incompatible save models in the same panel

Provider fields are a draft: `Save` / `Cancel`, plus a `window.confirm` when another provider's `Edit` would discard the draft (`ProviderModelSettings.tsx:679-687, 693-697`). Everything else writes immediately:

- adding a model — `addModel()` calls the API at once, no confirm (`:784-823`);
- deleting a model — immediate, but guarded by `window.confirm` (`:825-863`);
- deleting a provider — immediate, guarded by `window.confirm` (`:751-754`);
- the default-model select — immediate (`:879-896`).

The same panel therefore mixes revertible and irreversible actions with no visual cue for which is which. Collapsing the row or expanding another one hides an unsaved provider draft with no prompt at that moment (`:699-701`), and the prompt only arrives later, when the settings dialog is closed — by then the user has usually forgotten the draft exists.

### 3. Registering *every* listed model is the silent default, and choosing models is hidden

With no explicit choice, `Save & connect` fetches the vendor list and registers all of it (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:324-339`). To choose a subset the user must first press `Fetch model list` (`:828-841`) and only then do checkboxes appear. The only warning is the small plan line "Save & connect registers every model the provider lists" (`:838`), while the manual path that most users need when discovery fails is behind `Advanced configuration`, a fold that otherwise looks like protocol/proxy plumbing. Nothing states before saving that the first registered model will become the global default; that effect is only reported afterwards (`:414-421, 433-450`).

### 4. The default task model is edited in two places with different commit semantics

The registry heading has a `Global default task model` select that writes instantly (via `replaceDefaultModelOverride`, `App.tsx:5259-5269`). The same value is also edited in **Settings → Global → Task model**, which is a draft saved by the dialog's own Save (`App.tsx:5217-5219`). Two controls, one field, opposite commit behaviour — the difference is invisible until someone loses an edit.

### 5. Vocabulary: seven labels for four concepts

`Connect model`, `Save & connect`, `Add model`, `Add to list`, `Fetch model list`, `Refresh list`, `Advanced configuration` vs `Advanced connection settings` (`i18n/messages.ts:675-720, 738, 771`). "Connect", "register", "add" and "save" are used interchangeably for one operation, while "fetch"/"refresh" is the only genuinely different one.

### 6. Success does not end the flow

`resetPlan()` clears only the model plan (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx:157-164`); the API key, provider name, base URL and success banner stay (`:433-450`). Pressing `Save & connect` again therefore creates a second provider with the same display name — allowed by the store (`services/api/src/store.ts:2758-2779` has no name uniqueness check) — and there is no explicit "done" state to tell the user the wizard has finished.

## Actual vs expected

| | Actual | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Entry points | Six ways to register a model across three levels (wizard, provider row, manual form), plus a default-model control duplicated in another tab | One way for each intent: add a provider; add models to a provider; pick the default model |
| Commit model | Provider fields staged, models and default immediate, deletes confirmed one by one | One commit model for the whole registry, with the same confirmation rule for every destructive action |
| Model choice | Register-all unless the user discovers `Fetch model list`; manual entry inside `Advanced configuration` | The listing visible by default with checkboxes, "register all" an explicit choice, manual entry next to it |
| Default model | Same field, two controls, two commit semantics, no indication of which wins | One control, or a link to the canonical one |
| After success | Form keeps the key and name; second press creates a duplicate provider | Clear, collapsed or "done" state; a duplicate name is warned about |

## Where

- `apps/web/src/ProviderModelSettings.tsx` — registry heading, wizard mount, provider rows, per-row add/delete, manual form toggle, default-model select, provider draft.
- `apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx` — `resolveModelPlan` (register-all fallback), advanced fold, footer plan summary, success state.
- `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:675-720, 722-723, 738, 771, 915` — the button and heading vocabulary.
- `apps/web/src/App.tsx:5217-5219, 5250-5280` — Mounting of the registry and of the Global settings group that edits the same default.

## Root cause

One component serves four jobs at once — registry list, provider editor, model picker, default-model setter — and each job brought its own persistence style and its own copy. The wizard was added later to make first-run setup one step, but it kept the provider editor's advanced fields *and* gained model registration, so provider creation and model registration now overlap instead of composing: the wizard can register models, the provider row can only add one at a time, and the provider editor cannot touch models at all. The `Add model` label was reused from the existing manual form for three controls that do different things.

## Suggested direction

1. **One control per intent.** `Add provider` (the wizard) and a single `Add model` per provider, opening one dialog that shows the fetched listing with checkboxes and keeps manual entry as a fallback in the same dialog. Remove the separate advanced/manual toggle, and stop using `Add` both for "register this listed model" and "open a form".
2. **Pick one commit model for the registry** and keep it: either stage every edit behind Save (provider fields, models, default) or make every action immediate with an undo. Apply the same confirmation rule to add, delete model and delete provider.
3. **Make model selection visible in the wizard.** Fetch the listing as soon as the key is entered, show it above the fold, and make "register all listed models" an explicit checkbox instead of the silent fallback. State the "first model becomes the global default" consequence before `Save & connect`.
4. **De-duplicate the default-model control.** Keep one, and link to it from the other place instead of rendering the same field twice with different commit semantics.
5. **End the flow on success.** Clear the key and name, collapse the wizard or show a `Done` state, and warn when a provider with the same name already exists.
6. **Copy pass.** Unify `Connect model` / `Save & connect` / `Add model` / `Add to list`, and keep `fetch`/`refresh` for the vendor listing only.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed issues for `model registry`, `Connect model`, `wizard`, `Add model`, `provider` and `usability`. #39 (closed) introduced the one-step connection wizard and is the origin of this overlap; #632 (closed) and #684 cover the *searchable model picker* rather than the registration flow; #686 covers the rendering of the provider `Test` control. None reports the overlapping entry points, the mixed save semantics or the duplicated default-model control.

issue:696.body:
## Context

ScienceDiscovery needs to run on Windows as a first-class desktop product: an Electron shell (`win_desktop/`) that owns the backend stack lifecycle, Windows platform facades in runner / api / cas, a Windows runtime (startup chain, execution router, micromamba envs, fail-closed permissions), and an NSIS installer that carries the whole payload — five service venvs plus the JiuwenSwarm venv, one bundled base interpreter, micromamba, and the web/desktop UI builds.

The delivery lands as a single combined PR that supersedes #640, #644, #667 and #694. This issue tracks the concrete problems that delivery fixes and the engineering lessons baked into the build tooling, so the rationale survives review.

## Problems fixed

1. **Skill one-click enable/disable (desktop mode)** — skills could not be switched on/off from the desktop. Fixed with the `SCIENCE_AGENT_SKILL_SELECTION=desktop` gate, conditional `useEverySkillEverywhere()`, and a reconcile pass; #694 additionally fixed the edge case where disable silently no-ops when no `read_skill` tool is exposed — already-imported skills now always turn off.
2. **paper venv interpreter mismatch** — a service venv can drift to a different Python minor than the bundled base interpreter (it happened once: paper on 3.11 against a 3.12 base). Wrong-ABI compiled extensions then die off-machine with SRE module mismatch / DLL load failures. Fixed with `.python-version` pins (`services/paper`, `services/adapter`) and an assemble-time gate: every bundled venv must match the bundled interpreter version or the build fails.
3. **Payload integrity gates** — the packaging script now fails the build instead of shipping a broken payload: stale `dist/` (src newer than dist — a real incident shipped old code with the fixes present only in src), stale editable `.pth`/finder mappings (a venv carried over from a moved checkout maps into paths that no longer exist), venv version drift (above), and missing patch-set / micromamba inputs.
4. **Process-tree shutdown** — a GUI app has no console to Ctrl-C. The shell stops the stack via `start-stack`'s killTree handlers and escalates to `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` after a grace window, so no orphaned python/node children survive app exit.
5. **First-run precompile** — payload Python bytecode is precompiled at assemble time (checked-hash, PEP 552) so the first-run compile step is a no-op and downstream copy chains (electron-builder → NSIS → data dir) can restamp mtimes without invalidating anything.
6. **Verification false positive (the 0.3.0 installer regression)** — the previous 0.3.0 installer was built from a packaging tree that had never merged main's #685, so the first-run wizard's model-config step regressed (misaligned model field) even though the fixes were already in main. The packaging tree is now based on the same commit as the combined PR and the payload carries the fixed `apps/desktop` build. Lesson: a build tree that diverges from the PR branch silently voids "fixed in main" claims — the branch and the installer must come from the same commit.
7. **PR conflict stitching** — the three suite PRs (#640 / #644 / #667) plus #694 overlap on the same files; merging them one-by-one re-creates the same conflicts every time. The combined branch resolves them once, with the platform-tag test files following #694's declarations (our side's changes to those files were label-line-only; verified zero content loss).
8. **Platform tags for CI collection** — tests missing `os`/`arch` tags caused `NODE_COLLECTION_FAILED` in CI. The tag commits carried from #694 fix collection and declare platform expectations explicitly.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Combined PR green in CI
- [ ] Windows installer (0.3.0, built from the combined branch) installs via the GUI installer, passes first-run wizard step 2 (model config, aligned per #685), reaches the workbench
- [ ] Skill one-click enable and disable verified in the installed app
- [ ] #640 / #644 / #667 / #694 closed by the combined PR

issue:701.body:
﻿## Problem

JiuwenSwarm (workswarm 0.2.6) pays a large, avoidable startup tax on every launch, which lands directly on the ScienceDiscovery desktop's "agent cluster starting" latency:

- the feishu SDK is imported up front even when the feishu channel is disabled (~4.7s);
- the AgentServer import chain pulls in pandas / pdfplumber / milvus (~6.8s before the server can even start binding);
- the heartbeat import chain (~2.8s) and the heavy `tui_connect` module (~1.8s) run before the ports are up;
- the Gateway<->AgentServer connect path blocks on warmup (~9.5s) and the post-listen warmup blocks readiness for another ~15.6s.

Same-machine A/B on gateway startup stage logs (Windows desktop line): warm restart ~17.5s without the fixes vs ~5-7s with them; user-perceived cold start 50s+ vs 20-25s.

## Proposal

We carry these as local patches today and would much rather see them land natively. The patch set (lazy-import guards, an off-critical-path preload for `tui_connect`, a shorter channel-config settle window, and gating the post-listen warmups behind the first request) is available in #700 as concrete, measured reference implementations — happy to split them into individually reviewable PRs against whatever layout the maintainers prefer.

| change | measured saving |
|---|---|
| feishu SDK lazy import | ~4.7s |
| tui_connect preload | ~1.8s |
| channel-config window 0.75s -> 0.2s | ~0.55s |
| heartbeat lazy import | ~2.8s |
| AgentServer import slimming | ~6.8s |
| unblock ws connect on warmup | ~9.5s |
| gate post-listen warmup | ~15.6s |

## Environment

Windows 11, ScienceDiscovery desktop packaging, workswarm 0.2.6, measured via gateway startup stage logs.

issue:708.body:
### What is wrong

`packages/cas/src/index.ts` gives the two methods that have the same three-layout search the same first-path-wins bug that `#706` reports for `read()`, but the consequences are different and each one is a separate failure.

**`stream()` (`packages/cas/src/index.ts:108-124`) hands unverified bytes to the caller.** It opens the first path that exists, yields every chunk from it, and only then compares the running digest:

```ts
async *stream(hash: string): AsyncGenerator<Buffer> {
  for (const path of this.readPaths(hash)) {
    // opens path; yields every chunk; digest is checked after the last chunk
    if (digest.digest("hex") !== hash) throw new Error("CAS integrity failure");
    return;
  }
```

A corrupt copy in the current pool is therefore delivered in full and the generator throws only afterwards, so every byte is already out of the store when the error surfaces. The only caller of `CasStore.stream` in the tree, `materializeArtifact` (`services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.ts:20`), pipes those chunks into `publishWorkspaceFile`, which writes them to a temporary file, computes the size and digest, and then fails in `packages/cas/src/workspace-copy.ts:76-77` with `Workspace copy source size changed` / `Workspace copy checksum mismatch`. The temporary file is removed in that function's `finally` (`:106-108`), so nothing corrupt is left on disk — but artifact materialization fails (500 to the caller) even though an intact copy sat in the legacy layout the whole time, and the error names a size/checksum mismatch rather than a corrupt source.

**`retain()` (`packages/cas/src/index.ts:127-138`) refuses an intact legacy copy.** It copies the first existing path into the target pool and compares the digest of that copy only:

```ts
const target = await new VersionStore(this.dataDir).putFile(pool, path);
if (target.digest !== `sha256:${reference.hash}` || target.size !== reference.size)
  throw new Error("Legacy reference integrity failure");
```

so a corrupt current-pool copy makes promotion fail even when the legacy `cas/sha256/<first-two>/<hash>` copy is intact. `retain()` exists to promote legacy references, which is exactly the case where the object lives only in the legacy layout.

### Reproduction on `3fe9f9c9fca9e5c26ab8c53a3c15666823d3ab02`

Stored one 31-byte blob, corrupted the current-pool copy (`versioning/agent-state/blobs/sha256/<hash>`), left an intact copy at `cas/sha256/<first-two>/<hash>`:

```
stream: THREW after delivering 19 bytes -> CAS integrity failure
stream: consumer already saw: "corrupted pool copy"
retain: THREW Legacy reference integrity failure
```

Expected after the fix, with the same setup:

```
stream: delivers the 31 intact bytes from the legacy layout, no throw
retain: returns an object ref for the promoted intact copy
```

### Expected

1. **`stream()` never emits bytes it cannot verify.** Before yielding from a candidate, verify that candidate (for example hash it first, or hash while streaming into a buffer small enough to discard); on a mismatch continue with the next layout. If every candidate is corrupt, throw `CAS integrity failure` **without having yielded anything**.
2. **`retain()` tries the remaining layouts.** A digest mismatch on one copy is not terminal; it must continue and only throw `Legacy reference integrity failure` when every candidate it found is corrupt.
3. **Both stay byte-identical on the happy path.** Existing behaviour when the first layout is intact does not change: same chunk sequence for `stream()`, same target ref for `retain()`.

### Acceptance probes

- (a) corrupt pool copy + intact legacy copy → `stream()` yields exactly the original 31 bytes and no error; `retain(ref, "data")` returns a ref whose digest matches.
- (b) corrupt every copy → `stream()` throws `CAS integrity failure` with **zero** bytes yielded; `retain()` throws `Legacy reference integrity failure`.
- (c) intact first layout → unchanged behaviour for both, including the multi-chunk case for `stream()` (feed a payload bigger than one chunk).

### Scope and sequencing

- Same root cause as `#706`, different methods: `#706`/`#707` fix `read()` and must not be widened there.
- This fix touches the same function file as `#707` but sits in different functions; the branch is based on current `main` and will be rebased if `#707` lands first.
- `has()`/`verify()` predicates are out of scope (`#679`/`#680`).

### Environment

main `3fe9f9c9fca9e5c26ab8c53a3c15666823d3ab02`; `packages/cas/src/index.ts` blob `584cf1eaefc7ec9b5c4c2125de7bf13c39039ba0`. Line numbers are from that blob.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product

Branch: dev1/fix/run-stream-turn-placement
Base: 0e7075c475fe
At: 2026-11-01T17:46:50Z

## Environment

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- live `main` sha: `0e7075c475fe657a7e772d7efdaa55cab1bcd9ba` (2026-11-01T17:05:39Z)
- Node v22.23.2; the desktop reducer is plain TypeScript and needs no Electron runtime.

## Reproduction (headless, no UI)

The desktop transcript folds a run's events with `reduceRunStream` in `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts`. The existing test file already has the helpers `fold`, `responseStarted(responseId, turn)` and `delta(text, responseId)`.

1. Add this test to `apps/desktop/tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts`:

```ts
test("a later turn's text is not folded into turn 1 when its response.started arrives late", () => {
  const state = fold([
    responseStarted("r1"),
    delta("first turn", "r1"),
    { responseId: "r1", type: "assistant.response.settled" } as RunStreamEvent,
    delta("HELLO", "r2"),
    responseStarted("r2", 2),
    delta(" WORLD", "r2"),
  ]);
  const second = state.turns.find((turn) => turn.turn === 2);
  assert.deepEqual(state.turns[0]!.responses.map((response) => response.content), ["first turn"]);
  assert.equal(second?.responses[0]?.content, "HELLO WORLD");
});
```

2. Run it:

```
cd apps/desktop && node --import tsx --test tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts
```

3. Observed on live main: `# tests 39`, `# pass 38`, `# fail 1`.

```
not ok 9 - a later turn's text is not folded into turn 1 when its response.started arrives late
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
        'first turn',
    +   'HELLO WORLD'
      ]
```

## Current vs expected

Current state after folding the script above:

```json
[
  { "turn": 1, "responses": [{ "id": "r1", "text": "first turn" }, { "id": "r2", "text": "HELLO WORLD" }] },
  { "turn": 2, "responses": [{ "id": "r2", "text": "" }] }
]
```

Expected:

```json
[
  { "turn": 1, "responses": [{ "id": "r1", "text": "first turn" }] },
  { "turn": 2, "responses": [{ "id": "r2", "text": "HELLO WORLD" }] }
]
```

The second turn's whole answer is drawn inside the first turn, and the second turn is left with an empty answer block.

## Code evidence

- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:366-382` — `withResponse` handles a `responseId` it has never seen by creating a turn with the hard-coded `turn: 1` (`const created: AssistantTurn = { ..., turn: 1 }`), for every event type, including one whose start frame will later announce another turn.
- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:107-111` — `assistant.response.started` adds a blank block to *its own* turn and does not adopt the block already created for the same `responseId`, so the same response exists twice.
- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:404-411` — `locateTurn` returns the first turn that owns the `responseId`, so after the start frame arrives every later delta keeps landing in the wrongly-anchored turn-1 block; turn 2's block stays empty forever.
- `apps/desktop/src/run-stream/reducer.ts:357-365` — the comment at `withResponse` documents this ordering as supported ("A frame that arrives before its `assistant.response.started`, or with no open response at all, opens a block rather than dropping the text").
- `apps/desktop/tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts:139-142` — the existing coverage is a single-turn orphan (`fold([delta("orphan text")])`, no `responseId`, no second turn), which is why this gap is green today.

## Why it happens in practice

- A frame that cannot be read is folded as `null` while its cursor still advances (`reducer.ts:88-96`, and PR #616 made that path explicit). If the unreadable frame is an `assistant.response.started`, its deltas are then anchored to turn 1 by the branch above.
- The same comment block says older records omit `responseId` on text frames (`reducer.ts:357-365`). Such a delta is routed by `locateTurn(state, undefined)` to the newest turn's newest block; when that text belongs to turn 2 before turn 2 exists, `withResponse` again creates `turn: 1`, and the subsequent `assistant.response.started(turn 2)` leaves an empty second block.
- Replay (`foldRunRecords`) reuses the same reducer, so a finished run opened from the desktop transcript reproduces the same wrong attribution, not just the live stream.

## Suggested fix (one file, ~10-20 lines)

In `withResponse`, remember a block created for an unknown `responseId` (for example a `pending` map on the state, or a block placed at `turn: 1` that is moved when its start frame arrives): on `assistant.response.started`, adopt/move the existing block for that `responseId` instead of appending a blank one. Keep the current single-turn fallback when no start frame ever arrives, so `apps/desktop/tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts:139-142` stays green.

## Acceptance

- The test above is added and passes; the file reports `# tests 39` / `# pass 39` / `# fail 0`, i.e. the 38 existing tests stay green.
- `node --import tsx --test tests/run-stream-reducer.test.ts` in `apps/desktop`.

## Impact

The desktop transcript misattributes a turn's answer text to the previous turn and renders an empty answer block, and because tools and subagents are placed on the newest turn (`reducer.ts:146-196`), the transcript's step order no longer matches what happened. The same reconstruction feeds replayed finished runs, so the error persists after reload instead of being a live-only glitch.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed issues and pull requests: `reduceRunStream`, `run-stream reducer`, `"response.started" turn`, `"turn 1" transcript`. Results are the feature PR that introduced the reducer (#500) and the frame-error PRs (#505, #616); none of them reports or fixes the turn placement above.

issue:712.body:
## Environment

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` `main` at `0e7075c475fe657a7e772d7efdaa55cab1bcd9ba` (2026-11-01T17:05:39Z)
- `packages/cas/src/index.ts`: `readPaths()` `:173-177`, `read()` `:102-122`, `stream()` `:129-146`

## What is wrong

The two methods search the same three layouts, but they disagree about what a corrupt first copy means.

- `read()` (`:102-122`) skips a copy whose digest does not match and keeps looking, so a corrupt `versioning/agent-state` copy does not hide an intact `versioning/data` one (`#707` / `#706`).
- `stream()` (`:129-146`) keeps the older rule: the first copy that exists decides. A corrupt first copy fails the whole call even when the mirror is intact.

Measured on the source, with one 210,000-byte object written by `CasStore.put()` (agent-state) plus `new VersionStore(root).put("data", bytes)` (intact mirror), then only `versioning/agent-state/blobs/sha256/<hash>` overwritten with `corrupt`:

```
read(hash)           -> returned the 210000 original bytes
stream(hash)         -> THREW Error("CAS integrity failure") after 7 bytes
```

## Current vs expected

Current: `read()` and `stream()` of the same hash disagree — one returns content, the other refuses it.
Expected (this issue asks which one, and makes both follow it): either both fall back to the intact mirror, or neither does. The choice belongs with the maintainers; the code should not depend on which accessor a caller happens to use.

## Why it is reachable

`materializeArtifact()` (`services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.ts:20`) is the only `stream()` caller in the tree, and it fails the request when the primary copy is corrupt even though `read()` would have served the same object. `services/api/src/artifacts/materialize.test.ts:64-66` pins the current `stream()` behaviour by corrupting only `versioning/agent-state/blobs/sha256/<hash>` and asserting the request fails.

## Suggested test

In `packages/cas/src/index.test.ts`, one case that stores a blob, writes `corrupt` over the agent-state copy, keeps an intact copy in the other pool, and asserts that `read()` and `stream()` reach the same conclusion — whatever that conclusion is.

## Scope

- Not a duplicate of `#708` (that one asks for `stream()` to verify before it yields; this one is the accessor disagreement that `#708`'s fix exposed) or of `#706`/`#707` (those are `read()`-only).
- No PR from us yet: recorded, benched, and not picked up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 8a3e9527b33f4e999955db3b813f1bec
Branch: dev2/fix/workspace-upload-quoted-filename
Base: 84c81b806a527ce0a70dd63cbc004d7d5f5edc08
At: 2026-11-02T00:28:25Z

## Environment

- `main` = `84c81b806a527ce0a70dd63cbc004d7d5f5edc08` (2026-11-01T18:23:35Z)
- Node v22.23.2, Node built-in test runner; no local changes needed to reproduce.

## Steps to reproduce

Add the suggested red test below to `services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` and run it:

```bash
cd services/api
node --import tsx --test src/workspace-upload.test.ts
```

Before adding it the file is green (`# tests 8 / # pass 8 / # fail 0`); with it:

```text
not ok 9 - readMultipartUploads keeps a quoted filename that contains a semicolon
  Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
  + actual - expected

    [
  +   'trial'
  -   'trial;phase2.csv'
    ]
# tests 9
# pass 8
# fail 1
```

A multipart request whose part header is exactly what a browser or curl sends for a file named
`trial;phase2.csv` is:

```text
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="files"; filename="trial;phase2.csv"
```

Running `readMultipartUploads()` on that body, then `uploadWorkspaceParts()` on the result, prints:

```text
parsed parts: ["trial","plain.csv"]      # second part: filename="plain.csv"
uploaded:     [{"name":"trial","path":"trial","status":"created"}, ...]
on disk:      ["plain.csv","trial"]
```

So the file is persisted as `trial` — truncated at the `;`, extension gone. The same line also
percent-decodes the quoted value: a part with `filename="100%25.txt"` parses to `100%.txt`, and
`filename="a%2Fb.csv"` decodes to `a/b.csv`, which then trips the basename guard.

## Current behaviour vs expected

- Current: `filename="trial;phase2.csv"` is stored as `trial`; `filename="100%25.txt"` is stored as
  `100%.txt`; `filename="a%2Fb.csv"` decodes to `a/b.csv`, `sanitizeUploadFilename` rejects it with
  `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH`, and because `uploadWorkspaceParts` rethrows that code the **whole upload
  request fails**, including the other files in the same batch.
- Expected: the quoted parameter is read to its closing quote (`trial;phase2.csv`), a plain
  `filename` value is used verbatim (RFC 7578 §4.2: only `filename*` is percent-encoded), and an
  invalid name fails only its own entry.

## Code evidence

`services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts:127`

```ts
const rawFilename = contentDisposition?.match(/\bfilename\*?=(?:UTF-8''|")?([^";]+)"?/i)?.[1];
```

`[^";]+` stops at the first `;` or `"` even when the value is inside a quoted-string, so everything
after a semicolon is dropped. The captured value is then decoded unconditionally by
`decodeUploadFilename` (`:143-149`):

```ts
function decodeUploadFilename(raw: string): string {
  try {
    return decodeURIComponent(raw.trim());
  } catch {
    return raw.trim();
  }
}
```

That decode is only correct for `filename*`; the plain `filename` parameter the browsers send is not
percent-encoded (`"`, CR and LF are the only characters the HTML spec escapes, as `%22`, `%0D`, `%0A`),
so a name that legitimately contains `%XX` is rewritten, and `%2F` / `%5C` turn into a separator.

The failure then reaches `sanitizeUploadFilename` (`:84-88`), which throws `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH`, and
`uploadWorkspaceParts` rethrows that code instead of recording a failed entry (`:348`):

```ts
if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH") throw error;
```

Existing coverage does not exercise anything but plain ASCII names: `readMultipartUploads keeps
zero-byte file parts` uses `filename="empty.txt"` / `filename="notes.txt"`
(`services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts:87-111`), so the parser's quote handling is untested.

## Suggested red test

File: `services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` (same helpers as the existing multipart test).

Name: `readMultipartUploads keeps a quoted filename that contains a semicolon`

```ts
test("readMultipartUploads keeps a quoted filename that contains a semicolon", async () => {
  const boundary = "----sa-quoted-name";
  const body = Buffer.from(
    [
      `--${boundary}`,
      'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="files"; filename="trial;phase2.csv"',
      "Content-Type: text/csv",
      "",
      "a,b",
      `--${boundary}--`,
      "",
    ].join("\r\n"),
  );
  const request = Readable.from([body]) as unknown as IncomingMessage;
  request.headers = { "content-type": `multipart/form-data; boundary=${boundary}` } as IncomingMessage["headers"];
  const parts = await readMultipartUploads(request, limits.maxRequestBytes);
  assert.deepEqual(parts.map((part) => part.filename), ["trial;phase2.csv"]);
});
```

A second assertion for the same fix: `filename="100%25.txt"` must come back as `100%25.txt`.

## Impact

- The stored workspace path and `originalName` lose the file's extension whenever the name contains
  `;`, so the uploaded CSV/TSV no longer opens in the table viewer and `inferMediaType`
  (`workspace-upload.ts:375`) returns `undefined`; provenance and the memory-graph `SourceFile` node
  record the truncated name too.
- A name whose decoded form looks like a path (`%2F`, `%5C`) aborts the entire multi-file upload
  instead of failing that one entry.
- Any client that quotes a filename containing `;` (browsers and curl do) is affected.

## Fix direction

One helper in `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts`: split `Content-Disposition` parameters with a
quote-aware scan (respect `"…"` and `\"`), take `filename` verbatim, and percent-decode only a
`filename*` value (`UTF-8''…`). No schema, route or desktop change; the existing basename guard stays
as it is.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed issues and pull requests for `form-data`, `Content-Disposition`, `multipart`,
`filename`, `filename*`, `semicolon`, `readMultipartUploads`, `workspace upload`: the only related
items are #606 and #506, which sanitize the name on the desktop side before it is sent, and #342,
which is about PDF parsing. No issue or pull request covers the server-side quoted parameter, and
`readMultipartUploads` has no hits at all.

## Background

Measuring Windows desktop startup timelines (`python -X importtime`) on workswarm0.2.6 showed `jiuwenswarm.common.config` pulling in a full `portalocker` -> `portalocker.redis` -> `redis asyncio` stack at import time — **~1.00s cold, 95% of which is the redis asyncio stack** (portalocker itself is ~7ms).

```
import time: self [us] | cumulative | imported package
...
      25 |       6795 | portalocker
...
     972 |    999000 |   redis.asyncio.client        <- the actual tax
```

`config.py` is an all-entry import (every jw process — `app_agentserver`, `app_gateway`, `app` — imports it at module load), so this ~1s was paid by **every process, every launch**, even though:

- `update_config()` is a rare write path (uses `portalocker.Lock` only when persisting config changes)
- the same module-level `import portalocker` pattern is repeated in `gateway/cron/store.py` and `common/media_capability_config.py`

`portalocker.redis` is a wrapper that unconditionally imports the full redis client even when you only ever use plain file locks — so any module importing portalocker for file locking pays the redis tax.

## What we did (desktop line, patch 0017)

Three-file fix, <30 lines of product code:

1. **`common/config.py`** — `import portalocker` moved into `update_config()`; the lock dependency only pays on first write.
2. **`gateway/cron/store.py`** — moved into `_call_under_file_lock()`; only the locked store operations pay.
3. **`common/media_capability_config.py`** — the interesting one: `migrate_media_capability_switches()` runs at module load of every jw process. After the first run the `.env` already carries all explicit switches and `os.environ` has them exported, so the locked read-modify-write is a no-op. Added a fast path: if all `MEDIA_CAPABILITY_ENV_FIELDS` keys are already present in the environment, `return {}` — the process never touches the lock branch at all. The first cold run (or a `.env` missing switches) still takes the locked path.

## Measured Effect

Same-machine A/B on the Windows desktop installer line (f25 -> f26):

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| portalocker/redis in importtime chain (agentserver/gateway) | ~1.0s | 0 hits |
| hot-start gateway `run_entered` | ~4.8s | ~4.7s (R0, cold pyc) |
| first-start net (total minus wizard) | 33.3s | 28.1s |

The hot-start number is partially masked on machines where 360/Defender rescans fresh `.pyc` files (our R0 was all-cold bytecode); the first-start number (28.1s, full first-launch timeline) is the cleaner signal — ~5s of that comes from this patch plus the AgentServer construction re-chain of 0016 (AgentServer listen 13.95s -> 1.53s in the f26 field logs).

## Suggestion for upstream

Either of these would benefit any embedding product that imports `jiuwenswarm.common.config` at entry:

1. **Cheap**: move `import portalocker` into the lock-using functions (as we did — happy to upstream this as a PR).
2. **Upstream of us**: `portalocker.redis` importing the full redis asyncio stack eagerly is the root cause; if you depend on plain file locking only, consider whether `portalocker` is worth ~1s of every process's import time, or use `os.open` + `msvcrt.locking`/`fcntl.flock` directly for the file-lock use cases.

Happy to provide the three-file patch (diff against workswarm0.2.6, shipped as `0017-lazy-portalocker-imports.patch` in our desktop patch chain) as a starting point.

## Version

- workswarm0.2.6 (commit `70aa671`)
- Windows 11, Python 3.12

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: f885e1e336b14b23b4ab7e6bf28554da
Branch: dev2/feat/evolve-gate-evidence
Base: 8bcc2237e4b5e4aa992267bedbb7e9cc591cc79f
At: 2026-11-02T07:37:21Z

## What the user sees

An `/evolve` run finishes with one number, `bestTestScore`: the pass rate of the best candidate on the held-out gate shards. The run detail presents it as the evidence that the search made progress it did not optimise against. One evaluation of one candidate — with no evaluation of the baseline on the same cases — cannot support that claim. A run that wins 5 of 8 cases and a baseline that wins 5 of 8 report the same "improvement" as a run that wins 8 of 8 against a baseline that wins 3 of 8; likewise a 5/8 candidate that happens to sit on an easy split looks like progress. The payload carries no pairing, no n, and no verdict.

## Evidence on live main `8bcc2237e4b5e4aa992267bedbb7e9cc591cc79f`

- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/test_gate_domain.py:139-146` — the gate already computes `selected` (case → passed), then keeps only `cases`, the names of failed cases, and the rate. The per-case pairing a statistic needs is discarded before it leaves the domain.
- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/puct_engine.py:746-760` — `finish()` evaluates only `best.program.code` on `self.domain.test_shards` and emits `best_test_score=test_score`; the baseline program is never evaluated on those shards.
- `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/events.py:293-315` — `search_finished()` payload, observed by calling it on this tree:

```
search_finished keys: ['bestNodeIndex', 'bestTestScore', 'candidates', 'expansionsPlanned', 'status', 'stopReason', 'type']
has per-case evidence: False
```

- `packages/schema/src/evolution.ts:395` (`bestTestScore: number | null`) and `:596` (`gateScore?: number`) — the wire shape carries only point estimates.

## Red probe (fails today)

```python
from sciencediscovery_evolve import events

def test_search_finished_reports_paired_gate_evidence():
    event = events.search_finished("completed", 3, 12, best_test_score=0.625,
                                   stop_reason="budget", expansions_planned=20)
    assert "gateEvidence" in event, sorted(event)
```

```
E   AssertionError: ['bestNodeIndex', 'bestTestScore', 'candidates', 'expansionsPlanned', 'status', 'stopReason', ...]
E   assert 'gateEvidence' in {'bestNodeIndex': 3, 'bestTestScore': 0.625, 'candidates': 12, 'expansionsPlanned': 20, ...}
1 failed
```

The probe imports the evolve sources of `8bcc2237` directly (no new module is needed to see the gap; the acceptance test below adds the module the probe asks for).

## Smallest mergeable slice (one PR, Dev-2, <= 1 week)

1. New `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/acceptance.py`: `paired_evidence(baseline: Mapping[str, bool], candidate: Mapping[str, bool], alpha: float = 0.05)` returning `{wins, losses, ties, n, pValue, verdict}`. Exact paired sign test with `math.comb`; `verdict` is `"established"`, `"not established"` or `"insufficient"`; `wins + losses < 6` is `insufficient` (no rank or p-value is invented to fill the gap).
2. `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/test_gate_domain.py`: carry the per-case results out of the domain (`caseResults`, about 6 lines), reusing the `selected` map that already exists.
3. `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/puct_engine.py` `finish()`: evaluate the baseline program on the same gate shards, pair the cases by id, and emit `gate_evidence` on `search_finished`; leave it absent (and say why in the log) when the run has no gate shards or the baseline cannot be evaluated.
4. `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/events.py` `search_finished()` and `packages/schema/src/evolution.ts` SearchFinished type: `gateEvidence?: { wins: number; losses: number; ties: number; n: number; pValue: number; alpha: number; verdict: string }`.
5. New `services/evolve/tests/test_acceptance.py`: 8-0 `established` at alpha 0.05, 7-1 `not established`, 3-3 `insufficient`, empty input `insufficient`; and an engine test where a positive point estimate with 5-3 reports `not established`.

Acceptance: `cd services/evolve && uv run --extra test pytest tests/test_acceptance.py tests/test_puct_engine.py -q`. The red probe above turns green, and no verdict other than `insufficient` is possible with fewer than 6 decided cases.

Smallest user-visible outcome: a finished run's result says whether the improvement over its own baseline is established at the stated alpha, and says `insufficient` instead of implying progress when the gate cannot tell.

## Caveat the implementation must keep

The exact sign test assumes the paired gate cases are independent. Cases from one suite can correlate (shared fixtures, one broken import, one flaky test), which makes the p-value optimistic. The verdict is evidence at a stated alpha, never a guarantee; a later change may replace the statistic with a cluster-aware one if suites show correlation.

## Deduplication

Searched open and closed issues and PRs for `paired_evidence`, `gateEvidence`, `sign test`, `conformal`, `bestTestScore`, `evolution acceptance`, `test_shards` — no issue or PR covers per-case paired evidence for a finished evolve run. #567 is documentation for `/evolve` and #54 is the RSI direction; neither covers the acceptance statistic.

**Label note.** This account cannot write labels on the repository (403). Please add the repository's feature label when triaging; `agent-ready` was deliberately not requested.

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 964fdbe623a640019c6b9325759c2d3f
Branch: dev1/fix/723-escape-nested-window-guard
Base: 8bcc2237e4b5e4aa992267bedbb7e9cc591cc79f
At: 2026-11-02T08:43:15Z

## ScienceDiscovery evidence-backed issue

**Live main:** `8bcc2237e4b5e4aa992267bedbb7e9cc591cc79f` (`test(launcher): cover unavailable Runner startup warning`)
**Area:** `apps/web` — memory-graph explorer vs. nested artifact viewer (CSV workspace / Mol*)
**Filed by:** ScienceDiscovery Product

### Summary

Pressing **Escape** while a CSV workspace or Mol* viewer is open on top of the memory-graph explorer tears down **both**: the nested window and the whole explorer layer. The same interaction is already guarded in the standalone artifact viewer — the explorer is the only layer without the guard, and its embedded artifact modal is the exact place where the guard is skipped.

### Current behavior (file:line)

1. **`apps/web/src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:1051-1055`** — unconditional global close:

   ```tsx
   useEffect(() => {
     const onKey = (event: KeyboardEvent) => { if (event.key === "Escape") onClose(); };
     window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
     return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey);
   }, [onClose]);
   ```

2. **`apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:719-726`** — the same interaction with the opposite semantics, plus the embedded bypass at `:720`:

   ```tsx
   useEffect(() => {
     if (embedded) return;                                   // :720 — bypassed inside the explorer
     function onKey(event: KeyboardEvent): void {
       if (event.key === "Escape" && !csvWindowOpen && !molstarOpen) onClose();   // :722
     }
     window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
     return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey);
   }, [csvWindowOpen, embedded, molstarOpen, onClose]);
   ```

3. The two nested windows each bind their own window-level Escape and neither stops propagation, so one keypress runs both handlers:
   - `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/CsvArtifactWindow.tsx:156-168` — `if (event.key === "Escape") onClose();`, no `stopPropagation`.
   - `apps/web/src/MolstarWindow.tsx:129-133` — `if (event.key === "Escape") onClose();`, no `stopPropagation`.

4. **Reachability:** `ScientificArtifacts.tsx:872`/`:829` keep the CSV workspace and Mol* viewer mounted while `ScientificArtifacts.tsx:932` renders the explorer above the artifact section; the explorer in turn embeds the artifact modal at `MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:1700-1715` (`embedded` on `:1702`). So "explorer open + nested CSV/Mol* open" is a normal state, not a corner case: open a dataset preview, open the CSV workspace, click "view in memory" (`:928`), then press Escape. In embedded mode the artifact layer's own guard is gone (`:720`), and the explorer's unconditional handler is the only one left.

5. **Same file already knows the pattern:** `apps/web/src/MemoryGraphTour.tsx:74-86` binds Escape in the capture phase and calls `stopPropagation()`, with the comment "it must NOT collide with the explorer's global Escape → onClose (which closes the whole explorer)". That guard exists for the tour only; the embedded artifact windows were never given one.

### Expected semantics

Escape closes the **topmost** layer only: with the CSV workspace or the Mol* viewer open inside the explorer, Escape closes that window and leaves the explorer mounted (selected node, filters, unfolded set and viewport preserved); a second Escape, with neither nested window open, closes the explorer. The standalone artifact viewer keeps its current double-Escape behavior (CSV/Mol* first, modal second).

### Impact

One keypress destroys the exploration state the user built: the selected node and its detail/artifact panel, the unfolded/scope-expanded node set, the active chain highlight, the search query and filter chips, and the canvas pan/zoom. The user has to re-open the explorer and re-drill to the same node, and the CSV/Mol* window they were reading is gone at the same instant. This reads as "Escape closed everything" rather than "Escape closed the window I was in".

### Verification plan (no DOM harness in this repo)

`apps/web/package.json` has no jsdom, happy-dom or @testing-library; tests use `react-dom/server` `renderToStaticMarkup` (383 call sites), and `tests/MemoryGraphEntryFocus.test.tsx:25-27` states the canvas is "a WebGL island the SSR test harness cannot run". Two jsdom-free precedents apply:

- pure predicate extraction from this very file — `shouldFocusEntryNode` (`MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:736`) tested in `tests/MemoryGraphEntryFocus.test.tsx`;
- source-text assertions for wiring, e.g. `tests/SidebarDrawer.test.tsx:75-80`, `tests/ProxySettingsEditor.test.tsx:154`.

Acceptance:

1. Export `shouldCloseOnEscape(csvWindowOpen: boolean, molstarOpen: boolean): boolean` from `apps/web/src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx`, returning `!csvWindowOpen && !molstarOpen`.
2. New `apps/web/tests/MemoryGraphEscapeGuard.test.tsx` covering all three combinations: `(true,false)→false`, `(false,true)→false`, `(false,false)→true`.
3. Wire the explorer's global Escape effect to that predicate with the live nested-overlay state of the embedded artifact modal (the embedded modal already tracks `csvWindowOpen`/`molstarOpen` at `ScientificArtifacts.tsx:494-495`); any wiring that satisfies the observable below is acceptable.
4. Observable acceptance: with a CSV workspace or Mol* viewer open inside the explorer, one Escape closes only that window and the explorer stays mounted with its selected node, filters and unfolded set; the next Escape closes the explorer. Standalone artifact viewer behavior unchanged.

Red evidence on live main today — the module imports headlessly, and the guard does not exist:

```
$ cd apps/web && node --import tsx -e "import('./src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx').then(m=>{console.log('exports:', Object.keys(m).join(','));console.log('shouldCloseOnEscape =', typeof m.shouldCloseOnEscape)})"
exports: CHAIN_BUTTONS,MemoryGraphExplorer,NODE_LABELS,buildScopeChildCounts,countScopeChildren,countVisibleAndTotal,findArtifactNodeInGraph,findCodeNodeInGraph,findSourceFileNodeInGraph,mergeChainScopeExpansions,mergeExpansions,shouldFocusEntryNode
shouldCloseOnEscape = undefined
```

```
$ grep -rn "Escape\|shouldCloseOnEscape" apps/web/tests/
tests/ProxySettingsEditor.test.tsx:154:  assert.match(source, /event\.key === "Escape"/);
tests/SidebarDrawer.test.tsx:75:  // Escape closes the drawer, ...
```

No test covers Escape in the explorer today; `node --import tsx --test tests/MemoryGraphEntryFocus.test.tsx` passes 6/6, so the harness and the predicate precedent are proven.

### Not a duplicate

Open-issue search (`Escape in:title`, `escape explorer`, `memory graph close`, `MemoryGraphExplorer`) finds no report: the only Escape-titled issue is closed #672 (HTML entity decoding). Our open PRs `#311/#648/#658/#663/#664/#676/#678/#680/#709/#722` touch none of these files or handlers (#648 is the web test build, #658/#663 text truncation, #664 fetch guard, #676 desktop, #678/#680/#709 CAS, #722 evolve evidence, #311 evolve trigger).

issue:736.body:
## Problem

The nightly real journey `J5` (shard `research-9`) failed with `locator.click: Test timeout of 600000ms exceeded` while reading the run timeline. Playwright had already resolved the first `details.timeline-disclosure.tool` summary, but the element never became visible and 1049 click retries consumed the whole test budget.

## Cause

A live run folds adjacent exploration steps into a collapsed `<details class="timeline-exploration">` (`apps/web/src/timeline/RunTimeline.tsx`). Whether that wrapper exists depends on the tool sequence the model happens to produce, which a journey does not pin. `test/helpers/journeys.ts` expanded only the tool card itself, so a card nested in a closed group stayed invisible.

The trigger is model-dependent, which is why it is intermittent: reruns on a local model that only called `run_shell` passed 4/4 and produced no exploration group.

A second gap surfaced in review: the region name is localized, and the two `zh-CN` journeys that call `expandToolStep` resolved zero regions, so the expansion was a silent no-op there.

## Fix

PR #735 expands the timeline's own grouping containers before reading or locating tool cards, matches both UI locales (`Agent activity` / `Agent 活动`), and caps a card-summary click at 30s so a future timeline layout change fails fast with an attributable visibility error instead of spending the 600s test budget.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `J5` passes repeatedly against the nightly model, including runs that produce exploration tool steps.
- [ ] `journey-first-run` and `journey-artifact-archive` (`zh-CN`) still expand and read tool steps.
- [ ] A timeline layout change fails a journey in seconds with a visibility error, not in 600s.

## Evidence

- Nightly failure: first summary resolved, `element is not visible`, 1049 retries, 600s timeout.
- Local DOM probe with the same structure: the nested summary is invisible while the group is closed, and expands/clickable after the group is opened.
- Local reruns on the helper: `research-9` planned 1 / executed 1 / passed 1, twice (1.1m, 2.5m).

Refs #735

issue:774.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

The desktop first run walks a new user through three screens: the workspace directory page (`win_desktop/src/wizard.html`), the startup/loading page (`win_desktop/src/loading.html`), and then the SPA's model-configuration step. The first two draw a generic beaker glyph on a blue gradient tile in the top-left brand row, while the app's rail — and every screen after the wizard — uses the ScienceDiscovery "SD" monogram. The product identity therefore changes twice within the first minutes of use: beaker, then monogram, then the mark the rest of the product keeps.

This asks for one product mark across the whole first-run flow, the same mark the rail already uses, so a user sees one identity from the first screen onward.

This is the desktop counterpart of #151. That issue covers the web app's favicon, README and in-app brand slot in `apps/web`; it does not cover the desktop first-run pages, so it is not duplicated or superseded here.

### Design Ideas

The mark itself is not the open question — the product already has one (the SD monogram in `apps/desktop/src/assets/brand/app-mark.png`, used by the rail). The question is how the two shell pages, which are plain HTML bundled into `win_desktop/dist`, can draw it.

Options considered:

1. Keep an inline SVG per page (status quo). It works, but it is a second drawing of the brand and drifts from the rail on the next identity change — exactly the bug being fixed.
2. Point the shell pages at the SPA's brand asset. The shell pages are loaded from `dist` next to the packaged app, not from the SPA source tree, so the file has to be copied beside them at build time.
3. Draw a tile with letters or a CSS-only glyph. Cheap, but it is not the product mark and reintroduces the same divergence.

Chosen: option 2. `win_desktop/scripts/build.mjs` copies the existing app icon to `dist/app-mark.png` beside the bundled pages, and all three first-run headers use a 32×32 background image. The SPA wizard's brand row points at the existing `assets/brand/app-mark.png`. The two images are the same artwork (decoded both, downscaled to a common size, mean channel difference 2.03/255, identical alpha bounding box), so the first-run flow and the rail now show the same mark.

Known follow-up, deliberately not part of this change: the artwork still exists as two source files — `win_desktop/build/icon-256.png` (the Windows application/tray icon) and `apps/desktop/src/assets/brand/app-mark.png` (the SPA UI asset). A later change should generate both sizes from one source in `build.mjs` rather than hand-maintaining the pair. The tray icon is created from `dist/icon.png` at 256 px, so that follow-up must not simply repoint the tray at the 128 px asset.

### Involved Public APIs

None. This is static HTML, CSS and a build-time asset copy. No HTTP API, IPC channel, preload bridge or configuration surface changes.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `apps/desktop`: the SPA wizard header (`SetupWizard.tsx`) and its styles (`styles/wizard.css`).
- `win_desktop`: the two shell pages and the asset copy in `scripts/build.mjs`.
- `apps/web` (#151): unaffected; the desktop reuses the existing desktop brand asset and does not touch the web app.
- Packaging: the build must continue to ship the extra file next to the bundled pages; a build that skips the copy would render an empty header box.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Build both packages: `pnpm --dir win_desktop build` and `pnpm --dir apps/desktop build`.
- Asset presence: assert `win_desktop/dist/app-mark.png` exists after the build and that both shell pages reference `url("app-mark.png")`; assert the built SPA stylesheet references the hashed `app-mark-*.png` asset.
- Visual check at 1440×900: open the three screens (workspace, loading, SPA model step) and confirm each header shows the SD monogram at 32×32 with the header layout unchanged.
- Regression check: no beaker SVG path or gradient-tile rule remains in the three first-run files.
- Repository layers: `pnpm ci:l1`, `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The first-run workspace page, loading page and SPA model-configuration step each show the SD monogram, not the beaker tile.
- [x] The mark renders at 32×32 and the header layout, spacing and wordmark are unchanged.
- [x] The shell pages load the mark from a file shipped beside them at build time; there is no external URL and no duplicated inline drawing.
- [x] No beaker SVG or `.wizard-brand-mark svg` rule remains in the three first-run files.
- [x] A check that fails on the previous head and passes now: the pre-change shell pages contain the inline beaker SVG and no `app-mark.png`, while the built pages now contain `url("app-mark.png")` and `dist/app-mark.png` exists.
- [x] Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1`, `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e`.

### Additional Information

Implemented and merged as #726. This issue is filed for traceability and will be closed as completed; the single-source follow-up described under Design Ideas is intentionally left for its own change.

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 9d9ba398ccce4763b47f946f890661f6
Branch: dev2/fix/777-named-entity-decoding
Base: 7942ad1fd495cc623df67234d8a01201430da204
At: 2026-11-03T02:07:55Z

## ScienceDiscovery evidence-backed issue

**Live main:** `7942ad1fd495cc623df67234d8a01201430da204` (`test(cas): cover the multi-chunk intact layout and align the materialize contract with #708`)
**Area:** `packages/data-source` — HTML text extraction used by the free search engines
**Filed by:** ScienceDiscovery Product

### Problem

`decodeEntities` resolves only five named references (`amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`) and leaves every other named reference literal, so search-result titles and snippets reach the model and the report as `café`, `5–10`, `—`, `…`, `O'Brien`.

### Reproduction on live main

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

Actual output (main `7942ad1f`):

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

Expected (browser-equivalent text): `café — 5–10 … O'Brien`, `<b> stays text` (single pass preserved), `♦ … ’`.

### Evidence (file:line on this main)

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:27-33` — `NAMED_ENTITIES` contains exactly `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot`, `nbsp`.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:46-53` — `decodeEntities` matches **any** named reference (`([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*)`) and returns `NAMED_ENTITIES.get(name) ?? match`, i.e. everything else falls through as literal text.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts:55-58` — `textOf` (strip tags → decode → collapse) is the shared extractor.
- Call sites that turn this into user-visible text: `packages/data-source/src/web/native/free-engines.ts:64`, `:69`, `:136`, `:141`, `:183`, `:192` (titles/snippets), plus `:68`, `:135`, `:181` for result URLs.

### Impact

DuckDuckGo/Bing/Brave result titles and snippets are what `web_search` returns to the model and what reports cite; a page title like "Café culture — a review" is rendered literally, so the evidence shown to the user (and fed back into the prompt) carries entity codes instead of text. Entity-heavy pages are exactly the older/European and encyclopedia sources a science search hits often.

### Expected vs actual

- Expected: named references decode the same way a browser renders them (at minimum the typographic and Latin-1 names that appear in titles: `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `rsquo`, `lsquo`, `ldquo`, `rdquo`, `eacute`, `egrave`, `ouml`, `apos`, `middot`, `times`, `deg`, `plusmn`, …).
- Actual: only 5 names decode; the rest stay literal.

### Acceptance

1. `decodeEntities` resolves the named references it matches (full HTML5 named set, or a documented bounded table that covers at least the names listed above).
2. The single-pass guarantee from #672 is preserved: `&lt;` → `<`, `&amp;` → `&`; decoded output is never rescanned.
3. Surrogate / non-character rejection stays as it is (`�` etc. remain literal).
4. `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts` gains cases for the named references above, and the existing five keep passing.
5. No change to numeric-reference behavior (`A`, `A`, `😀`).

### Not a duplicate

Open-issue search for `entity`, `entity decode`, `html text extraction`, `named entity` returns no open report; the only entity issue is closed #672 (double decoding), whose fix this preserves. No open PR touches `html.ts` (`#663`/`#678` are the UTF-16 truncation family in other modules).

issue:779.body:
## Title

Node.js API server crashes with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT during streaming session messages — missing `response.headersSent` guard in catch-all error handler

## Summary

The ScienceDiscovery API server (`@sciencediscovery/api`) crashes with an uncaught `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT` exception when an error occurs during streaming response to `POST /api/sessions/{id}/messages`. The crash is caused by a missing `response.headersSent` check in the catch-all error handler at `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3639`. The correct guard pattern already exists elsewhere in the same file at line 3159. The crash kills the Node.js process (exit status 1), which triggers a full stack restart via tini, causing approximately 20 seconds of service unavailability and returning 502 Bad Gateway to the client.

This bug has been observed 3 times in production-like testing. The exact error that triggers the catch block inside `streamAgentRun()` after headers have been flushed has not been identified.

## Affected Version

- **Package**: `@sciencediscovery/api` version `0.0.0`
- **Source file**: `services/api/src/http/index.ts` (3718 lines)
- **Defect location**: Line 3639 (catch-all error handler)
- **Correct pattern location**: Line 3159 (streaming error handler with guard)
- **Image**: `sciencediscovery-pure:incremental-002` (built 2026-11-02)

## Runtime Environment

| Component | Version |
|-----------|---------|
| Node.js | v22.23.4 |
| OS | Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) |
| Container runtime | Docker (tini as init) |
| Architecture | x86_64 |

## Steps to Reproduce

**Stable reproduction has NOT been achieved.** The crash occurs non-deterministically during streaming session message requests. The following describes the observed conditions:

1. Start the ScienceDiscovery stack (`services/api` + adapter + JiuwenSwarm gateway/agentserver)
2. Create or access an existing session
3. Send a `POST /api/sessions/{id}/messages` request with a message that triggers agent execution
4. The agent begins streaming its response (SSE)
5. At some point during streaming, after response headers have been flushed, an error occurs inside `streamAgentRun()`
6. The error propagates to the catch-all handler at `index.ts:3607`
7. The error is not matched by any specific error type check, falls through to the `else` branch
8. `sendError(response, 500, "Internal server error")` is called at line 3639
9. `sendError` → `sendJson` → `send` → `response.writeHead()` throws `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT`
10. The uncaught exception crashes the Node.js process

**Observed frequency**: 3 crashes in ~1 hour of active testing with multiple concurrent sessions.

**Suspected triggers** (not confirmed):
- Client disconnects during SSE streaming
- LLM Gateway returns 503 during agent execution
- Internal timeout during long-running agent tasks

## Expected Behavior

When an error occurs during streaming response (after headers have been sent), the server should:
1. Log the error with full context
2. Check `response.headersSent` before attempting to send an error response
3. If headers are already sent, destroy the connection gracefully (`response.destroy(error)`)
4. If headers are not yet sent, send the appropriate error response
5. The Node.js process should NOT crash

This is the pattern already implemented at `index.ts:3159`:
```typescript
if (response.headersSent) {
  response.destroy(error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)));
} else {
  sendError(response, 502, error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
}
```

## Actual Behavior

The catch-all error handler at `index.ts:3633-3640` does not check `response.headersSent`:

```typescript
} else {
  apiLog.error("unclassified_request_error", {
    errorMessage: shortErrorMessage(error),
    method: request.method ?? "UNKNOWN",
    path: requestPath,
    status: 500,
  });
  sendError(response, 500, "Internal server error");  // ← crashes if headers already sent
}
```

When `sendError` is called after headers have been flushed, Node.js throws:

```
node:_http_server:354
    throw new ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT('write');
          ^

Error [ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT]: Cannot write headers after they are sent to the client
    at ServerResponse.writeHead (node:_http_server:354:11)
    at send (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/response.js:15:14)
    at sendJson (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/response.js:24:5)
    at sendError (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/response.js:27:5)
    at Server.<anonymous> (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/index.js:3237:17) {
  code: 'ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT'
}
```

This uncaught exception crashes the Node.js process with exit status 1.

## Error Stack Trace

```
node:_http_server:354
    throw new ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT('write');
          ^

Error [ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT]: Cannot write headers after they are sent to the client
    at ServerResponse.writeHead (node:_http_server:354:11)
    at send (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/response.js:15:14)
    at sendJson (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/response.js:24:5)
    at sendError (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/response.js:27:5)
    at Server.<anonymous> (file:///app/services/api/dist/http/index.js:3237:17) {
  code: 'ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT'
}

Node.js v22.23.4
A ScienceDiscovery process exited with status 1; stopping the stack.
```

**Cascade failure** (Adapter layer):
```
legacy_proxy_failure request_id=<sanitized>
  method=POST
  path=/api/sessions/<session-id>/messages
  phase=headers
  elapsed_ms=1993
  causes=[RemoteProtocolError in proxy.py:91]

→ Client receives: 502 Bad Gateway
```

## Timestamped Failure Sequence

| Time (relative) | Event | Source |
|-----------------|-------|--------|
| T+0s | `POST /api/sessions/{id}/messages` → 200 OK (prior successful request to same session) | API access log |
| T+0s | `GET /health` → 200 OK | Health check log |
| T+1s | **ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT thrown** at `index.js:3237` | Node.js stderr |
| T+1s | `A ScienceDiscovery process exited with status 1; stopping the stack.` | tini supervisor |
| T+2s | `legacy_proxy_failure ... RemoteProtocolError ... elapsed_ms=1993` | Adapter log |
| T+2s | `POST /api/sessions/{id}/messages` → 502 Bad Gateway | API access log |
| T+3s | `Shutting down` × 2, `Finished server process [215]`, `[48]` | Service shutdown log |
| T+3s | `Starting the sandbox runner daemon...` | tini auto-restart |
| T+10s | All services started, health checks passing | Service startup log |
| T+20s | `run-binding start/release` operations resume | Agent run log |

**Total downtime**: ~20 seconds (from crash to full recovery)

## Impact on API and Agent Sessions

### Direct Impact
- **Node.js API process crash**: The entire `services/api` process exits with status 1
- **Full stack restart**: tini supervisor stops and restarts all services
- **Service unavailability**: ~20 seconds of complete service downtime
- **Client impact**: In-flight requests receive 502 Bad Gateway

### Data Impact
- **No data loss observed**: Session state is persisted before the crash point
- **No state corruption observed**: Service recovers fully after restart
- **Agent runs interrupted**: Any in-flight agent run is terminated; run status may be left in an intermediate state

### Recurrence
- **3 occurrences** in ~1 hour of active testing
- **Non-deterministic**: Depends on timing of error during streaming
- **Auto-recovery**: Service restarts automatically each time

## Root Cause Assessment

### Classification
**B. PROBABLE_UPSTREAM_BUG** — The code defect is confirmed in upstream ScienceDiscovery native code, but the exact triggering error (what fails inside `streamAgentRun()` after headers are sent) remains unidentified.

### Defect
Missing `response.headersSent` guard in the catch-all error handler at `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3639`.

### Contributing Factor
The triggering error occurs during streaming response inside `streamAgentRun()`. After response headers have been flushed to the client, any error that propagates to the catch-all handler will cause the crash. The specific error has not been captured because the crash destroys the in-flight error object.

### Why the Correct Pattern Was Not Applied Everywhere
The correct guard pattern exists at `index.ts:3159` (in a different catch block for streaming responses). The catch-all handler at `index.ts:3639` was likely added later and did not include the guard, suggesting an oversight rather than a design choice.

## Evidence References

1. **Crash stack trace**: Captured from Node.js stderr (see Error Stack Trace section above)
2. **Source code location**: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3639` (TypeScript source)
3. **Compiled code location**: `services/api/dist/http/index.js:3237` (compiled JavaScript)
4. **Correct pattern**: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3159` (existing guard in same file)
5. **Historical occurrences**: 3 crashes in Docker container logs over ~1 hour
6. **Cascade failure log**: Adapter `legacy_proxy_failure` with `RemoteProtocolError`
7. **Recovery log**: tini auto-restart, all services recovered in ~20 seconds

## Workaround / Recovery Observation

### Current Workaround
The service auto-recovers via tini supervisor. No manual intervention is required. Downtime is approximately 20 seconds per crash.

### Proposed Fix
Add `response.headersSent` guard to the catch-all handler at `index.ts:3639`:

```typescript
} else {
  apiLog.error("unclassified_request_error", {
    errorMessage: shortErrorMessage(error),
    method: request.method ?? "UNKNOWN",
    path: requestPath,
    status: 500,
  });
  if (response.headersSent) {
    response.destroy(new Error("Internal server error (after headers sent)"));
  } else {
    sendError(response, 500, "Internal server error");
  }
}
```

This follows the exact pattern already used at `index.ts:3159`.

### Additional Recommendation
Audit all other catch blocks in `index.ts` that call `sendError()` to ensure they include the `headersSent` guard. There may be other locations with the same defect.

### Diagnostic Improvement
Consider logging the full error object (not just `shortErrorMessage`) in the `unclassified_request_error` handler to aid diagnosis of the triggering error:

```typescript
apiLog.error("unclassified_request_error", {
  errorMessage: shortErrorMessage(error),
  errorStack: error instanceof Error ? error.stack : undefined,  // ← add this
  method: request.method ?? "UNKNOWN",
  path: requestPath,
  status: 500,
});
```

## Sanitization Notice

This issue report has been sanitized:
- ✅ No API keys or authentication tokens included
- ✅ Session IDs replaced with `{id}` placeholders
- ✅ Request IDs replaced with `<sanitized>` placeholders
- ✅ Internal IP addresses limited to standard Docker networking (127.0.0.1, 172.18.0.1)
- ✅ No user data or conversation content included
- ✅ Internal file paths limited to source code locations relevant to the bug

## Metadata

- **Reporter**: CatalystPI project (Huawei collaboration)
- **Date**: 2026-11-03
- **Severity**: High (service crash with data plane impact)
- **Priority**: High (affects production stability)
- **Component**: `services/api` (Node.js HTTP server)
- **Labels**: `bug`, `crash`, `error-handling`, `streaming`
