pr:1030.body:
The Docker image job failed in the merge queue because the pinned micromamba download from GitHub releases returned `504` three times in a row. `scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs` gave up after about six seconds: three attempts, two and four seconds apart. GitHub release downloads fail in bursts that last longer than that, and the Docker job builds cold on purpose (its comment explains why it is uncached), so it has no cache to fall back on. The same downloader runs for every `docker compose build`.

## Back off for about a minute

`downloadBytesWithRetry` now makes up to six attempts with exponential backoff: 2, 4, 8, 16 and 30 seconds between them, about a minute in all, with each delay capped at 30 seconds. Which failures are retried is unchanged: 408, 429, 5xx, network errors and timeouts are; a 404 or a checksum mismatch still fails at once. The log line names the next delay.

No cache was added. The Docker job's cold build is deliberate, and the downloader's existing `BINARY_CACHE_DIR` / `BINARY_CACHE_URL` / conda mirror options remain the way to avoid the network when that is wanted.

## Validation

- `node --test scripts/binary-release/fetch-managed-micromamba.test.mjs`: 11 tests, 11 passed. One new test returns `504` five times and asserts the delays `[2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 30000]` and the sixth-attempt success. It then asserts that six consecutive `504`s give up with the `504` error after five waits. The wait is injected, so the test does not sleep.
- `node --test scripts/binary-release/*.test.mjs`: 33 tests, 32 passed. The one failure, `runner-sea.test.mjs`, imports `packages/executor/dist/runner-bundle.js`, which this unbuilt worktree does not have; the test does not touch the downloader.
- The Docker image was not rebuilt locally. The change is confined to the retry loop, which the tests above exercise.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable: no product, API, CLI or Runner behaviour changes. The only path affected is building the image, and it changes only how long a transient download failure is retried.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: `docker compose build` and the Docker CI job ride out about a minute of micromamba download errors (502/503/504, 429, timeouts) instead of failing after about six seconds.
Compatibility and migration: none.

pr:1031.body:
Closing the API closed the store's database but did not wait for the store's file writes. State arrays (`session-runs`, and the like), run stream appends, subagent mutations and workspace-file mutations each run on a per-path queue (`mkdir`, temporary file, rename). A write queued by a run or probe that ended during shutdown kept going after `closeApiServer` resolved. On SIGTERM the process exits right after `closeApiServer`, which can cut such a write off. In tests, the fixture removes the data directory while the write is still in flight.

That race failed four merge queue UT runs on 2026-11-09, each time in a different `services/api/src/server.test.ts` case: `desktop skill switches…`, `global Runner management routes…`, `updating SSH credentials immediately probes…` and `request errors after headers…`. The worker events show the two forms. In three runs, a pending `mkdir` recreated a directory being removed: `ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir` in the after hook. In the other, a pending `session-runs` state rename found its directory gone: `ENOENT … rename …/session-runs/.state-…`.

## The API waits for queued writes before closing the store

`SessionStore.whenWritesSettle()` awaits every entry of the store's write queues and the catalog save queue, then checks again, because a write that settles can queue another. The re-check is bounded at 100 passes, so a writer that keeps re-queuing cannot hold shutdown forever. The API lifecycle awaits it as the last cleanup step, immediately before `store.close()`. The SIGTERM path keeps its existing 15-second limit.

## Test fixtures remove data directories with retries

Writes the store does not own (a probe, a sidecar) can still land after close. `removeTestRoot` already retried for that reason (`maxRetries: 10`). Six `server.test.ts` fixtures removed their directory with a plain `rm`, including three of the four that failed. They now use the same options, defined once as `retryingRemoval`.

## Validation

- New `store.test.ts` case: a state write blocked on a gate, which queues a second write when it finishes. `whenWritesSettle()` does not resolve while the gate is closed; after release, both files hold their values and no temporary file is left. As a reverse check, a `whenWritesSettle()` that returns immediately makes this case fail.
- `node --import tsx --test src/server.test.ts`: 112 tests, 110 passed, 2 failed. Both failures are pre-existing in this environment and fail identically on unmodified `main` files: the PDF upload case needs `services/paper/.venv`, and `API runs one observable subagent through task and keeps nested task denied` fails its assertion on `main` as well.
- `node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` in `services/api`: 2044 tests, 2033 passed, 11 failed, 0 cancelled. All 11 fail the same way with this change's three source files restored to `main`, or fail on missing local prerequisites: five need Python virtualenvs this worktree does not have (`services/paper/.venv` for three PDF cases, `services/evolve/.venv` for the IdeaTree and evolve-thinking journeys); five are `specialist-runtime/process-adapters.st.test.ts` Claude/ACP transport cases, which also fail on `main` here; one is the subagent case above. None involves shutdown or data-directory removal.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: no errors.

## E2E user journeys

Not run. No request, response or UI behaviour changes: the change orders shutdown steps (queued writes before the store closes) and is covered by the store test above and by every API test that closes a server. A user-visible journey would need a SIGTERM delivered while a write is queued, which the existing E2E layers do not drive. This is a coverage gap, not a pass.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: stopping the API (SIGTERM) no longer exits while queued run-state or stream writes are still being written; flaky `server.test.ts` failures in UT stop.
Compatibility and migration: none. Shutdown can take as long as the queued writes, within the existing 15-second SIGTERM limit.

pr:168.body:
This PR adds an opt-in, user-perspective JiuwenSwarm → `antibody-design` Skill → Ascend NPU journey, alongside the lower-level mocked NPU binding test. It depends on Skill backport PR #159; duplicate Skill PR #167 was closed.

## User journey

A fresh Project/Session is created with a live model and selected 131 Runner. The driver uploads the user's two PDBs and sends a high-level request through the public Session Runs API. It does not invoke any model script, choose a Python environment, or preseed model assets. The real Agent must load the Skill, inspect/select a managed environment, push inputs, perform first-use preparation and validation, run RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Protenix → screening on NPU, pull results, declare report/CSV/CIF Artifacts, and explain the result. The test observes automatic wake Runs, committed execution receipts, nonempty remote and local stage files, completed transfers, and final Artifacts. It never resubmits an accepted user Run; a pipeline retry is accepted only after the preceding execution has a confirmed, committed failure. Any `unknown`/unconfirmed execution fails the test.

The real case is tagged `npu:required`, `model:real`, `status:external`, collected but deselected by ordinary PR CI until gated NPU hardware exists. The mocked binding/ST case remains for CI.

## Real-hardware verification (2026-09-24)

- **Full-Agent E2E: PASS (1/1)** on a fresh Project `9df41ef6-e2ea-4096-8e3a-6f8f5783e546`, Session `fb3dbdac-e218-40d5-a50c-565167421e4e`, initial user Run `a62cd447-a1e6-4570-8ddc-de3937edb97d`. The Agent loaded `antibody-design` itself, selected a managed environment, pushed inputs, and completed first-use preparation `74864a72-89e7-475d-af6e-ebf34495deaf` and validation with committed zero-exit receipts. One NPU pipeline Execution `a91eb590-1457-491a-977e-be73e98ba73c` finished `completed / committed / exitCode=0` on the selected remote Runner. RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, Protenix, and screening each produced files. Report, CSV, and CIF were transferred to the Session, declared as Artifacts, and explained by the Agent across the original and an automatic wake Run.
- The full live submission used the test driver at `9afed0fa`; the final `ae556055` driver passed by **read-only observation of the same Run**, after fixing a test-only assertion that had incorrectly required three `declare_artifact` tool calls even though the Agent legitimately declares multiple Artifacts in one call. No extra NPU job was submitted for that verification. The final Agent response also names the report, CSV, and CIF. The WSL product source snapshot was labelled `89a3ac7c` and included the Skill backport.
- Earlier fresh full-Agent Run `8d3814fa-f681-4957-a647-a55c81ac06e8` is **not a pass**: first-use preparation `4eb49ef9-8c60-4708-8996-9db8fec44500` became `unknown/unconfirmed` after `fetch failed`. A first pipeline attempt then had a confirmed Runner workspace-snapshot `ENOENT` on a transient MindScience `__pycache__` file; the Agent recovered and its later NPU pipeline/output delivery succeeded, but the preparation receipt remained unconfirmed. This is a real stability risk to address separately, not a result hidden by the passing rerun.
- The older prepared-environment NPU Run `c1ba1acc-2968-417f-8714-7947ee3e1b32` is lower-level evidence only, not the full-Agent E2E result.
- `node --check`, CI contract, E2E metadata (0 errors, 11 pre-existing legacy warnings), and diff whitespace checks passed locally. The previous CI run had ST, UT, Docker, both binary builds and CLA passing; the latest push starts a fresh CI run, so its final state is not yet claimed. The hardware case is intentionally deselected in CI.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`
User impact: no runtime code change; adds regression coverage for the complete Agent-to-NPU workflow.
Compatibility: merge Skill backport PR #159 before this PR.

pr:196.body:
Users who route through Requesty currently have to set it up as a custom OpenAI compatible provider by hand. This adds it as a built-in preset alongside OpenRouter, with the same shape: OpenAI chat completions, `GET /models` discovery, and a models.dev mapping for catalog facts and prices.

## Preset
`packages/schema/src/model-provider-presets.ts` gets a `requesty` entry right after OpenRouter: base URL `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, `apiVariant: "openai"`, `modelDiscovery: "openai-models"`, docs `https://docs.requesty.ai`, key page `https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys`. `ModelProviderPresetId` in `model-provider.ts` gains `"requesty"`. The wizard and settings UI read the preset list, so nothing else changes there. Requesty is not made a default anywhere.

## models.dev mapping
models.dev publishes a `requesty` provider whose `api` is `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, so the host check in `pricesApplyToPreset` accepts its prices for this preset. It is mapped after OpenRouter, in the aggregator block, so first publish wins still hands capability facts to the vendor listings. The ordering test in `packages/model/src/models-dev.test.ts` now counts `requesty` as an aggregator so a misplaced insert would fail it.

## How to test
Pick Requesty in the connect wizard, paste a key from https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys, and choose a listed model such as `openai/gpt-4o-mini` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`. For EU routing, edit the base URL to `https://router.eu.requesty.ai/v1`.

## Validation
Run on macOS arm64 at ae150eb, with deps installed only for `@sciencediscovery/model` and its workspace dependencies.
- `pnpm typecheck` in `packages/schema` and `packages/model`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: OK, 276 package source files checked.
- Package unit tests with `node --test "src/**/*.test.ts"`: schema 12 passed / 0 failed, model 45 passed / 0 failed (including "every aggregator mapping sits after every vendor mapping"). These files are tagged `os:linux`, so on macOS I ran them with `process.platform` reported as linux; nothing else was changed.
- Live check through the package's own code: `listProviderModels` with the preset's `baseUrl` and discovery strategy returned 762 models including `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, and `streamModelTurn` with the preset's protocol and variant streamed a reply from `openai/gpt-4o-mini` with usage reported.
- Not run: `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` and `apps/web` tests. The UT and E2E layers need a bubblewrap sandbox on Linux, which this macOS host does not have.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED on this host (no Linux sandbox for the local stack). The change adds one entry to a list the connect wizard already renders, and the live check above covers the provider's discovery and chat path. Happy to add or rerun a journey if you want one for this.

## Release
Release category: release:feature (label pending a maintainer, I cannot apply labels)
User impact: Requesty appears as a provider preset in the model connect wizard.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Disclosure: I work at Requesty. Happy to adjust anything to match project conventions.

pr:222.body:
## Summary

Ready for maintainer review and merge. This PR extracts Idea Tree from the evolve process into an independently runnable Python service and exposes its research capabilities as session-scoped MCP tools.

Current head: `867ffa43` (rebased onto main `82507f9e` on 2026-11-06) — the squashed service extraction plus the review-fix commits listed below. Related to #101 and #84; partial delivery of the broader integration acceptance scope, so keep #101 open. This establishes the service boundary ahead of the evolve migration in #102.

## Changes

- Move the Idea Tree engine, service layer, models, prompts and templates out of evolve's vendored implementation into `services/idea-tree`. Preserve the existing research algorithm and remove the old evolve router registrations.
- Add a dedicated FastAPI process with a health endpoint, shutdown cleanup, internal-token authentication and loopback port `4314`. Require a single ASGI worker because active research tasks and short-lived capabilities are process-local.
- Persist research, trees and settings in a service-owned data directory. Copy legacy records once without deleting originals; conflicting destination records fail migration rather than overwrite data.
- Publish `create_idea_research`, `get_idea_research`, `control_idea_research` and `view_idea_tree` through scoped MCP endpoints. Project/session identity and model callback credentials come from the trusted control plane rather than model arguments. Capabilities expire after five minutes; revoking a transport capability does not stop autonomous research.
- Replace the old API Python client with `IdeaTreeServiceClient`. Discover tool schemas from the service, preserve historical graph reads, research-created messages and SSE forwarding, and keep the six existing frontend research/graph/settings routes and response shapes.
- Include the service in stack startup (`scripts/start-stack.sh` and `scripts/start-stack.mjs`), Docker packaging, the Windows desktop payload, isolated browser-test configuration, test discovery and coverage. Update English and Chinese developer documentation.

## Review fixes included

- Restore complete `evolveAvailability` initialization and bootstrap wiring.
- Restore the actual `research_service.py` service layer instead of the accidentally duplicated engine module.
- Migrate remaining tests away from the removed Python client and evolve vendor modules; remove the unused compatibility adapter.
- Remove the Evolve-readiness guard from independent Idea Tree routes.
- Disable Uvicorn access logging in the application lifespan as well as the launcher, preventing MCP capability URLs from being logged with direct `uvicorn ...:app` startup. Include a direct-Uvicorn regression.
- Correct stale developer-document paths and replace the redundant listener-address type assertion identified by CodeCheck with a runtime guard.
- Persist, validate and round-trip `roleThinkingEfforts` in the service settings, validate the merged assessor weights on read, and pin both with a settings round-trip test.
- Stage, start and port-map the service in the Windows desktop and the dev launcher: `services/idea-tree` and its own `envs-template/idea-tree` venv are staged into the payload (both editable `.pth` conventions are handled), `portsForEpoch` gives it `4314 + epoch` with the URL tracking the port, the loading page has an `idea-tree` stage, `packagedEnv` exports its interpreter, and `start-stack.mjs` provisions/health-checks it with the same URL/token contract as evolve.
- Fail the payload build on any editable `.pth` entry that escapes the repo, not just `_editable_impl_*.pth`: the rules moved to `scripts/lib/pth-guard.mjs` and are unit tested, so a stale plain `<name>.pth` from the standalone project can no longer ship (review hardening request).

## Validation

| Surface | Result |
| --- | --- |
| L1 static checks | PASS |
| UT | PASS |
| ST | PASS |
| L2 mocked browser E2E (governed, literature, research, standard-config, standard-journeys) | PASS on `4e71b37a` (all five shards green); CI for `867ffa43` is running |
| Coverage | PASS |
| GitCode CodeCheck | PASS |
| GitCode SCA, anti-poison and blacklist checks | PASS |
| CLA | All contributors confirmed signed |
| `win_desktop` unit tests | 168/168 (`node --import tsx --test test/*.test.ts`), including 8 new `pth-guard` cases |
| `services/idea-tree` standalone tests / API + web regressions | PASS at the review-fix commits (see the individual commit messages) |

Real L3/L4/L5, binary release and Docker execution are skipped by this PR's CI policy; they are not counted as passes. The statuses above are job outcomes, not invented test-case counts.

Local validation was split across rounds: the squashed candidate had identical source to the preceding validated head, and the later commits are the review fixes above, each with its own tests. The Windows desktop packaging pipeline itself was not executed on my host (no assembled payload there), so the new payload staging is CI-verified rather than locally built.

## Deployment and scope

- Stop the old stack before upgrading. The maintained stack scripts and Docker packaging start the new service; custom supervisors must provide its process and matching URL/token configuration. On Windows, the desktop payload ships `envs/idea-tree` and shifts the port with the rest of the stack's epoch.
- Session ownership, chat-message writes and model-secret provisioning remain in the API control plane. Research still uses the existing run-bound LLM callback pending #102; provider API keys are not passed to the service.
- Artifact/provenance/CAS ownership remains outside this PR (#98).
- Not covered here: `services/launcher/src/serve.ts` (the embedded `ScienceDiscovery serve` payload path) still starts only runner/memory-graph/evolve; covering it needs an `ideaTree` entry in the payload manifest and the binary-release payload shipping `envs/idea-tree`. Flagged rather than silently assumed.
- Targeted public-route, SSE and create-time message regressions are included. A complete baseline/candidate differential of all six public routes and a complete chat/agent event-stream golden trace are not claimed. These remaining broader #101 acceptance items must stay tracked explicitly rather than be inferred from green CI.

## Maintainer review and merge request

Please review and merge this PR after confirming acceptance of the independent Idea Tree service boundary: its process/port, internal token, state and settings ownership, one-time migration, and API-to-service protocol. The `needs-human` decision still requires a maintainer; this request does not claim it has already been approved.

Every review thread on this PR is resolved. Please re-review the current head and grant approval if the service boundary and the explicitly documented scope are acceptable for merge. No automatic merge has been enabled.

Release category: `release:feature` (label applied).

pr:231.body:
## Purpose

Add a repository-owned independent PR review skill at `.agents/skills/sciencediscovery-review/SKILL.md`, with focused references for repository contracts and the optionally configured daily brief.

- Pin reviewed base/head and record the exact canonical skill bytes loaded.
- Route reviews through architecture, permissions/sandbox, orchestration, artifact provenance, user journeys, and current CI contracts.
- Distinguish observed evidence from author claims, mocked checks, and unavailable live-model validation.
- Keep daily selection conditional: known complete label catalog, exact priority/ready rules, new commit deltas, and a ten-PR per-repository daily cap.
- Produce local findings only; the skill grants no posting, approval, merge, model-spending, or security-setting authority.

Closes #260. `E2E_SWARM_TASK` was a test-only declaration: `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exported it for the JiuwenSwarm backend and twelve specs gated on it. It verified nothing, was always `1` in CI, and made DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on the native loop, although that loop delegates sub-agents through the platform `task` tool as well. The stack now says how it runs agent turns, and the journeys check that instead.

## `/health` reports how agent turns run

`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `/health` and `/api/health` include `agent: { executor, subagents }`, taken from the same `jiuwenSwarmConfigFromEnv()` result the API uses to start agent turns. `executor` is `jiuwenswarm` or `native`; `subagents` is `task` or `jiuwenswarm`, and always `task` on the native loop. This lives in the API rather than the adapter's `/agent/info` because the API decides delegation in both modes, and a native stack has no adapter. The adapter forwards `/health` to the API, so a JiuwenSwarm stack answers the same way.

The L1 contract baseline (`test/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json`) records `/health` bodies and will show the added `agent` key on a manual `--compare`. The baseline is not regenerated here: its README reserves that to a human review, and the comparison is not part of any CI layer.

## Journeys check the stack instead of a variable

`test/helpers/e2e.ts` adds `requireAgentStack()`. It reads `/health` and fails as BLOCKED, quoting what the stack reported, when sub-agents are not delegated through `task`. With `{ executor: "jiuwenswarm" }` it also requires that executor.

- Journeys that test JiuwenSwarm's own behaviour require the JiuwenSwarm executor: `swarm-research`, `swarm-specialist-mcp`, `swarm-tool-failure`, `artifact-revision` and the four `literature-review-*` specs.
- The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) require only `task` delegation and run on either executor. Their score metrics now record the reported executor instead of a constant `"jiuwenswarm"`, so a native run is labelled native.
- Combined gates are split. `E2E_SWARM_EXCLUSIVE` and `E2E_LITERATURE_FIXTURE` keep their own checks and messages, as do `E2E_SWARM_COMPACTION` and `E2E_MCP_FAULT_PROXY`. They protect exclusive stacks and fixtures, not the stack's identity.

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, the specs, `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`, `jiuwen_swarm/tests/README.md` and the three benchmark READMEs. `git grep E2E_SWARM_TASK` finds nothing.

## Validation

Local host, on `9f8fcc6a`, with a scratch `HOME` so the layers use a JiuwenSwarm instance of their own (see #251).

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | 3714 | 3714 | 3714 | 0 | 0 |
| ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| E2E mocked (`pnpm ci:e2e`, profile `pr`) | 70 | 70 | 70 | 0 | 0 |

- New API test "health reports how agent turns run": passed natively (`agent` = `native`/`task`) and in the UT layer, which runs the API on JiuwenSwarm (`jiuwenswarm`/`task`); both `/health` and `/api/health` are checked.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes for the changed specs and helper.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** on `9f8fcc6a`, local isolated stack with the JiuwenSwarm backend. The research batch (20/20) contains every Swarm-gated mocked journey: each one now passes its precondition by reading the stack's `/health` through the adapter, with no `E2E_SWARM_TASK` set anywhere. The standard (44/44) and literature (6/6) batches also passed.

The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) cannot run on a pull request. Their gate now accepts either executor as long as sub-agents use platform `task` delegation, which is what a native Nightly needs. Their next run will show it.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none for product use. `/health` gains an additive `agent` field describing the deployment.
Compatibility and migration: anyone running journeys by hand no longer sets `E2E_SWARM_TASK`; the stack's own configuration decides. A stack older than this change does not report `agent` and its Swarm-gated journeys report BLOCKED.

CSV 重复 ID 处理生成的后缀可能与输入中已有的 ID 相同，导致多条记录共用一个内部标识。点击值为 `333` 的记录时，会同时高亮两行，详情面板却显示 `111`。

## 保证 CSV 记录的内部标识唯一

- 为记录分配内部标识时，检查其是否与已分配的标识冲突；缺少原始 ID 时生成的标识也执行相同检查。
- 为每个基础标识记录下一次可尝试的后缀，避免大量重复 ID 反复扫描已占用的后缀。
- 保留原始 CSV 单元格值和解析结果的确定性，每条受影响的记录只计入一次重复 ID 警告。

复现数据：

```csv
id,value
sample#4,111
sample,222
sample,333
```

打开 CSV 可视化，切换到 **Data table（数据表）**，点击值为 **333** 的记录。修复后只高亮这一行，详情面板显示 **333**。

## 验证结果

测试提交：`82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7`，基于 `main` 的 `c33c1ae2b7100ab86de451afb02aefe0bd7a3045`。

- CSV 测试：**通过 29 / 失败 0 / 跳过 0**。其中三项 ID 冲突回归用例在修复前均失败。
- 性能回归：包含 20,000 个已占用后缀 ID 和 20,000 个重复 ID 的 40,000 行 CSV，在加入后缀游标前超过子进程的 10 秒时限；加入游标后，本地测试约 287 毫秒完成。
- UT（`pnpm ci:ut`）：计划 **3723**，执行 **3723**，通过 **3723**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- ST（`pnpm ci:st`）：计划 **2**，执行 **2**，通过 **2**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 静态检查（`pnpm ci:l1`）：计划 **4**，执行 **4**，通过 **4**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 使用模拟模型的浏览器 E2E（`pnpm ci:e2e`）：计划 **71**，执行 **71**，通过 **71**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 加入后缀游标后，独立代码审查未发现仍需处理的问题。

此前测试失败及原因：

- 首次 UT **3721/3723** 通过：本机 bubblewrap 0.6.1 不支持 `--disable-userns`，且克隆固定版本的研究评估器时发生 TLS 连接中断。
- 另一次 UT **3720/3723** 通过。其中两项评估相关失败在未修改的 `main` 上同样出现（**3717/3719** 通过）：Python 3.14 与固定版本的 SciPy 不兼容，以及全局评估器路径覆盖使另一项契约检查暴露出依赖缺失。将固定版本的评估器准备到预期缓存位置，并使用 Python 3.12.13 后，两项问题均解决。其余一项权限队列断言属于间歇性失败：该用例在 `main`、较早的修复分支测试，以及使用全新服务状态的最终完整测试中均通过。
- 首次完整浏览器测试执行 **71** 项，**通过 70 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**；CSV 流程已通过。唯一失败是 J3 的托管 Python 环境前置条件，Conda 下载依赖时出现 `SSL routines::unexpected eof while reading`。未修改的 `main` 执行 **70** 项，**通过 69 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**，复现了相同问题。修复分支重新测试时使用单独复制并补齐的依赖缓存。

## E2E 用户流程

提交 `82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7` 在浏览器和本机进程运行的产品环境中验证**通过**。完整模拟模型浏览器测试 **71/71** 通过，**失败 0 / 阻塞 0 / 跳过 0**。

CSV 流程的 **4/4** 个用户步骤全部通过：通过真实沙箱生成并声明 CSV 产物、打开可视化、点击 **333**，再依次切换 **111 → 222 → 333**。预期与实际结果一致：始终只高亮一条记录，选中数量为 1，详情值与所选记录一致，并保留原始 ID。同一操作也已在正在运行的本地产品中手动验证。

可复用用例位于 `test/journey-inspect-csv-records.spec.ts`，纳入 `pnpm ci:e2e`。该流程使用独立的本地模拟模型，覆盖无需真实模型凭据的 PR 测试场景。最终完整测试使用单独复制并补齐的科学计算依赖缓存，J3 的环境创建、使用、审计和删除流程也全部通过。

## 发布说明

发布类别：`release:fix`

用户影响：选择存在 ID 冲突的 CSV 记录时，详情面板显示该记录的数据，并且只高亮所选行。

兼容性与迁移：无需迁移。原始 CSV 值保持不变；重新打开 CSV 时，受影响的内部行标识会重新生成为唯一值。

贡献者账号没有上游仓库写入权限，GitHub 的 `release:fix` 标签需由维护者添加。

pr:285.body:
## Summary

Fixes #264.

Make proxy setup usable from one **Network and proxy** settings entry, and keep local application transport independent of outbound proxy failures. Reuse the existing proxy registry, downloader cache/retry, and environment-readiness mechanisms rather than adding an automatic external-network startup gate.

## Changes

- Offer environment configuration, a custom HTTP(S)/SOCKS5 proxy, or direct access. Keep named proxies, bypass hosts and Web/MCP overrides under advanced settings; existing model overrides remain compatible.
- Stage proxy changes across settings tabs. The footer saves them; Cancel/X discards unsaved changes. Add an authenticated, non-persisting download-source connection diagnostic.
- Declare and lock Python HTTP/WebSocket SOCKS dependencies. Adapter loopback HTTP/WebSocket connections explicitly bypass outbound proxies; external HTTP clients are initialized lazily.
- Add small source-loadable shared routing/download helpers. Resolve model requests against their actual target, respect bypass rules, and pass the global policy to managed environment setup/create/install operations without mutating process-wide environment variables.
- Wire the saved global route into both Runner clients: the control plane's own local Runner, and every remote Runner that `RemoteComputeClient` deploys or installs into. Environment mode resolves on the remote Runner itself; a custom URL pointing at the control host's loopback is refused with the reason and the two ways out, because forwarding it would make the remote Runner call itself.
- Refuse proxy settings that cannot be applied instead of degrading silently: a `url` policy without an address, and a proxy URL carrying a path or query (rejected at save time as well, so a stored value cannot fail only per request). The generated `NO_PROXY` lists `::1` rather than `[::1]`, which no consumer matches against a bare hostname.
- Preserve underlying, redacted network errors and existing pinned versions, SHA-256/TLS verification, caches and retries. Update English/Chinese configuration, architecture and REST documentation, including the settings-projection contract change (environment summaries now mask credentials and query strings).

## Rebase onto `main` (`b31f74eb`)

- The branch was 699 commits behind and conflicted in three files. `packages/model/src/client.ts`, `services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts`, `packages/executor` and the gateway tests were re-derived from `main`, then the PR's own deltas re-applied one hunk at a time.
- `normalizeUsage` is gone from this PR: `main` moved it to `packages/model/src/usage.ts` and already reads the protocol field per dialect with alias fallback, so the bug this branch started from is fixed upstream. Keeping the branch copy would have reverted that.
- The branch's `services/adapter/uv.lock` is dropped because `main` deleted the lockfile (`feat(sizeopt)`).
- The branch's last commit (`a49f92ed`, "preserve current runtime interfaces after rebase") is dropped: it reverted `model-connectivity.ts`, `client.ts` and the adapter `network.py` to the branch's older shape, i.e. it undid upstream work rather than preserving the PR. Its only real purpose was to make the stale branch compile, which the re-application above now covers.

## Validation

No real LLM API calls or paid tokens were used.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm --filter` builds: `schema`, `data-source`, `model`, `executor`, `runner`, `api` | Passed |
| `pnpm --recursive typecheck` plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | Passed |
| Proxy transport, resolver, connectivity (`packages/data-source`, `services/api`) | 14 passed |
| Model client and dispatcher regressions (`packages/model`) | 46 passed |
| Runner client proxy propagation (`packages/executor`) | 7 passed |
| Web settings component suite (`apps/web`) | 258 passed |
| `pnpm architecture:check` / `pnpm ci:selftest` | 43 / 16 passed |
| `services/runner` environment-store, `services/api` store/server suites | Not runnable on this Windows host (`os:linux` tags, bubblewrap, SQLite unlink); CI covers them |
| Adapter hermetic pytest | Not runnable here (no usable Python); CI covers it |

The browser journeys use a real local API/Swarm stack, not mocked settings storage. They cover basic defaults; custom proxy save/cancel; cross-tab drafts; reload persistence; NO_PROXY; Web/MCP overrides and inheritance; rejection of deleting an in-use proxy; and removing references plus deleting the proxy in one save. Only the first journey's connection-test response is browser-mocked; transport ST tests exercise local HTTP/SOCKS proxy fixtures and authentication failures without external access.

The legacy layout E2E is adapted but remains quarantined and was not run. No production service was restarted.

## Scope and boundaries

- This does not grant sandbox network access or add an automatic direct fallback when a configured proxy fails.
- The manual diagnostic checks one download source, not every provider or model credentials. There is no new startup preflight framework or traffic dashboard.
- Saving multiple settings sections is sequential, not a cross-section transaction: a later failure does not roll back earlier successful requests. Unsaved changes remain drafts.
- SOCKS5 support in Undici remains experimental. Remote end-to-end proxy reachability, binary installation and real external providers have not been newly exercised by this PR.

## Summary

Add all **132 DeepResearchBench II tasks** as a release-only L5 benchmark, following the existing tagged Playwright real-E2E framework. L5 now selects **151** real cases (19 inherited + 132 DRB II); L4 remains 19. No new paid cases enter PR/L2 or merge/L3 gates.

## Design and scope

- Statically declare every task identity; collection is offline and cannot silently shrink when data or credentials are absent.
- Each task receives an isolated research worker through the existing matrix/reconciliation path. Preserve original task text and blocked-source instructions; only append artifact delivery instructions. Rubrics are never research-Agent input.
- Do **not** carry over the experimental two-subagent prompt cap. Product quotas still apply and are recorded. Memory Graph is disabled for DRB II workers.
- Download upstream only at execution time: `imlrz/DeepResearch-Bench-II@b38f360603db9531b102aef8c166cedb8509b6f6`, shallow/blob-filtered/sparse checkout of necessary files, locked Python dependencies, and dataset/evaluator hash checks. No upstream dataset or report corpus is vendored. Verified local `.git` size was about 708 KB.
- Reuse upstream rubric prompts and scoring; add strict response completeness/type checks and a non-destructive JSON parser (upstream's repair regex can corrupt valid compact JSON).
- Account for upstream task 116's duplicate rubric texts: 56 raw entries / 50 distinct scored entries, matching upstream text-keyed output rather than making the task fail permanently.
- Record reports, rubric results, per-call Judge usage including retries, model/config identity and separate generation/evaluation durations. Delivery/evaluation failure fails the case; valid low scores are review evidence, **not** hidden failures or an invented quality threshold.

## Configuration and release impact

Uses the existing `nightly-ci-ds` generator/Judge settings. `DRB2_JUDGE_API_STYLE` defaults to `openai`; set it to `deepseek` for DeepSeek transport. Judge output starts at 32,768 tokens and increases on truncation up to 65,536. One Judge request at a time, 15 rubrics per batch, at most three attempts.

Generation budget: 120 minutes/task; evaluation: 30 minutes/task; existing research job ceiling: 240 minutes including preparation. The workflow retains two concurrent jobs. At 30 minutes generation/task, DRB II alone is approximately 66 worker-hours / 33 wall-clock hours, before setup and judging. **A tag-triggered release now incurs this full paid benchmark and waits for its gate.** A timeout is not a spending cap.

DRB II workers do not require DRB I, HF or Jina evaluator prerequisites. Configured research providers may separately require keys. Per-task upstream licenses still apply, notably CC BY-NC for tasks 26 and 110.

## Verification

- CI contract suite: **59/59 passed**, including new selection/sharding, prompt isolation, score completeness and mocked Judge transport tests.
- L1: **4/4 passed**.
- Actual offline Playwright collection: **151 release identities**, exactly **132 DRB II**; daily remains **19**.
- Runtime shallow/sparse preparation and pinned checks: passed.
- Local transport smoke against the **actual pinned upstream evaluator and all 132 task rubrics**, with a synthetic loopback Judge: **132/132 passed**, no LLM tokens. This proves evaluator plumbing, **not research quality**.
- E2E metadata check: 0 errors (existing legacy warnings unchanged).
- Documentation checks, lint of modified runbooks, and `git diff --check`: passed.

## Explicit limitations / not claimed

- Full 132-task paid Agent execution was **not** run as part of this PR. Prior local four-report real experiments are not a full-suite result and are not this branch's E2E verification.
- No historical quality regression threshold and no claim of official leaderboard comparability; Judge model and execution conditions matter.
- Existing session token summaries can omit intermediate/child calls and are labelled **not a billing total**. Judge calls have their own detailed usage ledger.
- This PR does not fix the existing 5-second status-poll recovery policy, long-task resource pressure, or persistence performance. Failures remain failures; assertions are not relaxed to hide them.

Runbook: `test/benchmarks/deepresearchbench-ii/README.md`.

pr:311.body:
## What does this PR do / why do we need it

Implements the **full three-layer plan** for natural-language program evolution (GitHub issue #310): turn `/evolve-design` from a hidden slash command into something a natural-language sentence can trigger, with the framework actively recommending a tree-search evolution and the interaction staying natural-language end to end.

Today `/evolve-design` is a hidden slash command: a user must already know the prefix to start an evolution search, and the only visible entry is a button in the artifact detail modal that fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` (still requiring manual completion). The interaction is command-shaped, not natural-language.

### Layer 1 — Composer intent recognition (frontend)

- **`apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts`** (new): pure `detectEvolveIntent(message)` — true only when an improvement verb pairs with an evolvable target (`program` / `code` / `algorithm` / `function` / `model` / `script` / `artifact` …). Non-evolvable targets (`formatting` / `layout` / `description` / `explanation`) never match, and bare "better" with no target never matches. `isEvolveDesignCommand()` separates the explicit slash command from natural language.
- **`EvolveSuggestionBar`** (new): a low-intrusion confirmation bar. Detection only *offers*; the user must explicitly accept before the algorithm picker opens — an evolution search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations), so a false positive is worse than a missed suggestion.
- **`App.tsx`**: an explicit `/evolve-design` command opens the algorithm picker directly (existing behavior preserved); a natural-language intent shows the confirmation bar first, and only an accepted suggestion opens the picker. Both flags reset when the message leaves evolve intent.

### Layer 2 — Agent-driven recommendation (backend)

- **`packages/evolve/src/index.ts`**: the `create_evolve_run` tool description now tells the agent to **recommend** an evolution search when the user asks in natural language to improve a program / code / algorithm / model / result against a measurable target — not only when they type `/evolve-design`. The agent phrases it as a plain suggestion ("this looks like a search-shaped problem; want me to run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") and starts only after the user confirms. This builds on the evolve-design skill, whose description already lists natural-language triggers.

### Layer 3 — Visible entry points (frontend)

- **Composer**: a new sparkle "program evolution" button fills a natural-language prompt (`Improve the program: ` / `改进一下这个程序：`) instead of a slash command; `detectEvolveIntent` recognises it and offers the suggestion bar.
- **Artifact detail modal**: the evolve button now fills a natural-language seed prompt (`Make the artifact X better: ` / `让产物 X 变得更好：`) instead of the `/evolve-design ...` command text.
- **`intent.ts`**: adds `artifact` / `产物` as evolvable targets and `变得更好` as an improvement verb so both seed prompts are recognised.

### Why confirmation before the picker?

A search spends real budget. Detection is a guess, so it must only offer; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This is the core false-positive guard — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never routed into an expensive search.

### Why verb+target pairing?

Intent detection is deliberately narrow: `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `这个更好` / `make this better` all stay silent; only sentences pointing at an evolvable target (program / code / algorithm) match.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Closes #310.

## Review follow-up (2026-10-29)

- Closing keyword corrected to plain `Closes #310`; the earlier markdown-link form left GitHub's `closingIssuesReferences` empty, so the merge would not have auto-closed the issue.
- Blocking item "CI green on this tip" is already satisfied **on this tip**: run [40645827814](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40645827814) (attempt 2) is `success`, 17 checks success (L1, ST, UT, Coverage, merge-gate, 5x L2, Freeze mocked E2E, CodeCheck); L3/L4-L5/Docker/Binary are `skipped` by policy.
- Remaining blocker is the human one: re-approval and the `needs-human` product-risk decision. The tip is unchanged (`070820a6`), so no CI re-run was triggered by this edit; the label is left untouched.

## Test Plan and Test result

Verification commit: `f9fe5846` (9 files, +192/-5, single commit, based on GitHub main `cc974a14`)

- Web typecheck: `tsc --noEmit` passed, 0 errors
- Web unit tests: **107 passed / 0 failed** (includes 8 new evolve-intent tests)
- Web vite build: passed

Intent recognition behaviour verified:

| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` / `让程序跑得更好` | triggers |
| `Make the artifact X better` / `让产物 X 变得更好` | triggers (seed prompts) |
| `make this better` / `这个更好` | no trigger (no explicit evolvable target) |
| `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `改进一下说明文字` | no trigger (non-evolvable target) |
| `the first one is better` | no trigger (ordinary conversation) |
| explicit `/evolve-design` command | opens the picker directly, no confirmation bar (existing behavior preserved) |

## Self-checklist

- [x] **Design**: follows the issue's three-layer plan; confirmation-bar guard and narrow verb+target detection address false positives and budget protection

- [x] **Interface**: no public API change; reuses the existing `/api/evolve/runs` chain, `EvolveToolRuntime` and `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`
- [x] **Docs**: no website-doc change required for this frontend layer

## Review follow-up (sciencediscovery-bot review 5697796828, 2026-10-30)

Both points from that review are closed in code, not in prose. The branch was rebased onto today's `main` (`4e4837a9`) with no conflicts, and now carries three commits: the feature commit, the red test commit `85a78ad8`, and the fix `54889783`. New tip: `54889783e4831af67df7df517f7bd65912ea1da4`. Diff against `4e4837a9`: 15 files, +846/−14 (the two new files are the gate and its tests).

### 1. `requestConfirmation` is required, and the gate itself fails closed

- **`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:587`** — `EvolveTurnContext.requestConfirmation` is now required (`RequestEvolveConfirmation`, declared at `:203`), so any new evolve construction site that forgets it is a compile error instead of a silent spend. `tsc -p services/api` is what enforces it.
- **`services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts:385-387`** — the `turn.approvalMode !== "ask_for_dangerous"` fallback is gone; the runtime asks the gate and returns its refusal.
- **`services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts:88-97`** — when the callback is absent (only reachable from a caller outside the type system: an untyped script, a stale build, a test double), the gate returns
  `{ confirmed: false, refusedBecause: "confirmation unavailable: this turn has no approval path, so the evolution search was not started" }`.
  **Caller-visible behaviour:** `createEvolveRun` returns that string as its `refusedBecause`; the tool layer hands it to the agent, which relays it; no run is created, no discrimination probe runs, no budget is spent. It is the same data-not-exception shape as the existing "not confirmed by the user" refusal.
- **Why required rather than only fail-closed:** the field is what makes the *next* construction site safe at compile time; the runtime guard alone would only cover callers the type system never sees, and those must still be refused rather than allowed.

On `always_allow`: with the gate wired, an `always_allow` session still short-circuits inside `store.requestPermission` (`services/api/src/store.ts:5532`) — that is the product's meaning of the mode for every privileged action (`run_shell`, `direct_code`, …). The defect the review named was the *absent* gate falling back to that mode; a missing gate can no longer start a search. Making evolve pop a card in `always_allow` would make it stricter than every other privileged action, which is a permission-model decision rather than this PR's change.

### 2. Grant matching is by `resource`, so the resource now names the search

Read, not inferred:

- **`services/api/src/store.ts:5545-5552`** — `const matcherResource = permissionMatcherResource(action, resource)`, then `permissionGrants.find(grant => grant.action === action && (grant.resource === matcherResource || grant.resource === resource) && grant.state === "active" && grant.scope !== "once" && (global / project / conversation / session …))`. A standing grant is matched by **action + resource**, and non-`once` scopes are reusable.
- **`services/api/src/store.ts:5621-5629`** — deciding `allow_matching` creates a grant with `resource: permissionMatcherResource(request.action, request.resource)` and `scope: "session"`.
- **`packages/governance/src/permission-policy.ts:56-62`** — for `code` the matcher resource is the resource verbatim, so any suffix survives matching.
- **`services/api/src/store.ts:5471-5485`** — `authorizeByJiuwenSwarm` does look a record up by `toolCallId`, but only to avoid double-booking the decision row; it is not the grant lookup.

So the old `evolve-search:<sessionId>` really did let one "allow matching" click cover every later search in the session. Fixed at **`services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts:64-76`**: the key is now `evolve-search:<sessionId>:<fresh id>`, one per attempt — the card approves the search the user was shown and nothing after it, and even a retried call asks again. Wording follows the implementation in **`packages/evolve/src/index.ts:361`** ("That card approves one search: a later search in the same conversation raises its own card") and in the card label **`apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:449`** / **`:3422`** ("this evolution search only" / "仅限本次演进搜索").

### Revert proof (fix reverted on the same tree, then restored)

```
$ git checkout 85a78ad8 -- services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts
not ok 1 - a turn with no approval path refuses the search instead of allowing it
not ok 2 - each search attempt gets its own grant key, even for a repeated call
not ok 3 - a grant from one search does not authorize the next search in the same session
not ok 4 - the gate asks with the call's identity and the search it is paying for
# tests 4
# pass 0
# fail 4
$ git checkout 54889783 -- services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts   # restored
```

The red commit `85a78ad8` carries the same four tests, failing on the unfixed gate. Test 3 drives the real `SessionStore`: it decides `allow_matching` on the first search's resource, shows the same search is then allowed, and asserts the next search is still pending (a card).

### Ran on this tip

- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts` → **4/4 pass**
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/evolution/*.test.ts` → **165/165 pass**
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → **exit 0** (this is the check that enforces the required field)
- `cd packages/evolve && node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` → **10/10 pass**; `tsc -p packages/evolve` → **exit 0**
- `cd apps/web && tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → **1183/1183 pass**; `tsc -p apps/web` → **exit 0**

**Not run:** L2/L3, Docker and binary layers, and the full `pnpm check`.

CI: pushing a new tip re-triggers the pull-request gates for it; the previous tip's green run does not carry over to `54889783`.

## Low finding follow-up (sciencediscovery-bot review 5706765348, inline 4419359334)

`PermissionDecisionActions` no longer offers **Allow same type** for an `evolve-search:` request. Each evolution search asks with a fresh single-use key (`evolve-search:<session>:<uuid>`), and a `code` grant is matched on the whole resource, so a same-type grant could never authorize a later search: the button promised a decision the backend drops, and it printed the attempt id in the help text and left a dead grant in `PermissionGrantManager`. That card now offers **Allow once** or **Deny**; ordinary `code` requests keep the button.

`RunTimeline` shows the localized scope (`permissions.evolveResource`) in its details **Resource** row instead of the raw per-attempt resource, matching the collapsed card that already hid it.

# 学科知识引擎：摄取/生长/消解/消费全链 + 会话绑库与反幻觉运行时

> 与 GitCode MR [!125](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/125) 内容一致（对应 GitCode issue #86）。

把「学科知识」做成 SD 的一等资产：文献与结构化源摄取为带锚点溯源的知识图谱，图谱可离线生长、实体消解、社区聚类；对话内绑定知识库（kb scope）后，图谱成为受约束的知识来源，输出必须引用锚点，与证据账本 / 新颖性检查 / 引用核验构成多层反幻觉链路。

**283 文件，+50.8k，4 个按路径分组的 commit**（KE 核心 / agent 运行时 / Web / 技能与测试）。

---

## 新增功能

### 1. 知识引擎核心（`packages/knowledge-engine` + `services/api/src/knowledge-engine`）

- **存储域**：SQLite（知识库/文档/锚点/实体/边/社区/合并/作业/引用/公式），带迁移机制；算法核与存储分离，可独立评测
- **摄取**：LaTeX-first arXiv 通路（tar.gz 解包 + `\input` 递归内联）、JATS XML、视觉增强 PDF 解析；溯源门抽取——每个抽取结论挂文档锚点
- **生长**：离线 grow job，MMR + anchor-aware 多样本选择、收敛信号、结构化反思 directive 反哺下一轮
- **实体消解**：在线门 + 离线 job、物理合并与回滚（`ke_entity_merges`）、louvain 社区、根实体、社区报告
- **消费面**：`kb_search` / `kb_expand` / `doc_grep` 工具、entity_unified_search、三级文档阅读器（全文/结构/锚点）、引用 API（意图徽章 supporting / contrasting / mentioning + Similar / References / Cited-By）
- **REST**：`/api/ke/*` 全套 + 前端知识引擎页（cytoscape 图谱画布、生长控制面板、阅读器、引用面板）

### 2. 会话绑库（kb scope）

- session 设置新增 `kbScopeKbIds` / `kbScopeWebSearch` 运行时覆盖项；composer 底部选择器一键绑定/解绑，写路径为 fresh-GET 读改写，避免并发选择器互相回滚
- resident-summary 上下文贡献者持续注入**在库**图谱摘要（成熟度分级）；范围外知识库对工具面与摘要均不可见（防泄漏包装）
- 系统 prompt m8.3.1：上下文时钟、kb-scope 自管理指引、反编造纪律句——均在既有 5000 字符保护段预算内

### 3. 反幻觉与研究运行时

- 三级注入：证据账本（`evidence_ledger`）、新颖性检查（`novelty_check`）、引用核验（`verify_citation`）；KE 工具输出逐字文本打 nonce 不可信围栏
- finish-gate 收尾审计：技能声明 `metadata.pre-finish-audit` 即在收尾前注入审计 directive，有界续跑（≤2 次）
- 研究世界模型 `research_state`：目标钉住 / 计划生命周期 / 未决问题 / 已排除路径防复活 / 已试去重，JSON 文件锁崩溃可恢复
- 审批门计划生命周期（`packages/plan-mode`）：`propose_plan` / `revise_plan` 工具、约束级审批、版本绑定决策、决策日志；与上游 `update_plan` 快照机制共存（`AgentRunBindings` 同时携带 `planRepository` 与 `planStore`）
- stall-guard：模型调用无进展按空闲窗踢出重试（≤3 次），外层空闲看门狗兜底
- 记忆图谱镜像 `observeSessionPlan`；MCP 配置文件内容签名失效（保留上游按服务器签名比较，叠加文件级变更检测）

### 4. 技能包与评测

- 15 个方法论技能：knowledge-engine-explore/grow、evidence-notes、hypothesis-tournament、tree-search、robin-chain、virtual-lab、idea-debate、systematic-review、precise-qa、long-form-writing/audit、progressive-report、report-writer、table-analysis（多数声明 pre-finish-audit）
- 评测套件 `scripts/ke-*-eval.mjs`：growth delta-recall、discoverer 诚信维度、pairwise、citation（ALCE 三指标）、resolution、bench 539 题；`skill-test-runner` + ER 数据集构建器
- KE 旅程 E2E 9 条 + kb-scope / finish-gate 旅程，ke-stub 离线可跑

## 验证

Linux（Ubuntu WSL2），分支 `pr/knowledge-engine`（基于 upstream/main 最新 `ef65b6f`，4 个按路径分组的 commit）。

- 29 个 workspace 项目全量构建通过（含 web vite build）；`architecture:check` 通过（293 文件）
- 触及包测试全绿：workspace 119/119、context 50/50、tools 61/61、runtime-core 36/36、memory 35/35、schema 12/12、plan 5/5、plan-mode 2/2
- **services/api 全量套件 1020 tests / 1019 pass / 0 fail**（`node --test dist/*.test.js dist/**/*.test.js`，123s 干净退出）
- 与纯 upstream/main 对照树同环境跑 server.test.js 验证无回归：upstream 86/86，本分支 86/86；期间修复了三处合并引入的问题（MCP transport 双重 close、内置技能清单落位、保护段预算超限），并把 KE sqlite 连接补上服务器关闭回收（否则每个 boot 泄漏 db+wal+shm 句柄并在进程退出时挂起 drain）
- 双计划系统共存验证：propose_plan 审批门与 update_plan 快照在同 run 注册、互不干扰（context-assembly 集成测试覆盖）

ScienceDiscovery's issue, review and CI queues need explicit handoffs: the next actor, the missing evidence and the condition that permits progress. This proposal adds an operator-invoked development-loop skill and guide, linked from CONTRIBUTING.

## What changes

- Three queues: issue implementation, PR review, and CI/acceptance.
- Seven decision points: requirement claim, design/dependencies, implementation, source review, CI repair, real acceptance and release sign-off.
- Role-separated contributor/reviewer/maintainer TODOs, verified versus suggested ownership, release impact and recheck triggers.
- Exact-head review history, current readiness refreshes, pagination/error coverage and duplicate-request prevention.
- ScienceDiscovery's PR L1/L2, merge-group L3, daily L4 and release L5 stay distinct. Fix commits first reuse the automatic synchronize run; pending runs do not invite duplicate reruns.

Related: release tracker #249 and source-review skill proposal #231. This complements source review and does not adopt an unmerged proposal as trusted policy. Magpie is credited for unified agent/model routing and instruction-library inspiration; this is not represented as an imported upstream PR-loop skill.

Documentation and agent instructions only. No scheduler, workflow, paid research, credentials or repository settings are installed or changed. pr:372.body:
Session-enabled connectors stayed listed, and the agent received none of their tools, when the MCP server was switched off or could not connect. The catalog already recorded that state. The connector list ignored it.

## Disabled servers stay out of the picker and the agent

A server that is turned off, or that never entered the resolved server table, is reported as `disabled` once a catalog has been applied. `GET /api/connectors` omits those connectors, so the composer, settings, the project form, and the specialist form no longer offer them. Tool injection is unchanged: a disabled source has no available tools, so the agent is not given `mcp__<source>__*` tools even when the session still names the connector. The MCP server settings page still shows the disabled server and its switch, so it can be turned back on. Turning it back on returns the connectors to the picker with the previous selection.

## Connection failures stay visible

An enabled server that fails to connect or to list its tools stays in the connector list. Each of its connectors carries `connectionError`: the server's error text and the time the catalog was checked. The picker shows that text under the connector. The composer control shows a failure count when a selected connector failed. A partial tool mismatch (`degraded`) and a catalog that was never refreshed are left as they were: they are not hidden, and they are not labeled as connection failures.

A direct edit of `extensions_config.json` appears after the next catalog refresh (process start, `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload`, or saving a custom server). That is the same moment the agent sees the change.

## Compatibility

When an applied catalog does not contain a server, source status is `disabled` rather than `unavailable`. The governance broker rejects a call in that case with `MCP server is disabled or not configured: <id>`. Connectors of a disabled server are absent from `GET /api/connectors`.

Related to #325.

## Validation

Recorded on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`.

- Typecheck for the web, api, mcp, data-source, schema, and artifact-manager packages, plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: passed.
- Package tests: web 890/890, data-source 51/51, mcp-sources 28/28, schema 12/12, mcp 1/1, artifact-manager 2/2.
- `services/api`: 1128 passed, 3 failed. The failures are PDF extraction tests and exit with `spawn … ENOENT` because `services/paper/.venv` is not present in this checkout. They do not call the connector list.
- `pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm architecture:check`, and `pnpm ci:selftest` (55/55) passed. The E2E meta check reported 0 errors.

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. Those layers provision JiuwenSwarm outside the repository tree, which this environment does not allow. This pull request is a draft until those layers have results.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the connector journey on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`. Local stack, native executor, runner and API on ports 4480 and 4481.

`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts`: 3 passed, 0 failed. Two custom MCP servers are used, one healthy and one that exits during the handshake. Both appear, and only the failing one shows its error. Turning the healthy server off removes its connector from the picker and from the next run's tool list; the settings row and switch remain. Turning it on brings the connector back, still selected.

`journey-plugin-composition`: the connector-panel step passed. A later step expects `todo_create`, which the native executor does not provide. That failure is outside this change.

The mocked `pnpm ci:e2e` layer was not run.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: connectors whose MCP server is off disappear from the picker and are not offered to the agent. A connector whose enabled server fails to connect stays listed and shows the connection error.

Compatibility and migration: callers that treated "missing from an applied catalog" as `unavailable`, or that expected those connectors to remain in `GET /api/connectors`, need to handle `disabled` and the shorter list. No configuration change is required.

pr:390.body:
This PR exports the existing main-agent/independent-worker Issue-to-PR workflow as opt-in contributor tooling. Scheduling decisions stay with the main agent rather than a script-driven queue controller. It does not modify ScienceDiscovery's research agent runtime, CI policy, repository settings or the operator's running pipeline.

## Scope

- Add `.agents/skills/repo-issue-pipeline` with the coordination policy, worker contract and operational guidance: claim before admission, reproduce before implementation, full accepted-scope delivery, original-thread resume, change-driven discussion/CI/conflict maintenance, independent main-agent review and explicit human/authority boundaries.
- Export a portable one-turn Codex SDK transport with an optional executable override instead of a machine-specific CLI path. Requests explicitly acknowledge full host access; per-session locks prevent concurrent hosts, saved threads resume in their original worktree, and private session/events/final/failure records survive handoff. An incomplete or failed stream cannot be reported as successful.
- Add 16 hermetic tagged tests to the existing `scripts/*.test.mjs` discovery path, without introducing a second CI definition or requiring model tokens.

pr:441.body:
Researchers can now inspect and retrieve structured scientific data from five built-in database connectors, then download selected files through governed artifact jobs. GEO uses actual provider file listings and bounded sample metadata queries; AlphaFold DB adds retrieval of existing predictions and confidence files. The change also strengthens ChEMBL measurement filtering, ClinVar submission preservation and experimental PDB provenance.

Refs #420. **Partial fix; keep #420 open.** This is a draft because broad verification is not green and provider failure-path coverage remains incomplete.

## Scope

- GEO: discover real matrix/SOFT/supplementary files, validate download selection, preserve study/sample/platform metadata, paginate sample annotations and avoid bulk-query timeouts. Correct accession request parameters and GEO directory buckets.
- ChEMBL: validate measurement constraints and preserve units, relations, target/molecule/assay identifiers and assay confidence. Advance pagination over scanned provider rows even when local confidence filtering returns an empty page.
- ClinVar: retrieve versioned VCV/RCV records and preserve individual SCV assertions and conflicting classifications, without inventing a consensus. Reject oversized XML explicitly.
- RCSB PDB: preserve experimental-method/revision evidence and include it with structure download candidates.
- AlphaFold DB: add existing-prediction lookup by UniProt accession and governed model/confidence downloads, with explicit predicted status and model version. This does not run prediction software.
- Reuse the existing Inspector for built-in sources, using the same broker/audit path; preserve AlphaFold selections across store reloads, refresh changed connector caches, register evidence graph tools and document all five sources in English and Chinese.

## Reproduction and acceptance evidence

Baseline: `0d31e155a206c23f6d6a0c9632e44f516b326bbe` (GitHub history). Product-validation candidate: `42a96f3f2613d34487ecc6041c61b5854b692d4c`. PR head: `bcd56b74bd9b79564e392da33e4977d94dd65034`. pr:470.body:
Pull requests from `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]` stay mergeable when `license/cla` has appeared and is not `success`. If that check never appears, the merge gate does not fail because of it. For every other author, including other bots, an appeared non-success check fails the gate. `license/cla` is not added to the ruleset required checks: a required check that never runs would block pull requests the CLA app did not mark.

## CLA policy
The merge gate calls `claGate` after the existing job aggregation. The workflow only fetches commit statuses and the pull request author.

The newest status whose context is exactly `license/cla` on the head SHA wins (GitHub lists statuses newest first). An absent context passes. `success` passes. `pending`, `failure`, `error`, and any other non-success state fail, unless the pull request author has `type` `Bot` and login exactly `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. The comparison is case-sensitive and includes the `[bot]` suffix. The author is the pull request `user`, not `github.actor`. Another bot such as `dependabot[bot]`, a `User` with that login, a human, and an unknown author are not exempt.

A failed status read fails closed for every author, including `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. It is not treated as an absent check. On `merge_group`, if the pull request number or author cannot be resolved, there is no exemption: an absent context or `success` still passes, and a present non-success status fails.

On `merge_group`, the pull request number is parsed from the single `gh-readonly-queue` head ref and that pull request's user is loaded. Statuses are read on the queue head SHA, not the original pull request head. `push`, `workflow_dispatch`, and `schedule` are not subject to this check.

The merge-gate job requests `contents: read`, `statuses: read`, and `pull-requests: read`. The workflow permission stays `contents: read`. No status or pull-request write scope is added. The same rule is stated in `.ci/README.md`. The `Require CLA policy` step has no `if:` and sets `CI_CLA_RESULT` to `${{ steps.cla.outputs.result }}`. An empty result fails closed.

## Current head
`4bf3ff891beb4ff0c8e9bf2776dc5882e28a551f` is a merge of `3bde9d39e9c9d7cfe3204650d6bfab2a930fe928` and `origin/main` `f4ceca57b74b7f5a10b4f8f77313513a09886c02`. The merge tree matches a clean merge. No conflict was resolved by hand. `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`, `.ci/cla-gate.test.mjs`, and the CLA steps in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` are unchanged from `3bde9d39`. The CLA paragraph in `.ci/README.md` is unchanged; other README edits came in from `main`.

GitHub Actions run [40210190231](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40210190231) completed with conclusion `success` on this head:
- UT: planned 4853, executed 4853, passed 4853, failed 0, skipped 0.
- ST: planned 24, executed 24, passed 24, failed 0, skipped 0.
- Mocked E2E, four shards combined: planned 118, executed 118, passed 118.
- Coverage and merge-gate succeeded. L3, L4/L5, Docker, and the binary release were skipped by policy.
- `Require CLA policy` ran. This pull request's own `license/cla` status was `success`, so the bot exemption was not the path that made the gate pass.

## Validation
Focused checks on `3bde9d39e9c9d7cfe3204650d6bfab2a930fe928`, before the merge:
- `node --test .ci/cla-gate.test.mjs`: 24 passed, 0 failed. After the TAP summary the process aborted with status 134. That abort is a host behavior and not a failed assertion.
- Static collection of `.ci/cla-gate.test.mjs` reported no dynamic registration.

Earlier local layers were run on `92b80223847f35c5630029394304fc2b15f4f38d`, before the exemption was narrowed. They are not the result for the current head.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: planned 4453, executed 4453, passed 4452, failed 1, skipped 0. The failure was `services/runner/src/egress-gateway.test.ts` (the scratch directory was already 86 bytes). That case passed when rerun with a shorter temporary directory.

The GitHub run above is the result for `4bf3ff89`. The earlier local UT failure in `packages/executor/src/remote-compute-prune.test.ts` did not fail this run.

## E2E user journeys

The earlier local mocked run on `92b80223847f35c5630029394304fc2b15f4f38d` failed one pre-existing layout assertion: the empty-state connect control measured 601.23px against an expectation narrower than 580px. Counts for that older run: planned 100, executed 100, passed 99, failed 1, skipped 0.

pr:544.body:
A terminal user can start an evolve search or an Idea Tree research and then only see an id. Progress and stop live on the Web cards. `evolve` and `idea` call the HTTP routes those cards already use, and they read the bearer token from the same data directory as `run`.

Fixes #50

## Commands

```text
ScienceDiscovery evolve list [--session <id>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve get <run-id> [--candidate <hash>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve watch <run-id> [--after <sequence>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve stop <run-id>

ScienceDiscovery idea list --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea get <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea watch <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea pause|continue|stop <research-id> --session <id>
```

`evolve stop` posts `POST /api/evolve/runs/<id>/stop`, the dashboard Stop route. `idea stop` posts `operation: "end"`, the card's End research route. Pause and continue are only on Idea Tree, because an evolve search has no pause. `evolve list` stays global; `--session` only forwards the route's existing `sessionId` filter. There is no `run --wait`. A long run is followed with `watch`.

Output matches `run`: readable text on a terminal, and one JSON object per line when stdout is a pipe, so `jq` works. `watch` adds `reconnect` lines and a final `result` line. A failure is an `error` line.

`watch` replays, then follows live, and returns when the engine stops running. A dropped connection reconnects for about three minutes. Evolve continues after the last printed event sequence, so an event is not repeated. An Idea Tree frame is a full snapshot with no sequence, so a reconnect shows the current state and skips a frame already shown. `--after <sequence>` continues an evolve watch in a new process.

Ctrl-C stops watching and exits 130. It does not stop the engine. `stop` does that. This is different from `run`, where Ctrl-C cancels the turn `run` started.

Exit status follows `run` (0 completed, 1 failed, 130 cancelled):

| Exit status | evolve | idea |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `succeeded` | `completed` |
| 130 | `stopped` | `ended` or `paused` |
| 1 | `failed` or `budget_exhausted` | `interrupted` |

A paused Idea Tree research exits 130 whether a person paused it or the token budget paused it. The engine records both as `paused`. `watch` also exits 1 when the run is missing, the token is refused, or the stream cannot be recovered.

## Validation

On `dada3d08c9ac343492e26e87cf95141eac92b28e` (parent `9c33627b5ffc3c3ef397c114e267de6e6cc6dd10`, clean worktree):

- `node --import tsx --test services/launcher/src/engine-commands.test.ts` — 26 pass, 0 fail
- `cd services/launcher && pnpm typecheck` — no errors
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` — exit 0
- `cd services/launcher && pnpm test` — 188 pass, 0 fail (includes the CLI journey below)
- `node test/api/engine-cli-journey.mjs` — `outcome` PASS, repeated 5 times on this commit
- L1: architecture boundaries OK; CI test catalog OK; `docs:check` 0 issues; e2e metadata 0 errors (11 pre-existing legacy warnings)

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. The single-file binary smoke was not run; `run --help` is unchanged.

## E2E user journeys

PASS on `dada3d08c9ac343492e26e87cf95141eac92b28e`. Surface: CLI against the API process. Not a browser journey.

Command: `node test/api/engine-cli-journey.mjs`

The built CLI reads the token from the data directory. The journey uses a local fake model server and the evolve sidecar venv.

| Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recorded evolve search: list, get, candidate source, watch, `--after`, stop, missing id | Piped output is JSON. Watch of a finished success exits 0. Resume does not replay earlier events. Stop of an already finished success stays `succeeded`. A missing id exits 1. | PASS. Watch printed 6 events and exited 0. `--after 4` printed 2 events. |
| Live evolve watch, dropped connection, then CLI stop | Event sequences stay contiguous with no repeat. Stop uses the dashboard route. The run becomes `stopped` and watch exits 130. | PASS |
| Idea Tree watch, then pause | Watch follows the running research and exits 130 once it is paused. | PASS |
| Continue that research, then stop | Stop sends the card's end operation. The research ends. | PASS |
| A second research runs to completion | Watch exits 0. | PASS |

The live evolve step mounts the real evolve route handlers and orchestrator inside the API process. The public HTTP API has no route that creates a search, and API startup marks an unfinished search failed, so that step is not a separately started product process. Its sidecar is a stub. The same SSE routes forwarded through the default JiuwenSwarm adapter were not run. The CLI calls the same paths the Web cards call.

## Release

Release category: release:feature

User impact: from a terminal, evolve searches and Idea Tree researches can be listed, inspected, watched, and stopped. Idea Tree research can also be paused and continued. The commands, options, and exit statuses are in `help` and in the English and Chinese CLI reference.

pr:648.body:
Fixes #647

Owner: Dev1
Written-by: Dev-1
Branch: `dev1/fix/647-web-test-module-resolution`

## Problem

A clean tree cannot run the web test suite. Every workspace package publishes its runtime entry from `dist/` (`packages/*/package.json` → `"default": "./dist/*.js"`) and no `dist/` is committed, so a package-level run that does not build first resolves those imports to files that do not exist:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx
# tests 448
# pass 385
# fail 63
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/operational-logging/dist/diagnostics.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/ErrorDiagnosticActions.tsx
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../@sciencediscovery/schema/dist/index.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/Markdown.tsx
```

The repo's own `pnpm test` hides this because it runs `pnpm build` first; the per-package script (`tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`) does not. The 63 victims are not defects — they fail at import time, before any assertion runs.

The failure is not specific to `operational-logging`: `schema`, `skill`, `plugin-sdk` and their transitive workspace dependencies fail the same way.

## Commits (red first)

1. `test(web): prove the suite dies when the workspace packages are unbuilt` — one test asserting that every `@sciencediscovery/*` entry the web app imports resolves to a file that exists. Red on the unbuilt tree:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts
not ok 1 - every workspace package the web app imports resolves from its built entry
  error: '@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/manifest resolves to
   .../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/dist/manifest.js,
   which does not exist; the workspace packages need building first'
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

Full suite on the same tree: **449 tests / 385 pass / 64 fail** (63 pre-existing + this one).

2. `fix(web): build the workspace packages the test suite imports` — `apps/web`'s `test` script now runs `scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs .` before `tsx --test`. The script walks `apps/web`'s workspace dependencies transitively and builds only the packages whose `dist/` is missing, using the repo's `typescript` and each package's own `tsconfig.json` — exactly what `pnpm build` would produce. It is a no-op once they are built, so the CI path that already ran `pnpm build` pays one directory listing and nothing else.

No test file is modified, and production resolution is untouched: the runtime entry stays `dist/`, which `node dist/server.js` and vite both need.

3. `test(scripts): pin the ensure-workspace-dist skip and build order` — the builder had no test of its own behaviour. Two cases run against a throwaway workspace (a copy of the script, fixture packages, and a stand-in `tsc` that records where it was pointed and writes the `dist/` the compiler would emit, so no TypeScript build is paid for):

- a package without `dist/` is built, a package that already has `dist/` is not rebuilt (its `dist/` is left untouched), and a second run of the script is silent;
- a package is built only after everything it depends on (`leaf` → `middle` → `top`, plus an unrelated sibling, built in that order).

Both cases are green as written. Their red side is a mutation, checked locally on the working tree and not committed: dropping the `dist/` skip fails the first case (`a second run must not rebuild a built package`), and moving `ordered.push(dep)` before the dependency visit fails the second.

## Verification

Red (clean tree, before the fix) → green:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # no dist/
# tests 449   # pass 385   # fail 64
$ node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web
built workspace packages without dist: @sciencediscovery/operational-logging,
@sciencediscovery/external-urls, @sciencediscovery/schema, @sciencediscovery/cas, …
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # deps built
# tests 1131   # pass 1131   # fail 0
```

The suite grows from 449 to 1131 because the files that could not load now run. Typechecks: `apps/web` `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0; repo `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` → 0. A second run of the builder prints nothing (idempotent).

## Labels and timing

`agent-ready` could not be applied to the issue by the team (the token gets 403 on label writes) and the owner's 60-minute deadline takes precedence over the usual 24-hour wait, so this is pushed ahead of the label being restored.

## Ran

- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts` → 0/1 before the fix, 1/1 after
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → 385/449 before, **1131/1131 after**
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (repo root) → 0
- `node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web` twice → 17 packages the first time, silent the second
- `node --test scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.test.mjs` → 2/2, and the same two cases fail under the two mutations above
- `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` → 70/71: the one failure is `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`, which shells out to `uv` and dies on the read-only `~/.cache/uv` on this host, unrelated to this change
- `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check` → `CI test catalog OK: 7 cases, 24 tags, 4 layers`

## Not run

- The shared tagged plan end to end (`node test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list`): on this tree it stops during collection with `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: apps/web/tests/markdown-math.test.ts:16`, a file this branch does not touch and which fails the same way alone at the base commit. The new file was collected on its own instead (`node-collect.mjs` → 2 cases, `category:ut`).
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` verbatim: on this host pnpm's dependency-status check aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` / `EROFS` on the pnpm store (outside the workspace, read-only), so the script's two commands were run directly, in order.

Release: fix

pr:678.body:
Fixes #673

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts` capped an extracted page with a bare `text.slice(0, MAX_DOCUMENT_CHARS)` (4096 UTF-16 units), so a character that straddles the cut left a lone high surrogate at the end of the body handed to the model.

Reproduction (`main` before the fix, logic copied verbatim):

```
$ node -e 'const MAX=4096; const text="x".repeat(MAX-1)+"😀"; console.log(JSON.stringify(text.slice(0,MAX).slice(-2)))'
"\ud83d"
```

Red commit `c6765ab2d6fea7fb2f9ba7e6bfb4cd8eb5b6d6b0` on this branch, before the fix:

```
not ok 13 - document truncation never ends in half a surrogate pair
  ---
  failureType: 'testCodeFailure'
  error: 'Expected values to be strictly equal: ... actual ends in \ud83d'
```

## What changed

- `document()` in `fetch.ts` now drops a dangling high surrogate after the cut, so the result ends on a code point, never exceeds the 4096-unit budget, and creates no new lone surrogate. The same rule the artifact preview uses.
- New test `document truncation never ends in half a surrogate pair` covers both `renderTavilyExtract` and `renderExaContents` with an emoji straddling the boundary, plus a lone-surrogate check on the rendered document.
- Nothing else changes: same cap, same `# title\n\n` prefix, same vendor normalizers.

## Verified locally

Red commit `c6765ab2d6fea7fb2f9ba7e6bfb4cd8eb5b6d6b0` (test only, on top of `7057aaf6`):

```
# tests 16

```

Green commit `5ad9b21b6aeb5d7f30556de8ddafc07d1246d85e` (branch rebased onto `7057aaf6`):

ok 71 - document truncation never ends in half a surrogate pair
exit=0

exit=0
