Default deployment routing, shared proxy resource creation/editing/deletion, and provider/MCP proxy selection are reviewed together. Credential-bearing URLs are encrypted when the operator submits them and stay encrypted in `proxy_server_secrets` and in the configuration draft bridge. Saving neither probes a proxy nor grants destination, private-network or execution permission. Failed connection validation precedes mutation.

The authenticated settings read is a separate path. `GET /api/proxy/settings` (`getProxySettings` / `proxyServerSettingsView`) decrypts a `custom_url` entry into `url` so the operator can see and edit that proxy in the settings panel. That projection is already on `main`; this pull request does not add it. Configuration cards and discovery stay on metadata only (`id`, `name`, `kind`, `hasUrl`) and do not decrypt a URL. The browser journey asserts the settings response on purpose: `created.url` equals the URL that was just saved.

## Overlap with #285

#285 (`fix(network): unify proxy configuration and protect local transport`) is still open. It also edits `services/api/src/store.ts` and is the change that unifies how a saved route is resolved for outbound transport (`packages/network`, `packages/model/src/client.ts`, and the Runner clients), including local-transport bypass.

This pull request owns the stored choice: `proxyPolicy` on the deployment default, providers, models, MCP servers, and web/sandbox settings, written by the configuration adapters and validated against the registered proxy list. It does not add a second runtime resolver.

Intended order: land this pull request first. #285 then rebases and reads these stored `proxyPolicy` values through its resolver. If #285 merges first, this branch rebases onto it and keeps that resolver instead of teaching each adapter to interpret the policy itself.

This PR is narrowed to the current release requirement: propose, manually confirm, and save the deployment-wide **local MemoryGraph participation switch** from a conversation.

## Scope

- Add only `memory.enable` with `enabled: boolean`, using the existing v3 confirmation card.
- Require the saved backend to be `local`. A non-local backend is rejected; backend changes invalidate an older confirmation.
- Save the participation flag and its receipt in the existing shared transaction. Refusal, Stop, failed receipt writes, and repeated confirmations preserve the existing safeguards.
- Apply the gate to subsequent memory operations. In-flight work may finish, stored graph data remains, and a bound original configuration wait may continue.
- Explain that saving does not install, start, restart, or verify the MemoryGraph service. The deployment may require the operator to start the service and restart the API.
- Keep English and Chinese labels specific to the local workbench graph rather than the global Reviewer switch.

The previous Neo4j backend, connection, password, destination-consent, exact-password normalization, and formal API changes have been removed from this PR. Existing main behavior in the formal MemoryGraph settings API, Neo4j implementation, and proxy settings API remains unchanged. This PR does not claim to harden those existing paths.

The diff is now **17 files, 378 additions and 17 deletions**, down from 35 files, 1,925 additions and 69 deletions. The branch still contains **one commit**.

## Candidate and validation

- Published head: `8cd4786b29b2f8324dcf67e8425e0bd80a272626`.
- Parent: `578a9505e24bffefe2a0e3ec61d25a356f791669`.

- Full build and typecheck: passed.

Command: `node --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=4 services/api/src/configuration/*.test.ts apps/web/tests/ConfigurationRequestCard.test.tsx apps/web/tests/ConfigurationRequestApi.test.ts`, with proxy environment variables unset for owned loopback fixtures.

Consolidates the existing MCP settings work into one module: metadata, call timeout, enable/disable, removal of saved HTTP/SSE header groups and STDIO environment overrides, custom-server deletion, and replacement of existing credential header values. Connection-cache and credential-redirect fixes remain included.

## Scope of this revision

- Supersedes #764, #765, #766, #767, #768, #769, #771 and #772. One squashed commit with parent `578a9505e24bffefe2a0e3ec61d25a356f791669`.
- Neo4j is deferred for this release. Removed `memory.credential`, its adapter, schema/registry/discovery/UI entries, Memory-only journeys, and changes to the pre-existing Memory settings API. The existing main-branch Memory behavior is unchanged; its legacy password writer still trims surrounding whitespace.
- Preserved the shared exact encrypted-draft mechanism because MCP credential-header replacement requires it. Destination consent, target binding, manual confirmation, finite fields, CAS, durable external receipts and resolve-only recovery remain.
- Added regressions that the deferred capability is neither advertised nor accepted, and that the existing Memory writer retains its old normalization. The production HTTP registry still requires all seven MCP capabilities.
- This diff is 64 files, +2966/-72.

Saving does not probe a server, start a process or grant execution permission. Existing connections can keep old settings until normal reconnection. New MCP URLs, server creation, OAuth and arbitrary header/environment editing are outside this PR. MCP HTTP/SSE requests reject all redirects, including same-origin redirects; use the final server URL.

## Validation

Published head: `5d981b8e67186cc044d75b2ce2d4afad2bc9d2b6`. Validated local commit: `b1928a8673c20fd7d026081aa147b545fce137d4`; source tree: `266628f6862e81d398ebf0c75328d152b2136614`. The published tree is verified identical after fetching it back.

- Web configuration card/client tests: **58 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Legacy Memory normalization regression: **1 passed, 0 failed**.
- Local L1: **4 planned, 4 executed, 4 passed**.
- Local full UT: **incomplete**, blocked during Node collection; no full-UT pass claimed.
- Local ST: **51 planned, 43 executed, 36 passed, 7 failed, 8 unexecuted**. Unmodified main `578a9505` reproduced the same seven failed identities (five sandbox process-adapter cases, Evolve distribution/runtime, and Swarm SDK contract); both local runs were incomplete because a worker terminated. This does not establish a full ST pass.
- Local mocked browser E2E: **blocked** by missing pinned Chromium. The run was stopped after confirming browser launch failures. No browser assertion or screenshot is credited.

Host HTTP/HTTPS/ALL/NO proxy variables were unset for isolated test processes. No assertion was relaxed and no sandbox or browser substitute was used. The [CI run for this exact published head](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42606079680) is pending. The previous head’s successful CI does not validate this tree.

## E2E user journeys

**8 isolated public-API journeys, 32/32 steps passed** on the actual compiled API from the validated source tree:

- All seven `test/api/configuration-mcp-*.mjs` journeys: metadata, timeout, availability, header removal, environment removal, header credential replacement and deletion.
- `test/api/mcp-credential-redirect-boundary.mjs`.

Each used its documented `E2E_*_ISOLATED=1` flag, owned loopback fixtures and synthetic credentials. They verify persisted outcomes and the credential/redirect boundary. Browser options were not enabled. These are separate API journeys, not a combined browser or real-vendor/model journey. Windows/WSL and real-service/model authentication remain unverified.

## Compatibility and migration

The encrypted custom-MCP store retains the legacy plain-map shape while its operation journal is empty. The first journaled settings edit can write encrypted v2; the first deletion writes v3, and the store stays v3 afterward. Older binaries cannot read either envelope. Settings and receipts remain one atomic encrypted write. There is no automatic downgrade: restore the pre-upgrade file, or start with an empty store and re-add servers. The English/Chinese MCP setup and protocol docs describe recovery; regressions cover the legacy shape, the permanent v3 boundary, full-journal rejection and unreadable-row recovery.

There is deliberately no migration-specific warning or recovery UI. Version detection happens in the encrypted custom-MCP store; a load error propagates during API startup. There is no migration/recovery UI screenshot to attach.

## UI evidence

Fresh bilingual captures are being prepared against the actual combination of this published backend and the shared Desktop UI from #1017. No new combined-browser pass or screenshot is claimed here yet; the API-only journeys above do not substitute for those captures. Existing Web UI functionality is retained.

## Review and release

Earlier catalogue, MCP Chinese-label, journal-capacity and unreadable-row findings remain fixed and covered. The Neo4j-only label and public-API compatibility changes no longer form part of this PR.

The [maintainer discussion](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/773#issuecomment-6730247941) records acceptance of the consolidated module, documented downgrade boundary and known browser/real-service gap. It is not an approval vote. **Real zh-CN/en before-and-after screenshots of MCP credential replacement and a destructive flow, plus two reviewer approvals, remain outstanding.** `needs-human` and `UI` are retained. No merge, approval bypass or protection change is requested.

`web_fetch`/`web_search` handed search-result titles and snippets to the model with named HTML references still encoded. Only `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot` and `nbsp` decoded, so a page title like `Café — a review` reached the prompt and the report verbatim, and the sources a science search cites most often (encyclopedias, European sites) are exactly the entity-heavy ones. This decodes every named reference a browser resolves, in the same single pass as before.

## What changed

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts`: the five-name map is replaced by the full WHATWG named character reference set — 2125 semicolon-terminated names — expanded into a `Map` once at module load. `nbsp` keeps its existing ordinary-space mapping; numeric references, the single-pass rule (`&lt;` → `<`) and unknown names (`&bogus;` stays literal) are unchanged. The decoding loop is the same one-scan replace it was; only the data changed shape and moved out of this module.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html-entities.ts` (new): the table itself — a `name;code point;…` constant, 246 folded lines — under a 37-line header that states the source (WHATWG named character references via CPython's `html.entities.html5`, 2231 keys of which the 2125 semicolon forms are what this pattern accepts), the retrieval date, the exact `python3` snippet that regenerates the body, and the licence position: the standard's table reproduced as factual data — names and code points any HTML parser needs — not copied from another project's source. `html.ts` keeps the decoder and goes from 79 lines to 90 (+11); 368 is only the shape this branch's previous commit had with the table inline, and this commit moves it out. The data is 246 of the new file's 284 lines.
- `tsconfig.base.json`: one line, `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`. The import in `html.ts` keeps a `.ts` extension so `node --experimental-strip-types` — the command the issue reproduces with — resolves the sibling source instead of failing with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; that option is what lets tsc accept the specifier and still emit `./html-entities.js` (verified: the built `dist/web/native/html.js` line is `import { NAMED_ENTITIES_PACKED } from "./html-entities.js";`). It belongs in the base config rather than the package one: the root tests config used by `pnpm typecheck` extends only `tsconfig.base.json`, and with the option in `packages/data-source/tsconfig.json` alone that check fails with `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts(73,39): error TS5097: An import path can only end with a '.ts' extension when 'allowImportingTsExtensions' is enabled.` From the base config both the package build and that check pass. It changes nothing else in the tree — the only `test/` file that `tsc` type-checks imports `.js` paths; the Playwright specs under `test/` are not in any tsconfig.
- `html-entities.ts` is force-added: `.gitignore`'s `data-*/` rule also matches the `packages/data-source/` directory (`git check-ignore -v` reports `.gitignore:91`). I left that rule alone to keep this PR single-purpose; say the word if you would rather have it anchored as `/data-*/` and I will open a separate issue.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts`: cases for the names in the issue (`eacute`, `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `apos`, `diams`, `rsquo`, `ldquo`/`rdquo`, Latin-1, symbols), case sensitivity, an unknown name, the single-pass rule after the table widened, and a guard that the exported table still has exactly 2125 entries plus one two-scalar value (`NotEqualTilde`), so a dropped or mis-chunked line cannot pass as a smaller table. The test file is unchanged by the move.

Size, whole PR: 4 files, 344 insertions, 8 deletions (`html-entities.ts` +284, `html.test.ts` +41/−1, `html.ts` +18/−7, `tsconfig.base.json` +1).

## Red first

Decoder tests. Command:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/web/native/html.test.ts
```

Before the fix:

```
# Subtest: decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
not ok 3 - decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
  expected: "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
  actual: 'café — 5–10 … O'Brien'
# Subtest: decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
not ok 4 - decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
  expected: 'Ää'
  actual: 'Ää'
# pass 5
# fail 2
```

Table guard. The guard lands in its own commit before the export exists, so it is red on the change that adds only the test:

```
# pass 0
# fail 1
SyntaxError: The requested module './html.js' does not provide an export named 'NAMED_ENTITIES'
```

and it fails the way it is meant to when one entry is dropped from the packed constant (mutation check, one `AElig;c6;` field removed, then restored):

```
not ok 8 - keeps every entry of the generated WHATWG table
  expected: 2125
  actual: 2124
# pass 7
# fail 1
```

Green after the implementation, same command as the decoder run: `# pass 8`, `# fail 0`. The package suite goes from 74 to 75 tests with the guard: `# tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0`.

## The issue's reproduction

Command from #777:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

On this tip:

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

The middle line is the single-pass guarantee: the decoded ampersand does not start a second scan.

## Gates

On this tip, in `packages/data-source` unless noted:

```
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json                                        # exit 0 (build)
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit                               # exit 0
$ node --experimental-strip-types -e 'import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(...)'
  café — 5–10 … O'Brien                                          # exit 0
$ npm test                                                        # # tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0
$ cd ../.. && node scripts/check-architecture.mjs                 # 333 source files, boundaries OK
$ cd ../.. && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json        # exit 0
$ cd ../.. && pnpm --recursive typecheck                          # 34 packages Done, exit 0
```

`pnpm architecture:check` is **98 passed / 1 failed** on this host: `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs` shells out to `.ci/run-research-python.sh race`, which needs a writable uv Python install and network (`Read-only file system` at `~/.local/share/uv/python`); it does not touch `packages/data-source`. `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` itself is green, as shown above.

## Not run

- Repo-level UT/ST/E2E, CodeCheck (GitCode) and the Docker/binary layers: CI. This PR changes one package's text extractor and its test, plus one compiler option; the package tests, both tsc configurations, the architecture check and the recursive typecheck were run locally.

pr:821.body:
Fixes #812

Draft. Evolve can score a search from an NPU shell execution, and a scorecard can limit which fields a candidate is allowed to change.

## Summary
- An NPU search submits a signed `POST /shell-executions` to the Runner and waits. Success is `completed` with `device` equal to `npu`. A queued, running, failed, or non-NPU result has no numeric score, and it is not stored as 0. The local sandbox is not used as a fallback.
- The scorecard names `direction.editable`. A candidate that is not that JSON object, or that changes any other field, is refused before it is scored. A search with no direction is unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] `services/evolve/tests/test_npu_direction.py`: 4 passed. Covers a fixed-field rejection, refusal without a direction or a runner, a non-NPU result, and one signed submit that waits from running to an NPU score.
- [ ] A real Runner with an Ascend device.

pr:826.body:
Related to #812

Partial. Keep #812 open.

A directed search can now run on the conversation's selected runner. A JSON the search had already measured was still spending a round, and a reply that was not a JSON object was spending one too. The NPU path handed the search library one task, which that library refuses to start on. A search that does not name editable fields stays the existing free program search.

## Directed edits

The chat agent starts the run and does not pick later steps. PUCT chooses which measured node to expand. The model then proposes one JSON object. Only the fields the user ticked may change. A proposal that matches an edit already measured, a reply that is not a JSON object, and an edit that leaves the declared fields are not sent to the runner. The model is asked again, inside the same slot, up to three extra times. If it is still not a runnable edit, that reply is rejected before the runner and has no score.

There is no task-specific update rule. The model sees the measured values and their scores and proposes the next JSON itself.

## NPU scoring

Each candidate is one fresh shell execution on the conversation's selected runner, in a sandbox with no network. The fixed program computes the score. The candidate is JSON bound as input, not the program that runs. Success is a completed execution whose result says the device is `npu` and includes a number. A job that is still queued or running is waited on and does not take another slot. A failure, a cancellation, or a missing result has no score and is not stored as 0.

The search library requires at least four tasks and a hold-out fraction strictly between 0 and 1. An NPU search supplies four task ids and holds one out. The domain caches the measurement, so those ids do not each use the card.

## Field table

The run shows the ticked fields. Each candidate row shows which field changed, the old value, the new value, and the score.

## Review follow-up

- Each submitted execution retains the runner that accepted it. Polling and cancellation no longer depend on the current runner order or NPU-card selection. A disconnected accepting runner produces an error rather than redirecting the execution. Execution IDs are isolated by run, cannot be resubmitted, and retain their route after an uncertain submit response.
- The field list now distinguishes loading and source-read failures, with localized retry in English and Chinese. Changing the run or source clears stale rows and ignores late responses.
- A repeated-edit prompt shows at most eight recent edits, with each preview capped at 200 characters. The full measured-edit set still prevents duplicate execution.
- `-inf` is an internal ranking sentinel, not a wire score. `events.seeded` and `events.expanded` normalize non-finite scores through `finite()` to JSON `null`. `encode_ndjson(..., allow_nan=False)` rejects a missed non-finite value before it can emit invalid JSON. A regression test covers both null conversion and fail-closed encoding.

## Validation

The checks in this section were recorded on the earlier head `eff542cc`. See the workbench follow-up for validation of the new head.

- Directed/NPU Python tests: 22 passed.
- Runner proxy, preflight, proposal and orchestrator tests: 79 passed, including 9 runner-proxy tests.
- FieldDirection React tests: 6 passed, covering both locales, failed load followed by retry, source/run replacement and stale responses.
- `pnpm typecheck`: passed. Local L1: 4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed.
- [Earlier-head CI](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42500907449) passed: L1, UT, ST, all five mocked L2 E2E shards, Coverage and merge-gate. Real L3/L4/L5 E2E were skipped; these results do not replace the required real-browser captures.
- [Previous head `7b6dcbf7` CI](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42497149247) passed: UT 6949/6949, ST 51/51, mocked E2E 136/136, and merge-gate.
- Full local layers cannot be claimed green on this cloud host. Its sandbox cannot create the required NETLINK_ROUTE socket, and inherited proxy settings also affected local tests. On the previous tree the full Evolve suite had 390 passes and the same 21 failures reproduced on unmodified main; the original ST failure set also matched main. The new focused checks above passed without weakening those assertions.

## E2E user journeys and captures

**Required visual evidence remains BLOCKED.** The requested before/after captures in `zh-CN` and `en` are not attached yet: the pinned Chromium download on this host returns an unavailable or invalid archive, so no browser or viewport verification is claimed for this update. The outstanding captures are the declared-field header, changed-value rows with a missing score, a long field table, and a free-program run with no editable fields.

The React tests establish state/retry behavior, not rendered layout. The passing prior mocked E2E suite does not replace these specific captures.

Earlier local NPU evidence recorded for this PR, not rerun for this follow-up: one selected card completed 10 requested rounds and stored 10 new measurements. Seven repeated proposals were re-asked within the same round without being sent to the card. That run did not exercise a non-JSON reply; the branch is covered by unit tests. The field table was not clicked through in that earlier run.

## Release

Release category: release:feature

User impact: a search can score candidates on the conversation's selected NPU runner, and can limit edits to named JSON fields. A reply that is not a runnable edit is asked again inside the same round.

Compatibility and migration: none for a search that does not ask for a runner or a field list. That path stays the existing program search.

## Workbench UI screenshots

The composer shows how many fields may change after the user confirms the scope. The scope card shows the task, the initial values, and the fields the user can select. It also offers a task-based draft, JSON upload, and row controls for adding, editing, or removing fields.

![Confirmed edit scope in the composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0761c1e5-df60-4c12-a247-952cb16561f9)

![Edit scope card with one editable field](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7bf2dca1-ee66-4b8e-9851-36d346de55bf)

### New desktop workbench UI (served in the browser)

These screenshots show the new desktop workbench served in the browser with `SCIENCE_AGENT_WEB_DIR=apps/desktop/dist`. The first shows the optional **Set edit scope** action beside the existing composer. The second shows the JSON draft and field selection card, using the task already entered in the composer.

![New desktop workbench composer with Set edit scope](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01930862-60be-43f4-b3a2-1c8ea6bbed0b)

![New desktop workbench edit scope card with a generated JSON draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dca69a40-5f72-4277-aed6-da7623f6d50d)

## Workbench follow-up

The existing Evolve setup still selects the algorithm and places the command in the conversation composer. The composer remains the only place to enter the task. **Set edit scope** is optional. It uses the composer text to generate a starting JSON draft or accepts a user-provided file. The user can edit, add, remove, and select fields before confirming. Confirming the scope saves it on the draft. Sending the task remains a separate action. The API binds the confirmed baseline and editable fields before creating the search.

The same workflow is available in the desktop workbench when it is served in a browser. Set `SCIENCE_AGENT_WEB_DIR=apps/desktop/dist` and restart the API to serve it at the root path.

### Follow-up validation

- WSL workspace build and both renderer type checks passed.
- 24 API proposal tests and 21 Python direction tests passed.
- The draft endpoint was exercised with a local model fixture. It returned a task-specific draft without starting Evolve.
- Chromium verified both workbenches. The original Web workbench was checked at desktop and narrow widths for draft generation, JSON upload, row edits, and scope confirmation. The browser-hosted desktop workbench was checked for the original composer flow, the disabled draft action before typing, draft generation from the composer text, and scope confirmation without sending the task.
- A full real Evolve search was not run. Full local UT, ST, and mocked E2E results are incomplete after a WSL interruption. The PR author requested that GitHub CI run the full checks on this revision.

### CI follow-up after rebasing

Rebased onto main at `9feafa27`. The platform conflict was limited to imports. The rebased code keeps main's stop-run and active-run guard and still passes the user-confirmed proposal to the orchestrator.

The WSL workspace build, both renderer type checks, all 35 focused API tests, and all 21 Python direction tests passed on `4e48ca3`. Full checks for the rebased head are tracked in [GitHub Actions run 42572726350](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42572726350).

## Summary

Part of #835.

This is the first KE core slice proposed in #835. It introduces only the pure text, extraction, and entity-resolution domain of the Knowledge Engine; it does not register API routes, agent tools, UI, background jobs, or runtime settings.

### Included

- Text parsing and retrieval primitives, including JATS, LaTeX, document levels, trigram/search, and citation helpers.
- LLM extraction schemas/prompts and the provenance gate requiring document anchors for extracted knowledge.
- Entity normalization, matching, merge policy, offline resolution, and sample evaluation data.
- Independent-review hardening for single-line display math, relevance-ordered FTS over-fetch, repeated citation anchors on one line, JATS formula alternatives, optional LaTeX macro defaults, and token-safe entity endpoint matching.
- Additional bot-review hardening: bounded worker-based regex execution, Unicode entity screening, LaTeX preamble removal, multiword/CJK entity and novelty matching, and grouped JATS citation IDs.
- CodeCheck cleanup for loop style and redundant non-null assertions, without changing test expectations.
- Follow-up review hardening: grep input is capped before worker cloning, worker startup and regex execution have separate deadlines, and large-corpus hits survive with honest scan truncation. The provenance fallback now requires ordered token evidence (including single-character entity tokens), rejecting word-permuted or semantically inverted quotes.
- Package-local unit tests and the package/lockfile wiring needed to build `@sciencediscovery/knowledge-engine`.

### Explicitly excluded

- Graph, growth, and evaluation orchestration modules.
- SQLite/API services, connectors, PDF workers, agent integration, and Web UI.
- `pairs.realworld.json` and other large/local fixtures.
- qa/, .tmp/, credentials, and local development artifacts.

The package index exports only modules present in this stage. Four graph-dependent resolution tests from the full reference implementation remain for the graph stage; no production module was stubbed to hide that dependency.

pr:853.body:
The nightly research and BioMnibench runs need a consistent model configuration and more resilient handling of transient model failures. This change uses the `nightly-research` environment, preserves requested DeepSeek reasoning settings through session configuration, and retries interrupted model turns only before answer text or tool calls are emitted.

## Nightly model configuration

- Configure real-model generators and the BioMnibench judge for DeepSeek thinking enabled at low effort by default; environment variables can override the API variant and thinking settings.
- Preserve explicitly requested DeepSeek thinking effort in model and session settings; default to high when no effort is supplied.
- Read the configured API variant consistently in all six real-model journeys and validate Biomni's persisted thinking snapshot against the controls supported by that variant.

## Reliability

- Recover transient mutation errors within a shared deadline.
- Retry interrupted reasoning-only model streams within the shared request retry budget, buffering reasoning so discarded attempts are not sent to callers.
- Improve network permission tool guidance and cover the model, gateway, evolution and BioMnibench changes with focused tests.

## Validation

- Current head: `fa34928`.
- `pnpm --filter "@sciencediscovery/schema..." build` passed.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/model test` passed (7 test files).
- `pnpm typecheck` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Real-model E2E, including the previously reported L3-files journey and binary release x86_64 workflow, has not been rerun on this head; the previous run was not green and remains unresolved pending fresh CI evidence.

## E2E user journeys

The prior run's basic real-model journey did not settle the L3-files file-editing run within its 120-second wait. This PR does not claim that failure is resolved; a successful rerun is still required.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: explicitly configured DeepSeek thinking effort is retained, and some transient model stream failures can be retried before an answer or tool call is emitted.

Compatibility and migration: no migration required; nightly real-model jobs use `nightly-research`, which must contain their required model and data credentials.

pr:857.body:
Fixes #816

#816 describes a chat that kills the API process on Windows. Two things have to be true for that: the state write must fail on a transient sharing violation, **and** the failure must escape somewhere nobody observes. Both had to be fixed; only one of them still needs this PR.

## The half `main` already has

`b24dc2f8` — *fix(api): retry an atomic replace Windows refuses while it is watched* — added `services/api/src/atomic-file.ts`. Its `replaceFile` retries a rename that raises `EACCES`, `EBUSY` or `EPERM` ten times with 1, 2, 4, … 512 ms backoff, and lets every other code through as itself so a full disk is not retried for a second. `SessionStore` and the evolution store already write through it, so "an antivirus scanner held the freshly written file" no longer fails a save.

That is why the platform facade this branch used to carry (`services/api/src/platform/os/replace.ts` and its call sites) is **not** in this diff: `main` landed the same fix while the branch was open, and keeping both would either duplicate the retry or replace `main`'s call site with an equivalent one. The retry half is withdrawn here rather than re-litigated.

## The half this PR still has to carry

`scheduleSessionRuns` starts its writing loop with `void`; on the current `main` (line 3720) it still ends with:

```ts
  })();
}
```

Nothing observes that promise. The `finally` blocks inside the loop throw in two reachable ways — the terminal `updateSessionRunStatus` write when `session-runs/<id>.json` cannot be replaced, and the follow-up `listSessionRuns` — and a throw there becomes an unhandled rejection in the API process while a chat run is live. That is the process death in #816.

This PR contains that boundary:

```ts
  })().catch((reason: unknown) => {
    runLog.error("run_scheduler_failed", {
      errorMessage: reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : String(reason),
      sessionId,
    });
  });
```

The run keeps the last status it managed to persist, and `recoverSessionRuns` marks it `interrupted` at the next start, so containment loses no state — whereas swallowing the failure silently would. No retry logic is added, removed or changed by this PR.

## Evidence

Red first, on this tree with the `.catch` removed (`git checkout main -- services/api/src/runs/index.ts`, then the new case alone):

```
$ node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "contained where the scheduler starts it" services/api/src/runs/index.test.ts
not ok 1 - a failed state write is contained where the scheduler starts it instead of killing the API
  ---
  duration_ms: 131.545727
  failureType: 'unhandledRejection'
  error: 'EPERM: operation not permitted, rename'
  code: 'EPERM'
  stack: |-
    SessionStore.<anonymous> (.../services/api/src/runs/index.test.ts:423:25)
    Object.apply (node:internal/test_runner/mock/mock:765:20)
    publishRunEvent (.../services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3107:26)
    <anonymous> (.../services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3601:25)
    async <anonymous> (.../services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3607:9)
  ...
# tests 1 / # pass 0 / # fail 1
[exit 1]
```

The failure is the shape the issue reports — an unhandled rejection carrying the rename error — not an assertion about a type. With the `.catch` restored the same case passes and the file is 24/24.

## Why the containment also has to back off

Containing the escape is not sufficient on its own, because of which write usually throws. The first `await` in the loop is the `queued`→`running` transition (`updateSessionRunStatusIfCurrent`); when that fails, the run is still `queued` on disk, so the `finally`'s reschedule re-enters the scheduler immediately and hits the same write again — no delay, no attempt counter. Measured on this tree with that one write mocked to raise `EPERM`: **5,508 `listSessionRuns` calls in one second** (~2,750 transition attempts), the process never idle. After this change the same measurement is **4 calls in one second**: the reschedule waits `500 ms × 2^(n-1)` (capped at 30 s) and stops after 5 consecutive escapes, logging `run_scheduler_stopped` and leaving the run `queued` for the next scheduler start or an API restart — the state it would have kept if the process had died, without the death.

## The same escape, observed without this diff

`main`'s gap is not only theoretical. `#908`'s UT run — Actions run [42585890178](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42585890178), head `cefe1ebd`, base `main` `9feafa27` — failed a test whose name has nothing to do with run state, because the API's background writer escaped into the process:

```
Error: Run not found
    at SessionStore.appendRunStreamEvent (services/api/src/store.ts:7010:21)
    at async SessionStore.appendSessionRunEvent (services/api/src/store.ts:6976:12)
    at async publishRunEvent (services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3107:14)
    at async <anonymous> (services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3678:11)
```

Source: that run's `ut-results` artifact (id `13660905872`), file `ut/tagged/group-514/worker-1-events.jsonl` — one record with `type: "test:fail"`, `message: "Run not found"`, `error.code: "ERR_TEST_FAILURE"`, and the `cause.stack` quoted above. The case that failed is `request errors after headers terminate the response without rejecting the HTTP listener`.

That PR's diff is `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts` plus a test, so it does not create this: the outermost frame in the stack is the run loop's `finally` awaiting `publishRunEvent` at `runs/index.ts:3678` on `main` — the same voided scheduler, rejecting because the run disappeared from the store ("Run not found"), not because a rename failed. That is a third rejection site inside the same `finally`, beyond the two the code comment above enumerates; the containment is at the scheduler boundary, so it covers whichever `await` inside the loop rejects, but the comment's list should not be read as exhaustive.

## Ran

- `node --import tsx --test src/runs/index.test.ts` (from `services/api`) → **25/25 pass**, including the new backoff case and the containment case.
- Red first for the containment (`.catch` removed): exit 1, `failureType: 'unhandledRejection'`, `error: 'EPERM: operation not permitted, rename'`, as quoted above.
- Red first for the backoff (the `escaped` flag and the delayed reschedule removed, everything else kept):
  `not ok 1 - a scheduler that escapes does not restart itself at full speed while the run stays queued` ·
  `error: 'the scheduler re-entered 978 times in 300 ms; it must back off instead of spinning'`.
- Direct measurement of the same path with `updateSessionRunStatusIfCurrent` mocked to throw: 5,508 `listSessionRuns` calls per second before, 4 after.
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → exit 0.

## Not run

- The `platform/os` and `store` replace tests: those files are no longer touched by this PR (the retry half is `main`'s).
- The full UT slice locally: this machine's pnpm store is read-only, so the slice's own install fails before it runs; the file above is the reading for the changed code, and CI runs the slice.

pr:861.body:
Fixes #858

The usage page header announced **every model ever recorded** while the token total beside it and the model list below it were narrowed by the selected dates. With `from=to=2026-08-04`, where all usage that day came from one model, the page read `30 tokens across 2 models` — a count that contradicts both the sentence's own token total and the single-row list underneath. Fixes #866

## What this fixes

`sanitizeUploadFilename()` in `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts` guarded an empty name, a NUL byte, absolute paths, drive letters and traversal, but not Windows reserved device names. On a Windows workspace `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`, `LPT1`–`LPT9`, `CONIN$` and `CONOUT$` resolve in every directory and with any extension, so `con.csv`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log` passed the guard and failed later inside the workspace write with a raw `EPERM`/`ENOENT` that the upload response reports as an unclassified error (`CON` targets the console device instead of failing).

The fix rejects them with the same `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` code and error shape the other guard branches use, names the offending file in the message, and strips trailing dots/spaces first because Windows ignores them (`nul.`, `CON .csv`). Legal stems that only begin with a reserved word (`conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `auxiliary.csv`) and two-digit ports (`com10.csv`) keep working — the same test asserts both directions.

The guard is platform-independent on purpose, so Linux and macOS reject these names too: portability — an upload must be writable on every supported host, and a file accepted on Linux but unusable on a Windows workspace would only fail later there.

## Red → green

The test was written first and fails on `main` `8708320f`:

```
not ok 2 - sanitizeUploadFilename rejects Windows reserved device names
  error: 'Missing expected exception: CON must be rejected as a Windows reserved device name'
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
# tests 16
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

After the fix: `node --import tsx --test src/workspace-upload.test.ts` → `# tests 16 / # pass 16 / # fail 0`.

Commits keep the pairing: `96b34e1d` test (red), `a2cebfbc` fix.

## Must-fix from review: the refused name now answers 400, not 500

`agent-ci-infra-bot` found the gap: `sanitizeUploadFilename` rejects the new names with `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH`, but the request handler decides 400-vs-500 **by message** (`isKnownClientInputError`, `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:20-32`), and the new message names none of the seven classified patterns. So the exact scenario this PR exists for — uploading `CON.csv` — answered `500 Internal server error` instead of naming the file.

Fixed on the same branch, tip `1a7b1b997bfe5e23af38d3abab59893a33e32ddd`, in two commits:

- `c0173957` (test, red first): a **route-level** test in `services/api/src/server.test.ts` (`WSP-004`) that uploads `CON.csv` through the real HTTP surface and asserts the status, the file name in the body, and that the workspace stayed empty. Before the fix: `500 !== 400`.
- `1a7b1b99` (fix): `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` joins the handler's existing stable-code branches (`services/api/src/http/index.ts`, one line beside `SKILL_LIBRARY_VALIDATION`), so the 400 follows the **code** rather than the prose a later wording edit could change. Every branch of the guard is tagged with that code, so this covers the whole family, not just the reserved-name message — no regex added, and no message reworded to please a pattern.

One consideration on where it went: the reviewer's finding points at the message classifier, and adding a ninth prose pattern there would have worked for this message only. The code branch is the smaller and more durable of the two, and it does not loosen any other 400/500 decision.

`services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` is unchanged and still 16/16 — the function-level contract this PR added is untouched; what changed is the status a client sees.

## Second finding from the same review: the stream syntax (same guard, not a new rule)

The device-name guard took its stem up to the first `.` and never looked at `:`, so `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA` were accepted while `nul.txt` was refused. Windows resolves both to the device in every directory, so that was the same reservation under another spelling:

```
"CON.csv"      -> rejected
"nul.txt"      -> rejected
"NUL. "        -> rejected
"nul:stream"   -> accepted before this commit
"con:$DATA"    -> accepted before this commit
"report:2024.csv" -> accepted before and after
```

Fixed as the **sixth branch of the same predicate**, not as a character rule: `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` now takes its stem before the colon as well as before the dot, and refuses only when that part names a device. A colon in front of an ordinary stem is a legal file name on Linux and macOS, so `report:2024.csv` and `data:2024.tsv` keep passing unchanged — refusing every `:` would have traded this bug for a portability one.

Red first, `services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` on `1a7b1b99`:

```

    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

    +   'accepted',
    +   'accepted'
    -   'rejected',
    -   'rejected'
      ]
```

The same test carries the over-rejection guard (`assert.equal(sanitizeUploadFilename("report:2024.csv"), "report:2024.csv")`), which was green before the fix and stays green after it. After: `# tests 18 / # pass 18 / # fail 0` across `workspace-upload.test.ts` and `error-classification.test.ts`.

Nothing outside `sanitizeUploadFilename` had to change for this — the handler branch from the first finding already answers 400 for the code — so this stays one pull request rather than becoming a second one against #866.

pr:870.body:
Fixes #862

## What this fixes

`SessionStore.writeArray()` published state through a `.state-<pid>-<uuid>.tmp` file and ran its cleanup in `finally` without a guard:

```ts
} finally {
  await rm(temporaryPath, { force: true });
}
```

When `rename` was refused (on Windows an antivirus scanner, search indexer or backup agent holds the freshly written file, so `MoveFileEx` returns `EPERM`) and the `rm` was refused for the same reason, the `finally` threw the bare cleanup `EPERM` and **replaced** the error that explains the loss. The caller then saw an unclassified `EPERM` on a `.tmp` path instead of the classified replace failure, so nothing could tell a locked file apart from a full disk.

The fix swallows the cleanup failure (`.catch(() => undefined)`); the replace error is the one that says what was lost.

## Red → green

| | |
|---|---|
| **Red** `88e6aa07` | `node --import tsx --test src/store-replace-cleanup.test.ts` → `2 tests / 1 pass / 1 fail`; failing assertion `the cleanup failure must not replace the replace error` (the surfaced error is the mocked `rm` EPERM, the `rename` EPERM is gone) |
| **Green** `0bae8739` | same command → `2 tests / 2 pass / 0 fail` |
| **Review round** `09b4ccb7` | adds the `attempts === 20` / `cause.code` assertions (inert before #857, live after) — same command → `2/2` |

The Security review's anti-forgery assertions are in `09b4ccb7`: when the surfaced error is a `FileReplaceError` (the classified shape #857 introduces on `main`), the test pins `attempts === 20` and `cause.code === "EPERM"`. On this base `writeArray` still calls plain `rename`, so that branch is inert here and becomes live the moment #857 lands — no follow-up tip is needed for it.

The two tests are split (per the Security review): **A** asserts the caller still sees the replace failure when both `rename` and the cleanup `rm` report `EPERM` (it accepts either the raw replace error before #857 or a `FileReplaceError` whose `cause` is it — the check reads `error.cause?.message` too); **B** asserts a failing replace still removes its temporary file, so no `.tmp` is left behind.

Both mocks use `syncBuiltinESMExports()` because `store.ts` imports `rename`/`rm` as named ESM bindings, and both only touch paths whose `basename` starts with `.state-` — the store's own temporary files — so no other write in the fixture is affected. The mock hands control back to the host after the test (`active` flag plus restore) so the next test is not affected by the still-bound ESM export.

1. `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → **0**
2. `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → **0**
3. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/store-replace-cleanup.test.ts` → **0** (`2/2`)
4. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/store.test.ts` → **0** (`121/121`, no regression in the existing store suite)

Compatibility and migration: none — the cleanup still runs and still removes the temporary file; only its own failure stops overriding the error that caused it.

pr:872.body:
Fixes #867

## What the user sees

A workspace file of `1_048_575` bytes (1 MiB − 1) prints **`1024.0 KiB`** in the file-provenance modal, and `1_073_741_823` bytes print **`1024.0 MiB`**. The unit was picked from the *unrounded* value (`1023.999… KiB`, so the loop stopped at KiB) while the printed value came from `toFixed`, which rounded up to `1024.0` — a number no KiB value can hold. The CSV artifact inspector had the same boundary and additionally never left MiB, so `1_073_741_823` bytes always read `1024.0 MiB` there.

The size is the only quantitative evidence in a provenance record, so a value labelled with the wrong unit is the record itself being wrong.

## Change

- New `apps/web/src/formatBytes.ts` with one ladder (`KiB → MiB → GiB → TiB`) shared by both call sites. The unit is chosen from the **same rounded value that is printed**, so a size never prints at or above its unit's own base.
- The decimal policy is not changed: `"adaptive"` keeps `>= 10 ? 1 : 2` decimals (`1.50 KiB`, `12.3 MiB`), and the CSV inspector keeps its fixed one decimal.
- `WorkspaceFileProvenanceModal.tsx` drops its local `formatBytes` and uses the shared ladder.
- `csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts`'s exported `formatBytes` keeps its name and signature but delegates to the ladder with one decimal, and gains `GiB`/`TiB`.
- Bytes stay bytes (`1023 B`), an exact MiB stays `1.00 MiB` / `1.0 MiB`.

Readings after the fix: provenance `1_048_575 → 1.00 MiB`, `1_073_741_823 → 1.00 GiB`; CSV `1_048_575 → 1.0 MiB`, `1_073_741_823 → 1.0 GiB`, `1_099_511_627_775 → 1.0 TiB`.

  error: '1024.0 KiB must not be printed: ...<dd>1024.0 KiB</dd>...'

The two passing tests are the "keeps the readings it already had" ones (`1023 B`, `1.00 MiB`, `1.50 KiB`, `5.50 MiB`, `1.5 KiB`, `5.5 MiB`), which pin the unchanged behaviour.

Fixes #871

## What this fixes

`queuedCancelToast()` (`apps/web/src/run-stream/model.ts:130`) returned four hardcoded English titles and two hardcoded details, and `App.tsx:3802` pushed them verbatim. With the UI in Simplified Chinese the Runs panel said `取消排队中的运行` but the answer was `Queued run cancelled`; the "already started" branch even pointed the user at an English `Stop` button. Fixes #879

## What the user sees

The desktop attachment tray prints a file of `1_048_575` bytes (1 MiB − 1) as **`1024KB`**, and `1_073_741_823` bytes (1 GiB − 1) as **`1024MB`**; the upload limit line prints the same boundary as **`1024 MiB`**. Fixes #877

## What this fixes

Four routes in the same family read one artifact id. `content` (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3353`) asks `store.getArtifactVersion()` first and answers 404; `provenance` and `diff` called `artifactVersionProvenance()` / `artifactVersionDiff()`, which throw a bare `new Error("Artifact version not found")` (`services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:169` and `:349`). The top-level mapper only turns `Project|Session|Proxy server|Provider|Model not found`, `Execution|Transfer|Timer|Subagent not found: …` and a few codes into 404, so both fell through to the 500 branch — and wrote an `unclassified_request_error` log for what is simply a stale version id.

Now both routes check the version before calling the helper, exactly like `content`, and answer `404 {"error":"Artifact version not found"}`.

The same defect exists one level up, on both versions *list* routes: `/api/projects/:p/artifacts/:a/versions` and its Session-scoped sibling pass the id straight to `store.listProjectArtifactVersions()`, which throws a bare `Error("Artifact not found")` — again a 500 plus an `unclassified_request_error`. Both now check the project/Session and the artifact first and answer `404` naming what is missing (`Project not found: …` / `Artifact not found`); the success path is untouched.

`diff` keeps its two comparison-base cases apart, per the issue's expected shape:

- `?against=<id>` given but not found → **404** (a requested resource is missing);
- `?against` absent and the previous version does not exist → **400** `A previous artifact version is unavailable for comparison` (the request asks for a diff this artifact cannot have yet, which is a client-side input problem, not a missing `to` version).

The helpers are unchanged, so their defensive throws still hold for any caller that skips the route.

Both screens now read one decision from a new `apps/web/src/tokenCountFormat.ts`
(`compactTokenParts`): the tier, the rounding and the `".0"` trimming live
there, and each surface only spells the unit it already printed — the usage
page `K`, the model badge `k`. Before this, the badge rounded to whole millions
from 10M (`10_500_000 → "11M"`) while the usage page kept the fraction
(`"10.5M"`) for the same count.

Tiers, now shared:

- 1M and up: one decimal, dropped when it is `".0"` (`1_000_000 → "1M"`,
  `10_500_000 → "10.5M"`, `12_345_678 → "12.3M"`).
- 10K–1M: whole thousands (`200_000 → "200K"` / `"200k"`).
- 1K–10K: one decimal (`6_600 → "6.6K"` / `"6.6k"`).
- Below 1K: the plain count.

```text

pr:886.body:
Fixes #883

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What changed

`_NODE_LIMIT` is a hard cap of 500 nodes, and the contract at `query.py:319` says only results **beyond** it carry `truncated: True`. The flag was computed *after* a Cypher `LIMIT` bound to exactly the cap, so the Python side could never observe a 501st row: a complete 500-row answer and a cut one were indistinguishable and both reported `truncated: true`. The panel then drew `N of 500+ (truncated) match(es) in view` — the `+` asserting a further match that does not exist — and a session graph of exactly 500 nodes was badged as partial.

`query.py` now has one helper, `_cap_page(rows)`, returning the kept page and `len(rows) > _NODE_LIMIT` as the flag. Two shapes use it:

- **Cypher-driven reads** — `query_match` (`:431`), `by_node_type` (`:465`), `by_edge_type` (`:518`), `get_subgraph` (`:272`) and `_serialize_subgraph` (`:1298`): the Cypher limit is bound to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`, the page is cut to `_NODE_LIMIT` and the extra row alone decides the flag. `query_match`/`by_node_type` count the **raw rows** before `_to_hit`, the variant the issue prefers: a row dropped because its label has no id field is not a truncation. In `get_subgraph` the node-id set used to filter edges and synthesize the folded scope→product surrogates is built from the kept page, so no rendered edge points at a node the caller did not receive.
- **Assembled reads** — `get_scope_expansion` (`:898`) and `get_group_expansion` (`:1024`): these build their node set from several queries (children + produces subtree + edge endpoints; group members + one surrogate edge each) and have **no Cypher `LIMIT`** to raise, so `cap + 1` does not apply to them. The cap is applied to the assembled page instead, and an edge whose endpoint fell outside the page is dropped rather than rendered against an absent node. `get_group_expansion` and `_serialize_subgraph` were not in the issue's list of five: they carry the identical predicate (`len(...) >= _NODE_LIMIT` over a set that had not been cut at all — flagging a page they never truncated), so they are fixed in the same slice rather than left as the same defect on two more surfaces.

`total` keeps its previous meaning (the number of rows the response carries), so no client contract changes; `services/api` and the web panel forward the flag verbatim and need no edit.

## Red first

Test commit `9ce6d309` (test only), base `89cd2d30`:

```
$ cd services/memory-graph && uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q
14 failed in 0.50s
```

Three distinct failure shapes prove the tests reach the real paths:

- `assert True is False` — a complete 500-row answer reported as truncated (the reported defect, once per capped reader);
- `assert 500 == (500 + 1)` — the reader bound `$limit` to the cap itself, so the flag cannot be decided at all;
- `assert 501 == 500` — the two assembled readers returned all 501 nodes: the page had not been cut even though it was flagged.

Green at `e1957043`: the same command gives `14 passed in 0.15s`.

## Validation

The branch is rebased onto the current main tip `89cd2d30` (it was first based on a mirror that still served `8708320f`); `services/memory-graph` has no upstream drift between the two, and every reading below was taken again at the rebased commits.

| memory-graph suite, same tree without the new file (baseline) | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `109 passed, 14 warnings, 78 errors` |
| error set | `diff` of the `ERROR tests/...` lines of the two runs | identical (78 lines) |

The 78 errors are the pre-existing `@needs_neo4j` suite on this host — every one fails in setup with `Failed: needs a live Neo4j`, and the set is node-for-node the same with and without this diff (`187` collected before, `201` after the 14 new cases).

The cases assert more than the flag: for each reader a 501-row result must return exactly 500 rows; the assembled readers must drop the spine edge that points into the cut row; `_serialize_subgraph` and the four Cypher readers must bind `$limit` to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`.

Not run: anything needing a live Neo4j (the Cypher and the rendered panel text itself), because there is no graph on this host and `ci.yml` has no memory-graph job — the issue notes this, so the local pytest output above is the acceptance evidence. The TypeScript gates (`pnpm --recursive typecheck`, `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`) are not run: the diff touches no TypeScript.

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…e1dee252`: 3 files, `+656/−19` (`query.py` `+93/−19`, `tests/test_node_limit.py` `+320`, `tests/test_node_limit_rule.py` `+243`). No existing assertion is relaxed.

## Review fix (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` on `e1957043`, review `5773456818`)

`yuanzhou75` found that the new test file stopped the whole `UT` layer before a single case ran: the tagged audit (`test/support/tagged/python/science_tags.py:103-108`) accepts only `pytest.mark.parametrize` arguments that pass `ast.literal_eval`, and `CAP` / `CAP + 1` are a `Name` and a `BinOp`. Because the audit runs in `pytest_collect_file`, collection aborted with `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: .../test_node_limit.py:107` and `merge-gate` never evaluated. Fixed at `04ce9c89`, in the shape the review asked for:

- **All seven** parameter tables (lines 105/123/155/181/227/266/290) are now `[(500, False), (501, True)]` with their existing ids, and each case opens with `assert query._NODE_LIMIT == 500  # the table above is literal on purpose`. `CAP` stays and is still used by the body assertions, including the one requiring `$limit == CAP + 1`.
- One more registration defect the audit then exposed: the module carried **no** `science_tags` module mark, so once the audit passed the catalog step raised `ValueError: Missing tag group: category` — the same `PYTHON_COLLECTION_FAILED` for the layer, one step later. 201 tests collected in 0.99s     # exit 0
```

That is the command `coordinator.mjs`'s `collect()` runs — same `-p science_tags`, `--strict-markers`, `--rootdir`, `--science-catalog`, plugin autoload off — over every source `pythonSources('memory-graph')` globs. The catalog it wrote has 201 entries, 14 of them from this file, tagged `category:ut, os:linux, arch:amd64, arch:arm64, tier:l2, status:reviewed, ...`. Before the change the same command died at `:107`; with only the tables fixed it died again at the missing `category`.

| gate | command | reading at `04ce9c89` |
