| tag audit | `science_tags.audit_source(tests/test_node_limit.py)` | exit 0 |
| tagged collection, whole project | `pytest -p science_tags --collect-only` over `services/memory-graph/tests/test_*.py` | `201 tests collected`, exit 0, 201 catalog entries |
| new cap cases | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed, 1 warning` |
| memory-graph suite | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ -q` | `129 passed, 16 warnings, 78 errors` |

The one warning the module adds is `PytestUnknownMarkWarning: Unknown pytest.mark.science_tags`, which every sibling module in this suite emits when pytest runs without the tagged plugin (`tests/test_logging_config.py` on its own gives `1 passed, 1 warning`); the plugin registers the marker and the collection above passes `--strict-markers`. The 78 errors are the unchanged `@needs_neo4j` setup failures.

No other file changed; the five commits stay separate: `9ce6d309` red test, `e1957043` fix, `04ce9c89` this registration fix, `86bbd1a5` the rule cases below, `e1dee252` the rule fix.

### Second review: one meaning for `truncated` (thread `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM6zusPi`)

The review found three counting conventions for one flag in the same PR. I took the first of its two options and made it the only one: **`truncated` means the backend returned more rows than `_NODE_LIMIT`, counted on the rows that were read and *before* a row is dropped for having no identity.**

Why this rule and not "count only renderable hits":

- **Only the returned-row count can be decided.** Each Cypher read binds `LIMIT` to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`, and that one extra row is the whole probe. Filtering first spends the probe on a row that cannot be rendered: 500 readable hits plus an unrenderable 501st would look *complete* although a renderable 502nd may exist, which is a completeness claim nothing checked. The returned-row count claims only what the extra row proves — the answer went past the cap.
- **It is the question the panel text asks.** `N of 500+ (truncated)` says the graph holds more matches than are shown. True when 501 rows came back even if one cannot be drawn; false when 501 came back and the response says "complete".
- **A short page stays complete.** 500 rows with one unrenderable row → 499 rendered, `truncated: false`: nothing was left unread, so there is nothing to disclose. Both directions are pinned below.

What changed:

- `get_subgraph` now caps the returned `(label, node)` rows and then runs `_node_identity`; `_serialize_subgraph` caps the returned rows and then runs `_to_hit`. Those are the two readers that capped the *filtered* list.
- `query_match`, `by_node_type`, `by_edge_type` already capped the returned rows; `query_match`'s comment argued the opposite and now states the rule, and the other two carry the same sentence.
- `get_scope_expansion` and `get_group_expansion` cap the assembled page, where every element already has an identity by construction, so "rows read" and "renderable rows" coincide there — no behaviour change, and the comment says so.
- `_cap_page`'s docstring states the rule once, and why the filter has to run after the cut. The review's nit (`nodes = list(hit_rows)` and a rebind on the next line) disappears with the restructure: `nodes` is built directly from the kept rows.

`tests/test_node_limit_rule.py` (new, 6 cases) pins the rule rather than the arithmetic: an unrenderable row as the 501st sets the flag on `query_match`, `by_edge_type`, `get_subgraph` and `_serialize_subgraph`, and a complete 500-row page that holds one unrenderable row stays complete on `query_match` and `get_subgraph`. Two of the six fail on `86bbd1a5` — `assert False is True` on the two readers that filtered first — and pass on `e1dee252`; the four that already held are there so a future reader cannot silently move one side into the other's shape again.

Deferred, deliberately not in this PR: `get_scope_expansion` / `get_group_expansion` still read every child/member and cut in Python, so the cap bounds the response and not the query work — same as before this PR, noted for follow-up.

Readings at `e1dee252`:

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rule cases | `pytest tests/test_node_limit_rule.py -q` | `6 passed` |
| cap cases | `pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed` |
| whole suite | `pytest tests/ -q` | `129 passed, 16 warnings, 78 errors` (the 78 unchanged) |
| tag audit, both files | `science_tags.audit_source(...)` | exit 0 each |
| tagged collection | `pytest -p science_tags --collect-only` over `services/memory-graph/tests/test_*.py` | `207 tests collected`, exit 0, 207 catalog entries |

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: a memory-graph search that matches exactly 500 nodes no longer says `500+ (truncated)` — it reports the count as complete — and a session graph of exactly 500 nodes is no longer badged as partial. A query that really has more than the cap still reports `truncated` and still returns 500 rows.
Compatibility and migration: none.

pr:890.body:
Fixes #887

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What changed

`POST /api/sessions/:id/files` resolved `body.path` through `resolveWorkspaceFile` — which only refuses absolute paths and escapes — and wrote the result straight to disk. On a Windows workspace that makes `CON` target the console device and `nul.txt` fail with a raw `EPERM` the handler never classifies, so the client saw `500 Internal server error`. The reserved-device-name guard existed only in the upload path.

Chosen fix: **direction 2** — the predicate became a workspace invariant instead of an upload-only check.

- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` — new exported `isWindowsReservedDeviceName(name)`, sitting directly beside `assertWorkspacePath`. It matches the stems Windows resolves in every directory (`con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com1`–`com9`, `lpt1`–`lpt9`, `conin$`, `conout$`), strips trailing dots/spaces first (`nul.`, `CON `), and treats everything before the first dot as the stem, because the extension is irrelevant to a device. It is exported through the package index (`export * from "./workspace.js"`).
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts` — the write route walks **every segment** of `relative(workspaceRoot, target)` (the helper is a segment rule, so `CON/notes.txt` is refused before `mkdir("…/CON")`) and answers **400 naming the offending segment**. The route keeps accepting nested relative paths; the upload path's "plain basename only" rule is still not imposed here.

Why not direction 1 (call `sanitizeUploadFilename` in the handler): on this base that function has **no** reserved-name branch — it only rejects empty/NUL/absolute/traversal names, which `resolveWorkspaceFile` already enforces — so calling it today would be a no-op for the reported defect. Adding the rule inside it here would duplicate `#868`'s open hunk in the same function (and that PR exists to fix exactly that statement). Putting the predicate beside `assertWorkspacePath` gives both write paths one home once they meet.

### Relation to `#868` (open)

`#868` carries the identical rule inline in `sanitizeUploadFilename`. This diff deliberately does **not** touch `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts`, so the two do not overlap: when `#868` lands, its guard should call `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` and drop the inline copy (one hunk), leaving main with a single implementation. Whichever merges second does that; if `#868` lands first I will rebase this branch and make that change here.

## Review fix — P2, a device name in a directory segment (review `5773758545`, reviewed at `93af68c8`)

The first version applied the predicate to `basename(target)`, i.e. only the last segment. The route accepts nested relative paths, so `body.path = "CON/notes.txt"` had basename `notes.txt` and passed the guard; the write then reached `mkdir(dirname(target), { recursive: true })`. On a Windows host `CreateDirectory("…/CON")` fails (Node surfaces `EPERM`/`ENOENT`), which is the same unclassified 500 this PR removes; on Linux it creates an unportable `CON/` directory. The helper was already documented as a segment rule, so the call site was the narrow part.

Fixed as asked: the route now splits `relative(workspaceRoot, target)` on the host separator and refuses the first reserved segment. That subsumes the old last-segment case, and the message names the segment the client must change (`"CON"` for `CON/notes.txt`, `"nul.dir"` for `nul.dir/x.csv`) instead of a basename it never sent.

The predicate's doc comment no longer claims to be called from every writer. It states the per-segment rule, names where it is applied today (this route), and says that the agent-side workspace tools, which write through `assertWorkspacePath`, are not wired to it yet.

`WSP-005` (`services/api/src/server.test.ts`) now covers, in addition to the top-level names (`CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, `CON .csv`, and the named-stream forms added below) and the look-alikes from the first version:

- `CON/notes.txt` → 400, the message names `CON`
- `nul.dir/x.csv` → 400, the message names `nul.dir` (stem before the first dot is `nul`, and Windows refuses the directory too)
- `notes/CON.txt` → 400 (control: clean directory, device-name file — refused before this change too)
- `conifer/notes.txt` → 201 (control: the walk must not start refusing legitimate nested paths)

## Review fix — F1, a device's named stream (`nul:stream`, `CON:$DATA`)

The predicate cut the stem at the first dot only, so Windows' named-stream spellings slipped through: `nul:stream` kept its colon, `/^(?:con|prn|aux|nul|com[1-9]|lpt[1-9]|conin\$|conout\$)$/i` never matched, `CON:$DATA` likewise, and the write route answered 201 and created a file a Windows host resolves to the device's stream rather than to a file. Windows takes everything before the colon as the device, so the stem is now cut at the first dot and then at the first colon:

- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` — `name.split(".")[0]?.split(":")[0]?.replace(/[. ]+$/, "")`. `con:$DATA` → `con`, `nul:stream` → `nul`, `NUL:stream` → `NUL`; `conin$`/`conout$` keep the `$` because no colon splits them; the trailing-dot/space strip still runs last, so `nul.` and `CON ` match exactly as before.
- The route needed no change: it already walks every segment through the predicate, so `{"path":"nul:stream"}` now answers 400 naming `nul:stream`.
- `#903` is re-scoped: F1 (named streams) is fixed here, so the follow-up keeps only D2, the POSIX segment split (`CON\notes.txt` when the host separator is `/`).

## Red first

Original case at base `89cd2d30` (test commit `1c3259df`, now the first half of `WSP-005`):

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
not ok 1 - WSP-005 a reserved device name in a session file write answers 400 and names the file
  error: CON must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

The two new directory cases are red at the previous tip `93af68c8` (`0a1ca4fc` is test only). The loop stops at the first failure, so each was run as the only new case:

```
$ node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
  error: CON/notes.txt must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
$ (same command, `nul.dir/x.csv` as the only new case)
  error: nul.dir/x.csv must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
```

`notes/CON.txt` and `conifer/notes.txt` are green at `93af68c8` by design: they are the controls, so they carry no red reading.

Named-stream case at `c4fb33d4` (test commit `ddd14462`):

```
$ cd packages/workspace && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern isWindowsReservedDeviceName src/workspace.test.ts
not ok 1 - isWindowsReservedDeviceName treats a named stream as its device
  error: nul:stream names a device stream
  false !== true
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1

$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
not ok 1 - WSP-005 a reserved device name in a session file write answers 400 and names the file
  error: nul:stream must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

The API route test reads `@sciencediscovery/workspace` from `dist`, so the package was rebuilt from `c4fb33d4` before this red run; an older local `dist` otherwise masks the defect.

## Review fix — F2/F3, the host separator and the superscript ports

- **F2** (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3815`): the segment walk split on `sep`, so on a POSIX host `CON\notes.txt` stayed one filename and passed (`relative(...)` → `"CON\\notes.txt"` in this shell, `segments ["CON\\notes.txt"]`, `reserved segment none`). The walk now splits on `/[\\/]+/`, which is what the predicate's "platform-independent" comment promises.
- **F3** (`packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts:464`): the class was ASCII-only, so `COM¹.txt` (`false` on the old tip) was accepted. It is now `com[1-9¹²³]|lpt[1-9¹²³]`, matching the copy in `#868`; `com⁴.csv`, `com⁰.csv` and `lpt¹⁰.log` stay ordinary names.

Red first — `fb2d5262` (tests only, source `fdb835fb`):

```
not ok 4 - isWindowsReservedDeviceName treats a named stream as its device
  error: |-
    COM¹.txt names a device

    false !== true
# tests 60
# pass 59
# fail 1

not ok 1 - WSP-005 a reserved device name in a session file write answers 400 and names the file
  error: |-
    COM¹.txt must be refused as a bad request

    201 !== 400
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

After (`484cab8f`, rebased onto `9feafa27`): `packages/workspace` `# tests 68 # pass 68 # fail 0`; WSP-005 `# tests 1 # pass 1 # fail 0`; the direct probe reports `reserved segment: CON` and `COM¹.txt: true`.

## Rebase — `9feafa273088` (2026-11-09)

The branch was cut at `89cd2d30`; main moved to `9feafa27` and the pull request showed `mergeable=false` / `dirty`. The same eight commits (four test, four fix, alternating — the red-first pairing is unchanged) were replayed onto `9feafa27`. Nothing was squashed or amended.

One conflict, on the `node:path` import line of `services/api/src/http/index.ts`: main added `join` (used eight times in the file), this branch needs `relative` and `sep` (one use each), and `basename` became unused once the last commit switched the split to `/[\\/]+/`. Resolution: `import { dirname, join, relative, resolve, sep } from "node:path";`. Both review fixes survive unchanged — `.split(/[\\/]+/)` in the write route and `com[1-9¹²³]|lpt[1-9¹²³]` in the predicate.

New tip `484cab8f8e5d26f7d1454380f9d7dcd2c9b34ea0`; the diffstat against the new base is identical to before the rebase (4 files, `+149/−6`). Re-read on the new tip: workspace unit `68/68/0`, WSP-005 `1/1/0`, `tsc` api/tests/workspace exit 0.

## Validation

The API tests load `@sciencediscovery/workspace` from its built `dist`, so the package is built first (CI does the same: the shared runner runs `pnpm build` before the heavy layers).

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| workspace build | `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/workspace/tsconfig.json` | exit 0 |
| typecheck (api) | `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| typecheck (workspace) | `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/workspace/tsconfig.json --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| tests typecheck | `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| predicate case | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern isWindowsReservedDeviceName src/workspace.test.ts` (`packages/workspace`) | `1/1` pass |
| route case | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts` (`services/api`) | `1/1` pass |
| workspace route group | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "WSP-00" src/server.test.ts` (`services/api`) | `3/3` pass |
| package UT | `npm test` (`packages/workspace`) | `101 tests / 101 pass / 0 fail` |
| api server suite | `node --import tsx --test src/server.test.ts` (`services/api`) | `109 tests / 108 pass / 1 fail`: `PDF upload extracts full text and tables into the session workspace` needs `reportlab` in `services/paper/.venv` (environment, not this diff) |
| api UT (full, earlier run at `c4fb33d4`) | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` | `1866 tests / 1860 pass / 6 fail`: 5 environment (`No module named uvicorn` in `services/evolve/.venv`; `No module named 'reportlab'` ×3; missing `@openai/codex-linux-x64`), 1 load flake in `evolution/orchestrator.test.ts` (`timed out waiting for the run to finish`) that passes on its own (`--test-name-pattern "settled"` → `3/3`). None touch this diff. |

Not run: a real Windows host — the guard is deliberately platform-independent, so the Linux route test exercises the same code path; there is no Windows-only branch in it.

`git diff --stat 9feafa27…HEAD`: 4 files, `+149/−6` (unchanged by the rebase) (`workspace.test.ts` `+29/−1`, `workspace.ts` `+31`, `http/index.ts` `+20/−5`, `server.test.ts` `+69`). No existing assertion is relaxed; the two edits to existing test lines are the look-alike loop gaining `conifer/notes.txt` and the top-level refusal loop gaining `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA`.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: writing a session file whose name or directory component is a Windows device (`CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, `CON .csv`, `CON/notes.txt`, `CON\notes.txt`, `nul.dir/x.csv`, `COM¹.txt`, and the named-stream forms `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA`) now answers 400 naming the offending segment, on every platform, instead of returning 201 and creating a file a Windows host cannot open (or a write that silently goes to the console or fails as a 500). Ordinary names such as `conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `com10.csv` and `conifer/notes.txt` are unaffected.
Compatibility and migration: none — only names Windows itself cannot create are refused.

pr:908.body:
Fixes #884

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What is wrong

`GET /api/sessions/:session/artifact-versions/:version/diff` answered **500 `Internal server error`** when either version of the pair is not textual, and logged a false `unclassified_request_error`. `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:357` threw a plain `Error("Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions")`, whose prose matches no client-input pattern in `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` and no not-found mapper in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, so the top-level catch classified a client-input problem as a server fault.

Measured at `7057aaf6` with two `application/zip` versions of one artifact in one session (red commit `0be111de` only):

```
GET /api/sessions/<id>/artifact-versions/<version>/diff
500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
```

The same request, with logging configured the way `startPlatform` does (not by `createApiServer` alone), wrote:

```
ERROR [api] event=unclassified_request_error errorMessage="Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions" method=GET path=/api/sessions/<id>/artifact-versions/<version>/diff status=500
```

## The fix — option 2 from the issue, in the helper

`artifactVersionDiff` now throws `new ApiStatusError(400, "Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions")`. The rejection is classified by **class** (the top-level catch answers `ApiStatusError.statusCode` before any prose matching), and it sits where the rule lives, so every caller of the helper answers the same 400 instead of only this route. No new message pattern was added to `isKnownClientInputError`.

The versions both exist; this is not a missing resource, which is why it is a 400 and not the 404 family `#881` adds.

### Why the route was not touched (overlap with #881)

`#881` (ours, open) rewrites the `diff` route block in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` for the missing-`to` / missing-`against` cases. Hoisting the media-type check into that same block would (a) collide textually with `#881`, and (b) put the from-version resolution in two places: the route would have to repeat what the helper already computes, and the next caller of the helper would get the 500 again. This fix touches only `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts`; the two behaviours are complementary (`#881` = missing version, this = both present but not comparable), so whichever lands second keeps both without a conflict.

### Import note

`services/api/src/runs/index.ts` already imports `artifacts/index.ts`, so importing `ApiStatusError` from `runs` inside `artifacts` would have closed a cycle between two large modules. The class therefore lives in `services/api/src/http/api-status-error.ts`, which imports nothing; `runs/index.ts` imports it and re-exports it (its public API is unchanged, so the existing import in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` still works), and `artifacts/index.ts` imports the leaf directly. No reverse edge was added and no cycle exists.

The leaf move keeps the identity check honest: `services/api/src/http/index.ts` still matches `error instanceof ApiStatusError` against the class the helper throws, which the new test proves by driving that exact path — a divergent class object would answer 500, not the 400 asserted there.

## Red → green

`services/api/src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` (test-only commit `0be111de`) seeds versions through `SessionStore.createArtifactVersion` and asks the real route, so no execution is driven: an `application/zip` pair, a pair that switches from `text/markdown` to `application/zip`, and a `text/markdown` control pair that must keep diffing.

Red at `7057aaf6`:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts
not ok 1 - a non-textual artifact pair answers a client error instead of 500
  error: |-
    binary pair must answer 400 with the reason, not 500
      body: { error: 'Internal server error' }
      status: 500
# tests 1 / # pass 0 / # fail 1
```

Green at `207243a7` (same command): `1 test / 1 pass / 0 fail`, exit 0. That run was still green by luck — see the review fix below.

The false log is gone in the same manual repro: `STATUS 400 {"error":"Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions"}`, `grep -c unclassified_request_error` → `0`, and the request is logged as `http_request_failed … statusCode=400`.

## Review fix — the fixture seeded after the server's `ready` chain

`sciencediscovery-bot`'s thread on `artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts:130` is right and this is a test-only correction: `createApiServer` returns before `ready` (which ends in `store.load()`) has run, and the fixture seeded after `server.listen`, so the test passed only when the seeds landed before that load. Two commits, no product code changed:

- `b3eb58b8` makes the ordering explicit: a request settles `ready` before the seeds. It is red, deterministically, on a machine that starts the server quickly:
  ```
  not ok 1 - a non-textual artifact pair answers a client error instead of 500
      binary pair must answer 400 with the reason, not 500
      +     error: 'Internal server error'
      +   status: 500
  ```
  (the 500 is the pre-fix behaviour: the route's `store` has already loaded a catalog without these versions, `getArtifactVersion` returns `undefined`, and `artifacts/index.ts` throws the plain `Error("Artifact version not found")`.)
- `76e911b5` removes the race instead of winning it: `startHttpFixture` is split into `createFixture` + `startHttpServer(context, fixture)`, the test writes every version first and starts the server afterwards, so `ready` loads a catalog that already contains them. No wait, retry or timeout is involved.

Green five consecutive runs of the same command, one process each:

```
[run 1] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 2] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 3] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 4] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 5] # pass 1 # fail 0
```

`tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` exit 0; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` exit 0. This review fix alone is `1 file, +14/−7` (`git diff --stat 207243a7..76e911b5`).

## Validation

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| new test, red | `node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` | `1/0/1`, exit 1 (at `7057aaf6` + test commit) |
| new test, green | same | `1 test / 1 pass / 0 fail`, exit 0 (at `207243a7`) |
| UT slice for the touched module | `node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts src/artifact-lifecycle.test.ts src/provenance.test.ts src/dashboard.test.ts` | `88 tests / 88 pass / 0 fail`, exit 0 (at `207243a7`) |
| typecheck (api) | `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` | exit 0, 0 errors |
| typecheck (tests project) | `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | exit 0, 0 errors |

Environment note, so the numbers are reproducible: this worktree's `node_modules` predates the current lockfile and the sandbox cannot write to the pnpm store, so `@types/ssh2` (declared by `packages/executor`) and the `packages/feedback-worker/node_modules` workspace link were missing before the first typecheck run. Without them the api typecheck reported 18 errors, all in `packages/executor/src/ssh-connection.ts` / `ssh-keys.ts` (missing `ssh2` declarations) and the tests typecheck 4 in `packages/feedback-worker` — none in the touched files. Installing the declared `@types/ssh2` into the local `node_modules` and adding that workspace link brings both to exit 0; no repository file was changed for it.

Not run: the full `services/api` UT suite (only the module slice above), the L2/ST/E2E layers, and a real server with a real artifact-producing execution — the route test seeds the catalog directly because the media-type rule is checked before any CAS read, which is exactly the point the issue makes.

`git diff --stat 7057aaf6…HEAD`: 4 files, `+247/−13` (`artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` +199, `http/api-status-error.ts` +34, `runs/index.ts` +6/−12, `artifacts/index.ts` +8/−1), 5 commits (`0be111de` test, `b6de0d8e` fix, `207243a7` the class move that removes the import cycle, `b3eb58b8` red and `76e911b5` green for the review fix above).

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: comparing two binary artifact versions (two `.zip` uploads, a text version against a later binary one) now answers `400 {"error":"Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions"}` instead of `500 Internal server error`, and the server no longer logs a false `unclassified_request_error` for a request the client can avoid. Textual pairs still diff as before.

Compatibility and migration: none — the 400 body is the message the helper already carried; only its status and classification change.

## Rebase onto `9feafa27` (2026-11-09)

The branch was `dirty`, so it was rebased onto current `main` `9feafa273088aa1c422fc2369f1d4001df9c0c9a`. New tip **`cefe1ebd7956b373e0fa67eb7849f8c2d7353507`**.

pr:922.body:
Fixes #665

`web_fetch`'s public-URL guard lets several IPv6 families through even though each one carries an IPv4 address the guard already knows how to judge. A model-supplied URL such as `http://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/` or `http://[2002:a9fe:a9fe::]/` reaches loopback or the link-local metadata endpoint, while the equivalent `::ffff:127.0.0.1` is rejected. This closes those holes, pins that public addresses in the same forms keep working, and — after review — refuses the non-canonical suffixes of the local-use NAT64 prefix rather than guessing where their IPv4 address sits.

## What was wrong

`ipv6Blocked()` consulted `ipv4Blocked()` only for IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) and IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d`) forms, where the embedded IPv4 address sits in the last two hextets. Other families carry the same address elsewhere:

| family | prefix | where the IPv4 address sits | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NAT64 well-known | `64:ff9b::/96` | last 32 bits | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| NAT64 local-use | `64:ff9b:1::/48` | last 32 bits **only for the canonical `/96` sub-layout** | canonical `/96` decoded; every other suffix under the `/48` rejected |
| 6to4 | `2002::/16` | hextets 2–3 | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| IPv4-translated | `::ffff:0:0:0/96` | last 32 bits, after `ffff` and 16 zero bits | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| Teredo | `2001:0::/32` | last 32 bits, bitwise inverted | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| site-local (deprecated) | `fec0::/10` | no IPv4 — the range itself is non-public | reject |

No branch inspected those positions, so each form fell through to `return false`.

The local-use row is the review fix. `64:ff9b:1::/48` is wider than the `/96` an embedded address needs, and RFC 8215 allows deployments to use other suffix lengths — a deployment that puts the IPv4 address in bits 64–95 is not judged by hextets 6–7. Reading hextets 6–7 of *every* address in the `/48` therefore judged the wrong bits: `64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808` was interpreted as the public `128.8.8.8`.

## What changed

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts`: one helper, `dotted(high, low)`, and `ipv6Blocked()` extracts the embedded address for the rows above and hands it to the existing `ipv4Blocked()`. There is no second copy of the IPv4 block list, no blanket range ban, and no refactor of the existing mapped/compatible branches.

For the local-use prefix the rule is now explicit and fail-closed: decode the canonical `64:ff9b:1:0:0:0::/96` sub-layout, and **return blocked for every non-canonical suffix** under `64:ff9b:1::/48` (`return true`, never `return false` — an unknown suffix must not become the way around the guard). The well-known `64:ff9b::/96` prefix is untouched by that rule.

## Red first

The new test (`providers.test.ts`), run against the unfixed `url-guard.ts`:

```
not ok 11 - web_fetch judges NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local literals by their embedded IPv4
  error: |-
    64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808

    false !== true

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  expected: true
  actual: false
# tests 16
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

The assertion loop stops at its first failing literal, so every blocked literal was also probed one by one against the unfixed predicate, and every public one against the fixed predicate. Values are `blocked` / `allowed` from `isBlockedAddress`; the flipped rows are the review fix, all in the tightening direction:

| address | before `e9e7358c` review fix | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `64:ff9b::7f00:1` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b::808:808` | allowed | allowed |
| `64:ff9b:1::7f00:1` (canonical `/96`) | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1::a9fe:a9fe` (canonical `/96`) | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1::808:808` (canonical `/96`) | allowed | allowed |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:1:0:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:0:1:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:dead:beef:cafe:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:7f00:1` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:a9fe:a9fe` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |

Five flips in this probed set, all `allowed → blocked`; zero `blocked → allowed`.

## Only tighter

The same probe run before and after the review fix differs in exactly one line — the tightened address. Everything a legitimate client may reach still resolves as public:

```
ALLOW  literal 64:ff9b::808:808            (NAT64 well-known, public)
ALLOW  literal 64:ff9b:1::808:808          (NAT64 local-use canonical /96, public)
ALLOW  literal 2002:808:808::              (6to4 for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal ::ffff:0:808:808            (IPv4-translated for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal 2001:0:808:808::f7f7:f7f7   (Teredo for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal 2606:4700:4700::1111        (native IPv6)
ALLOW  resolver 64:ff9b::808:808 for http://example.com/
ALLOW  resolver 2606:4700:4700::1111 for http://example.com/
```

These are asserted in the test too (`assert.equal(isBlockedAddress(...), false)` and `assert.equal(await assertPublicUrl(...), url)`), so the guard cannot be "fixed" by blocking a prefix.

## After the fix

```
# tests 16
# pass 16
# fail 0
```

The test now has 17 blocked addresses and 6 public ones (23 assertions across the literal and resolver paths), including the canonical `/96` cases in both directions and the non-canonical suffixes.

Diffstat against `main` `f4dd1813`:

```
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts | 71 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts      | 35 +++++++++++-
 2 files changed, 106 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

This branch is `f4dd1813` + four commits, two files, nothing else:

1. `dd29d921` test: pin NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local fetch targets
2. `eb818998` fix: judge NAT64, 6to4 and IPv4-translated literals by their embedded IPv4
3. `e4bb3e67` test: judge the local-use NAT64 prefix by its canonical /96 only
4. `e9e7358c` fix: decode only the canonical /96 under the local-use NAT64 prefix

It does not contain any commit from #915; the three-file view was the reviewer's worktree.

Ran:
- `node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts` in `packages/data-source` — `# tests 16 # pass 16 # fail 0`; the same command on the unfixed source is the red above (`# pass 15 # fail 1`).
- `tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- Per-address probe of the 17 blocked and 6 public literals before and after the review fix — the before/after table and the only-tighter block above.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` (full layers) were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser/API/CLI journey was added: the change is a predicate inside the `web_fetch` URL guard, and the mocked E2E subset does not exercise NAT64/6to4 literals.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: a model-supplied `web_fetch` URL that encodes a private, loopback or link-local IPv4 address in NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated, Teredo or site-local form is rejected with `PublicUrlError` instead of being fetched; public addresses in the same forms keep working, and non-canonical suffixes of the local-use NAT64 prefix are rejected rather than guessed at.

Compatibility and migration: none. A deployment that puts the NAT64 IPv4 address in bits 64–95 of `64:ff9b:1::/48` is now rejected instead of silently misjudged; the canonical `/96` layout and `64:ff9b::/96` behave exactly as before.

pr:924.body:
Fixes #839

A delimited dataset preview derived one number, `Math.max(header.length, widest)`, and used it for two jobs: the grid width and the column count it reported. A two-column `.csv` with one 200,001-field line rendered 1,001 mostly-blank columns and announced `The file has 200001 columns; the preview shows the first 1001.` Both halves now come from the header: the column count *is* the header, and a wider line may add only a small, capped set of unnamed surplus columns.

## What was wrong

- **The count.** `clippedColumns.total` was `Math.max(header.length, widest)` — a data line's field count presented as the file's schema. The only sentence the reader gets was built from it, so a two-column file was described as a 200,001-column one, and the same outlier cells were named twice ("has N columns" and "M cells past the preview width").

- **The width.** `width = min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`, so one outlier line decided how wide the grid was. Taking the width from the *returned* rows instead would make the column set depend on the client's `maxRows` (the previous defect), so neither end of the file may own the width.

## What changed

`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `parseDelimitedTable` only:

- `totalColumns = header.length` — the header is the schema; a wide row is a row.
- `surplusLimit = Math.min(16, Math.max(2, header.length))` — the cap `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts` already uses (`surplusColumnLimit`). A wider line may contribute at most that many **unnamed** surplus columns; a header at or past sixteen keeps every named column (`surplusLimit` only ever adds).
- `width = Math.min(header.length + surplusShown, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`, where `surplusShown = min(widest - header.length, surplusLimit)` — `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS` stays the absolute payload limit.
- `clippedColumns = { shown: Math.min(header.length, width), total: header.length }` — `shown` is the number of named columns the preview shows, so it is consistent with the new width and never exceeds the header. The column sentence therefore fires only when the header itself is wider than the preview.
- Cells past the width still go to `clippedCells`; a header wider than the payload cap is still reported through `clippedColumns`, exactly as before.
- A line past the row window may still set the width — the column set must not depend on the caller's `maxRows` — and the returned rows are padded to it, as before. What changes is that the padding is no longer silent: `paddingOnlyColumns = surplusShown - shownSurplus` (the surplus only an unseen line justifies) and `paddingOnlyCells = paddingOnlyColumns * rows.length` produce `The preview pads N unnamed columns (M blank cells) because the file has a wider line past the first K rows, which is not shown.` `clippedCells` keeps counting only returned rows' cells past the width, and a returned outlier produces no padding sentence.

Measured on the fixtures (all asserted in `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts`):

| fixture | columns | clipped | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2-column header + one 200,001-field line inside the window | `4` | `clippedCells 199997` | issue fixture: was 1,001 columns |
| 2-column header, no outlier | `2` | `clippedCells 0` | a narrow table is not widened to the cap |
| 8-column header + one 100-field line | `16` | `clippedCells 84` | header + capped surplus |
| 20-column header + one 200,001-field line | `36` | `clippedCells 199965`, all 20 names in order | the cap never takes a named column |
| 200,001-column header | `1001` | `clippedColumns {shown: 1001, total: 200001}` | `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS` still the absolute limit |

## Red first — the column count

The new count test run against the unfixed `parseDelimitedTable`, with the two stale assertions in `dashboard.test.ts` already corrected (the tree a reviewer replays with the test commit):

```
not ok 62 - a delimited preview caps a pathological line and counts what it leaves out
  error: |-
    the column count comes from the header; the wide row is cells, not columns
    + actual - expected
      { shown: 1001, + total: 200001 - total: 2 }

not ok 63 - a wide line past the row window does not become the file's column count
  error: |-
    the file has as many columns as its header

    5000 !== 2

# tests 67
# pass 65
# fail 2
```

## Red first — the width

The width assertions run against the same unfixed source (the final tree of this PR's tests):

```
not ok 62 - a delimited preview caps a pathological line and counts what it leaves out
    1001 !== 4
not ok 63 - a wide line past the row window does not become the file's column count
    1001 !== 4
not ok 64 - the surplus cap never takes a named column and scales with the header
    1001 !== 36
not ok 66 - a delimited preview shows the same columns whatever maxRows it is asked for
    1001 !== 4

# tests 68
# pass 64
# fail 4
```

## Red first — padding from a line past the row window

`agent-ci-infra-bot`'s F1: a file whose only wide line falls past the row window still widens the grid, and the payload said nothing about it (`clippedCells 0`, `warnings []`). Pinned in `621c3dcf` before any source change; fixture `a,b` + 100 x `1,2` + one 5,000-field line, so the grid is 4 columns and the outlier is row 101:

```
not ok 63 - a wide line past the row window does not become the file's column count
  error: |-
    the padding of an out-of-window line needs a warning of its own: []

    0 !== 1

# tests 68
# pass 67
# fail 1
```

The same test now also carries the in-window control: an outlier the preview does return is still counted as 4,996 cells past the width (`clippedCells`), and it must not produce the padding sentence.

## Red first — the padding count under the column cap

`agent-ci-infra-bot`'s next finding: the sentence assumed the grid is `header + surplusShown`, but `width` is `Math.min(header + surplusShown, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`, so a wide header makes it claim unnamed columns the grid does not hold. Pinned in `921ec1d4` before any source change:

```
not ok 64 - the padding sentence counts the unnamed columns the capped grid really holds
  error: |-
    the capped grid has no unnamed column, so there is nothing to report as padding
    + [
    +   'The preview pads 15 unnamed columns (1500 blank cells) because the file has a wider line past the first 100 rows, which is not shown.'
    + ]
    - []

not ok 65 - the padding sentence names the row window it is talking about
  error: 'the sentence counts rows, singular: The preview pads 2 unnamed columns (2 blank cells) because the file has a wider line past the first 1 rows, which is not shown.'

# tests 70
# pass 68
# fail 2
```

The fix counts from the grid that was actually built (`renderedSurplus = max(0, width - totalColumns)`), so a 1,001-column header with a hidden 1,016-field line reports no padding at all, and a 1,000-column header reports exactly the one unnamed column the cap leaves room for.

## After the fix — readings

```
# tests 70
# pass 70
# fail 0
```


Commits (test → fix, twice):

2. `8a78ef4a` fix: take a delimited preview's column count from its header
3. `5575361e` test: cap the unnamed surplus, never the header's own columns
4. `4c4cd346` fix: cap only the unnamed surplus columns of a delimited preview

- No browser journey: the rendered `DatasetTable` shows the payload's `columns` / `warnings` verbatim, and those are what the assertions pin.

## Payload semantics

`clippedColumns` is part of the preview payload, so this changes what one of its fields counts — it is not only an extra sentence:

| field | before this PR | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clippedColumns.total` | `Math.max(header.length, widest)` — a data line's field count | `header.length` — the header is the schema |
| `clippedColumns.shown` | `Math.min(total, width)` | `Math.min(header.length, width)`, so `shown <= total` holds again |
| `columns.length` vs `clippedColumns.total` | equal | `columns.length` may exceed `total` by up to `surplusLimit` unnamed surplus columns |
| `clippedCells` | cells of returned rows past the width | unchanged |
| `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS` | 1,001 | unchanged |

A consumer that read `clippedColumns.total` as "the file's column count" now gets the header's count, which is the schema #839 asked for. The unnamed surplus is the `columns.length - clippedColumns.total` gap, and `warnings` names it when an unseen line is the reason. `apps/web`'s `DatasetTable` renders `columns`, `clippedColumns` and `clippedCells`; it does not render `warnings` today, so the new sentence reaches the API payload only. Showing it in the table (with a localized sentence) is a separate `apps/web` follow-up, not part of this PR.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: a delimited preview no longer renders hundreds of blank columns because of one outlier line, and no longer tells the reader a column count the header does not have. A header wider than the payload cap still gets its explicit clipped-column signal.

Compatibility and migration: none. The payload shape is unchanged; `clippedColumns.total` now counts header columns, `clippedColumns.shown` counts the named columns shown, and the grid width is bounded by header + capped surplus.

Under zh-CN — the product default — the Session activity panel prints the two values it takes from
server data as raw API tokens:

  so a running execution reads `running`;
- the execution meta line renders `item.provenance` verbatim (`工作区 ws_a · 溯源 pending`), and the

## Cause

`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` rendered `item.state` / `item.provenance` straight into the
tree, and `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` carried the 25 `activity.*` chrome keys but no keys for
those two value domains. Every other surface already translates them (`WakeNotice.tsx` maps wake
states through `chat.wakeNoticeState.*`, `GovernedDownloadCards.tsx` does the same for downloads);
this was the one activity surface left in English.

Product: two files, +51/−8.

  `ProcessRecord` labels and the `executionMeta` call.

`cancellable`, the `progress.length` accounting, and every other badge in the app. A transfer's
`partial`, a reminder's `fired` and provenance `unconfirmed` are out of scope and keep their raw

appears in the fixture and keeps its token by the same lookup, without a dedicated assertion.

pr:932.body:
Fixes #930

A caller-supplied string that is over its length limit answered `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}`, so a provider form could not tell the user which field to shorten. The store already produces the right message (`The LLM API token is too long`); the shared request classifier just never recognised the shape and fell through to the catch-all.

## What was wrong

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` listed eight legacy validation messages that stay `400` (`is required`, `must`, `cannot`, `invalid`, …). In `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, `POST /api/providers/preview-models` calls `normalizeApiToken(body.apiToken)` before any network call, and `services/api/src/store/secrets.ts` throws a plain `Error("The LLM API token is too long")` once the trimmed token passes 16 384 characters. That message matched none of the eight patterns, so it reached the `unclassified_request_error` branch and became a 500.

The same shape appears at seven throw sites, all rejecting a client-supplied string, so they all leaked the same way:

| site | message |
| --- | --- |
| `store/secrets.ts` | `The LLM API token is too long` |
| `store/settings.ts` | `The proxy URL is too long` |
| `store/settings.ts` | `neo4jHttp is too long` |
| `store/settings.ts` | `neo4jUser is too long` |
| `store.ts` | `The Neo4j password is too long` |
| `store.ts` | `Model ID is too long` |
| `store.ts` | `The stored ${kind} is too long` |

## What changed

One pattern in the classifier, nothing else:

```ts
/\bis too long\b/i,
```

No new error code, no change to `normalizeApiToken` or any limit, no change to a throw site, and `services/api/src/http/index.ts` is untouched (`#929` owns the dispatch line next to the chain and this change does not meet it). The message already produced by the store is passed through unchanged, so the client sees `{"error":"The LLM API token is too long"}`.

The test file extends the existing table with the seven length messages above and adds one negative case that mentions a length without the validation shape (`Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget`), which must stay a 500; the existing `Database invariant failed` assertion is unchanged.

## Red first

Commit `341a5007` is the test only, on the unfixed classifier:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts
not ok 1 - keeps known validation failures at 400 without hiding internal faults
  error: |-
    The LLM API token is too long

    false !== true
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

Per message, before the fix (`isKnownClientInputError(new Error(message))`):

```
false  The LLM API token is too long
false  The proxy URL is too long
false  neo4jHttp is too long
false  neo4jUser is too long
false  The Neo4j password is too long
false  Model ID is too long
false  The stored runnerToken is too long
false  Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget
false  Database invariant failed
```

Route level, against the same unfixed tree, with a temporary probe that started the real `createApiServer` (offline MCP transport, temp data dir) and sent the issue's requests (probe file not committed):

```
STATUS 500 TEXT {"error":"Internal server error"}          POST /api/providers/preview-models  apiToken "k"×20000
STATUS 400 TEXT {"error":"The LLM API token cannot be empty"}  same route, apiToken ""
STATUS 201 ...                                             POST /api/providers, apiToken 16384 chars
```

The empty-token and valid-token readings are the control: the validator was already healthy at both ends, only the length case escaped.

## After the fix

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts
# tests 1
# pass 1
# fail 0
```

Same probe, fixed tree:

```
STATUS 400 TEXT {"error":"The LLM API token is too long"}
STATUS 400 TEXT {"error":"The LLM API token cannot be empty"}
STATUS 201 ... POST /api/providers apiToken 16384 chars
```

Per message, after the fix: the seven length messages are all `true`, and both non-validation messages (`Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget`, `Database invariant failed`) are still `false`, so a genuine internal fault still answers 500.

Diffstat against `main` `2908e9e8`:

```
 services/api/src/http/error-classification.test.ts | 10 ++++++++++
 services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts      |  3 +++
 2 files changed, 13 insertions(+)
```

- Temporary route probe as above (unfixed: 500; fixed: 400 with the store's message; empty token 400; valid token 201) — file deleted before the commit, so the diff stays at two files.

- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
