pr:933.body:
Fixes #910

Classification: **hygiene, not a product fix.** Test-only change to `source-health.test.ts`; product behaviour is unchanged. Excluded from sprint window scoring and today's KPI on the Lead's ruling.

The harm is real but indirect: the injected-fault wait timing out turns `UT` red for pull requests that do not touch `packages/data-source` at all. `#872` hit exactly this (`NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED: packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts`, `planned 6279 / failed 1`) although all four of its changed files are under `apps/web`. That is a false red, not a defect in the code under test.

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts` gave its injected fault a wall-clock budget of about 200 ms (200 polls × 1 ms). On a loaded runner — four UT worker processes (`UT_WORKERS = 4`, one Node file each) plus coverage instrumentation — the fault lands later than that, the helper falls through to `assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection")`, and the `UT` job turns the only required status check red on a pull request that does not touch this package. Two pull requests were blocked by exactly this identity on 2026-11-04.

## What was wrong

```ts
async function waitFor(predicate: () => boolean) {
  for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) { if (predicate()) return; await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1)); }
  assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection");
}
```

The budget is a fixed count of sleeps, so any event-loop delay counts against it. The product behaviour was never wrong; the wait was.

## What changed — the first proposal at `07c82091`

This is the shape the branch had before the rebase; the code on the current tip is in "Rebase and the review findings" below, which keeps the 10 s deadline but reads it with `performance.now()` and carries a diagnosis.

The helper now waits on a deadline instead of a fixed budget:

```ts
const FAULT_OBSERVATION_DEADLINE_MS = 10_000;
async function waitFor(predicate: () => boolean, timeoutMs = FAULT_OBSERVATION_DEADLINE_MS) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) { if (predicate()) return; await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1)); }
  assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection");
}
```

The poll interval stays 1 ms, so a healthy run is as fast as before; a loaded run waits for the observation up to 10 s; a genuinely missing fault still fails, and the new test pins that it fails quickly rather than hanging the layer. The failure message is unchanged, so a real regression keeps the same identity.

This touches only the test file — no product code, no other test. As first proposed the three existing `waitFor` call sites were unchanged; the rebase later gave each of them a diagnosis (see below).

## Red first

Commit `731bc426` adds the regression test only, on the old helper:

```ts
let observed = false;
const timer = setTimeout(() => { observed = true; }, 500);
try { await waitFor(() => observed); } finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
```

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/source-health.test.ts
ok 1 - 429 cooldown rejects later agent rounds without another upstream request or wait
not ok 2 - the fault wait tolerates a loaded runner instead of a 200 ms budget
  error: 'Timed out waiting for local fault injection'
ok 3 - parallel 429 callers share cooldown, drain their queue and do not retry inside one slot
...
# tests 17
# pass 16
# fail 1
```

A 500 ms observation is a stand-in for a busy runner: it is the same event-loop delay the ci hit, only deterministic, so the failure reproduces without needing a loaded machine.

## After the fix

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/source-health.test.ts
# tests 17
# pass 17
# fail 0
```

The new test also asserts the fail-fast path after the fix, so widening the deadline cannot hide a missing fault:

```ts
await assert.rejects(() => waitFor(() => false, 50), /Timed out waiting for local fault injection/);
```

Diffstat against `main` `2908e9e8`:

```
 packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts | 17 +++++++++++++++--
 1 file changed, 15 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
```

Commits: `731bc426` test (red), `07c82091` fix — the first proposal only. The four commits on the current tip are `21921b4f` test (red) → `58b85992` fix → `4c3535b7` test (red) → `7413208f` fix, listed under "Rebase and the review findings".

Ran:
- `cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/source-health.test.ts` — `# pass 16 # fail 1` on the red commit (`not ok 2`, `Timed out waiting for local fault injection`), `# pass 17 # fail 0` on the fix.
- `tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut` (the whole layer, 6 281 cases) was not run locally; CI runs it on this pull request, and the fix is confined to one UT file.
- `pnpm ci:st` / `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run: the change is a test helper, not product behaviour.

## Release

Release category: `release:test` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: none directly. A flaky UT identity that could turn the required check red on unrelated pull requests now waits for the observation it was already waiting for, so it stops blocking merges it has nothing to do with.

## Rebase and the review findings (`9feafa273088`, 2026-11-09)

The branch was cut from `2908e9e8` and the pull request showed `mergeable=false` / `dirty`. It is now rebased onto `9feafa27`; one conflict, in `waitFor` itself, resolved by taking this branch's deadline version.

Two review threads were still open on the previous tip and are answered here.

**F1 — the deadline is not a bound while `Date` is mocked.** Correct. One pre-existing call site (`cooldown admits one recovery probe…`) runs under `t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ["Date"] })`, where `Date.now()` stands still and only `t.mock.timers.tick()` moves it, while `setTimeout` stays real — so a `Date`-based deadline never arrives and a predicate that never becomes true spins instead of failing. The new guard test below adds a second such call site on purpose. Red evidence on the pre-fix helper: a never-true predicate under a mocked `Date` never returns —

```
$ timeout 20 node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "stays bounded while Date is mocked" src/source-health.test.ts
exit=124        # killed after 20 s: the wait never timed out
```

The helper now measures its bound with `performance.now()`, which the `Date` mock does not touch, so the deadline is real in all three call sites. The new test `the fault wait stays bounded while Date is mocked` pins it (red on the previous helper: `AssertionError ... Timed out waiting for local fault injection`, i.e. no elapsed report and no diagnostics).

**Timeout diagnostics.** A timeout now reports how long it waited and what it was waiting for; the three call sites pass the state a future red gate needs:

- `parallel 429 callers…` → `calls=N settled=[SOURCE_COOLDOWN, RATE_LIMIT_QUEUE_FULL, …]` (the errors that settled while waiting).
- `cooldown admits one recovery probe…` → `calls=N invocations=[…]`.
- `queue exhaustion, timeout and cancellation…` → `calls=N invocations=[…]`.

Example message: `Timed out waiting for local fault injection after 10012 ms: calls=1 settled=[RATE_LIMIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT, …]`.

**F2 — the worker count.** Correct: the `UT` slice runs four child processes (`UT_WORKERS = 4` in `test/support/tagged/scheduler.mjs`, one Node file per process), not sixteen; the 16 in the artifact is this file's test count. Both the comment and this body now say four.

## Validation on the rebased tip

- `node --import tsx --test packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts` → `# tests 18 / # pass 18 / # fail 0`, ten consecutive runs, every one identical (`run 1 … run 10: # tests 18 / # pass 18 / # fail 0`).
- `npx tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → exit 0.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` → exit 0.
- diffstat against `9feafa27`: 1 file, `+91/−13` (`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts`).

**F5 — the mocked-`Date` scope was overstated, and the snippet was stale.** Correct on both counts, and this is the wording fix rather than a behaviour change. An instrumented copy that recorded `Date.now !== realDateNow` at every `waitFor` entry printed `[false,false,true,false,true,false]`: the two `true` are `cooldown admits one recovery probe…` and the new guard test, not three call sites. The comment in the file and this body now say one pre-existing call site plus the guard, and the "What changed" snippet and commit list above are marked as the pre-rebase proposal, with the current four commits named.

Commit `43ccb4de` (`test(data-source): name the call sites the mocked Date actually covers`) carries the comment reword. It is pushed in the tip below, together with the determinisation that also settles the reason the reword was needed — see the next section.

## The CI red on `7413208f`: two L2 slices, neither reachable from this diff

Run `42581062474` is `failure` on two mocked E2E jobs, and the required `merge-gate` follows them:

- `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config)` (job `129041926772`, `planned 58 / executed 58 / passed 57 / failed 1`): `journey-prepare-environment.spec.ts:57` — `Error: BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: micromamba setup failed)`, failed in 231 ms, i.e. in environment provisioning, not in test logic.
- `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)` (job `129041926835`, `planned 87 / executed 87 / passed 86 / failed 1`): `journey-plugin-composition.spec.ts:36` — `getByLabel('artifact-json plugin')`: expected `"disabled"`, received `"inherit"`.

This diff is one test file, `packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts`; it cannot reach Python base provisioning or the plugin-composition settings UI. `L1`, `UT`, `ST`, `L2 research`, `L2 governed`, `L2 literature` and `Coverage` are all success in the same run.

## The determinisation at `f2fcfd44`, and why F5 no longer needs a comment

The deadline this pull request added in `58b85992` and `7413208f` bounds a wait; it does not remove it. Three observations still polled a clock for a moment this suite itself triggers: the 12 parallel callers and the recovery probe wait for their request to reach the transport, and a loaded runner can only make that late.

`nextCall(target)` makes the observation an event instead. The fixture's transport resolves every waiter whose call has arrived, so `await f.nextCall(1)` returns exactly when the first request enters it — no interval, no deadline, nothing a slow runner can turn into a failure:

- `parallel 429 callers share cooldown…` → `await f.nextCall(1)`, then release the fault.
- `cooldown admits one recovery probe…` → `await f.nextCall(2)`.
- `queue exhaustion, timeout and cancellation…` → `await f.nextCall(1)`.

F5's correction (one pre-existing mocked-`Date` call site plus the guard, not three) is in `43ccb4de`, and the paragraph that used to overstate the count is gone from the code.

**F6 then retired `waitFor` at `fd97a589`.** After the three observations moved, `waitFor` was reachable only from its own contract tests and `describeSettled` had no caller — and an unguarded rendezvous turns a regression into a stall, because `nextCall` returned a promise nothing settles and the tagged worker's 300 s test deadline would replace the 10 s failure with its diagnosis. The bound and the diagnosis moved into the rendezvous instead: `nextCall(target, wait)` keeps `FAULT_OBSERVATION_DEADLINE_MS` (10 s, `performance.now()` + `setTimeout`, so the mocked-`Date` cases are unaffected) and rejects with `Timed out waiting for local fault injection after N ms: <state>`; `describeSettled` and `describeInvocations` feed the three call sites, so `calls=… settled=[…]` and `invocations=[…]` can appear in a real failure again. `waitFor` and its two contract tests are gone; the rendezvous contract test covers both duties — it resolves only on the named call, and it fails with the observed state while `Date` is mocked.

Red first, kept as two commits: `5a1d2a7a` converts the three observations and adds `the call rendezvous names the call it waits for and resolves only on it` while the fixture has no `nextCall`, so the suite reads `# tests 19 / # pass 15 / # fail 4` with `error: 'f.nextCall is not a function'` on the four; `f2fcfd44` adds the rendezvous and the suite reads `# tests 19 / # pass 19 / # fail 0`.

The two L2 reds on the previous tip are unchanged by this and are recorded above: `standard-config` failed in 231 ms inside `micromamba` provisioning, and `standard-journeys` failed on a settings-select initial value in `journey-plugin-composition.spec.ts`. Neither slice runs this file; the same two slices are green on `#868` in the same window.

pr:934.body:
Fixes #918

`GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests` gained two cases in `#915` that assert the walk stays *quiet*: a generated workspace file is not reported, and a file removed between the listing and the read is skipped. Both assert a negative, so nothing in the suite would fail if the walk stopped reporting anything at all — a future narrowing of `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` or `_files` could silence the boundary check while every test stayed green.

This adds the positive half: a file the walk *should* report is reported.

## Why

The two existing cases are `assertNotIn`, so they pass for any walk that returns an empty list. The only test that pins the positive direction is `ArchitectureBoundaryTests.test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names`, and it asserts the *absence* of findings on the real tree — it cannot go red when the walk is narrowed either, because the tree happens to be clean. A walk that silently ignores `services/api` would keep the entire module green, and vendor naming could escape the boundary unnoticed.

The new case reuses the mocking shape of the removed-after-listing case at `:162`: patch `_files` and let the patched listing hand the walk a path. It differs in what the listing returns — a file that still exists, with a vendor token in it.

## What changed

One test, `services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py` only. No product code.

```python
self.probe = self.positive_probe_path()   # apps/web/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts
self.addCleanup(self.probe.unlink, missing_ok=True)
self.probe.write_text("// deerflow vendor token\n", encoding="utf-8")
original = _files

def only_the_probe(root: Path):
    # Keep the real listing (so IGNORED_DIRECTORIES still governs) and drop
    # every other file, so the assertion cannot depend on the working tree.
    if root == self.API_ROOT:
        return (path for path in original(root) if path == self.probe)
    return original(root)

with mock.patch.object(sys.modules[__name__], "_files", only_the_probe):
    failures = _node_boundary_failures()
self.assertIn(f"content: {self.relative_probe()}", failures)
```

`only_the_probe` delegates to the real `_files`, so the ignore rules still decide what is listed; it only drops unrelated files so the assertion does not depend on whatever else is in the working tree. If `services/api` is ever added to `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES`, the real listing yields nothing and the case fails.

## Red first

Temporarily add `services/api` to the walk's ignore set — the equivalent of a future narrowing that the two negative cases cannot see:

```diff
-IGNORED_DIRECTORIES = {"__pycache__", ".tmp", "dist", "node_modules"}
+IGNORED_DIRECTORIES = {"__pycache__", ".tmp", "dist", "node_modules", "api"}
```

```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_architecture_boundaries.py'
....F.
======================================================================
FAIL: test_a_vendor_reference_outside_a_generated_workspace_is_still_reported
  (test_architecture_boundaries.GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests)
The cases above only prove the walk stays quiet; this proves it still speaks.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py", line 200,
  in test_a_vendor_reference_outside_a_generated_workspace_is_still_reported
    self.assertIn(f"content: {self.relative_probe()}", failures)
AssertionError: 'content: services/api/src/probe-boundary-5.ts' not found in []

----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 6 tests in 0.885s

FAILED (failures=1)
```

The other five tests stayed green under the same mutation, which is exactly the gap: only the new case noticed.

## After reverting the mutation

```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_architecture_boundaries.py'
......
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 6 tests in 1.271s

OK
```

Diffstat against `main` `2908e9e8`:

```
 services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py | 65 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 65 insertions(+)
```

## Rebase and F1 — the positive probe moves out of the egress scan

Rebased onto `9feafa273088` (2026-11-09); the branch was cut at an older main and the pull request showed `mergeable=false` / `dirty`. One commit, replayed unchanged.

F1 (thread `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM60He32`): the positive case planted `services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts`, which `services/api/src/mcp/datasource-egress-contract.test.ts` reads — its `sourceFiles()` walks every `.ts` under `packages/` and `services/` skipping only `dist`, `node_modules` and `.tmp`, and `readFile`s each hit with no ENOENT tolerance. With `UT_WORKERS = 4`, a parallel worker could read the probe between creation and `addCleanup`, and a killed run would leave a vendor token in a tracked source directory.

Fixed with the reviewer's second option: the probe now lives at `apps/web/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts`. `NODE_ROOTS` includes `apps/web`, so `_node_boundary_failures()` still walks and reports it — the positive half of the contract is unchanged — while `sourceFiles()` never scans `apps/web`, so no other worker reads a file this case creates and removes. `only_the_probe` now filters on the walked root; see F4 below for why the first revision of that filter was wrong.

Red first (`2c41f812`): a test that mirrors the egress predicate —

```
EGRESS_SCANNED_ROOTS = ("packages", "services")
EGRESS_IGNORED_DIRECTORIES = {"dist", "node_modules", ".tmp"}
def _egress_scan_reads(path: Path) -> bool:
    ...
```

and asserts the probe path is not readable by it:

```
$ cd services/gateway && python3 -m pytest tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py -q
1 failed, 6 passed
AssertionError: ... services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts is read by the datasource egress worker while it exists; plant the probe under apps/web instead
```

After (`20318a36`): `7 passed`.

diffstat against `9feafa27`: 1 file, `+65/−0` (`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py`; three commits — the original positive case, the red egress test, and the move).

Ran:
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_architecture_boundaries.py'` — `Ran 6 tests ... OK` on the branch; `FAILED (failures=1)` with the assertion excerpt above under the temporary `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` narrowing, then `OK` again after reverting it.
- The probe file is created under `apps/web/` and removed by `addCleanup`, so the working tree is clean after the run (`git status --porcelain` empty).

Not run:
- `pnpm gateway:test` (the whole `services/gateway/tests` discovery) was not run locally; only this module was, and CI runs the full discovery.
- No UT/ST/E2E layers: the change is one gateway test, no product code.

## Release

Release category: `release:test` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: none. It makes the architecture boundary check able to fail when the walk is narrowed, instead of only when it is noisy.

## F2 — the probe moves back into `services/api`, with the four checks a killed run needs

At `20318a36` the positive half ran only over `apps/web`. The reviewer's mutation showed why that is not a narrowing guard: with `"api"` added to `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES`, or `services/api` dropped from `NODE_ROOTS`, the suite still printed `7 passed`. `Fixes #918` would have closed the issue without covering the tree it names first.

This tip takes the reviewer's first option and keeps the probe inside that tree: `PROBE_ROOT = services/api/src`, probe name `probe-boundary-<pid>.mdx`.

Two positive assertions, so a rename cannot pass for a fix:

- `test_the_positive_probe_lives_in_the_root_the_issue_names` — the path sits under `services/api/src` (`assertIn("services/api/src/", relative)`) and carries the probe suffix. Moving the probe back to `apps/web` fails it.
- `test_the_walk_enumerates_and_reads_the_positive_probe` — `_files(PROBE_ROOT)` enumerates the probe and `_node_boundary_failures()` reports `content: services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.mdx`. That is the whole reason `.mdx` still counts: `.mdx` is in `TEXT_SUFFIXES` (`test_architecture_boundaries.py:48`), while `sourceFiles()` in `services/api/src/mcp/datasource-egress-contract.test.ts:394` collects only files whose `extname` is `.ts`, so the egress worker never opens it. A suffix outside `TEXT_SUFFIXES` fails this case.

The four checks a killed run needs, one line each:

1. **Location is pinned both ways** — the two positive assertions above; `apps/web` fails the first, `.bin` fails the second.
2. **`.gitignore` is exact** — `/services/api/src/probe-boundary-*.mdx` (comment plus one line). Not `*.mdx`, not `probe-boundary-*`, not the directory. `git check-ignore -v services/api/src/probe-boundary-12345.mdx` prints `.gitignore:100:/services/api/src/probe-boundary-*.mdx`, and `git ls-files services/api/src | grep -c '\.mdx'` is `0`.
3. **Every exit path cleans up** — `_guard_probe_against_signals()` runs in `setUp`, before any probe exists, so both probe-writing cases (and any added later) are covered rather than the one test that happened to install it. It installs `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` handlers that unlink the probe, restore the previous handler and re-raise the same signal, plus an `atexit` hook for a `sys.exit` or an interpreter that ends before unittest cleanups; both hooks read `self.probe` when they fire, so they unlink the probe the current test wrote. Verified in child processes: `SIGTERM` → probe gone, child exits `143` (the signal is never swallowed); `sys.exit(0)` → probe gone, exit `0`. `setUp` also sweeps probes a dead run left behind, keeping any file whose pid still answers `os.kill(pid, 0)`, so a parallel shard is never deleted (`SIGKILL` cannot be caught — that sweep is its fallback).
4. **No real values** — the probe content is the fixed marker `// deerflow vendor token`; the diff adds no `os.environ`/`getenv` read and no token, secret or path interpolation.

Readings on `75d5b7e2`:

- `cd services/gateway && python3 -m pytest tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py -q` → `16 passed, 1 warning` (was 7 before this round; the two new positive cases, the F4 filter case and the six sweep cases are the additions).
- Child-process checks: `SIGTERM` → probe gone, exit `143`; `sys.exit(0)` → probe gone, exit `0`.
- diffstat against `9feafa27`: 2 files, `+156/−0` (`.gitignore` +4, `services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py` +152).
- Mutation table, all on this tip: probe under `apps/web` → location case FAIL; `PROBE_SUFFIX = ".bin"` → walk-read case FAIL; `"api"` in `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` → positive case FAIL; `services/api` dropped from `NODE_ROOTS` → positive case FAIL; `apps/web` dropped from `NODE_ROOTS` → PASS (coverage no longer depends on it).
- Working tree clean after the suite: no `probe-boundary-*.mdx` left in `services/api/src`.

Not run: the rest of `services/gateway/tests` discovery (CI runs it), and no UT/ST/E2E layers — the change is two gateway test files' worth of test code plus one ignore line.

## F3 — the sweep runs before the walk, and it tells a dead run from a live shard

`ArchitectureBoundaryTests.test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` walks the real tree and is collected before the class that writes probes, so a probe a killed run left behind failed `:117` before `GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests.setUp` could delete it. `_remove_stale_probes(root, pattern)` is now a module function, called from `setUpModule()` — ahead of every case — and again from `setUp` as an idempotent second pass.

Its judgement, with the values actually in the file:

- **same pid**: skipped outright, never swept;
- **dead pid**: deleted;
- **live pid on a host with `/proc`**: deleted when the probe's mtime predates that process's own start by more than `PROBE_START_MARGIN_S = 3 s`. Start time is `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 over `os.sysconf('SC_CLK_TCK')` (measured **100** here, not hard-coded) plus `/proc/stat`'s `btime`. The margin absorbs `btime`'s one-second truncation and an NTP step: on this host `_process_started_at(getpid())` = `1794221689.93` against a wall clock of `1794221690.69`;
- **no usable `/proc`**: pid liveness plus `PROBE_STALE_AGE_S = 10 s`. The slowest probe-holding case measured `0.65 s` (`pytest --durations=0`), so 10 s is more than ten times a full probe life. The path is chosen by whether the `/proc` reads succeed, not by `sys.platform`: `test_process_start_time_is_none_when_proc_is_absent` mocks `open` to raise on `/proc/...`, and `test_without_proc_the_age_fallback_decides` mocks the start time to `None` and requires the age rule to delete an old probe.

Red and green, both residues: with either a `probe-boundary-999999.mdx` (dead pid) or a `probe-boundary-1.mdx` with a ten-minute-old mtime on disk, `python3 -m pytest services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py -q` was `1 failed, 8 passed` before the change and is `16 passed` after, with the residue gone. Collection order is deterministic: `services/gateway/pyproject.toml` depends on `pytest==9.0.2` only — no `pytest-randomly`, no `pytest-xdist`, no `pytest.ini`/`conftest.py` overriding it — so `setUpModule()` is guaranteed to precede `:117`.

What was deliberately **not** done, because it would be passing the gate by hiding the failure: no `probe-boundary-*` filter or `continue` in `_files()`, no probe pattern in `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES`, no extra ignore table, no `skipTest`/`skipIf`/early return in the real-tree case, no weakening of `assertEqual(failures, [])` to `assertNotIn`, and no vendor whitelist in `VENDOR_NAME`.

## F4 — the filter now keys on the root the walk visits

`only_the_probe` compared `root == self.PROBE_ROOT`, but `_node_boundary_failures()` only ever passes `NODE_ROOTS` entries, which contain `services/api`, not `services/api/src` — so the branch never matched and the positive case walked every root unfiltered. `_filtered_listing()` now filters on `self.API_ROOT`, and the positive case routes its patched listing through it.

The isolation is proved, not assumed: `test_the_positive_filter_drops_another_shards_probe` feeds the API-root listing this case's probe plus a sibling's same-pattern probe and an ordinary `neighbour.py`, and requires `[self.probe]` back; feeding the `PROBE_ROOT` listing returns all of them unchanged, pinning the distinction that was wrong. Checked on the tip: `PROBE_ROOT in NODE_ROOTS == False`, `API_ROOT in NODE_ROOTS == True`. `test_the_positive_probe_lives_in_the_root_the_issue_names` and `test_the_walk_enumerates_and_reads_the_positive_probe` both stay, and the red path is intact: with `"api"` added to `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` the positive case fails with `'content: services/api/src/probe-boundary-3.mdx' not found in []`.

## Known limitation: two shards sharing one checkout are not supported

`:117` deliberately walks the real tree and the sweep must not delete a live shard's file, so a sibling's in-flight probe can fail it. Forcing that overlap (one process holds its probe while another runs the module) gives `1 failed, 15 passed` with `AssertionError: Lists differ: ['content: services/api/src/probe-boundary-4.mdx'] != []`. Two shards run side by side on one checkout were green in three rounds (`16 passed` each) because the probe lives under a second inside a 2.4 s run, but the collision remains possible by construction. CI gives each job its own checkout, so this does not occur there; introducing xdist would need the probe moved or the walk redesigned, not a skip marker.

Readings on `75d5b7e2`: `16 passed`; dead-pid and live-pid-old residues both `16 passed` after starting from `1 failed, 8 passed`; `PROBE_ROOT in NODE_ROOTS == False` / `API_ROOT in NODE_ROOTS == True`; `SC_CLK_TCK = 100`, `PROBE_START_MARGIN_S = 3.0`, `PROBE_STALE_AGE_S = 10.0`; diffstat against `9feafa27`: 2 files, `+320/−0`.

pr:936.body:
Fixes #935

The Specialist settings pane prints "Internal server error" for ordinary client mistakes: a name that is already taken, an id that no longer exists, an edit of a read-only built-in. The three routes forward the store's plain `Error`s straight to the catch-all, whose classifier recognises none of those messages, so every rejection becomes a 500. The neighbouring MCP-servers surface already answers these shapes — 400 for a rejected input, 404 for a missing id — and so do the model, provider, proxy-server, project and permission-grant routes, so the Specialist routes were the outlier rather than the norm.

## What changed

`services/api/src/http/index.ts` only, in the block the three Specialist handlers occupy:

- `POST /api/specialists`, `PUT /api/specialists/:id` and `DELETE /api/specialists/:id` now run through `answerSpecialistRoute`, which keeps the store's message verbatim and picks the status from `specialistErrorStatus`:
  - `Specialist not found` → `404`;
  - the store's own rejections → `400` — `Specialist name already exists`, `Specialist skills|connectors are unavailable…`, `Built-in specialists are read-only…`, and the messages the shared classifier already recognises (`is required`, `must`, `cannot`, …);
  - anything else → rethrown to the catch-all, so a genuine internal fault still reads `500` instead of being relabelled as client input.
- `readJson` is still evaluated before the guarded call, so a malformed body keeps the 400 the classifier gives it.

Untouched, as the issue requires: `services/api/src/store.ts` (its wording is the message the pane shows), `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` (held by the in-flight length-rejection fix), and `apps/web` (the client prints whatever the server says).

## Red first

Commit `3a3c9de4` adds the route test only, against the unfixed server. Six cases: the four rejected shapes fail, the two regression cases (the built-in `enabled` toggle answering 200, deleting a built-in answering 400) already pass.

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/specialists-http.test.ts
not ok 1 - a taken Specialist name is a 400 that keeps the store's wording
  error: |-
    a duplicate name is client input, not a server fault

    500 !== 400
not ok 2 - an unknown Specialist id on PUT is a 404       500 !== 404
not ok 3 - an unknown Specialist id on DELETE is a 404    500 !== 404
not ok 4 - editing a built-in Specialist is a 400 …       500 !== 400
# tests 6
# pass 2
# fail 4
```

The same four shapes answer `{"error":"Internal server error"}` in the issue's probe; this test reproduces them through the real `createApiServer` on a temporary data directory.

## After the fix

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/specialists-http.test.ts
# tests 8
# pass 8
# fail 0
```

The two extra cases are the "must not regress" half of the acceptance, and both were checked to bite:

- **an unexpected fault is still a 500.** The store has no injection seam (`ApiServerDependencies` exposes `webProvider`, `connectorFetch`, `fetchModelCatalog`, `fetchUsageExchangeRate`, `ideaTreeRepository`, `mcpTransport`, `remoteCompute` — no store), so the test fails the HTTPS response itself from inside the guarded block: the injected throw must reach the catch-all as `500 Internal server error`, not be claimed as a 400. Making the route relabel every fault as 400 (the naive fix) turns exactly this case red and nothing else.
- **the status mapping is pinned directly** on `specialistErrorStatus`: 404 for the not-found message, 400 for each store rejection, and no status at all for `Catalog database is not initialized`, `database is locked` and `ENOTDIR: not a directory`.

Diffstat against `main` `2908e9e8`:

```
 services/api/src/http/index.ts            |  38 ++++++++---
 services/api/src/specialists-http.test.ts | 125 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 163 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)
```

Commits: `bd14fcef` test (red), `faff19d2` fix, `3f2fb978` test (red), `1ab96e0b` fix — four commits, rebased onto `9feafa27`.

## Rebase — `9feafa273088` (2026-11-09), and the exact-wording list

The branch was cut at `70b66fa4`; main moved to `9feafa27` and the pull request showed `mergeable=false` / `dirty`. The four commits were replayed onto `9feafa27`, nothing squashed.

One conflict, in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`: main added `extractReplacementModelId` exactly where this branch adds its two helpers. Resolved by keeping both — main's function first, then `specialistErrorStatus` and `answerSpecialistRoute`.

The remaining review finding (thread `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM60HOgb`) was that `specialistErrorStatus` still fell back to `isKnownClientInputError`, so any fault whose message happens to contain "must" or "cannot" was relabelled 400. The fallback is gone; the function now matches the store's own wording, one entry per throw in `services/api/src/store.ts`: `Specialist not found` (404), `Specialist name is required`, `Specialist description is required`, `Specialist description must be 1-500 characters`, `Specialist instructions must be 1-20000 characters`, `Specialist name already exists`, `Specialist (skills|connectors) are unavailable: …`, both built-in rejections, the referenced-Specialist rejection, and `enabled must be a boolean` (400). Any other message returns `undefined`, so it reaches the catch-all and reads 500. `SpecialistRuntimeConfigError` is untouched: it carries `SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID`, which the generic handler already answers with 400.

Red first (`3f2fb978`, source unchanged): `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/specialists-http.test.ts` → `# tests 10 # pass 9 # fail 1`; the failure is `only the store's own wording is client input; this fault must read 500: Catalog contains an unknown value` / `400 !== undefined`. The same commit pins all twelve store messages, so losing one mapping is caught.

After (`1ab96e0b`): `# tests 10 # pass 10 # fail 0`; `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` exit 0. diffstat against `9feafa27`: 2 files, `+223/−7`.

## Validation

Ran:

- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/builtin-specialists.test.ts` — `# tests 5 # pass 5 # fail 0`; the built-in catalog itself is unchanged.

pr:941.body:
Fixes #937

## What happens

`#932` classifies any message matching `/\bis too long\b/i` as client input, and the dispatch at
`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3938` answers a classified error `400` **with its text**. Two
executor messages contain the phrase mid-sentence and embed a filesystem path, so with `#932`'s
pattern they answered `400 {"error":"Runner bundle path is too long for tar: /…"}` instead of
`500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` — before `#932` both were 500 and the path stayed hidden.

## Change

One pattern, at `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:37`:

```diff
-/\bis too long\b/i,
+/\bis too long\.?\s*$/i,
```

Anchored at the end of the message, so only a message that *ends* with the phrase is client input.
Between the phrase and the end this allows exactly two things: an optional sentence period (`\.?`)
and trailing whitespace (`\s*`), which is what copy that ends with `is too long.`, `is too long\n` or
`is too long. \r\n` needs.

Why this shape and not something looser:

- **Not `\b…\b` (#932's unanchored form).** Any mid-sentence mention would classify, and the two
  executor faults (`packages/executor/src/runner-bundle.ts:76,80`,
  `packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts:777`) put the phrase in the middle of a sentence that
  carries an absolute path — the client would get `400` with that path in the body.
- **`\.?` plus `\s*$`, not `.*$`.** The only tolerated trailing characters are the sentence
  terminator and whitespace. `… is too long for tar: <path>` still has text after the phrase, so it
  stays a fault, and a path can never appear in the `400` body. The same holds for
  `… is too long for a Unix socket: <path>`.

Nothing else changes: no new code, no change to the limits, no change to a throw site.

## Tests

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.test.ts`:

- the eight legitimate length messages pinned **by name** (not by count), including
  `pip indexUrl is too long` (`packages/schema/src/environment.ts:393`), which the first draft of
  #937 missed;
- the two executor messages as **negative** assertions: they must not become client input. The
  runner-bundle fixture spells its path `/srv/ws_a/data/model.bin` — a neutral absolute path, not the
  CI builder's home. This test file ships inside the release payload, and
  `scripts/binary-release/build-payload.sh` (`assert_no_build_paths`) rejects any payload file carrying
  the builder's own `HOME`; the merge-queue run `42148873426` failed `Binary release (x86_64)` and
  `(aarch64)` on exactly that literal. The sentence shape the case pins (a length phrase followed
  mid-sentence by an absolute path) is unchanged;
- the existing negatives stay: `Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget` and
  `Database invariant failed` are still faults;
- three **shape** probes, one test each so a regression names the shape it dropped — trailing
  newline (`"The LLM API token is too long\n"`), trailing period (`"The LLM API token is too long."`)
  and period-plus-CRLF (`"The Neo4j password is too long. \r\n"`) — all expected `true`.

## Red first

Two red runs, in this order, both before the code they pin.

**1. The anchor itself.** With the product pattern reverted to `#932`'s unanchored `/\bis too long\b/i`
and the by-name test kept, the run before the anchor commit was:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts
not ok 2 - a length rejection ends with the phrase, so a path-bearing executor fault stays a fault
  error: |-
    Runner bundle path is too long for tar: /home/runner/work/ws_a/data/model.bin
    true !== false
# tests 2
# pass 1
# fail 1
```

**2. The terminator.** On the anchored tip `60e36dbe` (`/\bis too long$/i`), the three shape probes
were added with the product pattern untouched, and all three went red on `false !== true`:

```
not ok 3 - a length rejection survives a trailing newline
not ok 4 - a length rejection survives a trailing period
not ok 5 - a length rejection survives a trailing period and CRLF
# tests 5
# pass 2
# fail 3
```

After `\.?\s*$`: `# tests 5 / # pass 5 / # fail 0`. Per message, `#932` pattern → this tip (probe
importing both modules; the probe is not committed):

```
true  -> true   The LLM API token is too long
true  -> true   The proxy URL is too long
true  -> true   neo4jHttp is too long
true  -> true   neo4jUser is too long
true  -> true   The Neo4j password is too long
true  -> true   Model ID is too long
true  -> true   The stored runnerToken is too long
true  -> true   pip indexUrl is too long
true  -> false  Runner bundle path is too long for tar: /srv/ws_a/data/model.bin
true  -> false  The remote data directory path is too long for a Unix socket: /tmp/sc-remote/ws_a/.agent.sock
false -> false  Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget
false -> false  Database invariant failed
```

And the three shapes, previous tip `is too long$` → this tip `is too long\.?\s*$`:

```
false -> true   "The LLM API token is too long\n"
false -> true   "The LLM API token is too long."
false -> true   "The Neo4j password is too long. \r\n"
```

## Relation to #932

`#937` is the follow-up Security filed on `#932`, and `#932` must not be re-tipped for it. The shipped
change is therefore self-contained: this PR introduces the phrase with its own terminator handling
(`/\bis too long\.?\s*$/i`), so it does not depend on `#932` merging, and `#932`'s branch stays
untouched at `8b4c124c`. `#932`'s pattern is the input this PR narrows from, and the red run above
uses exactly that pattern, so the readings stay comparable. If `#932` lands first, this PR reduces on
rebase to the `\b` → `\.?\s*$` change on the line `#932` introduces, plus the test.

## Reads

Tip `08fc9b7694f03b746f1f332df9d66053aa6503f9` (tree `f37490d96a`), branch
`dev/937-bug-the-is-too-long-client-error-pattern`, base `main` `e4c206d1`. Diff vs `main`: 2 files,
+58/−0 (test +50, product +8).

Ran:

- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts` —
  `# tests 2 / # pass 1 / # fail 1` with `#932`'s pattern (first red); `# tests 5 / # pass 2 / # fail 3`
  with the shape probes against `is too long$` (second red); `# tests 5 / # pass 5 / # fail 0` at this
  tip.
- the payload path scan, applied to the file the binary-release job flagged, with the same
  boundary-anchored `grep -rIlE` shape and needles `build-payload.sh` uses: no match for
  `/home/runner`, `/home/xuke` or `/home/`; the only match is the fixture's neutral `/srv/…` path,
  which is not a needle.
- `cd services/api && npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0 (product; the package config
  excludes `*.test.ts` from the build).
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p .local/tsconfig.937.json --noEmit` — exit 0; a probe config extending
  `tsconfig.tests.json` with `types: ["node"]`, including only
  `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` and its test.
- `git diff --numstat upstream/main..HEAD` — `45 0` test, `8 0` product.
- `node --import tsx .local/probe-937.mts` — the per-message table above, `#932`'s module against this
  tip's module.
- `grep -rn "is too long" --include=*.ts packages services` — the eight legitimate throw sites all
  end with the phrase; the only mid-sentence ones are the two executor throws.
  `packages/model/src/client.ts:279-281` also lists `input is too long` / `prompt is too long`, but those
  are markers for `isModelInputTooLargeError`, a different classifier that additionally requires a
  400/413/422 status.

Not run:

- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (root) in this worktree: it fails on unrelated packages
  because `packages/feedback-worker` has no `node_modules/@sciencediscovery` link here
  (`TS2307 @sciencediscovery/operational-logging/feedback`); the probe config above type-checks the
  changed files with the same settings.
- `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / the E2E layers — CI runs them on this PR.
- A route-level HTTP probe on this head. The dispatch line is unchanged and the classifier is its
  only input; `#932` already carries route-level 400 readings for the same path.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` — two pathological executor failures keep the generic 500 instead of
echoing a filesystem path, while the eight length rejections and their punctuated/newline-terminated
variants still answer 400 with their message.

The label itself needs repository write access, which this fork does not have, so a maintainer has to
apply `release:fix`.

pr:943.body:
Fixes #942

## What happens

In the feedback dialog one multi-select of 10 screenshots attaches 8 (the cap in
`packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts:40`) and says nothing at all: no error, no hint, no count.
`prepareFeedbackImages` left the loop silently, `result.error` stayed `undefined`, so the
`feedback-inline-error` line in `FeedbackDialog.tsx` rendered nothing. The two dropped files were lost
without a word, and the user submitted believing all 10 were attached.

The function's own comment promised the opposite ("stops at the first failure so the dialog can show
the reason instead of silently dropping the rest"): it stopped on failure, but the cap — the far more
common path — dropped the remainder silently.

## Change

Three files, and `apps/web` only.

1. `apps/web/src/feedback-images.ts` — `prepareFeedbackImages` now returns `skipped: number` next to
   `images` (and `error`, unchanged). A pick that does not fit the cap is counted instead of dropped:
   the loop turns the old `break` into a `continue` that counts, so every file still costs no decode.
   This is purely additive: `images` and `error` keep exactly the semantics they had, and an image
   that fails type/decode/size still returns early with its error.
2. `apps/web/src/FeedbackDialog.tsx` — the dialog holds `skippedImages` next to `images` and renders
   one neutral hint (`feedback-hint`, `role="status"`) naming the cap and the count:
   `Only the first 8 screenshots were attached; 2 skipped.` It is **not** the `imageError` slot: that
   slot is keyed by `ImagePrepareError` and describes an image that failed, while this one explains a
   partially successful pick. The count is cleared when the dialog reopens, after a successful
   submit, and when a thumbnail is removed — it always describes the newest pick.
3. `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` — `feedback.images.truncated` in both locales.

The English copy is number-neutral on purpose. The issue's suggested wording
(`…; {skipped} were skipped`) is `1 were skipped` at `skipped: 1`, so this PR uses the number-neutral
`{skipped} skipped` instead: `Only the first {max} screenshots were attached; {skipped} skipped.` reads
correctly for every count, and the Chinese wording (`只附加了前 {max} 张截图，另有 {skipped} 张被跳过。`)
already was.

## Tests

New `apps/web/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` (6 tests). The four acceptance directions, all driven
through a mounted `FeedbackDialog` and its real hidden file input, with only the browser pieces
(`createImageBitmap`, canvas `toBlob`, `FileReader`) stubbed:

1. **at the cap** — pick 10: 8 thumbnails, notice
   `Only the first 8 screenshots were attached; 2 skipped.`
2. **under the cap** — pick 2: 2 thumbnails, no notice at all;
3. **remove then pick** — pick 10 (8 attached), remove one (7 left), pick 2: 8 thumbnails and the
   notice says `1 skipped` — the count describes the newest pick, not the previous one;
4. **both locales** — the zh-CN dialog renders `只附加了前 8 张截图，另有 2 张被跳过。`

Two unit tests keep the pure return value pinned: `skipped === 2` for 10 picks at the cap and
`skipped === 0` for 2 picks under it.

Not covered (coverage boundary, not defects — the code paths exist and behave as written, no test drives
them; follow-up tests are tracked separately, not in this PR): the notice disappears immediately when a
thumbnail is removed (`FeedbackDialog.tsx:323`); an image failure and the truncation notice can render
together when one pick both drops images at the cap and fails one (`:484`/`:488`); reopening the dialog
and a successful submit each reset the count (`:163`/`:288`); and picking once more while already at 8
yields `0 added, 1 skipped`.

## Red first

**1. The missing signal.** Test first, product code untouched, on base `9871f2dd`:

```
$ cd apps/web && ./node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx
not ok 1 - ten picks at the eight-image cap report the two that were skipped
    undefined !== 2
not ok 2 - two picks under the cap report nothing skipped
    undefined !== 0
# tests 2
# pass 0
# fail 2
```

`images.length` was already 8 and 2, so the failing half is exactly the absence of a truncation
signal.

**2. The missing notice.** With the `FeedbackDialog.tsx` change reverted and `skipped` still returned,
the dialog tests fail where the user-visible behaviour is missing:

```
ok 1 - ten picks at the eight-image cap report the two that were skipped
ok 2 - two picks under the cap report nothing skipped
not ok 3 - the dialog names the cap and the dropped count after an over-cap pick
ok 4 - the dialog says nothing extra while every pick fits
not ok 5 - removing a thumbnail frees a slot for exactly one more pick
not ok 6 - the Chinese dialog carries the same notice with its own wording and numbers
# tests 6
# pass 3
# fail 3
```

Test 4 passing there is the point of the test: nothing extra may appear while everything fits.

After both halves: `# tests 6 / # pass 6 / # fail 0`.

## Reads

Tip `8ebaedfabf447a0c23770899f8a87133029c7b7f` (tree `2ce76c1f7a`), branch
`dev1/fix/942-feedback-image-truncation`, base `main` `9871f2dd`. Diff vs `main`: 4 files, +278/−5
(`feedback-images.ts` +11/−5, `FeedbackDialog.tsx` +14, `messages.ts` +2, new test +251).

Ran:

- `cd apps/web && ./node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` —
  `# tests 2 / # pass 0 / # fail 2` red first, `# tests 6 / # pass 6 / # fail 0` at the tip.
- `cd apps/web && ./node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` (the package's own
  `test` script) — `# tests 1250 / # pass 1250 / # fail 0`.
- `cd apps/web && ./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- Rendered-state check: the dialog tests assert the thumbnails, the notice text and its absence
  through `react-test-renderer` on the real component; the hint uses the existing neutral
  `feedback-hint` style and `role="status"`, so it is announced but not styled as an error.

Not run:

- `./.local/typecheck-app-tests.sh apps/web/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` — the probe reports the same
  pre-existing noise every `react-test-renderer` test in this repo produces (`TS2591` for
  `node:assert/strict` without `types: ["node"]`, `TS7016` with no `@types/react-test-renderer`), and
  no gate type-checks `apps/web/tests` (`apps/web/tsconfig.json` includes only `src/**` and
  `vite.config.ts`). Verified by running the same probe on `apps/web/tests/ComputeReadiness.test.tsx`
  and `apps/web/tests/ConfigurationRequestCard.test.tsx` on the base tree: they fail the same way.
- A browser-level E2E journey for the feedback dialog — none exists in the repo for this dialog, and
  the component test above drives the real handler.
- `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / the E2E layers — CI runs them on this PR.

## Scope

`apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts:116` carries a copy of this function with the same
silent cap drop, and its own dialog has the same gap. This change is the `apps/web` face only; the
desktop copy is left untouched and needs the same fix, tracked separately.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` — the feedback dialog now names the eight-image cap and the number of
screenshots it dropped instead of losing them silently.

The label itself needs repository write access, which this fork does not have, so a maintainer has to
apply `release:fix`.

Eleven previously quarantined browser specs now execute as **41 identities** on the shared PR plan. Narrow/mobile, low-height and Composer viewport matrices are retained. ## Preview and journey fixes

Pending results stay out of the cache, completed previews recover normally, old clients retain HTTP 409, and real failures such as HTTP 503 still propagate.

The recorded shell-result fields `workspaceSnapshot` and `workspaceVersion` are retained in the seed streams and explicitly omitted from portable research-package results. The seed regression checks the `*Ref` scope; it does not claim that every agent-state-shaped object is removed. pr:963.body:
The daily and release case table was leaving judge tokens, tool calls, and most session token cells as n/a even when the run had already recorded them. The table reads the staged projection, and that projection keeps only the numbers `executionMeasurements` returns. DeepResearchBench stores each judge call under `evaluation.judge_calls`, and staging then dropped that ledger, so the judge-token column stayed empty. Journeys other than Biomni never recorded a tool-call count at all.

Judge tokens now fall back, after the existing measured sources, to the sum of `evaluation.judge_calls[].usage.total_tokens`. Every recorded call must be a non-negative safe integer. One missing value, or an empty list, leaves the cell empty. There is no partial sum and no invented 0. A value the case already stored in `measurements.judge_tokens` still wins.

Real cases that have a Session collect shared measurements before cleanup, from the same public session API the Web client uses:

- Generated tokens and total tokens come from `GET /api/sessions/:id/usage`, one invocation at a time. If any invocation is not reported, or any of input, output, or total is missing, both cells stay empty. The summary bucket skips unreported calls, so a document that already carries the raw invocation list now follows the same rule instead of publishing that partial bucket.
- Tool calls are distinct `trace.id` values on `tool.started` and `tool.completed`, plus `toolCallId` on tool steps in each subagent stream. PUCT also reads evolve run events. The same id counts once. Model invocation count is never used as a tool count. Every stream read and no tool call records 0. A missing stream, truncated history, a tool event without an id, or a catalog tool step that no stream recorded leaves the cell empty.
- Collection does not throw. It borrows 60 seconds and then returns that time plus the time it actually used, so it cannot turn a passing case into a failure or a failing case into a pass. Duration is still only `generation_duration_ms`. Nothing new is invented from the Playwright timeout.

DeepResearchBench, TC-E2E-01, and PUCT-COMPRESS keep their existing metrics document and only add these numbers. The basic, runner-recovery, inline-card, and J5 journeys write `case-metrics.json`, which contains the plan case id, the tagged key, and the numbers. The staging allowlist and the table's filename match include that name. Two metrics documents for one case still blank the row, so each case keeps one document.

Peak memory, the score column, and the merge gate are unchanged. The score is still only `evaluation.overall_score`, then `total_score`, then `score`. `evaluation.race.overall_score` is still not read. A missing measurement stays n/a and does not fail the case.

Replaying the raw DeepResearchBench metrics from Nightly run 42153537119 through this projection changes only four judge-token cells: DRB-58 739.6K, DRB-59 744.3K, DRB-64 185.1K, and DRB-75 146.6K. Those match the `judge_calls` sums from that run (739606, 744286, 185142, 146570). DRB-62 did not run its evaluation and stays n/a. Score, peak memory, the other cells, and the row counts stay as published. The projected file does not keep `judge_calls` or the prompt. Tool-call counts and the new `case-metrics.json` numbers are not in that old evidence; they show up on the next daily or release run. TC-E2E-01 and PUCT do not write `judge_calls`, so their judge-token cells stay n/a.

A provider-fault retry can already write a second metrics document in another instance directory, and the table then blanks that case. This change does not fix that. A retry of a journey that now writes `case-metrics.json` can blank the new row the same way, which leaves n/a rather than a wrong number.

Follow-up to #850. That issue stays closed.

## Validation

On `6072aee0392ed70873665efc085bec4fdcd65032`:

- `node --test .ci/case-execution.test.mjs`: 10 passed, 0 failed. The new cases cover a complete judge-call sum, a missing call, reported session usage, an unreported call, distinct tool ids, an empty tool stream as 0, a truncated or missing stream as n/a, `case-metrics.json` identity, a second document blanking the row, and a projection that publishes the judge total without the ledger.
- `node --import tsx --test test/helpers/case-measurements.unit.ts`: 2 passed, 0 failed. Collection does not throw, the borrowed timeout is returned, and `case-metrics.json` contains only the identity and the numbers.
- `node --test .ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`: 28 passed, 0 failed, including the new filename on the staging allowlist.

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not re-run for this change. The author also reported `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs` at 128 passed / 0 failed, the tagged daily plan still listing the same 19 real cases, and release listing those 19 plus 50 Biomni L5 cases. This review did not repeat that broader suite or the Nightly artifact replay.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable. There is no new product entry, API, CLI, or Runner behavior. Real cases write one extra numeric metrics document from session APIs that already exist, and a missing number does not change the journey result. No mocked browser journey and no paid real-model run was executed for this change. The pull-request checks still run the usual layers.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: none in the product. The next daily or release case table can show judge tokens, generated tokens, total tokens, and tool calls where the run recorded them. Missing values stay n/a.

Compatibility and migration: none.

pr:964.body:
The desktop app could turn scientific memory on, but there was nothing to do with it: a final report's `[evidence1]` and `[artifact1]` references rendered as literal brackets, and the graph had no surface a reader could reach from the report they were reading. This change makes those references citations the reader can follow, and keeps the one remaining memory surface — the switch — where the reader can act on it. ## A report's citations become chips The alias → node map is persisted on the report version (`references`), and the Markdown reader turns a token only when that map answers for it. `[note]`, an unknown alias, and every report written before the back-fill render as the plain text they are. The transform runs on the mdast tree rather than on rendered text: a chip is a link node carrying `graph://`, so it survives emphasis and line breaks inside a sentence, and the `a` renderer turns it into a button. `urlTransform` lets `graph://` through and still applies the default safety transform to every other URL. Chips travel with the run stream too. The server back-fills `references` onto the persisted message right before `run.completed`, so a live answer and its replay show the same chips instead of the replay falling back to text. ## An artifact citation opens the document, not a record about it An artifact chip opens `ArtifactDialog` over the report: the version the citation pins (not the newest one), with its own picker, and a 溯源 tab. An evidence chip opens the node's own fields — type, locator, confidence, source, recorded time — plus a 溯源 tab with the linear walk the graph recorded: the evidence, the paper or record it came from, the skill that read it, the session that ran it. Neither dialog is a library: closing it leaves the reader in the sentence they were reading. An 上游文件 link inside provenance opens the dependency in the panel beside the dialog instead of replacing the document under the cursor, and the dialog steps aside while the panel is showing it. Pointing the panel anywhere else ends that gesture, so the dialog never keeps an offset for a surface that no longer shows the dependency. ## Settings carries the switch and its state The header capsule polled `/api/health` on a timer whether or not memory was on. It is gone. Whether the service answers is now a line beside 启用科学记忆, read once when the switch turns on, and again only when the reader presses 重新检查. Where the graph is stored stays the memory service's own configuration — the page asks for nothing it does not show. 科学记忆 moves to 智能, after 专家. The line has two readings: 运行正常, or 连接失败. A store that has not been given its credential (a Neo4j deployment's own configuration) used to read 需要密码 here; that named a step no control in this window could take, so it now reads as any other service that is not working, and the state, label and style rule are gone. ## Reading a document twice is a render, not a second read Version bytes are cached module-side per version id, keyed by the client and session, with in-flight reads deduplicated and an LRU cap (24 MB total, 4 MB per entry) so a run of large documents cannot grow without bound. Reopening the artifact dialog, or opening a citation whose dependency is already on screen, issues no second request. The JSON and CSV previews parse once per content instead of once per paint, and `AssistantTurns` is memoised so opening a dialog does not re-parse every answer in the session. ## The memory sidecar can no longer take the stack down `scripts/start-stack.mjs` pins the sidecar's store under the app data directory (an explicit `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_DATA_DIR` still wins), derives its URL from the port this stack binds instead of inheriting a stale one, and degrades to `memoryGraph="degraded"` when the sidecar does not become healthy rather than aborting the whole start. The two behaviours that differ from `start-stack.sh`, and the way back to an existing store, are under Compatibility and migration below. ## Validation **Rebase.** While this pull request was open, `main` advanced 132 commits from `e4c206d1` to `6292b9b2` — 18 of them since the previous rebase point `947d93d0`, touching 58 files (research package, evolve, run-failure cards, MCP and workspace work). The branch was rebased twice; every commit id below is the id from the current rebase. Seven files are touched by both sides — `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`, `app/use-workspace.ts`, `text/en.ts`, `text/zh.ts`, `views/AssistantTurn.tsx`, `views/ConfirmDialog.tsx` and `tests/assistant-turn.test.tsx` — and one of them conflicted: both sides reworked the Escape handling in `ConfirmDialog`, where `main` still runs its hand-rolled `claimsEscape` keydown effect and this branch's `85285d1f` replaces the same effect with `useTopmostEscape(onDismiss)`. The resolution keeps this branch's hook, which is the commit that builds the escape stack, and `main`'s `useState` for the replacement model. Each paragraph's measurement was made on the tree that commit names before the rebase and describes the same content. On the rebased head `772769a6`: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` passes, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes, the desktop unit suite passes 959/959 (`# pass 959`, `# fail 0`, `# skipped 0`), and `pnpm ci:l1` passes 4/4. `git range-diff` maps all 14 commits; only `85285d1f` differs, and that difference is the resolution above. pr:965.body:
## Summary

Part of #835.

This is the independent tool-output trust-boundary slice from the staged landing plan. It introduces category-driven fencing for model-visible untrusted content while preserving raw stored evidence and observer behavior. It does not register Knowledge Engine tools or change kbScope, research state, finish-gate, or agent memory.

### Included

- Per-registry nonces and explicit `untrustedCategory` classification, with legacy-name and MCP-remote fallback behavior.
- Fencing for tool-domain, MCP, remote, and error payloads; only genuine framework-control messages bypass the boundary.
- Durable output sidecars preserving trust and neutralization metadata through line, character, and search readbacks. New records carry an explicit trust format version; pre-metadata records fail closed as untrusted legacy content, while authenticated fence metadata prevents planted fence-shaped tool text from changing durable status or evidence.
- Connector-controlled tool-search results are fenced and neutralized. Model-facing tool descriptions and schema `description`/`title`/`$comment` metadata receive the same protection without changing property identifiers, enum values, or the execution-time schema.
- A shared TypeScript/adapter/durable-store nonce, with native web and subagent history fenced at the actual model-request and dynamic-context rehydration boundaries. Existing fences are unwrapped during hydration only at a legacy anchored position or when framework metadata authenticates the category and nonce; missing trust wiring fails closed.
- Tool identity resolution through assistant `tool_call_id` mappings, including OpenAI tool messages without `name`; platform output is not double-fenced.
- Equivalent native-history handling for JiuwenSwarm housekeeping/default compression requests. Housekeeping selects a provider only when platform-call history proves one unique active run through its `_sd_run`; concurrent runs stay isolated, and finished, foreign, or ambiguous history fails closed instead of borrowing another run's model, credentials, or nonce.
- Framework truncation/readback/failure guidance kept outside untrusted fences, including explicit post-fence overflow notices and durable readback references.
- Final model-message fitting that enforces byte/line limits, truncates only the untrusted body, preserves complete markers, and fails closed when the trust envelope cannot fit.
- Authority-tag neutralization for remote-origin and subagent content, including custom categories and durable `runtime_context_data` wrappers; generic corpus content remains byte-exact except forged fence markers.
- Protected fence semantics and concise answer discipline in prompt `m8.5.1`.

## Validation

In a fresh WSL validation tree:

- Full recursive build: passed.
- Full recursive typecheck, including `tsconfig.tests.json`: passed.
- Tools: **94 passed, 0 failed**.
- Context: **52 passed, 0 failed**.
- Workspace: **101 passed, 0 failed**.
- Native-agent: **44 passed, 0 failed**.
- JiuwenSwarm agent: **111 passed, 0 failed**.
- Adapter non-external suite: **291 passed, 0 failed**; live-gateway and real-model suites are excluded because their external service configuration is not present in the validation tree.
- Full API suite: **1804 passed**; the 9 remaining failures are all environmental in the validation tree (three `services/paper` and one `services/evolve` venv-ENOENT cases, and six Claude/ACP transports that require external credentials and fail identically on a clean `main` checkout).
- Targeted API subagent integration cases: **4 passed, 0 failed**.
- Excluded-feature and scratch-file audit: clean.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

pr:976.body:
`L2 E2E (mocked, research)` failed in CI because one Playwright assertion expected artifact body text (`Recovery succeeded`) in the activity timeline, but the current UI surfaces `read_artifact` results as artifact metadata. This PR updates the test to assert on stable metadata rendered by the tool result instead of volatile content text.

- **Root-cause alignment**
  - In `test/swarm-research-mocked.spec.ts`, the failing check now validates `read_artifact` activity details using artifact identity fields (name + version) rather than recovered body content.

- **Assertion hardening (minimal scope)**
  - Replaced content-string dependency with metadata-based matching:
    - `fixture-sources.md`
    - `"version": 1`
  - Keeps the original behavioral intent (artifact read succeeded and is traceable) while removing UI-format brittleness.

```ts
expect(activity.tools.some((tool) => /read_artifact/.test(tool.summary)
  && /fixture-sources\.md/.test(tool.details)
  && /"version"\s*:\s*1/.test(tool.details))).toBe(true);
```

pr:989.body:
## Summary

Fixes #982: a research continuation whose source session was deleted made the status route answer `404 Session not found` forever, and the desktop poll retried that terminal error every three seconds with no bound. A stale copy also kept overwriting the current conversation's error UI after a session switch.

## Change

**Backend** (`services/api/src/http/index.ts`): the continuation status route now reads the durable operation first — `getContinuation` reads the operation file and still verifies its `sourceSessionId` matches the URL, so ownership is unchanged. A deleted source no longer hides a durable terminal (`failed`/`ready`) operation. The create route (`POST`) still requires the source session.

**Desktop** (`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`): the copy-poll effect now:
- Treats a `404` as terminal: stop polling, clear the stale copy, show a localized `copyMissing`.
- Retries transient failures a bounded 5 times, then clears the copy with a localized `copyPollingFailed`.
- Binds the poll and its status to `copy.sourceSessionId`, so a session switch stops the poll and its error never overwrites the current conversation's UI; the background copy still finishes server-side and is picked up on return.

**Text** (`zh.ts` / `en.ts`): added `researchPackage.copyMissing` and `researchPackage.copyPollingFailed`, localized in both languages.

## Tests

- API: `research-package-http.test.ts` — a finished continuation stays readable after its source session is deleted, and a mismatched source id answers 404.
- Desktop: the copy poll's state machine is extracted to `copyPollStep` and covered by `research-package-copy-poll.test.ts` (404 → `copyMissing`, fifth transient failure → `copyPollingFailed`, success keeps polling). The session-switch ownership is applied in the view (poll bound to `copy.sourceSessionId`).

pr:992.body:
## Summary

Fixes the desktop half of #981: exporting a conversation could leave a persistent `legacy_unavailable` banner.

That string is the adapter's legacy proxy answering `502` with the internal code `legacy_unavailable` when the legacy API it forwards to is briefly unreachable. The desktop client surfaced that raw code as the error message, and the export poll retried it every three seconds with no bound, so the unexplained English code stayed on the page.

## Change

- `apps/desktop/src/api/client.ts`: add `isLegacyUnavailableError(reason)` (status 502 + message `legacy_unavailable`), mirroring `apps/web/src/api/auth.ts`.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`: the export poll now distinguishes outcomes:
  - `404` is terminal: the stale task is marked failed with a localized message (`exportMissing`).
  - `legacy_unavailable` is a transient service failure: show a localized `legacyUnavailable` retrying message, retry at the existing 3 s interval, and stop after 5 consecutive failures.
  - Other transient rejections retry a bounded 5 times, then show `exportPollingFailed`.
- `zh.ts` / `en.ts`: added `legacyUnavailable`, `exportPollingFailed`, `exportMissing`, localized in both languages.
- `apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts`: assert the 502 code is recognised and only for that code.

## Scope

This is the unclear-message + poll-churn half. The export/save interaction redesign and multi-task tracking are tracked separately in #986. The full root cause of *why* the legacy API was unreachable is not diagnosed here, per the issue's own note that this should be captured during reproduction rather than inferred.

pr:993.body:
## Summary

Fixes #984: imported and research-copy sessions allocate a fresh executor session, so JiuwenSwarm — which holds and compresses its own per-session context — starts with no model-visible history. The restored transcript was displayed but never reached the model, so continuing an imported conversation lost the prior context (dialogue-only packages broke the central continuation promise).

## Change

Seed the restored history once, on the first continuation turn, as an equivalent model-context assembly:

- **`history-seed.ts`** folds the gateway history into a bounded, role-labelled block: `user:` / `assistant:` / `tool call:` / `tool result:` ordering is preserved, tool calls are named with their arguments, and a character budget keeps a large transcript from crowding out the turn (the opening user message is kept as an anchor).
- **`jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`** prepends that block to the system prompt only when the run opts in via the new `seedModelContext` flag.
- **`runs/index.ts`** opts the run in when the session has an `imported_snapshot` / `research_copy` snapshot that has not been seeded yet, and marks `researchSnapshot.modelContextSeeded` once the first run completes — so subsequent turns, retries and restarts never duplicate the seed.
- **`packages/schema`** adds the `modelContextSeeded` marker; **`packages/workspace`** adds the `seedModelContext` option.

Native/specialist executors are unaffected: the flag is ignored by the native loop, which already assembles gateway history into its model context.

## Why this shape

JiuwenSwarm 0.2.6's `chat.send` contract has no history/messages field, and its session context lives only in-process (its own `warmup_session_context` reads its own `history.jsonl`, which SD's restored transcript never enters; there is no external history-write RPC). A cross-repo `history.seed` patch is the heavier alternative; this PR delivers the "equivalent model-context assembly" the issue allows, entirely on the SD side.

## Tests

- `history-seed.test.ts` covers role ordering/labelling, tool call/result recognition, budget bounding with the anchor, and empty/irrelevant-message handling.
- The issue's acceptance criteria (synthetic fact recall + first-model-request inspection, source present/deleted/clean destination, essential/full exports, no duplication on retry/restart, prefix-only branches inherit upstream) remain an end-to-end check I did not run here; the code path is unit-covered.

A Project row keeps its `+` and `⋯` controls behind the fold's own name. The
toggle is a flex item, and a button's automatic minimum size is its content, so
a name longer than the column made the toggle lay out past the row instead of
shrinking. The controls were pushed outside the column, which clips horizontal
overflow, and became unreachable: neither hover nor keyboard focus nor the open
Project could reveal them. A Session row never had this problem because its
button already sets `min-width: 0`; the Project toggle was missing the same
line.

## The toggle can shrink

`.side-row.side-project .side-project-toggle` now carries `min-width: 0`.
Nothing else changes: the label's existing ellipsis starts working, so a long
name ends in `…` inside the row, and the existing hover, `:focus-within` and
active rules reveal `+` and `⋯` within the row's box instead of beyond it. The
full name stays in the button's tooltip, and double-click rename is unaffected.
