row carries no controls at all, even while hovered; the chevron is pushed off
the row too. In the "after" shots the name ends in `…` and the chevron, `+` and
`⋯` all sit inside the row's right edge.

## Coverage

A mocked desktop e2e case renders a Project with a 72-character name and
asserts that the label computes `text-overflow: ellipsis` and has
`scrollWidth > clientWidth`, that both controls are hidden at rest, and that
hover brings them back inside the row's bounding box. Without the CSS line the
case fails at the truncation assertion, so the regression is caught rather than
described.

## Validation

Run on commit 58a78978.

- Desktop package unit tests (`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`):
  821 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Desktop mocked e2e (`apps/desktop/e2e/projects.spec.ts`): 4 passed, 0 failed.
- UT layer (`pnpm ci:ut`): planned 6587, executed 6558, passed 6545, failed 13,
  skipped 0. All 13 failures reproduce with identical counts on unmodified
  `main` (5033f026) in a separate detached worktree, so none is introduced by
  this change. They are host conditions:
  - `services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts` (5) and
    `services/launcher/src/source-evolve.test.ts` (5): a stray
    `/tmp/package.json` outside the repository declares `"type": "module"`, so
    the CommonJS `dist/server.js` the launcher spawns is treated as ESM.
  - `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` (1): the trajectory
    database cannot be opened in this host's temporary directory.
  - `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` (1): the host bubblewrap
    rejects `--disable-userns`, an option the sandbox test passes.
  - `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs` (1): the interrupt simulation restores
    its mirror on this host instead of reproducing the interrupted write.
- ST layer (`pnpm ci:st`): planned 51, executed 51, passed 49, failed 2. Both
  failures are local provisioning, not the change: the JiuwenSwarm SDK check
  could not install `chromadb` because the run was pinned offline against a
  cache that predates it, and the Evolve distribution journey downloads the
  pinned Python runtime and source from the network, which the same offline
  run blocked.

### CI on this head

Run `42477401587` on `58a78978` is green: `L1`, `UT`, `Coverage`,
`CodeCheck (GitCode)`, `ST` (51 of 51), all five mocked shards, and
`merge-gate`. `L3`/`L4`/`L5`, `Binary release` and `Docker image` are skipped
by the pull-request profile.

Four earlier runs on the same head were red for reasons outside this diff:
GitHub's release download host was answering `502`/`504`, so
`test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` could not fetch the pinned
`python-build-standalone` runtime, `astral-sh/setup-uv@v6` could not install
`uv`, and `standard-config` reported `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready
(failed: micromamba setup failed)`. The same failures hit unrelated pull
requests in the same window — `fix/jiuwenswarm-skill-authority-896` (run
`42468248524`) and `fix-986-export-save-dialog` (run `42470653800`) — and
`main` at `239dde7d` (run `42465227603`). The green run was triggered once the
host was stable; nothing in the diff changed between it and the red runs.

## E2E user journeys

PASS — local, mocked, tested commit 58a78978 on
`fix/desktop-long-project-name`. Browser: desktop Chromium via
`apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts`.

- A Project with a 72-character name → the name is ellipsized inside the row,
  both controls are hidden at rest, and hovering reveals `+` and `⋯` inside
  the row → PASS.
- Existing Project journeys in the same spec (rename through a reload, delete
  with confirmation, delete the Project of the open Session) → PASS.

Totals: 4 passed / 0 failed / 0 blocked / 0 skipped.

**The desktop shell is deliberately out of CI.** `apps/desktop/e2e` is not
referenced by any workflow in `.github/workflows` or `.ci`; the mocked matrix
drives `apps/web`, which needs the Python control plane, and its fixture puts a
project, a token and a model in place before a spec starts — the opposite of a
desktop journey, which has to begin from an empty workspace. Keeping the suite
local is the design, not an oversight, so this evidence is reported as local
rather than as a CI gate. Wiring the desktop shell into the matrix would be its
own change.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
GitHub label: `release:fix` is pending a maintainer — this fork has no write
access to apply labels, so the category is stated here instead.
User impact: A Project whose name does not fit the column now shows a
truncated name with `…` and keeps its `+` (new session in the Project) and `⋯`
(rename/delete) controls reachable on hover, keyboard focus or when the
Project is active.
Compatibility and migration: none.

pr:999.body:
Fixes #986

## What changed

### Desktop shell (`win_desktop`)
- New export IPC: a native "save as" dialog that remembers the last chosen directory and asks before overwriting (`sd-shell:export-save-dialog`), a write bound to that destination (`sd-shell:export-write`), open-file-location (`sd-shell:export-show-in-folder`) and the OS downloads dir (`sd-shell:export-downloads-dir`).
- **The renderer never handles a filesystem path.** The dialog issues an opaque token, the main process keeps the chosen path (`ExportDestinations`), and the write/reveal handlers accept only that token — a token this process did not issue is refused. Renderer code therefore cannot address a file the user did not pick, so the window's `sandbox`/`contextIsolation` isolation is not bypassed.
- Exposed as `window.sdShell.exportFile` in the preload; `lastExportDir` is persisted (`export-state.json`) so the next export defaults to the last used folder.

### Desktop export flow (`apps/desktop`)
- **Choose the destination first**: confirming export opens the native save dialog (default name `会话标题_YYYYMMDD_HHmm.sdresearch`, default folder = last used folder, else the OS downloads folder). Cancelling the dialog aborts the export without starting a packaging task.
- **Automatic save**: once packaging completes, the archive is written to the chosen destination automatically — no second Download click.
- **Independent exports**: each export keeps its own task id, destination and result; starting a second export no longer overwrites the first's tracking.
- **Unobtrusive feedback**: small bottom-page text shows "N exports in progress" (expandable, each task cancellable); a green/red completion flash appears for a few seconds and disappears on its own, with an "open file location" action. Cancel is offered only while the server task can still be cancelled; a cancel that races completion keeps the finished package and saves it.
- The export dialog keeps a persistent "saved packages" list with open-location and retry-save (a save failure reuses the already-generated archive rather than repackaging).

### API
- `POST /api/projects/{id}/research-package/exports/{task}/cancel` plus a `canceled` terminal state. Cancellation is re-checked after the archive is written and during packaging, so a cancelled export never leaves or advertises a package.

### Browser fallback
In a plain browser (no Electron shell) there is no pre-packaging native save dialog; the supported equivalent is a browser download after packaging completes, through the browser's own save prompt, keeping the same automatic-save-on-completion behaviour. Multiple concurrent exports each keep their own entry.

## Screenshots

Captured on a Windows dev checkout at head `d466d61e` (before the destination-token binding and the flash-timer fix; the visible flow is unchanged, and the completion flash now auto-dismisses after ~4 s instead of staying until a refresh).

**1. Native save dialog, opened before any packaging starts** (title 导出研究包, folder 下载, name 脓毒症内型评分聚类分析_20261108_1858, type ScienceDiscovery 研究包):

![Save dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-986/pr-999/01-save-dialog.png)

**2. Packaging in progress — small bottom-page text:**

![Export in progress](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-986/pr-999/02-export-in-progress.png)

**3. Saved automatically — green completion flash with 打开文件位置:**

![Export saved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-986/pr-999/03-export-saved.png)

**4. Same-name collision asks before replacing:**

![Overwrite confirmation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-986/pr-999/04-overwrite-confirm.png)

### Runtime verification (Windows native dev checkout, base main `239dde7d`)
- `pnpm build` and the shell build pass.
- Save dialog opens before a task exists; cancelling it (ESC / 取消 / 否 on overwrite) starts no export task and creates no file.
- Confirmed exports write without a second click: necessary 965 KB, complete 3.2 MB — consistent with the preview estimate.
- 打开文件位置 opens Explorer at the saved file.
- Choosing an existing file asks 确认另存为; answering 否 leaves the original untouched (mtime unchanged).
- The last directory round-trips through `<userData>/export-state.json`.
- Two cosmetic notes, not defects: Windows hides the matching extension in the name field while the file is written with `.sdresearch`; the in-progress line and a just-finished flash can overlap for one render.

## Tests
- `win_desktop/test/export-tokens.test.ts`: destination issuance, refusal of an unissued token, written marking, eviction.
- `win_desktop/test/export-state.test.ts`: last-directory persistence.
- `services/api/src/research-package-exports.test.ts`: cancelled queued/running exports never produce a download, and a late cancel leaves a finished package downloadable.
- `apps/desktop/tests/research-package.test.ts`: cancel + archive-blob client coverage.
- `apps/desktop/e2e/research-package.spec.ts`: updated for automatic save and completion feedback.

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Three review findings from #870, #878 and #888 are real but cannot ride those pull requests without invalidating approvals they already hold, so they are recorded here instead of being lost when the threads close. Each item names the file and line on `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`.

## 1. `#870` — the leftovers test matches the sentinel on the error message only

`services/api/src/store-replace-cleanup.test.ts:107`

`await assert.rejects(writeRun(store, sessionId), /sentinel-rename/)` matches only the thrown error's own `message`. Test A in the same file (`:88`) deliberately concatenates `error.cause?.message`, test B does not. Today `writeArray` still calls plain `rename` (`services/api/src/store.ts:2159`), so the mock's `EPERM` carries the sentinel in its own message and the assertion passes.

Once #857 replaces that call with `renameReplace`, the thrown error is a `FileReplaceError` whose message is `Could not replace <dest> after 20 attempts (EPERM)` and whose sentinel lives only in `cause`, so this test fails for the wrong reason. The fix is to assert `cause.message`, or `error.name === "FileReplaceError"` plus the sentinel, the same way test A does.

## 2. `#878` — the "unexpected status" toast test never reaches the fallback branch

`apps/web/tests/QueuedCancelToast.test.ts:50`

`interrupted` is terminal (`isTerminalRunStatus`, `apps/web/src/run-stream/model.ts:127`), so `queuedCancelToast("interrupted", t)` returns `app.queuedCancelOutcome.finished` and the assertion `assert.match(toast.title, /更新|结束/)` passes on the terminal branch. Of the seven statuses only `queued` reaches `app.queuedCancelOutcome.statusDetail`, and that branch has no `detail`, so `/undefined/` can never appear either. A regression that drops `{ status }` from `statusDetail` stays green.

Coverage only — no user-visible defect.

## 3. `#878` — the fallback detail interpolates a raw enum token

`apps/web/src/run-stream/model.ts:145`

`t("app.queuedCancelOutcome.statusDetail", { status })` prints the raw value, so an unexpected status renders `当前状态：queued` in the Chinese UI — the same mixed-language outcome #871 was filed about, one layer deeper. The catalog has one status label today (`app.queued` = "Queued" / "排队中", `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:2516` and `:5482`). The sentence also hard-codes the Stop button's name (`messages.ts:2520`, `:5486`) instead of interpolating `composer.stop` (`messages.ts:406`).

## 4. `#888` — the desktop tool card keeps the English headings

`apps/desktop/src/app/tool-io.ts:60-63`, `apps/desktop/src/views/ToolCard.tsx:128`, `apps/desktop/src/text.ts`

The web card localises `Result` / `Error` / `Created files` / `Produced artifacts` in #888, but the desktop shell renders the same card from its own parser markers and its own catalog, so a zh-CN user in the desktop app keeps the English headings next to `输入`-style ones. #885 as filed only names the web card; localising the desktop twin is a separate change with its own catalog.

## Expected behaviour

1. `store-replace-cleanup.test.ts` asserts the sentinel through `cause` (or on `error.name`), so it fails for the right reason after #857.
2. `QueuedCancelToast.test.ts` drives a status that actually reaches `app.queuedCancelOutcome.statusDetail` and asserts the rendered detail.
3. The fallback detail maps the status through the existing run-status labels and interpolates the Stop label from `composer.stop`.
4. The desktop tool card localises the four headings from its own catalog, with the same zh-CN strings the web card now uses.

## 5. `#868` and `#887` each carry a copy of the reserved-name predicate — fold them into one when the second lands

`#866` (PR `#868`) added `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` inside `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts`; `#887` (PR `#890`) added the same predicate in
`packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts`, exported through the package index, because on the base the sanitizer had no reserved-name branch at all.

Both PR bodies say "whichever merges second folds the copy into `sanitizeUploadFilename`". That sentence is not a work item, so it is recorded here:
after both land, `workspace-upload.ts` should call the exported helper and drop its inline copy, and the superscript-digit class
(`com[1-9¹²³]` / `lpt[1-9¹²³]`) must be the same in both spellings while the copy still exists.

Expected: one predicate in `packages/workspace`, one call site in the sanitizer, no second regex in `services/api`, and the reject lists in
`workspace-upload.test.ts` and the workspace package tests agreeing.

## 6. The setup wizard's GB tier is the top of the ladder, so a free disk at or above ~1024 GiB prints `1024.0GB`

`apps/desktop/src/views/SetupWizard.tsx:127-128`

`scaledSize(size, printed, 4)` stops at unit 3 and the terminal branch prints `value.toFixed(1) + "GB"` with no further level, so the rule the
#879 rewrite enforces ("the unit follows the number that is printed") has no answer at the top: `formatWizardFreeSpace(1024 ** 4)` → `"1024.0GB"`,
`formatWizardFreeSpace(2 * 1024 ** 4)` → `"2048.0GB"`, switching at `1_099_457_940_685` bytes (1023.95 GiB, the first value whose one-decimal GB
rounds to 1024.0).

This is **pre-existing**, not introduced by #879/#880 — the base printed the same above 1 GiB — so it does not block that fix; it is a product call:

- add a TB tier so the ladder ends at `1.0TB`, or
- accept `1024.0GB` above 1 TiB and say so in the doc comment.

Expected: one of the two, decided explicitly, with the reading at and just below `1_099_457_940_685` pinned in `apps/desktop/tests/size-boundary.test.ts`.

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
## What happens

`apps/web/tests/` holds 126 `*.test.ts` / `*.test.tsx` files, and no TypeScript configuration in the repository includes any of them. The suite runs under `tsx`, which strips the annotations without checking them; the package `typecheck` and the root test type-check both look elsewhere. A type error in a web test therefore cannot turn CI red: `pnpm typecheck` — the `check:typecheck` gate — stays green.

## Where

1. `apps/web/package.json:9` — `"test": "tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx"`. `tsx` transpiles and runs; it does not type-check.
2. `apps/web/tsconfig.json:9` — `"include": ["src/**/*.ts", "src/**/*.tsx", "vite.config.ts"]`. The package's `typecheck` script (`apps/web/package.json:10`, `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`) therefore cannot see `tests/`.
3. `tsconfig.tests.json:23-28` — its `include` names `packages/*/src/**/*.test.ts(x)` and `services/*/src/**/*.test.ts(x)` only. Its own comment (`tsconfig.tests.json:13-15`) states: "`apps/web` is not here: its tests sit in `tests/`, which its own `include` (`src/**`) never reached, so the base exclude takes nothing away from it." The root `typecheck` script (`package.json:51`) ends with `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`, so the one configuration meant to own test files leaves the web tests out on purpose.

CI runs that script as `check:typecheck` (`test/support/tagged/checks.mjs:23` → `pnpm typecheck`), so this is a hole in a required gate, not just in a local command.

## Measured on `main` at `5c893570`

- 126 files match `apps/web/tests/*.test.ts(x)` (git tree).
- `tsc -p apps/web/tsconfig.json --listFilesOnly` lists 0 files under `apps/web/tests/`.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --listFilesOnly` lists 0 files under `apps/web/tests/` (1,805 files listed in total).
- A throwaway config extending `apps/web/tsconfig.json` with `"exclude": []` and `"include": ["tests/**/*.test.ts", "tests/**/*.test.tsx"]` lists exactly the 126 files and reports 444 `error TS` diagnostics across 71 files (10 in `.test.ts`, 434 in `.test.tsx`). Those diagnostics are latent today; nothing in CI can see them.

## How to reproduce

1. Append `const notAString: string = 42;` to any `apps/web/tests/*.test.ts`.
2. `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` — exits 0: `tsx` runs the file and never checks the annotation.
3. `pnpm typecheck` — still exits 0: neither configuration includes the file.

## Suggested fix

Give the web tests an owner and a gate:

- Add `apps/web/tsconfig.tests.json` extending `apps/web/tsconfig.json` with `"exclude": []` and `"include": ["tests/**/*.test.ts", "tests/**/*.test.tsx"]`, and run it from the package `typecheck` (or from the root `typecheck` right after `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`). Adding `apps/web/tests/**` to the root `tsconfig.tests.json` include is the alternative, but that config extends `tsconfig.base.json`, not the web package's settings, so it would need the jsx / DOM / `vite/client` options that belong to `apps/web` — a second config is the cleaner shape.
- The 444 existing diagnostics have to be fixed for the gate to pass. If that is too large for one change, stage it: enable `tests/**/*.test.ts` first (10 diagnostics) and `tests/**/*.test.tsx` (434) in a follow-up. Enabling the config while it reports errors leaves the gate red and is not mergeable.

Acceptance: with the new config wired into `pnpm typecheck`, the deliberate `const notAString: string = 42;` makes `pnpm typecheck` (and therefore `check:typecheck`) fail naming that file and line, while `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` keeps its current behaviour.

closed_recent.author: HugoXK
closed_recent.body:
## What happens

A delimited dataset preview is capped at `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS = 1_001` columns and `MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS = 100` rows, and the payload reports what left the preview (`clippedColumns {total, shown}`, `clippedCells`, `warnings`). The viewer renders that report only through `DatasetTable` — and `.csv` artifacts never render `DatasetTable`.

## Where (at `981fdf51`, the merge commit of `#830`)

- `apps/web/src/csvArtifact.ts:73-82` — `detectCsvArtifact` sends every `.csv` name, `text/csv` media type or CSV-looking content to the CSV viewer.
- `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:874` — `artifact?.kind === "dataset" && csvDetection && !(structureFormat && source)` renders `CsvArtifactPreview` (`:205`), not the dataset table.
- `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:831-832` — `clippedCells` / `clippedColumns` are passed only to `DatasetTable` (`:239`, meta line at `:254`).
- `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` — the JSON record-array path always returns `clippedCells: 0` and `clippedColumns {shown: total}`, so `.tsv` (and generally delimited content that is not detected as CSV) is the only kind whose clipped numbers reach a reader.

## Measured

- A `.csv` artifact with 200,001-field lines: the API preview comes back `1001` columns / `clippedColumns {shown: 1001, total: 200001}`, and the artifact panel shows only the "open CSV workspace" card — none of the new text, because the CSV workspace parses the source client-side.
- The same content saved as `.tsv`: `DatasetTable` renders `1 row (showing 1001 of 200001 columns) (N cells past the preview width are not shown)`.

## Why it matters

`#830`'s stated contract is that clipping "is reported, not silent" — and for the most common delimited artifact kind (`.csv`) the reader is told nothing. The new i18n strings (`artifact.tableClippedColumns`, `artifact.tableClippedCells`) and the two props have no reachable CSV path.

## Suggested fix

Either pass the clipped numbers into `CsvArtifactPreview` / the CSV workspace window and render the same meta line there, or render the dataset table for a CSV artifact whose payload was clipped. One signal per loss, no duplicate sentences; keep the CSV workspace's own surplus-column handling (`csv.importSurplusColumns`) separate from this panel-level notice.

Related: `#839` (the width rule that creates the mismatch), `#840` (the payload `warnings` field has no consumer), `#841` (`maxRows` / column-cap contract for outside API callers).

closed_recent.body:
## Problem

In the Chinese activity panel, a reminder's state still prints as a raw English token, and the same holds for the transfer file-progress rows.

- `AgentActivity.timers[].state` is `"pending" | "fired" | "cancelled"` (`apps/web/src/api/runs.ts:40`)
- `STATE_KEYS` (`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:34-41`) only covers the execution vocabulary (`queued|running|completed|failed|cancelled|unknown`), and `stateLabel` falls back to the raw token when a key is missing (`:54-57`)
- so a reminder that has not fired renders `pending` inside an otherwise Chinese panel, and after it fires, `fired`; `cancelled` is named because it happens to share the execution vocabulary.

The same gap applies to the transfer file rows, whose per-file progress states are outside the eight keys `#925` enumerated.

## Where it came from

Raised twice on `#929`/`#927` review rounds (`sciencediscovery-bot` at 2026-11-05T13:49:27Z, confirmed still reproducing at `0da863ea` at 15:38:57Z, and `agent-ci-infra-bot` F2 at 15:58:53Z). `#925` deliberately bounded itself to eight keys; this issue is the slice that was left out, not an oversight in that PR.

## Suggested fix

A separate `TIMER_STATE_KEYS` map (so `pending` keeps its execution meaning intact) plus the transfer file-progress keys, both going through `stateLabel`. Values live in the existing `activity.*` section of `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`; the badge `className` keeps the raw token for styling and comparisons.

## Acceptance

1. zh-CN and en both name `pending`, `fired` and the transfer file-progress states; no raw token is visible in either locale.
2. `fired` has its own unit assertion — it is the state a reader sees long after the dialog closed.
3. The badge `className` still carries the raw token (no test may assert localized text through the class).
4. An unknown value outside both maps still renders its raw token (no blanking).

## Summary

On 2026-10-26 every GitHub issue in `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` was classified against the nine requirement rows in #249. Pull requests were excluded. The three counts agreed: `gh issue list --state all`, REST pagination of 100 items per page, and the issue search counter. The total is **232** issues, **116 open** and **116 closed**.

Whether an issue is developed was judged from `origin/main` at `65eddde1`, not from the open or closed flag. An open issue can already be on `main`. A closed issue can still be undeveloped when it was closed as a duplicate or as not planned, or when the change never reached `main`.

This issue records that snapshot. It does not close, retitle, or implement any of the issues below.

## Counts

| | |
| --- | --- |
| bug / feature / other | 73 / 151 / 8 |
| bug severity P0 / P1 / P2 / P3 | 1 / 24 / 44 / 4 |
| mapped to a #249 row / unmapped | 139 / 93 |
| developed / partial / not developed / not applicable | 103 / 39 / 82 / 8 |
| marked complex | 122 |

Severity is the impact of the defect itself. It is not lowered because a later commit fixed it. "Not applicable" is used only for the eight items in **other**, which have no defect or feature to build. "Complex" means the work crosses modules, depends on an external system, or packs several independent pieces into one issue.

## Rules

1. An issue maps to one of the nine names in the #249 table, or to **unmapped**.
2. Issues already closed before the 2026-10-10 v0.3.0 kickoff stay unmapped, even when the topic matches a row. An issue closed on 2026-10-10 counts as inside the cycle. This rule sets aside 20 topic matches: CI engineering refactor 4, componentized architecture 10, documentation and website 5, routine bug fixes 1. Those four counts are part of the snapshot. The 20 issue numbers are not listed separately.
3. A feature maps by topic and never lands in Routine bug fixes.
4. A bug in behavior that a requirement row delivers maps to that row. Other bugs inside the release cycle map to Routine bug fixes.
5. A defect in the test or CI harness (a wrong gate, lost end-to-end evidence, broken test discovery) maps to CI engineering refactor. A product defect that CI happened to catch still maps to Routine bug fixes.
6. **Other** is a calendar, a call for release-note feedback, a discussion, or a usage question. #249 itself is other and unmapped: it is the calendar that holds the table.
7. Developed means the requested behavior is on `origin/main` at `65eddde1`. Evidence is a merge that is an ancestor of that commit, or a path on that commit. Early pull requests, roughly #3 through #111, were rewritten out of that ancestry and were checked by subject or by path. A number in an older write-up that is actually a GitCode id was not treated as a GitHub pull request.
8. Closed as duplicate or not planned stays **not developed**, even when the same behavior later arrived through another issue.
   - #405 was closed as a duplicate of #406. The behavior landed with #406 in pull request #407. #405 stays not developed.
   - #327 was closed as not planned and superseded by #330. The behavior landed with #330 in pull request #356. #327 stays not developed.

## Severity that is already on main

The only P0 is #371, MCP TypeScript SDK 1.30.0 below the OAuth credential-binding fix. It is closed and developed: pull request #374 is an ancestor of `65eddde1`, and `services/api` resolves `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` to 1.31.0. #369 (undici below 8.10.2; `main` has 8.12.2) and #370 (katex below 0.18.2; `main` has 0.18.10, including the copy brought in by rehype-katex) are P1, and both are also developed in #374. ## Open bugs not fully on that main commit

These GitHub issues were still open on 2026-10-26, and the requested behavior was not fully present on `65eddde1`.

**P1**

- #471 A project cannot be deleted. Not developed. Also in the uncertain list below.
- #519 Nightly session-title assertion, failed-shard accounting, and two unit-test timeouts. Partial.
- #541 An unconfirmed shell observation is stored as a failed execution run. Not developed.
- #557 The assessment-screening skill references `rubric-overall.md`, which does not exist. Not developed.

**P3**

- #429 Dataset table cells are right-aligned under left-aligned headers. Not developed.
- #505 One bad server-sent event frame ends the desktop run stream. Not developed.
- #558 The report-writer skill has an unmatched code fence, and `skills/` is outside the markdownlint globs. Not developed.
- #559 Skill-package validation accepts an empty description that the docs forbid. Not developed.

#423 was still open, rated P2, and already developed on `65eddde1` (`pnpm ci:ut` no longer stops before discovery because the JiuwenSwarm patch target is missing). #210 was still open, rated P1, and already developed (the local memory-graph folded-subgraph query is bounded).

## Could not judge developed or not

- #170 Literature-research handoffs. The issue states a direction and does not give acceptance criteria, so a skill-text instruction to resume is not enough to call it done. Counted as partial under recovery of failed long-running tasks.
- #398 NPU task recovery. Pull request #542 reconciles remote execution in general. Whether that is a partial landing of the NPU requirement needs the owner. Counted as partial.
- #452 The report does not include the version, the second connection error, or a root cause, so later model-setting changes on `main` cannot be shown to fix it. Counted as not developed.
- #471 Deleting a project fails, without the failing request or a server stack. It is not possible to tell a fix on `main` from an old build or a WSL2-only failure. Counted as not developed.

## Other

These eight have no deliverable defect or feature. Development status is not applicable, and all eight are unmapped.

- #1 How to obtain the binary package. Answered as a usage question.
- #48 Feedback comparing this project with other 2026 science workbenches.
- #107 Call for end-to-end scenarios the community wants protected. The issue itself specifies no implementation.
- #213 JiuwenSwarm beta release notes and feedback. Closed as superseded by #343.

- #249 October 2026 release calendar.

# 中文版

## 版本定位

ScienceDiscovery **`0.3.0-rc1`** 与 [`0.3.0-beta`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/releases/tag/0.3.0-beta) 同属 **0.3.0 正式版前的预发布版本**：在既有 JiuwenSwarm 科研工作台能力之上，继续收敛质量与工程化交付，为正式版做候选验证。

上一版本为 `0.3.0-beta`（2026-09-30）。本版本汇总 **2026-10-01 → 2026-10-16**（Asia/Shanghai）已合并进 `main` 的变更。

> 本文是面向社区征求意见的 **Release Note 草案**，不是正式发版公告；正式 GitHub Release / tag 将另发。

## Release Note 草案

### 新功能

- **L1–L5 多级 CI 门禁**：按 PR → merge → daily → release 分层累积质量检查，Nightly/Release 真实 E2E 与 hermetic 检查并行落地（#259，相关 #280、#255、#258）。

### 主要修复

- **沙箱 / Runner 未就绪**：启动与 Runner 就绪解耦；执行仍 fail-closed；Agent 可通过 `check_runner` / `wait_for_runner` 等待，并弹出重试/切换/取消恢复卡片；区分「展示等待」与「授权修复」（#275 / #265，#282）。
- **不可解析 tool call**：长科研 run 中改为扣留并恢复，不再误报为模型配置错误并整段结束主/子 Agent（#247 / #236）。
- **自定义模型设置**：任一设置接口失败时保留 provider 预设，避免 Custom provider 空表单卡死（#288 / #281）。
- **交付签收**：接受带可选章节号的 Methods/Results/References，避免临近预算误触发重写（#294 / #292）。
- **产物提交**：CAS ref commit 复用已校验对象元数据，降低长轨迹提交开销（#250；#230 仍开）。
- **真实 E2E 稳定化**：J5 等待托管 Python（#287 / #286）；主 Agent run 链完成后再做终局断言（#253）；中断时保留已完成旅程证据（#266 / #263）；Nightly flaky 断言（#207、#279）；L3 改为真实用户旅程（#272）。
- **CI 配套**：job 重跑覆盖同名 artifact（#302 / #301）；分数与诊断产物分离（#240）；Mock E2E 四 worker、UT 并行等（#273、#277、#268、#242）；Biomni DA-13-3 / DA-14-1 恢复进 daily/release，Nightly 结构化挂载 `science-research-team`（#270、#306）。

### 行为变更

- 启动不再强依赖本地沙箱可用；未就绪时执行被拒绝，需经恢复流程后再下发（#275）。
- Nightly Biomni 挂载 `science-research-team` 后，分数不可与 beta 裸题基线直接对比（#306）。

<details>
<summary>已合并 PR（28）</summary>

#207 #240 #242 #243 #244 #247 #250 #253 #255 #256 #258 #259 #266 #268 #270 #272 #273 #275 #277 #279 #280 #282 #287 #288 #294 #300 #302 #306

</details>

## 社区反馈

欢迎在本 Issue 讨论：

- 草案表述是否清楚、是否遗漏重要合入
- RC1 作为正式版前候选，你最关心的验证场景
- 文案、分类或中英对照的改进建议

请尽量附上复现步骤、日志或相关 PR/Issue 链接。

# English version

## Release positioning

ScienceDiscovery **`0.3.0-rc1`**, like [`0.3.0-beta`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/releases/tag/0.3.0-beta), is a **pre-release ahead of the formal 0.3.0**. It builds on the existing JiuwenSwarm scientific workbench and continues to tighten quality and delivery engineering as a release candidate.

The previous version is `0.3.0-beta` (2026-09-30). This draft covers changes merged into `main` from **2026-10-01 through 2026-10-16** (Asia/Shanghai).

> This is a **community draft** for feedback, not a formal release announcement. The GitHub Release / tag will be published separately.

## Draft release notes

### New features

- **L1–L5 multi-level CI gates**: layered quality checks across PR → merge → daily → release, with Nightly/Release real E2E alongside hermetic checks (#259; related #280, #255, #258).

### Major fixes

- **Sandbox / Runner not ready**: decouple workbench startup from Runner readiness; execution remains fail-closed; the Agent can wait via `check_runner` / `wait_for_runner` and present retry / switch / cancel recovery cards; distinguish “show waiting UI” from “authorize repair” (#275 / #265, #282).
- **Unparseable tool calls**: hold and recover during long research runs instead of misreporting a model-configuration error and killing the main or sub-Agent (#247 / #236).
- **Custom model settings**: keep provider presets when any settings request fails, avoiding a stuck empty Custom provider form (#288 / #281).
- **Deliverable acceptance**: accept Methods/Results/References headings with optional section numbers so near-budget rewrites are not triggered incorrectly (#294 / #292).
- **Artifact commits**: reuse validated object metadata on the CAS ref-commit path to cut long-trajectory commit cost (#250; #230 remains open).
- **Real E2E stabilization**: wait for managed Python on J5 (#287 / #286); assert only after the main Agent run chain completes (#253); retain completed-journey evidence on interrupt (#266 / #263); Nightly flaky assertions (#207, #279); L3 as real user journeys (#272).
- **CI follow-ups**: overwrite same-named artifacts on job re-run (#302 / #301); separate score and diagnostic artifacts (#240); Mock E2E four workers and UT parallelism (#273, #277, #268, #242); restore Biomni DA-13-3 / DA-14-1 to daily/release and structurally attach `science-research-team` on Nightly (#270, #306).

### Behavior changes

- Startup no longer requires a ready local sandbox; execution is rejected until recovery completes (#275).
- After Nightly Biomni attaches `science-research-team`, scores are not directly comparable to the beta bare-prompt baseline (#306).

#207 #240 #242 #243 #244 #247 #250 #253 #255 #256 #258 #259 #266 #268 #270 #272 #273 #275 #277 #279 #280 #282 #287 #288 #294 #300 #302 #306

</details>

## Community feedback

Please comment on this issue with:

- Whether the draft is clear or missing important merges
- Scenarios you care most about validating for RC1
- Wording, categorization, or bilingual improvements

Include repro steps, logs, or related PR/issue links when possible.

## 🚀 Background Description

The desktop app (`apps/desktop`) does not support scientific memory yet. In the new UI, readers cannot follow a citation in the final report to the evidence or artifact behind it, and cannot configure scientific memory in settings. The old web UI already has the full capability: citations in a report are clickable, evidence and artifacts show their details and provenance, and scientific memory is configurable.

This issue asks for the same capability in the desktop app, without a graph view: after a literature review run (see `docs/zh/domains/literature-research.md`), clicking `[evidenceN]` / `[artifactN]` in the final report opens the evidence/artifact card with its details and provenance.

Related documents:

- Literature research sample: `docs/zh/domains/literature-research.md`
- Scientific memory setup: `docs/zh/advanced-setup/science-memory-setup.md`
- Scientific memory design: `docs/zh/developer-docs/science-memory.md`

## Design Ideas

- **Settings › Scientific memory**: a new settings group with an enable switch, storage backend (local / Neo4j), Neo4j endpoint and user, write-only password, and the current status.
- **Report citations**: `[alias]` tokens in a final report render as clickable chips. A chip shows only the alias the report wrote; no extra "evidence" / "artifact" wording.
- **Press a chip**: open a card with "Details" and "Provenance" tabs.
  - Evidence provenance keeps only the literature source, matching the old UI's `EvidenceModal`: a paper card with title, abstract, and link.
  - Artifact provenance follows the old UI's provenance tab: derived from (parent artifacts / uploaded files), code with script download, execution log (status, exit code, working directory, stdout/stderr, process environment), and managed package environment.
- **Status capsule**: a capsule in the top-right corner reports whether scientific memory is available (available / unavailable / disabled / needs password); pressing it opens the scientific memory settings.
- **No graph canvas**, and no right-rail scientific memory panel from the old UI.
- When scientific memory is off or the sidecar is unreachable, say so explicitly instead of treating the API's `reason` as "nothing was recorded".

## Involved Public APIs

No new server public APIs. The desktop app only reads the existing routes:

- `POST /api/memory/query/by-node-type`
- `POST /api/memory/query/chain`
- `GET/PUT /api/memory/settings`
- `GET /api/health` (the `memoryGraph` status)
- `GET /api/sessions/:sessionId/artifacts/:artifactId/versions`
- `GET /api/sessions/:sessionId/artifact-versions/:versionId/provenance`
- The `references` field on a report version

No breaking change to existing public APIs.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `services/api`: memory read proxy and settings reads/writes (already present; reused as-is).
- `services/memory-graph`: source of evidence/artifact provenance data (already present).
- Artifact panel and document preview: "Open in the artifact panel" already exists; this feature only calls it.
- Report rendering: desktop rendering of `version.references` into chips (new).
- Provenance semantics must match the old web UI so one feature does not acquire two explanations.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Unit tests** (`apps/desktop/tests/scientific-memory.test.ts`, `memory-chips.test.ts`, `api-memory.test.ts`): citation resolution (evidence by id, an artifact pinned to the cited version, a version-less artifact taking the latest, a mismatched label, a kind the graph has no label for); chip URL round-trip, escaping and malformed input; which nodes an evidence source chain shows (deduplicated, the evidence itself removed); the memory query and settings payloads the client builds.
- **Component tests** (`apps/desktop/tests/settings-pages.test.tsx`, plus the card's own states): the 设置 › 科学记忆 pane reads and writes enable, backend and the write-only password; the card's detail and provenance tabs; disabled and unreachable states render a message and a way to the settings pane instead of an empty provenance.
- **End-to-end** (`apps/desktop/e2e/scientific-memory.spec.ts`, mocked memory service and report): open a report → press an `[evidenceN]` chip → details and a single literature card with its abstract → press an `[artifactN]` chip → dependencies, code with script download, execution log and managed environment → open the artifact in the panel; separately, a disabled memory graph, an unreachable chain, and the header capsule driving the settings switch.
- **Regression:** Markdown without `references` renders exactly as before; non-report documents show no chips; the web scientific memory surfaces are unchanged; ordinary sessions keep their text placement and artifact panel.
- **Real journey (L3):** the literature review sample below, run against a real model and search connectors, with the final report's chips followed end to end.
- **Performance and memory, memory off vs on:** on one fixed Session and report (one `[evidenceN]`, one `[artifactN]`), toggle 设置 › 科学记忆 off and on and repeat the same path on the same build: opening the report, pressing an evidence chip until the card is ready, pressing an artifact chip until provenance is ready, and opening the settings pane; report the median of 10 runs. Measure resident memory after idle and after 50 card reads for the memory sidecar, the API process and the desktop renderer, plus the growth of the memory-graph data directory. Take the UI timings against the mocked service (L2) and repeat the end-to-end timings against the real sidecar (L3); record the machine specs and build SHA with the table.

Commands that must pass: `pnpm check` (repo typecheck and unit tests); `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` in `apps/desktop`; the desktop e2e suite (`playwright test --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The literature research sample in the scientific memory introduction document runs successfully: complete one review from the desktop app following `docs/en/domains/literature-research.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/literature-research.md`) — configure search, submit the task, obtain a final report whose citations are chips, and open the evidence/artifact card from that report.
- [ ] The UI design passes preliminary review: the 设置 › 科学记忆 pane, the report citation chips, the card's details and provenance tabs, and the header status capsule are reviewed against the agreed design and all review comments are closed.
- [ ] A document without `references`, and any non-report document, looks exactly as it did before the change: no chips and no new controls.
- [ ] The memory off/on comparison is recorded in this issue: medians for opening the report, an evidence card, an artifact card and the settings pane, and the sidecar / API / renderer memory plus the graph directory growth, for both the mocked and real-service runs. No new interaction adds a visible pause, and sidecar memory stays bounded across repeated reads.
- [ ] Commands that must pass: `pnpm check`; `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` in `apps/desktop`; the desktop e2e suite.

## Additional Information

- Old UI references: `apps/web/src/EvidenceModal.tsx`, `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx`.
- The desktop app already has settings groups and dialog components; reuse them rather than introducing a new interaction model.

---

## 🚀 背景描述

桌面端（`apps/desktop`）目前尚未接入科学记忆。用户在新 UI 中无法看到最终报告引用背后的证据与产物，也无法在设置里配置科学记忆；而旧版 Web UI 已经具备完整能力：报告里的引用可点击、证据/产物可查看详情与溯源、科学记忆可在设置中配置。

本次希望把同一套能力带到桌面端，但不引入图谱界面：读者完成一次文献调研（见 `docs/zh/domains/literature-research.md`）后，在最终报告里点击 `[evidenceN]` / `[artifactN]`，即可查看该证据/产物的详情与溯源。

相关文档：

- 文献调研样例：`docs/zh/domains/literature-research.md`
- 科学记忆配置：`docs/zh/advanced-setup/science-memory-setup.md`
- 科学记忆设计：`docs/zh/developer-docs/science-memory.md`

## 设计思路

- **设置 › 科学记忆**：新增配置分组，包含启用开关、存储后端（本地 / Neo4j）、Neo4j 地址与用户、密码（只写）、以及当前状态提示。
- **报告引用**：最终报告的 `[alias]` 渲染为可点击 chip，chip 只显示别名本身，不额外标注“证据 / 产物”等字样。
- **点击 chip**：打开卡片，包含“详情”和“溯源”两个页签。
  - Evidence 的溯源只保留文献来源，与旧 UI `EvidenceModal` 一致：文献卡片展示标题、摘要、链接。
  - Artifact 的溯源沿用旧 UI 产物溯源页：派生自（上游产物 / 上传文件）、代码（含下载脚本）、执行日志（状态、退出码、工作目录、stdout/stderr、进程环境）、受管软件包环境。
- **状态胶囊**：新 UI 右上角以胶囊形式展示科学记忆当前状态（可用 / 不可用 / 已关闭 / 需要密码），点击进入科学记忆设置。
- **不提供图谱画布**，也不再保留旧 UI 右侧的科学记忆框。
- 科学记忆关闭或 sidecar 不可达时给出明确提示，不把接口返回的 `reason` 当作“没有记录”。

## 涉及的公共 API

不新增服务端公共 API。桌面端只读复用现有接口：

- `POST /api/memory/query/by-node-type`
- `POST /api/memory/query/chain`
- `GET/PUT /api/memory/settings`
- `GET /api/health`（读取 `memoryGraph` 状态）
- `GET /api/sessions/:sessionId/artifacts/:artifactId/versions`
- `GET /api/sessions/:sessionId/artifact-versions/:versionId/provenance`
- 报告版本的 `references` 字段

对现有公共 API 无破坏性修改。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `services/api`：记忆读请求代理与设置读写（已有能力，仅复用）。
- `services/memory-graph`：证据/产物溯源数据来源（已有能力）。
- 产物面板与文档预览：从卡片“在产物面板中打开”已有能力，本次只做调用。
- 报告渲染：`version.references` → chip 的桌面端渲染（新增）。
- 与旧版 Web UI 的溯源语义需保持一致，避免同一功能出现两套解释。

## 测试设计与测试计划

- **单元测试**（`apps/desktop/tests/scientific-memory.test.ts`、`memory-chips.test.ts`、`api-memory.test.ts`）：引用解析（按 id 命中证据、锁定报告所引版本、未带版本时取最新、标签不匹配、图谱无对应标签的 kind）；chip URL 的往返、转义与畸形输入；证据来源链保留哪些节点（去重、去掉证据节点自身）；客户端构造的记忆查询与设置请求体。
- **组件测试**（`apps/desktop/tests/settings-pages.test.tsx`，以及卡片自身的状态）：设置 › 科学记忆页读取并写入启用开关、后端与只写密码；卡片的详情与溯源页签；关闭与不可达状态给出说明和进入设置的入口，而不是一片空溯源。
- **端到端**（`apps/desktop/e2e/scientific-memory.spec.ts`，模拟记忆服务与报告）：打开报告 → 点击 `[evidenceN]` chip → 详情与一张带摘要的文献卡 → 点击 `[artifactN]` chip → 派生自、代码与下载脚本、执行日志、受管环境 → 在产物面板中打开；另外验证记忆关闭、链路不可达，以及右上角胶囊驱动设置开关。
- **回归**：无 `references` 的 Markdown 渲染与改动前完全一致；非报告文档不出现 chip；Web 端科学记忆界面行为不变；普通会话的文本归位与产物面板不受影响。
- **真实链路（L3）**：下述文献调研样例，在真实模型与检索连接器上运行，并完整走通最终报告中的引用。
- **性能与内存（开启前后对比）**：固定同一个会话与报告（一条 `[evidenceN]`、一条 `[artifactN]`），在同一构建上分别关闭与开启 设置 › 科学记忆，重复同一条路径：打开报告、点击证据 chip 直到卡片就绪、点击产物 chip 直到溯源就绪、打开设置页；取 10 次运行的中位数。分别记录记忆 sidecar、API 进程与桌面渲染进程在空闲时和 50 次卡片读取后的常驻内存，以及 memory-graph 数据目录的增长。UI 耗时先对模拟服务测（L2），再对真实 sidecar 复测端到端耗时（L3）；表格需一并记录机器规格与构建 SHA。

必须通过的命令：`pnpm check`（仓库类型检查与单元测试）；`apps/desktop` 下的 `pnpm typecheck` 与 `pnpm test`；桌面 e2e 套件（`playwright test --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts`）。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 成功运行科学记忆介绍文档中的文献调研样例：在桌面端按 `docs/zh/domains/literature-research.md`（英文版 `docs/en/domains/literature-research.md`）完整走完一次文献调研——配置检索、提交任务、得到带 `[evidenceN]` / `[artifactN]` 引用的最终报告，并从报告中的引用打开证据/产物卡片。
- [ ] UI 设计通过初步评审：设置 › 科学记忆页、报告引用 chip、卡片的详情与溯源页签、右上角状态胶囊均对照约定设计评审，评审意见全部关闭。
- [ ] 没有 `references` 的文档与非报告文档在界面上与改动前完全一致：不出现 chip，也不新增控件。
- [ ] 科学记忆开启前后的对比已记录在本 issue：打开报告、证据卡片、产物卡片、设置页的中位数耗时，以及 sidecar / API / 渲染进程内存与图谱目录增长，模拟服务与真实服务两组都要有。新增交互不引入可感知的停顿，sidecar 内存在重复读取后保持有界。
- [ ] 必须通过的命令：`pnpm check`；`apps/desktop` 下的 `pnpm typecheck` 与 `pnpm test`；桌面 e2e 套件。

## 补充信息

- 旧 UI 行为参考：`apps/web/src/EvidenceModal.tsx`、`apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx`。
- 桌面端已有设置页结构与弹窗组件，可直接复用，避免引入新的交互范式。

## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## Detailed Description of the Problem

`.agents/skills/sciencediscovery-dev/SKILL.md` tells a contributor to replace the repository git identity before every commit. The section "提交与作者身份" says both the author and the committer must be HongyeZhou, and it gives these commands:

```
git config user.name "HongyeZhou"
git config user.email "HongyeZhou@users.noreply.github.com"
```

It also says not to open a pull request until `git log -1` shows that identity. The repository config on this checkout is `wang_cheng_zhao <wangchengzhao1@huawei.com>`, which is the identity already used by the existing history. Following the skill attributes the commit to a different GitHub account.

That rule was added in `5bd8e757449d9a82f3dd1dea1839467bfd8690ec` (`fix(reviewer): default Reviewer Specialist on for new and legacy catalogs`) and is present on `main`. Pull request #849 was opened from commit `46653520deb5546d65a8f9147fecb8252ece81f0`. Its author and committer are `HongyeZhou <HongyeZhou@users.noreply.github.com>` because the change followed this skill. The pull request itself was opened by `zhaozhaozz`.

Expected: a commit uses the identity already configured for this repository, `wang_cheng_zhao <wangchengzhao1@huawei.com>`, unless the person making the commit deliberately chooses another identity.

Actual: the skill overwrites that identity with HongyeZhou.

The commit on #849 is being rewritten so its author and committer match the repository identity. The skill on `main` still needs to stop requiring HongyeZhou.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery
- Branch: main, which contains the skill text
- Affected pull request: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/849
- Affected commit before the rewrite: `46653520deb5546d65a8f9147fecb8252ece81f0`
- Rule introduced by: `5bd8e757449d9a82f3dd1dea1839467bfd8690ec`

## Additional Information

The fix is to delete the requirement that every commit use HongyeZhou. Keep the repository `user.name` and `user.email` that are already configured. Do not set them to another GitHub user as part of preparing a commit.

## Version Information

`main` at `c4f5ecb36ca0439d8e45cc30f1e8d0210413ea70`, which contains `.agents/skills/sciencediscovery-dev/SKILL.md`.

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

### What happens

An evolve search cannot be **stopped from the conversation**. The agent only gets `create_evolve_run`, `get_evolve_run` and `get_evolve_budget`; there is no stop/cancel tool. When the user corrects the scoring formula mid-run (a completely normal thing to do while tuning an evolve-design case), the agent has no way to stop the running search, so it launches a **second** search in the same session. Both then run concurrently against the same workspace and the same token budget.

### Evidence (session `dcfe6ace-c7d1-45c7-a781-9928f5c29c0e`)

Two PUCT runs were left `running` at the same time, two minutes apart:

```text
GET /api/evolve/runs?sessionId=dcfe6ace-…          (2026-11-08T09:24Z)

c870cf09-1632-4d5b-a54d-052e6a1dbea0  status=running  candidates=12  createdAt=09:02:18Z   ← old formula
fee68bb2-3d9a-47c3-bc18-30918d7303ef  status=running  candidates=1   createdAt=09:04:27Z   ← corrected formula
```

The agent says so itself in the turn transcript (translated):

> “The search cannot be cancelled through `execution_cancel` (it is not a Shell execution).”

…and then, because the user had supplied the correct score formula, it simply started another search:

> “I need to restart the search with the new formula.” → “Search re-launched with the correct scoring formula.”

### Tool surface vs HTTP surface

The tool names the agent can see (repository-wide literals):

```text
"create_evolve_run"   6 occurrences
"get_evolve_run"      7 occurrences
"get_evolve_budget"   4 occurrences
"stop_evolve_run" / "cancel_evolve"   0 occurrences
```

But the server already has the capability, used by the web UI:

```text
services/api/src/http/index.ts:3541
  const evolveRunStopMatch = url.pathname.match(/^\/api\/evolve\/runs\/([^/]+)\/stop$/);
  if (evolveRunStopMatch && request.method === "POST") { … handleEvolveStopRun(…) }
```

So a human can stop a run from the UI, but the assistant that created it cannot.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start an evolve-design case (e.g. the compression case in `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`) so a PUCT search is running.
2. In the same session, tell the assistant the score formula was wrong and give the correct one (“得分 = clamp((1 − 压缩后字节数 / 原始 UTF-8 字节数) / 0.75, 0, 1)”).
3. The assistant explains it cannot cancel the running search and starts a second one. `GET /api/evolve/runs?sessionId=…` now lists two `running` runs; both keep expanding candidates.

### Expected

- The agent has a way to stop/cancel an evolve run it started (the same operation `POST /api/evolve/runs/{id}/stop` already performs for the UI), and can then restart with the corrected scoring.
- At most one evolve search runs per session/workspace at a time, or a second start is refused/queued with a clear message.

### Observed

- Two PUCT searches run concurrently on the same session; the abandoned one keeps consuming the token budget (`tokens`/`candidates` keep growing) and both write into the same workspace.
- The user cannot resolve this from the conversation and must find the stop button in the UI themselves.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

```text
Host        Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 (local stack)
Mode        local source checkout, scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-build
Component   adapter :4310, API :4410, Runner :4311, evolve sidecar, JiuwenSwarm gateway :20001
Node v22.23.4, pnpm 11.1.2, uv 0.13.7, Python 3.12
Model       glm-5.2 over an OpenAI-compatible relay
Case        docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md (compress/decompress, stdlib only)
```

## Additional Information

Related but distinct: #948 (search keeps expanding after reaching the 1.0 target), #812 (NPU-backed evolve evaluation feature). Neither covers “cannot stop a run from the conversation”.

The run budget shown in the turn was `20 expansions × 4 workers`, ~600k tokens / 7200 s, so a duplicated search is not free.

## Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- Tested commit: `947d93d0f09a375a0a6ddc8325010e86263cb046` (main, 2026-11-08T00:33:08Z)
- Runner reported version: `947d93d0`

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [ ] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] I understand that environment information and a minimal reproduction are needed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Export currently starts background packaging but requires the user to return and manually download the finished package. Exporting already expresses the intention to save the package; requiring another download action is an unnecessary and easily missed step.

The user also reports that starting a second export replaces the first export's visible task/download entry, forcing them to export again to retrieve the earlier result. The frontend currently maintains one `exportTask` in `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`; starting another export replaces this state. This demonstrates loss of task tracking in the UI, not proof that the backend archive itself was overwritten.

Long-lived export status/download controls also remain on the main page and interfere with normal conversation use.

#### Reproduction

1. Export conversation A and confirm the export options.
2. Wait for background packaging to complete: saving still requires a separate download action.
3. Start another export for conversation B before downloading A.
4. Observe that the visible task/download control now refers to B and A is no longer accessible from that control.
5. Observe that export status remains prominently on the main page instead of disappearing after completion.

This combines user-observed behavior with inspection of the single frontend task slot. Latest-main reproduction is pending.

#### Required behavior

1. **Choose the destination before packaging:** ask for the save path/file name when the user confirms export. Cancelling the save dialog cancels that export attempt without starting an unnecessary packaging task.
2. **Automatically save on completion:** after confirmation, package in the background and save the resulting `.sdresearch` file to the chosen destination automatically. Do not require a second Download click.
3. **Keep exports independent:** each confirmed export owns its task ID, destination, completion handling, and result. Starting export B must not overwrite tracking of A or prevent A from being saved. Existing destination-file conflicts must be handled explicitly rather than silently overwriting a previous package.
4. **Use unobtrusive packaging feedback:** show small text indicating packaging in progress at the existing bottom-page location. Keep normal conversation interactions available.
5. **Show brief completion feedback:** once packaging AND saving succeed, show a green completion message in the same location, keep it visible for a few seconds, then dismiss it automatically. Do not leave a permanent status panel or download button on the main page. Do not implement a continuously flashing animation.
6. **Report real failures accurately:** packaging success followed by a save failure is not a successful export. Provide a readable, localized failure/recovery path and preserve an already-generated archive for retry where available; do not force repackaging merely because saving failed.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery Windows desktop x64, research-package/session export UI.
- User tests Simplified Chinese UI.
- Current session's test installer: `0.3.0-pr970.a933f7fe`.
- Browser-only platforms may have different save-picker capabilities; explicitly define their supported equivalent rather than promising arbitrary filesystem paths through browser downloads.

### Additional Information

Related implementation: #970; research package feature #803. This issue addresses the export/save interaction and concurrent task tracking, separately from #985's export payload/performance defect.

#### Design and module relationships

- `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`: confirmation flow, independent task tracking, background completion, and transient localized feedback. Replace the single-result overwrite behavior with the minimum tracking needed for multiple exports.
- Desktop shell/preload (`win_desktop`): native save-dialog and safe destination-bound save integration, if the current bridge lacks this capability. Associate the selected destination with the correct export task; avoid exposing unrestricted filesystem writes to the renderer.
- Export API/client and backend task lifecycle: retain task-specific download results and support automatic retrieval after completion; a second export must not invalidate the first result.
- Localization/styles: Chinese/English progress, completion, cancellation, and save-error messages; small bottom-page text and green temporary success feedback consistent with the existing UI.

#### Test design / acceptance criteria

- One export: confirm options → select destination → background packaging → automatic file save, with no second download action.
- Cancel destination selection: no package task is started and no file is created.
- Two or more exports: confirm independent destinations, allow varied completion order, and verify every package is saved to its own destination with correct contents.
- Same-name/existing-file collision: explicit conflict handling; no silent overwrite.
- Switch conversations or close the export options while packaging: confirmed tasks still finish and save correctly without replacing each other's state.
- Progress appears as small bottom-page text; green completion appears only after successful save and disappears after a few seconds. Verify with controlled timers in UI tests.
- Packaging failure, permission/disk/save failure, and retrieval interruption: no false success; localized actionable feedback; retry saving an existing result without unnecessary repackaging where supported.
- Chinese and English desktop journeys; supported browser fallback tested separately.

### Version Information

Test build `0.3.0-pr970.a933f7fe`, inspected commit `a933f7fe35d5bb5a084302402715253228471134`. Latest-main verification pending.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Export requires a redundant download step and loses earlier task tracking when another export starts

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
Refs #978.

### What happens

A shell execution the Runner already accepted can still lose its 401 during **finalization** (retrieving the result), not only during submission. In #978's fourth reproduction:

```text
shell_execution_unconfirmed executionId=shell:30b80e03… accepted=true stage=finalization errorMessage="Runner request failed (401)" httpStatus=401
```

The agent then reported the Shell as "still deadlocked" and worked around it by passing the candidate program inline instead of running its evaluator.

### Root cause

`services/api/src/shell-executions.ts`:

- #987 added `rejectSubmission` for a **submission**-stage 4xx (`!execution.accepted && submissionRejected(error)`), which settles the record `failed` (committed).
- A **finalization**-stage 4xx (`accepted=true`) still falls through to `unavailable(...)`, which writes `state: "unknown"`, `provenance: "unconfirmed"`, `finalization: "pending"`, and (for 401/403/404) `retryable=false`. The record never reaches a terminal state, so the tool call never returns and the run stays `running` until the idle watchdog.

Same invariant as #978 — an execution that produced no tool result must reach a terminal state — but on the finalization side.

### Expected

A finalization-stage 4xx on an accepted execution reaches a terminal state with a visible, non-retryable error (or an explicit recovery path), instead of staying `unknown`.

### Environment

Same as #978: Windows 11 + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 local stack, `947d93d0`, model glm-5.2. Session `dcfe6ace-c7d1-45c7-a781-9928f5c29c0e`, run `5a0ec486-51ae-43e1-b6e5-37944cbf0476`.

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
## Background Description

ScienceDiscovery users need to move a completed research conversation to another project or installation and continue working without losing the information behind its messages and results. They also need to start an independent conversation from an intermediate reply without changing the original conversation or inheriting later research as if it already existed.

The required outcome is reliable research handoff and conversation continuation: necessary and complete `.sdresearch` packages export successfully, imports restore the declared content and its relationships, and users can continue chatting or branch from an intermediate reply. The imported research must remain inspectable after restart, with explicit scope limitations instead of broken navigation or unrelated runtime errors.

PR #498 is the implementation intended to resolve this issue. This issue defines the user requirements and acceptance boundary; it is not a roadmap starting after that PR.

## Design Ideas

### Necessary and complete exports

- Both profiles retain all visible messages of the selected conversation scope and their order.
- Necessary export retains current artifact versions, required input versions, relevant workspace files, execution/code/log evidence, and the related review, trajectory and scientific-memory information required by its declared scope. Optional historical records may be omitted explicitly.
- Complete export retains the available history within the selected scope. Full trajectory and full scientific-memory options remain explicit; do not imply that the profile automatically includes every optional detail.
- Preserve selected contents, dependency relationships and omissions in the package. Re-exporting a necessary import as complete must not invent previously omitted history.
- Export previews must reflect the selected revision and options. Background export status and download remain discoverable after navigation/reload; stale output must not be presented as the current package.

### Import and continue chatting

- Inspect and validate the package before restoring its declared files and records. Restore messages, artifact/file versions, execution logs, available trajectory details and provenance with consistent identity mapping.
- Keep the imported evidence snapshot read-only. Provide a visible **Create a new session to continue research** action that creates an independent writable conversation with the retained history and materials. The user must be able to send a follow-up and receive a normal response in this copy.
- Use the receiving installation's model, Runner and permissions. Do not restore credentials or reuse historical permission grants. Missing local configuration produces a specific, actionable state rather than an internal error or silent loss of imported context.
- Original content, file names, timestamps and version relationships must remain attributable. Missing historical evidence must be described as unavailable or omitted, not replaced by the latest file.

### Start an independent conversation from an intermediate reply

- A completed assistant reply in an eligible writable conversation exposes **Branch to a new chat**.
- The branch includes the conversation prefix through that reply and the historical files/evidence attributable to that boundary; later messages and later versions must not leak into it.
- For an imported read-only snapshot, first create the writable continuation, then branch at the chosen historical reply. Explain this path clearly rather than presenting a nonfunctional branch action.
- The branch can accept new messages, preserves a persistent link to its immediate source reply, and never changes the source conversation. A branch can itself be branched with the same rules.

### Integrity and recovery

- Validate content hashes, archive paths and reference relationships. Reject malformed packages before they become accessible research sessions.
- Make import/continuation/branch operations retry-safe. Busy source conversations are rejected clearly; failed operations do not expose writable half-restored sessions.
- Preserve status across navigation and reload. On interruption or service restart, report a recoverable or failed state explicitly rather than claiming completion.
- A package that never contained scientific memory must not fail solely because the graph service is unavailable. If a package contains a graph that cannot be restored, retain an explicit incomplete/blocked state and do not present the research as fully restored.

Alternatives not selected: trajectory-only export; allowing edits to the imported evidence snapshot; replacing missing historical files with current bytes; copying credentials; or branching by copying the current workspace regardless of the selected reply.

## Involved Public APIs

Use the project/session-scoped research-package inspect, preview, export/status/download, import and import-eligibility operations, continuation operations, and conversation-branch/source-navigation operations implemented by PR #498. Exact route names and schemas are owned by its HTTP and client contracts.

Reuse session, message, workspace-file, artifact/version, provenance, execution and trajectory APIs for inspection and follow-up conversations. All reads and mutations remain subject to project/session authorization and snapshot read-only guards. Retrying a mutation must not create duplicate restored or branched sessions. Existing ordinary-conversation behavior must remain compatible.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Responsibility in this issue |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/research-package` | Archive/manifest, profiles, content checksums, inspection and format compatibility |
| `packages/schema` | Snapshot, continuation and branch contracts; shared read-only state |
| `packages/cas`, workspace and artifact versioning | Restore exact retained bytes and historical relationships without latest-version substitution |
| `packages/trajectory` | Preserve selected indexes and detail payloads so imported history remains inspectable |
| `services/api` package/snapshot/history/continuation/branch modules and store | Scope selection, identity mapping, restoration checks, operation lifecycle, read-only enforcement and source lineage |
| `services/memory-graph` | Export/restore selected scientific memory or summary and report unavailable restoration accurately |
| `apps/web` package controls, conversation controls, workspace/trajectory viewers | Export/import, continuation, branching, progress, file inspection, omission and error states |
| Existing agent/executor and model configuration | Receive the restored conversation context and run new follow-up turns using local settings |

Do not duplicate authoritative session state in the UI. Do not create a new agent loop or execution system for imported conversations.

## Test Design and Test Plan

These are required tests, not claims of existing passing results. Use the exact candidate SHA and isolated source/destination data directories.

### Unit and component tests

- Fixture: one source conversation with multiple visible turns, three artifact versions, input/code/image/text files, successful and failed executions, review evidence, trajectory details and scientific memory. Include a historical artifact dependency from another session.
- Verify necessary vs complete selection, independent trajectory/graph toggles, correct dependency closure, all visible messages, and persistent omission disclosures after repeat export.
- Verify unsafe paths, duplicate entries, damaged/missing objects and unsupported formats are rejected; imported identifiers and references remain consistent.
- Verify all snapshot write paths reject mutation, continuation retries are idempotent, branch boundaries exclude later messages/evidence, and source links survive restart.
- Verify revision-aware previews, pending/stale states, background operation tracking, original-name downloads, file previews and explicit historical omissions.
- Verify restored trajectory detail resolution and scientific-memory summary/full-graph states. Do not claim unavailable records are present.

### End-to-end user journeys

| Journey | User steps | Required result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Necessary handoff | Export necessary → import into a clean destination → inspect messages, final files, code/logs and available provenance | Retained content matches the source; omitted history is explained and does not cause broken-session errors |
| Complete handoff | Export complete with full options → import → inspect old versions, execution history and trajectory/graph details → restart | Selected retained history and relationships remain readable and correct |
| Continue an import | Import → create writable continuation → send a follow-up requiring an inherited fact and file → inspect reply/new output | The agent receives the retained context and can use inherited materials; original snapshot remains unchanged |
| Branch midway | In the writable continuation select an intermediate completed reply → branch → send a follow-up → return to source | Correct prefix and historical evidence; no later content; independent response and persistent source navigation |
| Branch again | Branch an existing branch → restart → navigate to its immediate source | Correct lineage and independent content after restart |
| Background and retry | Start export/copy → navigate/reload → reopen progress → retry an uncertain request | No duplicate sessions, no focus theft, correct status and downloadable result |
| Failure and configuration | Use damaged package, busy source, interrupted copy, missing model configuration, unavailable graph with/without graph payload | Specific actionable states; no falsely completed or writable partial restore; valid packages without a graph are not blocked by graph absence |
| Isolation and repeat export | Modify a copy/branch → inspect originals → re-export/import the copy | Source unchanged, retained evidence correct, inherited omissions preserved |

Browser journeys use the pinned Playwright environment, the shipping executor, isolated services and numbered step reports. Add external-client API/local-stack coverage for restoration and access contracts; internal unit tests are not substitutes for these journeys.

A deterministic mocked-model journey must verify that inherited context/files actually reach the follow-up path, not merely that a send request succeeds. Before acceptance, run a bounded real-model journey covering import → continue → follow-up and intermediate branching; missing credentials are a reported coverage gap, not a pass. Protect private data in reports.

Run the required implementation gates (`pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm architecture:check`, `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e`) and applicable repository checks and targeted journeys on the exact candidate. Report planned/executed/passed/failed/skipped counts, blocked prerequisites and baseline attribution. This issue edit does not execute product tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Necessary and complete packages export and import successfully with accurate profile/option previews and explicit omissions.
- [ ] Retained messages, files, versions, execution logs, trajectory details, reviews and scientific-memory relationships match the declared source scope after import and restart.
- [ ] Imported records open without internal errors or unexplained broken references; genuinely missing/omitted data is distinguished from restoration failure.
- [ ] A user can create an independent writable continuation and receive normal follow-up responses using the retained conversation context and files.
- [ ] A user can branch from an intermediate completed reply in a writable conversation, continue independently and navigate back to the source reply; later research is excluded.
- [ ] Originals remain unchanged; retries, interruption, busy sources, unavailable services and missing local configuration have explicit outcomes without exposing incomplete writable sessions.
- [ ] UI review covers export/import, necessary/complete scope, continuation, intermediate branching, progress and failure/omission states.
- [ ] Required gates and relevant browser/API/local-stack journeys are reported for the exact candidate, with no unreported coverage presented as passing.

## Additional Information

Implementation: PR #498.

The completion boundary is evidence export/import, correct restoration, conversation continuation and intermediate branching. Environment recreation, automatic experiment reruns, numerical comparators, paper-target management and scientific failure diagnosis are **outside this issue**. Neither profile claims a reproduction guarantee.

The exact conversation characteristics, export mode (essential/full), export completion status, timing/frequency, and behavior after refreshing or switching conversations have not yet been established. No stack trace or diagnostic logs were supplied. Do not assume a root cause from the code alone.

closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched for related issues.
- [ ] Verified on latest main.
- [x] Environment and reproduction are provided below.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

User reports that dialogue-only conversations export/import quickly and display their history, but continuing the imported conversation loses the previous context. This breaks the central continuation promise even without artifact files.

#### Confirmed implementation root cause

SD restores transcript data without bootstrapping the executor's model context for the newly allocated session ID.

- `research-snapshots.ts` allocates new session IDs and restores messages via `store.restoreMessages`; writable continuation similarly creates a new research-copy session. No JiuwenSwarm runtime history restoration is performed by this path.
- `agent-run/create-agent-run.ts` passes `gatewayHistory` to the agent, but this does not mean the JiuwenSwarm model receives it: `jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` uses it for `DurableContextStore` / plugin state.
- `jiuwenswarm-agent.ts:627` sends a new session key and the latest prompt to the adapter without history. `jiuwenSwarmSessionKey` uses the SD session ID for the main agent.
- `services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/agent_runs.py` explicitly states that JiuwenSwarm owns/compresses context and the adapter neither sends nor rebuilds history. Its request to JiuwenSwarm contains the current prompt under the new key.
- `jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:141` translates the messages supplied by JiuwenSwarm; it does not merge restored SD history into that model request.
- Existing `jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` test named `no part of the conversation is sent to the adapter: JiuwenSwarm holds the context` explicitly asserts that a provided earlier answer is absent from the adapter payload. That contract is suitable for an existing live runtime session but leaves imported/new-ID sessions without prior context.

This is a separation between displayed transcript and model-visible history, not evidence that the imported messages were lost from storage. Reusing the original runtime session key would create cross-session coupling and is not an acceptable portability fix.

#### Reproduction

1. In a dialogue-only conversation, tell the assistant a unique synthetic fact, e.g. `For this test, my sample code is ORCHID-7429`; get an acknowledgement.
2. Export and import it, then create its writable continuation.
3. Ask `What sample code did I give you earlier?` without repeating the value.
4. Capture the first actual model request for the new session using synthetic data. Check whether the earlier user message and acknowledgement (or an adequate restored context representation) are present. Visible transcript alone is not success.
5. Repeat with the source removed and in a clean destination runtime to avoid accidentally reusing cached executor context.

User-observed result: earlier context is unavailable. Code-path analysis confirms the missing context-bootstrap mechanism. No real-model end-to-end run was performed during this investigation; the reproduction above is the required acceptance test.

#### Expected behavior / correction direction

Bootstrap the new executor conversation from the restored portable history before its first continuation turn. Define a safe, idempotent history-seeding protocol or equivalent model-context assembly, including role ordering, tool-call/result closure, supported attachments, and context-budget handling. Prevent duplication on subsequent turns/retries/restarts. Do not rely on original JiuwenSwarm storage, original IDs, or source existence.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

Windows desktop x64; user tests Simplified Chinese UI; dialogue-only research packages. Primary diagnosed executor: JiuwenSwarm. Native/specialist executors need independent regression coverage rather than assuming identical behavior.

### Additional Information

Related #803, #498, #970. Distinct from #983: #983 prevents a writable copy from being published for certain execution histories; this issue concerns a successfully created copy whose model does not receive prior conversation context.

Acceptance: synthetic fact recall and inspection of the actual first model request; source present/deleted/clean destination; essential/full exports; restart/retry without history duplication; prefix-only branches inherit upstream messages and exclude downstream messages. Imported transcript, source data, and unrelated runtime conversations remain intact.

### Version Information

Test installer `0.3.0-pr970.a933f7fe`; inspected commit `a933f7fe35d5bb5a084302402715253228471134`. Latest-main verification pending.
