items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
### Background

ScienceDiscovery does not have a recognizable product icon.

The browser tab has a title and no favicon. `apps/web/index.html` has no `rel="icon"` in `<head>`, so the product is indistinguishable from a generic page among bookmarks and tabs.

The in-app brand mark is a generic flask outline (`BrandIcon` in `apps/web/src/icons.tsx`) on an accent square. It fills the slot, but it is not a mark for this product, and it does not read at a 16px tab or bookmark size.

The README opens with a text title and a UI animation. It has no product mark.

### Expected

One product icon, the same mark in all of these places:

1. Browser favicon (at least 16×16 and 32×32, legible on both light and dark tab bars).
2. The in-app brand slot (today’s `.brand-mark`), replacing the generic flask outline.
3. The top of the English and Chinese READMEs, as a product mark. It does not replace the existing UI animation.

The mark has to stay recognizable at small sizes. Do not rely on hairline strokes alone. The drawing, colors, and whether it includes a wordmark are not decided here; this issue does not pre-select a design.

### Out of scope

- The icon is not a control that opens settings.
- The product name and copy stay as they are.
- A desktop or installer icon, if one is needed, belongs with [#34](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/34) (a native desktop window). It does not block the favicon and the in-app mark.

### Acceptance

- [ ] After opening the local web app, the browser tab shows the product icon, not the browser’s default page icon.
- [ ] The sidebar brand slot uses the same mark, not the generic flask outline.
- [ ] The English and Chinese READMEs show the same mark at the top, and the existing UI animation remains.
- [ ] The small icon stays legible on a light UI and on a dark system tab bar.
- [ ] The icon ships in the repository (for example an SVG source plus the small favicon sizes). It does not depend on an external URL.

### Environment

Against current `main` of `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`: `apps/web/index.html` has no favicon, and `BrandIcon` is a flask outline.

items.author: Birfy
items.body:
## Summary

ScienceDiscovery can already evolve the things a user brings it — a program, a prompt, a protocol. It cannot evolve **itself**. I would like RSI support: given a dataset of tasks, search over the agent's own harness — system prompt fragments, specialist instructions, skill methodology, tool and skill selection — score each variant by running it against that dataset, and surface the winner for a human to adopt.

The search machinery for this already exists in `services/evolve`. What is missing is the candidate being the harness, the evaluation being an agent run, and a reviewed promotion step.

## What is already there

This is deliberately an extension, not a new engine.

- **The search sidecar**, `services/evolve`, runs on `agentdescent>=0.4.6` — `evolve()` / `async_evolve()`, `FlatPuct`, the ledger, the verifier and the policies — behind two engines: flat-PUCT tree search (`puct_engine.py`) and MAP-Elites islands with ring migration (`openevolve_engine.py`).
- **Non-program candidates are first class.** `text_candidate.py` exists precisely because "a prompt or an abstract has no docstring", and `judge_domain.py` states its purpose plainly: it "is what makes `/evolve` work on things that are not programs over tables: a prompt, an abstract, a protocol, a plan". Evolving prompt text is not a new capability — it is the existing one pointed at a different file.
- **Four scoring seams**, already cut: `scorecard_domain` (a metric over a dataset), `test_gate_domain` (a suite's pass rate), `script_domain` (a scorer the drafting model writes), `judge_domain` (a rubric read by a model).
- **Anti-reward-hacking is already solved once.** `test_gate_domain` freezes in two layers — a proposal filter over `frozen` globs in the prompt, and enforcement below it — with the upstream note this issue should quote rather than restate: *"without it the shortest path to a high score is to weaken the thing measuring it."* That is the single most important property RSI needs, and the pattern is in the tree.
- **Held-out splitting exists.** `create_evolve_run` already accepts `caseSplit` with `gateGroups`, `rolloutGroups` and `testGroups`, which is the shape needed to keep a harness from overfitting the tasks it was tuned on.
- **Trajectories are recorded.** `packages/trajectory` captures per-session entries with the context blocks that were actually sent, which is the raw material for judging whether a harness change helped.
- **Parts of the harness are already frozen.** Built-in specialists reject edits to `instructions` / `description` / `name` / `connectorIds` / `enabledSkillIds`; only `enabled` is user-mutable. RSI has to open that door deliberately rather than by accident.

## What is missing

1. **The candidate is never the harness.** Today a candidate is one text-shaped artifact the user owns. The agent's own scaffolding lives elsewhere and is not reachable by a search: prompt assembly (`packages/context/src/prompt-renderer.ts`, `assembler.ts`), specialist instructions (`packages/specialist/src/builtins.ts`), skill methodology (`skills/*/SKILL.md`), and the skill/connector selection for a run.

2. **There is no task-dataset scoring mode.** `scorecard_domain` scores a *program* over a table. RSI needs to score a *harness* over a set of tasks, where each evaluation is a full agent run with its own tool calls, sandboxed execution and artifacts. That is a different cost class and needs its own domain.

3. **There is no promotion path.** An improved harness must be diffable, reviewable, versioned and revertible. Nothing should ever be self-applied.

## Proposal

### 1. A harness candidate

A bundle rather than a single blob: prompt fragments, one or more specialist instruction sets, selected skills, and the run settings that go with them. The mutation prompt sees the bundle and rewrites part of it; the ledger records which part changed, so a win is attributable to something specific.

### 2. A `task_dataset` domain

A dataset entry is a task plus whatever the existing four modes need to score its outcome — a metric, a test suite, a scoring script, or a rubric. Evaluating one candidate means running the agent over the split and aggregating. Reuse `caseSplit` so the reported number comes from tasks the search did not tune against.

The honest problem here is cost: one candidate equals N agent runs, each with model calls and sandboxed execution. The design needs a budget per generation and an early-abandon policy, not just a score.

### 3. Freeze the things a self-improving search must not touch

Same two-layer shape `test_gate_domain` already uses, with a wider frozen set:

- the task dataset and its expected outcomes;
- the scorer, whichever mode it is;
- the permission, sandbox and approval layers — a harness that scores better by asking for fewer confirmations is not better;
- the evolve sidecar's own code and the freeze list itself.

A candidate that edits any of these is rejected at the proposal filter, not merely penalized.

### 4. Promotion is a human step

The winner lands as a reviewable proposal: a diff against the current harness, the score with its held-out number, and the trajectory evidence behind it. Adoption is explicit, versioned and revertible. The skill review flow and the built-in specialists' read-only rules already establish that shape; RSI should reuse it rather than invent a second one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A search can take the agent's harness as its candidate, not only a user artifact.
- [ ] A task dataset can be supplied, and a candidate is scored by running the agent over it.
- [ ] The reported score comes from a held-out split.
- [ ] The dataset, the scorer, and the permission/sandbox layers are frozen against modification by the search, enforced at the proposal filter.
- [ ] An improved harness appears as a reviewable, versioned proposal and is never self-applied.
- [ ] Reverting to the previous harness is one action.
- [ ] A run states its budget and stops at it.

## Open questions

- Should a run evolve one specialist at a time, or the whole bundle? One at a time attributes wins more cleanly; the whole bundle can find interactions.
- Where does a task dataset live — a repository artifact, a workspace file, or a first-class store object?
- Which engine fits better? PUCT refines one starting point; OpenEvolve's islands keep diversity, which may matter more when a prompt change can be good in one dimension and harmful in another.
- What is the minimum dataset size where a win is believable rather than noise, given the non-determinism the judge mode already documents?
- Should this reuse `/evolve-design`'s checkpointed design conversation, or have its own entry point?

Related: [#50](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/50) — the engines can be started but not observed or stopped from the CLI, which matters more for a search whose evaluations are full agent runs.
items.title: [Feature] RSI — evolve the agent's own harness against a task dataset, reusing the agentdescent search

items.author: Birfy
items.body:
## Summary

Both long-running engines — the evolution search and the Idea Tree — can be **started** from the command line but cannot be **observed, controlled, or stopped** from it. Their progress is designed to land on a frontend card, so a terminal user gets a run id and then nothing. I would like `evolve` and `idea` subcommands that reuse the HTTP endpoints the Web UI already calls.

## What happens today

Starting works. `ScienceDiscovery run "/evolve-design --algorithm puct …"` reaches the same control plane as the browser, the agent loads the `evolve-design` skill, and it calls `create_evolve_run`. Then the turn ends — deliberately. The tool's own result text instructs the model:

> The search runs for minutes to hours and its card streams live progress on its own — do not wait for it here, and do not poll `get_evolve_run`.

`create_idea_research` says the same thing:

> After success, report the handoff and end this turn; the existing tree card streams progress. Do not poll or start another research to wait for completion.

That is the right call for the agent loop — polling would burn the budget the search itself needs. But it means **the card is the only progress surface**, and the CLI has no equivalent. `ScienceDiscovery run` prints `Search created: <uuid>` and exits while the search keeps running server-side for hours.

`services/launcher/src/cli-options.ts` has no evolve or idea-tree subcommand and no related flag. So from a terminal today you cannot:

- list the searches or researches that exist;
- see how far one has got;
- fetch a candidate;
- stop one, or pause and resume it.

The only workaround is starting another `run` in the same session and hoping the model calls `get_evolve_run` / `get_idea_research` — a whole model turn spent reading a status field, using tools whose descriptions explicitly tell the model not to poll them.

## The endpoints already exist

The Web UI drives all of this over plain HTTP:

**Evolve**
- `GET /api/evolve/runs`
- `GET /api/evolve/runs/<id>/events?after=<cursor>`
- `GET /api/evolve/runs/<id>/candidates/<codeHash>`
- `POST /api/evolve/runs/<id>/stop`

**Idea Tree**
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research`
- `POST /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research` — `pause`, `continue`, `stop`, `defaults`
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research/<rid>/events`
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/graph`

## The client plumbing also already exists

`services/launcher/src/control-plane-client.ts` has an authenticated generic `request<T>(path, init)` and `subscribeRunEvents()`, a working SSE consumer that "mirrors the Web frontend's `subscribeRunEvents`: fetch with `accept: text/event-stream`, split frames". The launcher also already resolves the bearer token from the data directory. A `watch` subcommand is that SSE reader pointed at a different path — this is wiring, not new infrastructure.

## Proposal

```
ScienceDiscovery evolve list
ScienceDiscovery evolve get <run-id> [--candidate <hash>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve watch <run-id>
ScienceDiscovery evolve stop <run-id>

ScienceDiscovery idea list --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea get <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea watch <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea pause|continue|stop <research-id> --session <id>
```

Conventions, matching what `run` already does:

- **text on a TTY, JSONL when piped.** `run` already switches output mode this way; these commands should not invent a second convention.
- **`watch` resumes rather than replays.** The evolve event endpoint already takes `?after=<cursor>`; a dropped connection should continue from the last event seen.
- **Token and data-dir handling identical to `run`** — sharing a `--data-dir` with `serve` should mean no extra configuration.

One asymmetry to decide: evolve exposes only `stop`, while Idea Tree has `pause` / `continue` / `stop`. Either the CLI mirrors each engine's real capabilities, or evolve gains pause/resume — worth an explicit choice rather than an accident.

## Why it matters

- **Unattended and batch use.** Starting a search from a job script is pointless if the same script cannot poll it, stop it when a budget is spent, or collect the winning candidate.
- **Headless and remote machines.** On a workstation reached over SSH there is no browser to hold the card open. Today that machine can start a multi-hour search it cannot then observe.
- **Consistency.** The CLI is already positioned as the scriptable twin of the Web UI; the two most expensive operations in the product are exactly the ones it cannot drive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Evolve searches and Idea Tree researches can be listed, inspected, watched, and stopped from the CLI.
- [ ] `watch` streams live and resumes from a cursor after a dropped connection.
- [ ] Output follows the existing TTY/pipe convention, so `| jq` works.
- [ ] No new authentication path: the token comes from the data directory as `run` already does.
- [ ] Commands and options appear in `help` and in the CLI reference.
- [ ] Stopping from the CLI has the same effect as stopping from the UI card.

## Open questions

- Should `run` gain an optional `--wait` that blocks until a started engine finishes? Useful in scripts, but these runs last hours — probably better served by `watch`.
- Should `watch` exit non-zero when the run ends in failure, so a script can branch on it?
- Does `evolve list` need session/project scoping, given `GET /api/evolve/runs` is global today?

Related: [#30](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/30) (introduce the CLI in the README) — that issue is about making the CLI discoverable; this one is about the two workflows it cannot reach.
items.title: [Feature] CLI subcommands for the long-running engines — evolve and Idea Tree

items.author: Birfy
items.body:
## Summary

Remote execution today reaches exactly two kinds of target: a machine you can SSH into, and a Slurm cluster. There is no way to run a job on cloud compute — no serverless GPU, no Kubernetes, no cloud VM. A researcher without an HPC allocation or a GPU workstation has no path to accelerated compute at all.

## Current state

The remote-compute model is already well factored, which is why this is an extension rather than a rewrite:

- `RemoteHostConnectionKind = "direct" | "ssh"` — the product either deploys a Runner SEA over SSH (verified host key, SHA-256 checked upload, HTTP tunneled through SSH) or connects to a runner the user started.
- `RemoteJobCard` carries `command`, `inputPaths`, `outputs`, `resources`, `targetAlias`, and `mode: "slurm" | "ssh"`.
- Jobs pass through an approval step (`approvedAt`) before anything runs.
- The host probe records CPU, memory, architecture, scratch paths, and whether Slurm is present — and accepts Linux only.
- Ascend NPU has a dedicated host broker.

So the concepts a cloud backend needs — a job card, declared inputs and outputs, a resource request, an approval gate, a target registry — all exist. What is missing is a third `mode`.

## Why it matters

The Slurm and SSH paths assume the user already has institutional compute. Everyone else — an individual researcher, a small lab, anyone whose cluster queue is full — is limited to the local sandbox. Meanwhile a comparable open-source workbench offers user-owned serverless GPU runs bound to an approved image digest, which is exactly the "I need a GPU for twenty minutes" case we cannot serve.

## Proposal

### 1. A `cloud` job mode behind the existing card + approval model

Define a small provider interface — submit(image digest, command, inputs, resources) → poll status → fetch outputs → report cost — and let backends implement it. The job card, the approval UI, and the output staging stay as they are.

### 2. First backend: Kubernetes Job

Recommended as the first implementation, ahead of any specific vendor:

- works against on-prem clusters, every major cloud, and local clusters for testing;
- no vendor lock-in in a project whose selling point is being model- and vendor-agnostic;
- resource requests, GPU scheduling, and namespaces map cleanly onto `RemoteJobResources`;
- credentials are the user's own kubeconfig, not a service we broker.

A serverless GPU provider can follow once the interface has one real implementation behind it.

### 3. Keep the security contract explicit

Cloud execution is a bigger step than SSH to a known host, because **data leaves the workstation**. So:

- the approval card must show exactly which files are uploaded, where, and to whose account;
- image references must be content-addressed digests, not mutable tags;
- credentials stay user-owned; the product must never proxy compute through an account we control;
- an air-gapped deployment must be able to disable cloud targets entirely;
- show an estimated cost before approval — the governance and quota machinery already exists to hang this on.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A third job mode exists alongside `ssh` and `slurm`, reusing the current job-card and approval flow.
- [ ] At least one backend runs a GPU job end to end: inputs uploaded, job executed, outputs retrieved into the workspace.
- [ ] The approval card states what data leaves the machine and where it goes.
- [ ] Image references are digests.
- [ ] Cloud targets can be disabled by policy for restricted deployments.
- [ ] Failure modes — quota exceeded, image pull failure, job evicted — surface as actionable errors, not a stalled job.

## Open questions

- Kubernetes first, or a serverless GPU provider first for time-to-value?
- Should the cloud backend reuse the Runner SEA inside the container, or invoke the sandboxed executor directly?
- How should cost estimation work when pricing is provider-specific — a per-target rate the user configures?
- Does the Ascend NPU broker share this interface, or stay a separate path?
items.title: [Feature] Support general cloud compute as a third remote job mode

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

### What happens

After importing a `.sdresearch` evidence package, **two sessions are open for the user at once**: the read-only research copy that was just imported, and a second, ordinary writable session that can be chatted with immediately. The second one is the project's auto-created `Untitled session` (or the session the import dialog was opened from); the import flow neither replaces it nor removes it from view.

Expected product behaviour (as documented in `docs/zh/reference/research-package.md`): after import the user should only get the read-only research copy. A writable session may only appear **after** the user explicitly clicks “创建新会话继续研究 / Continue research”, which is also what the caption on the read-only snapshot says (“导入证据快照为只读，请创建新会话继续研究”).

So the default end state violates the read-only-snapshot model: one of the two sessions already accepts messages, and a user can easily type into the wrong one (the empty session) instead of continuing from the imported evidence.

### Evidence

Reproduced against a local stack at `947d93d0`, importing a 2-file package into a freshly created project:

```text
POST /api/projects {"name": "BUG-import-double-session"}      → 201
  firstSession = dc455d7a-4160-4d12-8765-8fb2e5923085         ("Untitled session")

sessions before import: 1
   dc455d7a…  "Untitled session"

POST /api/projects/{id}/research-package/import               → 201
  importedSessionIds = ["119daad8-0c15-41d1-b2f5-990e76b6e535"]

sessions after import: 2
   119daad8…  title="WIN-SRC-1550"   files=2  artifacts=2  runs=1     ← read-only research copy
   dc455d7a…  title="Untitled session" files=0 artifacts=0 runs=0      ← empty, writable, chat-ready
```

The write check on the copy is enforced correctly (`POST /api/sessions/119daad8…/messages` → `409 SESSION_EVIDENCE_LOCKED`), which makes the second session the only one that can be typed into — exactly the confusion described.

The client-side hand-off does not switch the view to the imported copy either: after a successful import the dialog only calls `onImported`, and in `apps/web/src/App.tsx` that handler just refreshes the session lists and, when the **current** session happens to be one of the imported ids, refreshes it. It never makes the imported session the active one, so the previously open writable session stays on screen alongside the new copy.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Local-source mode (`./scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local`), register a model, create a project (a project always comes with a first session, `Untitled session`).
2. From that session's “更多会话操作 → 导入证据包” import any `.sdresearch` package.
3. Look at the session list / open windows: the imported read-only research copy and the original writable session are both open. The writable one accepts messages right away.

### Expected

- After the import dialog completes, only the imported read-only research copy is open/active.
- The writable continuation session is created and opened only when the user clicks “创建新会话继续研究”.
- Ideally the project's auto-created empty `Untitled session` does not linger next to the imported copy when the project was created only to receive an import.

### Observed

- Two sessions open at once; the second is writable and immediately usable, contradicting the “read-only snapshot until you continue research” model.
- No automatic switch to the imported session, so on desktop the user is left looking at the wrong (empty) session.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

```text
Host        Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 (local stack), and the packaged Windows desktop build
Mode        local source checkout, scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-build
Component   adapter :4310, API :4410, Runner :4311, JiuwenSwarm gateway :20001
Node v22.23.4, pnpm 11.1.2, uv 0.13.7, Python 3.12
Model       glm-5.2 over an OpenAI-compatible relay
Package     necessary level .sdresearch (80 KB, 14 objects) and complete level (1.1 MB, 70 objects) — both show it
```

## Additional Information

Related: #803 (the feature that introduced import/continue). The read-only enforcement itself works; only the session-opening behaviour after import is wrong.

Code pointers that make this easy to find:

- `apps/web/src/App.tsx` — `onImported` handler of `ResearchPackageDialogs` (refreshes lists, never `setActiveSessionId` to the imported session).
- `apps/web/src/research-package/ResearchPackageActions.tsx` — `importPackage()` → `onImported?.(imported.importedSessionIds ?? [target.sessionId])`.
- `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts` — import result: `importedSessionIds: restoredSessionIds`.
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts` — `POST /api/projects` always returns a `firstSession`, which is what leaves the empty writable session beside the imported copy.

## Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- Tested commit: `947d93d0f09a375a0a6ddc8325010e86263cb046` (main, 2026-11-08T00:33:08Z)

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
## Background Description

ScienceDiscovery already has trusted, build-time installed plugins. This issue defines how to evolve that implementation into a clearer, maintainable extension architecture without breaking existing execution, permissions, settings, or historical data.

Current implementation:
- `packages/plugin-sdk` defines manifests, service contracts, configuration, and create/start/dispose lifecycle. Plugin scopes resolve dependencies and clean up failed activation in reverse order.
- Runtime contributions include tools, context factories, state providers, batch policies, and optional result submission.
- Skill, MCP, scheduler, Plan, source connectors, and JSON artifact viewing have plugin entry points.
- Settings inherit across global/project/session scopes; Run composition is frozen at execution start.
- Web extensions have settings, project-view, and artifact-viewer registration points.

Remaining boundaries:
- `services/api/src/plugins/catalog.ts` and `runtime.ts` explicitly register installed packages and wire their factories. New plugins still require host/build integration.
- Some capabilities reuse Workspace factories; some domain control-plane logic remains in the API host.
- The contribution contract does not allow general replacement of AgentLoop or the harness.
- Native and JiuwenSwarm use different loop/context execution paths. Plugin registration alone does not establish equivalent behavior across backends.
- Plugins are trusted in-process code; manifest permissions do not provide code isolation.

This issue delivers an architecture proposal and implementation breakdown. Dynamic installation, hot reload, and runtime replacement are options to assess, not implementation commitments.

## Design Ideas

1. **Preserve the existing capability model.** Keep domain-owned packages, public exports, explicit Ports, and one authoritative state store. Avoid exposing the whole Store or NativeAgent through a global container.
2. **Separate installation from activation.** Describe the flow as installed package → dependency/service/permission checks → effective scoped settings → frozen Run composition → lifecycle → contributions. Keep installed, available, authorized, and active states distinct.
3. **Reduce duplicate registration.** Evaluate build-time generation of separate API and client catalogs from an installation description. Server factories must not leak into browser bundles. Compare this with retaining explicit registration before selecting an approach.
4. **Define backend capabilities explicitly.** Produce a native/JiuwenSwarm matrix for every contribution type. Unsupported combinations must be rejected or diagnosed explicitly. Main, child, and reviewer agents must use the same frozen selection, with documented role-specific behavior.
5. **Add replaceable contracts only for concrete needs.** Evaluate runtime backend, model, and execution-provider seams. Specify cancellation, events, recovery, tool permissions, and artifact/result submission before proposing a new interface.
6. **Retain Run stability.** Configuration changes affect subsequent Runs. Evaluate draining old instances before disposal; an upgrade must not mix implementations inside a running composition. Define package/API/state-schema versions separately and retain historical read support.
7. **Make conflicts deterministic.** Specify tool-name collision handling, context budget allocation, batch-policy ordering, result-submission ownership, and dependency-disable behavior.

Options to compare:

| Option | Scope | Main tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Strengthen current capability plugins | Catalog consistency, Ports, diagnostics, lifecycle contracts | Lowest migration cost; host integration remains controlled |
| Add replaceable harness contracts | Backend/model/execution seams driven by concrete use cases | More flexibility; requires cross-backend semantic contracts |
| Introduce dynamic distribution | Package resolution, installation, client assets, upgrades and rollback | Largest operational and compatibility cost; untrusted code requires isolation |

Recommended starting direction: strengthen the current mechanism, then add narrowly scoped replacement contracts. Record evidence and alternatives in an architecture decision before choosing dynamic distribution.

## Involved Public APIs

This analysis does not change public APIs. Inventory and assess compatibility for:
- `PluginManifest`, `PluginDefinition`, `PluginInstance`, and `createPluginScope` in `packages/plugin-sdk`.
- `RuntimeContribution` in `packages/plugin-sdk/src/runtime.ts`.
- Plugin settings and scoped Bridge under `/api/projects/:projectId/plugins`, including configuration revisions, query/command authorization, and events.
- Domain package `./plugin`, `./manifest`, and `./web` exports.

Any proposed API change must include consumer impact, versioning, migration, and failure behavior. Distinguish proposed interfaces from contracts already implemented.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Relationship and analysis responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/plugin-sdk` | Manifest, lifecycle, negotiation, services, configuration and Bridge contracts |
| `services/api/src/plugins` | Installation catalog, factory wiring, scoped settings and control plane |
| `services/api/src/native-agent` | Run composition, contribution assembly, lifecycle and backend integration |
| `packages/runtime-core`, `packages/tools` | Loop invariants, tool execution, permissions, cancellation and result ownership |
| `packages/context` | StateView capture, state schema/revision, projection consistency and context budgets |
| `packages/workspace`, capability packages | Remaining factory coupling; domain Ports and ownership; avoid duplicate tool injection |
| JiuwenSwarm integration and adapter | Backend capability parity, event translation, cancellation and recovery boundaries |
| `apps/web/src/plugins` | Current UI registration, authenticated Bridge and server/client import separation |
| `apps/desktop` | Inventory actual client extension needs and current coverage; do not assume Web registration automatically applies |
| Store, CAS, Recorder and provenance | Settings transactions, frozen composition metadata and historical readability |
| Build and architecture checks | Package exports, dependency cycles, distribution completeness and browser-safe entry points |

## Test Design and Test Plan

The following cases are proposed validation requirements for follow-up implementation. They are not claims of tests executed by this analysis. Map each case to existing coverage first, then identify additions.

| Layer / case | Setup or action | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit: dependency validation | Missing/disabled dependency, duplicate ID, dependency cycle or incompatible service | Deterministic failure before unsupported contributions execute; useful plugin-specific diagnostic |
| Unit: lifecycle failure | Factory/start throws after earlier instances acquire resources | Created resources released once in reverse order; cleanup failures remain observable |
| Unit: cancellation | Cancel during start or tool execution, then dispose | Cancellation reaches async work; no remaining listeners, timers or child work |
| Unit: configuration | Combine global/project/session overrides, including explicit disable and inheritance | Correct effective settings; invalid fields rejected; existing Run stays unchanged |
| Unit: conflicts | Register duplicate tool names or competing policies/result owners | The documented conflict rule is enforced deterministically |
| Unit: state projection | Change live state after checkpoint capture; supply missing or incompatible state | Context and Recorder use the fixed checkpoint; incompatible state fails explicitly |
| Integration: backend matrix | Exercise each contribution through native and JiuwenSwarm | Supported contributions have observable effects; unsupported combinations produce explicit diagnostics |
| Integration: scope consistency | Start main, child and reviewer agents; change settings mid-Run | All use the frozen selection; only subsequent Runs use new settings |
| Integration: settings writes | Concurrent updates and stale expectedRevision through existing write paths | Existing transaction/CAS behavior preserved; conflicts do not partially apply configuration |
| Integration: package boundaries | Build API/client entries and run dependency checks | No reverse host imports, package cycles, duplicate registration or Node-only imports in browser entries |
| E2E: enable/disable journey | Configure a capability → run → disable → start another Run → open previous output | Disabled capability contributes no new execution; historical Plan/artifacts remain readable |
| E2E: clients | Exercise supported settings/view paths through Web and desktop | Scope and authorization preserved; client support gaps documented rather than silently hidden |
| Upgrade/recovery | Load a historical checkpoint after a plugin/schema change or failed upgrade | Supported migration/read path succeeds; unsupported versions fail clearly without corrupting history |

For implementation follow-ups, select affected UT/ST/E2E suites and run `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm architecture:check`, and affected builds. Record exact commands, results, and backend evidence. Real model/connector journeys are required only where mocks cannot establish backend or external execution semantics. Documentation-only analysis does not claim runtime validation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Publish a source-linked inventory of implemented extension points, registration paths and remaining coupling, including Web/desktop coverage.
- [ ] Publish a native/JiuwenSwarm contribution matrix with evidence, unsupported cases and links to follow-up gaps; coordinate backend findings with #572.
- [ ] Record an architecture decision comparing the three options in migration cost, security, deployment, compatibility and maintenance; explain the chosen scope and rejected alternatives.
- [ ] Define lifecycle ownership, in-flight work handling, conflict rules, settings consistency, Run version freezing and historical state compatibility.
- [ ] Describe one minimal capability integration end to end: package exports, installation, Ports, contributions, UI entry, build and verification.
- [ ] Map the test cases above to existing tests and proposed additions, with observable pass/fail conditions and responsible modules.
- [ ] Break implementation into bounded follow-up issues with dependencies, migration/rollback considerations and validation gates.
- [ ] Review the proposal against existing permission, approval, storage and execution semantics; unresolved decisions have explicit owners and follow-up items.

## Additional Information

- Current architecture: `docs/en/developer-docs/plugins.md` and `docs/zh/developer-docs/plugins.md`.
- #572 covers remaining plugin delivery/acceptance for JiuwenSwarm reuse; reuse its findings without duplicating implementation scope.
- Dynamic package installation, plugin marketplaces, untrusted in-process code, and arbitrary live AgentLoop mutation are outside this issue's implementation scope; any future adoption requires a separate reviewed proposal.

items.author: ink999107
items.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

The desktop app (`apps/desktop`, Electron + React) is the primary client, but program evolution (evolve) can only be designed, started, and watched from the web UI or the CLI via `/evolve-design`. Evolve is the one capability that keeps running after the turn that started it and keeps producing candidates: a user needs one surface to design the search, confirm its checkpoints, watch it live, inspect candidates and scores, and return to a finished search later. The desktop app has no such entry point or panel, so users must switch to the web client.

This issue tracks the full desktop delivery: the design entry point, checkpoints, the live panel, and result inspection, with the official tutorial's sample as the acceptance path.

Related issues: checkpoint token budget #780, natural-language entry point #310, `/evolve` documentation #55 / #567, desktop client delivery #400.

Related pull request: #715 — budget for the thinking a model cannot be told to stop (closes #780). It is the source of the per-call ceiling the checkpoint cards show.

## Design Ideas

- **A confirmation switch, chosen up front.** A toggle at the very start of the flow decides whether the checkpoints require a human confirmation. When it is off, the agent runs the remaining checkpoints and launches the search in one pass without stopping to wait; when it is on, each checkpoint pauses for confirmation as described below. The switch is set before anything is designed, so the user decides the pace once, not at every checkpoint.
- **Conversation-first.** No configuration form is added. `/evolve-design` opens the algorithm picker and a create dialog that collects only the two things a person knows — what should get better, and which search fits the problem — then hands that sentence to the conversation as the command it would have typed. The agent still designs the plan and scorecard and runs the checkpoints in the session.
- **Checkpoints stay in the conversation.** The four checkpoints (requirements, evaluation, scale, launch) appear as cards in the message stream; the user confirms or edits them there instead of navigating to another page.
- **A persistent session shelf.** A thin row under the session header lists the session's searches (running and finished); closing the panel never makes a running search unreachable, and a session that never used evolve renders nothing.
- **A result cockpit.** The panel answers the questions a person watching a search actually asks, in order: did it get better (best score), how did it get there (chart), what did it try (candidate table), why was that one rejected (inspector). On a narrow window the inspector becomes a drawer over the table.
- **Runtime install up front.** A first-time install of the evolve runtime happens inside the create dialog, not after the user has written a whole goal.
- **Events first, polling as fallback.** Subscribe to the evolve SSE stream; fall back to polling the run list when the stream is unavailable, and make an idle session cost nothing.

Alternatives considered and rejected: embedding the web page inside the desktop shell (splits interaction and state handling, and ships the whole web bundle), and a standalone search window (a search belongs to a session; a separate window makes both "return to the conversation" and "start another search" awkward).

## Involved Public APIs

No new public API. The desktop app reuses the existing evolve REST/SSE routes (runtime status, init, run list and detail, candidates, event stream), wrapped in `apps/desktop/src/api/evolve.ts`. The shared `EvolveRun` and evolve event types come from `packages/schema`, the same ones the web client uses. Any route change must keep the web client and CLI behavior unchanged and be described here.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `packages/schema`: evolve run and event types; the desktop app does not duplicate them.
- Desktop run pipeline: `run-stream` model and reducer must carry checkpoint and evolve state without disturbing text placement in ordinary conversations.
- Internationalization: every new string lands in both `text/zh.ts` and `text/en.ts`.
- The web evolve dashboard reads the same data; any behavioral difference between the two surfaces must be deliberate and documented.
- End-to-end tests: the desktop e2e fixtures need a mocked evolve runtime.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Unit tests:** command parsing (`/evolve-design`, the algorithm flag, a seeded goal); run status and label mapping; candidate reduction and best score; shelf folding (a running search is never folded away).
- **Component tests:** the create dialog's runtime install and error path; checkpoint cards; panel selection (clicking a row fills the inspector); the narrow-window drawer.
- **End-to-end (`apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts`, mocked runtime):** start a search from a session → checkpoints → run → live updates → select a candidate and inspect it → stop; plus a session with no search rendering exactly as before.
- **Two complex math smoke cases:** (a) symbolic regression — recover a closed-form expression for a nonlinear function from sampled points, scored by fit error; (b) numerical optimization — improve a numerical routine's accuracy or runtime (for example an ODE integrator or a linear solver), scored by error against a reference. In each case the pass bar is that evolve triggers normally and runs through several nodes (at least three expansions with recorded candidates); the full search does not have to finish.
- **Regression:** the web evolve dashboard and the CLI behave unchanged; ordinary sessions keep their text placement, tool cards, and artifact panel.

Commands that must pass: `pnpm check` (typecheck and unit tests); `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `apps/desktop`; the desktop e2e suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The sample in the Evolve tutorial runs successfully: complete one PUCT search from the desktop app following `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`) — design checkpoints, launch, watch live, finish, and open the result.
- [ ] The UI design passes review: the create dialog, checkpoint cards, session shelf, and result panel are reviewed against the agreed design and all review comments are closed.
- [ ] A session with no search looks exactly as it did before the change.
- [ ] Commands that must pass: `pnpm check`; `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` in `apps/desktop`; the desktop e2e suite.

## Additional Information

Tutorial sample: `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md` (Chinese: `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`). The implementation lives in the desktop worktree, and the panel follows the existing session shell and settings visual language.

---

## 🚀 背景描述

桌面端（`apps/desktop`，Electron + React）是主要客户端，但程序演进（evolve）目前只能在 Web 界面或命令行里通过 `/evolve-design` 完成设计、启动和观察。evolve 是唯一一个在对话结束后仍在后台运行、并且会持续产生候选产物的能力：用户需要在一个界面里完成方案设计、确认检查点、实时观察搜索、查看候选与得分，并随时回到已结束的搜索。桌面端缺少这套入口和面板，用户必须切到 Web 才能使用。

本 issue 跟踪桌面端支持 evolve 的完整交付，覆盖设计入口、检查点、实时面板与结果查看，并以官方教程中的样例作为验收路径。

相关 issue：evolve 检查点的预算展示 #780、自然语言入口 #310、`/evolve` 文档 #55 / #567、桌面客户端交付 #400。

相关 PR：#715——为无法被要求停止思考的模型预留预算（关闭 #780）。检查点卡片展示的单次调用上限即来自该改动。

## 设计思路

- **人工确认开关（开始时选定）**：流程最开始提供一个开关，决定检查点是否需要人工确认。关闭时，Agent 一次跑完余下的检查点并直接启动搜索，中途不停下等待；开启时，每个检查点仍按下面的方式暂停等待确认。开关在设计开始前就确定，用户只需决定一次节奏，而不是在每个检查点重复决定。
- **对话优先**：不新增配置表单。`/evolve-design` 打开算法选择器与创建对话框，只收集两件人真正知道的事——想让什么变好、哪种搜索适合这个问题——然后把这句话作为命令送进对话；方案、评分卡与检查点仍由 Agent 在会话中完成。
- **检查点留在对话里**：需求、评测、规模、启动四个检查点以卡片形式出现在消息流中，用户在对话里确认或修改，不跳到另一个页面。
- **常驻会话书架**：会话头部下方一条细书架列出该会话的搜索（运行中与已结束）；关闭面板不会让运行中的搜索不可达，没有搜索的会话不显示任何东西。
- **结果驾驶舱**：面板按观察搜索的人真正会问的顺序回答——有没有变好（最优分数）、怎么变的（曲线）、试过什么（候选表）、为什么没选那个（检查器）。窄窗口时检查器变为覆盖在表格上的抽屉。
- **运行时安装前置**：首次安装 evolve 运行时在创建对话框内完成，而不是写完全部目标后才发现没装。
- **事件优先、轮询兜底**：优先订阅 evolve SSE 事件；流不可用时退回运行列表轮询，空闲会话不产生请求。

考虑过但未采用的方案：在桌面端内嵌 Web 页面（交互与状态处理被割裂，且会带上整份 Web 资源）；单开一个独立搜索窗口（搜索属于会话，独立窗口会让"回到会话"和"再开一个搜索"都变得别扭）。

## 涉及的公共 API

不新增公共 API。桌面端复用现有的 evolve REST/SSE 接口（运行时状态、初始化、运行列表与详情、候选、事件流），客户端封装在 `apps/desktop/src/api/evolve.ts`。共享类型 `EvolveRun` 与 evolve 事件来自 `packages/schema`，与 Web 端使用同一份定义。任何接口调整都必须保持 Web 端与命令行行为不变，并在本 issue 中说明。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `packages/schema`：evolve 运行与事件类型；桌面端不复制定义。
- 桌面端运行流水线：`run-stream` 的模型与 reducer 需要承载检查点与演进状态，同时不能打乱普通对话的文本归位。
- 国际化：新增文案同时进入 `text/zh.ts` 与 `text/en.ts`。
- Web 端演进面板读取同一份数据；两套界面之间的行为差异必须是有意为之并记录下来。
- 端到端测试：桌面 e2e 的 fixture 需要模拟的 evolve 运行时。

## 测试设计与测试计划

- **单元测试**：命令解析（`/evolve-design`、算法参数、带初始目标的命令）；运行状态与文案映射；候选归并与最优分数；书架折叠规则（运行中的搜索永不折叠）。
- **组件测试**：创建对话框的运行时安装与错误路径；检查点卡片；面板选择语义（点击一行填充检查器）；窄窗口抽屉。
- **端到端（`apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts`，模拟运行时）**：从会话发起搜索 → 检查点 → 运行 → 实时更新 → 选择候选并查看检查器 → 停止；另外验证没有搜索的会话与改动前完全一致。
- **两个复杂数学冒烟用例**：（a）符号回归——从采样点恢复某非线性函数的闭式表达式，按拟合误差评分；（b）数值优化——改进某个数值例程的精度或耗时（例如 ODE 积分器或线性求解器），按与参考解的误差评分。两个用例的通过标准都是 evolve 正常触发、并能跑过若干节点（至少三次扩展且有候选记录），不要求完整跑完整个搜索。
- **回归**：Web 端演进面板与命令行行为不变；普通会话的文本归位、工具卡片与产物面板不受影响。

必须通过的命令：`pnpm check`（类型检查与单元测试）；`apps/desktop` 下的 `npm run typecheck` 与 `npm test`；桌面 e2e 套件。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 成功运行 evolve 介绍文档中的样例：在桌面端按 `docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`（英文版 `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`）完整走完一次 PUCT 搜索——设计检查点、启动、实时观察、结束并打开结果。
- [ ] UI 设计通过评审：创建对话框、检查点卡片、会话书架、结果面板均通过对照设计稿的评审，评审意见全部关闭。
- [ ] 没有搜索的会话在界面上与改动前完全一致。
- [ ] 必须通过的命令：`pnpm check`；`apps/desktop` 下的 `npm run typecheck` 与 `npm test`；桌面 e2e 套件。

## 补充信息

教程样例：`docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`（英文 `docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md`）。实现在桌面端工作树中进行，面板沿用现有的会话外壳与设置页视觉规范。

items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Scientific self-evolution here is two loops, and only the inner one is in scope for this issue. The inner loop improves the result of the current run: Evolve proposes a candidate, a scene executes it, the score is read from outside the candidate, and the loop repeats until the budget or a stop rule. The outer loop, later, turns a validated rule or program into something the next run can use. An inner winner is not published just because this run scored well. That outer loop, the antibody chain, and skill-library publish are not this issue.

This issue adds two capabilities to the Evolve that already ships on `main`. It does not replace that Evolve.

1. Evolve can run an NPU evaluation. The search stays next to the API: it proposes candidates and keeps the archive. Each candidate that needs this conversation's runner is scored in a sandbox created on that runner. The sandbox has no network. The cards the operator already selected are attached only when this score needs them. Submit, wait, recover, cancel, and the result use the existing shell-execution path. A search that does not use a runner keeps today's local sandbox, and that local sandbox is not given a network or a card.
2. A search can be directed. The thing being changed is a JSON object, not the pipeline. The scorecard names the fields a candidate may change. Anything else is not a legal candidate. A search that does not declare a direction stays the free program search that exists today.

The behavior of today's Evolve is the baseline. A scorecard, script, judge, or test-gate search that does not ask for these two capabilities must keep its current results, sandbox, and stop rules. New behavior is selected only by the scorecard. Weakening an existing test to make the new path fit is a failed change.

No stand-in model, scene name, sequence, or example metric belongs in product code, unit tests, or system tests. If a short scene later proves useful, it may be added only as its own end-to-end case, in a later change. It is not part of this issue's implementation, and it is not a unit or system test.

Evolve today ranks candidates through a `Domain` (`vendor/puct/domain.py`: initial program, `evaluate`, `reward`, rewrite prompt, metric name). `scorecard_domain.py` already plugs a task into that seam. The local candidate sandbox (`vendor/puct/sandbox.py`) stays the right confinement for short untrusted programs that do not need the runner: Bubblewrap or Seatbelt, no network, writes only in scratch, CPU and memory limits, one thread, no accelerator. `tests/test_puct_sandbox.py` locks that behavior in. A long NPU job does not fit inside that local sandbox, and giving every local candidate a network or a card would weaken that confinement without putting the job on the machine that has the card. The score that needs the card runs on the selected runner, in a sandbox that still has no network.

The same `Domain` can also rewrite a whole program. A scientific scene has a legal direction. Only fields the scene declares may change. Unknown fields fail closed. A missing result is not stored as `0`, because `0` would rank a failed job as a real score. `script_domain.py` is the wrong mode for the NPU path: it lets the model write the scorer. Prompt text is not the enforcement either. The program that computes the score is fixed and runs on the runner. The candidate only supplies the fields it is allowed to change. A number the candidate prints is not the score.

## Design Ideas

- **Today's Evolve stays the default.** PUCT, OpenEvolve, the existing `Domain` seam, and the four current measurement kinds stay. A search with no NPU measure and no `direction` follows the code path it follows on `main` now. `vendor/puct/search.py` is not rewritten, and the default local sandbox profile is not edited.
- **The NPU score runs on the selected runner.** The search loop stays beside the API, because it calls the model and writes the archive on the disk the API reads. One candidate is one shell execution, with its own execution id, on the runner this conversation selected. The runner creates the sandbox. The sandbox has no network. The cards already selected for that runner are bound only when this score needs them. Weights stay on the runner and are read by the fixed program. The candidate JSON is sent with the execution. Success is `completed`, not `succeeded`. Queue time counts toward that job's own time limit. At the limit, the job is cancelled. A search that names no runner does not submit a remote execution.
- **No silent CPU fallback.** If the device is not NPU, the job is a failure. `device` must be `npu`. A detector that falls through to CUDA or CPU must not be reused here.
- **The scene declares the legal move.** `direction.editable` lists the only top-level fields that may differ from the baseline JSON object. A candidate that is not that object, or that changes any other field, adds a field, or removes a field, is `valid=False`. It is not given a low score. A position inside one string cannot be locked on its own: that position has to be its own field. With no `direction`, the search remains free, as it is today.
- **Where the JSON comes from, and how the user sees it.** The JSON comes from the workspace when the user already has one. Otherwise the agent drafts it from the conversation and shows it before the run starts. The user corrects it in the conversation. The screen does not show the raw JSON. Before the run it shows a table. Each row has the field name, the current value, and whether this run may change it. The user ticks the rows, then agrees to start. A long value shows its beginning; the full value opens on click. The ticked rows are `direction.editable`. While the run is going, each row shows the field that changed, the old value, the new value, and the score. After the run has started, the search changes the ticked fields. The user is not asked to edit each try.
- **Seen edits and fault retries stay bounded.** An edit that was already kept is not a new node. Returning to a seen edit whose score does not improve on the score already stored for it is not adopted. Fault, cancel, and missing-artifact retries of the same edit are capped and do not spend another search slot. Waiting is not a fault and does not spend another slot. The guard does not generate the next candidate and does not reimplement the tree.
- **Three job states stay distinct.** Not finished (`queued`, `running`, `unknown`): wait, score empty. Failed, cancelled, or missing artifact: fault, score empty, never `0`. A valid NPU result: record the metric, including a genuinely low one. One card runs a limited number of jobs. The search may keep proposing. Scoring waits on the runner's queue. Waiting does not spend a second slot.

**Where a candidate runs**

| | Today on `main` | After this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Search | Next to the API. It proposes candidates and keeps the archive. | Same place. |
| Score that does not need a runner | Local sandbox. No network. No card. | Same local sandbox. |
| Score that needs the selected runner | Still the local sandbox. That sandbox cannot see the card. | One sandbox per candidate on that runner. No network. The selected cards are attached only when this score needs them. |
| Who computes the score | The measurement outside the candidate, for today's modes. | A fixed program on the runner. The candidate supplies the JSON. A number the candidate prints is not the score. |

**What the search is allowed to change**

| | Today on `main` | After this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Starting point | A program. | A JSON object. |
| What the model may rewrite | The whole program. | Only the named fields. |
| Before scoring | The candidate is scored as it is. | The candidate is compared with the starting point, field by field. |
| An unnamed field changed | It is still scored. | Rejected. No score. |
| A field added or removed | It is still scored. | Rejected. No score. |
| No field list | The whole program may be rewritten. | Still the whole program. This check is not applied. |

**Example input**

The pipeline stays as it is. Each round sends one JSON object into that same pipeline. The fixed program reads the object and returns the score.

Starting point:

```json
{
  "pos_2": "T",
  "pos_4": "K",
  "model": "fixed"
}
```

Fields this run may change: `pos_2`, `pos_4`.

A legal candidate. Only `pos_2` changed. This one is scored:

```json
{
  "pos_2": "A",
  "pos_4": "K",
  "model": "fixed"
}
```

Changing `model`, adding a field, removing a field, or replacing the object with a program does not get a score. On the confirmation screen this object is the table: three rows, and the user ticks `pos_2` and `pos_4`.

Alternatives considered and rejected: allowing network and devices inside every local candidate sandbox (breaks the confinement tests and gives untrusted code the accelerator); moving the whole search into that no-network sandbox (the search has to call the model, and the archive has to stay where the API can read it); treating "only edit these fields" as prompt text (the model can ignore it); letting the candidate report its own score; putting a particular model or scene into the product modules or into unit and system tests (that scene is not this change).

## Involved Public APIs

No new public HTTP API. The domain seam is unchanged: `evaluate(code, shards) -> (valid, metrics, error)`. The NPU path reuses the existing shell execution routes on the conversation's selected runner (`POST /shell-executions`, status, logs, cancel). The API already selects that runner and signs the request. Any change to those routes must keep current skill launches, including the antibody pipeline and CodonTransformer, behaving as they do now.

The new behavior is opt-in on the existing engines: a score that uses the selected runner, and an optional `direction` object taken from the fields the user ticked. The confirmation before the run shows the field table. This issue does not add a model-specific domain, skill, or fixture.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `services/evolve`: add the opt-in runner evaluation and the direction check. Existing measurement kinds keep their current behavior. Do not edit `vendor/puct/search.py` or the default local sandbox profile.
- `tests/test_puct_sandbox.py`: remains the lock on the local confinement. This issue is not done if those tests are weakened so that ordinary candidates can see the network or an accelerator.
- The evolve confirmation and the run panel: the field table before the run, and the old-value / new-value / score rows while it runs. Raw JSON is not that view.
- Skill execution: an NPU search uses the same shell-execution contract as the current NPU skills, including the runner sandbox and the already selected cards. It does not call `run_npu_job`.
- Antibody skills and MindSpore operators are not modified. An NPU job completing does not certify RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, or Protenix.
- Skill-library publish, replay, and the outer loop are out of scope. This issue must not write an inner winner into the skill library.

## Test Design and Test Plan

Default CI does not need an Ascend device. Tests use a runner double that speaks the shell-execution states. They do not name a model, load weights, or embed a scene. Unit tests and system tests stay free of any stand-in model. An end-to-end case, if one is justified later, is a separate change and is not part of `pnpm evolve:test`.

- **Unit, NPU job.** A completed record with `device=npu` returns `valid=True` and the metric from that record. The metric is the number returned by the fixed program. A number printed by the candidate is not stored. A queued, running, or unknown record, a missing artifact, a non-`npu` device, and a failed or cancelled execution each return `valid=False` with an empty score, not `0`. Each candidate is its own execution id. The unit test does not import a model runtime.
- **Unit, direction.** An unknown field is rejected. A change to a field that is not in `direction.editable` is rejected. A free-form program is rejected when a direction is set. A scorecard with no direction is not passed through this check. A previously seen edit that does not improve is not a new node. Fault retries stop at the cap and do not spend another search slot; waiting does not.
- **Unit, sandbox regression.** `tests/test_puct_sandbox.py` stays as it is: network denied, writes confined to scratch, no backend refuses to run unconfined, CPU budget floor unchanged. Constructing the NPU path does not flip the default local sandbox to allow network or devices. A search with no runner does not submit a remote execution.
- **The field table.** Before the run, the confirmation shows the field name, the current value, and a tick for whether this run may change it. During the run, a row shows the changed field, the old value, the new value, and the score. A long value shows its beginning until opened.
- **Regression, the baseline.** Existing scorecard, PUCT fidelity, script-domain, judge, and test-gate tests pass without changing their assertions. That is the proof that today's Evolve still behaves as it does on `main`. The antibody pipeline tests are not part of this issue and must not be edited to go green.
- **Not in unit or system tests.** No model-specific forward, fixture sequence, or scene skill. Hardware smoke, if it is ever run, is reported separately and is not folded into `pnpm evolve:test`.

Commands that must pass: `pnpm evolve:test`, with the same pass and skip counts the unmodified `main` suite has, plus the new tests above. A machine without an accelerator still passes that command.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An Evolve search that does not request an NPU job and does not set `direction` behaves as it does on `main`, including the current local sandbox. `tests/test_puct_sandbox.py` passes without allowing network or devices for every candidate. Existing Evolve tests pass without assertion edits.
- [ ] A search that uses the conversation's runner scores each candidate in a sandbox on that runner. The sandbox has no network. Cards are attached only when the score needs them. The search itself stays next to the API.
- [ ] An NPU evaluation scores only a completed `device=npu` result returned by the fixed program, and never writes `0` for a waiting, failed, cancelled, or missing result. It does not fall back to CPU or CUDA. Queue time counts toward that job's limit, and the job is cancelled at the limit.
- [ ] When `direction.editable` is set, a candidate outside those fields is rejected before scoring. When it is absent, the search stays free.
- [ ] Before the run, the user sees a table of field name, current value, and whether this run may change it, and ticks the rows. The raw JSON is not that view. During the run, each row shows the changed field, the old value, the new value, and the score.
- [ ] Product code, unit tests, and system tests contain no stand-in model, scene skill, or scene fixture. A later end-to-end case is out of this issue.
- [ ] `vendor/puct/search.py` is unchanged. No second search implementation lands under `skills/`.
- [ ] `pnpm evolve:test` passes. The inner result is not published to the skill library.

## Additional Information

Final scientific acceptance of the two-loop design remains a full antibody design run and is not an acceptance line of this issue.

## 🚀 背景描述

这里的科研自进化是两层循环。本 issue 只做内层。内层改进这一次 Run 的结果：Evolve 提出候选，场景执行，分数在候选程序外面读取，直到预算用尽或触发停止。外层以后才把经过独立验证的规则或程序交给后续 Run。内层赢家不能因为这一次分高就发布。外层、抗体设计链和技能库发布都不在本 issue 里。

本 issue 在 `main` 上已有的 Evolve 里加两件事，不换成另一套 Evolve。

1. Evolve 能跑 NPU 评分。搜索留在 API 旁边：它提出候选、保存档案。要用本轮对话选中的 Runner 时，每个候选在那台机器上的沙箱里评分。沙箱不上网。只有这次评分要用卡时，才把操作者已经勾选的卡放进去。提交、等待、恢复、取消和结果回传走现有的 Shell 执行路径。没有使用 Runner 的搜索仍用今天的本机沙箱，这个本机沙箱不获得网络，也不获得卡。
2. 搜索可以定向。被修改的是一份 JSON，不是整条流程。scorecard 声明候选可以改哪些字段。其余改动不是合法候选。没有声明方向的搜索，仍是现在这种自由的程序搜索。

今天 Evolve 的行为就是基线。没有要求这两项能力的 scorecard、脚本、评审或测试门搜索，必须保持现在的结果、沙箱和停止规则。新行为只由 scorecard 选中。为了让新路径通过而放宽已有测试，算失败。

正式代码、单元测试和系统测试里不放替身模型、场景名、序列或示例指标。如果以后某条短场景确实有用，只能在另一次改动里作为端到端用例加入。它不是本 issue 的实现，也不是单元测试或系统测试。

现有 Evolve 通过 `Domain` 给候选排序（`vendor/puct/domain.py`：起点程序、`evaluate`、`reward`、改写提示、指标名）。`scorecard_domain.py` 已经按这条缝接入。不需要 Runner 的短程序，仍用本机候选沙箱（`vendor/puct/sandbox.py`）：Bubblewrap 或 Seatbelt、无网络、只能写临时目录、有 CPU 和内存上限、单线程、没有加速器。`tests/test_puct_sandbox.py` 把这些行为锁住了。一次长的 NPU 作业不该塞进这个本机沙箱。给所有本机候选放开网络或发一张卡，会削弱这层隔离，作业也仍然不在有卡的那台机器上。需要卡的评分在选中的 Runner 上跑，那个沙箱同样不上网。

同一个 `Domain` 现在还可以改写整个程序。科学场景有合法方向。场景没有声明的字段不能改。未知字段直接失败。没有结果不能记成 `0`，否则失败作业会变成一个真实分数。`script_domain.py` 不适用于 NPU 这条路径，它让模型自己写评分程序。只在提示词里要求“只改这些字段”也不算约束。算分的程序是固定的，跑在 Runner 上。候选只提供允许改的字段。候选自己打印的数字不算分数。

## 设计思路

- **今天的 Evolve 仍是默认路径。** PUCT、OpenEvolve、现有 `Domain` 缝和现有四种评分方式都保留。没有 NPU 评分、也没有 `direction` 的搜索，走它现在在 `main` 上的路径。不改写 `vendor/puct/search.py`，也不改默认的本机沙箱配置。
- **NPU 评分在选中的 Runner 上跑。** 搜索循环留在 API 旁边，因为它要调用模型，档案也要写在 API 能读到的那块磁盘上。一个候选是一次 Shell 执行，有自己的执行编号，发到本轮对话选中的 Runner。沙箱由这台 Runner 创建。沙箱不上网。这台 Runner 上已经勾选的卡，只有这次评分需要时才绑进去。权重留在 Runner 上，由固定程序去读。候选 JSON 随这次执行送过去。成功状态是 `completed`，不是 `succeeded`。排队时间算进这次作业自己的时限。到点就取消。没有指定 Runner 的搜索不提交远程执行。
- **禁止悄悄退回 CPU。** 设备不是 NPU 时，作业失败。`device` 必须是 `npu`。会落到 CUDA 或 CPU 的探测不能用在这里。
- **场景声明合法动作。** `direction.editable` 列出相对基线 JSON 可以不同的最外层字段。候选不是这个对象，或者改了别的字段、多了字段、少了字段，就是 `valid=False`，不给一个低分代替。写在同一个字符串里的某一个位置不能单独锁住，这个位置必须自成一个字段。没有 `direction` 时，搜索仍是现在这种自由搜索。
- **JSON 从哪来，用户怎么看。** 用户已经有 JSON，就用工作区里的那份。没有的话，Agent 按对话写一份初稿，开始前给用户看。用户在对话里改。界面不直接显示原始 JSON。开始前用一张表，每一行是字段名、当前值、这次能不能改。用户勾选能改的几行，再同意开始。值太长时先显示开头，点开看全文。勾中的行就是 `direction.editable`。运行中，每一行显示改了哪一项、旧值、新值、多少分。运行开始以后，搜索去改勾中的字段。不会让用户逐次去改。
- **见过的修改和失败重试都有界。** 已经收成节点的修改不再是新节点。改回已经见过的修改时，分数没有超过该修改已记下的成绩，也不收成新节点。同一次修改因失败、取消或产物缺失而重试时有次数上限，并且不再另占一个搜索名额。等待不是失败，也不另占名额。这层检查不生成下一轮候选，也不重写树搜索。
- **三种作业状态分开。** 未结束（`queued`、`running`、`unknown`）：等待，分数为空。失败、取消或产物缺失：故障，分数为空，不写 `0`。有效的 NPU 结果：记下指标，哪怕这个指标确实很低。一张卡同时能跑的作业有限。搜索可以继续提议。评分排在 Runner 的队列后面。等待不再占第二个名额。

**候选在哪里跑**

| | 现在的 `main` | 这次改完之后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 搜索 | 在 API 旁边。它提出候选、保存档案。 | 还在这里。 |
| 不需要 Runner 的评分 | 本机沙箱。不上网。没有卡。 | 仍是这个本机沙箱。 |
| 需要选中 Runner 的评分 | 仍在本机沙箱。这个沙箱看不见那张卡。 | 每个候选在那台 Runner 上单独一个沙箱。不上网。这次评分要用卡，才绑已经勾选的卡。 |
| 谁算分 | 现有几种评分在候选外面算。 | Runner 上的固定程序算。候选只提供 JSON。候选自己打印的数字不算分。 |

**搜索可以改什么**

| | 现在的 `main` | 这次改完之后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 起点 | 一段程序。 | 一份 JSON。 |
| 模型可以改什么 | 整段程序。 | 只改点名的字段。 |
| 评分前 | 直接拿去评分。 | 先和起点逐项对照。 |
| 没点名的字段变了 | 照样评分。 | 拒绝，不评分。 |
| 多了或少了字段 | 照样评分。 | 拒绝，不评分。 |
| 没有名单 | 整段程序都可以改。 | 仍是整段程序。不走这层对照。 |

**输入例子**

整条流程不动。每一轮把一份 JSON 送进同一条流程。固定程序读这份 JSON，返回分数。

起点：

```json
{
  "pos_2": "T",
  "pos_4": "K",
  "model": "fixed"
}
```

这次允许改的字段：`pos_2`、`pos_4`。

合法候选。只改了 `pos_2`。这份会去评分：

```json
{
  "pos_2": "A",
  "pos_4": "K",
  "model": "fixed"
}
```

改了 `model`、多了字段、少了字段，或者把这份 JSON 换成一段程序，都不评分。确认界面上，这份 JSON 就是三行的表，用户勾选 `pos_2` 和 `pos_4`。

考虑过但未采用：给每一次本机候选沙箱放开网络和设备（隔离测试会失效，不可信代码也会拿到加速器）；把整个搜索放进那个不上网的沙箱（搜索要调用模型，档案也要留在 API 能读到的地方）；把“只能改这些字段”写成提示词（模型可以不遵守）；让候选自己报分；把某个具体模型或场景写进产品模块、单元测试或系统测试（那个场景不是这次改动）。

## 涉及的公共 API

不新增公共 HTTP API。域的缝不变：`evaluate(code, shards) -> (valid, metrics, error)`。NPU 路径复用本轮对话所选 Runner 上的现有 Shell 执行接口（`POST /shell-executions`、状态、日志、取消）。Runner 的选择和请求签名仍由 API 负责。这些接口若有调整，必须保持现有技能的启动行为不变，包括抗体流水线和 CodonTransformer。

新行为是现有引擎上的可选项：使用选中 Runner 的评分，以及用户勾选字段得到的可选 `direction`。运行前的确认显示字段表。本 issue 不新增针对某个模型的域、技能或夹具。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `services/evolve`：增加可选的 Runner 评分和方向检查。现有评分方式保持现在的行为。不改 `vendor/puct/search.py`，也不改默认的本机沙箱配置。
- `tests/test_puct_sandbox.py`：继续锁住本机隔离。若为了让普通候选看见网络或加速器而放宽这些测试，本 issue 不算完成。
- Evolve 的确认和运行面板：开始前的字段表，以及运行中的旧值、新值、分数。这个界面不直接显示原始 JSON。
- 技能执行：NPU 搜索使用和现有 NPU 技能相同的 Shell 执行约定，包括 Runner 上的沙箱和已经勾选的卡。不调用 `run_npu_job`。
- 不修改抗体技能和 MindSpore 算子。一次 NPU 作业完成不能证明 RFdiffusion、ProteinMPNN 或 Protenix 可用。
- 技能库发布、回放和外层循环不在范围内。本 issue 不得把内层结果写入技能库。

## 测试设计与测试计划

默认 CI 不需要昇腾设备。测试使用一个说 Shell 执行状态的 Runner 替身。测试不点名模型、不加载权重、不内置场景。单元测试和系统测试都不放替身模型。端到端用例如果以后确实要加，是另一次改动，不进入 `pnpm evolve:test`。

- **单元测试，NPU 作业。** `device=npu` 的完成记录返回 `valid=True`，分数来自固定程序返回的数字。候选自己打印的数字不记。排队、运行中、未知、产物缺失、设备不是 `npu`、失败或取消，都返回 `valid=False`，分数为空，不是 `0`。每个候选有自己的执行编号。单元测试不导入模型运行时。
- **单元测试，方向。** 未知字段被拒绝。不在 `direction.editable` 里的字段被改动时被拒绝。设置了方向时，自由形式的程序被拒绝。没有方向的 scorecard 不走这层检查。已经见过且没有提升的修改不成为新节点。失败重试到达上限后停止，并且不再另占搜索名额；等待不算重试。
- **单元测试，沙箱回归。** `tests/test_puct_sandbox.py` 保持原样：拒绝网络、写入限制在临时目录、没有隔离后端就拒绝运行、CPU 预算下限不变。构造 NPU 路径不会把默认的本机沙箱改成允许网络或设备。没有 Runner 的搜索不提交远程执行。
- **字段表。** 开始前，确认界面显示字段名、当前值，以及这次能不能改。运行中，一行显示改了哪一项、旧值、新值、分数。过长的值先显示开头，点开再看全文。
- **回归，也就是基线。** 现有 scorecard、PUCT 保真、script-domain、评审和测试门测试不改断言也要通过。这就是证明今天的 Evolve 仍和 `main` 上一样。抗体流水线测试不属于本 issue，不得为了变绿去改它们。
- **不放进单元测试或系统测试。** 不做某个模型的前向，不放场景技能或场景夹具。如果单独跑过硬件，单独报告，不算进 `pnpm evolve:test`。

必须通过的命令：`pnpm evolve:test`。未改过的 `main` 上原有用例的通过数和跳过数保持不变，再加上上面这些新测试。没有加速器的机器也必须能通过这条命令。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 没有要求 NPU 作业、也没有设置 `direction` 的 Evolve 搜索，行为与 `main` 上一致，包括当前的本机沙箱。`tests/test_puct_sandbox.py` 通过，且没有为所有候选放开网络或设备。现有 Evolve 测试不改断言也能通过。
- [ ] 使用本轮对话所选 Runner 的搜索，每个候选在那台 Runner 的沙箱里评分。沙箱不上网。要用卡才绑卡。搜索本身留在 API 旁边。
- [ ] NPU 评分只接受固定程序返回的、`device=npu` 的完成结果。等待、失败、取消或缺失的结果不写 `0`。不退回 CPU 或 CUDA。排队时间算进这次作业的时限，到点取消。
- [ ] 设置了 `direction.editable` 时，字段之外的候选在打分前被拒绝。没有设置时，搜索仍是自由的。
- [ ] 开始前给用户一张表：字段名、当前值、这次能不能改。用户勾选。这个界面不直接显示原始 JSON。运行中每一行显示改了哪一项、旧值、新值、多少分。
- [ ] 产品代码、单元测试和系统测试里没有替身模型、场景技能或场景夹具。以后的端到端用例不属于本 issue。
- [ ] `vendor/puct/search.py` 没有改动。`skills/` 下没有第二套搜索实现。
- [ ] `pnpm evolve:test` 通过。内层结果不发布到技能库。

## 补充信息

双层设计的最终科学验收仍是一次完整抗体设计，不是本 issue 的验收项。

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
## What happens

A delimited dataset preview (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `parseDelimitedTable`) takes its width from the **widest line of the whole file**, so one outlier line decides how many columns every returned row shows. A two-column file that contains a single line with 200,001 fields renders as 1,001 columns, 999 of them carrying an empty header and an empty cell in every row.

## Where

- `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` (at `0477d328`): `const widest = lines.reduce(...)`, `const totalColumns = Math.max(header.length, widest)`, `const width = Math.min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)` (`MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS = 1001`), and the blank header names built at `columns: header.length >= width ? header.slice(0, width) : [...header, ...Array.from({length: width - header.length}, () => "")]`.

## Measured at `0477d328` (default `maxRows`)

- two-column header plus one line of 200,001 fields: `columns 1001`, `clippedColumns {total: 200001, shown: 1001}`, rows padded to 1001 cells each, so 999 columns and ~99,900 cells in the payload are blank.
- the same file without the outlier line: `columns 2`.

## Why it matters

The preview is widened by a line that is not part of the returned rows, and the extra columns carry no header - the grid shows a two-column table as a 1,001-column one. `clippedColumns` does report `{total, shown}`, so the cut is signalled, but the blank columns themselves are still rendered.

## Suggested fix

Cap the *unnamed surplus* columns the way the CSV importer already does (`apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts`, `surplusColumnLimit`: `min(16, max(2, header.length))`) while never capping header columns, and keep reporting the dropped cells in `clippedCells` / `clippedColumns`.
items.title: [Bug] One outlier line sets a delimited preview's width, so a two-column file renders 1,001 mostly-blank columns

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
## What happens

The delimited-preview payload carries a `warnings: string[]` field that no consumer reads, and which duplicates text the client already composes and localizes.

## Where

- `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` (at `0477d328`): the `warnings` array is built at the end of `parseDelimitedTable` ("The file has {total} columns; the preview shows the first {shown}." and "{n} cells past the preview width are not shown.") and returned in the payload type (`:161`-ish in that revision).
- `apps/web/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` mirrors the field in the web payload type.
- The viewer does not use it: `ArtifactModal` passes `clippedColumns` / `clippedCells` down and `DatasetTable` composes its own sentences from `artifact.tableClippedColumns` / `artifact.tableClippedCells` (`apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx`).

## Why it matters

Two places decide what the user is told about a clipped preview: the server strings are English-only, so a Chinese UI would drift from them the moment anyone read them, and a future consumer could show untranslated text. Today the field is dead weight in every preview payload.

## Suggested fix

Either drop `warnings` from the payload and keep `clippedColumns` / `clippedCells` as the only source of truth (the client already localizes from them), or make the client render the server strings through the i18n layer. Pick one owner for the copy.
items.title: [Cleanup] The delimited preview payload's `warnings` field duplicates the client copy, is not localized, and has no consumer

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Follow-up work for #834 (`feat(sizeopt): slim the Windows installer 797.6 -> ~578.0 MiB, merge 6 envs into 2`). That PR's code is reviewed; this issue carries the parts deliberately left out of it, so they are not only recorded in a review thread.

## 1. Real-machine smoke (the minimum the maintainer asked for)

The full matrix (three install-root lengths timed, bilingual screenshots, 30–60 s recording) was reduced to one smoke pass:

- [ ] One clean Windows machine: install → first launch, with a first-launch timing next to the f26 baseline.
- [ ] Actually trigger the over-long install-root refusal (`win_desktop/build/installer.nsh:306-339`): what the dialog says, and whether choosing "No" really aborts the install instead of continuing into `InstFiles`.
- [ ] One pass through each side of the uninstall "also delete user data" branch (`installer.nsh:541`).

Screenshots or a short written record are enough.

## 2. First-run bytecode completeness

`treeHasPycache` (`win_desktop/src/bootstrap.ts:230-251`) skips the first-run `compileall` as soon as one `__pycache__` directory holds one `.pyc` (`:243`). At the default install root that compile is not runnable anyway — `63 + 1 + 192 + 14 > 259` — so a complete shipped `.pyc` set is load-bearing, and the only place that dependency is written down is the A5 advisory (`assemble-backend.mjs:990-996`), which exists only on the build machine.

- [ ] Write a manifest or count of the precompiled set at assemble time and check it at bootstrap, so an incomplete set (quarantined file, partial copy, interrupted unpack) fails the build or names itself at first launch instead of surfacing as an `ImportError` at first tool use.

## 3. Smaller items raised in review

- [ ] `win_desktop/scripts/after-pack-trim-locales.cjs` hardening (see the #834 review threads for the specific asks).
- [ ] Stale documentation references to the removed per-service `services/<member>/uv.lock` files.

## Not in scope here

- The `uv sync` SIGTERM defect in `scripts/start-stack.mjs` stays in #834: it is a reproducible bug on the current head, not follow-up work.
- The patch-0019 wording in #834's description has been corrected and is accurate on the current head.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
## What

`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py:156` (`GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, added by #915) pins only one direction of the walk: both new cases assert that something is **not** reported. Nothing asserts that a violation still **is** reported after the ignore list changed.

## Trigger

`IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` is widened again, or `_files()` is narrowed, so that a real source root (`services/api`, `packages`, `apps/web`, `test/api`) stops being walked. Every current case still passes:

- `test_a_generated_workspace_is_not_walked` and `test_a_workspace_file_removed_after_listing_is_skipped` assert absence only;
- `test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` asserts `failures == []`, which a walk that sees nothing also satisfies.

The boundary test then silently stops policing the Gateway boundary with no red test anywhere.

## Fix

Add the mirror case in `GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests`, reusing the `mock.patch.object(sys.modules[__name__], "_files", ...)` plumbing already present at `:162`:

- have the patched walk yield a path under `services/api/src` (for example `services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts`) whose content contains a vendor token;
- assert `_node_boundary_failures()` returns that path, as `path: <relative>` or `content: <relative>`.

Three lines in the test file. No production code changes.

## Why it is worth a line

Measured at `f99cc8a24495544988045699b9e5c2429553e332` (review comment on #915): a fabricated `services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts` does produce `['path: services/api/src/probe-zz-deerflow-boundary.ts']`, and with the pre-change ignore set a probe in `services/api/.tmp` produces `['content: services/api/.tmp/probe-manual-537457.ts']`. The guard works today; only its regression direction is untested.

Found while reviewing #915 and tracked here so the review thread can be closed without losing the gap.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
## What happens

`#866` / `#868` add a Windows reserved-device-name guard to the **upload** path. The sibling user-write path, `POST /api/sessions/:id/files`, still has no such guard, so the same device names remain writable there.

- Route: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3804` (`filesMatch` handler), `body.path` resolved at `:3807`.
- `resolveWorkspaceFile` (`packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts:2225`) delegates to `assertWorkspacePath` (`:456`), which only rejects absolute paths and escapes — it knows nothing about device names.
- The result goes straight to `writeFile(target, body.content ?? "", "utf8")` at `:3811`. `sanitizeUploadFilename` (`services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts:67`), where the reserved-name guard lives, is never called on this path.

On a Windows workspace that means `{"path": "con", "content": "x"}` targets the console device (the write silently goes to the console instead of a file) and `{"path": "nul.txt", ...}` fails with a raw `EPERM` that the handler does not classify — the client sees `500 Internal server error`. That is the exact failure shape `#866` reports, on a second user-write path.

## Expected

The reserved-name rule should be a workspace invariant, not an upload-only check: `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` with `CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, or `CON .csv` should answer **400** naming the file, and nothing should be written.

## Red first

`#868`'s guard is deliberately platform-independent, so this is testable on Linux without a Windows host: current `main` accepts the name and creates a file.

Suggested test (route level, next to `WSP-004` in `services/api/src/server.test.ts`): create project + session, then

```ts
const res = await fetch(`${origin}/api/sessions/${id}/files`, {
  method: "POST", headers: { ...authorization, "content-type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ path: "CON", content: "x" }),
});
assert.equal(res.status, 400);          // currently 201
assert.match((await res.json()).error, /reserved device name/);
```

and assert the workspace listing is unchanged. Legal look-alikes (`conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `auxiliary.csv`) and `com10.csv` must keep returning 201.

## Fix direction (maintainer's call)

Two shapes work; the first is smaller:

1. Call `sanitizeUploadFilename` (or the exported predicate) on the basename of `body.path` in the `filesMatch` handler before resolving the target.
2. Move the predicate into `packages/workspace` next to `assertWorkspacePath` and call it from both write paths, so the rule cannot drift again.

Either way the guard itself is already written and tested in `#868` (`workspace-upload.ts`, mirrored in `services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts`); this issue is about the second entry point.

## Scope

- In: the `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` write path.
- Out: upload paths (fixed by `#868`), read paths, and the desktop client.

## Origin

Raised as finding F2 in `agent-ci-infra-bot`'s review of `#868` (`https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/868#issuecomment-6637755714`), which classed it as a follow-up rather than a blocker for that PR. Filed so the second entry point is not left behind.
