items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

On Windows, killing a runner child with POSIX-style signals does not tear down the full process tree. Desktop Windows work needs a platform adaptation that terminates the child **and** its grandchildren (e.g. `taskkill /T /F`).

PR #478 (`Closes #477` / F3.1 CAS) already embeds `terminateTree` under `services/runner/src/platform/`. That belongs to **F3.2**, not F3.1 — track and accept it here (or split it out of #478).

## Expected

- `services/runner` (and any required API call sites) obtain tree-kill via `platform/index.ts` only.
- POSIX path remains signal-based; Windows uses an explicit tree terminate.
- Unit tests tagged `os:windows` cover child + grandchild cleanup.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows tree kill
- **Preconditions:** Windows host; spawn a Node/cmd child that itself spawns a grandchild that stays alive.
- **Steps:** Call `terminateTree(child)`; wait briefly; inspect process list for child and grandchild PIDs.
- **Expected / pass:** Both PIDs are gone; helper returns success/true.

### Case 2 — POSIX unchanged
- **Preconditions:** Linux or macOS.
- **Steps:** Run existing runner process-lifecycle / posix platform tests.
- **Expected / pass:** No behaviour change vs `main`; suite green.

### Case 3 — Facade only
- **Preconditions:** PR diff for this issue.
- **Steps:** Grep runner call sites for raw `taskkill` / `process.platform === \"win32\"` outside `platform/`.
- **Expected / pass:** No direct platform branches in consumer code; all go through `platform/index.ts`.

## Related

- Split from / Follow-up for PR #478 and #477 (F3.1)
- Parent: #400
items.title: [Feature] [F3.2] Runner/API process tree terminate on Windows (terminateTree / taskkill)

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

#494 adds `scripts/lib/venv-launchers.mjs` (trampoline replace + runtime DLL copy) with portable unit tests, but:

1. Nothing in-tree calls `replaceVenvTrampolines` / `copyVenvRuntimeDlls` (`assemble-backend.mjs` / bootstrap not present yet).
2. Comments claim a closed loop with `fixVenvHome`, but that helper does not exist — after swapping the launcher, `pyvenv.cfg` `home` can still point at the build machine, so the real `python.exe` still fails off-machine.
3. Tests only compare bytes; they do not spawn `Scripts\python.exe`, so the field failures (entity not found / `0xC0000135`) are not covered.

## Expected

- Call sites in assemble-backend (pack-time) and bootstrap (first-run repair) invoke the module.
- `fixVenvHome` (or equivalent) rewrites `pyvenv.cfg` `home` to the bundled interpreter root.
- A Windows smoke test builds a uv venv, relocates it, spawns `Scripts\python.exe -c "..."`, and asserts exit 0 with `sys.prefix` at the new path.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — pack-time wiring
- **Preconditions:** Payload contains a uv-created venv whose `Scripts\python.exe` is a trampoline; assemble-backend runs.
- **Steps:** Inspect `Scripts\python.exe` and `pyvenv.cfg` after assemble.
- **Expected / pass:** Launcher is a real CPython stub (no `uv trampoline` marker); `home` points at the bundled python root; runtime DLLs sit beside the launcher.

### Case 2 — first-run bootstrap repair
- **Preconditions:** `dataDir\envs` still has pre-fix trampolines (reinstall with valid unpack stamp).
- **Steps:** Start the shell once on a clean machine without system Python.
- **Expected / pass:** Bootstrap replaces trampolines, copies DLLs, fixes `home`; each venv `python.exe -c "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"` exits 0.

### Case 3 — Windows spawn smoke (CI or labeled job)
- **Preconditions:** `os:windows` (or equivalent) test runner with a bundled/minimal CPython + uv.
- **Steps:** Create uv venv → move tree → `spawn(Scripts/python.exe, ["-c", "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"])`.
- **Expected / pass:** Exit code 0; printed prefix equals the relocated venv path. Byte-only unit tests alone do not satisfy this case.

## Context

Refs #494, #493. Non-blocking Follow-up from HongyeZhou review of shell.04. #494 should use `Refs #493` until this loop lands (or fold wiring into the same PR).
items.title: [Feature] win-desktop-client: wire venv-launchers + fixVenvHome + Windows spawn smoke

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

`win-desktop-client/` is an independent pnpm workspace (not listed in the root `pnpm-workspace.yaml` packages: `config / apps/* / services/* / packages/*`). Architecture checks and `tsconfig.tests.json` also skip it. As a result, install / typecheck / unit-test failures under this tree are invisible to GitHub Actions (see #486: missing patch and empty `tsconfig` include were only found by local runs).

## Expected

A CI job (or matrix entry) runs on changes under `win-desktop-client/**` and exercises at least:

- `pnpm install` (lockfile present)
- `pnpm typecheck` (when sources exist)
- `pnpm test` for portable Node tests

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — install gate
- **Preconditions:** PR that only touches `win-desktop-client/` and references a missing `patchedDependencies` file (or otherwise breaks install).
- **Steps:** Open the PR; wait for CI.
- **Expected / pass:** The new job fails with a clear install error; root jobs that ignore this tree may still be green.

### Case 2 — typecheck / test gate
- **Preconditions:** PR adds a TypeScript error under `win-desktop-client/src/` or a failing `test/*.test.ts`.
- **Steps:** Open the PR; wait for CI.
- **Expected / pass:** typecheck or test step fails; merge is blocked by the required check once wired.

### Case 3 — no-op on unrelated paths
- **Preconditions:** PR only changes `apps/web/` (or another root package).
- **Steps:** Open the PR.
- **Expected / pass:** The win-desktop-client job is skipped or stays green without installing Electron unnecessarily.

## Context

Refs #486, #485. Non-blocking Follow-up from HongyeZhou review of shell.01.
items.title: [Feature] win-desktop-client: add CI job for independent Electron workspace

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

POSIX `chmod 0600` only toggles the read-only bit on Windows NTFS and does **not** strip inherited group/world access. Secrets, bootstrap tokens, and similar owner-only files need an ACL adaptation (`icacls` inheritance strip + grant current user).

PR #478 embeds `restrictToOwner` / `restrictToOwnerSync` under `services/api` and `services/runner` platform layers while claiming only F3.1 (#477). Track **F3.3** here so scope and AC are explicit (or split out of #478).

## Expected

- Sensitive write sites that previously `chmod`'d to owner-only use `restrictToOwner` via `platform/os` (api) / `platform` (runner).
- POSIX keeps `chmod`; Windows uses icacls with inheritance removed.
- Highest-sensitivity stores (e.g. master key / SSH private key paths) are included or explicitly deferred with rationale.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows ACL tightened
- **Preconditions:** Windows host; create a temp file that inherits group-readable ACLs.
- **Steps:** Call `restrictToOwner(file)`; run `icacls <file>` and inspect DACL.
- **Expected / pass:** Inheritance removed; current user has access; unintended group/world ACE gone (or equivalent owner-only outcome documented in the test).

### Case 2 — POSIX unchanged
- **Preconditions:** Linux or macOS.
- **Steps:** Run posix platform + existing secrets/bootstrap unit tests.
- **Expected / pass:** Mode bits still applied as on `main`; suite green.

### Case 3 — Sync path at startup
- **Preconditions:** Windows; data dir owned by another principal (or simulated failure).
- **Steps:** Exercise `restrictToOwnerSync` on bootstrap/token paths.
- **Expected / pass:** Failure mode is explicit (error message), not a silent weaken; documented in PR/issue notes.

## Related

- Split from / Follow-up for PR #478 and #477 (F3.1)
- Parent: #400
- Note from #478 review: `store/secrets.ts` / `store/ssh-config.ts` may still rely on raw `chmod` — include or call out as residual risk.
items.title: [Feature] [F3.3] Owner-restrict file ACLs on Windows (icacls / restrictToOwner)

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Background and environment

During a source installation on a Debian 13 cloud desktop on 2026-10-11, using main commit `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`, two problems required manual investigation:

1. The desktop terminal did not inherit the outbound proxy environment. The initial managed micromamba download failed with `ECONNREFUSED`; an installation environment with the required network configuration could complete the download.
2. When the adapter inherited a SOCKS proxy configuration, it failed to start because `socksio` was missing, affecting access to the application.

The first observation is an environment-triggered failure, not proof of a downloader implementation defect. The second has a concrete dependency declaration gap.

## Conditions and observed behavior

### A. Different proxy environments across installation and runtime entry points

- External access required a proxy, but the terminal initiating scientific-environment preparation did not inherit the corresponding configuration.
- The micromamba connection was refused and scientific-environment preparation could not complete.
- Installation succeeded through an official download/install path with the necessary network configuration, retaining the pinned version and SHA-256 verification.
- The scientific environment subsequently became ready, with Python 3.12, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and Matplotlib available.

### B. SOCKS configuration prevents adapter startup

- Create a clean adapter environment from the declared project dependencies and start it with a valid SOCKS proxy configuration.
- During HTTP client initialization, the missing socksio dependency prevents adapter startup.
- In this installation, adding socksio from official PyPI to the adapter's isolated environment restored startup; API health and page HTML checks then passed.

Source references:
- [Adapter declares plain httpx](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/pyproject.toml#L19-L25).
- [HTTP clients are constructed during startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/app.py#L47-L63).

## User impact

- Users may have already installed the source and other dependencies, yet still be blocked at first startup or scientific-environment preparation, preventing access to the workbench or relevant computations.
- Users must investigate differences between terminal and child-process proxy environments, and may need to install undeclared dependencies manually.
- A component-level failure can look like a failed installation of the entire application, leading to unnecessary reinstalls. This is not evidence that micromamba itself is unsuitable or unavailable.

## Expected behavior and proposed improvements

1. Unify installation/startup preflight checks: inspect the actual child process's proxy configuration, connectivity to required download sources, and dependencies for the selected proxy protocol. Report redacted status, never credentials.
2. Declare and lock SOCKS support, for example through `httpx[socks]`. Define the proxy boundary between loopback service calls and external requests, including correct `NO_PROXY` handling.
3. Identify the failing component, stage, underlying cause, and actionable next step. After configuration is corrected, allow retrying the failed step while reusing verified tools and caches.
4. Report Web entry point, adapter, and scientific-environment readiness separately instead of treating partial readiness as an all-or-nothing result.

The repository already has [download retry and cache mechanisms](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs#L179-L295), as well as [classified errors and mirror/preinstalled-tool recovery guidance](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/environment-store.ts#L1138-L1173). The goal is to connect these capabilities into a coherent first-run experience, not to replace the downloader.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean adapter environment starts with HTTP/SOCKS proxy configurations without manually installing undeclared dependencies.
- [ ] Missing or incorrect proxy configuration produces redacted, actionable diagnostics while retaining the underlying error.
- [ ] Correcting configuration allows retrying the failed step and reusing verified artifacts, without clearing all data or reinstalling.
- [ ] Version pinning and hash verification remain enforced; recovery does not disable TLS verification.
- [ ] Tests cover no proxy, HTTP/SOCKS proxies, unreachable download sources, and successful retry after correction; installation documentation is updated.

Related: #29 (actionable dependency preflight), #213 and #229 (onboarding feedback). This issue focuses on the observed proxy-related failures and first-install recovery experience.
items.title: [Bug] Improve proxy-aware installation: declare SOCKS support and unify preflight and recovery

items.author: hsliuustc0106
items.body:
## Cross-check needed

cc @zhaozhaozz @zy95-12 @HongyeZhou

### Three-layer defaults (important)
These coexist and are easy to conflate:

1. **Schema fallback**: `DEFAULT_SKILL_SELECTION_MODE = "all"` when unset (`packages/schema/src/runtime-settings.ts`).
2. **New Project product default**: `withDefaultProjectSkillSettings` writes `skillSelectionMode: "selected"` + empty `enabledSkillIds` / libraries (Skill Library intent: avoid silently expanding capability).
3. **JiuwenSwarm force-all**: on start, `http/index.ts` calls `store.useEverySkillEverywhere()` so the **effective** mode is `all` while Swarm is the backend (stored `selected` is kept and applies again when switching back to native).

Box smoke on Swarm therefore seeing `all` is **expected**, not accidental.

### Observation (box smoke, 2026-10-24 Asia/Shanghai)
- SHA: `main@9eb45d75`
- Backend: **JiuwenSwarm** (force-all path)
- Model: Zhipu `glm-5.3-flash`
- ~17 shipped skills effective, `thinkingEffort: high`
- Trivial user prompt → **~38k input tokens** (chat/history ≈ **165 bytes**)
- First visible assistant text ≈ **20s** wall

Progressive disclosure is **already implemented** (`docs/en/developer-docs/skill-progressive-disclosure.md`: metadata/path in prompt, body on demand). It does **not** prevent metadata/tool-surface growth when the effective selected set is the whole catalog under `all` / Swarm force-all.

### Questions for maintainers
1. Should end-user UX optimize for **Project `selected`** or accept **Swarm force-all** as the primary path?
2. Is there appetite to change schema DEFAULT, Swarm force-all, or both?
3. Have you seen the same **TTFT / cost** under Swarm vs native?

### Proposed performance watch split (do not mix into one Nightly bucket)
1. **UX / API latency lane** — queue → context → **TTFT** → run wall; short daily probe (`live.mjs ttft` + one real short chat), measure under **both** native and JiuwenSwarm, and under `all` vs `selected`.
2. **Correctness lane (existing L3 ×9)** — tool/files/cancel/etc.; keep **out of** TTFT gates.
3. **Research quality lane (L4 Nightly)** — DRB/Biomni/etc. as quality signal, **not** first-token UX.

### Possible directions (not proposing a fix yet)
- Keep progressive disclosure; also shrink **effective set** under Swarm (or stop force-all)
- Align schema DEFAULT with new-Project `selected`
- Cap / warn when resolved skill metadata size exceeds a threshold
- Surface skill-token cost in Usage / composer

### Non-goals
- Nightly research-bench red streak root-cause (separate)
- Tool-call accuracy eval (separate)

### Test coverage gap
- Unit coverage exists for settings semantics (`store.test.ts`: selected / all / `useEverySkillEverywhere`).
- **No CI gate** on TTFT or skill-token size; `live.mjs ttft()` logs only.
- Progressive disclosure tests do not cap catalog size under `all`.

Cross-check so far: skills-side review agrees the three-layer story; DigitalMate has no parallel issue. Nearby: #508, #93, #141.
items.title: [Bug] Swarm/default skillSelectionMode=all inflates context (~38k tokens) and TTFT (~20s)

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: 8a1b7dbd95c149489c75d01defcd079d
Branch: dev1/fix/fetch-document-codepoint-truncation
Base: 1e8865838ce8
At: 2026-10-29T04:57:48Z

## What is wrong

`document()` in `packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts:105-107` truncates the vendor's text with a raw `slice(0, 4_096)`, so a UTF-16 surrogate pair that straddles the budget is cut in half and the document handed to the model ends with a lone high surrogate.

## Reproduction (live main `1e8865838ce80b8519063e26b5910a5b23ff2027`)

`renderExaContents`/`renderTavilyExtract` both funnel through `document()`. Same logic copied verbatim, run with `node`:

```
$ node -e 'const MAX=4096; const text="x".repeat(MAX-1)+"😀"; console.log(JSON.stringify(text.slice(0,MAX).slice(-2)))'
"\ud83d"
```

The last code unit is `0xd83d` (high surrogate) with no low surrogate after it - an unpaired surrogate in the fetched document.

## Expected

Truncate at a code-point boundary, the way `#663` now does it for the artifact preview: drop the whole character instead of half of it, so the result is never longer than the budget and never contains a new unpaired surrogate.

## Why it matters

`web_fetch` output is fed back into prompts and can be cached and re-serialised as JSON; an unpaired surrogate is invalid UTF-8 text and `JSON.stringify` escapes it into a `\ud83d` sequence the model reads as a broken glyph. The same defect was reported for the artifact preview in `#660` and fixed there by `#663`; this call site is a different module (`packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts`) and is still raw, so this is not a duplicate.

## Fix scope

One small helper in the same file (or reuse of an existing code-point truncation helper if one is exported) plus its call in `document()`; tests next to the existing `renderExaContents`/`renderTavilyExtract` ones. About 10-15 lines, no new dependency.
items.title: [Bug] web_fetch document truncation splits a surrogate pair at the 4096-char budget

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem and user outcome

Researchers need to retrieve domain-specific scientific data through MCP and use it in traceable ScienceDiscovery workflows. Literature search alone does not satisfy this need: the objects are expression datasets, bioactivity measurements, variant assertions, and protein structures.

Provide supported, discoverable connections to **GEO, ChEMBL, ClinVar, RCSB PDB, and AlphaFold Protein Structure Database**, with reliable retrieval, explicit data boundaries, and provenance that survives downstream analysis.

## Context and existing implementation

Request inspired by this article: https://x.com/servasyy_ai/article/2112052770287284550
Related project documentation: https://aipoch.com/docs/guides/connectors/

Source inspection of ScienceDiscovery at baseline `0d31e155` found existing MCP implementations for GEO, ChEMBL, ClinVar, and PDB in `services/gateway/src/sciencediscovery_gateway/public_biomed_mcp.py`, plus manifests in `packages/mcp-sources/src/public-biomed.ts`. UniProt, Ensembl, and Reactome provide additional reusable patterns. No built-in AlphaFold DB adapter was found in that inspection.

This is a request to complete and validate domain database support, reusing existing adapters. It does not assume these databases are entirely unsupported. The baseline assessment was static inspection, not a live end-to-end availability test; recheck the target version before implementation.

## Requested scope

| Database | Required user-facing capabilities | Domain details to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GEO | Search studies, retrieve study/sample metadata, discover actual processed/supplementary files, and download selected analysis-ready data | GSE/GSM/GPL identifiers, organism, sample conditions, platform, and whether data are raw counts, normalized values, or other processed data |
| ChEMBL | Search molecules/targets, retrieve bioactivity measurements with useful filters, and perform similarity searches | Molecule/target/assay IDs, assay type, organism, relation, value, units, confidence, and source references |
| ClinVar | Search/lookup variants and retrieve individual clinical assertions | VCV/RCV/SCV identifiers where applicable, assembly, condition, review status, dates, and conflicting submissions |
| RCSB PDB | Search/lookup experimental structures and download supported structure files | PDB ID, experimental method, resolution where applicable, chains/entities, ligands, and source/version metadata |
| AlphaFold DB | Retrieve available predictions by protein accession and download model/confidence files when available | UniProt accession, model identifier/version, source URLs, and confidence information |

AlphaFold DB retrieval is separate from running AlphaFold prediction software. New prediction compute infrastructure is outside this request. PubMed and other literature databases are also outside this scope.

## Integration requirements

- Reuse the MCP client, connector selection, permission/audit, and artifact download mechanisms. Prefer official provider APIs behind MCP adapters; do not require providers to expose MCP themselves.
- Make supported sources and operations discoverable, with setup instructions and any credential requirements. Enable the source for the intended Session and support both Inspector validation and Agent use.
- Return structured domain data and standard evidence records with stable identifiers, source links, retrieval time, and provider version/release when available. Retain source caveats and attribution.
- A generic custom MCP connection currently preserves raw/structured content but produces empty standardized `records`; calling a tool successfully alone must not count as complete evidence integration.
- Transfer large datasets and structure files through governed artifact jobs, with source metadata and integrity checks. Keep file bytes out of model context and distinguish a proposed download from a completed, verified artifact.
- Handle pagination, provider rate limits, timeouts, invalid identifiers, missing records/files, and partial failures explicitly. Do not silently present a capped subset as the complete dataset.
- Document scientific limits: GEO standard matrix/SOFT candidate paths do not enumerate all supplementary files; not every expression matrix is suitable for count-based analysis; ClinVar submissions can conflict; experimental and predicted structures must remain distinguishable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the target version, document the existing capability and remaining gap for each of the five databases.
- [ ] All five sources can be configured/enabled and successfully called from the intended Session; tool inputs and results are inspectable and audited.
- [ ] Each database has a representative live provider validation with recorded identifiers, commands/steps, expected results, and actual results. Record unavailable-provider cases as blocked rather than passed.
- [ ] GEO: discover actual files for a public study, retrieve relevant sample annotations, and download/verify a real selected matrix. Validate its data type and dimensions before downstream analysis; report when count-based analysis is inappropriate.
- [ ] ChEMBL: retrieve a target/molecule-linked activity set with explicit assay/measurement constraints, preserving units and relations, and verify pagination or clearly disclosed limits.
- [ ] ClinVar: retrieve assertions and preserve conflicting classifications/review status without reducing them to one unsupported consensus.
- [ ] PDB: retrieve an experimental structure, complete a verified CIF/PDB download, and demonstrate that a downstream analysis step can read the artifact and inspect its metadata.
- [ ] AlphaFold DB: retrieve a known available prediction by accession, verify a model download and available confidence metadata, and clearly identify it as predicted.
- [ ] Returned evidence and downloaded artifacts retain their source identifiers/URLs and retrieval metadata in subsequent analysis outputs.
- [ ] Automated tests cover domain result normalization and representative missing-record, malformed-input, rate-limit, and download-failure paths. Product-level validation covers connector selection, Inspector/Agent execution, and completed artifacts; mocked success alone is insufficient.
- [ ] User documentation describes supported operations, limitations, configuration, and reproducible examples for each source.

Implementation may be split into linked changes, but this feature remains open until the full five-database acceptance scope is verified.

## Child work item — PDB entity and chemical-component identity verification (migrated from #448)

The PDB connector must let researchers verify a structure’s protein target and ligand identity against a ChEMBL record without relying on structure titles or compound names. This is a bounded sub-item of the PDB acceptance scope above, not a separate database integration.

### Required MCP operations

- Expose discoverable polymer and nonpolymer entity identifiers from an entry lookup (or an equivalent bounded entry expansion).
- `pdb_get_polymer_entity(pdb_id, entity_id)`: entity description/type, organism, UniProt/reference mappings, label/auth chain identifiers, sequence/coverage and construct/mutation information where available.
- `pdb_get_nonpolymer_entity(pdb_id, entity_id)`: ligand/component identity, label/auth chain mappings and provider cross-references.
- `pdb_lookup_chemical_component(component_id)`: CCD name, formula/charge, InChI, complete InChIKey, available SMILES and mapped external identifiers with provenance. Extended CCD IDs such as five-character `A1CEA` are valid.

All results must provide structured domain fields and nonempty standardized evidence records with stable identifiers, canonical URLs, retrieval time, attribution and provider version/revision where available. Missing UniProt/InChIKey mappings must remain missing; do not replace them with name-based identity assertions. Preserve salt/parent relationships, stereochemistry-aware complete identifiers, covalent/modified-component qualifications, and label versus author chain IDs.

### Required validation cases

- Positive chain: through MCP, enumerate `9OS6` entities; verify polymer entity `1` maps to UniProt `P00533`, nonpolymer entity `2` maps to CCD `A1CEA`, and `A1CEA` has complete InChIKey `OMZCMEYTWSXEPZ-UHFFFAOYSA-N`, matching ChEMBL free Canertinib `CHEMBL31965`. Preserve the distinct dihydrochloride `CHEMBL545315` and its parent relation. Display protein label/auth chain `A/A` and ligand `B/A` without conflation.
- Negative chain: retrieve `5VCW` polymer entity `1` and show UniProt `Q99640`; it must not be reported as an EGFR complex merely because Pelitinib has EGFR activity elsewhere.
- Complete a selected mmCIF artifact download using the governed artifact path, verify its checksum, read the file downstream and retain the linked cross-database evidence in saved outputs.
- Complete an Agent journey using MCP metadata tools without direct HTTPS/web-fetch fallback; separately record Inspector, stub-model and real-model evidence.
- Cover extended CCD IDs; invalid/missing entities; missing protein/chemical mappings; timeout/rate-limit/partial failure feedback; and label/auth-chain distinctions.
- Add English and Chinese documentation with the positive and negative identity-matching examples and limits.

Official reference endpoints: `/rest/v1/core/polymer_entity/9OS6/1`, `/rest/v1/core/nonpolymer_entity/9OS6/2`, `/rest/v1/core/chemcomp/A1CEA`, and `/rest/v1/core/polymer_entity/5VCW/1` at `data.rcsb.org`.
items.title: [Feature] Complete MCP integration for domain-specific scientific databases

## Goal

Make literature reports and review outcomes honestly verifiable: readers should see the evidence supporting material claims, know when evidence could not be verified, and never mistake a partial Quick review for full claim-fidelity verification.

## Workstream A — claim-to-evidence excerpts (from #415)

- [ ] For each material quantitative or clinical claim in a literature report, retain a short source excerpt or structured claim-to-evidence table with stable identifier and usable locator (for example PMID/DOI plus abstract/full-text location where available).
- [ ] Include the evidence in saved report/review artifacts without flooding model context; preserve source provenance and retrieval metadata.
- [ ] When an excerpt cannot be obtained, record an explicit evidence gap rather than silently presenting the claim as fully supported.

## Workstream B — visible unverifiable states (from #560)

- [ ] Extend the evidence/review schema with a visible `UNVERIFIABLE` status (or equivalent reasoned states such as identity unresolved and provider unavailable).
- [ ] Preserve the reason, affected claim/citation and review coverage in reports and review summaries. Do not silently discard identity-resolution or provider-availability findings.
- [ ] Keep the existing policy distinction: provider failure is not proof that a citation is false; it is an explicit limitation on verification.
- [ ] Align reviewer Skill instructions and runtime normalization so emitted states are representable and auditable.

## Workstream C — truthful automatic-review scope (follow-up to closed #414)

- [ ] A format/provenance-only Quick review must present itself as partial/format-only and disclose skipped claim checks with a reason.
- [ ] A claim-checked literature review must identify which claims were checked, supported, unsupported or unverifiable.
- [ ] Add regressions for stale report reviews, missing primary deliverables and the prior false-looking `ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED` Quick outcome.

## Validation

- [ ] Reproduce the CRISPR base-editing literature-report scenario from #415 and verify human-readable claim evidence or explicit gaps.
- [ ] Cover identifier mismatch, unresolved identity, unavailable provider, conflicting evidence, missing locator and provider timeout paths.
- [ ] Test Quick/Deep UI and saved artifact semantics independently; mocked provider success alone is insufficient.
- [ ] Document the distinction among supported, unsupported, unverifiable and not-reviewed claims.

Consolidates the unfinished scope of #415 and #560 and retains the relevant transparency regression from closed #414.
items.title: [Feature] Make literature evidence verifiable and review coverage explicit

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
## Goal

Track the remaining external-agent interoperability work after PR #424 merged the initial Specialist runtime slice. This issue deliberately keeps two protocol directions separate while coordinating their shared safety, session and artifact requirements.

## Delivered baseline

PR #424 merged support for explicit Specialist tasks using Codex, Claude Code and ACP executables, normalized task/event/handoff behavior, independent concurrent Workspace/Runner execution, configuration cards and thin runtime diagnostics. It does **not** complete either original Issue’s full acceptance criteria.

## Workstream A — ScienceDiscovery hosts external Specialist runtimes (remaining from #385)

Keep the existing Specialist model and require explicit `task(specialistId=…)` targeting for non-native execution. The platform remains the authority for Workspace, permissions, secrets, artifacts, audit and cancellation.

- [ ] Validate and document a successful live-auth matrix for supported Codex, Claude Code and ACP providers, including task completion, cancellation, timeout and declared-artifact handoff. Report unavailable credentials/providers as blocked, never passed.
- [ ] Decide and implement the supported iCode adapter path, or explicitly defer it with product rationale.
- [ ] Complete the Skills/MCP/tool bridge so an external runtime can request platform-governed tools without gaining undeclared native permissions.
- [ ] Finish the product configuration surface aligned with #278: persisted/this-run/alternate credential choices, usable error recovery and no secret leakage to catalog bodies, argv, logs or artifacts.
- [ ] Add the deferred UX: runtime picker/probe, fallback controls and handoff/diagnostics visibility.
- [ ] Add the deferred reliability coverage: multi-SDK stress, escape/isolation regressions, protocol backpressure/error bounds and process-crash recovery semantics.
- [ ] Evaluate deferred orchestration/operations separately: quota/priority/dependency graphs, shared pools only with an isolation design, and fuller metrics/cluster/multi-tenant monitoring.

## Workstream B — ScienceDiscovery is an ACP v1 Agent for editors (remaining from #64)

Editors are ACP Clients; ScienceDiscovery is the spawned ACP Agent. This is not the same as Workstream A, where ScienceDiscovery drives an external agent.

- [ ] Provide a supported ACP v1 stdio JSON-RPC entry point and `initialize` capability negotiation; do not multiplex it with MCP stdio or require a browser first.
- [ ] Implement session lifecycle mapping: `session/new`, `session/prompt`, streaming `session/update`, `session/cancel`, recoverable Project/Session/Run context and absolute workspace mapping.
- [ ] Map ACP permission requests to the existing governance and sandbox path; the ACP route must not be less restrictive than the Web UI.
- [ ] Return standards-compliant JSON-RPC errors and advertise only implemented capabilities; document any research-specific extensions.
- [ ] Verify against an actual ACP Client (for example Zed or a VS Code ACP extension): launch, prompt, streamed text, at least one tool call and denied permission behavior.
- [ ] Add unit, conformance and isolated E2E coverage for version negotiation, cancellation, authentication if enabled, sandbox equivalence and secret/session-body log redaction.
- [ ] Publish editor configuration documentation. ACP Registry publication is a separate product decision and must not block local interoperability.

## Shared boundaries

- Secrets never enter Specialist catalog bodies, argv, artifacts or unauthenticated ACP traffic.
- Existing sandbox, artifact provenance and permission controls remain authoritative.
- ACP v2 remains non-default until it is stable and separately accepted.

Supersedes the remaining scope of #385 and #64. PR #424 is delivered baseline, not proof that the above acceptance is complete.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
## Context

`GET /health` and `GET /api/health` on the API are answered before authentication: they are the first route in the request handler in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`. That is deliberate. Container health checks call the endpoint without a token: the `Dockerfile` `HEALTHCHECK` and the `docker-compose.yml` healthcheck both run `curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:4310/health`. The Runner's own `GET /health` is unauthenticated as well. `packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts` relies on that being known: when it connects to a direct Runner, it checks the token against an authenticated endpoint instead.

The question came up in the review of #261, which adds `agent: { executor, subagents }` to the API's `/health`. That field matters little next to what the endpoint already returns, so this issue is about the endpoint as a whole.

## What an unauthenticated caller receives today

From the API's `/health`:

- `sandboxNetwork`: the administrator's sandbox network settings, including `allowedDomains` and `allowPrivateNetwork`, plus the Runner's network capability.
- `runner`: the Runner's whole health record, passed through as-is. That includes `executionUser`, `platform`, `runnerVersion`, `sandbox`, `seccompBaseline`, `executionTimeoutMs`, the output and workspace limits, and the scientific-environment and NPU capabilities.
- `workspace`: the upload and workspace quotas.
- `memoryGraph` status and `milestone`; with #261, also `agent`.

The Runner's `/health` returns the same Runner record directly.

## Exposure

By default the API and the Runner both bind `127.0.0.1`, and Docker Compose publishes on `127.0.0.1`, so a default install shows this only to the local machine. The endpoint reaches the network in two cases:

- A user sets `SCIENCE_AGENT_PUBLISH_HOST=0.0.0.0` to open the UI to other machines.
- A user starts a Runner on another machine for remote execution, which has to listen on a reachable address.

An unauthenticated caller then learns the sandbox egress allowlist, whether the sandbox may reach private networks, the user commands run as, and the exact Runner version. None of that is a credential or user data, but it is the reconnaissance an attacker of the sandbox would want first.

## Proposal

- Keep `/health` public, but reduce the unauthenticated response to liveness: `service` and `status` for the API, `status` for the Runner. That is all the container health checks read.
- Return the detail only to a caller that presents a valid token, either on the same route or on a separate authenticated one. The web client already sends its bearer token on every request, including both of its `/health` reads (memory-graph status and workspace limits). The E2E helpers `requireRealStack()` and `requireAgentStack()` would send `E2E_API_TOKEN`.
- Stop the API from passing the Runner's full record through any unauthenticated response.
- Add tests asserting that an unauthenticated `/health` on either service exposes nothing beyond liveness, and that the health checks still pass.

Not in scope: what the authenticated health record contains.
items.title: [Bug] security(api): Unauthenticated /health returns deployment details, not just liveness

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
## Reproduction

On a clean checkout of `main` @ `69f40c9f` where workspace packages have not been built:

```bash
cd apps/web
node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx
```

Result on this machine: **448 tests, 385 pass, 63 fail**, and every failure is the same module resolution error from the `.tsx` files:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module
'.../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/operational-logging/dist/diagnostics.js'
imported from .../apps/web/src/ErrorDiagnosticActions.tsx
```

Single-test repro: `node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/AuthTokenPrompt.test.tsx` → exit 1, same error.

It goes away only after `packages/operational-logging` is built (`tsc -p packages/operational-logging/tsconfig.json`), i.e. the web suite silently depends on a build step that its own `test` script does not perform.

## Current behaviour vs expected

`packages/operational-logging/package.json` maps the runtime entry to a build artifact:

```json
"exports": {
  ".":             { "types": "./src/index.ts",       "default": "./dist/index.js" },
  "./diagnostics": { "types": "./src/diagnostics.ts", "default": "./dist/diagnostics.js" }
}
```

Types resolve to `src/`, but the runtime entry resolves to `dist/`, so an unbuilt tree makes `apps/web` (which depends on this package as `workspace:*`, `apps/web/package.json:13`) fail at import time. `apps/web`'s `test` script is plain `tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` and has no build step; CI passes only because the pipeline builds first.

Expected: `apps/web` tests run on a clean checkout without a manual build of the workspace dependency — either the in-repo runtime entry points at the TS source (tsx/vite compile it) or the test script builds what it needs.

## Code evidence

- `packages/operational-logging/package.json` — `exports["./diagnostics"].default` = `./dist/diagnostics.js` while `types` = `./src/diagnostics.ts`; no `dist/` in the repository.
- `apps/web/package.json:13` — `"@sciencediscovery/operational-logging": "workspace:*"`.
- `apps/web/package.json` scripts — `"test": "tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx"` (no build).
- Failure site: `apps/web/src/ErrorDiagnosticActions.tsx` imports `@sciencediscovery/operational-logging/diagnostics`.

## Suggested red test / acceptance

No new unit test is needed — the red state is the suite itself:

```bash
rm -rf packages/operational-logging/dist
cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts     # ts files pass today
cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.tsx    # 63 ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND today
```

Acceptance: with `dist/` absent, `tsx --test tests/*.test.tsx` reports **0 `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`** and the same pass count as with a built tree (448/448 on the tree where this was measured).

## Duplicate check (open + closed)

- `"operational-logging"` → no issue about its `exports` map or the missing build step.
- `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` → 0 hits in issues.
- `apps/web test` / web suite build → no open issue; `#467` is a UI fix, `#632` a feature.
- No open PR changes `packages/operational-logging/package.json` or the `apps/web` test script.

Found and measured by ScienceDiscovery while prewarming the web worktree for the `#646` sprint (448 tests, 63 `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` failures, worktree unmodified).
items.title: [Bug] apps/web test suite dies on a clean tree: 63/448 tests hit ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for the unbuilt operational-logging dist

- **B — split (our preference)**: #617 is reduced to the product fix, and one PR implements this issue.

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Motivation

Long-running offline computations and Agent conversations have different lifecycles. An Agent turn can finish while a training, simulation, or batch-processing task continues running. After evaluation, this is a feature-design topic about coordination between offline tasks and Agents, rather than a defect in turn completion.

This issue replaces #434 and preserves its motivating scenario.

## Motivating scenario

In the NatureBench reproduction session `93f897ca-cefe-4e7b-932d-8339cbef1459`, run `84d71b8a-77dd-42a7-bc81-15e326b14cb1` completed while a background `python run.py --instances mop_sc` computation continued. The final computation took approximately 1,587.7 seconds and produced `predictions.npy` with shape `(5693,)`.

The user had to inspect host processes and wait for the output manually. Starting another Agent run could also launch duplicate work. An Agent promising to return after a wall-clock delay is not a reliable scheduling mechanism.

## Feature scope

Design how long-running offline tasks collaborate with Agents across turns:

- Give supported offline tasks a queryable identity and lifecycle, with ownership linked to the originating session/run.
- Make ongoing computation visible even after the initiating Agent turn finishes.
- Let a later turn inspect, await, or resume coordination with the same task without starting duplicate computation.
- Define how task completion, failure, cancellation, and results become available to the user and Agent.
- Define the default turn-completion policy when a task is still running, including whether explicit detachment is required.
- Document lifecycle limits, including runtime/service restarts and the treatment of processes launched outside the supported task mechanism.

## Design decisions before implementation

- Turn completion: wait for the task, require explicit detach, or register it in the background and notify.
- Ownership and persistence: session-level versus run-level handles, and restart behavior.
- Minimum user interface: how users discover active tasks, inspect progress, and retrieve results.
- Agent continuation: explicit user-driven await/resume versus automatic completion notification or continuation.
- Delivery decomposition: build on existing execution/query/wait capabilities and split implementation into reviewable changes.

These are open design questions; this issue does not select a policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- A user starts a representative long-running computation and can distinguish Agent-turn completion from task completion.
- The same supported task remains discoverable and queryable across turns according to the documented lifecycle.
- The Agent can inspect or await that task and retrieve its final result without launching a duplicate.
- Completion, failure, and cancellation have defined, verifiable user-visible outcomes.
- The chosen turn-completion and restart policies are documented and covered by matching end-to-end scenarios.

## Related work

- #434: original report and evidence; superseded by this feature proposal.
- #439: redirected output buffering. Log buffering is a separate concern; coordinate where progress reporting intersects.
items.title: [Feature] Coordinate long-running offline tasks with Agents across turns

### Background

Follow-up to #96, under the backend migration tracked in #84. This issue carries forward the unfinished scope of #96 for release 0.4.0. Closing #96 is an administrative handover, not a claim that its original acceptance criteria have all passed.

Code review baseline: main at `5a86d0593a887e825d3a3da136f760b62807f797` (2026-10-28). This assessment is based on static inspection, not a fresh full acceptance run.

### Existing behavior to preserve

- Keep the existing Runner and its bwrap / Seatbelt sandbox. Do not switch to jiuwenbox or re-enable JiuwenSwarm host execution/file tools.
- Existing environment, execution and workspace functionality remains available through the legacy API behind the adapter proxy.
- Sandbox network settings already have permission-epoch rotation and persistent-kernel teardown behavior in the legacy API. Preserve and verify it rather than treating it as missing.

- [ ] Inventory every interface row from #96, including the expanded Runner-specific environment paths. Record its current owner, downstream target, existing coverage and remaining work. Preserve the original interface scope; explicitly justify any row requiring no migration.
- [ ] Complete adapter routing and necessary adaptation for local Runner environments, environment setup/revisions, execution records/status/logs/cancellation, kernel teardown, workspace listing/files/sync/deletion, and local Runner list/detail/connect/probe. Replace reliance on the generic legacy API fallback for this scope with explicit ownership and dispatch; reuse existing implementation where possible instead of rewriting the Runner.

## 背景 / 输入

NatureBench 复现会话在 run 前已通过 API 将 `approvalMode` 设为 `always_allow`：

```http
PATCH /api/sessions/{sessionId}
{"approvalMode":"always_allow"}
```

随后 Agent 大量调用工具（读文件、装依赖、跑 python、写报告等）。日志：`jiuwenswarm.log`。

## 问题是什么

即便会话级 `always_allow`，运行中仍出现大量 **`allow_once` 且 `persisted=False`** 风格的授权记录（约百余次量级），审批噪声大、不粘滞。长复现任务的可观测性被权限流水淹没；也与用户对「Always allow = 本会话不再追问」的心智模型不符。

（权限文案/网络同意相关体验另见 #392、#393。）

## 我们怎么规避的

- 仍设 `always_allow`，减少 UI 卡死概率。
- 监控与成功判据改看 workspace 文件与 run 状态，不依赖权限流水是否「干净」。

## 期望应该是什么样

1. `always_allow` 应对该 session（或同 permission epoch）的同类工具调用真正粘滞，而不是每次 `allow_once` + `persisted=False`。
2. 日志/UI 在 always_allow 下折叠或汇总授权，避免百级噪音。
3. 文档写清：哪些动作仍会突破 always_allow（若有硬例外），并与设置文案一致。

## 相关

- #392 Permission card: "Allow same type" is unclear
- #393 Resume after a sandbox network block needs three consecutive approvals
items.title: [Usability] session always_allow still floods allow_once / non-persisted authorizations

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem
On #381 head `fb2fe785` (Fixes #324), in Ask mode with a domain-allowlist policy, resuming a blocked retrieval takes three cards in a row:
1. **Run a shell script** (approve the original `run_shell`)
2. **Sandbox network** for the observed denied host ("Continue the sandbox retrieval blocked by this execution")
3. **Run a shell script** again, for the NEW `run_shell` that carries `network_authorization_id`

Every step is correct by itself, but together they are heavy for a single user intent ("let this retrieval reach host X").

## Expected
One network decision is enough to resume. The re-run that consumes the one-use network token should not ask again for shell approval the user just gave, as long as it is the same kind of execution.

## Proposal / security considerations
- Reuse the prior shell approval only for the token re-run: same Session/Agent/run, same Runner, and the token is consumed exactly once.
- Do not carry the approval over if the command changes materially. At minimum, show the new command in the network card or require re-approval when it differs from the blocked execution. Otherwise a token re-run becomes a way to run unreviewed code with network access.
- Never inherit Always Allow / direct-execution consent; keep child Agents and later runs excluded, as #381 already does.
- Alternative: merge steps 2 and 3 into a single card ("Allow network to X and re-run this command").

## Context
Refs #381, #324. Observed in a local box run (API + bubblewrap runner + egress gateway, scripted model).

## Verification cases
1. **Baseline repro (current behaviour)**
   - Preconditions: Ask approval mode; sandbox network `domain-allowlist` with `allowedDomains: ["pypi.org"]`; the model calls `run_shell` with `curl -sS -m 8 -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' https://example.com/`.
   - Steps: Allow once on the shell card → allow once on the `example.com:443` network card → the model issues a NEW `run_shell` with the returned `network_authorization_id`.
   - Expected (today): A third "Run a shell script" card appears. After it is approved, the first execution has failed (`CONNECT tunnel failed`, HTTP 000) and the second has completed with HTTP 200 (2 executions in total).
2. **Same command, token re-run: single network decision**
   - Preconditions/Steps: As in 1.
   - Expected (after fix): Exactly 2 cards in total (shell, network). The token re-run with the identical command starts without another shell card and ends with HTTP 200.
3. **Different command must re-ask (security)**
   - Preconditions: As in 1, but the token re-run uses a different command (e.g. appends `; echo changed > marker.txt`).
   - Expected: A shell card is shown again, or the network card displays the new command before approval. It never runs silently.
4. **Token is one-use**
   - Steps: After case 2, the model calls `run_shell` a third time with the same `network_authorization_id`.
   - Expected: The call is rejected ("Unknown, consumed or foreign sandbox network authorization"), and no execution is started.
5. **No carry-over across scope**
   - Steps: Use the token or reused approval from (a) a child Agent, (b) a later run in the same Session, (c) another Runner.
   - Expected: Each is rejected or re-prompts, and no shell approval is reused.
6. **Deny path**
   - Steps: As in 1, but Deny the network card.
   - Expected: No re-run and no third card. The assistant reports the retrieval as blocked/incomplete, and the sandbox network settings are unchanged.
items.title: [Usability] Resume after a sandbox network block needs three consecutive approvals

items.body:
Follow-up to #245, criterion 3. PR #617 delivers the measurement harness and the per-request wire diagnostics, but the real relay-vs-direct measurement is **not** delivered: the team's bot host has no relay or model endpoint credentials.

## What is missing

Criterion 3 of #245 asks for a comparison of a relay endpoint against a direct endpoint with the same model alias, the same request body bytes, the same workload and the same concurrency, with wire latency reported separately from agent duration and token counts. The harness exists (`scripts/model-endpoint-compare.mjs`, delivered in #617 and covered by `scripts/model-endpoint-compare.test.mjs` against local stub endpoints). What does not exist is a run against real endpoints, so #245 stays open as partially delivered.

## Who can run it

Someone on an owner-hosted machine that has both endpoint URLs and their credentials. The team's bot host cannot: it has no model credentials, and this is not a code problem.

## Command (fill the placeholders)

```bash
node scripts/model-endpoint-compare.mjs \
  --model <model-alias> \
  --prompt-file <one-prompt.txt> \
  --a-name relay  --a-base-url <relay-base-url>  --a-token-env A_TOKEN \
  --b-name direct --b-base-url <direct-base-url> --b-token-env B_TOKEN \
  --requests 20 --concurrency 2 --timeout-ms 300000 \
  --out compare.json
```

`--body-file <identical-body.json>` may be used instead of `--prompt-file` when the exact request body must be reused. The script refuses two different model aliases and refuses a workload where the two bodies would differ, so a latency delta cannot come from a body change.

## What to do with the result

Paste the comparison table the script prints (p50/p90/p95 per endpoint, failures, tokens) and attach or link `compare.json` in #245. That closes criterion 3.

## Notes

- Endpoint tokens are read from the environment variables named by `--a-token-env` / `--b-token-env`; they are never written into the report.
- No repository change is expected from this issue: it is a measurement task, not a code task.

Related: #245, #617.

items.author: hsliuustc0106
items.body:
## Goal

Make ScienceDiscovery a useful, approachable research product. A researcher should be able to understand what it can help with, get started with clear guidance, complete a task, and return to their work confidently.

The first experience we should deliver is simple:

**Open the app → connect a model → upload a CSV and ask a question → receive a useful chart → refine and save the result.**

The application should handle routine setup and organization, ask only for decisions that matter, and explain the next step in plain language. Technical details should be available when needed.

## Why this matters

During a trial of release 0.2.0, a new user encountered welcome cards that did not navigate, confusing model setup, unexplained `Unauthorized` messages, and an interface that opened even though analysis could not run on that computer. These problems prevented the user from experiencing the product's value.

This evidence comes from one installation. Check fixes in the current release and development branch before opening duplicate work. Related public feedback includes [difficulty finding the download](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1).

## Improvements

### 1. Make the starting point obvious

- Explain the product with one concrete example and show its finished result.
- Provide prominent **Get started**, **Try an example**, and **Watch the walkthrough** actions.
- Make every suggested action work. Clearly explain unavailable actions and how to enable them.
- Offer a visible English/中文 switch and consistent wording throughout the experience.

### 2. Guide the user through setup

- Provide one recommended download and setup path for each supported computer type.
- Ask for the minimum information needed to connect a model, with helpful defaults and a clear connection test. Explain any required API key, where to obtain it, and that provider usage may incur charges.
- Handle the app's internal connection automatically where possible. If a user must reconnect, take them directly to a guided recovery step.
- Check that analysis can actually run before showing the app as ready. Explain compatibility problems early and provide a concrete next action.
- Keep advanced configuration accessible outside the ordinary setup flow.

### 3. Make everyday work feel straightforward

- Let users start with a question or a file. Create the initial project/session automatically for the guided example.
- Show understandable progress based on what is happening, such as reading data or preparing a chart. Make waiting, required input, completion, and failure easy to distinguish.
- Provide visible stop/retry actions where appropriate. Preserve the user's question and files when something fails.
- Explain errors in plain language with a recovery action; place diagnostic details behind an expandable option.
- Present the result clearly, with an explanation, supporting evidence, and access to the producing code. Make follow-up requests, saving/exporting, and returning later easy to discover.

### 4. Provide two videos that help people understand the product

**Video 1 — From opening the app to a first result (5–7 minutes).** Show a real released version: download/open, connect a model, upload the supplied CSV, ask a question, inspect the chart, request a change, and reopen the saved work. Provide the sample file, prompt, transcript, and English/Chinese captions. Show required preparation and label accelerated waits.

**Video 2 — The same task with and without ScienceDiscovery (6–8 minutes).** Use IMO 2026 Day 2 Problem 5 to compare the same model in direct conversation and in ScienceDiscovery. Focus on the viewer's experience: what they ask, how much guidance they provide, how understandable and complete the answer is, and how easily they can inspect or continue the work. Also report actual time and cost.

Keep the problem, model, and budgets comparable; review the mathematical proofs and report the observed outcome, including ties or failures. The problem's answer is the family `f(x) = x + c`, with `c >= 0`; describe it as the complete solution family. See the [original problem](https://www.imo-official.org/assets/documents/problems/2026/2026_eng.pdf) and [published reference proof](https://github.com/AxiomMath/IMO2026/blob/main/IMO2026/Q5/solution.lean).

Both videos must reflect working released behavior. Their purpose is to explain the experience and demonstrate useful outcomes. Test the app's guidance with new users, including people who have not watched the videos, and fix the points where they get stuck.

### 5. Make feedback and contribution welcoming

- Provide an obvious way to ask for help or report a problem without requiring users to understand the architecture.
- Explain where contributions are reviewed and how GitHub visitors reach that destination. The [current contribution guide](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/907382ce42e1ebfe77e24281905dec0607aaf003/CONTRIBUTING.md) routes code contributions to GitCode.
- Offer a short first-contribution guide and a few bounded tasks with named reviewers. Useful examples include improving a confusing screen, contributing an analysis example, or fixing a connector.
- Document checks newcomers can run without paid model access or special hardware, and how maintainers help with the remaining validation.

## How we know this is better

- [ ] A new user can explain what ScienceDiscovery does and identify how to start.
- [ ] On a supported computer, the user can complete the sample analysis, refine the result, and reopen the saved work without live maintainer assistance.
- [ ] Setup problems are explained before the user starts dependent work; failures preserve their inputs and offer a clear next step.
- [ ] The main journey works in English and Chinese, and the displayed controls and instructions match the released app.
- [ ] Both videos are linked from the project entry page, use actual runs, and include the materials needed to follow or inspect them.
- [ ] A new contributor can find a suitable task, run the relevant checks, submit a change, and understand the review process.

Observe ten unfamiliar users and use eight completing the sample journey without intervention as an initial target. Also record where users get stuck, whether they return the following week, and whether contributors return for another contribution. These are proposed targets, not current results.

## Delivery

Prioritize the first-use journey and recovery from the problems already observed. Validate the downloadable release, record the videos, and improve the experience with a small pilot group before broader promotion. Give each follow-up a named owner.
items.title: [Rfc] Make ScienceDiscovery easy to understand, start, and use

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Background

ScienceDiscovery is strengthening its end-to-end test coverage. We want to collect the complete user journeys that the community believes must remain continuously protected.

This RFC does not prescribe an implementation. It focuses on four questions: **What task is the user trying to complete? What outcomes must be observable? Does the scenario require a real model? Should it run as a pull-request gate or as a scheduled test?**

## How to contribute

Copy the comment template below and add one row for each proposed test scenario. Maintainers will periodically consolidate actionable feedback into the main table.

Guidelines:

- **Test scenario**: describe a complete flow from the user's goal, rather than an internal function or an isolated component.
- **Observations**: list user-visible outcomes and critical states, such as the final answer, tool calls, permissions, artifacts, citations, and recovery after a refresh.
- **Test method**: use `Mock LLM`, `Real LLM`, or `Both`, and explain why a real model is necessary when applicable.
- **Estimated token usage**: use `0 (scripted)` for Mock LLM cases; for Real LLM cases, estimate total input and output tokens for one run.
- **Estimated duration**: give the target duration for one case, excluding first-time dependency installation.
- **Priority**: use `P0` for basic platform availability, `P1` for core scientific capabilities, and `P2` for enhancements or corner cases.
- **Notes**: record environment requirements, external services, credentials, cost, side effects, candidate benchmark sources, or stability risks.

## Initial candidates

The following entries are both examples of the requested format and an initial backlog. The community is welcome to refine their priority, observations, estimates, and execution method.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Basic multi-turn conversation and refresh recovery | The run completes; the second turn uses conversation history; message order, terminal state, and refreshed content remain consistent | Mock LLM | Session, Agent Loop, History, SSE | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | No external network |
| Tool call, permission, and continued reasoning | Permission moves from pending to allowed; the tool executes once; its result returns to the model; the Agent continues and finishes | Mock LLM | Tool, Permission, Runner, Agent Loop | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a safe local tool fixture |
| Plan creation, update, and completion | Plan and step states remain ordered and correct; updates do not block tools; the final state persists and recovers | Mock LLM | Plan, Context, Workspace UI | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a deterministic tool-call sequence |
| Subagent delegation and result return | The child Agent lifecycle is complete; tool ownership is correct; the result returns to the lead Agent; reasoning continues; refresh restores the state | Mock LLM | Subagent, Team, Tool, Context | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | No external provider |
| Generate and deliver an artifact | The file exists; deliverables are distinct from temporary files; preview and download work; provenance is traceable; the final answer references the artifact | Mock LLM | Workspace, Artifact, Provenance, Tool | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | Use a local Python or Shell environment |
| Literature review | The Agent searches multiple sources, retrieves and extracts selected papers, produces traceable citations, handles source failures, and delivers a review artifact | Both | MCP, Literature Sources, Governed Download, PDF Extraction, Citation, Review | 0 mocked; 20k–60k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Real run requires network access and may depend on source availability |
| Evolve a solution | The Agent defines an objective and evaluation, runs iterative candidates, preserves checkpoints and logs, compares results, and delivers the best reproducible solution | Both | Evolve, Runner, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Candidate source: Terminal-Bench-Science |
| Data analysis | The Agent inspects an input dataset, selects and executes a valid analysis, validates intermediate results, and delivers reproducible code, figures, and conclusions | Both | Workspace, Python/R, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 10–25 min | P1 | Candidate source: BiomniBench-DA |
| AI model workflow | The Agent prepares valid model inputs, invokes the model workload, exposes execution progress, preserves outputs and environment metadata, and explains the result | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, NPU, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Candidate tools/models: Protenix, ProteinMPNN, and similar workloads; hardware availability may constrain scheduling |
| Simulation tool workflow | The Agent prepares a valid simulation, invokes the selected simulator, reports progress and failures, and delivers reproducible configuration, logs, and results | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, Tool, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Real cases may require licensed software, large dependencies, or specialized hardware |
| Memory graph | Research outputs are written to the graph with correct identities and relations; retrieval returns relevant prior context; graph-backed citations remain traceable after refresh | Both | Memory Graph, Context, Provenance, Citation | 0 mocked; 8k–25k real | 5–20 min | P1 | Mocked case can use the local backend; scheduled case may use Neo4j |
| Agent team collaboration | The lead Agent decomposes work across multiple specialists; child scopes remain isolated; progress is observable; results return to the lead and are synthesized without loss or duplication | Both | Agent Team, Subagent, Context, Permission, Trajectory | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Include concurrent child execution and one recoverable child failure |
| Idea Tree research | The Agent starts an Idea Tree run, expands and evaluates candidates, supports pause and resume, persists the tree, and delivers the selected result with its reasoning trail | Both | Idea Tree, Evolve, Workspace UI, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Validate both tree state and the user-visible explorer |

## Comment template

Copy this table into a comment. Add more rows when proposing multiple scenarios.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Describe the complete user journey | List user-visible outcomes and critical states | Mock LLM / Real LLM / Both | List related capabilities | Estimate | Estimate | P0 / P1 / P2 | Add environment, cost, dependency, or stability notes |

## Suggested areas

- Agent Loop, tools, permissions, planning, and Agent teams;
- MCP, skills, Web Search, and Web Fetch;
- literature retrieval, paper download, PDF extraction, and scientific databases;
- artifacts, provenance, evidence, claims, citations, and review;
- context compression, long-running task continuity, and error recovery;
- local and remote Runners, scientific environments, NPU workloads, and background tasks;
- settings, onboarding, observability, and critical usability journeys;
- scenarios that can reveal issues only with a Real LLM or a real external service.

## Expected outcome

Community feedback will form a prioritized E2E case backlog, divided into:

- fast Mocked E2E cases executed for every pull request;
- comprehensive Mocked and Real LLM E2E cases executed on a schedule;
- real scientific-task acceptance tests executed before a release.

This issue is for collecting and clarifying test requirements. Implementation can be split into follow-up issues and pull requests by scenario.

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## Summary and current-release boundary

Multi-agent orchestration is a core JiuwenSwarm capability. ScienceDiscovery should explicitly evaluate whether and how to reuse it, rather than silently treating our existing orchestration as the final architecture.

For this release, retain the currently validated hybrid path: **ScienceDiscovery manages delegation through `task`; JiuwenSwarm executes both the main agent and the child agents.** This RFC does not request an immediate migration or block the current release. The eventual reuse decision must be documented with implementation evidence, validation results, and trade-offs.

## Current implementation

The current debugging deployment explicitly selects the platform `task` route. This is a deployment choice, not a claim that every Swarm-backed deployment uses this route.

```text
Main agent (Swarm loop)
  -> ScienceDiscovery task orchestration
  -> Child agent (independent Swarm loop)
  -> Platform task result
  -> Main agent continues
```

ScienceDiscovery currently prepares the specialist profile, enabled MCP/skills, workspace and handoff; manages permissions, concurrency, turn/time limits and cancellation; and records child progress, results and artifacts for the existing UI. The parent receives the result when the `task` call completes.

Swarm's native route uses `subagent_spawn` and `subagent_wait`, with Swarm owning child orchestration. Its integration with ScienceDiscovery-specific bindings has not been fully validated. This does **not** mean Swarm lacks tools, permissions or lifecycle management; the question is how its mechanisms map to the platform's existing behavior.

## Problem and existing evidence

Using Swarm only as the execution engine leaves an important part of its core capability unreused, while switching delegation tools alone risks losing platform behavior. We need a deliberate ownership boundary instead of two overlapping orchestration systems.

A recent real-LLM literature-research run completed through platform `task`: two Swarm-executed children used professional literature MCP tools, returned results, and the parent produced a registered report. This validates that hybrid route only; it does not establish native `subagent_spawn` MCP inheritance, comparative quality, or benchmark-wide reliability.

## Evaluation scope

Evaluate the native route against the current hybrid baseline on the same pinned versions and comparable model/task/tool settings.

| Area | Questions to resolve |
| --- | --- |
| Delegation and scheduling | Who owns creation, concurrency, waiting, completion, and nested delegation? Can we avoid duplicate schedulers and inconsistent state? |
| Context and capabilities | How do specialist instructions, skills, model selection and enabled MCP tools reach each child's actual LLM input? What is inherited versus explicitly handed off? |
| Workspace and science outputs | How do child workspace isolation, sandbox paths, artifact registration, provenance and parent access map to Swarm? |
| Permissions and lifecycle | How are manual approval, automatic approval, cancellation, turn/time limits and partial failures preserved? |
| Results and UI | How are streaming child progress, tool events, usage, errors and final results represented in the existing UI? Does the parent reliably continue? |
| Maintenance | Which extension points already exist? Which minimal upstream fixes/hooks are missing? What platform code could actually be removed? |

Prefer native Swarm capabilities for generic agent behavior. Keep differentiated science functionality in separate modules; intrusive Swarm changes should be limited to bug fixes or necessary extension hooks, not embedding science business logic.

## Candidate outcomes — not a predetermined selection

1. **Native Swarm orchestration plus science extensions:** reuse spawning/waiting/lifecycle and adapt platform capabilities and UI events.
2. **Staged migration:** retain `task` temporarily while closing named native-integration gaps, then transfer ownership with clear exit criteria.
3. **Retain platform orchestration:** acceptable only with concrete evidence explaining why native reuse is unsuitable, its maintenance costs, and conditions for revisiting the decision.

A tool rename or a single successful demo is insufficient to choose between these options.

## Validation and required conclusion

The decision should be backed by deterministic integration tests and a small set of comparable real research runs, not only code inspection.

- Verify actual child LLM tool lists, model routing, skill/context delivery and workspace access.
- Cover parallel children, successful result collection and parent continuation, one child failing, timeout/cancellation, and both approval modes.
- Verify child artifacts remain accessible and traceable, and UI progress reaches a correct terminal state.
- Compare task completion, result quality, token use, elapsed time and resource consumption under comparable conditions; record limitations and failures.

Before closing this RFC, publish a community-reviewed conclusion containing:

- the selected architecture and the rationale for reusing or not reusing native Swarm orchestration;
- a capability/gap matrix with concrete source or test evidence;
- ownership of scheduling, context/tool binding, permissions, lifecycle and science outputs;
- required changes, migration and rollback boundaries, and code that can be removed;
- remaining limitations and follow-up issues, with an explicit distinction between current-release acceptance and the long-term decision.

Related: #84 (Swarm migration), #107 (E2E scenarios).
items.title: [Rfc] Evaluate native JiuwenSwarm multi-agent orchestration versus the current platform task integration

items.author: Birfy
items.body:
## Summary

There is no update mechanism of any kind: `autoUpdate` / `checkForUpdate` appear nowhere in the codebase. A user who installed a binary months ago has no way to learn that a newer release exists, short of visiting the repository. Comparable workbenches ship auto-updating desktop builds; we do not even notify.

## Current state

- **Version is visible, staleness is not.** `ScienceDiscovery version` prints the release version plus bundled Node/CPython/micromamba versions. Nothing ever compares that against what has since been published.
- **Releases already carry the right metadata.** `scripts/package-binary-release.sh` emits `VERSION` and `SHA256SUMS` next to the artifacts, and the binary-release flow already verifies downloads by pinned SHA-256 (that is how Node, CPython, micromamba, and the uv wheel are fetched). The building blocks for a verifiable update check exist.
- **Side-by-side versions already work.** The payload cache is digest-keyed (`~/.cache/science-discovery/payload/<payload-id>`) and "an upgrade does not overwrite an older extraction", so an older release stays runnable — rollback is feasible today.
- **Remote runners can silently drift.** The Runner SEA is versioned by the build's Git commit prefix, and a mismatch between the local control plane and an already-deployed remote runner only produces a warning; it does not block or redeploy. So a long-lived SSH target can keep running a months-old runner.
- **No documented upgrade contract.** There is no guide covering data-directory compatibility across releases, what a new binary rebuilds on first `serve`, or how to roll back (also noted in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25)).

## Proposal

### 1. Update check (the part that matters most)

An opt-in check against a published release manifest — the existing `VERSION` + `SHA256SUMS` pair is already close to one.

- **Off by default in air-gapped installs**, and settable in system configuration. No telemetry beyond fetching the manifest; do not send an install identifier.
- Route the request through the configured network proxy, since proxy settings already exist.
- Surface the result quietly: a dismissible banner in the UI, a line in `ScienceDiscovery version`, and an explicit `--check-updates` for scripts.
- Fail silent on a network error. An offline workstation must never see an error toast because an update check could not reach the internet.

### 2. Self-update (optional second step)

`ScienceDiscovery update` that downloads the new artifact, verifies it against `SHA256SUMS` (ideally a signature too), swaps it atomically, and keeps the previous binary so a rollback is one command. The digest-keyed payload cache means the old version's extracted runtime is still there.

For Docker and source mode, print the right command instead of attempting anything — `docker compose pull` / `git pull && ./scripts/start-stack.sh` — rather than pretending a binary self-update applies.

### 3. Upgrade contract

Document, and enforce in code:

- what the data directory guarantees across versions, and what the first `serve` after an upgrade rebuilds;
- refusing to open a data directory written by a newer release, rather than half-migrating it;
- redeploying the matching Runner SEA to remote hosts when the control plane updates, instead of only warning about the mismatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user on an outdated release is told so, in the UI and on the CLI.
- [ ] The check is opt-in/opt-out, proxy-aware, and silent on failure.
- [ ] No update path installs an artifact whose SHA-256 was not verified.
- [ ] Rollback to the previous version is documented and works.
- [ ] Docker and source-mode users get correct upgrade instructions rather than a binary self-update.
- [ ] Remote runner drift is resolved automatically or reported as an actionable error.

## Open questions

- Where would the release manifest live, given the canonical repository is on GitCode and GitHub is a mirror? It needs one stable URL.
- Should releases be signed, or is SHA-256 against a manifest over HTTPS sufficient for this threat model?
- Default for the update check on a fresh install: on or off?
items.title: [Feature] Notify users of new releases, and support self-update
