items.body:
### 🚀 Background Description


`/evolve-design` is the only entry point for program evolution today, but it is a **hidden slash command** — a user must already know to type the `/evolve-design` prefix. The only visible entry is a button inside the artifact detail modal (it fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` and still requires the user to complete and send the sentence manually).

Two problems follow:

1. **We assume the user knows the command.** The UI never guides anyone toward `/evolve-design`; ordinary researchers will not type a slash command they have never seen.
2. **The interaction is command-shaped.** The user must learn command syntax (`--algorithm puct/openevolve`) instead of speaking naturally.

Goal: a user expresses improvement intent in **natural language** (e.g. "make this result better", "帮我优化这个程序"), the **framework actively recommends a tree-search evolution**, and the interaction stays natural-language end to end — no slash-command literacy required.



### Design Ideas

Land in three layers, reusing the existing `/evolve-design` chain (`EvolveAlgorithmPicker`, `EvolveToolRuntime`, `/api/evolve/runs`, the native-agent turn). No new capability surface.

#### Layer 1: Composer intent recognition (frontend, minimal)

Lightweight, testable, pure-function intent detection in the composer (no LLM round-trip):

- Match program-evolution intent:
  - the `/evolve-design` slash prefix (existing behavior, kept), **or**
  - a sentence pairing an **improvement verb** with an **evolvable target** (program / code / algorithm / function / model / script / …), in Chinese or English.
- When matched, offer a **low-intrusion suggestion bar** ("It looks like you want to improve a result or program. Run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") — the user must explicitly accept before anything is started.
- On accept, show the existing `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`; on select, fill `/evolve-design --algorithm X <natural language>` and send.

**Why confirmation before the picker?** Starting a search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations). Detection is a guess, so it must only *offer*; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This also protects against misreads — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never sent down an expensive search.

#### Layer 2: Agent-driven recommendation (backend, core value)

In the native-agent turn loop, recognise improvement intent in messages that do *not* carry the `/evolve-design` prefix:

- When the user asks to improve a program/result, the Agent **recommends** a tree-search evolution in its reply and offers to start it, reusing `EvolveToolRuntime`'s `create_evolve_run`.
- The interaction stays natural-language: the user replies "yes, go ahead", and the Agent starts the run.

#### Layer 3: Visible entry point (frontend, complete experience)

- A "program evolution" entry in the composer opens a **natural-language prompt** ("Which artifact? What does 'better' mean here?") instead of filling a slash command.
- The artifact-detail modal button opens the same prompt instead of generating `/evolve-design ...` text.

### Intent recognition rules

`detectEvolveIntent(message)` returns true only when **both** an improvement verb and an evolvable target are present, and no non-evolvable target is named:

| Example | Result | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` | true | verb + program target |
| `make this better` / `把这个做得更好` | false | no explicit evolvable target |
| `optimize the interface layout` / `优化一下界面布局` | false | layout is not evolvable |
| `improve the workflow steps` | false | steps are not evolvable |
| `this result is better than the last one` / `这个更好` | false | no verb+target pair |
| `improve the description` / `改一下格式` | false | formatting/explanation excluded |

`isEvolveDesignCommand(message)` distinguishes the explicit command (goes straight to the picker) from natural language (goes through the suggestion bar).

### API surface

- No new public API; reuse `/api/evolve/runs` and `/api/evolve/runs/:id/events`.
- Layer 2 reuses `EvolveToolRuntime`'s existing tools; no new registration.
- Intent detection is a pure frontend function, unit-testable.

### Affected modules

- `apps/web/src/App.tsx`: composer intent detection; `showEvolveAlgorithmPicker` trigger extension (currently matches only the `/evolve-design` prefix); suggestion-bar state.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/EvolveSuggestionBar.tsx` (new): confirmation bar.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts` (new): `detectEvolveIntent` / `isEvolveDesignCommand`.
- `apps/web/src/evolve/EvolveAlgorithmPicker.tsx`: reused unchanged.
- `apps/web/src/api/evolve.ts`: reused.
- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts`: turn-loop intent recognition and recommendation (Layer 2).
- `packages/evolve`: `EvolveToolRuntime` reused.
- i18n: suggestion-bar copy, composer entry copy (en + zh).

### Involved Public APIs

_No response_

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

_No response_

### Test Design and Test Plan

**Functional**

- [ ] Unit tests for `detectEvolveIntent`: Chinese/English verb+target, no-target messages, non-evolvable targets, negation phrases.
- [ ] Unit tests for `isEvolveDesignCommand`: command vs natural-language separation.
- [ ] Composer + natural-language improvement intent + artifact reference → suggestion bar appears.
- [ ] Accepting the suggestion → algorithm picker appears.
- [ ] Selecting an algorithm → `/evolve-design` evolution run starts.
- [ ] Ordinary messages (no intent) → nothing appears, normal conversation.
- [ ] Artifact modal button → opens natural-language prompt, not a filled command.

**Regression**

- [ ] Existing `/evolve-design` command path unchanged; explicit `--algorithm` no longer re-opens the picker.
- [ ] Existing evolve E2E / unit tests pass.

**User-perspective E2E**

- User expresses improvement intent naturally → framework recommends → natural-language confirm → evolution run starts.
- A message without improvement intent never triggers the evolution recommendation.

### Notes

- Follows the product direction: "the framework recommends tree search, but the interaction stays natural language."
- Layer 1 (frontend intent recognition + confirmation bar) can land as an independent MR first; Layer 2 (Agent-driven recommendation) depends on the turn-loop change and can follow.


### Additional Information

_No response_

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Motivation

Currently, every conversation must belong to a project, and creating a project requires too much configuration before users can start chatting.

This adds friction to the first interaction: users who simply want to ask a question or explore an idea must first create and configure a project, even when they do not yet need one. It also encourages creating projects for one-off conversations, making project management unnecessarily cluttered.

Users should be able to open the application and start a conversation immediately, then organize their work into projects when needed.

## Proposed direction for discussion

1. **Make project membership optional for conversations.**
   - Provide a prominent “New chat” entry that works without creating or selecting a project.
   - Support standalone conversations for quick questions, exploration, and one-off tasks.
   - Keep project-based conversations available for ongoing research and related work.

2. **Allow users to organize conversations into projects later.**
   - Let users move a standalone conversation into a new or existing project.
   - Preserve conversation history and associated artifacts when moving it.
   - Make it clear whether a conversation belongs to a project.

3. **Simplify project creation.**
   - Require only the minimum information needed to create a project, such as its name.
   - Provide sensible defaults and make advanced configuration optional.
   - Allow users to update project settings later instead of requiring them before the first conversation.

4. **Provide clear navigation for both workflows.**
   - Make standalone conversations and projects easy to find.
   - Let users start a conversation directly from the main interface.
   - Within a project, let users create conversations associated with that project.

## Example user flows

### Start chatting immediately

Open the application → New chat → Send a message.

No project creation or project configuration is required.

### Organize an exploratory conversation

Start a standalone conversation → Decide to continue the work → Move the conversation into a new or existing project.

### Start with a project

Create a project with minimal information → Start a conversation → Configure additional project settings when needed.

## Questions to settle

- Should standalone conversations remain in chat history by default, with an explicitly ephemeral mode handled separately?
- Which project settings can use defaults, and which are genuinely required before a project-specific capability runs?
- When an existing conversation moves into a project, how should project context and settings apply to subsequent messages?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user with no projects can open the application and send a first message without creating or configuring a project.
- [ ] Users can create and continue conversations outside projects.
- [ ] Users can still create conversations directly within a project.
- [ ] A standalone conversation can be moved into a new or existing project without losing its history or associated artifacts.
- [ ] Project creation requires only minimal information; advanced settings can be configured later.
- [ ] Navigation clearly distinguishes standalone conversations from project conversations.
- [ ] Existing projects and their conversations remain accessible.
- [ ] E2E coverage verifies starting a conversation with no projects, creating a project with minimal input, and moving a standalone conversation into a project.

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
### Background

We want to automate the workflow from issue submission through code changes, review, and PR merge. This requires clear repository conventions so contributors and automation can determine whether an issue is ready for implementation, whether a change meets its acceptance criteria, and whether a PR is ready to merge.

The existing `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers development setup, test commands, E2E testing, and some PR requirements. Extend it with issue, commit, review, and merge conventions, supported by templates and checks that all contributors can use.

### Scope

#### 1. Issue requirements

Provide templates for feature requests, bug reports, and other supported issue types. Identify required and conditional fields:

- Background, the problem to solve, and the expected outcome.
- Functional specifications, including inputs, outputs, behavior, boundary conditions, and applicable compatibility requirements.
- Scope and explicit exclusions.
- Verifiable acceptance scenarios with preconditions, actions, and expected results. Cover success, failure, permissions, and recovery where relevant.
- Reproduction steps, environment, actual behavior, and expected behavior for bug reports.
- Dependencies, open questions, and blockers that must be resolved before implementation.

Include a complete example and define when an issue is ready for development. Clarify ambiguities that affect implementation or acceptance before work begins. Update the issue when the specification changes during implementation.

#### 2. Commit and PR requirements

Document branch, commit, and PR conventions:

- Follow the existing fork and target-branch workflow, and define naming and commit message formats.
- Link the PR to its issue and explain the reason, resulting behavior, and scope.
- Map each issue acceptance criterion to its implementation and validation result.
- Provide reproducible test commands, results, and supporting evidence. Distinguish tests that were not run, failed, were blocked, or were skipped.
- Describe compatibility impact, configuration changes, data migration, and rollback where applicable.
- Update affected documentation and follow the existing release label requirements.

#### 3. Review and merge requirements

Provide a shared review checklist and define:

- Checks for specification compliance, acceptance coverage, correctness, module boundaries, and applicable security and compatibility requirements.
- The distinction between blocking findings and suggestions, including how findings are resolved.
- Responsibilities for automated and human review, including approval authority.
- Which checks and approvals must be repeated after a PR changes.
- Conditions for entering the merge queue and completing the merge, consistent with the existing CI and `merge-gate` mechanism.

#### 4. Rule checks

Maintain a rule list that states applicability, verification method, execution stage, and failure handling for each rule. Include:

- Required issue and PR information and their linkage.
- Type checks, tests, user-perspective E2E testing, and documentation checks.
- License headers, sensitive information, temporary files, and generated files.
- Module dependency boundaries and compatibility requirements.
- Required checks, review decisions, and unresolved blockers.

Enforce rules through templates or CI where they can be checked programmatically. Provide explicit instructions for rules that require human judgment. Unavailable test prerequisites must be reported as blocked. Document the reason, approver, and follow-up for any exception.

### Deliverables

- Extend `CONTRIBUTING.md` as the common entry point, linking to separate documents where needed.
- Add issue templates, a PR template, and a review checklist.
- Provide a feature issue example and a corresponding PR acceptance report example.
- Map rules to automated checks, distinguishing existing checks, checks added in this work, and follow-up work.
- Resolve duplicated or conflicting guidance and identify where each rule is maintained.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Contributors can find issue, commit, PR, review, and merge requirements from one entry point.
- [ ] The feature template requires functional specifications and verifiable acceptance scenarios; the bug template requires reproduction details.
- [ ] The PR template requires an issue link, per-criterion acceptance results, and test evidence.
- [ ] The review checklist defines blocking findings, approval responsibilities, and re-review requirements.
- [ ] Merge conditions are consistent with the existing CI, merge queue, and `merge-gate` contract.
- [ ] Important rules specify applicability, verification, and failure or exception handling.
- [ ] At least one complete issue-to-PR example is included.
- [ ] New or changed templates and automated checks are validated, and documentation checks pass.

This issue covers the guidelines, templates, and agreed checks. Implementation of the complete automation system can be tracked separately.

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem
The `CodeCheck (GitCode)` check run on GitHub PRs only says "GitCode labelled the merge request `ci-failed`" and links to the GitCode MR. It doesn't name the failing rule or file. The GitCode MR page/API is not reachable for every contributor or reviewer (WAF/login). So authors end up writing "CodeCheck is ignored" (e.g. #421, also failing on #412 and #391), and reviewers can't tell whether a failure comes from the PR.

## Expected
When CodeCheck fails, the GitHub check-run output lists the failing checker/rule, file:line and message (or a stable public log link), so authors and reviewers can act without GitCode access.

## Verification cases
1. **Failure details mirrored**
   - Preconditions: a PR whose head introduces a known CodeCheck violation (e.g. a lint rule the GitCode pipeline enforces).
   - Steps: push; wait for the sync; open the `CodeCheck (GitCode)` check run on GitHub.
   - Expected / pass: `output.summary` or `output.text` names the rule, file:line and message; conclusion `failure`.
2. **Clean head**
   - Preconditions: a PR with no violations.
   - Steps: push; open the check run.
   - Expected / pass: conclusion `success`; no stale failure text from an earlier head.
3. **Infra failure isn't shown as a code failure (negative)**
   - Preconditions: the GitCode pipeline fails for an infra reason (timeout/sync error).
   - Steps: trigger; open the check run.
   - Expected / pass: output says it's an infra/sync failure, not a code violation, and links to a retry path.
4. **No secret leakage (security)**
   - Preconditions: a pipeline log that contains tokens/env.
   - Steps: mirror the failure details.
   - Expected / pass: mirrored text contains no tokens, cookies or internal URLs with credentials.

## Context
Refs #421, Refs #385. Seen at #421 head f494792 (GitCode MR !296) and #412 head 29e724a.

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
## 背景

Codex/Claude Specialist（Phase2/3）体验中，配置与运维仍偏「懂进程 env + 懂 API」：

- 设置页**没有** runtime/SDK 选择器；UI 保存不发 `runtime`（只能 API 带 `runtime` 创建）。
- `SCIENCE_AGENT_CODEX_BASE_URL` **只能**写进 API 进程环境，改完需重启；主 Agent 工具 `configure_specialist_runtime` 只能改已有外部 runtime 的非密钥项，**不能**设 base URL、代填 key、引导 device-code，也不能把 native 改成 codex/cc。
- 有任务内配密卡（`CodexConfigCard` / `runtime-config`），但**没有**右侧 Specialist CLI 卡片，也**没有**「重启 specialist runtime」。

产品口径（维护者确认）：配置页保持简；复杂鉴权进主对话；保底是用户可直连 specialist，且可重启。

## 目标（三块合一，完整产品面）

### A. 配置页：选 runtime + 拉 SDK

- 配置页增加 **runtime 选择**（至少 `codex` / `claude-code` 等已支持 kind）。
- 选定后，系统下载/安装对应 SDK（失败有明确提示与可重试）。
- 表单保持简：**runtime + Skills + 描述**（名称可保留）；旁侧短文案提示：鉴权 / base URL / device-code 等在主对话由主 Agent 完成。
- 保存时 UI **必须**把所选 `runtime` 写入 create/update API（与现有 schema 对齐）。

### B. 主对话代配：加密输入 + device-code 引导

放开当前限制，主 Agent 在对话中可协助完成：

- **base URL / API key**：向用户发出**加密输入框**；用户把 key 填进输入框，**key 不进入对话正文**。
- **device-code**：主 Agent 把 code 交给用户，并说明如何在外部完成配置。
- 完成后写入平台侧安全存储 / `runtime-config` 路径，供后续委派使用（具体存储形态实现自定，验收看行为）。

### C. 右侧 Specialist 卡片 + CLI + 重启

- 会话右侧增加 **Specialist 卡片**。
- 点击后打开 **CLI 页**：展示主 Agent ↔ 该 specialist 的对话记录；用户也可在此页直接与 specialist 交互。
- 该页左侧提供 **「重启 specialist runtime」**（换 endpoint/凭证或进程异常后可重新拉起，无需整站重启 API）。

## 验收标准

- [ ] **A**：设置页可选 runtime；选定后触发 SDK 拉取；保存后 GET specialist 可见对应 `runtime.kind`；有「剩余配置在主对话完成」提示。
- [ ] **B**：主对话可走加密输入完成 base URL 与 key（正文日志/历史中不可见明文 key）；device-code 流程有用户可见引导；无需手改进程 env 即可完成常见第三方 endpoint 配置（至少覆盖当前 Codex→DeepSeek Responses 类场景的一条端到端路径）。
- [ ] **C**：右侧卡片可打开 CLI 页；可见主 Agent–specialist 记录且用户可交互；「重启 specialist runtime」可用，重启后可再次委派/交互。
- [ ] 不降低现有安全底线：Always Allow 不得代填密钥；密钥不进 specialist 元数据白名单。
- [ ] 有对应自动化或可重复手工验收步骤（可与 `test(specialist): HTTP runtime 契约` 姊妹 issue 互补，不重复）。

## 非目标

- 不在本 issue 只补 HTTP 静默丢 `runtime` 的测试（另开测试 issue）。
- 不要求设置页做成「覆盖所有鉴权形态的巨型表单」。
- 不要求提供完全脱离平台的独立 Codex CLI 产品面；本 issue 的「CLI 页」是平台内嵌的 specialist 交互面。

## 现状锚点（便于实现对照）

- UI 表单：`apps/web/src/Orchestration.tsx`（无 runtime 选择器）
- 主 Agent 工具：`configure_specialist_runtime`（`main-config.ts`）
- 配密卡：`CodexConfigCard` / `POST .../subagents/:id/runtime-config`
- Base URL：`SCIENCE_AGENT_CODEX_BASE_URL` 进程 env

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## User request

When I switch the model in a conversation, I want the next new conversation to start with that model automatically. I should not have to select it again or separately visit settings to make that choice stick.

Example: the configured default is model A. In session 1, I explicitly select model B in the conversation model picker. Every new conversation should initially use model B rather than returning to model A: this includes another session in the same project, a session in a different project, and the first session of a newly created project, even if the target project has a different default. If I later explicitly select model C, the next new session should start with C.

## Current behavior

The conversation picker changes a session override. New sessions inherit the project default model, falling back to the system default, so a choice made in the previous conversation is not automatically reused.

This is a request to change that behavior, rather than only explain it with a tooltip.

## Expected behavior and acceptance criteria

- [ ] After an explicit, successfully saved model selection in a conversation, every new conversation starts with that selected model, across all projects and including the first session of a newly created project, without an extra confirmation or a trip to settings.
- [ ] A remembered explicit selection takes precedence over project and system model defaults when initializing any new conversation.
- [ ] A later explicit selection becomes the remembered choice for subsequent new sessions. Merely opening an older conversation does not replace the remembered choice.
- [ ] The remembered choice survives page refresh and application restart.
- [ ] Existing conversations retain their own model selection; creating a conversation does not change other conversations or an in-flight run's model.
- [ ] If there is no remembered selection, normal project-default → system-default inheritance continues to work.
- [ ] If the remembered model has been removed or is no longer selectable, creation falls back to a valid configured default, or shows actionable model configuration feedback if none exists. It must not retain a dangling model selection.
- [ ] The model shown in the new conversation matches its effective saved model. Any scope hint accurately describes the new behavior in both English and Chinese.
- [ ] Repeatable browser regression coverage verifies A → select B → create session → B within the same project, across projects with different defaults, and in a newly created project; a subsequent selection of C; persistence after reload/restart, unchanged existing conversations, and missing-model fallback.

## Selection policy

Use one last explicitly selected model for new conversations, independent of project boundaries. The user requests a Codex-style experience: choose a model once and keep using that choice when starting new conversations. This is the requested interaction policy, rather than a claim about Codex implementation details.

Project boundaries must not reset the remembered selection. Merely viewing an older conversation must not count as choosing its model. Existing conversations retain their own selection. This specifies the initialization behavior; it does not require rewriting every project's settings or changing other users' preferences. The persistence mechanism should follow the product's user/preference model.

## Related issues and current PRs

- #44 describes the same source of confusion, but its proposed solution explicitly retains session-only switching and adds a scope hint. This issue requests remembered selection for new sessions instead. Keep the two acceptance contracts distinct; a hint-only change does not satisfy this request.
- PR #289 is currently an open draft for #44. Its description explicitly says persistence/configuration/selection callbacks are unchanged. It does not implement remembered selection; its hint wording will need to be reconciled if this feature lands.
- #278 concerns configuration from within a conversation and task continuation. It does not require new sessions to reuse the last selected model.
- Closed #336 is an analogous usability request about remembering approval mode/defaults, rather than model selection.

At filing time, a search of open/closed issues and current open PRs found no exact duplicate or open PR implementing this remembered-model behavior.
items.title: [Feature] New sessions should remember the last explicitly selected conversation model

## Purpose

Carry forward every unfinished or unverified acceptance item from #55, following the feature triage requested under #563 against release scope #249. This is an administrative split of partial delivery, not a declaration that the original feature is fully implemented.

## Existing delivery and evidence

PR56/60 delivered bilingual evolve explanation/how-to/tutorial/reference; current tree has core/evolve.md, domains/evolve-a-solution.md and EN developer-docs/evolve-standalone.md

Reviewed against upstream main `65eddde1` on 2026-10-27. Historical PR test results apply to their recorded candidate revisions only; no new product acceptance tests were run in this triage.

## Remaining work

Audit all original documentation criteria against the reorganized current docs, restore missing operational how-to/index/reference coverage if needed, and record an actual supplied-example tutorial run and bilingual parity/link results. Do not recreate pages that already exist.

## Release

Target: release/0.3.0. This remaining scope supports an explicit #249 release deliverable.

## Completion rule

- [ ] Account for every original criterion: delivered evidence, remaining implementation, explicit approved alternative, or separately linked follow-up.
- [ ] Run matching acceptance checks on the final candidate and retain actual results; do not treat workflow presence, merged status or historical green CI as full acceptance.
- [ ] Reconcile still-open PRs and original dependencies with the successor issue before merge.

## Original specification (preserved for traceability)

## Summary

`/evolve` is one of the largest features in the product and has **no user documentation in either language**. A researcher cannot learn what it does, when to reach for it, or how to drive it, without reading the source. I would like an explanation page, a how-to, and a tutorial — in English and Chinese — plus the existing Chinese architecture note fixed up and made reachable.

## What ships versus what is documented

What ships:

| Surface | Size |
|---|---|
| `services/evolve` Python sidecar | 23 modules, two search engines — flat-PUCT (`puct_engine.py`) and MAP-Elites islands with ring migration (`openevolve_engine.py`) |
| Scoring modes | four domain seams: `scorecard_domain` (dataset metric), `test_gate_domain` (test suite), `script_domain` (a scorer the model writes), `judge_domain` (LLM rubric) |
| Agent tools | `create_evolve_run`, `get_evolve_run` |
| Skill | `evolve-design`, a four-checkpoint design conversation with an algorithm choice |
| Web UI | 13 components — panel, algorithm picker, candidate stream, score chart, search graph canvas and table, budget bar, cell grid |
| UI strings | 188 `evolve.*` message keys |
| HTTP API | `/api/evolve/runs`, `/runs/<id>/events`, `/runs/<id>/candidates/<hash>`, `/runs/<id>/stop` |

What is documented:

| Language | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Chinese | **one** file, `docs/zh/explanation/evolve-standalone.md` (252 lines) |
| English | **zero** — the word "evolve" appears in exactly one English file, `docs/en/reference/web-frontend.md`, in passing |

And the single Chinese file has two problems of its own:

1. **It is unreachable.** `docs/zh/explanation/README.md` does not link it. The index lists `skill-library-management.md` and `skill-self-evolution.md` but not `evolve-standalone.md`, so the only way to find it is to list the directory. (Raised as an orphan page in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25).)
2. **It answers a different question.** Its own opening says it covers the two engines' differences and what it would take to run the sidecar as a standalone backend. That is an architecture note for a maintainer. Nothing in it tells a researcher what a search is for, when scoring will actually discriminate, or how to start one.

## What to write

### 1. `explanation/evolve.md` (EN + ZH)

What an evolution search is, and the honest limits: it rewrites a candidate dozens of times and keeps what scores higher, so it succeeds or fails on whether the scoring can tell a good candidate from a bad one — a scoring function that cannot shows up as a flat run, not as an error. Cover the four scoring modes and when each applies, the two engines and when to pick which, and the frozen-scorer rule that `test_gate_domain` enforces, whose upstream note is worth quoting: *"without it the shortest path to a high score is to weaken the thing measuring it."*

### 2. `how-to/run-an-evolution-search.md` (EN + ZH)

The operational path: preparing a starting point and a dataset or test suite, what `--algorithm puct` versus `--algorithm openevolve` changes, reading the score chart and the search graph, budgets and stopping, retrieving the winning candidate, and what the approval card asks for before a run starts.

### 3. `tutorial/…-evolve-a-solution.md` (EN + ZH)

One short end-to-end run a reader can actually complete: a small starting program, a dataset with a metric, the `/evolve-design` conversation answered checkpoint by checkpoint, then what to look at while it runs and how to tell a real improvement from noise. This is the piece [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) asks for in general, applied here.

### 4. Fix what exists

Link `evolve-standalone.md` from the Chinese explanation index, give it an English counterpart, and retitle it so its scope is obvious — it is the engine-internals and standalone-deployment note, not the feature's documentation.

### 5. Reference the surface

The four HTTP endpoints belong in `reference/rest-api.md`, and the two agent tools in `reference/builtin-tools.md`, so the feature is reachable from the reference tree as well as the prose.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An English reader can learn what `/evolve` is, when to use it, and how to run one, without reading source code.
- [ ] Explanation, how-to and tutorial pages exist in both languages and are linked from their indexes.
- [ ] The four scoring modes and the two engines are each documented with the case they suit.
- [ ] The frozen-scorer rule is stated where a user designing a search will meet it.
- [ ] The tutorial runs end to end on a supplied example, and says how to judge whether the result is real.
- [ ] `evolve-standalone.md` is linked, translated, and scoped by its title.
- [ ] The evolve endpoints and agent tools appear in the reference documents.

## Open questions

- Should the tutorial evolve a program (dataset metric) or a prompt (LLM judge)? The program case is more convincing; the prompt case is cheaper to run and needs no dataset.
- Can a small example — a starting program plus a labelled dataset — be committed for the tutorial, as [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) proposes generally?
- Does the Idea Tree engine want the same treatment in the same pass? It has the same shape of gap: `idea-tree-engine.md` is also Chinese-only.

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) (documentation completeness and the orphan pages), [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) (the tutorial series), [#54](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/54) (RSI, which builds directly on this engine and will be much harder to explain if the engine itself is undocumented).

## Original specification (preserved for traceability)

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #90](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/90) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Enter the app for the first time and figure out how to start my first analysis.

## What I saw instead

With no projects yet, the home screen shows a centered empty-state card listing three steps:

1. Configure a model (go to system settings → model registry, then save a provider token);
2. Create a project (its first session opens automatically);
3. Drop a CSV and ask (analyze the CSV and plot charts).

These are plain static list items (empty-state rendering in `apps/web/src/App.tsx`) with no click handlers: clicking "Configure a model" does nothing, and so does "Create a project". There is no composer, no upload area, no sample-data button, and no guided tour.

## Why this is confusing

New users have no idea where to click; the three steps are signposts, but every one of them requires the user to find the destination on their own.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- Turn each step into a real action: "Configure a model" opens the matching settings section directly; "Create a project" opens the creation dialog directly.
- Add a prominent primary button "Load sample data and try it now": automatically create an initial project and session, load a bundled sample CSV, and prefill a ready-to-send example prompt, so a new user sees their first chart within seconds.
- Open question (needs a product decision): the theme of the bundled sample CSV and its expected chart types are not decided yet — a public, license-clean scientific dataset should be picked first.

Design notes: making the empty-state steps interactive is low-risk frontend routing/dialog work; the one-click sample needs decisions on data source (bundled vs. downloaded on first run) and topic, which is why it is registered as an open question here.

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
> Converted from bug → feature per HongyeZhou (2026-10-27): this is a product/UX presentation improvement, not a hard defect.

## Feature request
When tool calls fail then recover mid-run, the default timeline narrative shows raw **failed** tool cards before a later success. #335 expected a clearer “retrying with fixed args” (or equivalent) presentation for the same logical operation. PRs #345 / #551 addressed missing required `prompt` on `task` before a deep createSubagent throw; they did **not** deliver the general failure→retry UI narrative (S6).

## Expected
When there is clear association evidence that a later call is a bounded correction of the same logical tool operation, the UI updates in place (or equivalent merged presentation): default view is a concise result; attempt count / errors / recovery detail are available on demand. Unrecoverable failures keep a clear reason. Real execution history and audit evidence are not rewritten as pure success. Do not blindly replay side-effecting operations to reduce cards.

## Verification cases

1. **In-place recovery presentation**
   - **Preconditions:** A recoverable invalid-argument or soft-fail path that retries within one logical operation (browser or hermetic UI fixture).
   - **Steps:**
     1. Trigger a tool call that fails then succeeds on a bounded correction.
     2. Inspect the timeline/card for that operation.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Default view is not a stack of contradictory failed+success cards for the same operation; recovery state/result is shown in place; history of attempts remains inspectable; independent operations are not wrongly merged.

2. **Side-effect boundary**
   - **Preconditions:** A tool invocation that may have already executed with side effects before observation failed.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Observe recovery/UI merge behavior.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** No blind resubmit of committed side-effecting work solely to tidy the timeline; audit/failure records stay consistent.

## Context
- Env: _not provided_ for a fresh UI journey this filing; scope from #335 expected narrative and product phase-3 note on that Issue.
- Refs: Parent #335; PRs #345 / #551 (merged) for prompt-path only.
- Notes: Related UX umbrella #330 is adjacent (timeline hierarchy) but not a substitute for this recovery-presentation bug.
items.title: [Feature] clearer fail-then-retry timeline narrative for tool recovery (from #335 S6)

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

PR #552 delivers standalone (inbox / 最近会话) chats and project folds, but membership is fixed at create time. Users still cannot move an existing recent conversation into a new or existing project without losing history or artifacts. That remaining acceptance item from #305 is out of scope for #552.

## Expected

A reader can move a standalone (recent / inbox) conversation into a new or existing project, and optionally move between projects or back to Recent, without losing messages, artifacts, or workspace accounting. Navigation and session lists stay consistent (no duplicate rows).

## Verification cases

1. **Move into existing project**
   - **Preconditions:** One Recent/inbox session with messages and at least one artifact; project P already exists.
   - **Steps:** From that session, choose move into project P (or equivalent UI).
   - **Expected / pass:** Session appears under P; history and artifacts intact; no longer listed under 最近会话; session bar / active project shows P.

2. **Move into newly created project**
   - **Preconditions:** One standalone session with history.
   - **Steps:** Move → create project with name only → confirm.
   - **Expected / pass:** Project created; session inside it; history/artifacts intact; gone from Recent.

3. **Move between projects / back to Recent**
   - **Preconditions:** Session already under a project.
   - **Steps:** Move to another project, then back to Recent (if supported).
   - **Expected / pass:** Membership updates; no duplicate rows in sidebar; workspace path and accounting remain consistent.

4. **E2E first-run remainder of #305**
   - **Preconditions:** Fresh user with no projects.
   - **Steps:** Start chat without a project → later move that chat into a project.
   - **Expected / pass:** Covers the #305 E2E acceptance remainder that #552 intentionally deferred.

## Context

- Refs #305 (remaining AC: organize / move conversations into projects later).
- Follow-up from review of https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/552 (`bde9143`); not blocking that PR.

items.author: hsliuustc0106
items.body:
## Context

Since July 2026 an open-source "science workbench" category has formed, triggered by Anthropic's Claude Science launch (2026-06-30). Three direct open-source alternatives appeared the same week and are now at scale: [synthetic-sci/openscience](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience) (~3.6K★), [aipoch/open-science](https://github.com/aipoch/open-science) (~4.2K★), and [ai4s-research/open-science](https://github.com/ai4s-research/open-science) (~1.7K★). Having compared ScienceDiscovery against them (and against the autonomous-scientist systems: Sakana AI-Scientist, InternScience/InternAgent + MLEvolve), here is a strengths/gaps assessment in the hope it helps prioritization. Facts below are from public repo data collected 2026-09-15.

## Strengths (keep — and communicate)

1. **Sandbox-first security model.** Fail-closed Bubblewrap/Seatbelt execution, operator-scoped NPU chip passthrough, opt-in Broker with fixed entry points and `shell: false`. None of the three competitors communicates a default-isolation story; the highest-engagement technical question on a competitor's launch thread was literally *"are the skills executed within a secure, containerized sandbox by default, or does the user manage isolation?"* — this repo already answers that question, but almost nobody knows it does.
2. **Provenance depth.** CAS with pinned-asset drift rejection, review checks, cross-session/SubAgent citation chains. The strongest provenance story in the category.
3. **Search-camp RSI engine.** The evolve sidecar (flat-PUCT tree + OpenEvolve MAP-Elites, discriminability probe, explicit "no model training, no search-rule modification") is a clean, honest scope with a real cousin in [InternScience/MLEvolve](https://github.com/InternScience/MLEvolve) (#1 on MLE-Bench).
4. **Ascend NPU path.** 910B sandbox passthrough + allowlisted workloads (Protenix/MindScience) is unique in the category and extends machine-verifiable research to device-scale workloads.
5. **Engineering discipline beyond repo age.** Bilingual doc set, CI tiers (UT/ST/mocked E2E), self-documented limitations (e.g., Idea Tree scores are model judgments, not experimental evidence).

## Gaps (ordered by leverage)

1. **Installation/onboarding.** No binaries in Releases — #1 (open since 08-19, rated 1/5) is the only organic user feedback this repo has received, and it is someone who *could not install the product*. All three competitors ship desktop installers and a <10-minute quickstart. This pairs directly with the first-experience goal in #22.
2. **No community surface.** All merged PRs are bots; there are zero human external PRs. For comparison: aipoch merges 6+ human PRs/day; ai4s-research power users file bugs *and* land the fixes (e.g., their stall-guard for looping agents came from a user). A "good first issue" ladder + a contributor guide + weekly maintainer RFC triage would start the flywheel.
3. **Category invisibility + an unverifiable benchmark claim.** 58★ vs 1.7–4.2K for peers; one promotion event found (Sina Finance 2026-08-16) whose headline claim (BiomniBench-DA "业界SOTA") is dual-claimed by aipoch's README badge on the same benchmark. Without published methodology/splits, the claim reads as marketing and hurts credibility with scientists — either publish the eval or drop the superlative.
4. **Adoption levers validated by competitors, still missing here:** headless CLI / task API (repeated cross-repo demand — researchers want CI and agent-to-agent use, not only a GUI), model-provider onboarding (subscription reuse, connectivity-test friction), Windows parity.
5. **Cross-model skill consistency.** The single most-validated complaint in the category: *"one flag switches the model, not whether the skill actually works"* (prompts tuned on one model degrade on smaller/local models). A per-skill model-compatibility matrix or a cross-model smoke-test suite for the 300+ skills would directly differentiate.

## Suggested next steps

- [ ] Ship Linux binaries + a 10-minute quickstart (pairs with #22)
- [ ] Publish evolve/idea-tree efficiency metrics (per-node token cost, CAS reuse rate, surviving-node quality on an independent benchmark) — the pruning+reuse efficiency story is genuinely differentiating and no competitor tells it
- [ ] Benchmark-claim triage: methodology for BiomniBench-DA or remove the SOTA wording
- [ ] Community ladder: CONTRIBUTING good-first-issues + a maintainer-reserved RFC-triage day

Happy to help flesh any of these out.
items.title: [Feedback] Strengths and gaps vs. the 2026 open-source science-workbench landscape

oldest.author: hsliuustc0106
oldest.body:
## Goal

Make ScienceDiscovery a useful, approachable research product. A researcher should be able to understand what it can help with, get started with clear guidance, complete a task, and return to their work confidently.

The first experience we should deliver is simple:

**Open the app → connect a model → upload a CSV and ask a question → receive a useful chart → refine and save the result.**

The application should handle routine setup and organization, ask only for decisions that matter, and explain the next step in plain language. Technical details should be available when needed.

## Why this matters

During a trial of release 0.2.0, a new user encountered welcome cards that did not navigate, confusing model setup, unexplained `Unauthorized` messages, and an interface that opened even though analysis could not run on that computer. These problems prevented the user from experiencing the product's value.

This evidence comes from one installation. Check fixes in the current release and development branch before opening duplicate work. Related public feedback includes [difficulty finding the download](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1).

## Improvements

### 1. Make the starting point obvious

- Explain the product with one concrete example and show its finished result.
- Provide prominent **Get started**, **Try an example**, and **Watch the walkthrough** actions.
- Make every suggested action work. Clearly explain unavailable actions and how to enable them.
- Offer a visible English/中文 switch and consistent wording throughout the experience.

### 2. Guide the user through setup

- Provide one recommended download and setup path for each supported computer type.
- Ask for the minimum information needed to connect a model, with helpful defaults and a clear connection test. Explain any required API key, where to obtain it, and that provider usage may incur charges.
- Handle the app's internal connection automatically where possible. If a user must reconnect, take them directly to a guided recovery step.
- Check that analysis can actually run before showing the app as ready. Explain compatibility problems early and provide a concrete next action.
- Keep advanced configuration accessible outside the ordinary setup flow.

### 3. Make everyday work feel straightforward

- Let users start with a question or a file. Create the initial project/session automatically for the guided example.
- Show understandable progress based on what is happening, such as reading data or preparing a chart. Make waiting, required input, completion, and failure easy to distinguish.
- Provide visible stop/retry actions where appropriate. Preserve the user's question and files when something fails.
- Explain errors in plain language with a recovery action; place diagnostic details behind an expandable option.
- Present the result clearly, with an explanation, supporting evidence, and access to the producing code. Make follow-up requests, saving/exporting, and returning later easy to discover.

### 4. Provide two videos that help people understand the product

**Video 1 — From opening the app to a first result (5–7 minutes).** Show a real released version: download/open, connect a model, upload the supplied CSV, ask a question, inspect the chart, request a change, and reopen the saved work. Provide the sample file, prompt, transcript, and English/Chinese captions. Show required preparation and label accelerated waits.

**Video 2 — The same task with and without ScienceDiscovery (6–8 minutes).** Use IMO 2026 Day 2 Problem 5 to compare the same model in direct conversation and in ScienceDiscovery. Focus on the viewer's experience: what they ask, how much guidance they provide, how understandable and complete the answer is, and how easily they can inspect or continue the work. Also report actual time and cost.

Keep the problem, model, and budgets comparable; review the mathematical proofs and report the observed outcome, including ties or failures. The problem's answer is the family `f(x) = x + c`, with `c >= 0`; describe it as the complete solution family. See the [original problem](https://www.imo-official.org/assets/documents/problems/2026/2026_eng.pdf) and [published reference proof](https://github.com/AxiomMath/IMO2026/blob/main/IMO2026/Q5/solution.lean).

Both videos must reflect working released behavior. Their purpose is to explain the experience and demonstrate useful outcomes. Test the app's guidance with new users, including people who have not watched the videos, and fix the points where they get stuck.

### 5. Make feedback and contribution welcoming

- Provide an obvious way to ask for help or report a problem without requiring users to understand the architecture.
- Explain where contributions are reviewed and how GitHub visitors reach that destination. The [current contribution guide](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/907382ce42e1ebfe77e24281905dec0607aaf003/CONTRIBUTING.md) routes code contributions to GitCode.
- Offer a short first-contribution guide and a few bounded tasks with named reviewers. Useful examples include improving a confusing screen, contributing an analysis example, or fixing a connector.
- Document checks newcomers can run without paid model access or special hardware, and how maintainers help with the remaining validation.

## How we know this is better

- [ ] A new user can explain what ScienceDiscovery does and identify how to start.
- [ ] On a supported computer, the user can complete the sample analysis, refine the result, and reopen the saved work without live maintainer assistance.
- [ ] Setup problems are explained before the user starts dependent work; failures preserve their inputs and offer a clear next step.
- [ ] The main journey works in English and Chinese, and the displayed controls and instructions match the released app.
- [ ] Both videos are linked from the project entry page, use actual runs, and include the materials needed to follow or inspect them.
- [ ] A new contributor can find a suitable task, run the relevant checks, submit a change, and understand the review process.

Observe ten unfamiliar users and use eight completing the sample journey without intervention as an initial target. Also record where users get stuck, whether they return the following week, and whether contributors return for another contribution. These are proposed targets, not current results.

## Delivery

Prioritize the first-use journey and recovery from the problems already observed. Validate the downloadable release, record the videos, and improve the experience with a small pilot group before broader promotion. Give each follow-up a named owner.

## Summary

There is no update mechanism of any kind: `autoUpdate` / `checkForUpdate` appear nowhere in the codebase. A user who installed a binary months ago has no way to learn that a newer release exists, short of visiting the repository. Comparable workbenches ship auto-updating desktop builds; we do not even notify.

## Current state

- **Version is visible, staleness is not.** `ScienceDiscovery version` prints the release version plus bundled Node/CPython/micromamba versions. Nothing ever compares that against what has since been published.
- **Releases already carry the right metadata.** `scripts/package-binary-release.sh` emits `VERSION` and `SHA256SUMS` next to the artifacts, and the binary-release flow already verifies downloads by pinned SHA-256 (that is how Node, CPython, micromamba, and the uv wheel are fetched). The building blocks for a verifiable update check exist.
- **Side-by-side versions already work.** The payload cache is digest-keyed (`~/.cache/science-discovery/payload/<payload-id>`) and "an upgrade does not overwrite an older extraction", so an older release stays runnable — rollback is feasible today.
- **Remote runners can silently drift.** The Runner SEA is versioned by the build's Git commit prefix, and a mismatch between the local control plane and an already-deployed remote runner only produces a warning; it does not block or redeploy. So a long-lived SSH target can keep running a months-old runner.
- **No documented upgrade contract.** There is no guide covering data-directory compatibility across releases, what a new binary rebuilds on first `serve`, or how to roll back (also noted in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25)).

## Proposal

### 1. Update check (the part that matters most)

An opt-in check against a published release manifest — the existing `VERSION` + `SHA256SUMS` pair is already close to one.

- **Off by default in air-gapped installs**, and settable in system configuration. No telemetry beyond fetching the manifest; do not send an install identifier.
- Route the request through the configured network proxy, since proxy settings already exist.
- Surface the result quietly: a dismissible banner in the UI, a line in `ScienceDiscovery version`, and an explicit `--check-updates` for scripts.
- Fail silent on a network error. An offline workstation must never see an error toast because an update check could not reach the internet.

### 2. Self-update (optional second step)

`ScienceDiscovery update` that downloads the new artifact, verifies it against `SHA256SUMS` (ideally a signature too), swaps it atomically, and keeps the previous binary so a rollback is one command. The digest-keyed payload cache means the old version's extracted runtime is still there.

For Docker and source mode, print the right command instead of attempting anything — `docker compose pull` / `git pull && ./scripts/start-stack.sh` — rather than pretending a binary self-update applies.

### 3. Upgrade contract

Document, and enforce in code:

- what the data directory guarantees across versions, and what the first `serve` after an upgrade rebuilds;
- refusing to open a data directory written by a newer release, rather than half-migrating it;
- redeploying the matching Runner SEA to remote hosts when the control plane updates, instead of only warning about the mismatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user on an outdated release is told so, in the UI and on the CLI.
- [ ] The check is opt-in/opt-out, proxy-aware, and silent on failure.
- [ ] No update path installs an artifact whose SHA-256 was not verified.
- [ ] Rollback to the previous version is documented and works.
- [ ] Docker and source-mode users get correct upgrade instructions rather than a binary self-update.
- [ ] Remote runner drift is resolved automatically or reported as an actionable error.

## Open questions

- Where would the release manifest live, given the canonical repository is on GitCode and GitHub is a mirror? It needs one stable URL.
- Should releases be signed, or is SHA-256 against a manifest over HTTPS sufficient for this threat model?
- Default for the update check on a fresh install: on or off?

## Summary

Remote execution today reaches exactly two kinds of target: a machine you can SSH into, and a Slurm cluster. There is no way to run a job on cloud compute — no serverless GPU, no Kubernetes, no cloud VM. A researcher without an HPC allocation or a GPU workstation has no path to accelerated compute at all.

## Current state

The remote-compute model is already well factored, which is why this is an extension rather than a rewrite:

- `RemoteHostConnectionKind = "direct" | "ssh"` — the product either deploys a Runner SEA over SSH (verified host key, SHA-256 checked upload, HTTP tunneled through SSH) or connects to a runner the user started.
- `RemoteJobCard` carries `command`, `inputPaths`, `outputs`, `resources`, `targetAlias`, and `mode: "slurm" | "ssh"`.
- Jobs pass through an approval step (`approvedAt`) before anything runs.
- The host probe records CPU, memory, architecture, scratch paths, and whether Slurm is present — and accepts Linux only.
- Ascend NPU has a dedicated host broker.

So the concepts a cloud backend needs — a job card, declared inputs and outputs, a resource request, an approval gate, a target registry — all exist. What is missing is a third `mode`.

## Why it matters

The Slurm and SSH paths assume the user already has institutional compute. Everyone else — an individual researcher, a small lab, anyone whose cluster queue is full — is limited to the local sandbox. Meanwhile a comparable open-source workbench offers user-owned serverless GPU runs bound to an approved image digest, which is exactly the "I need a GPU for twenty minutes" case we cannot serve.

## Proposal

### 1. A `cloud` job mode behind the existing card + approval model

Define a small provider interface — submit(image digest, command, inputs, resources) → poll status → fetch outputs → report cost — and let backends implement it. The job card, the approval UI, and the output staging stay as they are.

### 2. First backend: Kubernetes Job

Recommended as the first implementation, ahead of any specific vendor:

- works against on-prem clusters, every major cloud, and local clusters for testing;
- no vendor lock-in in a project whose selling point is being model- and vendor-agnostic;
- resource requests, GPU scheduling, and namespaces map cleanly onto `RemoteJobResources`;
- credentials are the user's own kubeconfig, not a service we broker.

A serverless GPU provider can follow once the interface has one real implementation behind it.

### 3. Keep the security contract explicit

Cloud execution is a bigger step than SSH to a known host, because **data leaves the workstation**. So:

- the approval card must show exactly which files are uploaded, where, and to whose account;
- image references must be content-addressed digests, not mutable tags;
- credentials stay user-owned; the product must never proxy compute through an account we control;
- an air-gapped deployment must be able to disable cloud targets entirely;
- show an estimated cost before approval — the governance and quota machinery already exists to hang this on.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A third job mode exists alongside `ssh` and `slurm`, reusing the current job-card and approval flow.
- [ ] At least one backend runs a GPU job end to end: inputs uploaded, job executed, outputs retrieved into the workspace.
- [ ] The approval card states what data leaves the machine and where it goes.
- [ ] Image references are digests.
- [ ] Cloud targets can be disabled by policy for restricted deployments.
- [ ] Failure modes — quota exceeded, image pull failure, job evicted — surface as actionable errors, not a stalled job.

## Open questions

- Kubernetes first, or a serverless GPU provider first for time-to-value?
- Should the cloud backend reuse the Runner SEA inside the container, or invoke the sandboxed executor directly?
- How should cost estimation work when pricing is provider-specific — a per-target rate the user configures?
- Does the Ascend NPU broker share this interface, or stay a separate path?

## Context

Since July 2026 an open-source "science workbench" category has formed, triggered by Anthropic's Claude Science launch (2026-06-30). Three direct open-source alternatives appeared the same week and are now at scale: [synthetic-sci/openscience](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience) (~3.6K★), [aipoch/open-science](https://github.com/aipoch/open-science) (~4.2K★), and [ai4s-research/open-science](https://github.com/ai4s-research/open-science) (~1.7K★). Having compared ScienceDiscovery against them (and against the autonomous-scientist systems: Sakana AI-Scientist, InternScience/InternAgent + MLEvolve), here is a strengths/gaps assessment in the hope it helps prioritization. Facts below are from public repo data collected 2026-09-15.

## Strengths (keep — and communicate)

1. **Sandbox-first security model.** Fail-closed Bubblewrap/Seatbelt execution, operator-scoped NPU chip passthrough, opt-in Broker with fixed entry points and `shell: false`. None of the three competitors communicates a default-isolation story; the highest-engagement technical question on a competitor's launch thread was literally *"are the skills executed within a secure, containerized sandbox by default, or does the user manage isolation?"* — this repo already answers that question, but almost nobody knows it does.
2. **Provenance depth.** CAS with pinned-asset drift rejection, review checks, cross-session/SubAgent citation chains. The strongest provenance story in the category.
3. **Search-camp RSI engine.** The evolve sidecar (flat-PUCT tree + OpenEvolve MAP-Elites, discriminability probe, explicit "no model training, no search-rule modification") is a clean, honest scope with a real cousin in [InternScience/MLEvolve](https://github.com/InternScience/MLEvolve) (#1 on MLE-Bench).
4. **Ascend NPU path.** 910B sandbox passthrough + allowlisted workloads (Protenix/MindScience) is unique in the category and extends machine-verifiable research to device-scale workloads.
5. **Engineering discipline beyond repo age.** Bilingual doc set, CI tiers (UT/ST/mocked E2E), self-documented limitations (e.g., Idea Tree scores are model judgments, not experimental evidence).

## Gaps (ordered by leverage)

1. **Installation/onboarding.** No binaries in Releases — #1 (open since 08-19, rated 1/5) is the only organic user feedback this repo has received, and it is someone who *could not install the product*. All three competitors ship desktop installers and a <10-minute quickstart. This pairs directly with the first-experience goal in #22.
2. **No community surface.** All merged PRs are bots; there are zero human external PRs. For comparison: aipoch merges 6+ human PRs/day; ai4s-research power users file bugs *and* land the fixes (e.g., their stall-guard for looping agents came from a user). A "good first issue" ladder + a contributor guide + weekly maintainer RFC triage would start the flywheel.
3. **Category invisibility + an unverifiable benchmark claim.** 58★ vs 1.7–4.2K for peers; one promotion event found (Sina Finance 2026-08-16) whose headline claim (BiomniBench-DA "业界SOTA") is dual-claimed by aipoch's README badge on the same benchmark. Without published methodology/splits, the claim reads as marketing and hurts credibility with scientists — either publish the eval or drop the superlative.
4. **Adoption levers validated by competitors, still missing here:** headless CLI / task API (repeated cross-repo demand — researchers want CI and agent-to-agent use, not only a GUI), model-provider onboarding (subscription reuse, connectivity-test friction), Windows parity.
5. **Cross-model skill consistency.** The single most-validated complaint in the category: *"one flag switches the model, not whether the skill actually works"* (prompts tuned on one model degrade on smaller/local models). A per-skill model-compatibility matrix or a cross-model smoke-test suite for the 300+ skills would directly differentiate.

## Suggested next steps

- [ ] Ship Linux binaries + a 10-minute quickstart (pairs with #22)
- [ ] Publish evolve/idea-tree efficiency metrics (per-node token cost, CAS reuse rate, surviving-node quality on an independent benchmark) — the pruning+reuse efficiency story is genuinely differentiating and no competitor tells it
- [ ] Benchmark-claim triage: methodology for BiomniBench-DA or remove the SOTA wording
- [ ] Community ladder: CONTRIBUTING good-first-issues + a maintainer-reserved RFC-triage day

Happy to help flesh any of these out.
oldest.title: [Feedback] Strengths and gaps vs. the 2026 open-source science-workbench landscape

## Summary

Both long-running engines — the evolution search and the Idea Tree — can be **started** from the command line but cannot be **observed, controlled, or stopped** from it. Their progress is designed to land on a frontend card, so a terminal user gets a run id and then nothing. I would like `evolve` and `idea` subcommands that reuse the HTTP endpoints the Web UI already calls.

## What happens today

Starting works. `ScienceDiscovery run "/evolve-design --algorithm puct …"` reaches the same control plane as the browser, the agent loads the `evolve-design` skill, and it calls `create_evolve_run`. Then the turn ends — deliberately. The tool's own result text instructs the model:

> The search runs for minutes to hours and its card streams live progress on its own — do not wait for it here, and do not poll `get_evolve_run`.

`create_idea_research` says the same thing:

> After success, report the handoff and end this turn; the existing tree card streams progress. Do not poll or start another research to wait for completion.

That is the right call for the agent loop — polling would burn the budget the search itself needs. But it means **the card is the only progress surface**, and the CLI has no equivalent. `ScienceDiscovery run` prints `Search created: <uuid>` and exits while the search keeps running server-side for hours.

`services/launcher/src/cli-options.ts` has no evolve or idea-tree subcommand and no related flag. So from a terminal today you cannot:

- list the searches or researches that exist;
- see how far one has got;
- fetch a candidate;
- stop one, or pause and resume it.

The only workaround is starting another `run` in the same session and hoping the model calls `get_evolve_run` / `get_idea_research` — a whole model turn spent reading a status field, using tools whose descriptions explicitly tell the model not to poll them.

## The endpoints already exist

The Web UI drives all of this over plain HTTP:

**Evolve**
- `GET /api/evolve/runs`
- `GET /api/evolve/runs/<id>/events?after=<cursor>`
- `GET /api/evolve/runs/<id>/candidates/<codeHash>`
- `POST /api/evolve/runs/<id>/stop`

**Idea Tree**
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research`
- `POST /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research` — `pause`, `continue`, `stop`, `defaults`
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/research/<rid>/events`
- `GET /api/sessions/<sid>/idea-tree/graph`

## The client plumbing also already exists

`services/launcher/src/control-plane-client.ts` has an authenticated generic `request<T>(path, init)` and `subscribeRunEvents()`, a working SSE consumer that "mirrors the Web frontend's `subscribeRunEvents`: fetch with `accept: text/event-stream`, split frames". The launcher also already resolves the bearer token from the data directory. A `watch` subcommand is that SSE reader pointed at a different path — this is wiring, not new infrastructure.

## Proposal

```
ScienceDiscovery evolve list
ScienceDiscovery evolve get <run-id> [--candidate <hash>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve watch <run-id>
ScienceDiscovery evolve stop <run-id>

ScienceDiscovery idea list --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea get <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea watch <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea pause|continue|stop <research-id> --session <id>
```

Conventions, matching what `run` already does:

- **text on a TTY, JSONL when piped.** `run` already switches output mode this way; these commands should not invent a second convention.
- **`watch` resumes rather than replays.** The evolve event endpoint already takes `?after=<cursor>`; a dropped connection should continue from the last event seen.
- **Token and data-dir handling identical to `run`** — sharing a `--data-dir` with `serve` should mean no extra configuration.

One asymmetry to decide: evolve exposes only `stop`, while Idea Tree has `pause` / `continue` / `stop`. Either the CLI mirrors each engine's real capabilities, or evolve gains pause/resume — worth an explicit choice rather than an accident.

## Why it matters

- **Unattended and batch use.** Starting a search from a job script is pointless if the same script cannot poll it, stop it when a budget is spent, or collect the winning candidate.
- **Headless and remote machines.** On a workstation reached over SSH there is no browser to hold the card open. Today that machine can start a multi-hour search it cannot then observe.
- **Consistency.** The CLI is already positioned as the scriptable twin of the Web UI; the two most expensive operations in the product are exactly the ones it cannot drive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Evolve searches and Idea Tree researches can be listed, inspected, watched, and stopped from the CLI.
- [ ] `watch` streams live and resumes from a cursor after a dropped connection.
- [ ] Output follows the existing TTY/pipe convention, so `| jq` works.
- [ ] No new authentication path: the token comes from the data directory as `run` already does.
- [ ] Commands and options appear in `help` and in the CLI reference.
- [ ] Stopping from the CLI has the same effect as stopping from the UI card.

## Open questions

- Should `run` gain an optional `--wait` that blocks until a started engine finishes? Useful in scripts, but these runs last hours — probably better served by `watch`.
- Should `watch` exit non-zero when the run ends in failure, so a script can branch on it?
- Does `evolve list` need session/project scoping, given `GET /api/evolve/runs` is global today?

Related: [#30](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/30) (introduce the CLI in the README) — that issue is about making the CLI discoverable; this one is about the two workflows it cannot reach.
oldest.title: [Feature] CLI subcommands for the long-running engines — evolve and Idea Tree

## Summary

ScienceDiscovery can already evolve the things a user brings it — a program, a prompt, a protocol. It cannot evolve **itself**. I would like RSI support: given a dataset of tasks, search over the agent's own harness — system prompt fragments, specialist instructions, skill methodology, tool and skill selection — score each variant by running it against that dataset, and surface the winner for a human to adopt.

The search machinery for this already exists in `services/evolve`. What is missing is the candidate being the harness, the evaluation being an agent run, and a reviewed promotion step.

## What is already there

This is deliberately an extension, not a new engine.

- **The search sidecar**, `services/evolve`, runs on `agentdescent>=0.4.6` — `evolve()` / `async_evolve()`, `FlatPuct`, the ledger, the verifier and the policies — behind two engines: flat-PUCT tree search (`puct_engine.py`) and MAP-Elites islands with ring migration (`openevolve_engine.py`).
- **Non-program candidates are first class.** `text_candidate.py` exists precisely because "a prompt or an abstract has no docstring", and `judge_domain.py` states its purpose plainly: it "is what makes `/evolve` work on things that are not programs over tables: a prompt, an abstract, a protocol, a plan". Evolving prompt text is not a new capability — it is the existing one pointed at a different file.
- **Four scoring seams**, already cut: `scorecard_domain` (a metric over a dataset), `test_gate_domain` (a suite's pass rate), `script_domain` (a scorer the drafting model writes), `judge_domain` (a rubric read by a model).
- **Anti-reward-hacking is already solved once.** `test_gate_domain` freezes in two layers — a proposal filter over `frozen` globs in the prompt, and enforcement below it — with the upstream note this issue should quote rather than restate: *"without it the shortest path to a high score is to weaken the thing measuring it."* That is the single most important property RSI needs, and the pattern is in the tree.
- **Held-out splitting exists.** `create_evolve_run` already accepts `caseSplit` with `gateGroups`, `rolloutGroups` and `testGroups`, which is the shape needed to keep a harness from overfitting the tasks it was tuned on.
- **Trajectories are recorded.** `packages/trajectory` captures per-session entries with the context blocks that were actually sent, which is the raw material for judging whether a harness change helped.
- **Parts of the harness are already frozen.** Built-in specialists reject edits to `instructions` / `description` / `name` / `connectorIds` / `enabledSkillIds`; only `enabled` is user-mutable. RSI has to open that door deliberately rather than by accident.

## What is missing

1. **The candidate is never the harness.** Today a candidate is one text-shaped artifact the user owns. The agent's own scaffolding lives elsewhere and is not reachable by a search: prompt assembly (`packages/context/src/prompt-renderer.ts`, `assembler.ts`), specialist instructions (`packages/specialist/src/builtins.ts`), skill methodology (`skills/*/SKILL.md`), and the skill/connector selection for a run.

2. **There is no task-dataset scoring mode.** `scorecard_domain` scores a *program* over a table. RSI needs to score a *harness* over a set of tasks, where each evaluation is a full agent run with its own tool calls, sandboxed execution and artifacts. That is a different cost class and needs its own domain.

3. **There is no promotion path.** An improved harness must be diffable, reviewable, versioned and revertible. Nothing should ever be self-applied.

## Proposal

### 1. A harness candidate

A bundle rather than a single blob: prompt fragments, one or more specialist instruction sets, selected skills, and the run settings that go with them. The mutation prompt sees the bundle and rewrites part of it; the ledger records which part changed, so a win is attributable to something specific.

### 2. A `task_dataset` domain

A dataset entry is a task plus whatever the existing four modes need to score its outcome — a metric, a test suite, a scoring script, or a rubric. Evaluating one candidate means running the agent over the split and aggregating. Reuse `caseSplit` so the reported number comes from tasks the search did not tune against.

The honest problem here is cost: one candidate equals N agent runs, each with model calls and sandboxed execution. The design needs a budget per generation and an early-abandon policy, not just a score.

### 3. Freeze the things a self-improving search must not touch

Same two-layer shape `test_gate_domain` already uses, with a wider frozen set:

- the task dataset and its expected outcomes;
- the scorer, whichever mode it is;
- the permission, sandbox and approval layers — a harness that scores better by asking for fewer confirmations is not better;
- the evolve sidecar's own code and the freeze list itself.

A candidate that edits any of these is rejected at the proposal filter, not merely penalized.

### 4. Promotion is a human step

The winner lands as a reviewable proposal: a diff against the current harness, the score with its held-out number, and the trajectory evidence behind it. Adoption is explicit, versioned and revertible. The skill review flow and the built-in specialists' read-only rules already establish that shape; RSI should reuse it rather than invent a second one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A search can take the agent's harness as its candidate, not only a user artifact.
- [ ] A task dataset can be supplied, and a candidate is scored by running the agent over it.
- [ ] The reported score comes from a held-out split.
- [ ] The dataset, the scorer, and the permission/sandbox layers are frozen against modification by the search, enforced at the proposal filter.
- [ ] An improved harness appears as a reviewable, versioned proposal and is never self-applied.
- [ ] Reverting to the previous harness is one action.
- [ ] A run states its budget and stops at it.

## Open questions

- Should a run evolve one specialist at a time, or the whole bundle? One at a time attributes wins more cleanly; the whole bundle can find interactions.
- Where does a task dataset live — a repository artifact, a workspace file, or a first-class store object?
- Which engine fits better? PUCT refines one starting point; OpenEvolve's islands keep diversity, which may matter more when a prompt change can be good in one dimension and harmful in another.
- What is the minimum dataset size where a win is believable rather than noise, given the non-determinism the judge mode already documents?
- Should this reuse `/evolve-design`'s checkpointed design conversation, or have its own entry point?

Related: [#50](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/50) — the engines can be started but not observed or stopped from the CLI, which matters more for a search whose evaluations are full agent runs.
oldest.title: [Feature] RSI — evolve the agent's own harness against a task dataset, reusing the agentdescent search
