items.body:
Related to #812

Partial. Keep #812 open.

A directed search can now run on the conversation's selected runner. A JSON the search had already measured was still spending a round, and a reply that was not a JSON object was spending one too. The NPU path handed the search library one task, which that library refuses to start on. A search that does not name editable fields stays the existing free program search.

## Directed edits

The chat agent starts the run and does not pick later steps. PUCT chooses which measured node to expand. The model then proposes one JSON object. Only the fields the user ticked may change. A proposal that matches an edit already measured, a reply that is not a JSON object, and an edit that leaves the declared fields are not sent to the runner. The model is asked again, inside the same slot, up to three extra times. If it is still not a runnable edit, that reply is rejected before the runner and has no score.

There is no task-specific update rule. The model sees the measured values and their scores and proposes the next JSON itself.

## NPU scoring

Each candidate is one fresh shell execution on the conversation's selected runner, in a sandbox with no network. The fixed program computes the score. The candidate is JSON bound as input, not the program that runs. Success is a completed execution whose result says the device is `npu` and includes a number. A job that is still queued or running is waited on and does not take another slot. A failure, a cancellation, or a missing result has no score and is not stored as 0.

The search library requires at least four tasks and a hold-out fraction strictly between 0 and 1. An NPU search supplies four task ids and holds one out. The domain caches the measurement, so those ids do not each use the card.

## Field table

The run shows the ticked fields. Each candidate row shows which field changed, the old value, the new value, and the score.

## Review follow-up

- Each submitted execution retains the runner that accepted it. Polling and cancellation no longer depend on the current runner order or NPU-card selection. A disconnected accepting runner produces an error rather than redirecting the execution. Execution IDs are isolated by run, cannot be resubmitted, and retain their route after an uncertain submit response.
- The field list now distinguishes loading and source-read failures, with localized retry in English and Chinese. Changing the run or source clears stale rows and ignores late responses.
- A repeated-edit prompt shows at most eight recent edits, with each preview capped at 200 characters. The full measured-edit set still prevents duplicate execution.
- `-inf` is an internal ranking sentinel, not a wire score. `events.seeded` and `events.expanded` normalize non-finite scores through `finite()` to JSON `null`. `encode_ndjson(..., allow_nan=False)` rejects a missed non-finite value before it can emit invalid JSON. A regression test covers both null conversion and fail-closed encoding.

## Validation

The checks in this section were recorded on the earlier head `eff542cc`. See the workbench follow-up for validation of the new head.

- Directed/NPU Python tests: 22 passed.
- Runner proxy, preflight, proposal and orchestrator tests: 79 passed, including 9 runner-proxy tests.
- FieldDirection React tests: 6 passed, covering both locales, failed load followed by retry, source/run replacement and stale responses.
- `pnpm typecheck`: passed. Local L1: 4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed.
- [Earlier-head CI](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42500907449) passed: L1, UT, ST, all five mocked L2 E2E shards, Coverage and merge-gate. Real L3/L4/L5 E2E were skipped; these results do not replace the required real-browser captures.
- [Previous head `7b6dcbf7` CI](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42497149247) passed: UT 6949/6949, ST 51/51, mocked E2E 136/136, and merge-gate.
- Full local layers cannot be claimed green on this cloud host. Its sandbox cannot create the required NETLINK_ROUTE socket, and inherited proxy settings also affected local tests. On the previous tree the full Evolve suite had 390 passes and the same 21 failures reproduced on unmodified main; the original ST failure set also matched main. The new focused checks above passed without weakening those assertions.

## E2E user journeys and captures

**Required visual evidence remains BLOCKED.** The requested before/after captures in `zh-CN` and `en` are not attached yet: the pinned Chromium download on this host returns an unavailable or invalid archive, so no browser or viewport verification is claimed for this update. The outstanding captures are the declared-field header, changed-value rows with a missing score, a long field table, and a free-program run with no editable fields.

The React tests establish state/retry behavior, not rendered layout. The passing prior mocked E2E suite does not replace these specific captures.

Earlier local NPU evidence recorded for this PR, not rerun for this follow-up: one selected card completed 10 requested rounds and stored 10 new measurements. Seven repeated proposals were re-asked within the same round without being sent to the card. That run did not exercise a non-JSON reply; the branch is covered by unit tests. The field table was not clicked through in that earlier run.

## Release

Release category: release:feature

User impact: a search can score candidates on the conversation's selected NPU runner, and can limit edits to named JSON fields. A reply that is not a runnable edit is asked again inside the same round.

Compatibility and migration: none for a search that does not ask for a runner or a field list. That path stays the existing program search.

## Workbench UI screenshots

The composer shows how many fields may change after the user confirms the scope. The scope card shows the task, the initial values, and the fields the user can select. It also offers a task-based draft, JSON upload, and row controls for adding, editing, or removing fields.

![Confirmed edit scope in the composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0761c1e5-df60-4c12-a247-952cb16561f9)

![Edit scope card with one editable field](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7bf2dca1-ee66-4b8e-9851-36d346de55bf)

### New desktop workbench UI (served in the browser)

These screenshots show the new desktop workbench served in the browser with `SCIENCE_AGENT_WEB_DIR=apps/desktop/dist`. The first shows the optional **Set edit scope** action beside the existing composer. The second shows the JSON draft and field selection card, using the task already entered in the composer.

![New desktop workbench composer with Set edit scope](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01930862-60be-43f4-b3a2-1c8ea6bbed0b)

![New desktop workbench edit scope card with a generated JSON draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dca69a40-5f72-4277-aed6-da7623f6d50d)

## Workbench follow-up

The existing Evolve setup still selects the algorithm and places the command in the conversation composer. The composer remains the only place to enter the task. **Set edit scope** is optional. It uses the composer text to generate a starting JSON draft or accepts a user-provided file. The user can edit, add, remove, and select fields before confirming. Confirming the scope saves it on the draft. Sending the task remains a separate action. The API binds the confirmed baseline and editable fields before creating the search.

The same workflow is available in the desktop workbench when it is served in a browser. Set `SCIENCE_AGENT_WEB_DIR=apps/desktop/dist` and restart the API to serve it at the root path.

### Follow-up validation

- WSL workspace build and both renderer type checks passed.
- 24 API proposal tests and 21 Python direction tests passed.
- The draft endpoint was exercised with a local model fixture. It returned a task-specific draft without starting Evolve.
- Chromium verified both workbenches. The original Web workbench was checked at desktop and narrow widths for draft generation, JSON upload, row edits, and scope confirmation. The browser-hosted desktop workbench was checked for the original composer flow, the disabled draft action before typing, draft generation from the composer text, and scope confirmation without sending the task.
- A full real Evolve search was not run. Full local UT, ST, and mocked E2E results are incomplete after a WSL interruption. The PR author requested that GitHub CI run the full checks on this revision.

### CI follow-up after rebasing

Rebased onto main at `9feafa27`. The platform conflict was limited to imports. The rebased code keeps main's stop-run and active-run guard and still passes the user-confirmed proposal to the orchestrator.

The WSL workspace build, both renderer type checks, all 35 focused API tests, and all 21 Python direction tests passed on `4e48ca3`. Full checks for the rebased head are tracked in [GitHub Actions run 42572726350](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42572726350).

items.body:
Fixes #995

## The defect

After a `.sdresearch` import, the dialog's `onImported` handler refreshed the session lists and then left the user on whatever session was open before. When the import creates a **separate** read-only research copy (the shape in the issue: target `dc455d7a…`, imported `119daad8…`), that produced the reported end state: the copy appears in the list, the previous writable session is still on screen, and since the copy rejects messages (`409 SESSION_EVIDENCE_LOCKED`) the writable one is the only place to type. One import looks like two open sessions, with the wrong one active.

## Change

`apps/web/src/App.tsx` — `onImported` now distinguishes the two outcomes instead of always leaving the view alone:

- **The import wrote into the session the user was already on** (the dialog imports into the current session when it can): keep that session and refresh it. Switching away would hide the history that was just restored into it.
- **A separate read-only copy was created** (the #995 shape): open it. The dialog has just told the user the package is a locked snapshot, so that is the session they asked for; the previous writable session — and the temptation to type into it — is no longer what they land on.
- Nothing is created here: a writable continuation still comes only from the explicit "创建新会话继续研究" action, which matches the read-only-snapshot model the dialog states.
- The imported id is adopted only when the refreshed list actually contains it, so a stale or rejected import keeps the previous behaviour.

The first attempt at this always opened the first imported id, and `test/journey-restore-research.spec.ts` caught it: in that journey the import targets the current session, so switching away from it left the imported transcript off screen after 「查看导入会话」 closed the dialog. The second commit fixes that by keeping the current session when it is one of the imported ids.

## Scope

- This is the web flow the issue reproduced. The Windows desktop import dialog has its own continuation hand-off (`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`, changed in #999) and is not touched here to avoid two PRs editing the same block.
- The issue's third point is marked "Ideally": *the project's auto-created empty `Untitled session` does not linger next to the imported copy when the project was created only to receive an import*. That one is not done: it means deleting a session, and the wording leaves it optional. If you want it, the shape is "delete the auto-created session when it is provably empty (no messages, runs or files) and it was created for this import" — say so and I will add it with that guard rather than delete anything that might hold work.

## Verification

`test/journey-restore-research.spec.ts` covers the import path end to end (import → close the dialog → act on the imported session), and its first run on the initial commit is exactly what proved the earlier version wrong. The corrected version is running on CI now.

## Screenshots

The two outcomes `onImported` now distinguishes, in zh-CN and en.

### Outcome 1 — import wrote into the session already open

The current session stays open and its restored history is reloaded; nothing switches.

**zh-CN**

![zh-CN: import into current session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1005/zh-current-after.png)

**en**

![en: import into current session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1005/en-current-after.png)

### Outcome 2 — a separate read-only copy was created

The imported read-only copy is opened; the previous writable session is left behind in the list rather than left on screen.

**zh-CN**

![zh-CN: read-only copy opened](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1005/zh-copy-after.png)

**en**

![en: read-only copy opened](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1005/en-copy-after.png)

The import-completion dialog for each is at `pr-1005/{zh,en}-{copy,current}-complete.png` on the same branch.

items.body:
Fixes #930

A caller-supplied string that is over its length limit answered `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}`, so a provider form could not tell the user which field to shorten. The store already produces the right message (`The LLM API token is too long`); the shared request classifier just never recognised the shape and fell through to the catch-all.

## What was wrong

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` listed eight legacy validation messages that stay `400` (`is required`, `must`, `cannot`, `invalid`, …). In `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, `POST /api/providers/preview-models` calls `normalizeApiToken(body.apiToken)` before any network call, and `services/api/src/store/secrets.ts` throws a plain `Error("The LLM API token is too long")` once the trimmed token passes 16 384 characters. That message matched none of the eight patterns, so it reached the `unclassified_request_error` branch and became a 500.

The same shape appears at seven throw sites, all rejecting a client-supplied string, so they all leaked the same way:

| site | message |
| --- | --- |
| `store/secrets.ts` | `The LLM API token is too long` |
| `store/settings.ts` | `The proxy URL is too long` |
| `store/settings.ts` | `neo4jHttp is too long` |
| `store/settings.ts` | `neo4jUser is too long` |
| `store.ts` | `The Neo4j password is too long` |
| `store.ts` | `Model ID is too long` |
| `store.ts` | `The stored ${kind} is too long` |

## What changed

One pattern in the classifier, nothing else:

```ts
/\bis too long\b/i,
```

No new error code, no change to `normalizeApiToken` or any limit, no change to a throw site, and `services/api/src/http/index.ts` is untouched (`#929` owns the dispatch line next to the chain and this change does not meet it). The message already produced by the store is passed through unchanged, so the client sees `{"error":"The LLM API token is too long"}`.

The test file extends the existing table with the seven length messages above and adds one negative case that mentions a length without the validation shape (`Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget`), which must stay a 500; the existing `Database invariant failed` assertion is unchanged.

## Red first

Commit `341a5007` is the test only, on the unfixed classifier:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts
not ok 1 - keeps known validation failures at 400 without hiding internal faults
  error: |-
    The LLM API token is too long

    false !== true
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

Per message, before the fix (`isKnownClientInputError(new Error(message))`):

```
false  The LLM API token is too long
false  The proxy URL is too long
false  neo4jHttp is too long
false  neo4jUser is too long
false  The Neo4j password is too long
false  Model ID is too long
false  The stored runnerToken is too long
false  Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget
false  Database invariant failed
```

Route level, against the same unfixed tree, with a temporary probe that started the real `createApiServer` (offline MCP transport, temp data dir) and sent the issue's requests (probe file not committed):

```
STATUS 500 TEXT {"error":"Internal server error"}          POST /api/providers/preview-models  apiToken "k"×20000
STATUS 400 TEXT {"error":"The LLM API token cannot be empty"}  same route, apiToken ""
STATUS 201 ...                                             POST /api/providers, apiToken 16384 chars
```

The empty-token and valid-token readings are the control: the validator was already healthy at both ends, only the length case escaped.

## After the fix

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts
# tests 1
# pass 1
# fail 0
```

Same probe, fixed tree:

```
STATUS 400 TEXT {"error":"The LLM API token is too long"}
STATUS 400 TEXT {"error":"The LLM API token cannot be empty"}
STATUS 201 ... POST /api/providers apiToken 16384 chars
```

Per message, after the fix: the seven length messages are all `true`, and both non-validation messages (`Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget`, `Database invariant failed`) are still `false`, so a genuine internal fault still answers 500.

Diffstat against `main` `2908e9e8`:

```
 services/api/src/http/error-classification.test.ts | 10 ++++++++++
 services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts      |  3 +++
 2 files changed, 13 insertions(+)
```

Commits: `341a5007` test (red), `8b4c124c` fix.

Ran:
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts` — `# pass 0 # fail 1` on the red commit, `# pass 1 # fail 0` on the fix.
- Temporary route probe as above (unfixed: 500; fixed: 400 with the store's message; empty token 400; valid token 201) — file deleted before the commit, so the diff stays at two files.
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `grep -rn "too long" services/api/src --include=*.test.ts` — no other test asserts one of these messages, so no existing expectation flips.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser journey: the changed surface is the request classifier, and the route-level probe above drives the real HTTP server rather than a browser.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: an over-long API token, proxy URL, Neo4j field, model id or stored credential now answers 400 with the validation message that names it instead of 500 "Internal server error". Genuinely internal failures still answer 500, and every accepted value behaves as before.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Fixes #665

`web_fetch`'s public-URL guard lets several IPv6 families through even though each one carries an IPv4 address the guard already knows how to judge. A model-supplied URL such as `http://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/` or `http://[2002:a9fe:a9fe::]/` reaches loopback or the link-local metadata endpoint, while the equivalent `::ffff:127.0.0.1` is rejected. This closes those holes, pins that public addresses in the same forms keep working, and — after review — refuses the non-canonical suffixes of the local-use NAT64 prefix rather than guessing where their IPv4 address sits.

## What was wrong

`ipv6Blocked()` consulted `ipv4Blocked()` only for IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) and IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d`) forms, where the embedded IPv4 address sits in the last two hextets. Other families carry the same address elsewhere:

| family | prefix | where the IPv4 address sits | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NAT64 well-known | `64:ff9b::/96` | last 32 bits | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| NAT64 local-use | `64:ff9b:1::/48` | last 32 bits **only for the canonical `/96` sub-layout** | canonical `/96` decoded; every other suffix under the `/48` rejected |
| 6to4 | `2002::/16` | hextets 2–3 | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| IPv4-translated | `::ffff:0:0:0/96` | last 32 bits, after `ffff` and 16 zero bits | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| Teredo | `2001:0::/32` | last 32 bits, bitwise inverted | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| site-local (deprecated) | `fec0::/10` | no IPv4 — the range itself is non-public | reject |

No branch inspected those positions, so each form fell through to `return false`.

The local-use row is the review fix. `64:ff9b:1::/48` is wider than the `/96` an embedded address needs, and RFC 8215 allows deployments to use other suffix lengths — a deployment that puts the IPv4 address in bits 64–95 is not judged by hextets 6–7. Reading hextets 6–7 of *every* address in the `/48` therefore judged the wrong bits: `64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808` was interpreted as the public `128.8.8.8`.

## What changed

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts`: one helper, `dotted(high, low)`, and `ipv6Blocked()` extracts the embedded address for the rows above and hands it to the existing `ipv4Blocked()`. There is no second copy of the IPv4 block list, no blanket range ban, and no refactor of the existing mapped/compatible branches.

For the local-use prefix the rule is now explicit and fail-closed: decode the canonical `64:ff9b:1:0:0:0::/96` sub-layout, and **return blocked for every non-canonical suffix** under `64:ff9b:1::/48` (`return true`, never `return false` — an unknown suffix must not become the way around the guard). The well-known `64:ff9b::/96` prefix is untouched by that rule.

## Red first

The new test (`providers.test.ts`), run against the unfixed `url-guard.ts`:

```
not ok 11 - web_fetch judges NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local literals by their embedded IPv4
  error: |-
    64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808

    false !== true

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  expected: true
  actual: false
# tests 16
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

The assertion loop stops at its first failing literal, so every blocked literal was also probed one by one against the unfixed predicate, and every public one against the fixed predicate. Values are `blocked` / `allowed` from `isBlockedAddress`; the flipped rows are the review fix, all in the tightening direction:

| address | before `e9e7358c` review fix | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `64:ff9b::7f00:1` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b::808:808` | allowed | allowed |
| `64:ff9b:1::7f00:1` (canonical `/96`) | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1::a9fe:a9fe` (canonical `/96`) | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1::808:808` (canonical `/96`) | allowed | allowed |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:1:0:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:0:1:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:dead:beef:cafe:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:7f00:1` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:a9fe:a9fe` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |

Five flips in this probed set, all `allowed → blocked`; zero `blocked → allowed`.

## Only tighter

The same probe run before and after the review fix differs in exactly one line — the tightened address. Everything a legitimate client may reach still resolves as public:

```
ALLOW  literal 64:ff9b::808:808            (NAT64 well-known, public)
ALLOW  literal 64:ff9b:1::808:808          (NAT64 local-use canonical /96, public)
ALLOW  literal 2002:808:808::              (6to4 for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal ::ffff:0:808:808            (IPv4-translated for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal 2001:0:808:808::f7f7:f7f7   (Teredo for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal 2606:4700:4700::1111        (native IPv6)
ALLOW  resolver 64:ff9b::808:808 for http://example.com/
ALLOW  resolver 2606:4700:4700::1111 for http://example.com/
```

These are asserted in the test too (`assert.equal(isBlockedAddress(...), false)` and `assert.equal(await assertPublicUrl(...), url)`), so the guard cannot be "fixed" by blocking a prefix.

## After the fix

```
# tests 16
# pass 16
# fail 0
```

The test now has 17 blocked addresses and 6 public ones (23 assertions across the literal and resolver paths), including the canonical `/96` cases in both directions and the non-canonical suffixes.

Diffstat against `main` `f4dd1813`:

```
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts | 71 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts      | 35 +++++++++++-
 2 files changed, 106 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

This branch is `f4dd1813` + four commits, two files, nothing else:

1. `dd29d921` test: pin NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local fetch targets
2. `eb818998` fix: judge NAT64, 6to4 and IPv4-translated literals by their embedded IPv4
3. `e4bb3e67` test: judge the local-use NAT64 prefix by its canonical /96 only
4. `e9e7358c` fix: decode only the canonical /96 under the local-use NAT64 prefix

It does not contain any commit from #915; the three-file view was the reviewer's worktree.

Ran:
- `node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts` in `packages/data-source` — `# tests 16 # pass 16 # fail 0`; the same command on the unfixed source is the red above (`# pass 15 # fail 1`).
- `tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- Per-address probe of the 17 blocked and 6 public literals before and after the review fix — the before/after table and the only-tighter block above.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` (full layers) were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser/API/CLI journey was added: the change is a predicate inside the `web_fetch` URL guard, and the mocked E2E subset does not exercise NAT64/6to4 literals.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: a model-supplied `web_fetch` URL that encodes a private, loopback or link-local IPv4 address in NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated, Teredo or site-local form is rejected with `PublicUrlError` instead of being fetched; public addresses in the same forms keep working, and non-canonical suffixes of the local-use NAT64 prefix are rejected rather than guessed at.

Compatibility and migration: none. A deployment that puts the NAT64 IPv4 address in bits 64–95 of `64:ff9b:1::/48` is now rejected instead of silently misjudged; the canonical `/96` layout and `64:ff9b::/96` behave exactly as before.

items.author: qingkwl
items.body:
Follow-up to #969. That PR made A6 **count** the precompiled bytecode so an incomplete set fails the build; this one adds a gate for the bytecode's **invalidation mode**, and a step that converts the files A6 was already counting but could not judge.

## The defect

release7 shipped **37,324 `.pyc`, of which 971 were in timestamp invalidation mode**. Every gate was green and none of them was wrong: A1/A1b import fine (the bytecode *is* valid), A5 measures path length, and A6 counts `.pyc` against `.py` — 971 files that ship in the **wrong mode** still count as shipped. Coverage and mode are different properties, and A6 only ever checked the first.

The installed tree pays for the difference. NSIS extraction restamps every `.py` to the install instant, so a timestamp-mode `.pyc` is stale the moment it lands and CPython recompiles it. Measured on a field install (`D:\ProgramData\ScienceDiscovery`): **the first launch rewrote 1,048 `.pyc`**, inside the same busy two minutes as `jiuwenswarm-init` and `proactive_engine`.

## Why step 7c did not already fix it

7c already runs `compileall --invalidation-mode checked-hash`. But `compileall` only **rewrites a `.pyc` it judges invalid**, and all 971 were judged **valid** in the build tree — the copy chain preserved each `.py`'s original mtime, so the timestamp check passed and skipping them was *correct behaviour*, not a coverage hole. Measured, four arms (`logs/w28-evidence/w28c-compileall-mode-experiment.mjs`, run with the bundled interpreter): valid timestamp-mode `.pyc` + checked-hash `compileall` → **still timestamp-mode**.

Blocking the copy points is not an option either. Reading `co_filename` from **all** 971 (not a sample) shows three provenances: 619 from the dev venv, **350 from uv's CPython distribution stdlib** (copied by a different statement, `assemble-backend.mjs:689`), and 2 with relative paths. Any per-copy-point fix leaks one of them.

## What the change does

**A1c — convert, in place, after the import self-checks.** `py_compile(CHECKED_HASH)` over exactly the sources whose `.pyc` shipped timestamp-mode, overwriting the stale file.

**A6-mode — fail the build on any timestamp-mode `.pyc`.** This is the net for a cause nobody thought to blocklist: a conversion that skipped a target, an interpreter that declined a file, or a future copy step that pulls dev-tree bytecode in *after* A1c ran. The limit is **exact zero, not a ratio**: mode is binary per file and the conversion is deterministic, so a tolerance would be a budget for the regression this stops. An **unparseable header also fails** — a mode nobody could read is not a mode that is fine.

The driver is an exported string constant (`RECOMPILE_DRIVER`) rather than a separate `.py`, so `test/pyc-mode.test.ts` asserts the text the build *actually* pipes to python and executes it against a real interpreter. A hand-copied replica would prove the replica.

### Three constraints each finding added

1. **A1c must run *after* A1/A1b.** Both execute a payload python, and an implicit import that has to compile a source writes **timestamp-mode** bytecode by default. Converting before them would let a self-check silently undo the conversion. The test suite pins this ordering textually, and the mutation sentinel injects "A1c moved before the probe" as a defect that must be caught.
2. **`sourceOfPyc` must agree with CPython, not with my intuition.** It splits at the first dot to match `importlib.util.source_from_cache`. Diverging would map to a path CPython never uses. There is a test that checks it against the real interpreter.
3. **The A5 advisory got sharper.** A5 reports `maxRel=192` against a build budget of 176, and that overage is safe *only* while the shipped checked-hash set stays complete — first-run precompile must remain a no-op. A6-mode is now what keeps that promise true.

## Scope and cost — three shapes measured, not assumed

| shape | measured cost | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| delete the stale `.pyc`, let `compileall` recreate them | **~500 ms/file to delete × 971 ≈ 8 minutes** | rejected |
| **recompile in place, overwriting (shipped)** | **8.4 s for all 971**, `recompiled=971 failed=0` | **chosen** |
| global `compileall -f` | **280.2 s** — recompiles all 37,998 sources to fix 971 (**33×**) | rejected |

The deletion cost is not a property of the payload: `w28c-c2-unlink-cost.txt` measured unlink at **~500 ms/file in the workspace, in its parent, and on a different volume**, and only **0.92 ms in `%TEMP%`**. Defender real-time protection was off and the volume is a healthy local NTFS SSD, so that 500× spread is an artifact of this machine's filesystem stack. Measuring it only at the convenient location would have chosen a fix ~150× slower in the real build directory.

## Verification

- `test/pyc-mode.test.ts`: **25 tests, 0 skipped**. The behavioural ones run a real python and read the header of the `.pyc` the driver produced — conversion, idempotence, and loud failure on a source it cannot compile.
- **Mutation sentinel** (`w28c-mutation-sentinel.mjs`): 10 injected defects — A1c moved before the probe, the walk stops counting, the gate stops failing, an inlined driver, a 1000-file tolerance, `UNCHECKED_HASH`, a driver that swallows errors, an inverted mode bit, a short header read as fine, a zero-`.pyc` pass — **all 10 caught, 0 survived, 0 not-applied**. A green suite alone proves nothing; a gate that can never fail prints the same line.
- **Gate on the real tree** (`w28c-gate-on-real-tree.mjs`): extracts A1c / the walk / A6-mode **verbatim out of this file** and runs them on a copy of the release7 payload (37,998 `.py` + 37,324 `.pyc`). Negative arm (no A1c) → A6-mode reports **971 timestamp, exit=3**. Positive arm (A1c) → **recompiled 971, failed 0 → 37,324 checked-hash, 0 timestamp, exit=0**, coverage unchanged (`maxRel=192`). Text assertions prove the wiring; this proves the body runs.
- Full suite on this head: **247 win_desktop tests** (0 fail, 0 skipped), **architecture gate 347 files OK**, **44 root script tests**.

## Measured net benefit — a real installer, not a projection

Built **release8** end to end from this change (`assemble-backend` → `electron-builder`): `ScienceDiscovery-0.3.0-win-x64-setup.exe`, **614,944,658 B = 586.5 MiB**, blockmap and 3 locale paks. In the real build A1c reported `converting 971 timestamp-mode .pyc` → `recompiled 971, failed 0`, and A6-mode reported **`37324 checked-hash, 0 timestamp, 0 unparseable`**. An independent re-walk of the staged tree (not assemble's own counters) agrees: `pyc=37324 hash=37324 timestamp=0 unparseable=0`.

Then the first-launch cost, measured as a **pair** (`w28c-net-benefit.mjs`): the same 971 sources in the same location under the same bundled interpreter, differing only in the invalidation mode of their `.pyc`, with every `.py` restamped to one install instant exactly as NSIS does. The judgement goes through CPython's own `SourceFileLoader.get_code()`, so it classifies, validates, and writes back on a miss — the real import path, without executing module bodies.

| work tree location | control (release7 timestamp-mode) | treated (release8 checked-hash) | **saving** |
|---|---|---|---|
| `%TEMP%` (C:) | 971 recompiled / 7.01 s | 0 recompiled / 1.59 s | 5.43 s |
| **D: (the production install volume)** | **971 recompiled / 8.73 s** | **0 recompiled / 1.82 s** | **6.92 s (7.1 ms/file)** |

**The D: number is the one that counts.** Same harness, same files, different volume — `%TEMP%` on this host is a fast outlier (0.92 ms vs ~500 ms for unlink), so measuring there understated the saving by 22%. That is the same trap the cost table above avoided.

Two honest limits on **6.92 s**:

- It is a **lower bound**. It isolates the 971 mode-attributable files; the field install rewrote 1,048, and a real first launch also carries `jiuwenswarm-init` and `proactive_engine` I/O, which contention would inflate further.
- It is **not** an end-to-end installed cold-start timing. Both installers share `appId cn.sciencediscovery.desktop` with `perMachine: false`, so silently installing the second one rewrites the HKCU uninstall entry the first one owns and leaves the tester's existing install without an uninstaller. That is an irreversible change to a machine that is not mine to spend, so the paired measurement above stands in for it. A full installed cold-start timing needs a volunteer machine or a distinct appId.

One measurement defect worth recording, because it produced a confident wrong number before it was caught: the first revision of this harness enumerated files with `glob("**/*.pyc")`, which **skips path components starting with a dot** — and most of this payload lives under `backend\jw\.venv\`. It measured **711 of 971** files. The "both arms agree" sentinel passed, because the omission is symmetric. The harness now receives the file list explicitly and reports `listed`/`measured`/`missing`, with a coverage sentinel that fails unless all 971 were exercised.

## Regression

`assemble-backend.mjs` gains 112 lines; `lib/pyc-mode.mjs` (317) and `test/pyc-mode.test.ts` (433) are new. Nothing existing is removed or re-timed: A6's budget gate, A5's path gate, and steps A1–A4 keep their behaviour, and A1c is additive between A1b and A2. A build that already shipped all-checked-hash bytecode converts nothing and is unaffected (`recompileTimestampBytecode` does not spawn an interpreter for an empty list — tested).

## Summary

Fixes #264.

Make proxy setup usable from one **Network and proxy** settings entry, and keep local application transport independent of outbound proxy failures. Reuse the existing proxy registry, downloader cache/retry, and environment-readiness mechanisms rather than adding an automatic external-network startup gate.

## Changes

- Offer environment configuration, a custom HTTP(S)/SOCKS5 proxy, or direct access. Keep named proxies, bypass hosts and Web/MCP overrides under advanced settings; existing model overrides remain compatible.
- Stage proxy changes across settings tabs. The footer saves them; Cancel/X discards unsaved changes. Add an authenticated, non-persisting download-source connection diagnostic.
- Declare and lock Python HTTP/WebSocket SOCKS dependencies. Adapter loopback HTTP/WebSocket connections explicitly bypass outbound proxies; external HTTP clients are initialized lazily.
- Add small source-loadable shared routing/download helpers. Resolve model requests against their actual target, respect bypass rules, and pass the global policy to managed environment setup/create/install operations without mutating process-wide environment variables.
- Wire the saved global route into both Runner clients: the control plane's own local Runner, and every remote Runner that `RemoteComputeClient` deploys or installs into. Environment mode resolves on the remote Runner itself; a custom URL pointing at the control host's loopback is refused with the reason and the two ways out, because forwarding it would make the remote Runner call itself.
- Refuse proxy settings that cannot be applied instead of degrading silently: a `url` policy without an address, and a proxy URL carrying a path or query (rejected at save time as well, so a stored value cannot fail only per request). The generated `NO_PROXY` lists `::1` rather than `[::1]`, which no consumer matches against a bare hostname.
- Preserve underlying, redacted network errors and existing pinned versions, SHA-256/TLS verification, caches and retries. Update English/Chinese configuration, architecture and REST documentation, including the settings-projection contract change (environment summaries now mask credentials and query strings).

## Rebase onto `main` (`b31f74eb`)

- The branch was 699 commits behind and conflicted in three files. `packages/model/src/client.ts`, `services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts`, `packages/executor` and the gateway tests were re-derived from `main`, then the PR's own deltas re-applied one hunk at a time.
- `normalizeUsage` is gone from this PR: `main` moved it to `packages/model/src/usage.ts` and already reads the protocol field per dialect with alias fallback, so the bug this branch started from is fixed upstream. Keeping the branch copy would have reverted that.
- The branch's `services/adapter/uv.lock` is dropped because `main` deleted the lockfile (`feat(sizeopt)`).
- The branch's last commit (`a49f92ed`, "preserve current runtime interfaces after rebase") is dropped: it reverted `model-connectivity.ts`, `client.ts` and the adapter `network.py` to the branch's older shape, i.e. it undid upstream work rather than preserving the PR. Its only real purpose was to make the stale branch compile, which the re-application above now covers.

## Validation

No real LLM API calls or paid tokens were used.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm --filter` builds: `schema`, `data-source`, `model`, `executor`, `runner`, `api` | Passed |
| `pnpm --recursive typecheck` plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | Passed |
| Proxy transport, resolver, connectivity (`packages/data-source`, `services/api`) | 14 passed |
| Model client and dispatcher regressions (`packages/model`) | 46 passed |
| Runner client proxy propagation (`packages/executor`) | 7 passed |
| Web settings component suite (`apps/web`) | 258 passed |
| `pnpm architecture:check` / `pnpm ci:selftest` | 43 / 16 passed |
| `services/runner` environment-store, `services/api` store/server suites | Not runnable on this Windows host (`os:linux` tags, bubblewrap, SQLite unlink); CI covers them |
| Adapter hermetic pytest | Not runnable here (no usable Python); CI covers it |

The browser journeys use a real local API/Swarm stack, not mocked settings storage. They cover basic defaults; custom proxy save/cancel; cross-tab drafts; reload persistence; NO_PROXY; Web/MCP overrides and inheritance; rejection of deleting an in-use proxy; and removing references plus deleting the proxy in one save. Only the first journey's connection-test response is browser-mocked; transport ST tests exercise local HTTP/SOCKS proxy fixtures and authentication failures without external access.

The legacy layout E2E is adapted but remains quarantined and was not run. No production service was restarted.

## Scope and boundaries

- This does not grant sandbox network access or add an automatic direct fallback when a configured proxy fails.
- The manual diagnostic checks one download source, not every provider or model credentials. There is no new startup preflight framework or traffic dashboard.
- Saving multiple settings sections is sequential, not a cross-section transaction: a later failure does not roll back earlier successful requests. Unsaved changes remain drafts.
- SOCKS5 support in Undici remains experimental. Remote end-to-end proxy reachability, binary installation and real external providers have not been newly exercised by this PR.

## Summary

Part of #835.

This is the first KE core slice proposed in #835. It introduces only the pure text, extraction, and entity-resolution domain of the Knowledge Engine; it does not register API routes, agent tools, UI, background jobs, or runtime settings.

### Included

- Text parsing and retrieval primitives, including JATS, LaTeX, document levels, trigram/search, and citation helpers.
- LLM extraction schemas/prompts and the provenance gate requiring document anchors for extracted knowledge.
- Entity normalization, matching, merge policy, offline resolution, and sample evaluation data.
- Independent-review hardening for single-line display math, relevance-ordered FTS over-fetch, repeated citation anchors on one line, JATS formula alternatives, optional LaTeX macro defaults, and token-safe entity endpoint matching.
- Additional bot-review hardening: bounded worker-based regex execution, Unicode entity screening, LaTeX preamble removal, multiword/CJK entity and novelty matching, and grouped JATS citation IDs.
- CodeCheck cleanup for loop style and redundant non-null assertions, without changing test expectations.
- Follow-up review hardening: grep input is capped before worker cloning, worker startup and regex execution have separate deadlines, and large-corpus hits survive with honest scan truncation. The provenance fallback now requires ordered token evidence (including single-character entity tokens), rejecting word-permuted or semantically inverted quotes.
- Package-local unit tests and the package/lockfile wiring needed to build `@sciencediscovery/knowledge-engine`.

### Explicitly excluded

- Graph, growth, and evaluation orchestration modules.
- SQLite/API services, connectors, PDF workers, agent integration, and Web UI.
- `pairs.realworld.json` and other large/local fixtures.
- qa/, .tmp/, credentials, and local development artifacts.

The package index exports only modules present in this stage. Four graph-dependent resolution tests from the full reference implementation remain for the graph stage; no production module was stubbed to hide that dependency.

## Validation

- Windows package build: passed.
- Windows package typecheck: passed.
- Fresh native WSL clone of this branch:
  - package build: passed;
  - package typecheck: passed;
  - **139 tests passed, 0 failed**, including all independent-review and bot-review regressions;
  - the catastrophic-backtracking regression completes in about 101 ms, bounded by the worker deadline;
  - architecture boundary check: passed across 364 package source files.
- Windows package build/typecheck: passed.
- Root test-source typecheck (`tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`): passed.

## Summary

Make provider token accounting a diagnostic instead of a real-E2E pass criterion, and keep the usage shapes it depends on pinned by deterministic tests. Functional task/delivery/quality assertions are unchanged.

## Rebased onto `main` (2026-11-07, `b9e5367`)

The branch had been open since 2026-10-14 and was 699 commits behind; it conflicted in three files. After the rebase:

- **The protocol-aware parser is no longer part of this diff.** `normalizeUsage` moved to `packages/model/src/usage.ts` on `main` and already takes the request's dialect, reading `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens` for Chat Completions and `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` for Responses ahead of the aliases, with a conflict diagnostic. The reported bug - a probe returning `completion_tokens: 31` next to an extra `output_tokens: 0`, which the shared normalizer used to prefer - is already fixed there, so `packages/model/src/client.ts` is untouched by this PR.
- **One design choice from the original branch was not carried over.** The original parser dropped the fallback to the other dialect's fields and to `total_tokens` arithmetic entirely. `main`'s version keeps a dialect-first-then-fallback design and documents it; overriding that here would be a behaviour change on shared accounting that the maintainers already settled. The assertions that encoded the stricter rule were dropped with it rather than left failing.
- What is left is this PR's other half plus its regression coverage: the documented CI policy, the journey that stops gating on usage, and the mixed/missing-accounting cases exercised end to end.

## Changes

- `.ci/README.md` - provider usage is diagnostic evidence, not an E2E success or scoring gate; missing accounting is not evidence of zero cost; protocol parsing correctness stays enforced by deterministic tests.
- `test/journey-basic-real-api.spec.ts` - the usage step attaches the ledger instead of asserting `inputTokens`/`outputTokens` are positive, and reads the route directly so a route that cannot answer still fails the case.
- `packages/model/src/client.test.ts` - a chat completion whose usage carries conflicting aliases reports the dialect's counts (35/31/66), and a stream without usage still completes with `usage: undefined`.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts` - the gateway forwards the protocol's usage unchanged and serves the turn with none, in both streamed and non-streamed responses.

## Summary

Part of #835.

This is the independent tool-output trust-boundary slice from the staged landing plan. It introduces category-driven fencing for model-visible untrusted content while preserving raw stored evidence and observer behavior. It does not register Knowledge Engine tools or change kbScope, research state, finish-gate, or agent memory.

### Included

- Per-registry nonces and explicit `untrustedCategory` classification, with legacy-name and MCP-remote fallback behavior.
- Fencing for tool-domain, MCP, remote, and error payloads; only genuine framework-control messages bypass the boundary.
- Durable output sidecars preserving trust and neutralization metadata through line, character, and search readbacks. New records carry an explicit trust format version; pre-metadata records fail closed as untrusted legacy content, while authenticated fence metadata prevents planted fence-shaped tool text from changing durable status or evidence.
- Connector-controlled tool-search results are fenced and neutralized. Model-facing tool descriptions and schema `description`/`title`/`$comment` metadata receive the same protection without changing property identifiers, enum values, or the execution-time schema.
- A shared TypeScript/adapter/durable-store nonce, with native web and subagent history fenced at the actual model-request and dynamic-context rehydration boundaries. Existing fences are unwrapped during hydration only at a legacy anchored position or when framework metadata authenticates the category and nonce; missing trust wiring fails closed.
- Tool identity resolution through assistant `tool_call_id` mappings, including OpenAI tool messages without `name`; platform output is not double-fenced.
- Equivalent native-history handling for JiuwenSwarm housekeeping/default compression requests. Housekeeping selects a provider only when platform-call history proves one unique active run through its `_sd_run`; concurrent runs stay isolated, and finished, foreign, or ambiguous history fails closed instead of borrowing another run's model, credentials, or nonce.
- Framework truncation/readback/failure guidance kept outside untrusted fences, including explicit post-fence overflow notices and durable readback references.
- Final model-message fitting that enforces byte/line limits, truncates only the untrusted body, preserves complete markers, and fails closed when the trust envelope cannot fit.
- Authority-tag neutralization for remote-origin and subagent content, including custom categories and durable `runtime_context_data` wrappers; generic corpus content remains byte-exact except forged fence markers.
- Protected fence semantics and concise answer discipline in prompt `m8.5.1`.

Fixes #879

## What the user sees

The desktop attachment tray prints a file of `1_048_575` bytes (1 MiB − 1) as **`1024KB`**, and `1_073_741_823` bytes (1 GiB − 1) as **`1024MB`**; the upload limit line prints the same boundary as **`1024 MiB`**. The unit was chosen from the *unrounded* value (`1023.999 KB` stops the ladder at KB) while the printed number was `Math.round(value)`, which rounds to `1024` — a number no KB value can hold.

## Change

- New `apps/desktop/src/app/size-units.ts` with one promotion ladder shared by both formatters. It promotes while the value the caller would **print** still reaches the base, so the unit choice and the printed number cannot disagree.
- `formatFileSize` (`attachments.ts`) and `formatByteLimit` (`upload.ts`) keep their own rounding policy — one decimal below a hundred units / whole numbers above it for the card, integer-or-one-decimal for a limit — and only the unit selection changes.
- Existing readings are unchanged: `0KB`, `512B`, `1KB`, `5.5KB`, `16.5KB`, `256KB`, `1MB`, `5MB`, `999 B`, `1 KiB`, `1 GiB`.

Readings after the fix: `1_048_575 → 1MB`, `1_073_741_823 → 1GB`, limit `1_073_741_823 → 1 GiB`.

## Red first (`#879` on `89cd2d30`)

```
not ok 1 - an attachment one byte under 1 MiB prints 1MB, not 1024KB
  expected: '1MB'
  actual:   '1024KB'
not ok 2 - an attachment one byte under 1 GiB prints 1GB, not 1024MB
  expected: '1GB'
  actual:   '1024MB'
not ok 3 - an upload limit one byte under 1 GiB prints 1 GiB, not 1024 MiB
  expected: '1 GiB'
  actual:   '1024 MiB'
# tests 4
# pass 1
# fail 3
```

The passing test is the "sizes that already read well" guard.

## After the fix

```
# tests 11
# pass 11
# fail 0
```

## Gates (at tip `2d40ed35`, exact commands)

```
pnpm --recursive typecheck                          -> exit 0
tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json                          -> exit 0
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck    -> exit 0
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test        -> exit 0  (# tests 729 / # pass 729 / # fail 0)
CI_E2E_PREPARED=1 pnpm ci:l1                        -> exit 0  (PASS 4/4)
app-test probe (tsc over apps/desktop/tests, `types: ["vite/client","node"]`) -> exit 0
```

## Diff (vs `89cd2d30`)

```
 apps/desktop/src/app/attachments.ts        |  6 +− 9
 apps/desktop/src/app/size-units.ts         | 36 +− 0
 apps/desktop/src/app/upload.ts             |  6 +− 8
 apps/desktop/src/views/SetupWizard.tsx     | 18 +− 7
 apps/desktop/src/views/WorkspacePanel.tsx  | 12 +− 5
 apps/desktop/tests/size-boundary.test.ts   | 98 +− 0
 6 files changed, 176 insertions(+), 29 deletions(-)
```

## Review round (`1ef302b9` → `67ab0fcb`)

Two points from the review, and the extra surfaces it asked about:

1. **The two ladders are deliberately separate.** `apps/web/src/formatBytes.ts` and `apps/desktop/src/app/size-units.ts` are independent products of the same rule living in two applications that share no code; the desktop app does not import from `apps/web`. They are not meant to be merged, and a future change to the rule has to touch both on purpose.
2. **Other desktop surfaces that print a byte size.** Searching the desktop app found two more, and both had the same boundary bug, so they now share `scaledSize` instead of their own ladder:
   - `views/SetupWizard.tsx` — the free-space line on the setup screen printed `1024MB` one byte under a GiB (`formatWizardFreeSpace`, now `scaledSize` with the shell's KB/MB/GB convention and whole megabytes);
   - `views/WorkspacePanel.tsx` — workspace file rows printed `1024.0 KiB` (`formatWorkspaceSize`, now `scaledSize` with binary units and one decimal).
   Their readings are pinned in the same test file.

## Second review round (`67ab0fcb` → `2d40ed35`): the promotion band

The review found one more spot of the same class, one level down from the exact
unit: `formatWizardFreeSpace` picked the unit from the value at **one decimal**
(`Number(value.toFixed(1))`) while KB and MB are **printed** as whole numbers.
So the band just under a unit — where one decimal still reads `1023.x` and the
printed number rounds to `1024` — stayed in its level:

```
1_073_600_000 -> "1024MB"   (1023.86 MB; 1_073_217_536 … 1_073_689_395)
1_048_064     -> "1024KB"   (1023.5 KB;  1_048_064 … 1_048_524)
```

The existing cases did not catch it because `1_048_575` and `1_073_741_823` are
`1024.0` at one decimal, so they promoted for the wrong reason.

Fix: `scaledSize` now asks the caller for the number **that level** prints
(`round(value, unit)`), and the wizard's `printed` helper is the same function
that formats the output — whole KB and MB, one decimal GB. The unit can then
never disagree with the printed number at any level. `attachments.ts`,
`upload.ts` and `WorkspacePanel.tsx` pass one-argument formatters and are
unchanged by this, because for them print and promotion were already the same
function.

Red first at `67ab0fcb` (two new cases, same file):

```
not ok 9 - the wizard's free-space line promotes KB inside the band, where one decimal still reads 1023.5
  expected: '1MB'
  actual:   '1024KB'
not ok 10 - the wizard's free-space line promotes MB inside the band, where one decimal still reads 1023.8
  expected: '1.0GB'
  actual:   '1024MB'
# tests 11
# pass 9
# fail 2
```

Green at `2d40ed35`: `1_073_600_000 → 1.0GB`, `1_048_064 → 1MB`, and the
neighbours that already read `1023` keep it (`1_073_217_535 → 1023MB`,
`1_048_063 → 1023KB`). `11/11`.

## Screenshot re-check on this tip

The four images in the evidence comment (`6637901377`) were taken before this
round. This round changed `scaledSize`'s promotion rule and the wizard's
free-space line, not `formatFileSize` or `formatByteLimit`, so the same desktop
harness was re-run on `2d40ed35` to read the tray again rather than assume it:

```text
$ SHOT_DIR=$PWD/.local/shots PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=$HOME/.cache/ms-playwright \\
    apps/desktop/e2e/node_modules/.bin/playwright test \\
    --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts zz-880-verify.spec.ts --reporter=list
[zh-CN] tray readings: ["BIN 1MB","BIN 1GB"]
[zh-CN] attach tooltip: 放进本次会话的工作区，智能体就能读到。单个文件最大 1 GiB。也可以直接把文件拖进界面。
[en] tray readings: ["BIN 1MB","BIN 1GB"]
[en] attach tooltip: Files go into this session's workspace, where the agent can read them. A single file may be up to 1 GiB. You can also drag files onto the window.
  2 passed (4.5s)
```

The two files were chosen through the composer's own button, as the real
`1_048_575`-byte and `1_073_741_823`-byte files: the cards read `1MB` and `1GB`
in both languages, and the attach button's tooltip states the `1 GiB` limit
(`单个文件最大 1 GiB` / `A single file may be up to 1 GiB`). The readings are the
tip's own, so the four images stay as they are — no re-shoot.

## Two polish items left in this tip (recorded, not changed)

The review at `67ab0fcb` raised no blocking finding and two small ones. Both are
kept out of the tip deliberately — a new commit would only re-open a review that
already says it has nothing to block — and they are written down here so they do
not live only in a thread:

1. **A third copy of the unit table** (`apps/desktop/src/views/WorkspacePanel.tsx`,
   `WORKSPACE_SIZE_UNITS`). It is the same `B/KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB` list as
   `attachments.ts` and `upload.ts`, all three consumed by `scaledSize`, so the
   *unit choice* cannot fork; only the print step's spacing and letter case are
   local. Moving the table into `apps/desktop/src/app/size-units.ts` (as
   `export const SIZE_UNITS`) is the right cleanup, and it is the one change that
   would have to touch all four call sites at once — a follow-up rather than a
   patch on a reviewed tip.
2. **Imports at the bottom of `apps/desktop/tests/size-boundary.test.ts`.** The
   two new view imports sit below the first tests; ESM hoists them so the file
   runs (9/9), but a reader meets the dependency after the assertions.

Neither changes a rendered string, a unit, or a test result. If a tracked ticket
is wanted for the pair, say so on the thread and I will open one; the code they
describe ships with this pull request, so they are recorded here in the meantime.

## Scope note

`#867` fixed the same class in `apps/web` (`formatBytes` for the provenance modal and the CSV inspector). `apps/desktop` has its own ladders and shares no code with `apps/web`, so that fix cannot reach these two call sites.

Release category: `release:fix` (the account cannot add the label itself — no push rights on labels).

items.body:
Fixes #937

## What happens

`#932` classifies any message matching `/\bis too long\b/i` as client input, and the dispatch at
`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3938` answers a classified error `400` **with its text**. Two
executor messages contain the phrase mid-sentence and embed a filesystem path, so with `#932`'s
pattern they answered `400 {"error":"Runner bundle path is too long for tar: /…"}` instead of
`500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` — before `#932` both were 500 and the path stayed hidden.

## Change

One pattern, at `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:37`:

```diff
-/\bis too long\b/i,
+/\bis too long\.?\s*$/i,
```

Anchored at the end of the message, so only a message that *ends* with the phrase is client input.
Between the phrase and the end this allows exactly two things: an optional sentence period (`\.?`)
and trailing whitespace (`\s*`), which is what copy that ends with `is too long.`, `is too long\n` or
`is too long. \r\n` needs.

Why this shape and not something looser:

- **Not `\b…\b` (#932's unanchored form).** Any mid-sentence mention would classify, and the two
  executor faults (`packages/executor/src/runner-bundle.ts:76,80`,
  `packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts:777`) put the phrase in the middle of a sentence that
  carries an absolute path — the client would get `400` with that path in the body.
- **`\.?` plus `\s*$`, not `.*$`.** The only tolerated trailing characters are the sentence
  terminator and whitespace. `… is too long for tar: <path>` still has text after the phrase, so it
  stays a fault, and a path can never appear in the `400` body. The same holds for
  `… is too long for a Unix socket: <path>`.

Nothing else changes: no new code, no change to the limits, no change to a throw site.

## Tests

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.test.ts`:

- the eight legitimate length messages pinned **by name** (not by count), including
  `pip indexUrl is too long` (`packages/schema/src/environment.ts:393`), which the first draft of
  #937 missed;
- the two executor messages as **negative** assertions: they must not become client input. The
  runner-bundle fixture spells its path `/srv/ws_a/data/model.bin` — a neutral absolute path, not the
  CI builder's home. This test file ships inside the release payload, and
  `scripts/binary-release/build-payload.sh` (`assert_no_build_paths`) rejects any payload file carrying
  the builder's own `HOME`; the merge-queue run `42148873426` failed `Binary release (x86_64)` and
  `(aarch64)` on exactly that literal. The sentence shape the case pins (a length phrase followed
  mid-sentence by an absolute path) is unchanged;
- the existing negatives stay: `Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget` and
  `Database invariant failed` are still faults;
- three **shape** probes, one test each so a regression names the shape it dropped — trailing
  newline (`"The LLM API token is too long\n"`), trailing period (`"The LLM API token is too long."`)
  and period-plus-CRLF (`"The Neo4j password is too long. \r\n"`) — all expected `true`.

## Red first

Two red runs, in this order, both before the code they pin.

**1. The anchor itself.** With the product pattern reverted to `#932`'s unanchored `/\bis too long\b/i`
and the by-name test kept, the run before the anchor commit was:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts
not ok 2 - a length rejection ends with the phrase, so a path-bearing executor fault stays a fault
  error: |-
    Runner bundle path is too long for tar: /home/runner/work/ws_a/data/model.bin
    true !== false
# tests 2
# pass 1
# fail 1
```

**2. The terminator.** On the anchored tip `60e36dbe` (`/\bis too long$/i`), the three shape probes
were added with the product pattern untouched, and all three went red on `false !== true`:

```
not ok 3 - a length rejection survives a trailing newline
not ok 4 - a length rejection survives a trailing period
not ok 5 - a length rejection survives a trailing period and CRLF
# tests 5
# pass 2
# fail 3
```

After `\.?\s*$`: `# tests 5 / # pass 5 / # fail 0`. Per message, `#932` pattern → this tip (probe
importing both modules; the probe is not committed):

```
true  -> true   The LLM API token is too long
true  -> true   The proxy URL is too long
true  -> true   neo4jHttp is too long
true  -> true   neo4jUser is too long
true  -> true   The Neo4j password is too long
true  -> true   Model ID is too long
true  -> true   The stored runnerToken is too long
true  -> true   pip indexUrl is too long
true  -> false  Runner bundle path is too long for tar: /srv/ws_a/data/model.bin
true  -> false  The remote data directory path is too long for a Unix socket: /tmp/sc-remote/ws_a/.agent.sock
false -> false  Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget
false -> false  Database invariant failed
```

And the three shapes, previous tip `is too long$` → this tip `is too long\.?\s*$`:

```
false -> true   "The LLM API token is too long\n"
false -> true   "The LLM API token is too long."
false -> true   "The Neo4j password is too long. \r\n"
```

## Relation to #932

`#937` is the follow-up Security filed on `#932`, and `#932` must not be re-tipped for it. The shipped
change is therefore self-contained: this PR introduces the phrase with its own terminator handling
(`/\bis too long\.?\s*$/i`), so it does not depend on `#932` merging, and `#932`'s branch stays
untouched at `8b4c124c`. `#932`'s pattern is the input this PR narrows from, and the red run above
uses exactly that pattern, so the readings stay comparable. If `#932` lands first, this PR reduces on
rebase to the `\b` → `\.?\s*$` change on the line `#932` introduces, plus the test.

## Reads

Tip `08fc9b7694f03b746f1f332df9d66053aa6503f9` (tree `f37490d96a`), branch
`dev/937-bug-the-is-too-long-client-error-pattern`, base `main` `e4c206d1`. Diff vs `main`: 2 files,
+58/−0 (test +50, product +8).

Ran:

- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts` —
  `# tests 2 / # pass 1 / # fail 1` with `#932`'s pattern (first red); `# tests 5 / # pass 2 / # fail 3`
  with the shape probes against `is too long$` (second red); `# tests 5 / # pass 5 / # fail 0` at this
  tip.
- the payload path scan, applied to the file the binary-release job flagged, with the same
  boundary-anchored `grep -rIlE` shape and needles `build-payload.sh` uses: no match for
  `/home/runner`, `/home/xuke` or `/home/`; the only match is the fixture's neutral `/srv/…` path,
  which is not a needle.
- `cd services/api && npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0 (product; the package config
  excludes `*.test.ts` from the build).
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p .local/tsconfig.937.json --noEmit` — exit 0; a probe config extending
  `tsconfig.tests.json` with `types: ["node"]`, including only
  `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` and its test.
- `git diff --numstat upstream/main..HEAD` — `45 0` test, `8 0` product.
- `node --import tsx .local/probe-937.mts` — the per-message table above, `#932`'s module against this
  tip's module.
- `grep -rn "is too long" --include=*.ts packages services` — the eight legitimate throw sites all
  end with the phrase; the only mid-sentence ones are the two executor throws.
  `packages/model/src/client.ts:279-281` also lists `input is too long` / `prompt is too long`, but those
  are markers for `isModelInputTooLargeError`, a different classifier that additionally requires a
  400/413/422 status.

Not run:

- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (root) in this worktree: it fails on unrelated packages
  because `packages/feedback-worker` has no `node_modules/@sciencediscovery` link here
  (`TS2307 @sciencediscovery/operational-logging/feedback`); the probe config above type-checks the
  changed files with the same settings.
- `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / the E2E layers — CI runs them on this PR.
- A route-level HTTP probe on this head. The dispatch line is unchanged and the classifier is its
  only input; `#932` already carries route-level 400 readings for the same path.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` — two pathological executor failures keep the generic 500 instead of
echoing a filesystem path, while the eight length rejections and their punctuated/newline-terminated
variants still answer 400 with their message.

The label itself needs repository write access, which this fork does not have, so a maintainer has to
apply `release:fix`.

items.body:
Fixes #839

A delimited dataset preview derived one number, `Math.max(header.length, widest)`, and used it for two jobs: the grid width and the column count it reported. A two-column `.csv` with one 200,001-field line rendered 1,001 mostly-blank columns and announced `The file has 200001 columns; the preview shows the first 1001.` Both halves now come from the header: the column count *is* the header, and a wider line may add only a small, capped set of unnamed surplus columns.

## What was wrong

- **The count.** `clippedColumns.total` was `Math.max(header.length, widest)` — a data line's field count presented as the file's schema. The only sentence the reader gets was built from it, so a two-column file was described as a 200,001-column one, and the same outlier cells were named twice ("has N columns" and "M cells past the preview width").

- **The width.** `width = min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`, so one outlier line decided how wide the grid was. Taking the width from the *returned* rows instead would make the column set depend on the client's `maxRows` (the previous defect), so neither end of the file may own the width.

## What changed

`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `parseDelimitedTable` only:

- `totalColumns = header.length` — the header is the schema; a wide row is a row.
- `surplusLimit = Math.min(16, Math.max(2, header.length))` — the cap `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts` already uses (`surplusColumnLimit`). A wider line may contribute at most that many **unnamed** surplus columns; a header at or past sixteen keeps every named column (`surplusLimit` only ever adds).
- `width = Math.min(header.length + surplusShown, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`, where `surplusShown = min(widest - header.length, surplusLimit)` — `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS` stays the absolute payload limit.
- `clippedColumns = { shown: Math.min(header.length, width), total: header.length }` — `shown` is the number of named columns the preview shows, so it is consistent with the new width and never exceeds the header. The column sentence therefore fires only when the header itself is wider than the preview.
- Cells past the width still go to `clippedCells`; a header wider than the payload cap is still reported through `clippedColumns`, exactly as before.
- A line past the row window may still set the width — the column set must not depend on the caller's `maxRows` — and the returned rows are padded to it, as before. What changes is that the padding is no longer silent: `paddingOnlyColumns = surplusShown - shownSurplus` (the surplus only an unseen line justifies) and `paddingOnlyCells = paddingOnlyColumns * rows.length` produce `The preview pads N unnamed columns (M blank cells) because the file has a wider line past the first K rows, which is not shown.` `clippedCells` keeps counting only returned rows' cells past the width, and a returned outlier produces no padding sentence.

Measured on the fixtures (all asserted in `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts`):

| fixture | columns | clipped | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2-column header + one 200,001-field line inside the window | `4` | `clippedCells 199997` | issue fixture: was 1,001 columns |
| 2-column header, no outlier | `2` | `clippedCells 0` | a narrow table is not widened to the cap |
| 8-column header + one 100-field line | `16` | `clippedCells 84` | header + capped surplus |
| 20-column header + one 200,001-field line | `36` | `clippedCells 199965`, all 20 names in order | the cap never takes a named column |
| 200,001-column header | `1001` | `clippedColumns {shown: 1001, total: 200001}` | `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS` still the absolute limit |

## Red first — the column count

The new count test run against the unfixed `parseDelimitedTable`, with the two stale assertions in `dashboard.test.ts` already corrected (the tree a reviewer replays with the test commit):

```
not ok 62 - a delimited preview caps a pathological line and counts what it leaves out
  error: |-
    the column count comes from the header; the wide row is cells, not columns
    + actual - expected
      { shown: 1001, + total: 200001 - total: 2 }

not ok 63 - a wide line past the row window does not become the file's column count
  error: |-
    the file has as many columns as its header

    5000 !== 2

# tests 67
# pass 65
# fail 2
```

## Red first — the width

The width assertions run against the same unfixed source (the final tree of this PR's tests):

```
not ok 62 - a delimited preview caps a pathological line and counts what it leaves out
    1001 !== 4
not ok 63 - a wide line past the row window does not become the file's column count
    1001 !== 4
not ok 64 - the surplus cap never takes a named column and scales with the header
    1001 !== 36
not ok 66 - a delimited preview shows the same columns whatever maxRows it is asked for
    1001 !== 4

# tests 68
# pass 64
# fail 4
```

## Red first — padding from a line past the row window

`agent-ci-infra-bot`'s F1: a file whose only wide line falls past the row window still widens the grid, and the payload said nothing about it (`clippedCells 0`, `warnings []`). Pinned in `621c3dcf` before any source change; fixture `a,b` + 100 x `1,2` + one 5,000-field line, so the grid is 4 columns and the outlier is row 101:

```
not ok 63 - a wide line past the row window does not become the file's column count
  error: |-
    the padding of an out-of-window line needs a warning of its own: []

    0 !== 1

# tests 68
# pass 67
# fail 1
```

The same test now also carries the in-window control: an outlier the preview does return is still counted as 4,996 cells past the width (`clippedCells`), and it must not produce the padding sentence.

## Red first — the padding count under the column cap

`agent-ci-infra-bot`'s next finding: the sentence assumed the grid is `header + surplusShown`, but `width` is `Math.min(header + surplusShown, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`, so a wide header makes it claim unnamed columns the grid does not hold. Pinned in `921ec1d4` before any source change:

```
not ok 64 - the padding sentence counts the unnamed columns the capped grid really holds
  error: |-
    the capped grid has no unnamed column, so there is nothing to report as padding
    + [
    +   'The preview pads 15 unnamed columns (1500 blank cells) because the file has a wider line past the first 100 rows, which is not shown.'
    + ]
    - []

not ok 65 - the padding sentence names the row window it is talking about
  error: 'the sentence counts rows, singular: The preview pads 2 unnamed columns (2 blank cells) because the file has a wider line past the first 1 rows, which is not shown.'

# tests 70
# pass 68
# fail 2
```

The fix counts from the grid that was actually built (`renderedSurplus = max(0, width - totalColumns)`), so a 1,001-column header with a hidden 1,016-field line reports no padding at all, and a 1,000-column header reports exactly the one unnamed column the cap leaves room for.

## After the fix — readings

```
# tests 70
# pass 70
# fail 0
```

Payload readings on the F1 fixture (`a,b` + 100 x `1,2` + one 5,000-field line, so the only wide line is row 101 and is never returned): `columns.length 4`, `clippedColumns {shown: 2, total: 2}`, `clippedCells 0`, and one warning — `The preview pads 2 unnamed columns (200 blank cells) because the file has a wider line past the first 100 rows, which is not shown.` The in-window control in the same test returns that outlier instead: `clippedCells 4996`, no padding sentence.

Diffstat against `main` `f4dd1813`:

```
 services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts |  51 ++++++-
 services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts     | 258 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++--
 2 files changed, 293 insertions(+), 16 deletions(-)
```

Commits (test → fix, twice):

1. `2d8a9835` test: pin a delimited preview's column count to its header
2. `8a78ef4a` fix: take a delimited preview's column count from its header
3. `5575361e` test: cap the unnamed surplus, never the header's own columns
4. `4c4cd346` fix: cap only the unnamed surplus columns of a delimited preview
5. `c562503b` test: pin a narrow two-column table and a twenty-column header
6. `621c3dcf` test: pin that padding from a line past the row window is reported
7. `b807482b` fix: report the padding a line past the row window adds
8. `921ec1d4` test: pin that the padding sentence matches the capped grid
9. `913da859` fix: count the padding from the grid the cap actually builds

Ran:
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` — `# tests 70 # pass 70 # fail 0`; the same file against the unfixed source is the four red blocks above (`# pass 65`, `# pass 64`, `# pass 67`, `# pass 68`).
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.

Not run:
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` (the whole api suite) and the `ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e` layers were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser journey: the rendered `DatasetTable` shows the payload's `columns` / `warnings` verbatim, and those are what the assertions pin.

## Payload semantics

`clippedColumns` is part of the preview payload, so this changes what one of its fields counts — it is not only an extra sentence:

| field | before this PR | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clippedColumns.total` | `Math.max(header.length, widest)` — a data line's field count | `header.length` — the header is the schema |
| `clippedColumns.shown` | `Math.min(total, width)` | `Math.min(header.length, width)`, so `shown <= total` holds again |
| `columns.length` vs `clippedColumns.total` | equal | `columns.length` may exceed `total` by up to `surplusLimit` unnamed surplus columns |
| `clippedCells` | cells of returned rows past the width | unchanged |
| `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS` | 1,001 | unchanged |

A consumer that read `clippedColumns.total` as "the file's column count" now gets the header's count, which is the schema #839 asked for. The unnamed surplus is the `columns.length - clippedColumns.total` gap, and `warnings` names it when an unseen line is the reason. `apps/web`'s `DatasetTable` renders `columns`, `clippedColumns` and `clippedCells`; it does not render `warnings` today, so the new sentence reaches the API payload only. Showing it in the table (with a localized sentence) is a separate `apps/web` follow-up, not part of this PR.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: a delimited preview no longer renders hundreds of blank columns because of one outlier line, and no longer tells the reader a column count the header does not have. A header wider than the payload cap still gets its explicit clipped-column signal.

Compatibility and migration: none. The payload shape is unchanged; `clippedColumns.total` now counts header columns, `clippedColumns.shown` counts the named columns shown, and the grid width is bounded by header + capped surplus.
