items.body:
Fixes #875

## What changed

Both screens now read one decision from a new `apps/web/src/tokenCountFormat.ts`
(`compactTokenParts`): the tier, the rounding and the `".0"` trimming live
there, and each surface only spells the unit it already printed — the usage
page `K`, the model badge `k`. Before this, the badge rounded to whole millions
from 10M (`10_500_000 → "11M"`) while the usage page kept the fraction
(`"10.5M"`) for the same count.

Tiers, now shared:

- 1M and up: one decimal, dropped when it is `".0"` (`1_000_000 → "1M"`,
  `10_500_000 → "10.5M"`, `12_345_678 → "12.3M"`).
- 10K–1M: whole thousands (`200_000 → "200K"` / `"200k"`).
- 1K–10K: one decimal (`6_600 → "6.6K"` / `"6.6k"`).
- Below 1K: the plain count.
- The rounding decides the crossing: `999_999 → "1M"`, never `"1000K"`.

Measured before the change on base `89cd2d30` (badge / usage page):

```text
    999999  badge  1000k   usage 1000K
   1000000  badge     1M   usage 1.0M
   1500000  badge     2M   usage 1.5M
   9960000  badge    10M   usage 10.0M
  10500000  badge    11M   usage 10.5M
  12345678  badge    12M   usage 12.3M
```

Below one million the number is shared and only the unit glyph still differs,
as it already did on both screens; the test pins that difference (`"200k"` vs
`"200K"`) so a later "one spelling" refactor is a conscious change. Two readouts
move as a consequence of one rule: the badge prints one decimal in the 1K–10K
tier (`2_000 → "2.0k"`, no test pinned the old `"2k"`) and a whole million loses
`".0"` (`1_000_000 → "1M"` on the usage page, which is also the direction of
#864).

## Rebased onto `48848578`, after #864 merged

`#864` (`489dedd0`, "never round a token count into a unit it has not reached")
landed on `main` after this branch was last pushed, so the branch is rebased onto
`48848578` (two commits, no merge commit), and the one textual overlap,
`apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts`, keeps both rules:

- **#864's boundary rule is kept**: the `Math.round(value / 1_000) >= 1_000`
  crossing lives inside `compactTokenParts` now, so `999_999` still reads as a
  million (never `1000K`) and `999_499` still prints `999K`.
- **This pull request's rule is kept**: `formatCompactTokenValue` delegates to
  the shared ladder, so the usage page and the model badge cannot disagree.

One expectation moved with the rebase, and it is a spelling, not a boundary:
USG-031 pinned `1.0M` for a whole million, while the shared ladder drops a
trailing `.0` on both screens (the badge has always printed `1M`). Those three
constants now read `1M`; the crossing and the `999K` neighbour are unchanged.
Readings on the rebased tip:

```text
   999499  badge 999k  usage  999K   below the crossing
   999500  badge   1M  usage    1M   crossing (this is #864's boundary)
   999999  badge   1M  usage    1M   never "1000K"
  1000000  badge   1M  usage    1M
  9960000  badge  10M  usage   10M
 10500000  badge 10.5M usage 10.5M
```

## Red first

`apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts` on base `89cd2d30`:

```text
$ cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts
not ok 1 - USG-020 the usage page and the model badge agree from one million up
  error: |
    Expected values to be strictly equal:

    '11M' !== '10.5M'
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

The same test pins the neighbours that were red before the fix: `9_960_000`
(`"10M"` vs `"10.0M"`) and `1_500_000` (`"2M"` vs `"1.5M"`), plus
`1_000_000 → "1M"` on both screens.

## After

```text
# tests 1
# pass 1
# fail 0
```

## Gates, all on the pushed tip `824b604a5c44b0234f0330048959dc98b0100928` (rebased onto `48848578`)

Ran:

- `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → exit 0 (34 projects)
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → exit 0
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web typecheck` → exit 0
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` → `# tests 1222 / # pass 1222 / # fail 0`, exit 0 — both sides of the rebase run here: `UsagePage.test.tsx` USG-031 (the case #864 landed) and `tokenCountFormat.test.ts` USG-020
- `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1 pnpm ci:l1` → `{"status":"PASS","planned":4,"executed":4,"passed":4,"failed":0,"skipped":0}`, exit 0
- collector: `apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts` is byte-identical to `aca6fe7b` (blob `504ada22…`), so the collection evidence below still stands; re-ran it on the rebased tree → `{"status":"PASS","planned":1,"passed":1,"skipped":0}`
- app-test probe (`tsc` over `apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts`, extending `apps/web/tsconfig.json` with `types: ["vite/client","node"]`) → exit 0

Not run locally: the L2/ST profiles beyond L1 (CI runs them) and any browser/E2E
journey — this change is one formatter plus its two call sites.

## Review round: the new case was not in the shared plan

The case above was green locally but **not collected by the shared plan**, so a
green UT slice never ran it. `apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts` imported
`test` from `node:test`; the collector only takes files whose source contains
`category:<slice>`, and `audit-node.mjs` rejects a non-type `node:test` import
(`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs:228`, `audit-node.mjs:47`). Every other file in
`apps/web/tests` declares `createTest(import.meta.url, { tags: [...] })` — 125 of
127 — and this one did not.

Before, on `67cf5e01`:

```text
$ node test/support/tagged/cli.mjs list \
    --path apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts --os linux --arch amd64 --import tsx
NODE_COLLECTION_FAILED; inspect node-collect.log

$ cat node-collect.log
Error: DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts:16;
use static declarations and move runtime work into hooks
    at fail (test/support/tagged/audit-node.mjs:21:29)
```

After, the file declares the same tags as its peers and the plan carries it:

```text
$ node test/support/tagged/cli.mjs list \
    --path apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts --os linux --arch amd64 --import tsx
… "id": "apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts::USG-020%20the%20usage%20page%20and%20the%20model%20badge%20agree%20from%20one%20million%20up",
    "tags": ["arch:amd64","arch:arm64","category:ut","fixture:standard","isolation:none",
             "judge:none","model:none","npu:none","os:linux","sandbox:none",
             "status:reviewed","swarm:none","tier:l2"]

$ node test/support/tagged/cli.mjs run \
    --path apps/web/tests/tokenCountFormat.test.ts --os linux --arch amd64 --import tsx
{"status":"PASS","planned":1,"passed":1,"skipped":0}
```

The tag set is byte-for-byte the one a peer collected case gets
(`apps/web/tests/IdeaResearchLabels.test.ts`, compared with `cli.mjs list`). The
package-level `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` path still runs the
same file: `compat.mjs` returns the native `node:test` module when no shared run
has registered a plan.

## What happened to the earlier merge-order note

The merge-order note this body used to carry is settled by `main`: #864 is in
(`489dedd0`), and its reconciliation lives in this pull request instead of in a
later flip. The badge assertions already on `main`
(`apps/web/tests/ProviderModelList.test.tsx:44-46` pins `compactTokenCount(1_000_000) === "1M"`
and `1_048_576 → "1M"`) print exactly what the shared ladder prints, so no other
test file moves: the only expectations this pull request flips are the three
`1.0M` constants in `UsagePage.test.tsx` USG-031 described above.

## Badge readings that move because the tiers are shared

The badge no longer rounds to whole millions from 10M, which is the point of
this fix, and two visible readings follow from that one rule:

- `1_500` goes from `2k` to `1.5k`: the 1K–10K tier keeps one decimal, because
  that is the tier both screens now share. No test pinned the old `2k`.
- 10K–1M still prints the lowercase `k` on the badge (`200_000` → `200k`) while
  the usage page prints `K`; that glyph difference is pinned in the test, so a
  later "one spelling" refactor has to be a conscious change rather than a silent
  one.

Settings › Models shows each provider row's context window and max output as a compact badge (`1M / 131k`). `compactTokenCount` rounded to whole units, so a declared 1,500,000 window rendered `2M` (and 1,400,000 rendered `1M`), and `999,999` rendered `1000k` — a count that reads as a million but is not. Fixes #871

## What this fixes

`queuedCancelToast()` (`apps/web/src/run-stream/model.ts:130`) returned four hardcoded English titles and two hardcoded details, and `App.tsx:3802` pushed them verbatim. With the UI in Simplified Chinese the Runs panel said `取消排队中的运行` but the answer was `Queued run cancelled`; the "already started" branch even pointed the user at an English `Stop` button. The catalog carried the action key and the failure key (`error.cancelQueuedRun`) but no key for any of the four outcomes, so nothing could be reused.

The function now takes the translator (`queuedCancelToast(status, t)`), the six strings live in `app.queuedCancelOutcome.*` in both `en` and `zhCN`, and the call site passes `t`. `ComposerRunAction`'s three assertions compare catalog keys instead of English literals, so a localization sweep cannot pin a sentence back into the source.

## Red → green

  error: 'cancelled: the toast must be translated, not hardcoded'
not ok 2 - a Chinese reader gets the cancel outcome in Chinese, including the Stop reference
not ok 3 - the catalog carries the six outcome strings in both locales
not ok 4 - an unexpected status keeps the status it reports

```

Green after the fix (`7fc17fe8`): `tests/QueuedCancelToast.test.ts` + `tests/ComposerRunAction.test.tsx` → `17/17 pass`, and the whole web suite → `1219/1219 pass`.

The new file covers all four outcomes plus the fallback (translator is consulted for every string, all keys under `app.queuedCancelOutcome.*`), the real `zh-CN` render (`已取消…`, and the started detail names `停止`, never `Stop`), both locales carrying all six keys with different text, and the fallback keeping the status value.

Fixes #858

The usage page header announced **every model ever recorded** while the token total beside it and the model list below it were narrowed by the selected dates. With `from=to=2026-08-04`, where all usage that day came from one model, the page read `30 tokens across 2 models` — a count that contradicts both the sentence's own token total and the single-row list underneath. A range that keeps no usage was worse: the header paired `0 tokens across N models` with a body that already says the view is empty.

## What changed

- The subtitle counts `filteredModelGroups.length` — the same date-scoped, model-filtered collection the list below renders — instead of falling back to `summary.byModel.length` (all time) whenever only dates are selected.
- One model reads `… across 1 model` through a new `usage.subtitleOne` key, so the singular sentence stays grammatical; existing keys keep their meaning.
- A range that keeps no usage returns a dedicated `usage.subtitleFilteredEmpty` (`No usage in the selected range`) instead of a zero-token sentence plus a model count, which matches the body's existing `usage.filteredEmpty*` state rather than restating it.

## Validation

Red first, on `89cd2d30`:
- `apps/web/tests/UsagePage.test.tsx` — `# tests 4 / # pass 3 / # fail 1`; `not ok 2 - USG-012 usage page renders model drilldown, chart and inline/table usage` because the header rendered `30 tokens across 2 models` while one model has usage on 2026-08-04; the empty-range case also rendered `0 tokens across …`.
- After the fix: `# tests 4 / # pass 4 / # fail 0`.

Gates at tip `dd33ea3490db70b16bf160c966b13ae775801639`:
- `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → exit 0
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → exit 0
- `pnpm ci:l1` → exit 0, `{"status":"PASS","planned":4,"executed":4,"passed":4,"failed":0,"skipped":0}`. Run with `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1`: the L1 runner's own prepare step shells out to `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which cannot run on this host because its pnpm store is read-only (`EROFS`); the four L1 checks themselves ran.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` → exit 0, `# tests 1215 / # pass 1215 / # fail 0`
- ST: not applicable — no case in the frozen ST plan covers the usage page (51 entries, none for usage rendering); this change has no server path.

Diffstat against `89cd2d30`: 3 files `+40/−3` (`UsagePage.tsx +11/−3`, `messages.ts +4`, `UsagePage.test.tsx +25`).

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED: no browser journey was run against a materialised stack for this change. The web UT reproduces the header/body mismatch through the real `UsagePage` component using the page's own fixtures (two models, dates 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-04, `overview.totalTokens` 30 for the filtered day).

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: the usage-page header now names the same date-scoped models as the token total and the model list it summarizes, and says the selected range holds no usage instead of showing `0 tokens across N models`.
Compatibility and migration: none.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Fixes #867

## What the user sees

A workspace file of `1_048_575` bytes (1 MiB − 1) prints **`1024.0 KiB`** in the file-provenance modal, and `1_073_741_823` bytes print **`1024.0 MiB`**. The unit was picked from the *unrounded* value (`1023.999… KiB`, so the loop stopped at KiB) while the printed value came from `toFixed`, which rounded up to `1024.0` — a number no KiB value can hold. The CSV artifact inspector had the same boundary and additionally never left MiB, so `1_073_741_823` bytes always read `1024.0 MiB` there.

The size is the only quantitative evidence in a provenance record, so a value labelled with the wrong unit is the record itself being wrong.

## Change

- New `apps/web/src/formatBytes.ts` with one ladder (`KiB → MiB → GiB → TiB`) shared by both call sites. The unit is chosen from the **same rounded value that is printed**, so a size never prints at or above its unit's own base.
- The decimal policy is not changed: `"adaptive"` keeps `>= 10 ? 1 : 2` decimals (`1.50 KiB`, `12.3 MiB`), and the CSV inspector keeps its fixed one decimal.
- `WorkspaceFileProvenanceModal.tsx` drops its local `formatBytes` and uses the shared ladder.
- `csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts`'s exported `formatBytes` keeps its name and signature but delegates to the ladder with one decimal, and gains `GiB`/`TiB`.
- Bytes stay bytes (`1023 B`), an exact MiB stays `1.00 MiB` / `1.0 MiB`.

Readings after the fix: provenance `1_048_575 → 1.00 MiB`, `1_073_741_823 → 1.00 GiB`; CSV `1_048_575 → 1.0 MiB`, `1_073_741_823 → 1.0 GiB`, `1_099_511_627_775 → 1.0 TiB`.

## Red first (`#867` on `89cd2d30`)

```
not ok 1 - a provenance size one byte under 1 MiB never prints 1024.0 KiB
  error: '1024.0 KiB must not be printed: ...<dd>1024.0 KiB</dd>...'
not ok 2 - a provenance size one byte under 1 GiB never prints 1024.0 MiB
  error: '1024.0 MiB must not be printed: ...<dd>1024.0 MiB</dd>...'
not ok 4 - the CSV inspector size crosses the unit boundary it prints
  expected: '1.0 MiB'
  actual:   '1024.0 KiB'
# tests 5
# pass 2
# fail 3
```

The two passing tests are the "keeps the readings it already had" ones (`1023 B`, `1.00 MiB`, `1.50 KiB`, `5.50 MiB`, `1.5 KiB`, `5.5 MiB`), which pin the unchanged behaviour.

## After the fix

```
# tests 5
# pass 5
# fail 0
```

## Gates (at tip, exact commands)

```
pnpm --recursive typecheck                      -> exit 0
tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json                      -> exit 0
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test        -> exit 0  (# tests 1220 / # pass 1220 / # fail 0)
CI_E2E_PREPARED=1 pnpm ci:l1                    -> exit 0  (PASS 4/4)
```

## Diff (vs `89cd2d30`)

```
 apps/web/src/WorkspaceFileProvenanceModal.tsx |  13 +---
 apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts     |   8 +-
 apps/web/src/formatBytes.ts                   |  43 +++++++++++
 apps/web/tests/sizeBoundary.test.tsx          | 104 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 153 insertions(+), 15 deletions(-)
```

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Fixes #925

## What happens

Under zh-CN — the product default — the Session activity panel prints the two values it takes from
server data as raw API tokens:

- the status badge on every execution, transfer and reminder record renders `item.state` verbatim,
  so a running execution reads `running`;
- the execution meta line renders `item.provenance` verbatim (`工作区 ws_a · 溯源 pending`), and the
  record's accessible label (fold summary, focus label) reads `local · main · running`.

## Cause

`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` rendered `item.state` / `item.provenance` straight into the
tree, and `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` carried the 25 `activity.*` chrome keys but no keys for
those two value domains. Every other surface already translates them (`WakeNotice.tsx` maps wake
states through `chat.wakeNoticeState.*`, `GovernedDownloadCards.tsx` does the same for downloads);
this was the one activity surface left in English.

## Change

Product: two files, +51/−8.

- `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` — `activity.state.{queued,running,completed,failed,cancelled,unknown}`
  and `activity.provenance.{pending,committed}` (en: `Queued … Unknown`, `Pending`/`Committed`; zh:
  `排队中/运行中/已完成/失败/已取消/未知`, `待提交`/`已提交`), added beside `activity.resumeAgentScope`
  in both catalogues without reordering anything else.
- `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` — two module-scope key maps plus `stateLabel(state)` /
  `provenanceLabel(provenance)`, which fall back to the raw value for anything the catalogues do not
  carry. Used in the three badge children (executions, transfers, reminders), the three
  `ProcessRecord` labels and the `executionMeta` call.

Untouched by design: the `activity-badge ${item.state}` class (styling keys on it), `live` /
`cancellable`, the `progress.length` accounting, and every other badge in the app. A transfer's
`partial`, a reminder's `fired` and provenance `unconfirmed` are out of scope and keep their raw
token: the state fallback is asserted (`paused` keeps its token), while `unconfirmed` provenance
appears in the fixture and keeps its token by the same lookup, without a dedicated assertion.

Test: `apps/web/tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx`, +38 — one new case, no assertion migration in
the eight existing cases.

Two mocked journeys asserted the raw token as visible text and now assert the sentence a reader
gets (+6/−3, test-only): `test/issue-85-foreground-exec-inbox.spec.ts` asserts `已完成` and keeps
pinning the raw state through `.activity-badge`'s class, and
`test/journey-execution-management.spec.ts` (en locale) asserts `Cancelled` instead of `cancelled`.

## E2E

`L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)` was red on the previous tip — run
[42038472807](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42038472807), job
`127286193611`, step 9, 13:56:58Z→14:11:46Z:

```
{"status":"FAIL","planned":60,"executed":60,"passed":58,"failed":2}
```

Both failures are this PR's own translation showing up as visible text, not a flake:

- `test/issue-85-foreground-exec-inbox.spec.ts:274` — expected substring `completed`, received
  `"local · main · 已完成local · main已完成shell:7d80e380… 工作区 ws_2a95ce6e… · 溯源 已提交查看日志取消执行"`.
- `test/journey-execution-management.spec.ts:88` (and `:90`) — expected substring `cancelled`,
  received `"local · main · Cancelled"`.

`main` carries neither string change, so re-running the same shard would reproduce them. The
migration is the fix: the record's visible text is now the catalogue sentence, and the raw token
stays pinned where it still lives — the badge class (`activity-badge completed`, which
`workspace.css:252` styles on) — instead of being asserted as prose.


## Red-first

Command, from `apps/web`: `node --import tsx --test tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx`

Before the fix (test present, product untouched) — only the new case fails, and the tree shows the
raw token exactly as the issue reports it:

```
not ok 9 - a zh-CN badge names its state and provenance instead of printing the API token
  Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
  + actual - expected
    [
      'activity-badge running',
  +   'running'
  -   '运行中'
    ]
# tests 9
# pass 8
# fail 1
```

After the fix: `# tests 9 / # pass 9 / # fail 0`, and the same render no longer contains
`溯源 pending` (it reads `溯源 待提交`), while the class is still `activity-badge running`.

The new case also pins both boundaries: an unknown state keeps its raw token
(`activity-badge paused` → `paused`, asserted), and `unconfirmed` provenance is a fixture value with
no dedicated assertion — it keeps its token by the same lookup; the case also renders
the panel under `initialLocale="en"` to confirm the English wording is `Running` / `provenance
Pending` — the eight existing cases (English chrome: `View logs`, `Cancel execution`, `Resume …`)
stay green, so no assertion migrated.

## Reads

Tip `0da863eab78172f50d7f4426cadc90c6d4c18067`, rebased onto `main` `70b66fa4a5e0` (the base moved
by the feedback PR plus the `#915`/`#892` merges), 5 files, +95/−11.

Ran:

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` — `# tests 1243 / # pass 1243 / # fail 0`

  build artifact the rebased `main` now imports).
- `node --import tsx --test tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx` — before the fix `9 / 8 pass / 1 fail`,
  after `9 / 9 / 0`.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` (in `apps/web`) — exit 0.
- A scratch render probe (written, run, deleted — not part of this diff) over `AgentActivityPanel`

  `activity-badge completed` + `已完成` and the record label `local · main · 已完成`; en cancelled
  renders `local · main · Cancelled` and `Inspect training output · Cancelled` — 2/2 pass. That is
  the component-level equivalent of the two migrated assertions.

Not run:

- The mocked E2E shard locally. Three attempts, all blocked by this box's network, not by the diff:
  the isolated stack's `uv sync` for the JiuwenSwarm venv stalls on `pypi.org`, and the stack's
  `paper` env needs ~24 MB of wheels (pygments/pypdfium2/cryptography/pillow/pdfminer-six/reportlab)
  that did not finish inside the health window even raised to `CI_E2E_STACK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1200`
  (readings: `BLOCKED: isolated E2E stack did not become healthy`, `planned 60, executed 0`). CI's
  `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)` on this tip is the authoritative read.
- `pnpm ci:l1` — its prepare step runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which cannot write the local

items.body:
Fixes #942

## What happens

In the feedback dialog one multi-select of 10 screenshots attaches 8 (the cap in
`packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts:40`) and says nothing at all: no error, no hint, no count.
`prepareFeedbackImages` left the loop silently, `result.error` stayed `undefined`, so the
`feedback-inline-error` line in `FeedbackDialog.tsx` rendered nothing. The two dropped files were lost
without a word, and the user submitted believing all 10 were attached.

The function's own comment promised the opposite ("stops at the first failure so the dialog can show
the reason instead of silently dropping the rest"): it stopped on failure, but the cap — the far more
common path — dropped the remainder silently.

## Change

Three files, and `apps/web` only.

1. `apps/web/src/feedback-images.ts` — `prepareFeedbackImages` now returns `skipped: number` next to
   `images` (and `error`, unchanged). A pick that does not fit the cap is counted instead of dropped:
   the loop turns the old `break` into a `continue` that counts, so every file still costs no decode.
   This is purely additive: `images` and `error` keep exactly the semantics they had, and an image
   that fails type/decode/size still returns early with its error.
2. `apps/web/src/FeedbackDialog.tsx` — the dialog holds `skippedImages` next to `images` and renders
   one neutral hint (`feedback-hint`, `role="status"`) naming the cap and the count:
   `Only the first 8 screenshots were attached; 2 skipped.` It is **not** the `imageError` slot: that
   slot is keyed by `ImagePrepareError` and describes an image that failed, while this one explains a
   partially successful pick. The count is cleared when the dialog reopens, after a successful
   submit, and when a thumbnail is removed — it always describes the newest pick.
3. `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` — `feedback.images.truncated` in both locales.

The English copy is number-neutral on purpose. The issue's suggested wording
(`…; {skipped} were skipped`) is `1 were skipped` at `skipped: 1`, so this PR uses the number-neutral
`{skipped} skipped` instead: `Only the first {max} screenshots were attached; {skipped} skipped.` reads
correctly for every count, and the Chinese wording (`只附加了前 {max} 张截图，另有 {skipped} 张被跳过。`)
already was.

## Tests

New `apps/web/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` (6 tests). The four acceptance directions, all driven
through a mounted `FeedbackDialog` and its real hidden file input, with only the browser pieces
(`createImageBitmap`, canvas `toBlob`, `FileReader`) stubbed:

1. **at the cap** — pick 10: 8 thumbnails, notice
   `Only the first 8 screenshots were attached; 2 skipped.`
2. **under the cap** — pick 2: 2 thumbnails, no notice at all;
3. **remove then pick** — pick 10 (8 attached), remove one (7 left), pick 2: 8 thumbnails and the
   notice says `1 skipped` — the count describes the newest pick, not the previous one;
4. **both locales** — the zh-CN dialog renders `只附加了前 8 张截图，另有 2 张被跳过。`

Two unit tests keep the pure return value pinned: `skipped === 2` for 10 picks at the cap and
`skipped === 0` for 2 picks under it.

Not covered (coverage boundary, not defects — the code paths exist and behave as written, no test drives
them; follow-up tests are tracked separately, not in this PR): the notice disappears immediately when a
thumbnail is removed (`FeedbackDialog.tsx:323`); an image failure and the truncation notice can render
together when one pick both drops images at the cap and fails one (`:484`/`:488`); reopening the dialog
and a successful submit each reset the count (`:163`/`:288`); and picking once more while already at 8
yields `0 added, 1 skipped`.

## Red first

**1. The missing signal.** Test first, product code untouched, on base `9871f2dd`:

```
$ cd apps/web && ./node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx
not ok 1 - ten picks at the eight-image cap report the two that were skipped
    undefined !== 2
not ok 2 - two picks under the cap report nothing skipped
    undefined !== 0
# tests 2
# pass 0
# fail 2
```

`images.length` was already 8 and 2, so the failing half is exactly the absence of a truncation
signal.

**2. The missing notice.** With the `FeedbackDialog.tsx` change reverted and `skipped` still returned,
the dialog tests fail where the user-visible behaviour is missing:

```
ok 1 - ten picks at the eight-image cap report the two that were skipped
ok 2 - two picks under the cap report nothing skipped
not ok 3 - the dialog names the cap and the dropped count after an over-cap pick
ok 4 - the dialog says nothing extra while every pick fits
not ok 5 - removing a thumbnail frees a slot for exactly one more pick
not ok 6 - the Chinese dialog carries the same notice with its own wording and numbers
# tests 6
# pass 3
# fail 3
```

Test 4 passing there is the point of the test: nothing extra may appear while everything fits.

After both halves: `# tests 6 / # pass 6 / # fail 0`.

## Reads

Tip `8ebaedfabf447a0c23770899f8a87133029c7b7f` (tree `2ce76c1f7a`), branch
`dev1/fix/942-feedback-image-truncation`, base `main` `9871f2dd`. Diff vs `main`: 4 files, +278/−5
(`feedback-images.ts` +11/−5, `FeedbackDialog.tsx` +14, `messages.ts` +2, new test +251).

Ran:

- `cd apps/web && ./node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` —
  `# tests 2 / # pass 0 / # fail 2` red first, `# tests 6 / # pass 6 / # fail 0` at the tip.
- `cd apps/web && ./node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` (the package's own
  `test` script) — `# tests 1250 / # pass 1250 / # fail 0`.
- `cd apps/web && ./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- Rendered-state check: the dialog tests assert the thumbnails, the notice text and its absence
  through `react-test-renderer` on the real component; the hint uses the existing neutral
  `feedback-hint` style and `role="status"`, so it is announced but not styled as an error.

Not run:

- `./.local/typecheck-app-tests.sh apps/web/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` — the probe reports the same
  pre-existing noise every `react-test-renderer` test in this repo produces (`TS2591` for
  `node:assert/strict` without `types: ["node"]`, `TS7016` with no `@types/react-test-renderer`), and
  no gate type-checks `apps/web/tests` (`apps/web/tsconfig.json` includes only `src/**` and
  `vite.config.ts`). Verified by running the same probe on `apps/web/tests/ComputeReadiness.test.tsx`
  and `apps/web/tests/ConfigurationRequestCard.test.tsx` on the base tree: they fail the same way.
- A browser-level E2E journey for the feedback dialog — none exists in the repo for this dialog, and
  the component test above drives the real handler.
- `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / the E2E layers — CI runs them on this PR.

## Scope

`apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts:116` carries a copy of this function with the same
silent cap drop, and its own dialog has the same gap. This change is the `apps/web` face only; the
desktop copy is left untouched and needs the same fix, tracked separately.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` — the feedback dialog now names the eight-image cap and the number of
screenshots it dropped instead of losing them silently.

The label itself needs repository write access, which this fork does not have, so a maintainer has to
apply `release:fix`.

## Summary
- Session header 「用量」 chip (`.session-usage-chip`) had a warped / kinked top border.
- Cause: `.session-bar .session-usage-chip` in `conversation.css` used `min-height: 28px` and `padding: 3px 9px` against an 8px radius + `line-height: 1` base chip (present since first commit, not a recent regression).
- Fix: drop the overly tight `min-height` / `padding` overrides; keep only the flex width constraints so the chip can breathe.
- Height tradeoff (F1/F2): default inherits shell `min-height: 38px` / `padding: 7px 10px` to stop the kink; `@media (max-height: 900px)` only sets `min-height: 32px` and keeps shell padding (7px) — no `4px` pad. That floor mainly affects the empty-usage chip; with a breakdown row content height already exceeds 32px (F3).

## 中文
会话栏「用量」卡片顶边扭曲：`conversation.css` 里 bar 内覆盖的 padding/min-height 过紧，与基样式圆角冲突。去掉过紧约束，只保留宽度相关 flex。
高度取舍：默认用 shell 的 38/7 消 kink；短视口（max-height 900px）只压 `min-height: 32px`，padding 继续用 shell 7px，不回到 3px/4px。有用量 breakdown 时内容高度已超过 32，该 band 主要作用于「尚无用量上报」空态。

## Validation
- Visual: session-bar usage chip top edge smooth; text not flush to top.
- Multi-size real UI (tip `e82ee51c`, empty usage 「用量 / —」): 1280×1000 (>900, ~38px); 1280×800 / 1366×768 / 900×800 (≤900, min-height 32); 600×800 narrow (chip squeezes to a thin bar). No two-row breakdown in this session.
- Diff limited to `apps/web` conversation.css session-usage-chip override + short-viewport height-only rule.

items.body:
Fixes #883

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What changed

`_NODE_LIMIT` is a hard cap of 500 nodes, and the contract at `query.py:319` says only results **beyond** it carry `truncated: True`. The flag was computed *after* a Cypher `LIMIT` bound to exactly the cap, so the Python side could never observe a 501st row: a complete 500-row answer and a cut one were indistinguishable and both reported `truncated: true`. The panel then drew `N of 500+ (truncated) match(es) in view` — the `+` asserting a further match that does not exist — and a session graph of exactly 500 nodes was badged as partial.

`query.py` now has one helper, `_cap_page(rows)`, returning the kept page and `len(rows) > _NODE_LIMIT` as the flag. Two shapes use it:

- **Cypher-driven reads** — `query_match` (`:431`), `by_node_type` (`:465`), `by_edge_type` (`:518`), `get_subgraph` (`:272`) and `_serialize_subgraph` (`:1298`): the Cypher limit is bound to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`, the page is cut to `_NODE_LIMIT` and the extra row alone decides the flag. `query_match`/`by_node_type` count the **raw rows** before `_to_hit`, the variant the issue prefers: a row dropped because its label has no id field is not a truncation. In `get_subgraph` the node-id set used to filter edges and synthesize the folded scope→product surrogates is built from the kept page, so no rendered edge points at a node the caller did not receive.
- **Assembled reads** — `get_scope_expansion` (`:898`) and `get_group_expansion` (`:1024`): these build their node set from several queries (children + produces subtree + edge endpoints; group members + one surrogate edge each) and have **no Cypher `LIMIT`** to raise, so `cap + 1` does not apply to them. The cap is applied to the assembled page instead, and an edge whose endpoint fell outside the page is dropped rather than rendered against an absent node. `get_group_expansion` and `_serialize_subgraph` were not in the issue's list of five: they carry the identical predicate (`len(...) >= _NODE_LIMIT` over a set that had not been cut at all — flagging a page they never truncated), so they are fixed in the same slice rather than left as the same defect on two more surfaces.

`total` keeps its previous meaning (the number of rows the response carries), so no client contract changes; `services/api` and the web panel forward the flag verbatim and need no edit.

## Red first

Test commit `9ce6d309` (test only), base `89cd2d30`:

```
$ cd services/memory-graph && uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q
14 failed in 0.50s
```

Three distinct failure shapes prove the tests reach the real paths:

- `assert True is False` — a complete 500-row answer reported as truncated (the reported defect, once per capped reader);
- `assert 500 == (500 + 1)` — the reader bound `$limit` to the cap itself, so the flag cannot be decided at all;
- `assert 501 == 500` — the two assembled readers returned all 501 nodes: the page had not been cut even though it was flagged.

Green at `e1957043`: the same command gives `14 passed in 0.15s`.

## Validation

The branch is rebased onto the current main tip `89cd2d30` (it was first based on a mirror that still served `8708320f`); `services/memory-graph` has no upstream drift between the two, and every reading below was taken again at the rebased commits.

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| new cap cases | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed` (7 readers × exactly-500 / 501) |
| memory-graph suite, tip | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ -q` | `123 passed, 15 warnings, 78 errors` |
| memory-graph suite, same tree without the new file (baseline) | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `109 passed, 14 warnings, 78 errors` |
| error set | `diff` of the `ERROR tests/...` lines of the two runs | identical (78 lines) |

The 78 errors are the pre-existing `@needs_neo4j` suite on this host — every one fails in setup with `Failed: needs a live Neo4j`, and the set is node-for-node the same with and without this diff (`187` collected before, `201` after the 14 new cases).

The cases assert more than the flag: for each reader a 501-row result must return exactly 500 rows; the assembled readers must drop the spine edge that points into the cut row; `_serialize_subgraph` and the four Cypher readers must bind `$limit` to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`.

Not run: anything needing a live Neo4j (the Cypher and the rendered panel text itself), because there is no graph on this host and `ci.yml` has no memory-graph job — the issue notes this, so the local pytest output above is the acceptance evidence. The TypeScript gates (`pnpm --recursive typecheck`, `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`) are not run: the diff touches no TypeScript.

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…e1dee252`: 3 files, `+656/−19` (`query.py` `+93/−19`, `tests/test_node_limit.py` `+320`, `tests/test_node_limit_rule.py` `+243`). No existing assertion is relaxed.

## Review fix (`CHANGES_REQUESTED` on `e1957043`, review `5773456818`)

`yuanzhou75` found that the new test file stopped the whole `UT` layer before a single case ran: the tagged audit (`test/support/tagged/python/science_tags.py:103-108`) accepts only `pytest.mark.parametrize` arguments that pass `ast.literal_eval`, and `CAP` / `CAP + 1` are a `Name` and a `BinOp`. Because the audit runs in `pytest_collect_file`, collection aborted with `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: .../test_node_limit.py:107` and `merge-gate` never evaluated. Fixed at `04ce9c89`, in the shape the review asked for:

- **All seven** parameter tables (lines 105/123/155/181/227/266/290) are now `[(500, False), (501, True)]` with their existing ids, and each case opens with `assert query._NODE_LIMIT == 500  # the table above is literal on purpose`. `CAP` stays and is still used by the body assertions, including the one requiring `$limit == CAP + 1`.
- One more registration defect the audit then exposed: the module carried **no** `science_tags` module mark, so once the audit passed the catalog step raised `ValueError: Missing tag group: category` — the same `PYTHON_COLLECTION_FAILED` for the layer, one step later. It now has the line every sibling in this suite has: `pytestmark = pytest.mark.science_tags(category='ut', os='linux', arch=('amd64', 'arm64'))`.

Verified at `04ce9c89` with the harness's own code, not a stand-in for it:

```
$ cd services/memory-graph && python3 -c "import sys; sys.path[:0]=['../../test/support/tagged/python']; import science_tags, pathlib; science_tags.audit_source(pathlib.Path('tests/test_node_limit.py'))"
(no output) exit 0        # before: ValueError: DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: tests/test_node_limit.py:107
```

```
$ PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 PYTHONPATH=<repo>/test/support/tagged/python \
  uv run --project services/memory-graph --extra test python -m pytest -p science_tags \
  --strict-markers --rootdir <repo> --collect-only -q \
  --science-root=<repo> --science-catalog=<file> $(ls services/memory-graph/tests/test_*.py)
201 tests collected in 0.99s     # exit 0
```

That is the command `coordinator.mjs`'s `collect()` runs — same `-p science_tags`, `--strict-markers`, `--rootdir`, `--science-catalog`, plugin autoload off — over every source `pythonSources('memory-graph')` globs. The catalog it wrote has 201 entries, 14 of them from this file, tagged `category:ut, os:linux, arch:amd64, arch:arm64, tier:l2, status:reviewed, ...`. Before the change the same command died at `:107`; with only the tables fixed it died again at the missing `category`.

| gate | command | reading at `04ce9c89` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tag audit | `science_tags.audit_source(tests/test_node_limit.py)` | exit 0 |
| tagged collection, whole project | `pytest -p science_tags --collect-only` over `services/memory-graph/tests/test_*.py` | `201 tests collected`, exit 0, 201 catalog entries |
| new cap cases | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed, 1 warning` |
| memory-graph suite | `uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ -q` | `129 passed, 16 warnings, 78 errors` |

The one warning the module adds is `PytestUnknownMarkWarning: Unknown pytest.mark.science_tags`, which every sibling module in this suite emits when pytest runs without the tagged plugin (`tests/test_logging_config.py` on its own gives `1 passed, 1 warning`); the plugin registers the marker and the collection above passes `--strict-markers`. The 78 errors are the unchanged `@needs_neo4j` setup failures.

No other file changed; the five commits stay separate: `9ce6d309` red test, `e1957043` fix, `04ce9c89` this registration fix, `86bbd1a5` the rule cases below, `e1dee252` the rule fix.

### Second review: one meaning for `truncated` (thread `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM6zusPi`)

The review found three counting conventions for one flag in the same PR. I took the first of its two options and made it the only one: **`truncated` means the backend returned more rows than `_NODE_LIMIT`, counted on the rows that were read and *before* a row is dropped for having no identity.**

Why this rule and not "count only renderable hits":

- **Only the returned-row count can be decided.** Each Cypher read binds `LIMIT` to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`, and that one extra row is the whole probe. Filtering first spends the probe on a row that cannot be rendered: 500 readable hits plus an unrenderable 501st would look *complete* although a renderable 502nd may exist, which is a completeness claim nothing checked. The returned-row count claims only what the extra row proves — the answer went past the cap.
- **It is the question the panel text asks.** `N of 500+ (truncated)` says the graph holds more matches than are shown. True when 501 rows came back even if one cannot be drawn; false when 501 came back and the response says "complete".
- **A short page stays complete.** 500 rows with one unrenderable row → 499 rendered, `truncated: false`: nothing was left unread, so there is nothing to disclose. Both directions are pinned below.

What changed:

- `get_subgraph` now caps the returned `(label, node)` rows and then runs `_node_identity`; `_serialize_subgraph` caps the returned rows and then runs `_to_hit`. Those are the two readers that capped the *filtered* list.
- `query_match`, `by_node_type`, `by_edge_type` already capped the returned rows; `query_match`'s comment argued the opposite and now states the rule, and the other two carry the same sentence.
- `get_scope_expansion` and `get_group_expansion` cap the assembled page, where every element already has an identity by construction, so "rows read" and "renderable rows" coincide there — no behaviour change, and the comment says so.
- `_cap_page`'s docstring states the rule once, and why the filter has to run after the cut. The review's nit (`nodes = list(hit_rows)` and a rebind on the next line) disappears with the restructure: `nodes` is built directly from the kept rows.

`tests/test_node_limit_rule.py` (new, 6 cases) pins the rule rather than the arithmetic: an unrenderable row as the 501st sets the flag on `query_match`, `by_edge_type`, `get_subgraph` and `_serialize_subgraph`, and a complete 500-row page that holds one unrenderable row stays complete on `query_match` and `get_subgraph`. Two of the six fail on `86bbd1a5` — `assert False is True` on the two readers that filtered first — and pass on `e1dee252`; the four that already held are there so a future reader cannot silently move one side into the other's shape again.

Deferred, deliberately not in this PR: `get_scope_expansion` / `get_group_expansion` still read every child/member and cut in Python, so the cap bounds the response and not the query work — same as before this PR, noted for follow-up.

Readings at `e1dee252`:

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rule cases | `pytest tests/test_node_limit_rule.py -q` | `6 passed` |
| cap cases | `pytest tests/test_node_limit.py -q` | `14 passed` |
| whole suite | `pytest tests/ -q` | `129 passed, 16 warnings, 78 errors` (the 78 unchanged) |
| tag audit, both files | `science_tags.audit_source(...)` | exit 0 each |

Fixes #673

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts` capped an extracted page with a bare `text.slice(0, MAX_DOCUMENT_CHARS)` (4096 UTF-16 units), so a character that straddles the cut left a lone high surrogate at the end of the body handed to the model.

Reproduction (`main` before the fix, logic copied verbatim):

```
$ node -e 'const MAX=4096; const text="x".repeat(MAX-1)+"😀"; console.log(JSON.stringify(text.slice(0,MAX).slice(-2)))'
"\ud83d"
```

Red commit `c6765ab2d6fea7fb2f9ba7e6bfb4cd8eb5b6d6b0` on this branch, before the fix:

```
not ok 13 - document truncation never ends in half a surrogate pair
  ---
  failureType: 'testCodeFailure'
  error: 'Expected values to be strictly equal: ... actual ends in \ud83d'
```

## What changed

- `document()` in `fetch.ts` now drops a dangling high surrogate after the cut, so the result ends on a code point, never exceeds the 4096-unit budget, and creates no new lone surrogate. The same rule the artifact preview uses.
- New test `document truncation never ends in half a surrogate pair` covers both `renderTavilyExtract` and `renderExaContents` with an emoji straddling the boundary, plus a lone-surrogate check on the rendered document.
- Nothing else changes: same cap, same `# title\n\n` prefix, same vendor normalizers.

## Verified locally

Red commit `c6765ab2d6fea7fb2f9ba7e6bfb4cd8eb5b6d6b0` (test only, on top of `7057aaf6`):

```
# tests 16

not ok 13 - document truncation never ends in half a surrogate pair

ok 71 - document truncation never ends in half a surrogate pair

exit=0
```

Ran: the whole `@sciencediscovery/data-source` test suite (74/74 pass, `providers.test.ts` is 16 of them, the new case runs as `ok 71`) and its `tsc --noEmit` typecheck, both exit 0.

Fixes #877

## What this fixes

Four routes in the same family read one artifact id. `content` (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3353`) asks `store.getArtifactVersion()` first and answers 404; `provenance` and `diff` called `artifactVersionProvenance()` / `artifactVersionDiff()`, which throw a bare `new Error("Artifact version not found")` (`services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:169` and `:349`). The top-level mapper only turns `Project|Session|Proxy server|Provider|Model not found`, `Execution|Transfer|Timer|Subagent not found: …` and a few codes into 404, so both fell through to the 500 branch — and wrote an `unclassified_request_error` log for what is simply a stale version id.

Now both routes check the version before calling the helper, exactly like `content`, and answer `404 {"error":"Artifact version not found"}`.

The same defect exists one level up, on both versions *list* routes: `/api/projects/:p/artifacts/:a/versions` and its Session-scoped sibling pass the id straight to `store.listProjectArtifactVersions()`, which throws a bare `Error("Artifact not found")` — again a 500 plus an `unclassified_request_error`. Both now check the project/Session and the artifact first and answer `404` naming what is missing (`Project not found: …` / `Artifact not found`); the success path is untouched.

`diff` keeps its two comparison-base cases apart, per the issue's expected shape:

- `?against=<id>` given but not found → **404** (a requested resource is missing);
- `?against` absent and the previous version does not exist → **400** `A previous artifact version is unavailable for comparison` (the request asks for a diff this artifact cannot have yet, which is a client-side input problem, not a missing `to` version).

The helpers are unchanged, so their defensive throws still hold for any caller that skips the route.

## Red → green

Red first (`6864420d`, test only), `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-missing.test.ts`:

```
content:    { status: 404, error: 'Artifact version not found' }
provenance: { status: 500, error: 'Internal server error' }
diff:       { status: 500, error: 'Internal server error' }
projects/:p/artifacts/:a/versions: { status: 500, error: 'Internal server error' }
# tests 1 / # pass 0 / # fail 1
```

Green after the fixes (`f67b91e9` for the version routes, `3c21ad91` for the list routes): same command → `1/1 pass`; `provenance.test.ts` + `dashboard.test.ts` → `86/86 pass`.

The test drives a real `createApiServer` (`offlineMcpTransport`, no runner) against a freshly created project/session, then asks all three version routes for the same random version id and compares status **and** error body, so a future 500 with a different message cannot pass quietly. It then asks the project-scoped list route for a random artifact id, the Session-scoped one, and a route with a random project id, each expecting 404.

## Ran / Not run

Ran (exit codes verbatim):

1. `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → **0**
2. `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → **0**
3. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-missing.test.ts` → **0** (`1/1`)
4. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/provenance.test.ts src/dashboard.test.ts` → **0** (`86/86`)
5. `pnpm architecture:check` (no lint script in this repo) → **1**, one failure `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`: sandbox `uv` cannot create a temp file (`Read-only file system (os error 30)`), unrelated to this diff.

Not run: the `?against=` 404 and the missing-previous 400 branches have no version fixture in this harness (creating an artifact version needs an execution), so the test pins the sibling-404 case the issue measured; the two `diff` branches are covered by the code path and stated above. The ST/E2E layer runs in CI.

## Diffstat

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…HEAD`:

```
 services/api/src/artifact-version-missing.test.ts | 78 +++++++++++++++++++++++
 services/api/src/http/index.ts                    | 41 +++++++++++--
 2 files changed, 112 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)
```


## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: asking for the provenance, the diff, or the version list of an artifact or artifact version that does not exist (an expired link, a version removed by retention, a diff pointing at a deleted version) now answers `404` with the reason instead of `500 Internal server error`; the artifact dialog can say the version is gone instead of failing, and the server no longer logs a false `unclassified_request_error`.
Compatibility and migration: none — existing `200` responses and the sibling `content` route's `404` are unchanged.

items.body:
Fixes #862

## What this fixes

`SessionStore.writeArray()` published state through a `.state-<pid>-<uuid>.tmp` file and ran its cleanup in `finally` without a guard:

```ts
} finally {
  await rm(temporaryPath, { force: true });
}
```

When `rename` was refused (on Windows an antivirus scanner, search indexer or backup agent holds the freshly written file, so `MoveFileEx` returns `EPERM`) and the `rm` was refused for the same reason, the `finally` threw the bare cleanup `EPERM` and **replaced** the error that explains the loss. The caller then saw an unclassified `EPERM` on a `.tmp` path instead of the classified replace failure, so nothing could tell a locked file apart from a full disk.

The fix swallows the cleanup failure (`.catch(() => undefined)`); the replace error is the one that says what was lost.

## Red → green

| | |
|---|---|
| **Red** `88e6aa07` | `node --import tsx --test src/store-replace-cleanup.test.ts` → `2 tests / 1 pass / 1 fail`; failing assertion `the cleanup failure must not replace the replace error` (the surfaced error is the mocked `rm` EPERM, the `rename` EPERM is gone) |
| **Green** `0bae8739` | same command → `2 tests / 2 pass / 0 fail` |
| **Review round** `09b4ccb7` | adds the `attempts === 20` / `cause.code` assertions (inert before #857, live after) — same command → `2/2` |

The Security review's anti-forgery assertions are in `09b4ccb7`: when the surfaced error is a `FileReplaceError` (the classified shape #857 introduces on `main`), the test pins `attempts === 20` and `cause.code === "EPERM"`. On this base `writeArray` still calls plain `rename`, so that branch is inert here and becomes live the moment #857 lands — no follow-up tip is needed for it.

The two tests are split (per the Security review): **A** asserts the caller still sees the replace failure when both `rename` and the cleanup `rm` report `EPERM` (it accepts either the raw replace error before #857 or a `FileReplaceError` whose `cause` is it — the check reads `error.cause?.message` too); **B** asserts a failing replace still removes its temporary file, so no `.tmp` is left behind.

Both mocks use `syncBuiltinESMExports()` because `store.ts` imports `rename`/`rm` as named ESM bindings, and both only touch paths whose `basename` starts with `.state-` — the store's own temporary files — so no other write in the fixture is affected. The mock hands control back to the host after the test (`active` flag plus restore) so the next test is not affected by the still-bound ESM export.

## Ran / Not run

Ran (exit codes verbatim):

1. `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → **0**
2. `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → **0**
3. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/store-replace-cleanup.test.ts` → **0** (`2/2`)
4. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/store.test.ts` → **0** (`121/121`, no regression in the existing store suite)

Not run: the full `services/api` suite and the ST layer locally for this revision; CI runs both.

## Diffstat

`git diff --stat main…HEAD`:

```
 services/api/src/store-replace-cleanup.test.ts | 111 +++++++++++++++++++++++++
 services/api/src/store.ts                      |   5 +-
 2 files changed, 115 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```


## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: when the temporary-file cleanup fails for the same reason the replace did (a Windows antivirus scanner or indexer holding the file), the caller now still receives the classified replace failure — with its errno and attempt count — instead of a bare `EPERM` from the cleanup.
Compatibility and migration: none — the cleanup still runs and still removes the temporary file; only its own failure stops overriding the error that caused it.

items.title: Keep the replace error when the temp-file cleanup also fails

items.body:
Fixes #647

Owner: Dev1
Written-by: Dev-1
Branch: `dev1/fix/647-web-test-module-resolution`

## Problem

A clean tree cannot run the web test suite. Every workspace package publishes its runtime entry from `dist/` (`packages/*/package.json` → `"default": "./dist/*.js"`) and no `dist/` is committed, so a package-level run that does not build first resolves those imports to files that do not exist:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx
# tests 448
# pass 385
# fail 63
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/operational-logging/dist/diagnostics.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/ErrorDiagnosticActions.tsx
# Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../@sciencediscovery/schema/dist/index.js'
#   imported from .../apps/web/src/Markdown.tsx
```

The repo's own `pnpm test` hides this because it runs `pnpm build` first; the per-package script (`tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`) does not. The 63 victims are not defects — they fail at import time, before any assertion runs.

The failure is not specific to `operational-logging`: `schema`, `skill`, `plugin-sdk` and their transitive workspace dependencies fail the same way.

## Commits (red first)

1. `test(web): prove the suite dies when the workspace packages are unbuilt` — one test asserting that every `@sciencediscovery/*` entry the web app imports resolves to a file that exists. Red on the unbuilt tree:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts
not ok 1 - every workspace package the web app imports resolves from its built entry
  error: '@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/manifest resolves to
   .../apps/web/node_modules/@sciencediscovery/artifact-json/dist/manifest.js,
   which does not exist; the workspace packages need building first'
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

Full suite on the same tree: **449 tests / 385 pass / 64 fail** (63 pre-existing + this one).

2. `fix(web): build the workspace packages the test suite imports` — `apps/web`'s `test` script now runs `scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs .` before `tsx --test`. The script walks `apps/web`'s workspace dependencies transitively and builds only the packages whose `dist/` is missing, using the repo's `typescript` and each package's own `tsconfig.json` — exactly what `pnpm build` would produce. It is a no-op once they are built, so the CI path that already ran `pnpm build` pays one directory listing and nothing else.

No test file is modified, and production resolution is untouched: the runtime entry stays `dist/`, which `node dist/server.js` and vite both need.

3. `test(scripts): pin the ensure-workspace-dist skip and build order` — the builder had no test of its own behaviour. Two cases run against a throwaway workspace (a copy of the script, fixture packages, and a stand-in `tsc` that records where it was pointed and writes the `dist/` the compiler would emit, so no TypeScript build is paid for):

- a package without `dist/` is built, a package that already has `dist/` is not rebuilt (its `dist/` is left untouched), and a second run of the script is silent;
- a package is built only after everything it depends on (`leaf` → `middle` → `top`, plus an unrelated sibling, built in that order).

Both cases are green as written. Their red side is a mutation, checked locally on the working tree and not committed: dropping the `dist/` skip fails the first case (`a second run must not rebuild a built package`), and moving `ordered.push(dep)` before the dependency visit fails the second.

## Verification

Red (clean tree, before the fix) → green:

```
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # no dist/
# tests 449   # pass 385   # fail 64
$ node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web
built workspace packages without dist: @sciencediscovery/operational-logging,
@sciencediscovery/external-urls, @sciencediscovery/schema, @sciencediscovery/cas, …
$ cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx     # deps built
# tests 1131   # pass 1131   # fail 0
```

The suite grows from 449 to 1131 because the files that could not load now run. Typechecks: `apps/web` `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0; repo `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` → 0. A second run of the builder prints nothing (idempotent).

## Labels and timing

`agent-ready` could not be applied to the issue by the team (the token gets 403 on label writes) and the owner's 60-minute deadline takes precedence over the usual 24-hour wait, so this is pushed ahead of the label being restored.

## Ran

- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/workspace-package-dist.test.ts` → 0/1 before the fix, 1/1 after
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → 385/449 before, **1131/1131 after**
- `cd apps/web && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` → 0
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (repo root) → 0
- `node scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.mjs apps/web` twice → 17 packages the first time, silent the second
- `node --test scripts/ensure-workspace-dist.test.mjs` → 2/2, and the same two cases fail under the two mutations above
- `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` → 70/71: the one failure is `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`, which shells out to `uv` and dies on the read-only `~/.cache/uv` on this host, unrelated to this change
- `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check` → `CI test catalog OK: 7 cases, 24 tags, 4 layers`

## Not run

- The shared tagged plan end to end (`node test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list`): on this tree it stops during collection with `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION: apps/web/tests/markdown-math.test.ts:16`, a file this branch does not touch and which fails the same way alone at the base commit. The new file was collected on its own instead (`node-collect.mjs` → 2 cases, `category:ut`).
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` verbatim: on this host pnpm's dependency-status check aborts with `ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY` / `EROFS` on the pnpm store (outside the workspace, read-only), so the script's two commands were run directly, in order.

Release: fix

# 学科知识引擎：摄取/生长/消解/消费全链 + 会话绑库与反幻觉运行时

> 与 GitCode MR [!125](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/125) 内容一致（对应 GitCode issue #86）。

把「学科知识」做成 SD 的一等资产：文献与结构化源摄取为带锚点溯源的知识图谱，图谱可离线生长、实体消解、社区聚类；对话内绑定知识库（kb scope）后，图谱成为受约束的知识来源，输出必须引用锚点，与证据账本 / 新颖性检查 / 引用核验构成多层反幻觉链路。

**283 文件，+50.8k，4 个按路径分组的 commit**（KE 核心 / agent 运行时 / Web / 技能与测试）。

---

## 新增功能

### 1. 知识引擎核心（`packages/knowledge-engine` + `services/api/src/knowledge-engine`）

- **存储域**：SQLite（知识库/文档/锚点/实体/边/社区/合并/作业/引用/公式），带迁移机制；算法核与存储分离，可独立评测
- **摄取**：LaTeX-first arXiv 通路（tar.gz 解包 + `\input` 递归内联）、JATS XML、视觉增强 PDF 解析；溯源门抽取——每个抽取结论挂文档锚点
- **生长**：离线 grow job，MMR + anchor-aware 多样本选择、收敛信号、结构化反思 directive 反哺下一轮
- **实体消解**：在线门 + 离线 job、物理合并与回滚（`ke_entity_merges`）、louvain 社区、根实体、社区报告
- **消费面**：`kb_search` / `kb_expand` / `doc_grep` 工具、entity_unified_search、三级文档阅读器（全文/结构/锚点）、引用 API（意图徽章 supporting / contrasting / mentioning + Similar / References / Cited-By）
- **REST**：`/api/ke/*` 全套 + 前端知识引擎页（cytoscape 图谱画布、生长控制面板、阅读器、引用面板）

### 2. 会话绑库（kb scope）

- session 设置新增 `kbScopeKbIds` / `kbScopeWebSearch` 运行时覆盖项；composer 底部选择器一键绑定/解绑，写路径为 fresh-GET 读改写，避免并发选择器互相回滚
- resident-summary 上下文贡献者持续注入**在库**图谱摘要（成熟度分级）；范围外知识库对工具面与摘要均不可见（防泄漏包装）
- 系统 prompt m8.3.1：上下文时钟、kb-scope 自管理指引、反编造纪律句——均在既有 5000 字符保护段预算内

### 3. 反幻觉与研究运行时

- 三级注入：证据账本（`evidence_ledger`）、新颖性检查（`novelty_check`）、引用核验（`verify_citation`）；KE 工具输出逐字文本打 nonce 不可信围栏
- finish-gate 收尾审计：技能声明 `metadata.pre-finish-audit` 即在收尾前注入审计 directive，有界续跑（≤2 次）
- 研究世界模型 `research_state`：目标钉住 / 计划生命周期 / 未决问题 / 已排除路径防复活 / 已试去重，JSON 文件锁崩溃可恢复
- 审批门计划生命周期（`packages/plan-mode`）：`propose_plan` / `revise_plan` 工具、约束级审批、版本绑定决策、决策日志；与上游 `update_plan` 快照机制共存（`AgentRunBindings` 同时携带 `planRepository` 与 `planStore`）
- stall-guard：模型调用无进展按空闲窗踢出重试（≤3 次），外层空闲看门狗兜底
- 记忆图谱镜像 `observeSessionPlan`；MCP 配置文件内容签名失效（保留上游按服务器签名比较，叠加文件级变更检测）

### 4. 技能包与评测

- 15 个方法论技能：knowledge-engine-explore/grow、evidence-notes、hypothesis-tournament、tree-search、robin-chain、virtual-lab、idea-debate、systematic-review、precise-qa、long-form-writing/audit、progressive-report、report-writer、table-analysis（多数声明 pre-finish-audit）
- 评测套件 `scripts/ke-*-eval.mjs`：growth delta-recall、discoverer 诚信维度、pairwise、citation（ALCE 三指标）、resolution、bench 539 题；`skill-test-runner` + ER 数据集构建器
- KE 旅程 E2E 9 条 + kb-scope / finish-gate 旅程，ke-stub 离线可跑

## 验证

Linux（Ubuntu WSL2），分支 `pr/knowledge-engine`（基于 upstream/main 最新 `ef65b6f`，4 个按路径分组的 commit）。

- 29 个 workspace 项目全量构建通过（含 web vite build）；`architecture:check` 通过（293 文件）
- 触及包测试全绿：workspace 119/119、context 50/50、tools 61/61、runtime-core 36/36、memory 35/35、schema 12/12、plan 5/5、plan-mode 2/2
- **services/api 全量套件 1020 tests / 1019 pass / 0 fail**（`node --test dist/*.test.js dist/**/*.test.js`，123s 干净退出）
- 与纯 upstream/main 对照树同环境跑 server.test.js 验证无回归：upstream 86/86，本分支 86/86；期间修复了三处合并引入的问题（MCP transport 双重 close、内置技能清单落位、保护段预算超限），并把 KE sqlite 连接补上服务器关闭回收（否则每个 boot 泄漏 db+wal+shm 句柄并在进程退出时挂起 drain）
- 双计划系统共存验证：propose_plan 审批门与 update_plan 快照在同 run 注册、互不干扰（context-assembly 集成测试覆盖）

Fixes #777

Owner: Dev2
Written-by: Dev-2
Tip SHA: 0bb3ee16884843a09d30278a63db007ba3f4da5d
Base: a429ba1d4eca17af8cfabb9f28abe9d651e38e6c (main at push; branch rebased onto it, no overlap)

`web_fetch`/`web_search` handed search-result titles and snippets to the model with named HTML references still encoded. Only `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot` and `nbsp` decoded, so a page title like `Café — a review` reached the prompt and the report verbatim, and the sources a science search cites most often (encyclopedias, European sites) are exactly the entity-heavy ones. This decodes every named reference a browser resolves, in the same single pass as before.

## What changed

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts`: the five-name map is replaced by the full WHATWG named character reference set — 2125 semicolon-terminated names — expanded into a `Map` once at module load. `nbsp` keeps its existing ordinary-space mapping; numeric references, the single-pass rule (`&lt;` → `<`) and unknown names (`&bogus;` stays literal) are unchanged. The decoding loop is the same one-scan replace it was; only the data changed shape and moved out of this module.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html-entities.ts` (new): the table itself — a `name;code point;…` constant, 246 folded lines — under a 37-line header that states the source (WHATWG named character references via CPython's `html.entities.html5`, 2231 keys of which the 2125 semicolon forms are what this pattern accepts), the retrieval date, the exact `python3` snippet that regenerates the body, and the licence position: the standard's table reproduced as factual data — names and code points any HTML parser needs — not copied from another project's source. `html.ts` keeps the decoder and goes from 79 lines to 90 (+11); 368 is only the shape this branch's previous commit had with the table inline, and this commit moves it out. The data is 246 of the new file's 284 lines.
- `tsconfig.base.json`: one line, `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`. The import in `html.ts` keeps a `.ts` extension so `node --experimental-strip-types` — the command the issue reproduces with — resolves the sibling source instead of failing with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; that option is what lets tsc accept the specifier and still emit `./html-entities.js` (verified: the built `dist/web/native/html.js` line is `import { NAMED_ENTITIES_PACKED } from "./html-entities.js";`). It belongs in the base config rather than the package one: the root tests config used by `pnpm typecheck` extends only `tsconfig.base.json`, and with the option in `packages/data-source/tsconfig.json` alone that check fails with `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts(73,39): error TS5097: An import path can only end with a '.ts' extension when 'allowImportingTsExtensions' is enabled.` From the base config both the package build and that check pass. It changes nothing else in the tree — the only `test/` file that `tsc` type-checks imports `.js` paths; the Playwright specs under `test/` are not in any tsconfig.
- `html-entities.ts` is force-added: `.gitignore`'s `data-*/` rule also matches the `packages/data-source/` directory (`git check-ignore -v` reports `.gitignore:91`). I left that rule alone to keep this PR single-purpose; say the word if you would rather have it anchored as `/data-*/` and I will open a separate issue.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts`: cases for the names in the issue (`eacute`, `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `apos`, `diams`, `rsquo`, `ldquo`/`rdquo`, Latin-1, symbols), case sensitivity, an unknown name, the single-pass rule after the table widened, and a guard that the exported table still has exactly 2125 entries plus one two-scalar value (`NotEqualTilde`), so a dropped or mis-chunked line cannot pass as a smaller table. The test file is unchanged by the move.

Size, whole PR: 4 files, 344 insertions, 8 deletions (`html-entities.ts` +284, `html.test.ts` +41/−1, `html.ts` +18/−7, `tsconfig.base.json` +1).

## Red first

Decoder tests. Command:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/web/native/html.test.ts
```

Before the fix:

```
# Subtest: decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
not ok 3 - decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
  expected: "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
  actual: 'café — 5–10 … O'Brien'
# Subtest: decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
not ok 4 - decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
  expected: 'Ää'
  actual: 'Ää'
# pass 5
# fail 2
```

Table guard. The guard lands in its own commit before the export exists, so it is red on the change that adds only the test:

```
# pass 0
# fail 1
SyntaxError: The requested module './html.js' does not provide an export named 'NAMED_ENTITIES'
```

and it fails the way it is meant to when one entry is dropped from the packed constant (mutation check, one `AElig;c6;` field removed, then restored):

```
not ok 8 - keeps every entry of the generated WHATWG table
  expected: 2125
  actual: 2124
# pass 7
# fail 1
```

Green after the implementation, same command as the decoder run: `# pass 8`, `# fail 0`. The package suite goes from 74 to 75 tests with the guard: `# tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0`.

## The issue's reproduction

Command from #777:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

On this tip:

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

The middle line is the single-pass guarantee: the decoded ampersand does not start a second scan.

## Gates

On this tip, in `packages/data-source` unless noted:

```
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json                                        # exit 0 (build)
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit                               # exit 0
$ node --experimental-strip-types -e 'import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(...)'
  café — 5–10 … O'Brien                                          # exit 0
$ npm test                                                        # # tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0
$ cd ../.. && node scripts/check-architecture.mjs                 # 333 source files, boundaries OK
$ cd ../.. && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json        # exit 0
$ cd ../.. && pnpm --recursive typecheck                          # 34 packages Done, exit 0
```

`pnpm architecture:check` is **98 passed / 1 failed** on this host: `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs` shells out to `.ci/run-research-python.sh race`, which needs a writable uv Python install and network (`Read-only file system` at `~/.local/share/uv/python`); it does not touch `packages/data-source`. `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` itself is green, as shown above.

## Not run

- Repo-level UT/ST/E2E, CodeCheck (GitCode) and the Docker/binary layers: CI. This PR changes one package's text extractor and its test, plus one compiler option; the package tests, both tsc configurations, the architecture check and the recursive typecheck were run locally.
