Eleven previously quarantined browser specs now execute as **41 identities** on the shared PR plan. Narrow/mobile, low-height and Composer viewport matrices are retained. The shared entry replaces the legacy Playwright project, `ci:e2e:legacy`, `test:legacy*`, `CI_ALLOW_LEGACY` and the `e2e.legacy` catalog case. The separate legacy agent backend is unaffected; workflow topology and required check names are unchanged.

Earlier review fixes preserve Project/Session selection boundaries, proxy help dismissal/scroll behavior, Stop persisted-state recovery, and journey-owned stub cleanup. The automatic merge gate then exposed an export-preview error in an otherwise completed approval journey.

## Preview and journey fixes

- Expected export-preview work-in-progress no longer becomes a browser resource error. Web preview clients opt into `Prefer: respond-async`; only typed `EXPORT_PREVIEW_PENDING` becomes HTTP 202. Pending results stay out of the cache, completed previews recover normally, old clients retain HTTP 409, and real failures such as HTTP 503 still propagate.
- Newly seeded sample Sessions omit absent agent-state CAS objects from `*Ref` fields used by trajectory readers. The recorded shell-result fields `workspaceSnapshot` and `workspaceVersion` are retained in the seed streams and explicitly omitted from portable research-package results. The seed regression checks the `*Ref` scope; it does not claim that every agent-state-shaped object is removed. Inline transcript and trajectory events remain available, and all five preview profiles are exercised by a regression. Existing seeded installations are not migrated.
- Background/Stop journeys wait for the selected Session and saved model name before continuing. The real Stop response gate is installed before opening long-lived streams; cancellation, fallback recovery and business assertions remain.
- The Evolve API journey waits through the API's documented HTTP 503 `starting` state after listening begins. Other health errors still fail immediately, and all provider/accounting/cancellation/recovery assertions remain. This is startup readiness polling, not test-case retries.

## Validation

Current HEAD: **`2c33bc5017f4ad195b0c1cb5746344d9c575f6f5`**, **one commit**, based on `239dde7d26964778c91ef364751a8737161511d0`.

[Current GitHub CI](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42480234752) completed successfully for `2c33bc5017f4ad195b0c1cb5746344d9c575f6f5`: L1, UT, ST, all five mocked L2 E2E shards (including `standard-journeys`), Coverage, CodeCheck and merge-gate succeeded. There are no failed or pending checks. Real E2E, binary and Docker jobs were skipped by the selected PR profile; those jobs are not claimed as executed.

At the requester's explicit instruction, local validation was stopped and the fixes were pushed directly. No complete local gate result is claimed for this final HEAD. Dependencies, virtualenvs, service ports, temporary storage and Fontconfig configuration were task-scoped; no system package installation or shared dependency upgrade was made.

Historical diagnostic results at the earlier candidate `54714370`: standard-journeys **87 planned / 87 executed / 87 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped**, L1 and Web/API typechecks passed; UT **6704/6705**, failing only the Evolve journey's first API health assertion (`503 != 200`, before any business action). Modified UT files passed **38/38**, including preview/sample regressions **34/34**. That Evolve journey passed in the unchanged `8a253314` baseline comparison, so the candidate failure was not dismissed as a confirmed baseline failure; explicit startup waiting was added in the final commit. The earlier candidate's ST was interrupted for this source change. These historical diagnostics do not substitute for the final HEAD's remote gates.

## E2E user journeys

The affected paths are AgentRun approval → completion → reusable composer with a strict console check; background Session switching; Stop recovery while the real terminal response is delayed; and narrow/low-height Composer reachability. The full earlier candidate's 87-case shard passed; the final SHA's GitHub mocked E2E gates have now all succeeded, as linked above. No console filters, added test retries or skipped identities were introduced. The accepted state-specific Composer floor is recorded below.

Full failure history and follow-up: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/951#issuecomment-6704576323

## Release and maintainer decisions

Intended release category: `release:fix` (preview error handling and newly seeded samples). Existing installations retain their data; old API clients retain the 409 contract. The `release:fix` label is applied and verified; `release:internal` is removed.

Accepted decisions, as recorded by collaborator @zhaozhaozz in the [approval review for this HEAD](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/951#pullrequestreview-5821155298):

- The separate legacy/quarantine browser entry points and `CI_ALLOW_LEGACY` are retired in this PR; the shared tagged plan replaces them. This retirement is accepted, not an outstanding proposal. Workflow topology and required check names are unchanged.
- The release category is `release:fix`, matching the applied label.
- The capped/chipped Composer transcript floor is 1/3; idle and running retain 55%. This state-specific floor is accepted, not deferred.

Outstanding human review items: whether Project-switch needs an additional direct regression, and review of the changed `.agents/skills` guidance. Neither item is recorded here as accepted or formally deferred. The existing reporter fresh/global ordering limitation remains outside this repair.

Part of #817.

## Conflict resolution

Rebased the single PR commit onto main `239dde7d26964778c91ef364751a8737161511d0`. The only textual conflict was `apps/web/src/api/plugins.ts`: main added an optional cancellation signal while this PR introduced the shared async-preview request helper. The merged implementation forwards `AbortSignal` through the helper into fetch while retaining `Prefer: respond-async`, pending-state handling and real error propagation. A range-diff confirms the remaining PR patch is preserved. Main's workflow, mocked accounting and tagged execution changes are retained. GitHub now reports **MERGEABLE**; required checks/review may still block merging. No local tests were started, following the requester's instruction; validation is the new remote run above.

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Fixes #997

## The defect

The agent could create, read and price an evolution search but not stop one. When the user corrected the scoring formula mid-run, the only move the tool surface allowed was to start a second search beside the first — the issue's evidence shows two concurrent PUCT runs on one session (`c870cf09` candidates=12, `fee68bb2` candidates=1, both `running`), each frozen against a different formula and splitting the same budget, with no way for the user to say which result counts.

The server could already stop a run (`POST /api/evolve/runs/{id}/stop`, which the desktop uses); only the agent-facing capability was missing.

## Change

- **`packages/evolve`**: `EvolveToolRuntime` gains an optional `stopEvolveRun`, and `createEvolveTools` registers `stop_evolve_run` only when the deployment can actually stop a run — the same shape `createIdeaResearch` already uses, so a deployment without the capability does not advertise a tool that pretends to work.
- The tool takes an explicit `runId` and no "most recent" default, because stopping is destructive. It answers with what actually happened: `stopping` for an active run, and the terminal status when the search had already finished (that case is not an error).
- **`services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts`** implements it on the same orchestrator call the desktop route uses, scoped to the asking session: an id from another session is refused, and an unknown id answers with the searches this session does have — the same help `get_evolve_run` gives, since the reader is a model deciding what to call next.
- The description carries the rule the issue is about: stop the running search **before** proposing a replacement, and never start a second search alongside a live one.
- Docs list the tool in both languages.

## Tests

`packages/evolve/src/index.test.ts`:
- the stop tool is absent without the capability and present with it;
- the run id is passed through unchanged and the reply names the run;
- an already-finished search is reported as such rather than as a stop.

CI covers the composition root: `native-agent.test.ts` builds a runtime without `stopEvolveRun` (the optional member keeps that fixture valid), and the `services/api` build exercises the new implementation.

## Scope

This is the agent-side capability the issue asks for. It does not add server-side rejection of a second concurrent run on the same session — the issue phrases that as "and/or", and the stop tool makes the correct sequence available. If the reviewers want the guard as well, that is a separate change and the issue can carry it.

A Project row keeps its `+` and `⋯` controls behind the fold's own name. The
toggle is a flex item, and a button's automatic minimum size is its content, so
a name longer than the column made the toggle lay out past the row instead of
shrinking. The controls were pushed outside the column, which clips horizontal
overflow, and became unreachable: neither hover nor keyboard focus nor the open
Project could reveal them. A Session row never had this problem because its
button already sets `min-width: 0`; the Project toggle was missing the same
line.

## The toggle can shrink

`.side-row.side-project .side-project-toggle` now carries `min-width: 0`.
Nothing else changes: the label's existing ellipsis starts working, so a long
name ends in `…` inside the row, and the existing hover, `:focus-within` and
active rules reveal `+` and `⋯` within the row's box instead of beyond it. The
full name stays in the button's tooltip, and double-click rename is unaffected.

## Captures

Taken with a throwaway spec in the mocked desktop suite — it uses the same
fixtures as the committed case and is not part of the diff — and cropped to the
sidebar. Each "before" pair was produced in a detached worktree at `main`
(`5033f026`), each "after" pair on this head. Both rows are hovered.

Sidebar width is 296px at a 1280px viewport and 256px at 1024px — the narrow
pair is the width where the failure bites hardest.

### zh-CN

| Wide (296px) — before, hovered | Wide (296px) — after, hovered |
| --- | --- |
| ![zh-CN before at 296px: the name runs past the clipped column, no controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/zh-CN/before-wide-hover.png) | ![zh-CN after at 296px: the name ends in an ellipsis and both controls sit inside the row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/zh-CN/after-wide-hover.png) |

| Narrow (256px) — before, hovered | Narrow (256px) — after, hovered |
| --- | --- |
| ![zh-CN before at 256px: the name runs past the column, no controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/zh-CN/before-narrow-hover.png) | ![zh-CN after at 256px: the name ends in an ellipsis and both controls sit inside the row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/zh-CN/after-narrow-hover.png) |

Active/focused (`:focus-within`), 296px:

![zh-CN after, keyboard focus on the toggle: the focus ring is drawn and both controls are revealed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/zh-CN/after-wide-focused.png)

### en

| Wide (296px) — before, hovered | Wide (296px) — after, hovered |
| --- | --- |
| ![en before at 296px: the name runs past the clipped column, no controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/en/before-wide-hover.png) | ![en after at 296px: the name ends in an ellipsis and both controls sit inside the row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/en/after-wide-hover.png) |

| Narrow (256px) — before, hovered | Narrow (256px) — after, hovered |
| --- | --- |
| ![en before at 256px: the name runs past the column, no controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/en/before-narrow-hover.png) | ![en after at 256px: the name ends in an ellipsis and both controls sit inside the row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/en/after-narrow-hover.png) |

Active/focused (`:focus-within`), 296px:

![en after, keyboard focus on the toggle: the focus ring is drawn and both controls are revealed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/assets/pr996-shots/en/after-wide-focused.png)

In the "before" shots the name stops at the clipped edge with no `…` and the
row carries no controls at all, even while hovered; the chevron is pushed off
the row too. In the "after" shots the name ends in `…` and the chevron, `+` and
`⋯` all sit inside the row's right edge.

## Coverage

A mocked desktop e2e case renders a Project with a 72-character name and
asserts that the label computes `text-overflow: ellipsis` and has
`scrollWidth > clientWidth`, that both controls are hidden at rest, and that
hover brings them back inside the row's bounding box. Without the CSS line the
case fails at the truncation assertion, so the regression is caught rather than
described.

## Validation

Run on commit 58a78978.

- Desktop package unit tests (`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`):
  821 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Desktop mocked e2e (`apps/desktop/e2e/projects.spec.ts`): 4 passed, 0 failed.
- UT layer (`pnpm ci:ut`): planned 6587, executed 6558, passed 6545, failed 13,
  skipped 0. All 13 failures reproduce with identical counts on unmodified
  `main` (5033f026) in a separate detached worktree, so none is introduced by
  this change. They are host conditions:
  - `services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts` (5) and
    `services/launcher/src/source-evolve.test.ts` (5): a stray
    `/tmp/package.json` outside the repository declares `"type": "module"`, so
    the CommonJS `dist/server.js` the launcher spawns is treated as ESM.
  - `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` (1): the trajectory
    database cannot be opened in this host's temporary directory.
  - `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` (1): the host bubblewrap
    rejects `--disable-userns`, an option the sandbox test passes.
  - `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs` (1): the interrupt simulation restores
    its mirror on this host instead of reproducing the interrupted write.
- ST layer (`pnpm ci:st`): planned 51, executed 51, passed 49, failed 2. Both
  failures are local provisioning, not the change: the JiuwenSwarm SDK check
  could not install `chromadb` because the run was pinned offline against a
  cache that predates it, and the Evolve distribution journey downloads the
  pinned Python runtime and source from the network, which the same offline
  run blocked.

### CI on this head

Run `42477401587` on `58a78978` is green: `L1`, `UT`, `Coverage`,
`CodeCheck (GitCode)`, `ST` (51 of 51), all five mocked shards, and
`merge-gate`. `L3`/`L4`/`L5`, `Binary release` and `Docker image` are skipped
by the pull-request profile.

Four earlier runs on the same head were red for reasons outside this diff:
GitHub's release download host was answering `502`/`504`, so
`test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` could not fetch the pinned
`python-build-standalone` runtime, `astral-sh/setup-uv@v6` could not install
`uv`, and `standard-config` reported `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready
(failed: micromamba setup failed)`. The same failures hit unrelated pull
requests in the same window — `fix/jiuwenswarm-skill-authority-896` (run
`42468248524`) and `fix-986-export-save-dialog` (run `42470653800`) — and
`main` at `239dde7d` (run `42465227603`). The green run was triggered once the
host was stable; nothing in the diff changed between it and the red runs.

## E2E user journeys

PASS — local, mocked, tested commit 58a78978 on
`fix/desktop-long-project-name`. Browser: desktop Chromium via
`apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts`.

- A Project with a 72-character name → the name is ellipsized inside the row,
  both controls are hidden at rest, and hovering reveals `+` and `⋯` inside
  the row → PASS.
- Existing Project journeys in the same spec (rename through a reload, delete
  with confirmation, delete the Project of the open Session) → PASS.

Totals: 4 passed / 0 failed / 0 blocked / 0 skipped.

**The desktop shell is deliberately out of CI.** `apps/desktop/e2e` is not
referenced by any workflow in `.github/workflows` or `.ci`; the mocked matrix
drives `apps/web`, which needs the Python control plane, and its fixture puts a
project, a token and a model in place before a spec starts — the opposite of a
desktop journey, which has to begin from an empty workspace. Keeping the suite
local is the design, not an oversight, so this evidence is reported as local
rather than as a CI gate. Wiring the desktop shell into the matrix would be its
own change.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
GitHub label: `release:fix` is pending a maintainer — this fork has no write
access to apply labels, so the category is stated here instead.
User impact: A Project whose name does not fit the column now shows a
truncated name with `…` and keeps its `+` (new session in the Project) and `⋯`
(rename/delete) controls reachable on hover, keyboard focus or when the
Project is active.
Compatibility and migration: none.

recent_merged.body:
Fixes #986

## What changed

### Desktop shell (`win_desktop`)
- New export IPC: a native "save as" dialog that remembers the last chosen directory and asks before overwriting (`sd-shell:export-save-dialog`), a write bound to that destination (`sd-shell:export-write`), open-file-location (`sd-shell:export-show-in-folder`) and the OS downloads dir (`sd-shell:export-downloads-dir`).
- **The renderer never handles a filesystem path.** The dialog issues an opaque token, the main process keeps the chosen path (`ExportDestinations`), and the write/reveal handlers accept only that token — a token this process did not issue is refused. Renderer code therefore cannot address a file the user did not pick, so the window's `sandbox`/`contextIsolation` isolation is not bypassed.
- Exposed as `window.sdShell.exportFile` in the preload; `lastExportDir` is persisted (`export-state.json`) so the next export defaults to the last used folder.

### Desktop export flow (`apps/desktop`)
- **Choose the destination first**: confirming export opens the native save dialog (default name `会话标题_YYYYMMDD_HHmm.sdresearch`, default folder = last used folder, else the OS downloads folder). Cancelling the dialog aborts the export without starting a packaging task.
- **Automatic save**: once packaging completes, the archive is written to the chosen destination automatically — no second Download click.
- **Independent exports**: each export keeps its own task id, destination and result; starting a second export no longer overwrites the first's tracking.
- **Unobtrusive feedback**: small bottom-page text shows "N exports in progress" (expandable, each task cancellable); a green/red completion flash appears for a few seconds and disappears on its own, with an "open file location" action. Cancel is offered only while the server task can still be cancelled; a cancel that races completion keeps the finished package and saves it.
- The export dialog keeps a persistent "saved packages" list with open-location and retry-save (a save failure reuses the already-generated archive rather than repackaging).

### API
- `POST /api/projects/{id}/research-package/exports/{task}/cancel` plus a `canceled` terminal state. Cancellation is re-checked after the archive is written and during packaging, so a cancelled export never leaves or advertises a package.

### Browser fallback
In a plain browser (no Electron shell) there is no pre-packaging native save dialog; the supported equivalent is a browser download after packaging completes, through the browser's own save prompt, keeping the same automatic-save-on-completion behaviour. Multiple concurrent exports each keep their own entry.

## Screenshots

Captured on a Windows dev checkout at head `d466d61e` (before the destination-token binding and the flash-timer fix; the visible flow is unchanged, and the completion flash now auto-dismisses after ~4 s instead of staying until a refresh).

**1. Native save dialog, opened before any packaging starts** (title 导出研究包, folder 下载, name 脓毒症内型评分聚类分析_20261108_1858, type ScienceDiscovery 研究包):

![Save dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-986/pr-999/01-save-dialog.png)

**2. Packaging in progress — small bottom-page text:**

![Export in progress](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-986/pr-999/02-export-in-progress.png)

**3. Saved automatically — green completion flash with 打开文件位置:**

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Fixes #998 (`Refs #978`)

## The gap

#987 settles one half of #978: `!execution.accepted && submissionRejected` → `rejectSubmission`, so a Runner that refuses the submission makes the tool call fail visibly.

The 4th #978 reproduction is the other half — `accepted=true stage=finalization`, where the Runner answers 401 `Execution not found for this Agent` while the finished execution's result is being handed over. That error does not match the submission branch, so it fell through to `unavailable()` → `state="unknown"`, `finalization="pending"`, `retryable=false`. No terminal state, no tool result, and the run stays `running` until the idle watchdog — the same missing invariant as #978, reached through a different stage.

## Change

- An accepted execution that the Runner answers with **401/403/404** is settled **failed with committed provenance**. Those answers mean "this execution is not readable by this Agent any more", which no amount of waiting changes, so leaving the record unknown only keeps the tool call and the run alive.
- The message states what is actually known rather than implying the command never ran: the Runner accepted the command, may have run it, would not return the result, and the workspace should be inspected before anything is re-run.
- The submission-stage path (#987) and the `PROCESS_STATE_UNVERIFIABLE` path are untouched. This only covers a Runner that refuses the hand-off of an execution it had already accepted.

## Tests

`services/api/src/shell-executions.test.ts` — for 401, 403 and 404: the record reaches `state="failed"` with committed provenance and committed finalization, carries a non-retryable observation error naming the unreadable result and the "inspect the workspace" recovery, and publishes a completion notice so the failure is visible.

## Scope

This is the finalization-stage settlement. The separate clock-skew lead in #978's investigation (two `model-sse-summary` records whose `completedAt` preceded `startedAt`) is not addressed here and is not claimed as a cause.

## Summary

Fixes the desktop half of #981: exporting a conversation could leave a persistent `legacy_unavailable` banner.

That string is the adapter's legacy proxy answering `502` with the internal code `legacy_unavailable` when the legacy API it forwards to is briefly unreachable. The desktop client surfaced that raw code as the error message, and the export poll retried it every three seconds with no bound, so the unexplained English code stayed on the page.

## Change

- `apps/desktop/src/api/client.ts`: add `isLegacyUnavailableError(reason)` (status 502 + message `legacy_unavailable`), mirroring `apps/web/src/api/auth.ts`.
- `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`: the export poll now distinguishes outcomes:
  - `404` is terminal: the stale task is marked failed with a localized message (`exportMissing`).
  - `legacy_unavailable` is a transient service failure: show a localized `legacyUnavailable` retrying message, retry at the existing 3 s interval, and stop after 5 consecutive failures.
  - Other transient rejections retry a bounded 5 times, then show `exportPollingFailed`.
- `zh.ts` / `en.ts`: added `legacyUnavailable`, `exportPollingFailed`, `exportMissing`, localized in both languages.
- `apps/desktop/tests/api-client.test.ts`: assert the 502 code is recognised and only for that code.

## Scope

This is the unclear-message + poll-churn half. The export/save interaction redesign and multi-task tracking are tracked separately in #986. The full root cause of *why* the legacy API was unreachable is not diagnosed here, per the issue's own note that this should be captured during reproduction rather than inferred.

recent_merged.author: ink999107
recent_merged.body:
A managed shell execution could stay `running` forever even though its command had already finished. `runSandboxed` waited only for the child process's `close` event, and Node emits `close` only after every writer of the inherited stdio pipes is gone. A descendant the command left behind — a background process, a fork, the egress bridge's child — keeps those pipes open, so `close` never arrives.

Managed executions are forced to `executionTimeoutMs = 0`, so the only other settle path (the timeout branch) never existed for them. Executions are serial per workspace root, so the stuck head kept every later execution `queued`, and `cancel` only sent SIGKILL without any join deadline: the API answered 200/202 while the record stayed `running`. In the report that prompted this change, a real E2E burned its whole one-hour budget on a command whose logs were already complete.

## Settle on `exit`, not only on `close`

`runSandboxed` now also listens for `exit`. Once the commanded process has exited, a bounded grace period (`DEFAULT_TERMINATION_GRACE_MS`, 10 s) starts for `close`; if `close` is still missing (a descendant holds the pipes), the exit itself is the outcome. Output already read is kept, and a paused stream is drained the same way the timeout branch does. `finish` clears both timers, and `stopError` (abort, quota, timeout) still wins over a signalled exit, preserving the existing semantics. A command that keeps running without a deadline is unaffected.

## Bound the join after a kill

SIGKILL is asynchronous, and a process in uninterruptible I/O — or a group that vanished — may never report `exit`. Every `stop()` now starts a join deadline. If the process has exited by then, it settles normally; if not, the run rejects with `ProcessTerminationUnverifiedError` (`code: PROCESS_TERMINATION_UNVERIFIED`). The `ExecutionManager` records that as `unknown` and quarantines the workspace through the existing mechanism, instead of fabricating `processTerminated: true` or committing a snapshot while a writer may still exist. Because the queue item resolves, the Workspace queue advances; work already queued behind the quarantine is rejected at dispatch with `EXECUTION_RESOURCE_QUARANTINED` rather than launched into unverified state.

## Cancel a queued execution immediately

`cancel()` used to abort a controller that the queued work would only observe after the head finished, so a cancelled `queued` execution looked unchanged indefinitely. A `queued` record now becomes `cancelled` (`not_started` evidence, `finishedAt`) and is aborted in the same call. The tail still waits on the head — one workspace stays serial — and the cancelled command is skipped at dispatch. A re-check after recovery validation closes the window where a cancellation arriving during that `await` could still launch a process, and a record that never launched is no longer briefly written back as `running`.

## Respect an operator-configured lifetime

`POST /shell-executions` used to overwrite `executionTimeoutMs` with 0 unconditionally. The client's waiting deadline is still not the process lifetime, but an operator who set `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS` now actually gets that lifetime bound for managed executions. The default remains unlimited.

## Validation

Run on this commit (`be90a20e`) with the repository's three layers.

- UT: planned 6905, executed 6876, passed 6861, failed 15, skipped 0. `services/runner` passes in full, including the three new cases (a managed execution settles when `close` is missed; a kill whose exit is never observed settles as unverified; a queued cancel is terminal without starting the next one). Every one of the 15 failures reproduces on unmodified `main` in this environment, so none is introduced here:
  - `services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts` (5) and `services/launcher/src/source-evolve.test.ts` (5): the stack they spawn exits with status 1 before its health gate.
  - `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs`, `services/api/src/evolution/evolve-thinking-entry.test.ts`: the same cases fail on `main`.
  - `services/api/src/server.test.ts`: a different single case fails in each run, which is flakiness rather than a fixed regression.
  - `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts`: the host's bubblewrap 0.6.1 has no `--disable-userns`, which the case hard-codes.
  - `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`: JiuwenSwarm cannot be installed here (the pinned `openai-codex` is absent from the local mirror); the same case fails on `main`.
- ST: planned 51, executed 51, passed 50, failed 1 — `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` cannot download the pinned CPython build from the GitHub release (HTTP 504 on this network); the unmodified `main` run fails there too. `check:swarm-sdk-contract` passed against an existing JiuwenSwarm install (79 tests and 20 subtests).
- E2E: planned 136 mocked browser cases. See the next section.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the batches that completed on `be90a20e` on this host, with the failures below attributed. Mocked browser layer against the real local stack (bubblewrap, JiuwenSwarm backend, pinned Chromium), six serial batches from the frozen 136-case plan:

- `mocked-governed` 5 passed / 0 failed, `mocked-literature` 6 / 0, `mocked-research` 21 / 0, `mocked-standard-config-fresh` 2 / 0.
- `mocked-standard-config-global` 37 passed / 3 failed. `journey-prepare-environment` was BLOCKED with `micromamba setup failed` (this host has no micromamba base Python for the managed environment). `journey-custom-provider-degraded-settings` missed its 10 s success-alert wait once and passed when the same spec was rerun against the same stack, so it is load-sensitive rather than a fixed regression. `journey-model-connect-wizard` fails its first layout assertion on this host: the submit button's bottom edge measures 598.2 px against a dialog footer fixed at 580 px. This commit changes only `services/runner` — no web code — so that measurement belongs to the host's renderer, not to this change.
- `mocked-standard-journeys` 56 passed / 0 failed before the local per-invocation cap stopped the batch with 6 of its 62 cases still queued behind the long sandbox-network and session journeys.

Totals executed: 130 of 136 — 127 passed, 3 failed, 0 skipped. The three failures are the environment BLOCKED case, the load-sensitive spec that passed on rerun, and the host layout assertion. GitHub Actions runs the full matrix with its own budget.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer; this account has no write access to the upstream repository)

User impact: a session no longer wedges when a command leaves a background process holding its pipes; Stop/cancel always reaches a terminal state, and the executions queued behind it run instead of waiting forever.

Compatibility and migration: none. The default lifetime stays unlimited; the new grace period only applies after the commanded process has exited or a kill was requested.

recent_merged.body:
The web front end is being replaced by the desktop entry, but the merged live literature review case still drove the old web page: it created its fixture through `createProjectAndSession`, opened the Session with `openProjectSession`, and submitted the question with `sendUserMessage`. This change moves the case to the desktop entry, so the journey keeps covering the surface a reader actually uses, without changing what it verifies about the literature work.

## The case now drives the desktop entry

`test/literature-review-immune-liver-real.spec.ts` becomes `test/desktop-literature-review-immune-liver-real.spec.ts`. It starts the Vite entry on 4178 (`startDesktopEntry`), seeds the shared token into the origin's localStorage before the first navigation (`seedDesktopOrigin` — the desktop app reads it from there rather than from the shared storage state), creates the fixture with `createDesktopFixture`, opens the Session with `openDesktopSession`, and submits the fixed question from `#composer-textarea` with `sendMessage`.

The stack health gate now probes the same origin the helper drives (`API_ORIGIN`). Previously the probe could pass against one port and the journey then drive another.

Everything the case verifies is unchanged and still read from the control API: the five literature MCP sources are installed and ready, only those connectors are enabled, every skill and specialist is off, PubMed and bioRxiv are each invoked successfully, the declared CSV has exactly 14 unique pathways with integer counts on both sides, the chart is a real PNG or SVG naming both populations, and the review has Methods / Results / Contradictory findings / References, names both databases, and cites at least four distinct papers. Only the entry point and the surfaces the reader acts on moved.

## The desktop fixture takes the shared catalog's model policy

`createDesktopFixture(page)` used to create an owned model from `E2E_LLM_VARIANT` (defaulting to `openai`) and start a Session with no thinking policy. That was enough for the evolve smoke, but the shared real catalog names the variant `E2E_LLM_API_VARIANT`, and the web journeys also set a thinking policy. `resolveModel` now reads `E2E_LLM_API_VARIANT` first and falls back to the old spelling, and `createDesktopFixture` accepts `{ name, model, session }`:

- `name` — the base name for the Project, the Session and an owned model profile;
- `modelId` — the id of a profile already on the stack; when set no profile is created and `model` is ignored. The helper's reuse path also accepts `E2E_LLM_MODEL_ID`, the shared catalog's spelling of `E2E_MODEL_ID`, so a stack that registers its model ahead of the run works without the `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL` credentials;
- `model` — extra profile fields such as `apiVariant`, `thinkingMode` and `thinkingEffort`. The profile is spread first in the create body, so it cannot replace the endpoint, the token or the name; `apiVariant` is taken from it when present and from the environment otherwise;
- `session` — fields set on the Session together with its model, kept in the same request because a mode switch must stay in its own request.

The defaults reproduce the previous behaviour exactly (`Desktop SRBench <suffix>`, `E2E_LLM_VARIANT`, no Session fields), so the evolve smoke is unaffected.

## Validation

The branch is rebased onto `upstream/main` at `95d5bdb5`; upstream has since advanced to `239dde7d`, and none of the new commits touch either changed file. The diff is +90/−45 over 2 files.

The review follow-up `f7865449` (reuse a pre-registered model) changes only the helper's reuse path and the fixture call; on it `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes and `pnpm ci:l1` passes 4/4. The runs below were measured on `373c6137`, which exercises the create path and the journey the follow-up does not alter.

Run locally on `373c6137` (Linux x64):

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UT | 6900 | 6900 | 6885 | 15 | 0 |
| E2E (mocked) | 136 | 136 | 133 | 3 | 0 |

The 15 UT failures are host limitations, none in this diff:

- **10 — `services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts` and `source-evolve.test.ts`.** They write CommonJS fixtures under `os.tmpdir()`; this host carries an unrelated `/tmp/package.json` with `"type": "module"`, so Node parses the fixture as ESM. Re-running the same tests with `TMPDIR=/var/tmp/...` passes. The same set was reproduced on a pristine `upstream/main` worktree when PR #964 recorded its baseline.
- **1 — `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs`, "the same harness FAILS on the pre-fix body that restored only on the happy path".** The same failure is present on pristine `upstream/main` on this host.
- **1 — `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`, the trajectory assertion.** The same failure is present on earlier branches of this work on this host.
- **1 — `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts`.** The host's `bwrap` has no `--disable-userns`.
- **1 — `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`.** A worker-level failure under the full run; the file passes 1/1 when run alone (`node --test scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`).
- **1 — `check:research-python-ut`.** `uv` cannot reach `pypi.org` from this host (`operation timed out` fetching `charset-normalizer`).

The mocked E2E layer ran 136 planned / 136 executed / 133 passed / 3 failed / 0 skipped. Two are the failures PR #964 already recorded on this host: `journey-model-connect-wizard` measures the connect card at 598.2 px against a `< 580` bound (a web layout measurement, `apps/web` untouched here), and `journey-prepare-environment` J3 is `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: micromamba setup failed)` because the pinned micromamba release is on `github.com`, which this host cannot reach. The third, `journey-custom-provider-degraded-settings`, is a full-suite flake: it timed out after 10 s waiting for the success alert its own stub produces, and both of its journeys pass 2/2 when the spec runs alone on the same commit (`CI_E2E_SPEC=test/journey-custom-provider-degraded-settings.spec.ts .ci/run-e2e.sh mocked`).

## E2E user journeys

Real stack, live model, on `373c6137` — PASS. The full run took 1119.1 s (18.7 min) with 3 of 3 journey steps passing:

| Step | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Turn skills, specialists and the Reviewer off, enable every literature MCP source | no skill whitelist, no specialist, automatic review off, only the literature connectors enabled, PubMed and bioRxiv ready | PASS |
| Ask the fixed liver immune-pathway question from the desktop composer and wait for the main Run chain | the desktop entry opens the Session, the model runs the prompt with literature-only MCP tools, the main Run chain reaches a terminal state | PASS |
| Verify live PubMed and bioRxiv searches and the 14-pathway delivery | PubMed returned records, bioRxiv ran successfully, 14 unique pathways with integer counts on both sides, a real PNG/SVG chart, and a review with all four sections citing at least four distinct papers | PASS |

The delivered evidence from that run: PubMed invoked 9 times returning 79 records; bioRxiv invoked 3 times returning 0 preprints in its trailing window (the review states this rather than inventing one); 14 CSV rows with 9 adult and 11 pediatric nonzero counts; the chart is a 36,964-byte PNG; 15 citations (8 PMIDs, 7 DOIs) across the review, with a Contradictory findings section present; final delivery status `passed` with no delivery errors. The runner ledger for the run shows 19 shell executions, all terminal (15 completed, 4 failed) — no execution left `running` or `queued`.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

The GitHub label is pending a maintainer: this account is an outside contributor and cannot apply labels to the upstream repository.

User impact: none — this is the repository's real E2E journey and its desktop fixture helper.

Compatibility and migration: none. Existing callers of `createDesktopFixture(page)` keep the previous defaults.

## Summary

Fixes #984: imported and research-copy sessions allocate a fresh executor session, so JiuwenSwarm — which holds and compresses its own per-session context — starts with no model-visible history. The restored transcript was displayed but never reached the model, so continuing an imported conversation lost the prior context (dialogue-only packages broke the central continuation promise).

## Change

Seed the restored history once, on the first continuation turn, as an equivalent model-context assembly:

- **`history-seed.ts`** folds the gateway history into a bounded, role-labelled block: `user:` / `assistant:` / `tool call:` / `tool result:` ordering is preserved, tool calls are named with their arguments, and a character budget keeps a large transcript from crowding out the turn (the opening user message is kept as an anchor).
- **`jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`** prepends that block to the system prompt only when the run opts in via the new `seedModelContext` flag.
- **`runs/index.ts`** opts the run in when the session has an `imported_snapshot` / `research_copy` snapshot that has not been seeded yet, and marks `researchSnapshot.modelContextSeeded` once the first run completes — so subsequent turns, retries and restarts never duplicate the seed.
- **`packages/schema`** adds the `modelContextSeeded` marker; **`packages/workspace`** adds the `seedModelContext` option.

Native/specialist executors are unaffected: the flag is ignored by the native loop, which already assembles gateway history into its model context.

## Why this shape

JiuwenSwarm 0.2.6's `chat.send` contract has no history/messages field, and its session context lives only in-process (its own `warmup_session_context` reads its own `history.jsonl`, which SD's restored transcript never enters; there is no external history-write RPC). A cross-repo `history.seed` patch is the heavier alternative; this PR delivers the "equivalent model-context assembly" the issue allows, entirely on the SD side.

## Tests

- `history-seed.test.ts` covers role ordering/labelling, tool call/result recognition, budget bounding with the anchor, and empty/irrelevant-message handling.
- The issue's acceptance criteria (synthetic fact recall + first-model-request inspection, source present/deleted/clean destination, essential/full exports, no duplication on retry/restart, prefix-only branches inherit upstream) remain an end-to-end check I did not run here; the code path is unit-covered.

A design search ends with a **step record**: a checkpoint-like card written after the search started, which asks for nothing and whose body is the longest text in the transcript. It was printed in full, so a four-step design read as four screens. A run started without a sandbox also kept saying so — a `无隔离` chip on the run card and a warning line above the task overview — after the reader had already answered the confirmation before the start. This is the follow-up to #972, which merged as `bebd64e9` with head `947ad817`. The merge queue entry was created before these commits, so they were not part of that merge. ## The closing step folds A record now renders as a `
` like an answered checkpoint: closed by default, with the step label and the model's headline in the band and the body one click away. It still carries no counter and no buttons. The live checkpoint that still asks is unchanged: it is the thing the reader is being asked to act on, so it stays open. ## The folded shape is one set of rules The folded styling was scoped to `.evolve-checkpoint.is-answered`, so the record — which emitted `is-record` — drew the browser's default marker, a title carrying the body's margins, and no chevron rotation. Both paths now emit one `is-folded` class when the card is answered or a record, and the rules are keyed on it; `is-answered` / `is-record` stay for a rule that wants to tint one state only. ## The no-sandbox marks are gone once the run is going The `无隔离` chip on the run card and the warning line above the task overview are removed, along with their strings. The risk is still stated where it is decided: the notice in the setup dialog and the confirmation the reader answers before the send, which `apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts` still covers. ## Screenshots Captured in the desktop app through the mocked e2e harness — a synthetic session, no live search was started, so the fixture is fake and the component and stylesheet are the real ones. **Before** is `main` at `bebd64e9`; **after** is this branch at `4668ff93`. Same fixture, same viewport, same session on both sides. ### 中文 **运行卡片与任务面板。** 前：卡片上挂着 `无隔离`，概览上方还有一条橙色提示；后：两处都不再出现。风险仍然在开始前的对话框与确认里说明。 | 前（`bebd64e9`）：卡片上的 `无隔离` | 后（本 PR）：没有标记 | | --- | --- | | | | **步骤记录。** 前：正文整段摊在会话里；后：收成一行，点开才显示正文，正文相对卡片有内边距。 | 前（`bebd64e9`）：正文整段展开 | 后（本 PR）：折叠成一行 | 后（本 PR）：展开 | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | ### English **The run card and the task panel.** Before, the card carried `No sandbox` and the overview had a warning line above it; after, neither is drawn. The risk is still stated in the setup dialog and the confirmation before the send. | Before (`bebd64e9`): the `No sandbox` chip | After (this PR): no mark | | --- | --- | | | | **The step record.** Before, its body was printed in full; after, it folds to one line, and opening it shows the body inset from the card's edge. | Before (`bebd64e9`): the body printed inline | After (this PR): folded | After (this PR): opened | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | ## Validation - Desktop unit suite: 842 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (`apps/desktop`: `tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx`). - Typecheck: `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json` clean. - Folded styles measured in a browser rather than read off the diff: a record computes `cursor: pointer`, summary padding `0px 24px`, title `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; font-size: 12px; margin: 0px`, and the opened body `16px 24px`. The answered path was measured the same way. ## E2E user journeys - Mocked desktop journey (`apps/desktop/e2e/evolve.spec.ts`): PASS — 12 passed, 0 failed, serial (`--workers=1`). Two earlier serial runs each had one flake (`the create dialog hands the goal to the conversation as the command`, then `a missing runtime greys out the start and is installed from the details`); each passed when run alone, and the last full run was 12/12. - Real-stack journey `test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts` gains a second nudge: a design that spends its whole turn budget re-deriving the evaluator is told to start with the evaluator and candidate already in the workspace. It needs `E2E_LLM_*` or `E2E_MODEL_ID` and a real model endpoint, so it was not run here and is not claimed. ## Release Release category: release:fix (a maintainer has to apply the GitHub label; this account cannot) User impact: a finished design step folds to its header, the folded card's body is inset from the edge, and a run started without a sandbox is no longer re-marked on the run card and the task panel once it is running. Compatibility and migration: none — UI only, no API or data-format change.

## Summary

Fixes #982: a research continuation whose source session was deleted made the status route answer `404 Session not found` forever, and the desktop poll retried that terminal error every three seconds with no bound. A stale copy also kept overwriting the current conversation's error UI after a session switch.

## Change

**Backend** (`services/api/src/http/index.ts`): the continuation status route now reads the durable operation first — `getContinuation` reads the operation file and still verifies its `sourceSessionId` matches the URL, so ownership is unchanged. A deleted source no longer hides a durable terminal (`failed`/`ready`) operation. The create route (`POST`) still requires the source session.

**Desktop** (`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`): the copy-poll effect now:
- Treats a `404` as terminal: stop polling, clear the stale copy, show a localized `copyMissing`.
- Retries transient failures a bounded 5 times, then clears the copy with a localized `copyPollingFailed`.
- Binds the poll and its status to `copy.sourceSessionId`, so a session switch stops the poll and its error never overwrites the current conversation's UI; the background copy still finishes server-side and is picked up on return.

**Text** (`zh.ts` / `en.ts`): added `researchPackage.copyMissing` and `researchPackage.copyPollingFailed`, localized in both languages.

## Tests

- API: `research-package-http.test.ts` — a finished continuation stays readable after its source session is deleted, and a mismatched source id answers 404.
- Desktop: the copy poll's state machine is extracted to `copyPollStep` and covered by `research-package-copy-poll.test.ts` (404 → `copyMissing`, fifth transient failure → `copyPollingFailed`, success keeps polling). The session-switch ownership is applied in the view (poll bound to `copy.sourceSessionId`).

The desktop app could turn scientific memory on, but there was nothing to do with it: a final report's `[evidence1]` and `[artifact1]` references rendered as literal brackets, and the graph had no surface a reader could reach from the report they were reading. This change makes those references citations the reader can follow, and keeps the one remaining memory surface — the switch — where the reader can act on it. ## A report's citations become chips The alias → node map is persisted on the report version (`references`), and the Markdown reader turns a token only when that map answers for it. `[note]`, an unknown alias, and every report written before the back-fill render as the plain text they are. The transform runs on the mdast tree rather than on rendered text: a chip is a link node carrying `graph://`, so it survives emphasis and line breaks inside a sentence, and the `a` renderer turns it into a button. `urlTransform` lets `graph://` through and still applies the default safety transform to every other URL. Chips travel with the run stream too. The server back-fills `references` onto the persisted message right before `run.completed`, so a live answer and its replay show the same chips instead of the replay falling back to text. ## An artifact citation opens the document, not a record about it An artifact chip opens `ArtifactDialog` over the report: the version the citation pins (not the newest one), with its own picker, and a 溯源 tab. An evidence chip opens the node's own fields — type, locator, confidence, source, recorded time — plus a 溯源 tab with the linear walk the graph recorded: the evidence, the paper or record it came from, the skill that read it, the session that ran it. Neither dialog is a library: closing it leaves the reader in the sentence they were reading. An 上游文件 link inside provenance opens the dependency in the panel beside the dialog instead of replacing the document under the cursor, and the dialog steps aside while the panel is showing it. Pointing the panel anywhere else ends that gesture, so the dialog never keeps an offset for a surface that no longer shows the dependency. ## Settings carries the switch and its state The header capsule polled `/api/health` on a timer whether or not memory was on. It is gone. Whether the service answers is now a line beside 启用科学记忆, read once when the switch turns on, and again only when the reader presses 重新检查. Where the graph is stored stays the memory service's own configuration — the page asks for nothing it does not show. 科学记忆 moves to 智能, after 专家. The line has two readings: 运行正常, or 连接失败. A store that has not been given its credential (a Neo4j deployment's own configuration) used to read 需要密码 here; that named a step no control in this window could take, so it now reads as any other service that is not working, and the state, label and style rule are gone. ## Reading a document twice is a render, not a second read Version bytes are cached module-side per version id, keyed by the client and session, with in-flight reads deduplicated and an LRU cap (24 MB total, 4 MB per entry) so a run of large documents cannot grow without bound. Reopening the artifact dialog, or opening a citation whose dependency is already on screen, issues no second request. The JSON and CSV previews parse once per content instead of once per paint, and `AssistantTurns` is memoised so opening a dialog does not re-parse every answer in the session. ## The memory sidecar can no longer take the stack down `scripts/start-stack.mjs` pins the sidecar's store under the app data directory (an explicit `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_DATA_DIR` still wins), derives its URL from the port this stack binds instead of inheriting a stale one, and degrades to `memoryGraph="degraded"` when the sidecar does not become healthy rather than aborting the whole start. The two behaviours that differ from `start-stack.sh`, and the way back to an existing store, are under Compatibility and migration below. ## Validation **Rebase.** While this pull request was open, `main` advanced 132 commits from `e4c206d1` to `6292b9b2` — 18 of them since the previous rebase point `947d93d0`, touching 58 files (research package, evolve, run-failure cards, MCP and workspace work). The branch was rebased twice; every commit id below is the id from the current rebase. Seven files are touched by both sides — `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`, `app/use-workspace.ts`, `text/en.ts`, `text/zh.ts`, `views/AssistantTurn.tsx`, `views/ConfirmDialog.tsx` and `tests/assistant-turn.test.tsx` — and one of them conflicted: both sides reworked the Escape handling in `ConfirmDialog`, where `main` still runs its hand-rolled `claimsEscape` keydown effect and this branch's `85285d1f` replaces the same effect with `useTopmostEscape(onDismiss)`. The resolution keeps this branch's hook, which is the commit that builds the escape stack, and `main`'s `useState` for the replacement model. Each paragraph's measurement was made on the tree that commit names before the rebase and describes the same content. On the rebased head `772769a6`: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` passes, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes, the desktop unit suite passes 959/959 (`# pass 959`, `# fail 0`, `# skipped 0`), and `pnpm ci:l1` passes 4/4. `git range-diff` maps all 14 commits; only `85285d1f` differs, and that difference is the resolution above. Run locally on `06f8c1cc` (Linux x64), when the branch had six commits on top of `upstream/main` at `e4c206d1`, every failure attributed: | Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | UT | 6541 | 6541 | 6528 | 13 | | ST | 51 | 51 | 50 | 1 | | E2E | 133 | 133 | 127 | 6 | The UT plan grew from 6536 to 6541 with the five tests this branch adds (three for the dialog stack, two for the version in a chip's URL). The 13 UT failures are the same set this branch showed before, all host or upstream, none in this diff: - **10 — `services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts` and `source-evolve.test.ts`.** They write a CommonJS fixture under `os.tmpdir()`; this host carries an unrelated `/tmp/package.json` with `"type": "module"`, so Node parses that fixture as ESM and the child exits 1. Re-running the same tests with `TMPDIR=/var/tmp/...` passes. - **1 — `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs`, "the same harness FAILS on the pre-fix body that restored only on the happy path".** Reproduced identically on a pristine `upstream/main` worktree. - **1 — `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`, the trajectory assertion.** The same failure is present on earlier branches of this work on this host. - **1 — `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts`.** The host's `bwrap` has no `--disable-userns`. The single ST failure, `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts`, downloads the pinned CPython runtime from `github.com`, which this host cannot reach; `curl` to that release URL fails from outside the suite as well. The repository E2E layer ran in full at `06f8c1cc`: 133 planned / 133 executed / 127 passed / 6 failed / 0 skipped. Five are the same failures the layer showed at `8ca815e6`; the sixth is this worktree's own immutability guard, not a product assertion — see the table under E2E user journeys. The four repository slices (L1/UT/ST/E2E) were **not** re-run on this commit: it touches no file under `apps/web` or the launcher, and the numbers above stay attributed to `06f8c1cc`. `130c28a4` and `73a1be77` (the paper abstract, read out of its markup) changed only `apps/desktop/**`. Re-run on `73a1be77`: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` passes, the desktop unit suite passes 878/878 (`# pass 878`, `# fail 0`, `# skipped 0` — 11 of them the new `paper-abstract.test.ts`), and the desktop browser suite passes 123/123. The evidence journey's fixture now carries a real `

`-sectioned abstract plus the record's `link`; it asserts the abstract renders as its prose paragraphs, that neither a `

` tag nor a section label (`Background/purpose`, `Methods`, `Results`) reaches the page, and that the link is drawn. The four repository slices were **not** re-run on these commits either, for the same reason. `d04af32e` (a paper's title read as text, not as escaped markup) also changed only `apps/desktop/**` — found by opening the card against the live graph, whose titles carry `<i>BRCA1</i>`. On it: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` passes, the desktop unit suite passes 881/881 (`# pass 881`, `# fail 0`, `# skipped 0`, 14 of them in `paper-abstract.test.ts`), and the full desktop browser suite passes 122/123 — the one failure, `evolve.spec.ts:218` (a typed design command's confirmation detour), passes 11/11 when its spec is re-run alone, so it is timing under the full suite's parallel load; no file this commit touches is in that journey. `d21cc960` (the provenance's section reads `上游文件` / `upstream file` instead of `派生自` / `derived from`) also changed only `apps/desktop/**`. On it: typecheck passes, the desktop unit suite passes 881/881, and `scientific-memory.spec.ts` passes 9/9. The screenshots of that tab were retaken on this commit. `371e9ae3` is documentation only (`docs/en|zh/advanced-setup/science-memory-setup.md` and `docs/en|zh/reference/configuration.md`): the local store's default is now stated per entry point — `/memory-graph` under `scripts/start-stack.mjs` and the single-file launcher, `~/.science-agent/memory-graph` under `scripts/start-stack.sh` or a directly launched service — with the note that an existing store is not moved automatically. The step now reloads `/projects//sessions/`, the app's normal restore path, where a Session named by the URL wins over the "first item" default. Assertions are unchanged. This commit is a pure rebase of the one that run measured (`git range-diff` reports no patch change), and [run 42373541505](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42373541505) on it is green in full — merge-gate, L1, UT, ST, Coverage, CodeCheck, Freeze mocked E2E, and all five L2 shards including `standard-journeys` — which is the journey's result. `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` and `pnpm ci:l1` (4/4) also pass locally; the shard itself could not be run on this host, where the isolated E2E stack is terminated before it listens. `772769a6` is documentation only (`docs/en|zh/advanced-setup/science-memory-setup.md`): `` is now named `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR`, the variable `scripts/start-stack.mjs` and the single-file launcher actually read, with `SCIENCE_AGENT_DATA_DIR` described as the logged compatibility fallback — matching the configuration reference in this same pull request. `pnpm docs:lint` passes (167 files, 0 issues). ## E2E user journeys The desktop front end has its own browser suite (`apps/desktop/e2e`, every `/api/**` answered by a stateful mock, `tier:l2`). It passes 123/123 journeys on `06f8c1cc`. The rows below describe the final head `772769a6`: three of them exercise commits that landed after `06f8c1cc` — the structured abstract (`130c28a4`, `73a1be77`), the `上游文件` reading (`d21cc960`) and the `needs-password` rendering (`81715f2c`) — and each of those commits' own runs re-ran this suite, as recorded under Validation. | Journey (`scientific-memory.spec.ts`) | Expected | Actual | | --- | --- | --- | | Escape closes the card opened over a report's dialog, not the dialog under it | the card closes and the dialog stays; a second Escape closes the dialog | PASS | | a report's evidence chip opens its details and provenance | the cited node's fields and its provenance walk open over the report; a structured abstract reads as plain paragraphs with no tag or section label on screen, and the record's link is drawn | PASS | | a report's artifact chip opens the artifact itself, in a dialog over the report | the pinned version, with its own picker and 溯源 tab, opens in a dialog | PASS | | a chip press draws the dialog's frame before the version's bytes land | the frame lands first; bytes fill it when they arrive | PASS | | a provenance tab opens at its first line, not where the preview was left | the walk starts at its top | PASS | | an 上游文件 link opens the dependency beside the dialog, not in place of it | the panel shows the dependency; the dialog steps aside | PASS | | a disabled memory graph says so in the card instead of an empty story | the card names the state instead of drawing an empty walk | PASS | | a provenance hop that cannot reach the graph is an error, not an empty story | an error is reported | PASS | | the memory state reads beside the switch, and only while the switch is on | status line only while on; 重新检查 re-reads; a `needs-password` reading shows as 连接失败, never 需要密码 | PASS | The position in 设置 (智能 › 科学记忆, after 专家) and the page's own data read are covered by the desktop unit suite (`settings-pages.test.tsx`). The repository E2E layer (`pnpm ci:e2e`, a frozen plan of 133 journeys over its mocked stacks — research, standard, literature, governed) ran 133 planned / 133 executed / 127 passed / 6 failed / 0 skipped on `06f8c1cc`. This diff changes no file under `apps/web`, and the layer brings its stacks up through `scripts/start-stack.sh`, which this diff does not modify. At `06f8c1cc` no failure was in the changed surface: | Journey | Expected | Actual | Attribution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `journey-jiuwen-configuration-on-demand` | the journey runs and reports its own result | fixture exited: `Formal journey requires an immutable candidate; E2E_DIAGNOSTIC_DIRTY=1 only labels diagnostic worktree runs` — `'M .gitignore' !== ''` | the worktree this run used carries an unrelated uncommitted `.gitignore` edit (a `dist-demo/` line, not part of this branch); the journey's guard refuses to run on a dirty candidate tree, so no product assertion was evaluated | | `journey-artifact-viewer-large-screen` J309 | a paragraph in the enlarged artifact viewer keeps a ≤ 760px measure | 774px | web layout measurement; `apps/web` untouched here | | `journey-model-connect-wizard` | the connect card stays under 580px | 598.2px | same: web layout measurement | | `journey-error-diagnostics` (en, zh-CN) | `.session-bar-session` is visible after `page.goto("/")` | element not found | web shell; reproduces with an emptied runtime data directory | | `journey-prepare-environment` J3 | the managed Python base reaches `ready` | `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: micromamba setup failed)` | the pinned micromamba release is on `github.com`, which this host cannot reach | The two earlier failures this layer showed — `journey-compact-process`, one of them failing with the suite's own instruction to reset the E2E layer's data directory — were stale state in the reused `.tmp/ci-runtime` workspace; this final run used a cleaned data directory (Python envs kept) and neither reproduces. ## Screenshots Captured in the desktop app running against this machine's live control plane (the Vite front end on `:5175`, the API on `:4312`, and the real memory sidecar), 1440×900, in 中文 and English. Evidence frames come from the session **BRCA1 literature and publication trends**; artifact frames from **Adult vs Pediatric Liver Immune Pathway Comparison**, whose `out/report/top14_pathways.tsv` records a dependency on `out/fig_top14_pathways_adult_vs_pediatric.png`. **Before** is the same live stack with the front end at `e4c206d1`; **after** is this PR's head. ### 中文 **报告的引用。** 同一份报告的同一段：`e4c206d1` 上 `[evidence4]`、`[evidence5]` 是字面文字；本 PR 里它们成为可点的引用。 | 前（`e4c206d1`） | 后（本 PR） | | --- | --- | | | | **证据卡片。** 预览给出证据本身的字段（类型、定位、置信度、记录时间），溯源是图谱记录的那条线（证据 → 文献）。文献摘要按正文分段显示：来源返回的是带 `

` 小标题的 HTML，卡片只取正文（小标题是出版方的导航，不是摘要本身），并给出来源链接。 | 预览 | 溯源 | | --- | --- | | | | **产物弹窗。** 引用固定版本打开（这里是 v1，版本选择器停在引用固定的那个版本上），溯源页给出产物自己的记录：上游是哪张图、跑过的代码与执行日志。 | 预览（版本选择器停在引用固定的 v1） | 溯源 | | --- | --- | | | | **上游文件。** 依赖在弹窗旁边的面板里打开，弹窗让位，不替换读者正在读的文档。 | | **设置 › 智能 › 科学记忆。** 状态行只在开关打开时出现，`重新检查` 是读者按的那一次读取；开关关闭后状态行随开关一起消失。 | 开启，运行正常 | 开启，连接失败 | | --- | --- | | | | | 关闭：没有状态行 | | --- | | | **卡片的失败状态。** 服务未开启与服务不可达是两种说法，各自给出下一步；都不会画一条空的故事线。 | 服务未开启 | 服务不可达 | | --- | --- | | | | **设置里的位置。** `智能` 分组原本没有 `科学记忆`，本 PR 把它放在 `专家` 之后（前图停在 `专家`，后图停在 `科学记忆`）。 | 前（`e4c206d1`） | 后（本 PR） | | --- | --- | | | | ### English **A report's citations.** The same passage of the same report: on `e4c206d1`, `[evidence4]` and `[evidence5]` are literal text; here they are pressable citations. | Before (`e4c206d1`) | After (this PR) | | --- | --- | | | | **The evidence card.** Preview shows the evidence's own fields; provenance is the line the graph recorded (evidence → paper). | Preview | Provenance | | --- | --- | | | | **The artifact dialog.** A citation opens the version it pins — v1 here, and the picker stays on it — and provenance is the artifact's own record: the figure it derives from, the script that ran, its execution log. | Preview (picker on the citation's v1) | Provenance | | --- | --- | | | | **上游文件.** The dependency opens in the panel beside the dialog, which steps aside instead of replacing the document the reader was in. | | **Settings › Intelligence › Scientific memory.** The state line appears only while the switch is on, `Check again` is the reader's press rather than a timer, and turning the switch off takes the line away with it. | On, running | On, cannot connect | | --- | --- | | | | | Off: no state line | | --- | | | **The card's failure states.** Off and unreachable are different readings, each with its own next step; neither draws an empty story. | Off | Unreachable | | --- | --- | | | | **Where it lives in Settings.** The `Intelligence` group had no `Scientific memory` entry; this PR adds it after `Specialists` (the before frame sits on Specialists, the after one on Scientific memory). | Before (`e4c206d1`) | After (this PR) | | --- | --- | | | | ## Release Release category: release:feature User impact: a final report's scientific citations become pressable chips that open the cited evidence or artifact with its provenance; 设置 › 科学记忆 reports the service's state beside the switch and only while the switch is on. Compatibility and migration: reports written before the server back-fills `references`, and reports whose aliases resolve to nothing, render exactly as they did before — the citation surfaces add nothing to what is stored. Two launcher behaviours change, both in `scripts/start-stack.mjs` (the Windows/host-process entry point; `start-stack.sh` is untouched): - **The sidecar's store moves under the stack's data directory.** The `.mjs` stack now passes `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_DATA_DIR=/memory-graph` (by default `.sciencediscovery-data/memory-graph`), where it previously left the sidecar to its own default, `~/.science-agent/memory-graph`. The new default keeps the graph inside the data directory the rest of the app already owns, and an explicit `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_DATA_DIR` is still honoured verbatim. **An installation that already has a graph at the old default opens an empty one after upgrading.** To keep it, set `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_DATA_DIR` to the old path, or move `~/.science-agent/memory-graph` to `/memory-graph` before the first start. Nothing is migrated automatically, and nothing needs to be: a report's `references` still name the same node ids, so pointing the variable back at the old store restores every existing citation as it was written. - **An unhealthy memory-graph no longer aborts the stack.** The `.mjs` stack warns, stops the child, and lets the API report `memoryGraph="degraded"` on `/api/health`, which is the state the settings line and the card already show; `start-stack.sh` still calls `wait_healthy` unguarded and aborts under `set -euo pipefail`. The divergence is deliberate — scientific memory is optional and the reader toggles it, and the bash entry point is left as-is for Linux/macOS and Docker users — and it is stated in the file's header. The URL follows the same rule: when this stack starts its own sidecar the API is pointed at the port it binds (an inherited `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_URL` is ignored with a warning), and when it starts none — `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_AVAILABLE=0`, or no Python — the operator's explicit URL is kept as-is. The chip URL gained a `?v=` suffix so two versions of one artifact stay distinct. It is built and parsed in memory only; no stored field, API response or persisted report carries it.

### Checklist
- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem
After a session analysis fails (e.g. model gateway 400 / Request error / Needs attention), refreshing the page and reopening the same session keeps the user prompt and usage counters, but the failure chrome (Needs attention, request-error banner) disappears. Trajectory may still show no matching records. The session then looks idle/successful even though the run never completed.

Minimal reproduction (Journey 1 style):
1. Start a session analysis that fails before tools run (observed with MiniMax Anthropic Messages + Adaptive thinking → `Unsupported gateway parameters: reasoning_split`).
2. Confirm Request error / Needs attention is visible.
3. Refresh the browser and reopen the same session.

Observed: error UI gone; one user message remains; no duplicate submit; failure not clearly persisted in Trajectory.
Expected: failed run remains visibly failed (banner and/or Trajectory/history), so the user does not mistake the session for an idle waiting state.

Evidence from quality-bot probe: `journey1/evidence/07-after-refresh.png`, `08-trajectory-empty.png` (web UI); desktop MiniMax session retained the failure text after refresh in a later probe—please verify both front ends.

### Detailed Environment Information Description
- OS: Linux
- Product: ScienceDiscovery source build, apps/web then apps/desktop Vite
- API: `http://127.0.0.1:4320`, desktop UI `http://127.0.0.1:5174`
- Sandbox: bubblewrap ready
- Browser: Chromium on box desktop

### Additional Information
Filed from Issue Bot Journey 1 usability notes (point 2). Related functional failure may be filed separately (`reasoning_split`); this issue is specifically about **failure-state persistence / discoverability after refresh**.

### Version Information
- Commit under test: `eae2cd354a366dab3796f46c9da8fe5dd7aff11c` (`origin/main` at probe time)
- Front ends: apps/web (4320 static) and apps/desktop (Vite 5174)
