items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
## What happens

`#866` / `#868` add a Windows reserved-device-name guard to the **upload** path. The sibling user-write path, `POST /api/sessions/:id/files`, still has no such guard, so the same device names remain writable there.

- Route: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3804` (`filesMatch` handler), `body.path` resolved at `:3807`.
- `resolveWorkspaceFile` (`packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts:2225`) delegates to `assertWorkspacePath` (`:456`), which only rejects absolute paths and escapes — it knows nothing about device names.
- The result goes straight to `writeFile(target, body.content ?? "", "utf8")` at `:3811`. `sanitizeUploadFilename` (`services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts:67`), where the reserved-name guard lives, is never called on this path.

On a Windows workspace that means `{"path": "con", "content": "x"}` targets the console device (the write silently goes to the console instead of a file) and `{"path": "nul.txt", ...}` fails with a raw `EPERM` that the handler does not classify — the client sees `500 Internal server error`. That is the exact failure shape `#866` reports, on a second user-write path.

## Expected

The reserved-name rule should be a workspace invariant, not an upload-only check: `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` with `CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, or `CON .csv` should answer **400** naming the file, and nothing should be written.

## Red first

`#868`'s guard is deliberately platform-independent, so this is testable on Linux without a Windows host: current `main` accepts the name and creates a file.

Suggested test (route level, next to `WSP-004` in `services/api/src/server.test.ts`): create project + session, then

```ts
const res = await fetch(`${origin}/api/sessions/${id}/files`, {
  method: "POST", headers: { ...authorization, "content-type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ path: "CON", content: "x" }),
});
assert.equal(res.status, 400);          // currently 201
assert.match((await res.json()).error, /reserved device name/);
```

and assert the workspace listing is unchanged. Legal look-alikes (`conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `auxiliary.csv`) and `com10.csv` must keep returning 201.

## Fix direction (maintainer's call)

Two shapes work; the first is smaller:

1. Call `sanitizeUploadFilename` (or the exported predicate) on the basename of `body.path` in the `filesMatch` handler before resolving the target.
2. Move the predicate into `packages/workspace` next to `assertWorkspacePath` and call it from both write paths, so the rule cannot drift again.

Either way the guard itself is already written and tested in `#868` (`workspace-upload.ts`, mirrored in `services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts`); this issue is about the second entry point.

## Scope

- In: the `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` write path.
- Out: upload paths (fixed by `#868`), read paths, and the desktop client.

## Origin

Raised as finding F2 in `agent-ci-infra-bot`'s review of `#868` (`https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/868#issuecomment-6637755714`), which classed it as a follow-up rather than a blocker for that PR. Filed so the second entry point is not left behind.
items.title: [Bug]: A Windows reserved device name still writes through the session file-write endpoint

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
## Summary

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts` gives its fault injection a wall-clock budget of about `200 ms` (`200` iterations at `1 ms`). On a busy runner that budget is exhausted before the injected fault lands, the case fails with `Timed out waiting for local fault injection`, and because `UT` is one of the jobs `merge-gate` aggregates, an unrelated pull request turns red on the only required status check in this repository.

Two pull requests were hit by the same identity in two different time windows today, and the same file passes in a normal run.

## Failing identity

```text
packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts::parallel 429 callers share cooldown, drain their queue and do not retry inside one slot@linux/amd64
message: "Timed out waiting for local fault injection"
```

## Evidence

**Hit 1 — `#872`**, `UT` job `126735548839`, run [`41875320473`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41875320473), read from the job's uploaded `ut-results` artifact (`group-227/worker-1-events.jsonl`; the job log itself only carries `Run`/`Done` lines). Group summary `planned 16 / executed 16 / passed 15 / failed 1`; whole layer `planned 6279 / executed 6279 / passed 6278 / failed 1`.

**Hit 2 — `#878`**, `UT` job `126741018427`, same identity, another window.

**Control — the same file passing**, `UT` job `126822084143` (`2026-11-04T19:54:21Z`): `Run 229/555: packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts (16)` → `Done (6210ms)`, layer `{"status":"PASS","planned":6281,"passed":6281,"failed":0}`.

Neither pull request touches `packages/data-source`: `#872` changes four files under `apps/web`, `#878` changes `apps/web` only. So the failing identity is unreachable from either diff.

## Cause

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts:98-101` polls for the first of 12 concurrent callers to observe the injected fault:

```ts
// ~200 iterations × 1 ms ≈ 200 ms total
```

When the event loop is loaded (parallel `UT` workers, coverage instrumentation), `200 ms` is not enough for the fault to be observed, and the wait falls through to `assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection")`. The product behaviour is correct; the budget is what fails.

## Effect

Any pull request can be blocked by this, and a re-run only helps if the runner happens to be less loaded. Contributors cannot re-run: `POST /actions/jobs/{id}/rerun` and `POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` answer `403 Must have admin rights to Repository` to a non-member token. So the only currently available recovery is asking a maintainer.

## Options

1. **Replace the fixed budget with a deadline** (for example `waitFor` with a `10 s` timeout and a short poll interval), so a loaded runner still passes and a genuinely missing fault still fails quickly enough.
2. **Wait on the event rather than polling** — if the injection can expose a promise or an emitter, awaiting it removes the timing assumption entirely.
3. If the current budget is deliberate, document the expected runner load and treat the red as a known flake; then it should not be able to block `merge-gate` for unrelated changes.

We can prepare option 1 as a pull request if that is the preferred shape; tell us which option you want and we will follow that instead of choosing for you.
items.title: [Bug] UT flake: source-health.test.ts waits only ~200 ms for the injected fault, so a busy runner fails "Timed out waiting for local fault injection"

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## What happens

The `UT` job fails intermittently with one test short of the plan, always in the same place:

```
- ut: status FAIL
- ut: passed 6939 of 6940 planned
- ut: 1 failed
- ut: NODE_WORKER_FAILED: worker-1
- ut: NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED: services/api/src/server.test.ts
- ut: FAIL: services/api/src/server.test.ts::updating SSH credentials immediately probes with the newly stored username and password@linux/amd64
```

`services/api/src/server.test.ts` has already logged `Done 512/605: services/api/src/server.test.ts (180712ms)` earlier in the same run, so the failure is not at an assertion in the test body: it is the file's teardown.

## Occurrences

Four times in one afternoon, on three unrelated PRs, every one of them a different head:

| PR | run | attempt | UT job | named test | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #999 | [42487399804](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42487399804) (merge queue) | 1 | [128752365509](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42487399804/job/128752365509) | `Workspace HTTP writes wait for the active writer and publish refs before returning` | 6909/6910 |
| #734 | [42482149231](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42482149231) | 1 | [128736356154](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42482149231/job/128736356154) | `updating SSH credentials immediately probes with the newly stored username and password` | 6939/6940 |
| #1004 | [42485316924](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42485316924) | 1 | [128745961451](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42485316924/job/128745961451) | `Workspace HTTP writes wait for the active writer and publish refs before returning` | 6906/6907 |
| #999 | [42503143754](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42503143754) (merge queue) | 1 | [128800209585](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42503143754/job/128800209585) | `updating SSH credentials immediately probes with the newly stored username and password` | 6935/6936 |

`#734` attempt 2 and `#1004` attempt 2, on the same commits, passed. Two of the four blocked the merge queue (`merge-gate` goes red as collateral), so each one costs a queue round-trip plus a nine-minute payload/CI re-run.

## Why this is the harness, not the PR under test

- `NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED` is emitted only for a `test:fail` event that carries no per-test token — a file-scope hook or a collection failure, by construction: `test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs:128`.
- `NODE_WORKER_FAILED: worker-1` means the `node --test` worker process for that file exited non-zero: `test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs:195`. So the process died, and the "1 failed" test is the plan's attribution of that, not a failed expectation.
- The named test changes between runs while the file is byte-identical, which a genuine assertion failure in one specific case would not do.
- The four runs span three PRs whose diffs never touch `services/api/src/server.test.ts`, the SSH credential path or the workspace writer path: #734 is configuration capabilities, #1004 is shell-execution settlement, #999 is desktop/API export saving.
- Every occurrence passes on a plain re-run of the same commit.

## Suggested fix

- `server.test.ts` registers many teardown hooks as `context.after(() => new Promise((resolve) => server.close(() => resolve())))` (`:868`, `:872`, `:2578`, `:2582`, `:1933`, ...). `server.close()`'s callback does not fire while an idle keep-alive client socket is still open, so such a hook can hang and take the worker down with it. The file already has the shared `closeApiServer()` helper (`:152`, `:160`) that the rest of the file uses; those hooks should use it too, or pair each `close()` with `closeAllConnections()` the way `:591` does for the adapter.
- The two named tests both start a probe against a stub server. Ending that probe explicitly in the test's own `after` hook, and awaiting it, removes the most likely lingering handle.
- Give the hooks a timeout so a stuck teardown reports the hook and the file by name, instead of surfacing as a worker exit with no reason attached.
- Complementary: have the coordinator include the worker's exit code and signal in the `NODE_WORKER_FAILED` annotation. Right now the only thing a reader gets is `worker-1`, which is what makes every occurrence cost a manual log dig.

Reported from PR review triage; not tied to any single PR.
items.title: [Bug] UT flakes at server.test.ts teardown: NODE_WORKER_FAILED worker-1 + NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED, 1 of ~6900 failed

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## What happens

The `Binary release (x86_64)` job fails at the very last step, after the artifact is built successfully:

```
Built /home/runner/work/sciencediscovery/sciencediscovery/dist/binary-release/ScienceDiscovery-d255bc9-linux-x86_64 (696.9 MiB, payload f381e6e7b55448e4f127d6fef344dc30)
Release artifact leaks a build-machine path: /home/runner
```

Two occurrences today, both in merge-queue runs for a PR that does not touch packaging (PR #999, which changes `apps/desktop` + `services/api` export saving):

| run | head | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [42491940459](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42491940459) | `fa9878e` | failed, same line |
| [42503143754](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42503143754) | `1c585656` | failed, same line |

The same job passed minutes earlier and later on sibling queue runs ([42505053918](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42505053918) for #1004, [42496441065](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42496441065) for #992), so it is intermittent rather than tied to a head.

Both times the payload scan before it passed: `Payload scan: no build-machine paths found.`

## Why this looks like the gate's own false positive

The gate is `assert_no_release_build_paths()` in `scripts/package-binary-release.sh:94-112`. It greps the whole single-file artifact for `$repository_root`, `$output_dir`, `$HOME` and `$USERPROFILE`. On a GitHub-hosted runner `$HOME` is `/home/runner`.

The payload inside that artifact has already been checked by `assert_no_build_paths()` in `scripts/binary-release/build-payload.sh:144-191`, which deliberately allows two things the artifact-level check cannot:

1. For the `$HOME` needle it excludes `jiuwenswarm/` and `adapter/` (that dependency closure legitimately mentions `/home/runner`).
2. It passes two supplier SBOMs through `scripts/binary-release/filter-upstream-sbom-paths.mjs`, because `pydantic_core-*.dist-info/sboms/pydantic-core.cyclonedx.json` and `watchfiles-*.dist-info/sboms/watchfiles_rust_notify.cyclonedx.json` carry upstream references of the form `path+file:///home/runner/work/pydantic/...` and `path+file:///home/runner/work/watchfiles/...`.

So the payload scan passing tells us the only `/home/runner` occurrences in the payload are the ones it has already ruled acceptable. The artifact-level scan then re-checks those same bytes with no allowance and no way to exclude a subtree, and the only needle that can match is the generic `$HOME` — a bare `/home/runner`, not this build's repository root.

Intermittency fits the layout: the artifact is the pinned `node` binary plus an injected SEA blob plus a `tar | zstd` payload plus a 48-byte footer (`scripts/binary-release/build-binary.mjs:232-262`), so the approved SBOM bytes only appear verbatim when zstd emits that region as a stored block.

## Impact

It blocks the merge queue for PRs that never touch packaging, and each occurrence costs a full payload build (about 9 minutes) plus a queue round-trip. #999 has been kicked out twice today; `merge-gate` goes red as collateral.

## Suggested fix

- Keep the artifact-level check for the build-specific needles only (`$repository_root`, `$output_dir`) — a match there cannot be an upstream coincidence — and drop `$HOME`/`$USERPROFILE` from it, since `build-payload.sh` already covers those with the allowances that a single compressed blob cannot apply.
- Or run the artifact-level check against the decompressed payload (the `--keep-payload` tree) so the SBOM filter can apply to it as well.
- Worth a case in the existing `scripts/binary-release/*.test.mjs` suite: a payload whose only `/home/runner` hits are the two approved SBOM references must pass both checks.

To confirm locally: build with `--keep-payload` and grep the payload tree for `/home/runner`; the hits should be exactly those two SBOMs plus anything under `jiuwenswarm/` or `adapter/`.

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 17fa595af9c94fc1b2bb977b4a4c9101
Branch: dev2/fix/specialist-client-errors
Base: 2908e9e8bb4f
At: 2026-11-05T14:14:26Z

## What happens

The Specialist settings surface turns ordinary client mistakes into a bare internal error. Saving a Specialist whose name is already taken, editing or deleting a Specialist that no longer exists, and editing a built-in Specialist all answer `500`:

```
POST /api/specialists {"name":"duplicate-name subject","description":"d","instructions":"i","connectorIds":[],"enabledSkillIds":[]}
  first call   → 201 {"name":"duplicate-name subject","id":"9c1f45d8-…"}
  second call  → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}

PUT    /api/specialists/nope                    → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
DELETE /api/specialists/nope                    → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
PUT    /api/specialists/assessment-screener {"name":"assessment-screener renamed"}
                                                → 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}   (built-in, read-only)
```

The same settings area already answers these shapes correctly on the neighbouring MCP-servers surface:

```
POST /api/mcp/servers {"name":"dup mcp","transport":"stdio","command":"echo","args":[]}
  first call   → 201
  second call  → 400 {"error":"A server with this name already exists"}
DELETE /api/mcp/servers/custom-000000000000     → 404 {"error":"MCP server not found"}
```

Other resource routes answer `404` for an unknown id as well (`GET/PUT/DELETE /api/models/nope`, `/api/providers/nope`, `/api/proxy/servers/nope`, `/api/projects/nope`, `/api/permission-grants/nope`), so the Specialist routes are the outlier, not the norm.

The user sees the generic text: `apps/web/src/Orchestration.tsx:262` (create/update) and `:275` (delete) hand the API message to `onError`, and `apps/web/src/api/auth.ts:26-36` (`ApiRequestError`) carries the server's `error` body verbatim — so the Specialist pane prints "Internal server error" where the store already knows the reason.

## What is expected

- a taken name → `400 {"error":"Specialist name already exists"}` (the message the store already produces);
- an unknown id on `PUT`/`DELETE` → `404 {"error":"Specialist not found"}`;
- an edit of a built-in Specialist → `400 {"error":"Built-in specialists are read-only; only their enabled flag can be toggled"}`.

## Where it comes from

- The routes: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1827-1843` — `POST /api/specialists`, `PUT|DELETE /api/specialists/:id` call the store with no error mapping at all.
- The throws they forward: `services/api/src/store.ts:4347` and `:4378` (`Specialist name already exists`), `:4358` and `:4387` (`Specialist not found`), `:4364` (`Built-in specialists are read-only; only their enabled flag can be toggled`).
- Why that becomes a 500: `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:23-32` recognises only `is required`, `must`, `contains an unknown value`, `cannot`, `does not match`, `invalid`, `unsafe … (archive|package|path)`, `plain basename`. None of the four messages above matches, so `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3938-3946` falls through to `500 "Internal server error"`.
- The shape the sibling surface uses: `services/api/src/http/custom-mcp.ts:87-90` — one `catch` that answers `404` for its not-found message and `400` with the store's message for everything else.

## Failing test (reproduce before the fix)

Any harness that starts the real API server works; the probe below reuses the isolated fixture style of `services/api/src/configuration/http.integration.test.ts` (temp data dir, stub Runner, `createApiServer`, `offlineMcpTransport`), creates one Specialist, then checks the four rejected shapes. Temporary probe file, not committed:

```ts
// services/api/src/configuration/zz-specialist-conflict-probe.test.ts
const specialist = { name: "duplicate-name subject", description: "d", instructions: "i", connectorIds: [], enabledSkillIds: [] };
await call("POST", "/api/specialists", specialist);
await check("duplicate name", "POST", "/api/specialists", specialist, 400);
await check("unknown PUT", "PUT", "/api/specialists/nope", { x: 1 }, 404);
await check("unknown DELETE", "DELETE", "/api/specialists/nope", undefined, 404);
await check("built-in edit", "PUT", "/api/specialists/assessment-screener", { name: "assessment-screener renamed" }, 400);
assert.deepEqual(failures, []);
```

Command and observed output:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/configuration/zz-specialist-conflict-probe.test.ts
not ok 1
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

    + [
    +   'duplicate name: expected 400, got 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}',
    +   'unknown PUT: expected 404, got 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}',
    +   'unknown DELETE: expected 404, got 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}',
    +   'built-in edit: expected 400, got 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}'
    + ]
    - []

# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

## Environment

- `main` @ `2908e9e8bb4f400eb8ad5fde0d7bd50225214349` (2026-11-05T13:01:38Z)
- node `v22`; from `services/api`: `node --import tsx --test src/<file>`
- the fixture's built-in Specialists come from the default catalog (`assessment-screener`, `code-engineer`, `creative-material-design`); no network, no model call.

## Smallest mergeable slice

One source block, one test file:

1. `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1827-1843` — wrap the three Specialist handlers in the same `try { … } catch` shape `custom-mcp.ts:87-90` already uses: `sendError(response, message === "Specialist not found" ? 404 : 400, message)` with a fallback message when the thrown value is not an `Error`. Keep the store's wording; do not reword any throw.
2. A route test (`services/api/src/specialists-http.test.ts`, or the existing HTTP test file the fixture lives in) pinning the four checks above plus the two that must not regress: toggling `enabled` on a built-in Specialists still answers `200`, and a genuinely internal failure still answers `500`.

Do not touch `services/api/src/store.ts` (its messages are right), do not add a pattern to `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` (that file is held by the in-flight length-rejection fix), and do not touch `apps/web` (the client already shows whatever the server says).

## Acceptance

- Duplicate name → `400` with `Specialist name already exists`; the first create still answers `201`.
- Unknown id on `PUT` → `404 Specialist not found`; on `DELETE` → `404 Specialist not found`.
- Editing a built-in Specialist's `name`/`description`/`instructions`/`connectorIds`/`enabledSkillIds`/`runtime` → `400` with its read-only message; `PUT {"enabled":false}` on a built-in still answers `200` and flips the flag.
- Deleting a built-in still answers `400 Built-in specialists cannot be deleted` (unchanged — it matches the classifier's `cannot` rule today; the route catch must preserve it).
- A real internal failure in the same block still surfaces as `500`: the catch keys on the not-found message and passes everything else through as `400` **only** for store validation, so the test must include at least one 500 case (e.g. a stubbed store method throwing an unexpected error) to prove the route did not turn every fault into a client error.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- Checked every open pull request's file list (`GET /search/issues?q=repo:openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery+is:pr+is:open`, 70 open, then `GET /pulls/<n>/files` for each): no open PR touches the Specialist handlers in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`; `#931` also edits that file but in the model-deletion routes, far from `:1827-1843`.
- Issue search for `specialist 500`, `already exists specialist`, `specialist name unique`, `duplicate specialist` returns no issue about rejected Specialist input answering 500.
- The in-flight length-rejection fix (`#930`) covers a different validator via the shared classifier; this one is route-level on a surface whose sibling already behaves this way, so the two fixes do not overlap.

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
## Problem

The in-flight length-rejection fix (`#932`) adds `/\bis too long\b/i` to `isKnownClientInputError` (`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:30`). Any message containing that phrase is then answered `400` **and the message text is sent back to the client**.

Two messages in the tree match that pattern and embed a filesystem path, while the client does not need that path to understand the rejection:

- `packages/executor/src/runner-bundle.ts:76` and `:80` — `` `Runner bundle path is too long for tar: ${file.path}` ``
- `packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts:777` — `` `The remote data directory path is too long for a Unix socket: ${prepared.dataDir}` ``

Before `#932` both answered `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` and the text stayed hidden. After it they answer `400` with the path in the body.

## Severity

Low, not a gate: the caller is already authenticated, the path has to be pathological (long enough to trip the length check), and it cannot be produced on demand. Reported by Security while reviewing `#932` at `8b4c124caf`.

## Suggested fix

Anchor the pattern to the end of the message:

```diff
-/\bis too long\b/i
+/\bis too long$/i
```

Every message the fix intends to reclassify ends with the phrase, so the anchor keeps them all and drops the executor ones. The eight legitimate ones are:

- `The LLM API token is too long`
- `The proxy URL is too long`
- `neo4jHttp is too long`
- `neo4jUser is too long`
- `The Neo4j password is too long`
- `Model ID is too long`
- `The stored runnerToken is too long`
- `pip indexUrl is too long` (`packages/schema/src/environment.ts:393`; added after Security's review of the first draft of this issue, which listed only seven)

## Acceptance

1. A unit test pins that the two executor messages above are **not** client input (a negative assertion): they must not become `400`-with-text.
2. All eight length messages listed above still answer `400` with their text. Pin them by name rather than by count, so a future narrowing of the pattern cannot silently drop one.
3. No change to the `500` path for anything else.

## Not for the current sprint window

`#932` must not be re-tipped for this: pushing a new tip dismisses the approval already recorded on it. This issue is the follow-up and is intentionally parked until after the window.
items.title: [Bug]: the "is too long" client-error pattern also matches two executor messages that carry filesystem paths

items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
## Problem

`POST /api/settings/web` answers a generic `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` for six shapes that are plainly the client's mistake. `normalizeWebSettings` (`services/api/src/store/settings.ts`) throws a bare `Error` for each of them, so the chain in `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3930-3936` falls through to the catch-all instead of the 400 it gives other validation failures.

| Input | Throw site | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `{"deepseekEnabled": "yes"}` | `store/settings.ts:374` | `deepseekEnabled must be a boolean` |
| `{"paidSearchProviders": ["bogus"]}` | `:384` | `paidSearchProviders must list supported paid search providers` |
| `{"freeSearchEngines": {"brave": "yes"}}` | `:396` | `freeSearchEngines.<engine> must be a boolean` |
| `{"searchCacheTtlSeconds": 1e9}` | `:403` | `<field> must be an integer between 0 and …` |
| `{"freeSearchEngines": {"nope": true}}` | `:392` | `Unknown free search engine: nope` |
| non-object body (`[]`, `"x"`, `null`) | `:370` | `Web settings must be an object` |

Impact: a client that retries on 5xx retries a request that can never succeed, while the message it needs is already in the response body. This is the same class of defect `#923` fixed for the unknown-key case one line above.

## Origin

Review comment on `#929` (`sciencediscovery-bot`, 2026-11-05T13:55:59Z, `store/settings.ts:374`) — recorded here as a follow-up so `#929` stays scoped to `#923`.

## Suggested fix

Give every throw in `normalizeWebSettings` the same `code: "INVALID_WEB_SETTINGS"` the unknown-key path already carries (message text unchanged), then let the existing route mapping answer 400. A small helper keeps it one line per throw.

## Acceptance

1. For each of the six shapes above: a test that asserts `400`, not `500`, with the message text preserved.
2. Negative assertions: `Catalog database is not initialized` and a genuine internal fault still answer `500`.
3. No change to any message wording; no change outside `normalizeWebSettings` and the route mapping.

items.body: ## English ### Checklist - [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help. - [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version. ### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem The evolution run does not stop when the given goal has already been met. Once a candidate's score reaches `1.0` (goal achieved), the search keeps expanding new nodes until the expansion budget is exhausted. Observed, from the evolution tree in the web UI: - Header: `扩展次数 23/24`, `深度 5`, `Token 608361` - Nodes `#1`, `#15`, `#18` all scored `1.000`, and `#15` is marked as the current best - After `#15` reached `1.000`, the run still produced and expanded `#16`–`#23` (several of them `没跑起来`) - The best-score curve keeps adding points after the line reaches `1.0` - The run terminates at the expansion cap (`23/24`), not because the target was solved ### Expected When any node reaches the goal (score `1.0`, i.e. at or above the solved threshold), the whole evolution tree should stop: - no further expansions are scheduled, neither from the winning branch nor from any other branch - the run ends with a solved / target-reached stop reason instead of the expansion cap - the tree is left as it is at that point ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Start an evolution run whose goal can be fully satisfied (target score `1.0`). 2. Let any candidate reach `1.0`. 3. Watch the evolution tree panel. Actual: new nodes keep being expanded after a `1.0` candidate exists, and the run only ends at the expansion budget. ### Additional Context - The scorecard already carries a `solvedThreshold` (`SOLVED_THRESHOLD_BY_SCORING` in `@sciencediscovery/schema`) and `search_finished` carries a `stopReason`, so the search is expected to end on the solved condition rather than only on the cap. - In this run three nodes reached `1.000`, yet the stop reason was the expansion cap. - I can provide the run event log (`seeded` / `expanded` / `search_finished`) if needed. ### Detailed Environment Information - Web UI, evolution tree view, Chromium on Windows 11 - Repository `main` @ `face1d40` (2026-11-06) - Run settings: expansion budget `24`, depth `5`, token usage `608361` ### Additional Information Screenshot of the evolution tree and the candidate list is attached below. ### Version Information `main` @ `face1d40` (2026-11-06); reproduced on the current web build. --- ## 中文 ### 检查项 - [x] 已搜索相关 issue，未找到有效帮助。 - [x] 该问题在最新版本中仍未修复。 ### 问题详细描述 进化功能在完成给定目标后不会主动停止。当某个候选节点的分数达到 `1.0`（即目标已达成）后，搜索仍会继续扩展新节点，直到扩展次数预算耗尽。 实际表现（来自 Web 端进化树）： - 顶部统计：`扩展次数 23/24`、`深度 5`、`Token 608361` - 节点 `#1`、`#15`、`#18` 均为 `1.000`，`#15` 被标记为当前最优 - `#15` 达到 `1.000` 后，仍继续生成并扩展 `#16`–`#23`（其中多个为“没跑起来”） - 最优分数曲线在达到 `1.0` 之后仍继续产生新点 - 运行以扩展次数上限（`23/24`）结束，而不是因为目标已达成 ### 预期结果 当任一节点达到目标（分数 `1.0`，达到或超过 solved 阈值）时，整棵进化树应全部停止： - 无论最优分支还是其他分支，都不再产生新的扩展 - 运行应以“已解决 / 目标达成”结束，而不是以扩展次数上限结束 - 树保持当时的状态不再变化 ### 复现步骤 1. 启动一个目标可完全满足（目标分数 `1.0`）的进化任务。 2. 等待任一候选节点达到 `1.0`。 3. 观察进化树面板。 实际结果：已存在 `1.0` 节点后仍继续扩展新节点，运行只在扩展预算耗尽时结束。 ### 补充信息 - 评分卡已带 `solvedThreshold`（`@sciencediscovery/schema` 中的 `SOLVED_THRESHOLD_BY_SCORING`），`search_finished` 也带 `stopReason`，说明搜索本应在 solved 条件上结束。 - 本次运行中有三个节点达到 `1.000`，但停止原因仍是扩展上限。 - 如需要，我可以提供运行事件日志（`seeded` / `expanded` / `search_finished`）。 ### 环境信息 - Web 界面，进化树视图，Windows 11 + Chromium - 仓库 `main` @ `face1d40`（2026-11-06） - 运行配置：扩展预算 `24`，深度 `5`，Token `608361` ### 其他补充 进化树与候选流水截图见下方 ### 版本信息 `main` @ `face1d40`（2026-11-06）；在最新 Web 构建上复现。

items.author: zhaochen39
items.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

The CI today is a cumulative gate model: PRs run L1/L2, the merge group runs L3, the nightly runs L4 and a release runs L5 (see the header comment of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). As the suite grows, three engineering capabilities have to be built in step:

1. **Test coverage**: the Coverage job merges only the UT and ST layers, the mocked browser E2E is not measured, and no gate reads the published coverage as an admission threshold.
2. **CI stability**: real-model E2E (L3/L4/L5) depends on external services and credentials, and occasional failures have no systematic mechanism for flake identification, isolation and tracking.
3. **Release CI efficiency**: the L5 release pipeline has no end-to-end budget of <5 hours, and the bulk data downloads (the ~1.5 GB JiuwenSwarm install, dependencies, datasets) happen again on every run.

Related files:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the L1–L5 pipeline: policy / ut / st / coverage / e2e-plan / real-e2e jobs)
- `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml` (real E2E; `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` inputs)
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (the L5 release)
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` (the case catalog and profile selection)
- `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`, `.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`, `.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs` (policy and result summaries)
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs` (coverage merge and summary)

## Design Ideas

### 1. Test coverage

**Baseline** — the `releases/v0.3.0.beta` line, authoritative run at `6d3c49a`:

| metric | whole repo | Node | Python |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| lines | 73.11% (105840/144777) | 73.19% | 72.08% |
| branches | 63.59% (39639/62335) | 63.85% | 59.63% |
| functions | 81.43% (7208/8852) | 81.43% | — |

- Weakest modules by line coverage: `idea-tree` 45.61%, `schema` 51.84%, `web` 56.14%, `scripts` 63.49%, `artifact-json` 63.16%, `specialist` 68.51%, `gateway` 68.40%.
- Cases: 3934 tagged — UT 3694/3806, ST 2/4, E2E 69/124; real-model 0/16, LLM judge 0/8, external 0/89, legacy 0/42.

**Gaps**

- Coverage is display-only: no gate reads it, and the `external` / `real` / `llm` classes are permanently 0.

**Plan**

1. Gate on industry health lines rather than the current 73%:

| metric | healthy | excellent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lines | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| branches | ≥70% | ≥85% |
| functions (Node) | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| statements | ≥80% | — |
| new / changed code (diff on a PR) | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| core paths (auth, sandbox execution, gateway, API routes) | ≥90% | ≥95% |
| per-package floor | ≥60% | — |

2. Land it in that order: diff coverage is enforced immediately (new code meets the line, existing code is not blocked), and the whole-repo figure ratchets upward and may never fall.

3. Starting gap: lines 73.11% (−6.89pt), branches 63.59% (−6.41pt), functions 81.43% (already passing). Four packages sit below the 60% floor — `idea-tree` 45.61%, `schema` 51.84%, `web` 56.14%, `services/runner` 0% — and each gets its own raise target.

4. Case-level coverage, not just a case count: a profile is the gate tier a run resolves to (`pr` / `merge` / `daily` / `release`), and `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` states which tag combinations each one selects. Today the 16 real-model, 8 LLM-judge and 89 external cases are selected by no profile at all, so they never run and read 0 forever; every case must either be selected by a profile or explicitly marked out of scope in the tag catalog, so the omission surfaces at review time.

5. Tie cases to modules: the tagged catalog carries the case-to-module mapping, so a new module without an executing case fails the gate, and `planned / executed / passed` remains the execution view beside it.

**Cases no profile can ever select.** `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` defines every profile as one of five rules (L1/L2 hermetic, L3/L4/L5 real), so a tag combination outside those rules never runs. On the `main` catalog (359 cases), 45 are permanently dead:

| tag shape | why no rule matches | cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status:legacy` | hermetic accepts only `reviewed`; real only `reviewed` / `external` | 42 |
| `status:quarantined` | same, with no path back in | 1 |
| `category:st` + `model:real` | the real rule is pinned to `category:e2e` | 1 |
| `npu:required` | all five rules require `npu:none` | 1 |

Four more shapes are structurally dead and simply have no case yet: `os:macos` / `os:windows`, `arch:arm64` outside real e2e, `judge:llm` combined with `model:none` / `mock`, and any case missing a `tier` tag — the old release-line catalog has no tier dimension, so under today's policy it would match nothing at all.

A further 131 cases read 0 without being dead: 61 UT and 70 real e2e do run, but the `ut` and `e2e-real` slice catalogs are never uploaded (`slices` registers only `e2e` and `st`), so their execution cannot be attributed.

- Fix the 45: delete or migrate the 42 `legacy` cases, give `quarantined` an exit, retag `st` + `real` as `e2e` or mark it out of scope, and open a separate NPU tier or declare it unsupported.
- Reachability check in the catalog check (`ci:catalog:check`, reusing the rule union exported by `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs`): a case whose tags match no profile fails catalog generation, so a dead case is caught at review time instead of reading 0 for months.

### 2. CI stability

- Automatic failure classification: product defect / environment / external dependency / test flake.
- Flake governance: when a case's failure rate over its last N runs crosses a threshold, mark it quarantined automatically — it keeps running and recording results, but its failure no longer blocks merges, and a tracking issue is opened for the owner. It leaves quarantine once it passes N consecutive runs, so a flaky case neither freezes the queue nor silently disappears.
- No blanket retry. A case is rerun only when its failure is attributable to network jitter or an unstable gateway / upstream — connect and read timeouts, connection resets, DNS failures, HTTP 429/5xx, interrupted streams. Every other failure, including a flaky real-model case, is reported as it happened and handled by the classification and quarantine above. A retry is labelled as an infrastructure retry, its count is visible per case, and sustained gateway failures beyond the retry budget are reported as an infrastructure incident rather than a test failure.
- Explore disabling the model's thinking mode, or setting the reasoning effort to its lowest level: much of the flakiness of the real-model cases comes from the randomness of the reasoning path; disabling or minimizing thinking narrows the output variance, makes the results more reproducible, and shortens per-case inference time (an efficiency win as well). The conclusion has to be backed by an A/B experiment — run both configurations N times each, compare pass rates and failure variance; if the pass rate does not regress beyond the accepted bound, fix it as a CI-only inference configuration applied to the L3/L4/L5 journeys only, leaving the product default untouched.

### 3. Release CI efficiency (<5h)

- Give the L5 pipeline a 5-hour end-to-end budget, add a timing view of actual per-job duration against that budget, and alert automatically when it is exceeded.
- Compress duration through caching (pnpm / uv / JiuwenSwarm are cached already), parallel test sharding (the mocked E2E matrix exists; extend it to UT/ST), and trimming redundant layers from the release profile.
- Run the real-model journeys at the lowest thinking effort: thinking off, or reasoning effort at its minimum, for L3/L4/L5 — reasoning tokens are the dominant cost of a case, so this shortens per-case latency directly. It is the same A/B switch as the stability item; here it is measured as p50/p95 duration per case against the 5-hour budget and fixed once the pass rate shows no regression.
- Data-download optimization: inventory the bulk downloads in the pipeline (the ~1.5 GB JiuwenSwarm install with its virtualenv, pnpm / uv dependencies, test datasets and fixtures, model and sidecar data, Docker images, and the base images of the release binaries) and eliminate the repeated ones item by item — pre-download into `actions/cache`, use an internal mirror / CDN, prefetch in parallel with the build steps, and key the cache on lockfiles / content hashes. Track download time separately in the budget view; a rerun with a cache hit must not download the bulk again.
- Produce an L5 duration baseline report marking the top-N slowest jobs and the optimization suggestions (including the share of download time).

## Involved Public APIs

No new or changed product public APIs; all of this is CI-internal capability.

- Reuse the existing CI-internal interfaces: `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list --profile ... --slice ...` (case selection), the `.ci-results` directory layout, and the `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` inputs of `real-e2e.yml`.
- The new outputs (coverage report and duration baseline report) are uploaded as artifacts, following the existing artifact naming convention (e.g. `node-coverage-summary-${scope}-${sha}`).

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `.ci/` scripts: the policy, matrix and summary scripts are extended to emit coverage and timing data.
- `test/support/tagged`: the case catalog gains coverage-ownership and flake-marker fields.
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`: a wider merge scope and a new output format.
- `release.yml`: the L5 budget check hooks into the existing `workflow_call` chain.
- No product code changes (apps/*, services/*); the model thinking-mode configuration is injected through the CI / E2E harness only and does not touch product defaults.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Coverage**: with a change of a known coverage delta, verify that the PR comment and the threshold block trigger correctly; verify the numbers are sound once the E2E layer is included.
- **Stability**: on a test branch, produce deterministic failures and random failures, and verify the classification, the quarantine isolation and the auto-issue flow; inject network jitter and gateway failures (timeout, connection reset, 429/5xx, interrupted stream) and verify the case is retried and, when it then passes, recorded as a pass with a visible retry count, while a product-defect failure is not retried; run the thinking-mode A/B experiment N times per arm, and verify that the failure variance narrows with no unacceptable pass-rate regression.
- **Efficiency**: take the last 3 release runs as the baseline, verify that the budget view times correctly and that the L5 end-to-end is <5 hours after the optimization; verify that the bulk data downloads take near-zero time on a cache hit; and record the per-case p50/p95 duration with thinking off or at its lowest, before and after.
- All of the above is CI behavior and automatable within L2; no new real-model cases are added (the existing L4/L5 journeys are reused).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Coverage is gated on the industry health lines: whole-repo lines ≥80%, branches ≥70%, functions ≥80% and statements ≥80%; new code ≥80% diff coverage; each package ≥60% and core paths ≥90%.
- [ ] Case-level coverage is closed: no case sits outside every profile, and every module maps to at least one case the gating profile actually executes.
- [ ] Flaky cases are identified and quarantined automatically; only failures caused by network jitter or an unstable gateway are retried, labelled as infrastructure retries and never applied to product defects; the thinking-mode (off / lowest) A/B experiment is concluded and, if viable, fixed as a CI-only inference configuration.
- [ ] The L5 release CI finishes end-to-end in <5 hours with in-pipeline over-budget alerts, every bulk download is cache/prefetch managed with no re-download on a cache hit, and the real-model journeys run at the lowest thinking effort with the latency gain recorded.

## Additional Information

- This is an engineering-effectiveness request; maintainers are invited to schedule it as the three sub-items above.

---

## 🚀 背景描述

当前 CI 采用累积门禁模型：PR 跑 L1/L2，merge_group 跑 L3，nightly 跑 L4，发布跑 L5（见 `.github/workflows/ci.yml` 头部注释）。随着用例规模增长，三个方面的工程能力需要同步建设：

1. **用例覆盖度**：Coverage 任务只合并 UT、ST 两层，mocked browser E2E 未被度量，且没有任何门禁把已发布的覆盖度作为准入阈值。
2. **CI 稳定性**：真实模型 E2E（L3/L4/L5）依赖外部服务与凭据，偶发失败缺乏系统性的抖动识别、隔离与跟踪机制。
3. **版本 CI 效率**：L5 发布流水线尚无 <5 小时的端到端时长预算约束，大额数据下载（JiuwenSwarm 安装约 1.5 GB、依赖、数据集）在每次运行中反复发生。

相关文件：

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`（L1–L5 主流水线：policy / ut / st / coverage / e2e-plan / real-e2e 等 job）
- `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`（真实 E2E；`profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` 输入）
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`（L5 发布）
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`（用例目录与 profile 选择）
- `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`、`.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`、`.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs`（策略与结果汇总）
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`、`scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`（覆盖度合并与摘要）

## 设计思路

### 1. 用例覆盖度

**基线**——取 `releases/v0.3.0.beta` 线（authoritative，SHA `6d3c49a`）：

| 指标 | 整仓 | Node | Python |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 行 | 73.11%（105840/144777） | 73.19% | 72.08% |
| 分支 | 63.59%（39639/62335） | 63.85% | 59.63% |
| 函数 | 81.43%（7208/8852） | 81.43% | — |

- 行覆盖率最弱的模块：`idea-tree` 45.61%、`schema` 51.84%、`web` 56.14%、`scripts` 63.49%、`artifact-json` 63.16%、`specialist` 68.51%、`gateway` 68.40%。
- 用例：3934 个，UT 覆盖 3694/3806、ST 2/4、E2E 69/124；真实模型 0/16、LLM judge 0/8、external 0/89、legacy 0/42。

**问题**

- 覆盖度只用于展示，没有任何门禁读取；`external` / `real` / `llm` 三类用例恒为 0。

**方案**

1. 门禁取业界健康线，而不是当前的 73%：

| 指标 | 健康线 | 优秀线 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 行覆盖 | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 分支覆盖 | ≥70% | ≥85% |
| 函数覆盖（Node） | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 语句覆盖 | ≥80% | — |
| 新增/变更代码（PR diff） | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 核心链路（认证、沙箱执行、网关、API 路由） | ≥90% | ≥95% |
| 单包下限 | ≥60% | — |

2. 按上述顺序落地：diff 覆盖立即生效（新代码按健康线走，不阻塞存量），整仓数值以棘轮方式只升不降。

3. 当前差距：行 73.11%（差 6.89pt）、分支 63.59%（差 6.41pt）、函数 81.43%（已达标）。4 个包低于 60% 下限——`idea-tree` 45.61%、`schema` 51.84%、`web` 56.14%、`services/runner` 0%——各自设定提升目标。

4. 用例维度覆盖，而不只是用例数量：profile 是一次运行解析出的门禁档位（`pr` / `merge` / `daily` / `release`），具体选中哪些 tag 组合由 `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` 定义。目前 16 个真实模型、8 个 LLM judge、89 个 external 用例不被任何 profile 选中，等于永远不跑、永远显示 0；要求每条用例要么被某个 profile 选中，要么在 tag 目录中显式标注「不在范围」，让遗漏在评审阶段就暴露。

5. 用例与模块绑定：tag 目录维护「用例 → 模块」映射，新增模块若没有可执行用例则门禁失败；`planned / executed / passed` 作为与之并列的执行视图。

**永远不会被任何 profile 选中的用例。** `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` 把每个 profile 定义为五条规则之一（L1/L2 hermetic、L3/L4/L5 real），不符合这些规则的 tag 组合永远不会被执行。以 `main` 目录（359 条）为例，45 条是彻底死用例：

| tag 形态 | 为何无规则命中 | 条数 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status:legacy` | hermetic 只收 `reviewed`，real 只收 `reviewed` / `external` | 42 |
| `status:quarantined` | 同上，且没有回到门禁的路径 | 1 |
| `category:st` + `model:real` | real 规则硬编码 `category:e2e` | 1 |
| `npu:required` | 五条规则全部要求 `npu:none` | 1 |

另有四类结构性死角，目前恰好没有对应用例：`os:macos` / `os:windows`、非 real e2e 的 `arch:arm64`、`judge:llm` 搭配 `model:none` / `mock`，以及任何缺少 `tier` 标签的用例——release 线那份旧目录没有 tier 维度，按当前策略会全部失配。

还有 131 条显示为 0 但并不属于死用例：61 条 UT 与 70 条 real e2e 实际在跑，只是 `ut` 与 `e2e-real` 两个切片的 catalog 从未上传（`slices` 只登记了 `e2e` 和 `st`），导致执行结果无法归因。

- 处置 45 条：删除或迁移 42 条 `legacy`；为 `quarantined` 补上出口；`st` + `real` 改 tag 为 `e2e` 或标注不在范围；`npu` 单独开档位或声明不支持。
- 在 catalog 校验（`ci:catalog:check`，复用 `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` 导出的规则并集）中增加可达性检查：用例 tag 若不属于任何 profile，catalog 生成即失败，让死用例在评审阶段暴露，而不是显示 0 数月。

### 2. CI 稳定性提升

- 失败自动归类：产品缺陷 / 环境 / 外部依赖 / 用例抖动（flake）。
- 抖动治理（quarantine）：同一用例近 N 次运行失败率超阈值时自动标记为隔离——它继续运行并记录结果，但失败不再阻断合并，同时自动创建跟踪 issue 派给 owner；连续 N 次通过后自动解除隔离，既不冻结合并队列，也不会让用例悄悄消失。
- 不做统一重试。仅当失败可归因于网络抖动或网关、上游不稳定（连接与读取超时、连接重置、DNS 失败、HTTP 429/5xx、流中断）时才自动重跑；其他失败——包括真实模型用例本身的抖动——如实上报，交由上面的失败归类与 quarantine 处理。重试会标注为基础设施重试，用例维度可看到次数，超出重试预算的持续性网关失败按基础设施故障上报，而不是记为用例失败。
- 探索关闭或调低模型思考模式（thinking / reasoning effort 设为最低档）：真实模型用例的抖动很大程度来自推理路径的随机性，关闭/调低思考模式可收窄输出方差、提升可复现性，同时缩短单用例推理耗时（兼具效率收益）。结论需以 A/B 实验数据支撑：对比开启 vs 关闭（或最低档）两组各 N 次运行的通过率与失败方差，若通过率无可接受退化，则固化为 CI 专用推理配置，仅作用于 L3/L4/L5 journey，不影响产品默认行为。

### 3. 版本 CI 效率提升（<5hr）

- 为 L5 流水线定义端到端时长预算 5 小时，pipeline 内增加各 job 实际耗时 vs 预算的计时看板，超预算自动告警。
- 通过缓存（pnpm / uv / JiuwenSwarm 已有）、用例分片并行（mocked E2E matrix 已具备，推广到 UT/ST）、release profile 裁剪冗余层级来压缩时长。
- 真实模型用例以最低思考强度运行：L3/L4/L5 关闭思考或把 reasoning effort 调到最低——推理 token 是单个用例的主要开销，这一步直接缩短单用例耗时。与稳定性项共用同一组 A/B 开关，这里以每条用例的 p50/p95 耗时对照 5 小时预算衡量，确认通过率无退化后固化。
- 数据下载优化：盘点流水线中的大额数据下载（JiuwenSwarm 安装约 1.5 GB 及其 virtualenv、pnpm / uv 依赖、测试数据集与 fixture、模型与 sidecar 数据、Docker 镜像、二进制基础镜像），逐项消除重复下载——预下载进 `actions/cache`、走内部镜像源 / CDN、与构建步骤并行预取、按 lockfile / 内容寻址命中缓存；下载耗时单独计时并纳入预算看板，缓存命中后的重复运行不应再产生大额下载。
- 输出 L5 耗时基线报告，标注 top-N 耗时 job 与优化建议（含下载耗时占比）。

## 涉及的公共 API

不新增、不修改产品公共 API；全部为 CI 内部能力。

- 复用现有 CI 内部接口：`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list --profile ... --slice ...`（用例选择）、`.ci-results` 结果目录格式、`real-e2e.yml` 的 `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` 输入。
- 新增产物（覆盖度报告、耗时基线报告）统一作为 artifacts 上传，遵循现有 artifact 命名约定（如 `node-coverage-summary-${scope}-${sha}`）。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `.ci/` 脚本：策略、矩阵、汇总脚本需扩展以输出覆盖度与耗时数据。
- `test/support/tagged`：用例目录需补充覆盖度归属与抖动标记字段。
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`、`scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`：扩展合并范围与输出格式。
- `release.yml`：L5 预算检查嵌入现有 `workflow_call` 链。
- 不改动产品代码（apps/*、services/*）；模型思考模式配置仅通过 CI / E2E harness 注入，不影响产品默认行为。

## 测试设计与测试计划

- **覆盖度**：构造已知覆盖变化的变更，验证 PR 评论与阈值拦截正确触发；验证 E2E 层纳入后报告数值合理。
- **稳定性**：在测试分支制造确定性失败与随机失败，验证分类、quarantine 隔离与自动建单流程；注入网络抖动与网关失败（超时、连接重置、429/5xx、流中断），验证用例被自动重试、重试后通过则记为通过且重试次数可见，而产品缺陷类失败不触发重试；思考模式 A/B 实验两组各跑 N 次，验证关闭/最低档下失败方差收窄且通过率无可接受退化。
- **效率**：以最近 3 次 release 运行作为基线，验证预算看板计时准确，优化后 L5 端到端 <5 小时；验证缓存命中后大额数据下载耗时趋近于零；记录关闭/最低思考强度前后每条用例的 p50/p95 耗时对比。
- 上述验证均为 CI 自身行为，属于 L2 可自动化校验范围；不新增真实模型用例（复用现有 L4/L5 journey）。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 覆盖度按业界健康线设门禁：整仓行 ≥80%、分支 ≥70%、函数 ≥80%、语句 ≥80%；新代码 diff 覆盖 ≥80%；单包 ≥60%、核心链路 ≥90%。
- [ ] 用例维度覆盖闭环：没有用例落在所有 profile 之外，每个模块都至少映射到一个门禁 profile 实际执行的用例。
- [ ] CI 具备抖动用例自动识别与 quarantine 机制；仅网络抖动 / 网关不稳定导致的失败自动重试，标注为基础设施重试且不适用于产品缺陷；完成模型思考模式（关闭/最低档）A/B 实验并形成结论，可行则固化为 CI 专用推理配置。
- [ ] L5 版本 CI 端到端时长 <5 小时，流水线内有超预算告警；大额数据下载全部纳入缓存/预下载管理，缓存命中后无冗余下载；真实模型用例以最低思考强度运行并记录耗时收益。

## 补充信息

- 本 issue 为工程效能类需求，建议 maintainer 按三个子项拆分任务排期。

## Overview This issue is the **v0.4.0-rc1 release** for the ScienceDiscovery community. It is intended to serve as the **pinned, single source of truth** for release milestones and community review meetings. **Key milestones** - **Nov 2:** `v0.4.0-rc1` release kickoff; confirm the requirements list and delivery milestones; - **Nov 3 & 4:** requirements review meeting; define the delivery scope and acceptance checklist for each requirement; - **Nov 5:** requirement implementation and acceptance review meeting; - **Nov 9:** requirement implementation and acceptance review meeting; create the `release/0.4.0` branch and start full verification (this branch only accepts bug fixes — no new feature code); - **Nov 11:** no new `v0.4.0-rc1` issues are added (issue freeze); - **Nov 13:** resolve all open bugs; publish the `v0.4.0-rc1` release; ## Major requirements and release scope | Requirement | Scope | Target release | | --- | --- | --- | | **Bring scientific memory, evolve, and paper reproduction to the desktop client** | • Desktop support for scientific memory Hu Yingtong [#801](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/801)
• Desktop support for evolve Hu Yingtong [#798](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/798)
• Paper reproduction Zhou Yuan / Zhao Jichen [#803](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/803) | v0.4.0-rc1 | | **Reduce first-response, install, session-switch, resource-load, and deletion latency** | • Optimize first-session response time Jiang Zhenguang [#799](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/799)
• Optimize Windows desktop installation and initialization time Jiang Zhenguang [#719](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/719)

• Optimize loading time of Skills, MCP, and Experts Hu Yingtong (no issue yet)
• Optimize time to delete projects and sessions Hu Yingtong (no issue yet) | v0.4.0-rc1 | | **Improve feedback, packaging, settings, UI consistency, and failure alerting** | • User feedback feature Zhao Yu [#844](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/844)
• Optimize installer package size Jiang Zhenguang [#808](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/808)
• Requirement analysis and breakdown for the Mac desktop app Jiang Zhenguang (no issue required)
• Enhance conversational settings Wang Yuheng [#820](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/820)

• ScienceDiscovery bot Wang Chengzhao [agent-CI-Infra/bot#122](https://github.com/agent-CI-Infra/bot/issues/122)

items.body:
## 背景

当前 ScienceDiscovery 的 Desktop 与 Web 客户端在工作区视图、对话交互、会话与产物管理、设置以及全局辅助能力方面存在一定差异。为便于评估桌面端功能补齐范围，现基于前端实现对差异进行集中梳理，并为后续需求拆分和验收提供参考。

**关联：#718**（`v0.4.0-rc1` 版本需求与发布计划）。其中“桌面端支持科学记忆、Evolve”和“评估旧 UI 功能迁移”等事项与本 Issue 直接相关。

> **说明**
> - 本文是基于当前代码和界面实现的**初步差异盘点**，并非全部条目的最终功能验收结论；具体表现仍需结合实际版本验证。
> - Desktop 并非 Web 的简单复制：它已有独立的 `SetupWizard` / `Guide` 初始化引导、`shell-bridge` 和面板组织方式。因此目标是评估并补齐关键能力，而非机械地复刻 Web UI。
> - 本 Issue 用于**集中跟踪差异与讨论优先级**；不表示所列功能均已纳入 `v0.4.0-rc1` 交付范围。建议在 #718 的评审中明确具体范围。

## 一、右侧工作区与探索视图

Web 右侧面板包含多种专项视图；Desktop 的 `WorkspacePanel` 当前主要开放 `artifacts` 和 `files` 两个 group。

| 功能 | Web 端现有能力 / 实现线索 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Evolve 进化搜索** | `evolve/*`：算法选择、搜索网格/图、候选详情、评分图表、运行卡片及轮询 | **缺失**对应专项视图 |
| **Memory Graph 记忆图** | `MemoryGraphView.tsx`、`MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx`、`MemoryGraphCanvas.tsx` 等 | 存在 API 类型声明，**缺少 UI** |
| **Idea Tree 思路树** | `IdeaTreeView.tsx`、`IdeaTreeCanvas.tsx`、`IdeaTreeExplorer.tsx` 等 | 存在 API 类型声明，**缺少 UI** |
| **CSV 可视化工作台** | `csv-artifact/*`：散点图、直方图、箱线图等 | **部分实现**：主要提供基础表格展示 |
| **执行视图** | 展示 Subagent 执行情况 | **缺少对应视图** |
| **审查专家视图** | 审查专家相关 UI | **缺少对应视图**，具体交互需进一步核对 |

## 二、对话交互与执行过程展示

| 功能 | Web 端现有能力 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **对话输入区** | 选择专家、数据连接器、权限审查模式及自动审查配置；Agent 执行期间可继续发送指令 | **部分实现**：缺少连接器与自动审查等入口，执行期间不能继续发送指令；Desktop 另外支持添加文件 |
| **思考 / 行动步骤展示** | 工具失败时可复制关键诊断信息并快捷跳转 GitHub Issue；最终答案尾部展示产物；Subagent 运行状态有更丰富的 UI | **部分缺失**，建议逐项核对并补齐交互 |
| **轨迹模式** | 提供区别于常规对话的 Agent 行动轨迹视图 | **缺失** |

## 三、会话、项目与产物管理

| 功能 | Web 端现有能力 / 实现线索 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **会话管理** | 重命名、删除、会话级设置、归档、筛选 | 缺少会话级设置、归档及筛选 |
| **项目管理** | 重命名、删除、项目级设置 | 缺少项目级设置 |
| **产物 / 文件下载** | 支持选择多个目标进行下载 | 主要支持单文件下载，批量选择能力不足 |
| **工作区文件来源** | `WorkspaceFileProvenanceModal.tsx` | 缺少文件来源查看 UI |
| **产物树 / 工作区文件树** | `artifactTree.ts` 支持产物树组织 | Desktop 有独立的 `file-tree.ts`，但主要覆盖文件列表，未提供对应的产物树结构 |

## 四、设置与能力管理

| 功能 | Web 端现有能力 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **全局默认配置** | 运行时默认值、可选扩展、连接器、Web 访问等 | 缺少对应的完整配置入口 |
| **Runner 管理** | 本地 Runner 状态、远程 Runner 添加 / 管理 | 有 `RemoteHosts` 配置，但缺少完整 Remote Jobs 面板及本地 Runner 状态展示 |
| **模型与扩展能力** | Model、MCP、Web、Memory、Idea Tree、Skill、Specialist 等 | **部分实现**：MCP 主要为内置能力，缺少自定义添加；Skill 有基础添加方式，但缺少 Web 端更完整的管理、探索及导入流程；Web、Memory、Idea Tree 等配置入口缺失 |
| **运行与资源** | 超时、配额、运行状态 | 缺少配额及运行状态等配置 / 查看入口 |
| **网络与访问** | 网络代理、沙箱网络、权限、前后端连接配置 | 主要提供沙箱网络配置，选项相对受限；部分连接设置属于 Web 架构特有能力，**不必直接迁移** |

## 五、其他全局能力

| 功能 | Desktop 现状（初步） |
| --- | --- |
| **全局搜索** | 缺少对应入口 / 能力 |
| **模型用量** | 缺少用量查看入口 / 能力 |

## 六、建议的处理方式与优先级

建议按业务价值、实现依赖及平台适配成本拆分，而非一次性迁移所有界面：

1. **优先评估版本明确提出的核心能力**：Memory Graph / 科学记忆、Evolve，以及与 #718 相关的旧 UI 迁移范围。论文复现虽在 #718 中列出，但不在本次差异表的核对范围，建议另行确认。
2. **评估影响核心使用流程的功能差异**：执行期间追加指令、执行 / 轨迹展示、工具失败诊断、产物管理及会话 / 项目设置。
3. **逐步补齐探索与管理能力**：Idea Tree、CSV 可视化、MCP / Skill 管理、用量及全局搜索等；优先级需结合需求评审确定。
4. **区分跨端通用能力与平台特有能力**：复用可共享的状态管理和组件逻辑；Desktop 已具备的初始化引导、Shell 桥接及平台特定设置应予保留。

## 七、后续待办 / 验收检查

- [ ] 逐项复核上述差异在目标分支和实际 Desktop 构建中的表现，标记“缺失 / 部分实现 / 已有替代实现 / 不适用”
- [ ] 对照 #718 确定 `v0.4.0-rc1` 的实际交付范围，避免将全部差异默认纳入 RC1
- [ ] 为确认需要补齐的功能明确负责人、依赖、实现方案及独立验收标准
- [ ] 优先验证 Memory Graph、Evolve 及核心对话 / 工作区流程
- [ ] 检查 Desktop 特有能力是否受到迁移影响，避免简单复制 Web 造成回归
- [ ] 对较大的独立功能拆分子 Issue / PR，并在此维护链接及进度

---

**预期结果**：形成可核验的 Desktop / Web 功能差异清单，并将确定需要补齐的能力转化为有优先级、有验收标准的实施任务。

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

When the model connection is reset after the model has already streamed part of its answer, the agent run fails. No layer retries it.

That is what ended three research jobs in the manual Nightly run [41852669139](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41852669139) on 2026-11-04 (branch `ci/l5-biomnibench-da`, head `b8819fc8b`, JiuwenSwarm backend, model `deepseek-flash` behind an OpenAI-compatible relay gateway).

### What failed

`research-1` (DRB-58) and `research-5` (DRB-75) both ended with:

```
run_error=[181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

The `[model-sse-summary]` lines in each job's `stack.log` (artifact `real-e2e-evidence-<shard>`) identify the request:

| Job | Request sent (UTC) | 200 headers | Connection reset | Streamed before reset | Attempts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| research-1 | 15:00:19.235 | 15:00:23.403 | **15:01:46.872** | 83 s, 848,494 bytes, text and tool calls | 1 |
| research-5 | 16:00:31.110 | 16:00:36.449 | **16:03:30.928** | 175 s, 2,791,403 bytes, text and tool calls | 1 |

`research-10` failed in the same way. Its run error reads `interaction round execution failed`, and each of its three failed runs directly follows a mid-stream reset (16:26:31.901, 16:31:37.391 and 16:49:24.951).

### The fault is external; the failure is ours

- 16 of the run's 382 requests to the gateway ended with `error.classification: network`. They came from 5 independent runners, and all of them fall between 15:01 and 16:50 UTC.
- The same gateway served 1,386 requests in the two earlier runs on this branch (03:07–06:38 and 10:09–12:50 UTC) without a single network reset.
- Streams of 176 s / 2.9 MB and 214 s / 2.8 MB completed normally in the same run, so a fixed size or duration limit is not the cause.
- 9 of the 16 resets were retried and recovered. They all came before any answer text or tool-call delta: either before the response opened, or while only reasoning had streamed. The head under test (PR #853) retries the second case.
- The other 7 happened after answer text or tool-call deltas had started. Nothing retried them. Every run failure in research-1, research-5 and research-10 follows one of these 7.

### Retry behaviour on `main` (`48848578`)

On the JiuwenSwarm backend, a model call travels Swarm → ScienceDiscovery model gateway (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`) → `packages/model/src/client.ts` → provider.

| Layer | What it retries | After the stream has started |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/model` `requestWithRetry` | Connect errors, header timeout, 429 and 5xx. Budget: `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_RETRIES=2`. Backoff: 0.5 s doubling up to 4 s, or a numeric `Retry-After`. Header timeout: `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600` | Nothing. The code says so: "Once the stream starts flowing, errors surface to the caller". `bodyTimeout: 0` also means a stalled body is never treated as lost |
| JiuwenSwarm model gateway | Nothing of its own. It holds response headers until the first answer byte, so a failure before the stream opens reaches Swarm as a real HTTP error | Forwards the error |
| Swarm's OpenAI SDK | Its built-in retries before a response arrives | Nothing |
| openJiuwen `agent_teams` `StreamController` | — | Re-drives a team member's round that failed with `181001`: up to 10 times, with a "continue" query. The main session run is not covered: research-1 and research-5 logged `run of <session> failed: [181001]` straight after the reset |
| Run | Nothing. `classifyRunFailure` maps ECONNRESET to `transport-error`, which is only displayed and recorded | — |

PR #853 adds one more retry in `streamModelTurn`: `network` and `timeout` errors are retried while `answerStarted` is still false. It cannot cover the 7 resets that came after output had started.

One safety property already holds. The gateway withholds tool-call arguments until the upstream turn finishes; in the meantime it sends empty deltas as progress. A stream cut mid-turn therefore never executes a partial tool call, so re-driving the failed turn cannot repeat a side effect. Text and reasoning deltas, on the other hand, are forwarded as they arrive. That is why the transport layer cannot replay the request transparently once text has started.

### How other agents handle a mid-stream drop

All rows except the DeepSeek API docs were read from current sources.

| Agent | Mid-stream drop | Budget and backoff | Partial output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) | Retries stream disconnects, connection failures, timeouts, 5xx and 429. A stream idle for `stream_idle_timeout_ms` (default 300000) counts as lost | `stream_max_retries` 5 and `request_max_retries` 4. Exponential backoff with jitter; server retry advice wins. After the budget runs out it falls back from WebSocket to HTTPS | Only items completed with `output_item.done` enter history. The retry re-samples from history: the partial item is dropped, completed tool calls are kept |
| [Grok Build](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build) | `StreamError` and `EventStreamError` are retried; `IdleTimeout` is not | 15 retries (`GROK_MAX_RETRIES`). 2 s doubling to 30 s, ±20% jitter. The first retry rebuilds the HTTP client; rate limits are retried once | The same request is re-sampled and the failed attempt is discarded |
| [pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) | Restarts the whole turn at the agent level, matching the error text (`terminated`, `socket hang up`, `other side closed`, `stream ended…`) | 3 retries, 2/4/8 s, capped at 60 s. Shows `Retrying (n/3)` and can be cancelled | The failed assistant message stays in the raw log but is hidden from the model; the agent continues from the previous message |
| [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) | Retries mid-stream errors, including `ECONNRESET` and `ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE` | 3 retries, 1/2/4 s. Failures before the stream opens have a separate policy (5 s up to 30 s) | Emits a `RETRY` event and resends the request |
| [DeepSeek API docs](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/rate_limit) | No agent. 500 and 503: "retry your request after a brief wait". Waiting streams receive `: keep-alive` comments, and the connection is closed if inference has not started within 10 minutes | — | No guidance on mid-stream drops |
| [DeepSeek-TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI) (third-party) | Retries only a stream that failed to open. A drop while reading the body is reported and not replayed, to avoid duplicated output | — | — |

The common pattern: retry at the turn, not at the HTTP request. Output counts only once an item or turn completes. On failure, the partial attempt is discarded and the turn is re-sampled from the last committed state, with a bounded, jittered backoff and a visible status.

## Design Ideas

1. **Re-drive the main run's failed turn on a transient transport fault.** This covers a `181001` caused by a network or stream error, or `transport-error`. Drop the failed round from the model's context and continue from the last committed round. openJiuwen already does this for team members, and pi does it for every turn. Budget 3–5 attempts with jittered exponential backoff capped at 30–60 s, honour cancellation, and show a retry status in the run timeline. Still to decide: whether this lives in the JiuwenSwarm patch set or in `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`. The native loop needs the same behaviour.
2. **Treat a stalled stream as lost.** Add an idle timeout on the response body (Codex uses 5 minutes), so a hung stream enters the same recovery instead of waiting forever.
3. **Use a fresh connection on the first retry**, as Grok Build does, so a reset does not reuse a broken pooled connection.
4. **Keep non-transient errors out:** authentication, quota, context-overflow, invalid-request and content-policy errors stay non-retryable.

Alternative, for comparison only: buffer text in the gateway as it already buffers tool calls, so the transport layer can replay the whole upstream request transparently. This would remove live text streaming on the Swarm path.

## Involved Public APIs

This may add settings for the turn retry budget and backoff and for the stream idle timeout, next to `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_RETRIES`. It may also add a run-timeline event for "retrying after a dropped model stream". No change to existing request or session APIs is expected.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `packages/model/src/client.ts`: retry policy, idle timeout, and the `retryErrors` wire diagnostics.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`, `jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`, the JiuwenSwarm patches, and the native loop.
- Web run timeline: the retry status, and partial text that a retry replaces.
- CI accounting (related to #813): `test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs` does not count these failures as provider faults; the run's verdict shows `provider faults 0`. The error text carries no 5xx status, and `PRODUCT_REPORT` (`main run must complete`, `delivery_status`) vetoes it in any case.
- PR #853: the retry it adds for interruptions during the reasoning phase.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- UT for `packages/model` and the gateway: a fake upstream returns 200, streams text and tool-call deltas, then resets the socket. Assert that the turn is re-driven within the budget, that no tool call from the cut attempt executes, and that exhaustion still fails with the original error and wire diagnostics.
- UT: a fake upstream stops sending bytes mid-stream. Assert that the idle timeout classifies the stream as lost and retries it.
- UT: 401/403, quota, context-overflow and invalid-request errors are not retried.
- Mocked E2E: the stub model resets the stream after some answer text. The run completes, the timeline shows the retry, and the answer text is not duplicated.
- Real nightly: wherever `[model-sse-summary]` shows a mid-stream `network` reset, a completed turn follows instead of a failed run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A stream reset after answer text or tool-call deltas have started no longer ends the main run while retry budget remains; the run continues from the last committed turn.
- [ ] No tool call from the interrupted attempt executes, and no completed tool call runs twice.
- [ ] The retry is visible in the run timeline and can be cancelled. When the budget is exhausted, the run fails with the original provider error preserved.
- [ ] Authentication, quota, context-overflow and invalid-request errors are not retried.
- [ ] The JiuwenSwarm and native backends behave the same.
- [ ] A test covering the mid-stream reset fails on current `main` and passes with the change.
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1` and `pnpm test:shared`.

## Additional Information

The other failures in run 41852669139 are outside this issue; they come from the head under test, not from the provider:

- `research-6`: none of the 16 evolve expansions produced a runnable candidate. The most common reason logged was that the 16000-token per-call cap was spent on reasoning.
- The mocked `standard-journeys` and `standard-config` workers: the head buffers reasoning deltas until answer text or a tool call starts.

The main scheduled Nightly that day ([41919338127](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41919338127), `main` `48848578`, provider called directly) passed, with no network reset in 826 requests.

items.body:
**Update:** `D1` is fixed inside `#890` itself at `fdb835fb6664acb85e77c2f64c1b3ebfb7fdb7ff` (red first in `ddd14462`; the stem is now cut at the first colon as well as the first dot, so `nul:stream` resolves to `nul` and `con:$DATA` to `con`, with `conin$`/`conout$` and trailing dot/space stripping unchanged). This issue therefore tracks `D2` only — the POSIX-side segment split where `CON\notes.txt` stays one segment and is accepted.

## Summary

`#890` adds a Windows-reserved-device-name guard to the session file write path — `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` in `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` plus a per-segment check in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`. It refuses `CON/notes.txt`, `nul.dir/x.csv` and `notes/CON.txt`.

**Residual coverage gap.** After `#890` (with `D1` fixed there), the input below is still accepted:

| Input | Predicate result at `#890`'s head | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CON\notes.txt` (POSIX host) | `false` | creates a file literally named `CON\notes.txt`; the same request is refused on a Windows host |

Both were raised as `medium, suggestion` review threads on `#890` (`F1` at `workspace.ts:479`, `F2` at `http/index.ts:3815`) and are tracked here instead of being fixed there. Expected behaviour for all of them: **`400`, naming the offending segment**, exactly as `CON/notes.txt` is answered today.

## D1 — `nul:stream` / `con:$DATA`: the stem keeps the colon, so the predicate misses the device

- **Where:** `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts:478-481` (predicate added by `#890`).
- **Cause:** the stem is everything before the first dot, so `nul:stream` keeps its colon, `WINDOWS_RESERVED_DEVICE_NAME` does not match it, and the predicate returns `false`. Windows resolves `nul:stream` as the `NUL` device plus the named stream `stream`, so the write does not create a file there.
- **Measured at `#890`'s head:** `"CON" → true`, `"nul.txt" → true`, `"nul.dir" → true`, but `"nul:stream" → false` and `"con:$DATA" → false`.
- **Failing input:** `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` with `{"path":"nul:stream"}` or `{"path":"con:$DATA"}`.
- **Observed:** on POSIX the route answers `201` and creates a file Windows cannot open; on Windows the write targets the device.
- **Expected:** `400`, naming the offending segment.
- **Suggested fix:** split the stem on `:` as well as `.` — for example `name.split(/[.:]/)[0]?.replace(/[. ]+$/, "")` — and add `nul:stream` / `con:$DATA` cases next to the existing ones. `conin$` / `conout$` do not contain a colon and must keep matching.

## D2 — `CON\notes.txt`: the segment walk splits on the host separator only

- **Where:** `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3815`.
- **Cause:** `relative(workspaceRoot, target).split(sep)` splits on `/` on Linux, so `CON\notes.txt` stays one segment, the stem reads `CON\notes`, and the predicate allows it — while the predicate and the route comment both claim the rule is platform-independent.
- **Failing input:** `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` with `{"path":"CON\\notes.txt"}` against a Linux server.
- **Observed:** `201` and a workspace file literally named `CON\notes.txt`; the same request is refused on a Windows host, so the answer depends on which platform serves it.
- **Expected:** refused on every host, with a test case alongside the existing `CON/notes.txt` one.
- **Suggested fix:** split on both separators (`relative(...).split(/[\\/]+/)`) and/or refuse `\` inside a segment.

## D3 — the duplicate private predicate in the upload path

- **Where:** `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts` (the upload path keeps its own private copy of the reserved-device-name check, wider in two respects: it recognises the named-stream form `NUL:anything` and superscript ports `[1-9¹²³]`).
- **Cause:** the same rule now lives in two places, so a later change to one does not reach the other — exactly how `D1` slipped past the shared predicate.
- **Expected:** after `#890` lands, the upload path imports `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` from `@sciencediscovery/workspace` instead of keeping a private copy (`workspace-upload.ts:19` already imports that package, so this is a one-line change plus deleting the local copy), and its tests keep covering the stream form and superscript ports through the shared predicate.
- **Why it belongs here and not in a new issue:** same family as `D2` — device-name detection precision and de-duplication — and it is one line of code once `#890` is on `main`.

## Acceptance

- All four inputs (`nul:stream`, `con:$DATA`, `CON\notes.txt`, and `notes\CON.txt`) answer `400` with the offending segment named.
- The `WSP-005` cases added by `#890` stay green.
- The guard's claim of being platform-independent holds on Linux and Windows.
- Any documentation or reply describing the guard must say **partial coverage** until this lands: `nul:stream`, `con:$DATA` and POSIX-side `CON\notes.txt` remain accepted.

items.body:
## Summary

`ST` fails on a clean `main` because the pinned Python runtime is fetched from `astral-sh/python-build-standalone` and that download either answers `504` or streams at 9–31 KB/s, far past the 5-minute `execFile` cap in the test. It fails before any code under test runs, so it is not attributable to the PR whose run turns red — but it does turn `merge-gate` red, which is the one required check in this repository, so it blocks merges.

Current instance: `#678` (tip `5ad9b21b6aeb5d7f30556de8ddafc07d1246d85e`) is approved and otherwise green except `ST`.

## Where

- Test: `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts::a user initializes the pinned release into an empty installation and completes a real Evolve task@linux/amd64`
- Downloader: `scripts/binary-release/fetch-runtime.mjs`
- Asset: `https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/releases/download/20260805/cpython-3.12.13+20260805-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-install_only_stripped.tar.gz` — `34,184,519` bytes

## CI evidence

Run [`41999191976`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41999191976), job `ST` `127150383484` (`2026-11-05T09:04:19Z` → `09:09:17Z`): `{"status":"FAIL","planned":51,"executed":51,"passed":50,"failed":1}`, the only red identity is the test above, first line:

```
Download failed (504): https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/releases/download/20260805/cpython-3.12.13+20260805-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-install_only_stripped.tar.gz
```

## Control: the same case on a clean `main`

`main` at `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673`, tracked tree clean, dependencies installed and built the same way, no branch of `#678` present:

- `node scripts/binary-release/fetch-runtime.mjs --runtime python --arch x86_64 --output … --cache …` → **exit 124** (killed at a 300 s cap; it had written 0 bytes to disk, because the script reads the whole archive into memory before writing).
- `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "pinned release" test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` → **exit 1** after **301 s** (`duration_ms: 300128`), i.e. it hit the same `execFile` 5-minute cap with the same command and the same URL.

So the same case fails on `main` without the change under review.

## Observed throughput for that asset

| Reading | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `curl -sI` (same URL) | `HTTP/2 302` |
| `curl -sL -r 0-1048575` (1 MiB range) | `206`, `1,048,576` bytes in `33.48 s` → `31,322 B/s` |
| `curl -L` (full, 45 s cap) | `200`, `818,498` of `34,184,519` bytes in `45 s` → `18,185 B/s` |
| bare `node fetch` | `status 200` in `1.1 s`, then 0 bytes for 60 s before abort |
| independent samples of the same URL, three machines | `9,445` / `25,735` / `18,312` B/s |

At `9–31 KB/s` the `34 MB` asset needs roughly **18 to 60 minutes**, while the test allows 5.

## It is not deterministic

Fifteen minutes before the red run, the same case passed in merge-group run [`41997396390`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41997396390) (`2026-11-05T08:52:58Z` → `08:53:41Z`, `42.6 s`). `main`'s own `ST` was green in run [`41997392457`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41997392457) (`08:52Z`). So the failure tracks the download path degrading, not a fixed defect in the test.

## Why this is worth a fix rather than a retry

`merge-gate` is the only required status check here, and `ST` is one of the jobs it aggregates, so any PR can be blocked for a reason that has nothing to do with its diff, and a re-run only helps if the CDN happens to recover. Retries also cost a full `ST` cycle (≈5 minutes each time) and cannot be triggered by contributors: `POST /actions/jobs/{id}/rerun` and `POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` both answer `403 Must have admin rights to Repository` for a non-member token.

## Options, in the order we would pick them

1. **Cache the pinned runtime between runs** (keyed by the asset version), so the network is used once per version instead of on every `ST` run.
2. **Verify against a mirror first** and fall back to the GitHub release, or honour `fetch-runtime.mjs`'s resume/cache path when a partial download exists instead of restarting from byte 0.
3. **Fail fast and name the cause**: if the download cannot reach a minimum rate within N seconds, fail with a message that says "external asset download too slow", so the red check is self-explanatory.
4. If none of the above is wanted now, an explicit **retry/exemption policy for `ST` on this identity** would at least stop it blocking unrelated PRs.

If the project prefers that this be reported differently, say so and we will follow that shape instead.
