Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product Claim-Id: 8c2885cfabeb4ba4ba2f1b4c6db60f65 Branch: dev/925-bug-activity-panel-prints-raw-english-st Base: 2908e9e8bb4f At: 2026-11-05T13:37:29Z ## What happens The Session activity panel (`Executions & reminders`) is fully translated except for the two values it takes from server data, which are printed as the raw API token even when the UI language is Chinese: - the status badge on every execution, transfer and reminder record renders `item.state` verbatim, so a running execution shows `running`; - the execution meta line renders `provenance` verbatim, so it reads `工作区 ws_a · 溯源 pending`, and the record's accessible label (fold summary, focus label) reads `local · main · running`. Chinese is the product default, so this is what a default-locale user sees. ## What is expected The badge keeps the state as its CSS class (styling must not change) but names the state in the UI language: `排队中`, `运行中`, `已完成`, `失败`, `已取消`, `未知`. The provenance reads `待提交` / `已提交`. Under English the labels stay the words the rest of the UI already uses: `Queued`, `Running`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Cancelled`, `Unknown`, and `Pending` / `Committed`. ## Where it comes from - `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:97`, `:111`, `:122` — `{item.state}`; the class must keep `item.state`, only the child text needs a label. - `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:98` — `t("activity.executionMeta", { provenance: item.provenance, workspace: item.workspaceId })` passes the raw token into the sentence. - `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:96`, `:110`, `:121` — the `label` prop of `ProcessRecord` interpolates `item.state`. - `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` carries 25 `activity.*` keys in both catalogues (en `2738-2759`, zh `5757-5778`) but none for these values, which is why this is the one activity surface that still shows English. Value domains, for whoever writes the keys: `packages/schema/src/execution.ts:45` (`queued|running|completed|failed|cancelled|unknown`), `apps/web/src/api/runs.ts:40` (timers: `pending|fired|cancelled`), `packages/schema/src/execution.ts:101` (provenance: `pending|committed|unconfirmed`). The other surfaces already do exactly this, so the pattern is in-tree: `apps/web/src/WakeNotice.tsx:72` maps wake states through `chat.wakeNoticeState.*`, `apps/web/src/GovernedDownloadCards.tsx:50` does the same for download states. ## Failing test (reproduce before the fix) Render the panel under the Chinese locale with one running execution and assert the tree does not carry the English token. The probe below is a temporary file — it is not part of the branch, it exists to prove the failure: ```tsx // apps/web/tests/zz-activity-badge-probe.test.tsx (temporary, not committed) const activity = { executions: [{ id: "job", agentId: "main", runnerId: "local", workspaceId: "ws_a", state: "running", provenance: "pending" }], transfers: [], timers: [], agents: [], }; const client = { getAgentActivity: async () => activity } as unknown as ApiClient; let view: ReactTestRenderer; await act(async () => { view = create(createElement(LocaleProvider, { initialLocale: "zh-CN" }, createElement(AgentActivityPanel, { client, sessionId: "session" }))); }); const tree = JSON.stringify(view!.toJSON()); assert.match(tree, /执行/); assert.doesNotMatch(tree, /running/); ``` Command and observed output: ``` $ cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/zz-activity-badge-probe.test.tsx not ok 1 - zh-CN badge names the state in Chinese error: |- The input was expected to not match the regular expression /running/. rendered fragment: {"type":"span","props":{"className":"activity-badge running"},"children":["running"]} # tests 1 # pass 0 # fail 1 ``` The same render shows the second half of this issue: `"工作区 ws_a · 溯源 pending"` — `provenance` is untranslated in the sentence produced by `activity.executionMeta`, and the process record's label is `local · main · running`. ## Environment - `main` @ `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673` - node `v22`; from `apps/web`: `node --import tsx --test tests/` - default locale zh-CN; the probe forces it with `LocaleProvider initialLocale="zh-CN"`, and the panel's own chrome in the same render is Chinese (`执行与提醒`, `查看日志`, `取消执行`), so the locale is applied and the English tokens are not a locale-detection artifact. ## Smallest mergeable slice Two files, about 30 lines, no logic change: 1. `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` — add `activity.state.{queued,running,completed,failed,cancelled,unknown}` and `activity.provenance.{pending,committed}`, one entry per key in the en block beside `activity.resumeAgentScope` and one in the zh block beside its counterpart. 2. `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` — a `stateLabel(state)` / `provenanceLabel(provenance)` helper that calls `t()` and falls back to the raw value for any value the catalogues do not carry (a newer API can add a state), used in the three badge children, the `executionMeta` call and the three `label` props. Boundaries: the `activity-badge ${item.state}` class, the `live`/`cancellable` predicates and the `progress.length` accounting stay exactly as they are; no assertion migration in existing tests; no change to any other badge or badge format in the app. ## Coverage note `#876` (merged today, `dev2/fix/874-activity-unknown-terminal`) is the only recent change to this file and it touched neither the badge text nor the `executionMeta` call — it moved `unknown` out of `live()` and switched `filesCommitted` to `progress.length`. There is no open pull request against `AgentActivityPanel.tsx`. ## Acceptance - The probe passes: under zh-CN the badge text is `运行中` while `className` is still `activity-badge running`, and the execution meta line no longer contains `pending`. - Under `initialLocale="en"` the visible text is unchanged from `main` apart from the badge/provenance wording, so `apps/web/tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx` keeps passing. - A state or provenance value the catalogues do not know renders its raw token rather than an empty string or a missing-key placeholder. - Scope stays at the eight keys above; a transfer's `partial`, a reminder's `fired` and provenance `unconfirmed` are deliberately out of scope and keep rendering their raw token.

Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Product
Claim-Id: 5fcbd6c7878d49f0af0d49f904d6851f
Branch: dev/930-bug-a-length-rejection-answers-500-inter
Base: 2908e9e8bb4f
At: 2026-11-05T13:49:58Z

## What happens

A provider form accepts a pasted API token of any length, and the API answers an over-long one with a bare internal error instead of naming the field:

```
POST /api/providers/preview-models
{"name":"Probe provider","baseUrl":"https://example.test/v1","apiProtocol":"openai-chat-completions","apiToken":"<20 000 chars>"}

HTTP 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
```

The very same validator rejects the empty-token case correctly, so one form gets two different failure shapes for two client mistakes:

```
POST … {"apiToken":""}      → 400  "The LLM API token cannot be empty"
POST … {"apiToken":"k"×20000} → 500  "Internal server error"
```

The `500` also reaches the user as the generic error surface, so the form cannot say which field to shorten.

## What is expected

`400` with the validation message the store already produced: `{"error":"The LLM API token is too long"}`. The same holds for the other length limits below — they are client input mistakes and must answer 400, not 500.

## Where it comes from

- The throw: `services/api/src/store/secrets.ts:194-199` — `normalizeApiToken` throws plain `new Error("The LLM API token is too long")` when the trimmed token exceeds 16 384 characters (`"…cannot be empty"` on the line above matches a known pattern, which is why only the length case leaks).
- The route: `services/api/src/http/index.ts:2174-2181` (`POST /api/providers/preview-models` → `validateLiveProvider` → `normalizeApiToken`) and `POST /api/providers` → `store.createProvider`, which normalizes the same token.
- The classification: `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:20-32` lists the legacy messages that stay 400 (`is required`, `must`, `cannot`, `does not match`, `invalid`, …) and has no pattern for a length rejection, so `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3944` falls through to the 500 branch at `:3946`.

Seven sites share this exact shape today, all of them client-supplied strings:

| site | message |
| --- | --- |
| `services/api/src/store/secrets.ts:198` | `The LLM API token is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:420` | `The proxy URL is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:348` | `neo4jHttp is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store/settings.ts:351` | `neo4jUser is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store.ts:3012` | `The Neo4j password is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store.ts:3858` | `Model ID is too long` |
| `services/api/src/store.ts:5533` | `The stored ${kind} is too long` (remote-host credential) |

`grep -rn "too long" services/api/src --include=*.ts | grep -v .test.` finds nothing else that throws: the remaining hits are prompt text (`session-naming.ts:26`, `:198`), comments, and `configuration/schema-normalizer.ts:86/104` which goes through `invalid()` and is already classified.

## Failing test (reproduce before the fix)

Any harness that starts the real API server works; the probe below reuses the isolated fixture style of `services/api/src/configuration/http.integration.test.ts` (temp data dir, provider stub, `createApiServer`), then makes one request:

```ts
// temporary probe, not committed
const f = await fixture(context);
const result = await f.call("/api/providers/preview-models", {
  name: "Probe provider", baseUrl: "https://example.test/v1", apiProtocol: "openai-chat-completions",
  apiToken: "k".repeat(20_000),
}, "POST");
assert.equal(result.status, 400, `status ${result.status}: ${result.text}`);
```

Command and observed output:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/configuration/zz-token-too-long-probe.test.ts
# STATUS 500 TEXT {"error":"Internal server error"}
not ok 1 - probe: an over-long provider API token is a client error, not a 500
  error: |- status 500: {"error":"Internal server error"}
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

## Environment

- `main` @ `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673`
- node `v22`; from `services/api`: `node --import tsx --test src/<file>`
- the request is a normal authenticated call with a JSON body well under the 10 MB request cap, so the body reader is not involved.

## Smallest mergeable slice

One source line, one test file:

1. `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` — add `/\bis too long\b/i` to the pattern list. That is the whole fix, and it converts all seven sites above from 500 to 400 with their original message preserved, without touching the modules that throw.
2. `services/api/src/http/error-classification.test.ts` — extend the existing table so the classifier is pinned on this shape: `The LLM API token is too long`, `The proxy URL is too long`, `Model ID is too long`, `The stored runnerToken is too long` are client input; a message that merely mentions length without the validation shape (e.g. `Database invariant failed`) stays 500.

Do not add a new error code, do not change `normalizeApiToken` or any limit value, and do not touch the throw sites — this is a classification fix, not a validation change. `POST /api/providers` and `preview-models` both reach the same normalizer, so the route assertion can use either.

## Acceptance

- The probe passes: an over-long `apiToken` answers `400` with `{"error":"The LLM API token is too long"}`.
- An empty `apiToken` still answers `400` with its existing message, and the classifier's existing eight patterns still classify as before (`apps` tests that rely on them keep passing).
- A genuinely internal failure still answers `500`: `isKnownClientInputError(new Error("Database invariant failed"))` stays false and the existing `http/error-classification.test.ts` assertion on it is unchanged.
- The other six length messages are covered by the classifier unit test, so a future endpoint that throws one gets the same 400 without another special case.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- No open pull request touches `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` (checked every open PR's file list); `#697` touches `services/api/src/store/secrets.ts` for a Windows platform change and does not alter this path.
- `#884` (binary artifact diff) and `#877` (artifact provenance/diff) are the same *symptom class* on different endpoints and are being fixed endpoint-locally; this one is the shared classifier, and fixing it does not change their behaviour.
- Issue search for a length-limit 500 (`too long`, `Internal server error` + validation, `client error 400 instead of 500`) returns no issue covering a length rejection.
items.title: [Bug]: A length rejection answers 500 "Internal server error" instead of 400

items.body:
> **Bilingual tracking issue.** The English sections are authoritative; the Chinese sections mirror them and are kept in sync. The separate Chinese tracking issue #806 has been merged into this issue and closed as a duplicate, so both languages now live here. Chinese is included on the requester's explicit ask.
>
> **双语跟踪 issue**：英文段为技术真源，中文段同步镜像。原独立的中文跟踪版 #806 已合并入本 issue 并以 duplicate 关闭，两种语言自此同处一文。中文段应提出者明确要求保留。

---

# English

## 🚀 Background Description

**Start point — what a user actually waits today.** On installed builds, the first message of a session takes **~60–135s** (field measurements from our Windows-desktop tracker: ~85s typical, ~135s on a fresh-install cold boot), while the same-session second message takes **~6s**. Every boot profile — cold first boot, warm restart, or a new session in a running app — pays the same kind of first-message tax.

**What the tax is made of** (log-line-timed decomposition, dev stack + field forensics):

| Chunk | Size | Owner | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCP catalog cold-start | **~48s** (zero once warm) | **SD side** | the bundled stdio MCP servers spawn and enumerate tools on the catalog's first refresh; a fresh install delays that refresh to the first chat run. Verified locally: catalog warmed at boot → first message pays zero here. |
| SD-side run preparation | **~14s** | SD API | serial RPC chain per run (`skills.list` ×3, `permissions.tools.update`, per-run MCP re-registration) plus API acceptance (~4s) |
| Session assembly | **~5.3s** warm / ~17s pre-0015 | JiuwenSwarm | per-session `create_instance`; the 0015–0017 patches already moved the ~5.2s import tax off this path |
| Tool-schema handling | **~7–8s every turn** | upstream default | ~72 tool definitions ≈ 28k input tokens ride every model call (`progressive_tool_enabled=false`; #582 measured the same) |
| Model network/TTFT + machine tax | remainder | — | real model latency, cold-file reads, antivirus scanning on installed machines |

**Where the "26.09s" figure belongs** (an earlier draft of this issue wrongly led with it): it is an **anatomy anchor, not the user-facing start point** — a dev-stack first message measured with a *warm catalog* and a *mock model*, versus 8.67s for the second message. Its only purpose is attributing each chunk to its owning side: it proves the 48s chunk is the SD catalog (JW `reconcile` only opens one local loopback shared-tools server, milliseconds), and it sizes the SD-side run-preparation chain. Quoting it as the baseline would understate the real-world problem by the catalog chunk and the model time.

**End point (expected, to be replaced by packaged A/B measurements).** With the full plan below landed: first message **6–10s** on a warm-restart profile (vs ~60–135s today), second message ~5s (vs ~6s), cold-install first message no longer carrying the ~48s catalog chunk. Total optimization space: **~50–120s off the first message, plus ~3.5s off every subsequent turn**.

Related upstream context: #582 documented the input-side half (72 tools ≈ 28k tokens on a short "你好"); jiuwenswarm has adjacent requests openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm#6683 (on-demand MCP registration), #7101 (request-level MCP registration failure bypass), #9938 (blocking snapshot out of the chat data plane).

## Design Ideas

Ordered by measured value. Options already invalidated by measurement are recorded so the discussion does not restart them.

1. **S1 — Warm the MCP catalog right after agent-ready** (implemented on the workstream branch; PR to follow).
   The shell's `watchAgentReady` already probes `/agent/info`. The moment `jiuwenswarm.reachable` turns true it now issues `GET /api/mcp/sources` in the background — the exact request the MCP settings page uses to refresh the catalog. The stdio spawns and tool enumeration then overlap the user's "ready screen" time instead of the first message. Best-effort: failures are logged to `shell.log` only; if the warmup loses the race the run path re-runs the same steps, so behaviour never forks.
   Direct evidence: catalog refreshed at boot → first message at +3min paid **zero** MCP chunk.

2. **S3 — Trim the per-run preparation chain in the control API** (planned, highest remaining value in the warm-catalog scenario).
   `executeAgentRun`'s head runs a serial RPC chain against JiuwenSwarm before `chat.send`: `skills.list` ×3 (~4s in the anatomy anchor), permission updates, and per-run MCP re-registration (~1–2s). Candidates: cache the skills list with invalidation on skill-set changes, collapse the three lists into one, and let the API prove "tool table unchanged" so the adapter skips its re-registration round trips. Session-creation-time pre-warm follows once the chain is idempotent.

3. **J2 — Progressive tool exposure** (needs upstream discussion; JiuwenSwarm native).
   `DEFAULT_PROGRESSIVE_TOOL_ENABLED=False` sends all ~72 tool schemas on every call (~28k tokens; ~7s of per-turn cost under a mock endpoint — not model time). Enabling the existing `ProgressiveToolRail` with a small direct-exposure whitelist would cut input tokens ~3× on **every** turn, first and subsequent. Upstream note: the constant's comment/docstring already says "enabled by default" while the code returns `False` — the drift is a low-controversy entry point. Recall-rate validation on real tasks is required before flipping any default.

4. **J3 — Session-assembly warm pool** (second batch).
   Extend the existing `AgentWarmPool` so the per-session adapter is pre-built on session create; measured remaining value ~5.3s → ~1–2s on hit, with a mandatory seamless fallback to today's full path.

**Invalidated by measurement (recorded to save re-litigating):**
- *J1 — concurrent MCP connect with timeouts in JW*: the JW-side reconcile only opens one local loopback server (ms-level); the 48s was the SD catalog. Kept only as a small upstream-hygiene proposal.
- *S2 — adapter-side pre-registration at lifespan*: the tool table is assembled by the control API per run and handed over `/agent/runs`; the adapter has no table to pre-register at startup, and an empty pre-registration would force a generation bump on the first real run.

## Involved Public APIs

- Existing: `GET /api/mcp/sources` (MCP settings page's refresh endpoint; now also called by the shell after agent-ready).
- No new HTTP APIs, IPC channels or configuration surfaces in S1. S3 may add an internal invalidation signal for the skills cache; any new surface will be listed in its PR.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `win_desktop`: shell `watchAgentReady` warmup hook + `first-chat-warmup.ts` (new, unit-tested).
- `services/api`: S3 target — `executeAgentRun` head, `jiuwenswarm-skills.ts` reconcile chain.
- `services/adapter`: `ensure_shared_tools` already diffs tool tables; S3 may hand it an "unchanged" fast path proof.
- JiuwenSwarm patches (`jiuwen_swarm/patches/`): no new patches for S1/S3; J3 would land as patch 0020+ (numbering shared with a parallel packaging workstream).
- `apps/desktop`: no UI change; the ready screen timing is unchanged.
- #582 (input-token analysis): complementary — J2 addresses that input directly.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **S1 (landed in branch)**: unit tests for URL/header construction and timeout (`win_desktop/test/first-chat-warmup.test.ts`); full shell suite 116/116 green and `win_desktop` build + typecheck clean, re-run on 2026-11-05.
- **Integration A/B** (per change): dev stack, mock OpenAI endpoint on loopback, `agent_server.log` line-timestamped segmentation; baseline vs change measured in the **same host-load window** (parallel packaging builds invalidate absolute numbers); first message of a fresh session vs second message of the same session, median of 3.
- **Cold-scenario check**: with the MCP catalog forcibly cold (fresh data dir), confirm the shell warmup completes before a human-plausible first message and the first run no longer contains the stdio-spawn chunk.
- **Regression**: shell build + full shell suite; `pnpm test` for the api package after S3; JiuwenSwarm smoke (gateway / agentserver / main chat / memory) where patches are touched.
- **Packaged validation**: GUI-interactive install (no `/S`), three boot profiles (cold first boot / warm restart / attach) with first-message timing recorded and the second message non-regressed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Shell warmup: after `jiuwenswarm.reachable` becomes true, `shell.log` shows `[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources -> 200` (or a failure line) without any change to the ready-screen timing or user-visible behaviour.
- [ ] Warmup failure never surfaces to the user, and a lost race falls back to today's run path with identical behaviour.
- [ ] Cold-install first message no longer contains the stdio-spawn/tool-enumeration chunk (field: ~48s of the 60–135s).
- [ ] Warm-restart first message: field baseline ~60–135s → **≤20s after S1+S3** [expected, to be replaced by packaged A/B] → **6–10s after the full plan** [expected].
- [ ] Second message ~6s is not regressed beyond noise, trending to ~5s with J2.
- [ ] Every-turn input: J2, where accepted upstream, cuts tool-schema tokens by ≥50% with zero regression on a fixed set of real-task scenarios (recall rate held).
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1` (static gate), `pnpm --dir win_desktop build`, `pnpm --dir win_desktop typecheck`, `pnpm --dir win_desktop test` (116/116), `pnpm test` for the api/desktop scopes touched by S3, plus the packaged three-profile run above.
- Performance threshold: the ready screen and every user-visible behaviour are unchanged; the warmup is off the critical path by construction (fire-and-forget, 60s timeout, logged only).

## Additional Information

- Measurement note: anatomy-anchor numbers were taken while a parallel packaging build was running on the host; they may read 10–25% high. Field numbers (60–135s) are user-measured and unaffected. The structural findings (chunk boundaries, catalog-warm ⇒ zero MCP chunk, JW loopback being ms-level) are load-independent. A/B pairs are always measured within one load window.
- Revision note (2026-11-03): this body was re-aligned after review — the original draft led with the 26.09s anatomy anchor as the baseline, which understated the user-facing start point. The start point is now the field measurement (~60–135s); the 26.09s figure is kept only as the internal attribution anchor it was measured to be.
- Revision note (2026-11-05): the two-language tracking was merged from #806 into this single issue (English first, Chinese mirrored below), and the body was re-aligned with the repository feature template added in #776 — `[Feature]:` title prefix, the seven template sections, and checkbox acceptance criteria naming the commands that must pass.
- S1 is implemented for the desktop shell only; Linux/macOS source-stack paths benefit indirectly through the same control-plane endpoint.
- Evidence pack (internal): session-creation timestamped `agent_server.log` segmentation, the mock endpoint fixture, and the run-preparation RPC chain listing are archived in the workstream's knowledge base.

---

# 中文

## 🚀 背景描述

**起点——用户今天实际要等多久**。装机器上，会话首条消息耗时 **~60–135s**（我方 Windows 桌面端跟踪实测：典型 ~85s，全新安装冷启 ~135s），而同会话第二条仅 **~6s**。无论哪种启动口径（全新首启 / 热启动 / 运行中开新会话），首条税都在。

**税的构成**（日志逐行对时分解，开发栈 + 现场取证）：

| 段 | 大小 | 归属 | 机制 |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCP catalog 冷启动 | **~48s**（热后归零） | **SD 侧** | 内置 stdio MCP 进程在 catalog 首次刷新时才拉起并枚举工具；全新安装把这次刷新推迟到首条消息。本机实证：启动时预热 → 首条此段为 0 |
| SD 侧 run 准备链 | **~14s** | SD API | 每轮 run 前的串行 RPC 链（`skills.list` ×3 + 权限更新 + MCP 重注册）+ API 受理（~4s） |
| 会话装配 | 热态 **~5.3s**（0015 补丁前 ~17s） | JiuwenSwarm | 每会话 `create_instance`；0015–0017 已把 ~5.2s import 税挪出该路径 |
| 工具 schema 处理 | **每轮 ~7–8s** | 上游默认 | 每次模型调用全量携带 ~72 个工具定义 ≈ 2.8 万 token（`progressive_tool_enabled=false`；#582 同口径实测） |
| 模型网络/TTFT + 机器税 | 其余 | — | 真实模型耗时、冷机文件读取、杀软扫描 |

**“26.09s”该放在哪**（本 issue 初版错误地拿它当起点）：它是**解剖锚点、不是用户侧起点**——开发栈上“目录已热 + mock 模型”条件下的首条耗时（对照第二条 8.67s）。它唯一的用途是给各段定归属：证明 48s 在 SD catalog（JW `reconcile` 只连 1 个本地回环服务器，毫秒级）、量出 SD 侧准备链大小。若拿它当基线，会把真实问题少算一个目录段和模型时间。

**终点（预期值，待装机 A/B 替换）**。全部方案落地后：热启动口径首条 **6–10s**（现状 ~60–135s），第二条 ~5s（现状 ~6s），冷装机首条不再带 ~48s 目录税。**总优化空间：首条省 ~50–120s + 每条再省 ~3.5s**。

关联上游背景：#582 记录了输入侧的另一半（一句“你好”也带 72 工具 ≈ 2.8 万 token）；jiuwenswarm 侧相邻诉求 openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm#6683（MCP 按需注册）、#7101（请求级 MCP 注册失败旁路）、#9938（阻塞快照移出对话数据面）。

## 设计思路

按实测价值排序。已被测量证伪的选项一并记录，避免重复讨论。

1. **S1 —— agent-ready 后立即预热 MCP catalog**（已在工作分支实现，PR 随附）。
   壳的 `watchAgentReady` 已在探测 `/agent/info`；`jiuwenswarm.reachable` 一变真即在后台发起 `GET /api/mcp/sources`——与 MCP 设置页的 refresh 是同一个请求。stdio 进程拉起与工具枚举由此与用户看“就绪界面”的时间重叠。尽力而为：失败只写 `shell.log`；若预热输了竞速，run 路径会重跑同样的步骤，行为不分叉。
   直接证据：catalog 启动时预热 → 3 分钟后首条该段为 **0**。

2. **S3 —— 精简控制面 API 的每轮准备链**（计划，目录已热场景下剩余价值最大）。
   `executeAgentRun` 头部在 `chat.send` 前对 JiuwenSwarm 跑串行 RPC 链：`skills.list` ×3（解剖锚点合计 ~4s）、权限更新、每轮 MCP 重注册（~1–2s）。候选：skills 列表缓存（技能集变化时失效）、三次 list 合并、API 证明“工具表未变化”使 adapter 跳过注册往返。准备链幂等后，会话创建时预热也在考虑范围。

3. **J2 —— 渐进式工具暴露**（需上游讨论；JiuwenSwarm 原生）。
   `DEFAULT_PROGRESSIVE_TOOL_ENABLED=False` 使每次调用全量携带 ~72 个工具 schema（~2.8 万 token；mock 端点下占每轮 ~7s——即非模型耗时）。启用现成的 `ProgressiveToolRail` 并配少量 direct 白名单，可把**每轮**输入 token 砍掉约 3 倍。上游切入点：该常量的注释/docstring 已写 “enabled by default” 而代码返回 `False`——低争议入口。翻默认值前必须做真实任务召回率验证。

4. **J3 —— 会话装配 warm pool**（第二批）。
   扩展现有 `AgentWarmPool`，会话创建时预建 adapter；实测剩余价值 ~5.3s → 命中 ~1–2s，必须无缝兜底回今天的全量路径。

**已被测量证伪（存档以免重议）：**
- *J1 —— JW 侧 MCP 并发连接+超时*：JW 侧 reconcile 只开 1 个本地回环服务器（毫秒级）；48s 在 SD catalog。仅留作小型上游卫生提案。
- *S2 —— adapter lifespan 预注册*：工具表由控制面 API 每轮组装后经 `/agent/runs` 交给 adapter；adapter 启动时刻无表可预热，空表预热反而迫使首跑换代重注册。

## 涉及的公开 API

- 现有：`GET /api/mcp/sources`（MCP 设置页 refresh 端点；壳层 agent-ready 后也调用）。
- S1 无新 HTTP API / IPC / 配置面。S3 可能为 skills 缓存增加内部失效信号，其 PR 会列明。

## 与其他模块的关系

- `win_desktop`：壳 `watchAgentReady` 预热挂点 + `first-chat-warmup.ts`（新增，有单测）。
- `services/api`：S3 目标——`executeAgentRun` 头部、`jiuwenswarm-skills.ts` reconcile 链。
- `services/adapter`：`ensure_shared_tools` 本就有工具表 diff；S3 可使其走上“未变化”快速通道。
- JiuwenSwarm 补丁（`jiuwen_swarm/patches/`）：S1/S3 不需要新补丁；J3 落为 0020+（编号与并行打包工作流协调）。
- `apps/desktop`：无 UI 变化；就绪屏时序不变。
- #582（输入 token 分析）：互补——J2 直接针对该输入。

## 测试设计

- **S1（已在分支）**：URL/头部构造与超时单测（`win_desktop/test/first-chat-warmup.test.ts`）；壳全量 116/116 绿、`win_desktop` 构建 + typecheck 干净，2026-11-05 复跑确认。
- **集成 A/B**（每改动）：dev 栈 + 本地 mock OpenAI + `agent_server.log` 逐行分段；基线与改动须在**同一主机负载窗口**内测量（并行打包构建会使绝对值失效）；新会话首条 vs 同会话第二条，3 轮取中位。
- **冷场景验证**：catalog 强制为冷（全新数据目录）时，确认壳预热在人类可感的首条消息前完成，且首个 run 不再含 stdio 拉起段。
- **回归**：壳构建 + 全量壳测试；S3 后 `pnpm test`（api 包）；触及补丁时 JW 冒烟（gateway/agentserver/主对话/记忆）。
- **装机验证**：GUI 交互安装（不用 `/S`），三档启动（全新首启/热启动/attach）+ 首响计时，第二条不回退。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 壳预热：`jiuwenswarm.reachable` 变真后 `shell.log` 出现 `[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources -> 200`（或失败行），就绪屏时序与用户可见行为无任何变化。
- [ ] 预热失败永不透出到用户；竞速失败时回落到今天的 run 路径，行为完全一致。
- [ ] 冷装机首条不再含 stdio 拉起/工具枚举段（现场口径 ~48s）。
- [ ] 热启动首条：现场基线 ~60–135s → **S1+S3 后 ≤20s**【预期，待装机 A/B 替换】 → **全部方案后 6–10s**【预期】。
- [ ] 第二条 ~6s 不回退（超出噪声），随 J2 降至 ~5s。
- [ ] 每轮输入：J2（上游接受后）工具 schema token -50% 以上，固定真实任务集零回归（召回率保持）。
- 必须通过的命令：`pnpm ci:l1`（静态门禁）、`pnpm --dir win_desktop build`、`pnpm --dir win_desktop typecheck`、`pnpm --dir win_desktop test`（116/116）、S3 触及包的 `pnpm test`（api/desktop），以及上述装机三档。
- 性能阈值：就绪屏与一切用户可见行为不变；预热按构造即在关键路径之外（fire-and-forget、60s 超时、仅记日志）。

## 附加信息

- 测量注记：解剖锚点数字测量时本机有并行打包构建，绝对值或偏高 10–25%；现场数字（60–135s）为实测，不受影响。结构性发现（分段边界、目录热则 MCP 段归零、JW 回环毫秒级）与负载无关。A/B 对永远同窗口测量。
- 修订记录（2026-11-03）：正文经评审后重新对齐——初版误以 26.09s 解剖锚点作为起点，低估了用户侧问题；起点已改为现场实测（~60–135s），26.09s 仅保留为其本来的内部归因锚点角色。

items.body:
## Current behaviour

`GET /api/sessions/:session/artifact-versions/:version/diff` answers **500 `Internal server error`** when either side of the pair is not a textual artifact, and logs a false `unclassified_request_error status=500`.

## Expected behaviour

A client error (400/422) that says the comparison is not available for those versions, consistent with the other client-input rejections on the same route.

## Where it comes from

`services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:355-357` (live `main` `89cd2d30`):

```ts
const isText = (mediaType: string) => mediaType.startsWith("text/")
  || /\b(?:json|javascript|xml|yaml)\b/i.test(mediaType);
if (!isText(from.mediaType) || !isText(to.mediaType)) throw new Error("Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions");
```

The plain `Error` matches none of the classification paths:

- `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:23-32` — the client-input patterns are `is required`, `must`, `contains? an unknown value`, `cannot`, `does not match`, `invalid`, `unsafe … (archive|package|path)`, `plain basename`; "available only for" matches none;
- the 404 message mapper in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` only knows `Project|Session|Proxy server|Provider|Model not found` and `Execution|Transfer|Timer|Subagent not found:`;
- so the top-level catch falls through to 500.

Found while reviewing #881 (`Fixes #877`), which fixed the *missing version* cases on this route family; that PR's reviewer classified this one as a non-blocking follow-up because it is not a regression — the binary pair answered 500 before #881 too. Verified against the code at `89cd2d30`, not by re-running the server.

## Suggested fix (either is one small change)

1. Hoist the media-type check into the route in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` next to the version-existence checks and answer 400 with a stable message, or
2. Throw `ApiStatusError` from `artifactVersionDiff` for this case, or add the message to `isKnownClientInputError` if a message-based classification is preferred.

Option 2 is the smaller diff but keeps classification tied to prose; option 1 matches how `#881` handles the missing-version case.

## Reproduce

Any two artifact versions of non-textual media types (e.g. two `.zip` uploads) in one session, then call the `diff` route with the later version id. No mock needed; the throw happens before CAS reads.

## Dedupe

Searched open+closed: `"Diff is available only for textual"` → 1 hit, this report (the phrase appears only in the source). `provenance 500` (13) and `unclassified_request_error` (3, #779/#784) are different sources; #877 covers the missing-version case only.

### Checklist - [x] I searched existing issues for this symptom and found none (search terms in "Duplicate check" below). - [x] I reproduced this on the latest `main` (`89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`), not on an older release. - [x] This report includes the environment and a minimal, runnable reproduction. ### Detailed Description **What the user sees.** On the Usage page, after choosing a date range that leaves out a model's older invocations, the page header still names the all-time model count while the token figure and the model list below are already scoped to the range. The header and the body contradict each other. **Minimal reproduction.** Render `UsagePage` with a summary that contains two models, where only one has an invocation inside the selected day, and with `filters = { from: "2026-08-04", to: "2026-08-04" }`: ```tsx const html = renderToStaticMarkup(React.createElement(UsagePage, { analytics, // overview.totalTokens = 30 (model-b only) filters: { from: "2026-08-04", to: "2026-08-04" }, onExport: () => undefined, onFiltersChange: () => undefined, onOpenSession: () => undefined, summary, // byModel = [model-a (Aug 3 only), model-b (Aug 4)] })); ``` Command: ```bash cd apps/web node --import tsx --test tests/zz-usage-subtitle-probe.test.tsx ``` Observed on `89cd2d30`: ```text # SUBTITLE "30 tokens across 2 models" # MODEL_GROUPS_IN_BODY 1 ``` The header claims two models while the filtered list renders one model card, and the 30 tokens it prints are the range-scoped number (model-b only, 30), not the all-time total (45). **Expected.** The subtitle counts the same range the tokens and the list use, e.g. `30 tokens across 1 model` (a singular form may be added; at minimum the count must not name models that the date filter excluded). **Where.** `apps/web/src/UsagePage.tsx` on `89cd2d30`: - `apps/web/src/UsagePage.tsx:991` — `models: filters.modelProfileId ? filteredModelGroups.length : summary!.byModel.length`. `filteredModelGroups` is the date+model filtered list (`:973-977`), while `summary!.byModel` is the unfiltered all-time summary. Then make `:991` always use `filteredModelGroups.length` and add a singular `usage.subtitleOne` message if the maintainers want `1 model` to read correctly. **Duplicate check (open and closed).** GitHub search over `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`: `"usage.subtitle"` → 0, `"tokens across"` → 1 unrelated (MCP SDK OAuth issue #371), `"across 2 models"` → 1 unrelated (CI workflow #2), `tokens across` → 38 results, none about the Usage page header count. ## Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues (open and closed) before filing this one.
- [x] This is a defect report, not a feature request.
- [x] I can reproduce it from the code path described below.

## Detailed Description of the Problem

`SessionStore.writeArray` writes a temp file, replaces the target, and removes the temp file in a `finally` block:

```ts
// services/api/src/store.ts:2156-2166
try {
  await writeFile(temporaryPath, `${JSON.stringify(values, null, 2)}\n`, "utf8");
  await renameReplace(temporaryPath, path);   // retries a transient EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY
} finally {
  await rm(temporaryPath, { force: true });
}
```

`renameReplace` classifies an exhausted retry as `FileReplaceError`, which keeps the errno in `code` and the original failure in `cause` so a caller can tell a locked file from a full disk. That classification is lost when the `rm` in the `finally` block itself throws: on Windows an antivirus scanner or an indexer can hold the same fresh temp file that made the replace fail, so `rm` raises a bare `EPERM`, the `finally` throws it, and it replaces the `FileReplaceError` on the way out. The caller then sees an unclassified `EPERM` — exactly the shape this area was just hardened against.

Current vs expected:

- current: replace exhausted → `rm` raises `EPERM` → caller receives a raw `EPERM` (no `FileReplaceError`, no `cause`, no attempt count).
- expected: the classified `FileReplaceError` reaches the caller; the cleanup failure must not substitute for the write failure.

The second half is coverage: the retry-success path asserts no `*.tmp` is left behind (`services/api/src/store-replace.test.ts:60-75`), but the exhausted-failure path has no assertion, so 'the finally still runs' is currently a code-reading claim rather than a checked behaviour.

### Minimal reproduction (red first)

In `services/api/src/store-replace.test.ts`, wrap the same fixture with `context.mock.method(fs, "rename", …)` throwing `EPERM` for every attempt **and** `context.mock.method(fs, "rm", …)` throwing `EPERM`:

```ts
await assert.rejects(() => store.writeArray(sessionId, values), (error) => {
  assert.equal(error.name, "FileReplaceError");          // currently fails: a bare EPERM arrives
  assert.equal(error.code, "EPERM");
  return true;
});
```

Observed now: the assertion fails with `error.name === "Error"` and the message `EPERM: operation not permitted, rm …`. Expected after the fix: `FileReplaceError`. Add a second assertion on the exhausted path that `readdir(sessionRunsDir)` contains no `*.tmp` entry.

### Fix

`services/api/src/store.ts` — the cleanup must not mask the write failure, e.g. `await rm(temporaryPath, { force: true }).catch(() => undefined);`. The retry policy, `FileReplaceError` and the non-transient errno behaviour stay as they are. This is deliberately **not** folded into #816: #816's tip is in review and the change is a separate failure mode.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository state: `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`
- File:line: `services/api/src/store.ts:2156-2166`, existing coverage `services/api/src/store-replace.test.ts:60-75`
- Node: `v22.23.2`; package manager: `pnpm 11.1.2`
- Command for the area: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/store-replace.test.ts`
- Reported by: ScienceDiscovery Security (review of #816 at `82d31f6111ff87be3e2709d7230dd8babc10d507`), filed by ScienceDiscovery Lead

## Version Information

- `main` @ `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`
- Reported 2026-11-04

## Before you start (three constraints on the tests, from a read of the fixtures)

1. **The two acceptances cannot live in one test.** If `rm` is mocked to always throw `EPERM`, the temp file necessarily stays on disk, so a `readdir` assertion that no `*.tmp` remains in the same test can never hold. Split it: **A** = `rm` throws `EPERM`, assert only that the classified error reaches the caller; **B** = `rename` is exhausted while `rm` is the real implementation, assert `FileReplaceError` *and* no `*.tmp` leftover.
2. **The mock needs `syncBuiltinESMExports()`, and the `rm` filter must match the file name, not a substring.** `store.ts:25` imports `rm` as a named ESM binding, and the existing `failReplaces` helper (`store-replace.test.ts:44-55`) is what lets a mock reach the store; without it the mock silently does nothing and the red assertion passes for the wrong reason. Also do not filter on `.tmp`: the fixture root is `<cwd>/.tmp/state-replace-<uuid>` (`store-replace.test.ts:23`) and the teardown calls `rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true })` (`:24`), so a substring filter mocks the teardown too and the test blows up in cleanup. Match `basename` against the `.state-<pid>-<uuid>.tmp` shape written by `store.ts:2156`.
3. **The assertions above do not stop a fake fix.** Asserting only `name`/`code`/no-leftover can be satisfied by wrapping any bare `EPERM` in a hand-built `FileReplaceError` higher up. Add the two cheapest discriminators: `assert.equal(error.attempts, 20)` (and confirm the attempt count with the mock's own counter) and `assert.equal(error.cause.code, "EPERM")`.

A note against over-fixing: the swallowed-cleanup leftover is **inert**. Only two `readdir` calls exist in `store.ts` — `.trash` (`:2103`) and `agent-workspaces` (`:2001`) — and nothing enumerates `session-runs/` or the array directory; `readArray` reads an exact path (`:2147-2153`). So no startup sweep and no retry on `rm` are needed; the fix stays one line plus the tests.

### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues for this symptom and found none (terms below).
- [x] I reproduced this on the latest `main` (`89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`).
- [x] This report includes the environment and a minimal reproduction.

### Detailed Description

**What the user sees.** In Settings › Models, each provider row shows the context window and the max output tokens as a compact badge (for example `1M / 131k`). Those badges round to a whole unit with `Math.round`, so a window of 1,500,000 is displayed as **`2M`** and a 1,400,000 window as **`1M`**. The badge is the only place the row shows these numbers (it has no tooltip), so the user reads a capacity the model profile does not have: a 1.5M-token window is advertised as 2M, and a request sized against that badge can exceed the real limit.

**Minimal reproduction** (pure function, no DOM):

```ts
import { compactTokenCount } from "./apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.js";
console.log(compactTokenCount(1_400_000)); // 1M
console.log(compactTokenCount(1_500_000)); // 2M
console.log(compactTokenCount(999_999));   // 1000k
```

Observed on `89cd2d30`:

```text
# 1050000 -> 1M
# 1400000 -> 1M
# 1500000 -> 2M
# 1999999 -> 2M
# 2000000 -> 2M
# 999999 -> 1000k
```

**Expected.** A declared 1.5M window reads `1.5M` (and 1.4M reads `1.4M`); compacting must not round across half a million tokens. `999,999` should read `1M` (or `999,999`), never `1000k`.

**Where.** `apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.tsx:188-193` on `89cd2d30`:

- `:190` — ``if (value >= 1_000_000) return `${Math.round(value / 1_000_000)}M`;`` — whole-million rounding is the source of `1_500_000 → 2M`.
- `:191` — ``if (value >= 1_000) return `${Math.round(value / 1_000)}k`;`` — the same boundary produces `1000k` for `999_999` (and for any `999_500..999_999`).
- `:209` — `ModelRowFacts` renders `{compactTokenCount(contextWindow)} / {compactTokenCount(maxOutputTokens)}` as a plain `<span className="fact">` with no title, so the compact string is the only reading a user gets.
- The same helper is re-exported through `apps/web/src/ProviderModelSettings.tsx:65` and used by `ModelConnectWizard.tsx:660`, so the badge appears in both the settings list and the connect wizard.

**Red-first fix proposal.** First add a test that fails on `89cd2d30`:

```ts
assert.equal(compactTokenCount(1_500_000), "1.5M");
assert.equal(compactTokenCount(1_400_000), "1.4M");
assert.equal(compactTokenCount(999_999), "1M");
```

then format with one significant decimal below 10 units (`(value / 1_000_000).toFixed(1)` trimmed of a trailing `.0`, e.g. `1.5M`, `1M`, `2M`) and promote a rounded `1000k` to `1M` instead of printing `1000k`. Values below the unit keep their current form.

**Duplicate check (open and closed).** GitHub search: `"compactTokenCount"` → 0; `"context window"` → unrelated issues (#686 test-button rendering, #845 model deletion, #824 connectivity); `"1000k"` → 0; `"1.5M"` → 0. No open PR touches `apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.tsx` (`#811` touches `usageFormat.ts`/`UsagePage.tsx` for reasoning tokens only). Issue #860 (filed today) is the same rounding pattern in the *usage* formatter `formatCompactTokenValue`, a different file and a different fix; this one is the settings badge.

### Environment

- Commit: `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (live `main`, read 2026-11-04).
- Node `v22.23.2`, pnpm `11.1.2`, Linux x86_64.
- Command: `cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/zz-compact-token-probe.test.ts` (temporary probe file, not committed).

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`
- Affected package: `apps/web` (`@sciencediscovery/web`)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

`services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts` `sanitizeUploadFilename()` guards an empty name, a NUL byte, absolute paths, drive letters and traversal — but not Windows reserved device names. On a Windows runner the OS resolves `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`, `LPT1`–`LPT9`, `CONIN$` and `CONOUT$` in **every** directory and with **any** extension, so `con.csv` and `nul.txt` pass the guard, reach `writeFile()`/`rename()` in the workspace and fail there with a raw `EPERM`/`ENOENT` that the upload path reports as an unclassified error. `CON` is worse than a failure: opening it targets the console device.

Minimal reproduction (no Windows needed — the guard is the defect):

```ts
import { sanitizeUploadFilename } from "./services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts";

sanitizeUploadFilename("CON.csv");   // expected: rejected; actual: accepted as "CON.csv"
sanitizeUploadFilename("nul.txt");   // expected: rejected; actual: accepted as "nul.txt"
sanitizeUploadFilename("COM1.log");  // expected: rejected; actual: accepted as "COM1.log"
sanitizeUploadFilename("conin$.txt");// expected: rejected; actual: accepted as "conin$.txt"
```

Observed on `main` `8708320f` (`node --import tsx --test services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` after adding the assertions):

```
not ok 2 - sanitizeUploadFilename rejects Windows reserved device names
  error: 'Missing expected exception: CON must be rejected as a Windows reserved device name'
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
# tests 16
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

The other half of the same defect is over-rejection, which any fix must avoid: `conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `auxiliary.csv` and `com10.csv` (two-digit port, not reserved) are legal names and must keep working.

References: <https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file#naming-conventions> — "Do not use the following reserved names for the name of a file: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1…COM9, LPT1…LPT9. Also avoid these names followed immediately by an extension; for example, NUL.txt and NUL.tar.gz are both equivalent to NUL." Windows also ignores a trailing dot or space on a segment, so `nul.` and `CON ` name the device too.

Expected: `sanitizeUploadFilename()` rejects those names with `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` and names the file in the message, before any write is attempted; legal stems that merely begin with a reserved word stay accepted.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- OS: Linux (Ubuntu, CI runner) — the guard is platform-independent; the failure it prevents is Windows-only.
- Node.js v22.23.2, pnpm workspace at commit `8708320f` (`main`).
- No Python or GPU dependency; reproduction is a single `node --import tsx --test` run.
- Windows behaviour per the Microsoft naming-conventions document quoted above.

### Additional Information

Found by dogfooding the `services/api` upload path (`SessionStore`'s atomic-write neighbour). The fix keeps the existing guard style (same `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` code, same `Object.assign(new Error(...))` shape) and is covered by one test with both directions: the reserved names above must throw `/reserved/`, and `conifer.csv` / `console.log` / `com10.csv` / `auxiliary.csv` must still sanitize unchanged.

### Version Information

`main` @ `8708320f` (2026-11-04). `services/api` `workspace-upload.ts` at line 67 (`sanitizeUploadFilename`).

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

From ten million tokens up, the same count is printed two different ways depending on the screen, and nothing states which one is intended.

- Model settings badges (`apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.tsx`, `compactTokenCount`) keep whole millions from 10M up: `10_500_000 → "11M"`.
- The usage page (`apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts`, `formatCompactTokenValue`) has no ≥10M branch: `10_500_000 → "10.5M"`.

Measured with `node --import tsx` on `main` `89cd2d30` plus the two open fixes (#864 for `formatCompactTokenValue`, #869 for `compactTokenCount`):

```text
value       badge (settings)   usage page
9_999_999   10M                10.0M
10_000_000  10M                10.0M
10_499_999  10M                10.5M
10_500_000  11M                10.5M
12_345_678  12M                12.3M
```

**Why it matters.** Both are honest for their own precision, but a user comparing a model's declared 10.5M window in Settings with a 10.5M figure on the usage page sees `11M` in one place; and the badge's own rule — whole millions from 10M because a `0.1M` fraction is below the badge's resolution — is not stated as a decision at the branch, only in the doc comment, and the test at `apps/web/tests/ProviderModelList.test.tsx:59` pins `10_500_000 → "11M"` without pinning the other side of the boundary (`10_499_999 → "10M"`).

**Expected.** One decision, stated and covered: either both surfaces print one decimal from 1M up (`10.5M` on both), or both switch to whole millions at 10M (`11M` on both), with the boundary pinned on both sides and the threshold's rationale next to the branch.

**Minimal reproduction** (no DOM):

```ts
import { compactTokenCount } from "./apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.js";
import { formatCompactTokenValue } from "./apps/web/src/usageFormat.js";

console.log(compactTokenCount(10_500_000));      // "11M"
console.log(formatCompactTokenValue(10_500_000)); // "10.5M"  (with #864 applied)
```

**Where.** `apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.tsx:190-197`; `apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts:19-25`; `apps/web/tests/ProviderModelList.test.tsx:59`; `apps/web/tests/UsagePage.test.tsx`.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`.
- `apps/web` (React + Vite), checked with `node --import tsx` on Node `v22.23.2`, pnpm `11.1.2`, Linux x86_64.
- Depends on the open fixes in #864 (usage formatter unit crossing) and #869 (model-settings badge fractions); both are pure functions, no browser needed.

### Additional Information

Raised in review of #869 (`apps/web/src/ProviderModelFields.tsx:193`). #869 intentionally keeps the ≥10M whole-million rule (that was the reviewed decision), so this is recorded here rather than folded into that tip.

items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Current:** the desktop attachment tray prints a file's size with the *next* unit's number still attached to the *previous* unit name. A file of `1_048_575` bytes (1 MiB − 1) reads **`1024KB`** on its card, and `1_073_741_823` bytes (1 GiB − 1) reads **`1024MB`**. The upload limit is printed by the same shape of ladder and shows **`1024 MiB`** for `1_073_741_823`.

The unit is picked from the *unrounded* value (`1023.999 KB`, so the loop stops at KB) while the printed number comes from `Math.round(value)` at that scale, which rounds up to `1024` — a number no KB value can hold.

**Expected:** a size one byte under 1 MiB reads `1MB`, one byte under 1 GiB reads `1GB`; the limit one byte under 1 GiB reads `1 GiB`. Never `1024KB` / `1024MB` / `1024 MiB`.

**Minimal reproduction** (pure functions, no DOM):

```ts
import { formatFileSize } from "./apps/desktop/src/app/attachments.js";
import { formatByteLimit } from "./apps/desktop/src/app/upload.js";

console.log(formatFileSize(1_048_575));      // 1024KB
console.log(formatFileSize(1_073_741_823));  // 1024MB
console.log(formatByteLimit(1_073_741_823)); // 1024 MiB
```

Observed on `main` `89cd2d30` (`node --import tsx`):

```text
value          formatFileSize   formatByteLimit
1_048_574      1024KB           1024 KiB
1_048_575      1024KB           1024 KiB
1_048_576      1MB              1 MiB
1_073_741_823  1024MB           1024 MiB
```

**Where.**

- `apps/desktop/src/app/attachments.ts:161-173` — `formatFileSize` (attachment card, `:167` loop condition `value >= 1024`, `:172` prints the rounded value).
- `apps/desktop/src/app/upload.ts:36-47` — `formatByteLimit` (upload limit line, `:42` loop, `:46` `Number(value.toFixed(1))`).

**Note on scope.** `#867` fixed the same class in `apps/web` (`formatBytes` in the provenance modal and the CSV inspector). The desktop app has its own ladders and shares no code with `apps/web`, so this is a separate defect in a separate app, not a duplicate: the web fix never reaches `apps/desktop`.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`.
- `apps/desktop` (`@sciencediscovery/desktop`), pure functions checked with `node --import tsx` on Node `v22.23.2`, pnpm `11.1.2`, Linux x86_64.
- No DOM, no running stack: both formatters are pure and are called by the attachment tray and the upload limit line.

### Additional Information

Found while dogfooding `apps/web` size formatting (`#867`) and checking the desktop shell for the same reading: `apps/desktop` builds its own unit ladders (`attachments.ts`, `upload.ts`, and a separate whole-GiB one in `resource-format.ts`).

### Version Information

- `main` `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (2026-11-04).
- `apps/desktop` package version as of that commit.

items.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate (terms and results at the end of this report).
- [x] I am on the current `main` (`89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`).
- [x] This is a defect in existing behaviour, not a feature request.
- [x] I can reproduce it offline, with no Neo4j and no model call.

## Detailed Description

The memory-graph sidecar caps every read query at `_NODE_LIMIT = 500` and reports
`truncated: true` when the result was cut. The cut flag is computed **after** the
Cypher `LIMIT`, so a result set that is exactly 500 nodes long cannot be told
apart from one that was cut — and the code reports it as cut:

`services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/query.py:431`
```python
"truncated": len(hits) >= _NODE_LIMIT,
```

The module's own contract, a few lines above, says the opposite:

`services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/query.py:319`
```
# shared hard cap (500); results beyond it carry ``truncated: True``.
```

"beyond the cap" is not "at the cap". The same off-by-one is repeated at every
read that returns the shared result shape:

- `query.py:272` — `get_subgraph` nodes
- `query.py:431` — `query_match` hits
- `query.py:465` — `by_node_type` hits
- `query.py:518` — `by_edge_type` edges
- `query.py:898` — member-scope nodes

Each of these runs its Cypher with `LIMIT $limit` bound to `_NODE_LIMIT`
(`query.py:424`, `:458`, `:496`, ...), so the Python side can never observe a
501st row and `len(...) >= 500` is true for a complete 500-node answer.

### What the reader sees

The flag is forwarded verbatim by the API (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3506`
for `POST /api/memory/query/match`, mapped in
`packages/memory/src/memory-graph.ts:1082`) and rendered by the memory-graph
panel:

`apps/web/src/MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:1336`
```tsx
setSearchNote(result.hits.length
  ? t(result.truncated ? "memory.search.matchesTruncated" : "memory.search.matches",
    { shown: onScreen, total: result.hits.length })
  : t("memory.search.noMatches"));
```
`apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:1376` — `"memory.search.matchesTruncated":
"{shown} of {total}+ (truncated) match(es) in view"`

So a query with exactly 500 matches in the graph reports

```
12 of 500+ (truncated) match(es) in view
```

The trailing `+` asserts that at least one additional match exists. There is
none: 500 is every match the graph holds. The subgraph badge path is the same
shape — `MemoryGraphExplorer.tsx:1718` draws the "(truncated)" badge from
`graph.truncated`, which `get_subgraph` sets by the same `>=` comparison, so a
Session whose graph is exactly 500 nodes is badged as a partial graph.

This is the class #655 ("Structure preview reports truncated: true while
returning the complete source") was fixed for in #659: the flag must mean
"content was left out", not "the last page came back full".

### Minimal reproduction (no Neo4j)

`services/memory-graph/tests/test_smoke.py` already has the pattern this needs:
a fake driver that satisfies `is_reachable()` and returns canned rows, so
`query_match` runs its real Python path. Add a fake result that yields exactly
`_NODE_LIMIT` rows, then:

```python
result = query.query_match("TP53")          # fake driver: 500 Paper nodes
assert result["truncated"] is False         # nothing was left out
```

Current output, on `89cd2d30`:

```
# rows=500 hits=500 truncated=True
AssertionError: exactly 500 matches (the graph holds nothing more) reported as truncated
```

and the control case at 501 is already correct apart from the count of returned
rows, which the fix has to keep at the cap:

```python
result = query.query_match("TP53")          # fake driver: 501 Paper nodes
assert result["truncated"] is True
assert len(result["hits"]) == 500
```

Run it with:

```
cd services/memory-graph
uv run --project . --extra test pytest tests/ -k truncated
```

### Expected

- exactly `_NODE_LIMIT` matches → `truncated: false`, and the web note drops the
  `+` and says "N of N match(es) in view".
- more than `_NODE_LIMIT` matches → `truncated: true`, `len(hits) == 500`, note
  keeps the `+`.
- a subgraph with exactly 500 nodes → no "(truncated)" badge.

### Fix direction (one slice, no new query)

Ask for one row more than the cap and let the extra row decide the flag:
bind the Cypher limit to `_NODE_LIMIT + 1`, take `cut = len(rows) > _NODE_LIMIT`,
return `rows[:_NODE_LIMIT]`, and set `truncated: cut`. The same two-line change
covers all five sites above; `total` keeps its current meaning (the number of
rows the response carries), so no client contract changes. A dev may prefer to
count the raw rows before `_to_hit` drops unknown labels — that is the more
correct variant, since a dropped label is not a truncation either.

## Environment

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`, commit `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`
- Component: `services/memory-graph` (Python sidecar), read path only
- Node v22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2, Python 3.10.12, `uv` project `services/memory-graph`
- No Neo4j needed for the reproduction (fake driver); a live graph is needed only to see the panel text itself

## Version Information

- ScienceDiscovery 0.3.0 development tree (`main` @ `89cd2d30`)
- Affected: memory-graph search note and subgraph "(truncated)" badge in `apps/web`, for any graph whose result set reaches the 500-node cap

## Duplicate check (open + closed)

Searched issues with `truncated`, `memory graph`, `500 matches`, `NODE_LIMIT`:

- #655 (closed) / #659 (closed), #649/#652 (closed), #650 (closed), #660/#663 (closed), #368 (closed) — artifact/structure/text **preview** truncation. Same class, different surface; #655's fix is the precedent this report follows, not a duplicate of it.
- #841, #842 (open) — artifact preview `maxRows` clamp and clipped-preview notice. Different endpoint, different flag.
- #210/#212 (closed), #836 (closed), #725/#723 (closed) — memory-graph folding, health request bound, Escape handling. Passed the same read path but none changes `truncated`.
- #770, #801, #345 — memory-graph configuration/desktop features. Not this flag.
- `NODE_LIMIT` returns no issue at all.

items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

Some settings can already be changed in the chat. The agent can pick a registered model, change thinking settings, choose a skill or a library, enable a connector that is ready, and change this session's review preference. Every other setting still sends the user to the settings page.

This issue brings the remaining ordinary settings onto that same path. The agent proposes a change. The card shows the current value, the new value, and where it will apply: the deployment, a shared resource, the project, or the session. The user checks the card and confirms in the chat. A later task uses the saved value.

### Design Ideas

Reuse the configuration service and the confirmation card that already exist. The agent reads the current value, where that value is inherited from, and the choices that are allowed, then proposes only those fields.

The settings this path must cover:

1. Package sources and runners. Choose an existing pip or conda preset. Assign a registered runner to a project or a session, or turn that assignment off.
2. Proxy. Manage the shared proxy. Choose the proxy a model provider uses, and the proxy MCP uses. Changing the deployment's default route is confirmed on its own.
3. Web search and credentials. Change search, fetch, and cache within what Native and JiuwenSwarm already support. Replace or clear the key of a supported provider through the secure input.
4. Review, exploration tree, JSON preview, and inheritance. Choose whether the reviewer takes part. Pick a registered exploration-tree template and a supported strength and budget. Turn the dedicated JSON preview on or off. A limited set of ordinary project and session settings can go back to being inherited.
5. Safety and approval. Change the sandbox network, this session's approval, the default approval for a new session, and the low-risk auto-save policy. Each of these is confirmed on its own.
6. Models and providers. Edit the metadata and API identity of a model that already exists, and edit a shared provider connection together with its credential. Before saving, check the real address that will receive the credential.
7. Memory and Neo4j. Turn the workbench memory graph on or off. Choose local or Neo4j. Set the address and the user name. Replace or clear the Neo4j password on its own.
8. MCP servers that are already registered. Edit the metadata, timeout, enabled state, and supported overrides. Replace an existing credential header through the secure input. Deleting a custom server is confirmed on its own.

A permission or a safety policy is never folded into an ordinary confirmation. A secret is typed only into the secure input. The proposal, the preview, and the receipt show no secret.

These stay on the settings page for this issue: creating an MCP server, changing an MCP URL, OAuth, arbitrary headers or environment variables, import, and install. Registering a runner or SSH, creating an environment, and installing or removing packages. Plugin-only settings. The global reviewer-specialist switch. Free prompt text, scoring weights, and round counts inside an exploration-tree template.

### Involved Public APIs

Extend the conversational configuration API that already exists: which capabilities it can propose, which fields a proposal carries, and which confirmation a change requires. Discovery, preview, and save stay the same mechanisms. Each setting keeps its own scope, its own checks, and its own place for credentials. A caller that draws the card follows the capability and the confirmation the response returns.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

The settings list, the card, and the request service are shared by every area above. The result has to hold for Native and for JiuwenSwarm, for a project value and a session value that inherits it, and for a queued task that already took a snapshot of its configuration. Proxy choices and safety policy change how web search, model calls, MCP, and the sandbox reach the network. When a save must reconnect an external service or restart a process, that step is part of accepting the change.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Start the real application. With a real model, use the browser chat to propose a change in each area above, confirm it, save it, refresh, and read the value back. Run a later task and see that it uses the new value. Where a restart or a reconnect is required, include that step.

Refuse a permission change, a credential change, a proxy change, and an external connection. The secret must be absent from the chat, the preview, and the receipt.

Record the code version, the environment, and the result. After the areas land together, the shared settings list, the card, and the request service still answer as they do now.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each setting listed above can be proposed in the chat. The card shows the current value, the new value, and where it applies.
- [ ] A permission, a safety policy, a credential destination, and deleting a custom server each wait for their own confirmation.
- [ ] A secret is entered only in the secure input and does not appear in the chat, the preview, or the receipt.
- [ ] After save and refresh, the value reads back, and a later task uses it.
- [ ] Settings named as out of scope above are unchanged.
- [ ] The check record names the code version, the environment, and the result.

### Additional Information

Package sources and runners are already in `main` (#727). The other areas are in #734, #737, #756, #758, #763, #770, and #773. This issue describes the change. Those pull requests are where the code is reviewed.

---

### 🚀 背景描述

有些设置已经能在对话里改。Agent 可以选择已注册的模型、调整思考参数、选择技能或技能库、启用已就绪的连接器、修改本会话的审阅偏好。其余设置仍要打开设置页。

本 issue 要做的是把其余的普通设置也放进这条路径。Agent 提出修改。卡片上显示当前值、新值，以及改完作用在部署、共享资源、Project 还是 Session。用户核对卡片，在对话里确认。之后的任务使用保存后的值。

### 设计思路

沿用已有的配置服务和确认卡片。Agent 先读取当前值、这个值从哪里继承、有哪些允许的选项，然后只提案这些字段。

这条路径要覆盖的设置：

1. 包源和 Runner。选择已有的 pip 或 conda 预设。把已注册的 Runner 分配给 Project 或 Session，或取消这项分配。
2. 代理。管理共享代理。选择模型供应商使用的代理，以及 MCP 使用的代理。修改部署的默认路由单独确认。
3. 网页搜索和凭据。在 Native 和 JiuwenSwarm 已经支持的范围内修改搜索、抓取和缓存。已支持供应商的 Key 通过专用输入替换或清除。
4. 审阅、探索树、JSON 预览和继承。选择 Reviewer 是否参与。选择已注册的探索树模板，以及支持的强度和预算。开关 JSON 专用预览。有限的 Project 和 Session 普通设置可以恢复为继承。
5. 安全和审批。修改沙箱网络、当前会话的审批、新会话的默认审批、低风险自动保存。每一项单独确认。
6. 模型和供应商。修改已有模型的说明信息和 API 身份，修改共享供应商的连接及其凭据。保存前核对真正接收凭据的地址。
7. Memory 和 Neo4j。开关工作台记忆图谱。选择本地或 Neo4j。填写地址和用户名。Neo4j 密码单独替换或清除。
8. 已经注册的 MCP。修改说明信息、超时、启用状态和支持的覆盖项。已有的凭据 header 通过专用输入替换。删除自定义服务器单独确认。

权限和安全策略不并进普通确认。密钥只在专用输入里填写。提案、预览和回执里不出现密钥。

本 issue 仍留在设置页的有：新建 MCP、修改 MCP 地址、OAuth、任意 header 或环境变量、导入和安装。注册 Runner 或 SSH、创建运行环境、安装或卸载软件包。插件专有设置。全局 Reviewer Specialist 开关。探索树模板里的自由提示词、评分权重和轮次。

### 涉及的公开接口

扩展已有的对话配置接口：它可以提案哪些能力、提案带哪些字段、一项修改需要哪种确认。发现、预览和保存仍用原来的机制。每项设置保留自己的作用范围、校验和凭据存放位置。绘制卡片的调用方按返回里的能力和确认要求来显示。

### 与其他模块的关系

设置清单、卡片和请求服务是上面每一块共用的。结果要同时适用于 Native 和 JiuwenSwarm，适用于 Project 的值以及继承它的 Session，也适用于已经拍下配置快照的排队任务。代理选择和安全策略会改变网页搜索、模型调用、MCP 和沙箱如何访问网络。一次保存如果必须重连外部服务或重启进程，这一步也算进验收。

### 测试设计与测试计划

启动真实应用。用真实模型，在浏览器对话里对上面每一块设置提出修改、确认、保存、刷新后读回。再跑一个后续任务，确认它用的是新值。需要重启或重连的，把这一步算进去。

拒绝一次权限修改、一次凭据修改、一次代理修改和一次外部连接。密钥不得出现在对话、预览或回执里。

记录代码版本、环境和结果。这些设置合在一起之后，共享的设置清单、卡片和请求服务仍按现在的方式响应。

### 验收标准

- [ ] 上面列出的每项设置都能在对话里提案。卡片显示当前值、新值和作用位置。
- [ ] 权限、安全策略、凭据接收地址、删除自定义服务器，各自单独等待确认。
- [ ] 密钥只在专用输入里填写，不出现在对话、预览或回执里。
- [ ] 保存并刷新后能读回该值，后续任务使用该值。
- [ ] 上面写明留在设置页的那些设置保持不变。
- [ ] 检查记录写明代码版本、环境和结果。

### 补充信息

包源和 Runner 已经在 `main`（#727）。其余几块在 #734、#737、#756、#758、#763、#770、#773。本 issue 描述这次改动。代码审查在这些 pull request 里进行。

items.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

The Windows desktop installer weighed **797.6 MiB** at the f26 baseline (`836,309,864 B`, SHA256 `9f82926d…`). A payload audit (per-package import scans plus reverse-dependency tracing) confirmed roughly **1.2 GB of uncompressed dead weight**: dependency packages never imported by runtime code, giant binaries pulled in by extras (claude.exe 237 MB, the codex toolchain ~437 MB, the playwright driver 88 MB, uv.exe 49 MB), lint-group dev tools (mypy/ruff/pylint ~40 MB), transitive dependencies of chromadb/jinja2/a2ui (kubernetes 37 MB, onnxruntime 42 MB, babel 32 MB, google_adk ~20 MB), and heavy duplication across the five Python service envs (pydantic/fastapi/uvicorn each stored five times).

Four waves of optimization have been implemented, taking the installer from f26 to **578.0 MiB (`606,126,666 B`), −219.6 MiB / −27.5%** — W1 dead-weight removal, W2 env merge, W3 version alignment, W4 build gates + locales trim. Each wave shipped its own installer and was verified independently. The uncompressed payload went **2827 → 1694 MB (−40%)**.

**Where the work stands.** The four waves live in **PR #834** (open, head `61c59a46`, base `main`), pushed to the author's fork branch `sizeopt/f26-6to2`. The PR is **not merged**, the repository has no `release4` tag or GitHub release (latest release is `v0.3.0`). So `578.0 MiB` is a **measured local build**, not a published artifact. This issue is the single tracking item for that work; the earlier Chinese-only twin has been merged into it and closed.

### Design Ideas

Wave-based: every wave produces its own installer, is verified on its own, and can be reverted alone (three independent commits, plus reversible JW patches).

Two units are used throughout and must not be mixed — every size figure below states which one it is:
- **uncompressed payload** (what assemble lays on disk), and
- **installer** (7z-compressed; f26 overall retention 29.6%).

The first projection round got this wrong and over-promised by 43–113 MB per wave, because it applied the *overall* retention to slices that compress far better than average. The corrected rule: project a wave with the **mixed retention of the content actually being removed**. W1 measured 18.6% on its removed slice (dominated by `.py` sources such as `claude_agent_sdk`).

**W1 — slim the JW payload + strip the codex vendor (done, installer −184.2 MiB → 613.4 MiB / `643,132,732 B`; payload 2827 → 1786 MB, −1041 MB)**

1. `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh`: `uv sync` gains `--no-default-groups`, so lint/test groups never enter the runtime venv (**measured ~40 MB**: mypy 12 + mypyc 5 + the `fb62009__mypyc` .pyd 19 + pylint/astroid/codespell etc.). The same change fixes a hard-coded POSIX `jw_bin` that broke setup under Git Bash — it now picks `Scripts/` by existence.
2. **claude/codex extras close (the bulk of this wave).** A fresh `uv sync` never installs extras; the old tree was an `--all-extras` leftover. Measured old-vs-new venv diff: `claude_agent_sdk` (238 MB) is no longer installed; playwright (104 MB) is then formally moved out of JW main deps by patch 0018. Together these took the JW venv **1578 → 895 MB** (746 MB after the patch).
3. New `win_desktop/scripts/lib/payload-slim.mjs`: an assemble-time whitelist sweep for transitive deps uv cannot exclude (kubernetes / onnxruntime / babel / google_adk / the mypy family / claude_agent_sdk / playwright / uv, plus venv `Scripts` launchers and the nested `google/adk`). Every rule carries an audit citation in-code, and the rule set is unit-tested (5/5). Backstop philosophy: fresh trees never install them; stale trees get swept.
4. assemble drops the `@openai/codex` vendored native toolchain (**~437 MB uncompressed**). Verified the SDK never touches those binaries at import time (it resolves them at `Codex` construction), so api startup is unaffected — only a codex specialist *run* fails at use time. That failure mode is the reason the degradation contract below exists.
5. JW patch chain gains `0018-desktop-slim-deps`: playwright/uv removed from main deps in JW's pyproject (uv.lock regenerated into the patch; chain **14 → 15** — `main` carries 14 patch files, 0001–0010 plus the 0015/0016/0016b/0017 startup patches), and `huawei_selectors.py`'s top-level import degrades to `Any` via try/except (**−156 MB**; every runtime call site was verified to be a function-level lazy import or pip fallback).

**W2 — merge five service envs into one uv workspace (done, installer −30.1 MiB → 583.3 MiB / `611,529,375 B`; payload → 1684.5 MB, envs-template 525.3 → 423.7 MB)**

1. A **virtual** workspace root at `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.uv.workspace]`, five members, no `[project]` so the root is never itself installed). The five per-service `uv.lock` files are deleted; one root `uv.lock` resolves 68 packages, every conflict taking the highest version inside the constraint intersection (fastapi 0.162 / websockets 17.4 / pydantic 2.14 / numpy 2.5.4 / pandas 3.1).
2. `start-stack.mjs`: five per-service syncs → one workspace sync (still including the evolve `candidates` extra); all four service pythons resolve to `envs/sd-services`.
3. `bootstrap.ts` `venvNames` → `["sd-services"]`; `assemble-backend.mjs` `VENV_NAMES` likewise.
4. Trade-off, stated explicitly: this revisits the earlier "never merge venvs" principle. After highest-version unification the only hard conflict was websockets (JW caps `<16`), handled by the W3 patch. The accepted cost is that **any single service's dependency upgrade now needs full-stack regression**, since there is one env.

**W3 — version alignment + a falsified idea (done; no installer-size wave of its own)**

JW patch `0019-align-workspace-versions` raises the websockets cap `<16` → `<18` and aligns numpy/pandas with the workspace (2.5.4 / 3.1.0), manifest 15 → 16. Two findings worth recording:
- websockets **17 is pinned out** by google-genai's `<17`, so the lock stays on 15.0.1 — zero behaviour change. Every call site was audited and carries a legacy→new-API fallback, which is what made raising the cap safe at all.
- **Hardlink dedup across venvs was designed, measured, and closed as ineffective.** Identical content across the JW venv and the shared venv measured 59.9 MB, but 7z solid-window mechanics plus venv isolation mean hardlinks buy nothing in the installer. Closing it avoided spending engineering effort on a lever that cannot pay. The merge benefit was already banked in W2.

**W4 — build gates + locales trim (done, installer −5.3 MiB → 578.0 MiB)**

assemble gained four hard gates, all modelled on the JW official packaging scripts and all following the same philosophy — *self-proving, always printed, hard-failing*:
- **precompile failure fails the build** (was a warning). This roots out the "payload pyc silently skipped" class of defect.
- **A1 payload import self-check** — run the *payload's own* interpreters and import the shipped modules (JW: `jiuwenswarm.common.config`, `gateway.app_gateway`, `server.app_agentserver`; services: `sciencediscovery_gateway/_memory_graph/_evolve/_adapter`). This is the gate that would have caught the silent precompile skip. It caught a real timing bug on its first run.
- **A2 RequiredFiles manifest** — 9 entries an installer must contain (SEA, patch manifest, the editable `.pth`), hard failure if any is missing.
- **A4 payload size always printed** at the end of assemble.

Electron locales were trimmed by a new afterPack hook (`win_desktop/scripts/after-pack-trim-locales.cjs`): **55 shipped → 52 removed → 3 kept** (en-US / zh-CN / zh-TW). The release4 build log records `[afterPack] trimmed 52 Electron locale pak(s)`; ~45 MB raw became ~5 MiB in the installer — the smallest of the four waves, and a good reminder that raw-MB and installer-MiB are different currencies.

**Phase 5 — quality governance triggered by install testing (code written; release5 packaging; install verification pending)**

Not in PR #834. Five items, all from measured install-tree evidence rather than projection:
- **Path budget (A5 gate + layout shortening).** Install root `D:\ProgramData\SD\ScienceDiscovery` measured `maxRel = 224` over 95,002 files → `maxAbs = 259` against a 259 usable budget, **margin 0**. Fixed by (a) a new assemble gate that walks the payload tree and prints `maxRel` with dual thresholds (runtime 189 / build-time 170) and fails over the limit, and (b) shortening the payload prefix `backend\.sciencediscovery-data\jiuwenswarm\src` → **`backend\jw`** (saves 36 chars, `maxRel` 224 → 188). A bug in the gate itself was found and fixed during calibration: it computed paths relative to the build dir, undercounting by 6 chars on short build trees — exactly enough to mask a violation.
- **Startup performance.** The hot-start breakdown attributed **12.42 s of 31.97 s (39%)** to a single synchronous import (`install_subagent_observability_hook()`, pulling 3,946 modules). JW patch `0020-lazy-observability-import` moves it to `asyncio.to_thread`, adds a third idempotent guard in `get_agent()` (matching the two already added by 0015/0016), and cancels the task in shutdown's `finally`. Patch chain 16 → **17**, `verify` exit 0. **Expected** hot start 31.97 s → ~19.5 s — *expected, not measured*.
- **`verifyPatches` fixed cost (0.87 s).** Fingerprint cache (patch name+size+mtime vs. the src manifest), with `--force-verify` / `JIUWENSWARM_FORCE_VERIFY=1` escape hatches. Implementing it exposed a genuine pre-existing bug: `recordVerified` called `writeFileSync` **without importing it**, the `ReferenceError` was swallowed by a surrounding `try/catch`, the marker never landed, and the cache never hit — so every start repaid the 0.87 s. That cost *is* the bug.
- **Wizard path validation.** `mkdirSync("E")` resolved drive-relative and created `<install-dir>\E`; `probeDataDir` rejected empty strings but not non-absolute ones. Added an `isAbsolute` + `parse().root` guard ahead of any filesystem side effect, plus defence-in-depth in `ensureWritableDir` (returns false instead of mkdir on a non-fully-qualified path). Shell unit tests 118 → **121** (3 new cases).
- **Measurement discipline.** Any startup number must now state its measurement tree (dev / packaged) and its end-to-end definition. The dev-tree figure of 17.8 s had been quoted externally as an install result; the real packaged number was 31.97 s — a 75% deviation. The f26 record itself says install testing was pending, and f26 was never measured on a real machine, so **no f26 hot-start baseline exists to compare against**; the three-profile release4 run is the first packaged baseline in this line.

**Degradation contract for what was cut** (added in response to review — this is the part that was previously one sentence):

| Capability removed | What the user sees | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `claude_agent_sdk` (claude CLI runtime) | Shows as **"not installed"** in the UI | JW's `external_cli_runtime` probes with `find_spec`; absence is a state, not an exception |
| codex vendored toolchain | **Fails at delegation time**, not at configuration time — this is the weak spot | `Codex` resolves the binaries at construction; api startup is unaffected |
| playwright (2 browser-skill scrape functions) | Skill function raises on use; module import is safe | `huawei_selectors.py` top-level import degrades to `Any` via try/except; call sites are lazy/pip-fallback |
| uv (JW self-upgrade / extension install acceleration) | Falls back to **pip**, slower but functional | uv removed from JW main deps |

None of these sit on the first-run or main-dialog path. The codex row is the one that needs a decision: `docs/en/advanced-setup/configure-specialists.md` still documents `runtime.kind: "codex"` (and `"claude-code"` / `"acp"`) as usable, so a user following the docs configures something that only fails when delegated to, on Windows only — an undocumented platform difference. The intended fix is an explicit *unavailable* state at configuration time (specialist runtime card + delegation error) rather than a use-time exception, plus a platform note in both language versions of that doc.

### Involved Public APIs

None. Every change is packaging/build-chain (assemble, setup scripts, the JW patch chain) or desktop-shell-internal (bootstrap env vars and payload paths). No HTTP API, IPC channel, preload bridge or configuration surface changes.

What does change is *availability* of four capabilities on Windows, per the degradation table above — and each has a pip/probe fallback, none on the first-run or main-dialog path.
