Fixes #884

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What is wrong

`GET /api/sessions/:session/artifact-versions/:version/diff` answered **500 `Internal server error`** when either version of the pair is not textual, and logged a false `unclassified_request_error`. `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:357` threw a plain `Error("Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions")`, whose prose matches no client-input pattern in `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` and no not-found mapper in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, so the top-level catch classified a client-input problem as a server fault.

Measured at `7057aaf6` with two `application/zip` versions of one artifact in one session (red commit `0be111de` only):

```
GET /api/sessions/<id>/artifact-versions/<version>/diff
500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
```

The same request, with logging configured the way `startPlatform` does (not by `createApiServer` alone), wrote:

```
ERROR [api] event=unclassified_request_error errorMessage="Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions" method=GET path=/api/sessions/<id>/artifact-versions/<version>/diff status=500
```

## The fix — option 2 from the issue, in the helper

`artifactVersionDiff` now throws `new ApiStatusError(400, "Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions")`. The rejection is classified by **class** (the top-level catch answers `ApiStatusError.statusCode` before any prose matching), and it sits where the rule lives, so every caller of the helper answers the same 400 instead of only this route. No new message pattern was added to `isKnownClientInputError`.

The versions both exist; this is not a missing resource, which is why it is a 400 and not the 404 family `#881` adds.

### Why the route was not touched (overlap with #881)

`#881` (ours, open) rewrites the `diff` route block in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` for the missing-`to` / missing-`against` cases. Hoisting the media-type check into that same block would (a) collide textually with `#881`, and (b) put the from-version resolution in two places: the route would have to repeat what the helper already computes, and the next caller of the helper would get the 500 again. This fix touches only `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts`; the two behaviours are complementary (`#881` = missing version, this = both present but not comparable), so whichever lands second keeps both without a conflict.

### Import note

`services/api/src/runs/index.ts` already imports `artifacts/index.ts`, so importing `ApiStatusError` from `runs` inside `artifacts` would have closed a cycle between two large modules. The class therefore lives in `services/api/src/http/api-status-error.ts`, which imports nothing; `runs/index.ts` imports it and re-exports it (its public API is unchanged, so the existing import in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` still works), and `artifacts/index.ts` imports the leaf directly. No reverse edge was added and no cycle exists.

The leaf move keeps the identity check honest: `services/api/src/http/index.ts` still matches `error instanceof ApiStatusError` against the class the helper throws, which the new test proves by driving that exact path — a divergent class object would answer 500, not the 400 asserted there.

## Red → green

`services/api/src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` (test-only commit `0be111de`) seeds versions through `SessionStore.createArtifactVersion` and asks the real route, so no execution is driven: an `application/zip` pair, a pair that switches from `text/markdown` to `application/zip`, and a `text/markdown` control pair that must keep diffing.

Red at `7057aaf6`:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts
not ok 1 - a non-textual artifact pair answers a client error instead of 500
  error: |-
    binary pair must answer 400 with the reason, not 500
      body: { error: 'Internal server error' }
      status: 500
# tests 1 / # pass 0 / # fail 1
```

Green at `207243a7` (same command): `1 test / 1 pass / 0 fail`, exit 0. That run was still green by luck — see the review fix below.

The false log is gone in the same manual repro: `STATUS 400 {"error":"Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions"}`, `grep -c unclassified_request_error` → `0`, and the request is logged as `http_request_failed … statusCode=400`.

## Review fix — the fixture seeded after the server's `ready` chain

`sciencediscovery-bot`'s thread on `artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts:130` is right and this is a test-only correction: `createApiServer` returns before `ready` (which ends in `store.load()`) has run, and the fixture seeded after `server.listen`, so the test passed only when the seeds landed before that load. Two commits, no product code changed:

- `b3eb58b8` makes the ordering explicit: a request settles `ready` before the seeds. It is red, deterministically, on a machine that starts the server quickly:
  ```
  not ok 1 - a non-textual artifact pair answers a client error instead of 500
      binary pair must answer 400 with the reason, not 500
      +     error: 'Internal server error'
      +   status: 500
  ```
  (the 500 is the pre-fix behaviour: the route's `store` has already loaded a catalog without these versions, `getArtifactVersion` returns `undefined`, and `artifacts/index.ts` throws the plain `Error("Artifact version not found")`.)
- `76e911b5` removes the race instead of winning it: `startHttpFixture` is split into `createFixture` + `startHttpServer(context, fixture)`, the test writes every version first and starts the server afterwards, so `ready` loads a catalog that already contains them. No wait, retry or timeout is involved.

Green five consecutive runs of the same command, one process each:

```
[run 1] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 2] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 3] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 4] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 5] # pass 1 # fail 0
```

`tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` exit 0; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` exit 0. This review fix alone is `1 file, +14/−7` (`git diff --stat 207243a7..76e911b5`).

## Validation

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| new test, red | `node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` | `1/0/1`, exit 1 (at `7057aaf6` + test commit) |
| new test, green | same | `1 test / 1 pass / 0 fail`, exit 0 (at `207243a7`) |
| UT slice for the touched module | `node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts src/artifact-lifecycle.test.ts src/provenance.test.ts src/dashboard.test.ts` | `88 tests / 88 pass / 0 fail`, exit 0 (at `207243a7`) |
| typecheck (api) | `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` | exit 0, 0 errors |
| typecheck (tests project) | `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | exit 0, 0 errors |

Environment note, so the numbers are reproducible: this worktree's `node_modules` predates the current lockfile and the sandbox cannot write to the pnpm store, so `@types/ssh2` (declared by `packages/executor`) and the `packages/feedback-worker/node_modules` workspace link were missing before the first typecheck run. Without them the api typecheck reported 18 errors, all in `packages/executor/src/ssh-connection.ts` / `ssh-keys.ts` (missing `ssh2` declarations) and the tests typecheck 4 in `packages/feedback-worker` — none in the touched files. Installing the declared `@types/ssh2` into the local `node_modules` and adding that workspace link brings both to exit 0; no repository file was changed for it.

Not run: the full `services/api` UT suite (only the module slice above), the L2/ST/E2E layers, and a real server with a real artifact-producing execution — the route test seeds the catalog directly because the media-type rule is checked before any CAS read, which is exactly the point the issue makes.

`git diff --stat 7057aaf6…HEAD`: 4 files, `+247/−13` (`artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` +199, `http/api-status-error.ts` +34, `runs/index.ts` +6/−12, `artifacts/index.ts` +8/−1), 5 commits (`0be111de` test, `b6de0d8e` fix, `207243a7` the class move that removes the import cycle, `b3eb58b8` red and `76e911b5` green for the review fix above).

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: comparing two binary artifact versions (two `.zip` uploads, a text version against a later binary one) now answers `400 {"error":"Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions"}` instead of `500 Internal server error`, and the server no longer logs a false `unclassified_request_error` for a request the client can avoid. Textual pairs still diff as before.

Compatibility and migration: none — the 400 body is the message the helper already carried; only its status and classification change.

## Rebase onto `9feafa27` (2026-11-09)

The branch was `dirty`, so it was rebased onto current `main` `9feafa273088aa1c422fc2369f1d4001df9c0c9a`. New tip **`cefe1ebd7956b373e0fa67eb7849f8c2d7353507`**.

Conflicts resolved by taking `main`, not by merging text: `main` has already absorbed the leaf-module refactor this branch carried, so
- `services/api/src/http/api-status-error.ts` is an add/add conflict — `main`'s copy and this branch's copy were identical in substance, and `main`'s file stays as-is;
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` now already does `import { ApiStatusError } from "../http/api-status-error.js"; export { ApiStatusError };`, so the branch's refactor commit reduces to the one import change in `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts`.

That is why the diffstat is smaller than before the rebase and why the file list changed — `main` moved, not this change:

```
git diff --stat 9feafa27..cefe1ebd
 .../api/src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts    | 199 +++++++++++++++++++++
 services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts                |   9 +-
 2 files changed, 207 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```

The five commits are unchanged in order and content (`96552957` test → `ae248cc0` fix → `d3c3c7dc` refactor → `e491b1bf` test → `cefe1ebd` test).

Readings on the rebased tip: `node --import tsx --test services/api/src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` → `# tests 1 / # pass 1 / # fail 0`; `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → exit 0; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` → exit 0.

Fixes #935

The Specialist settings pane prints "Internal server error" for ordinary client mistakes: a name that is already taken, an id that no longer exists, an edit of a read-only built-in. The three routes forward the store's plain `Error`s straight to the catch-all, whose classifier recognises none of those messages, so every rejection becomes a 500. The neighbouring MCP-servers surface already answers these shapes — 400 for a rejected input, 404 for a missing id — and so do the model, provider, proxy-server, project and permission-grant routes, so the Specialist routes were the outlier rather than the norm.

## What changed

`services/api/src/http/index.ts` only, in the block the three Specialist handlers occupy:

- `POST /api/specialists`, `PUT /api/specialists/:id` and `DELETE /api/specialists/:id` now run through `answerSpecialistRoute`, which keeps the store's message verbatim and picks the status from `specialistErrorStatus`:
  - `Specialist not found` → `404`;
  - the store's own rejections → `400` — `Specialist name already exists`, `Specialist skills|connectors are unavailable…`, `Built-in specialists are read-only…`, and the messages the shared classifier already recognises (`is required`, `must`, `cannot`, …);
  - anything else → rethrown to the catch-all, so a genuine internal fault still reads `500` instead of being relabelled as client input.
- `readJson` is still evaluated before the guarded call, so a malformed body keeps the 400 the classifier gives it.

Untouched, as the issue requires: `services/api/src/store.ts` (its wording is the message the pane shows), `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` (held by the in-flight length-rejection fix), and `apps/web` (the client prints whatever the server says).

## Red first

Commit `3a3c9de4` adds the route test only, against the unfixed server. Six cases: the four rejected shapes fail, the two regression cases (the built-in `enabled` toggle answering 200, deleting a built-in answering 400) already pass.

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/specialists-http.test.ts
not ok 1 - a taken Specialist name is a 400 that keeps the store's wording
  error: |-
    a duplicate name is client input, not a server fault

    500 !== 400
not ok 2 - an unknown Specialist id on PUT is a 404       500 !== 404
not ok 3 - an unknown Specialist id on DELETE is a 404    500 !== 404
not ok 4 - editing a built-in Specialist is a 400 …       500 !== 400
# tests 6
# pass 2
# fail 4
```

The same four shapes answer `{"error":"Internal server error"}` in the issue's probe; this test reproduces them through the real `createApiServer` on a temporary data directory.

## After the fix

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/specialists-http.test.ts
# tests 8
# pass 8
# fail 0
```

The two extra cases are the "must not regress" half of the acceptance, and both were checked to bite:

- **an unexpected fault is still a 500.** The store has no injection seam (`ApiServerDependencies` exposes `webProvider`, `connectorFetch`, `fetchModelCatalog`, `fetchUsageExchangeRate`, `ideaTreeRepository`, `mcpTransport`, `remoteCompute` — no store), so the test fails the HTTPS response itself from inside the guarded block: the injected throw must reach the catch-all as `500 Internal server error`, not be claimed as a 400. Making the route relabel every fault as 400 (the naive fix) turns exactly this case red and nothing else.
- **the status mapping is pinned directly** on `specialistErrorStatus`: 404 for the not-found message, 400 for each store rejection, and no status at all for `Catalog database is not initialized`, `database is locked` and `ENOTDIR: not a directory`.

Diffstat against `main` `2908e9e8`:

```
 services/api/src/http/index.ts            |  38 ++++++++---
 services/api/src/specialists-http.test.ts | 125 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 163 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)
```

Commits: `bd14fcef` test (red), `faff19d2` fix, `3f2fb978` test (red), `1ab96e0b` fix — four commits, rebased onto `9feafa27`.

## Rebase — `9feafa273088` (2026-11-09), and the exact-wording list

The branch was cut at `70b66fa4`; main moved to `9feafa27` and the pull request showed `mergeable=false` / `dirty`. The four commits were replayed onto `9feafa27`, nothing squashed.

One conflict, in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`: main added `extractReplacementModelId` exactly where this branch adds its two helpers. Resolved by keeping both — main's function first, then `specialistErrorStatus` and `answerSpecialistRoute`.

The remaining review finding (thread `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM60HOgb`) was that `specialistErrorStatus` still fell back to `isKnownClientInputError`, so any fault whose message happens to contain "must" or "cannot" was relabelled 400. The fallback is gone; the function now matches the store's own wording, one entry per throw in `services/api/src/store.ts`: `Specialist not found` (404), `Specialist name is required`, `Specialist description is required`, `Specialist description must be 1-500 characters`, `Specialist instructions must be 1-20000 characters`, `Specialist name already exists`, `Specialist (skills|connectors) are unavailable: …`, both built-in rejections, the referenced-Specialist rejection, and `enabled must be a boolean` (400). Any other message returns `undefined`, so it reaches the catch-all and reads 500. `SpecialistRuntimeConfigError` is untouched: it carries `SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID`, which the generic handler already answers with 400.

items.body:
Fixes #866

## What this fixes

`sanitizeUploadFilename()` in `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts` guarded an empty name, a NUL byte, absolute paths, drive letters and traversal, but not Windows reserved device names. On a Windows workspace `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`, `LPT1`–`LPT9`, `CONIN$` and `CONOUT$` resolve in every directory and with any extension, so `con.csv`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log` passed the guard and failed later inside the workspace write with a raw `EPERM`/`ENOENT` that the upload response reports as an unclassified error (`CON` targets the console device instead of failing).

The fix rejects them with the same `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` code and error shape the other guard branches use, names the offending file in the message, and strips trailing dots/spaces first because Windows ignores them (`nul.`, `CON .csv`). Legal stems that only begin with a reserved word (`conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `auxiliary.csv`) and two-digit ports (`com10.csv`) keep working — the same test asserts both directions.

The guard is platform-independent on purpose, so Linux and macOS reject these names too: portability — an upload must be writable on every supported host, and a file accepted on Linux but unusable on a Windows workspace would only fail later there.

## Red → green

The test was written first and fails on `main` `8708320f`:

```
not ok 2 - sanitizeUploadFilename rejects Windows reserved device names
  error: 'Missing expected exception: CON must be rejected as a Windows reserved device name'
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
# tests 16
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

After the fix: `node --import tsx --test src/workspace-upload.test.ts` → `# tests 16 / # pass 16 / # fail 0`.

Commits keep the pairing: `96b34e1d` test (red), `a2cebfbc` fix.

## Must-fix from review: the refused name now answers 400, not 500

`agent-ci-infra-bot` found the gap: `sanitizeUploadFilename` rejects the new names with `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH`, but the request handler decides 400-vs-500 **by message** (`isKnownClientInputError`, `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:20-32`), and the new message names none of the seven classified patterns. So the exact scenario this PR exists for — uploading `CON.csv` — answered `500 Internal server error` instead of naming the file.

Fixed on the same branch, tip `1a7b1b997bfe5e23af38d3abab59893a33e32ddd`, in two commits:

- `c0173957` (test, red first): a **route-level** test in `services/api/src/server.test.ts` (`WSP-004`) that uploads `CON.csv` through the real HTTP surface and asserts the status, the file name in the body, and that the workspace stayed empty. Before the fix: `500 !== 400`.
- `1a7b1b99` (fix): `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` joins the handler's existing stable-code branches (`services/api/src/http/index.ts`, one line beside `SKILL_LIBRARY_VALIDATION`), so the 400 follows the **code** rather than the prose a later wording edit could change. Every branch of the guard is tagged with that code, so this covers the whole family, not just the reserved-name message — no regex added, and no message reworded to please a pattern.

One consideration on where it went: the reviewer's finding points at the message classifier, and adding a ninth prose pattern there would have worked for this message only. The code branch is the smaller and more durable of the two, and it does not loosen any other 400/500 decision.

`services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` is unchanged and still 16/16 — the function-level contract this PR added is untouched; what changed is the status a client sees.

## Second finding from the same review: the stream syntax (same guard, not a new rule)

The device-name guard took its stem up to the first `.` and never looked at `:`, so `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA` were accepted while `nul.txt` was refused. Windows resolves both to the device in every directory, so that was the same reservation under another spelling:

```
"CON.csv"      -> rejected
"nul.txt"      -> rejected
"NUL. "        -> rejected
"nul:stream"   -> accepted before this commit
"con:$DATA"    -> accepted before this commit
"report:2024.csv" -> accepted before and after
```

Fixed as the **sixth branch of the same predicate**, not as a character rule: `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` now takes its stem before the colon as well as before the dot, and refuses only when that part names a device. A colon in front of an ordinary stem is a legal file name on Linux and macOS, so `report:2024.csv` and `data:2024.tsv` keep passing unchanged — refusing every `:` would have traded this bug for a portability one.

Red first, `services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts` on `1a7b1b99`:

```
not ok 1 - sanitizeUploadFilename rejects the stream syntax of a Windows reserved device name
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected

      [
    +   'accepted',
    +   'accepted'
    -   'rejected',
    -   'rejected'
      ]
```

The same test carries the over-rejection guard (`assert.equal(sanitizeUploadFilename("report:2024.csv"), "report:2024.csv")`), which was green before the fix and stays green after it. After: `# tests 18 / # pass 18 / # fail 0` across `workspace-upload.test.ts` and `error-classification.test.ts`.

Nothing outside `sanitizeUploadFilename` had to change for this — the handler branch from the first finding already answers 400 for the code — so this stays one pull request rather than becoming a second one against #866.

## Ran / Not run

Ran (exit codes verbatim):

1. `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → **0**
2. `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → **0**
3. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/workspace-upload.test.ts` → **0** (`16/16` pass)
4. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/*.test.ts` → **1**, `680 tests / 677 pass / 3 fail`; the 3 failures are all `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'reportlab'` from `services/paper/.venv/bin/python` (`papers.test.ts` PDF fixtures) — environment, not this diff, and they fail the same way on `main` in this sandbox.
5. `pnpm architecture:check` (this repo has no lint script, so the architecture gate is the substitute) → **1**, one failure `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`, `error: Could not create temporary file / Read-only file system (os error 30) at path "/home/xuke/.cache/uv/.tmp…"` — the sandbox blocks `uv`, unrelated to this diff.

Not run: the ST layer (E2E/standard journeys) locally; CI runs it.

Gates on the final tip `fdf840a8f18e6ce7ec912ba30b20e3336e0bcdc9`:

6. `pnpm --recursive typecheck` → **0**
7. `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` → **0**
8. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts src/workspace-upload.test.ts` → **0** (`18/18`, including the two stream-syntax refusals and the `report:2024.csv` accept)
9. `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-004 src/server.test.ts` → **0** (`1/1`; on `a2cebfbc` the same test is `500 !== 400`)

Not run: the whole `services/api` suite (its three `reportlab`-missing failures are the sandbox baseline in point 4, unchanged), and the `services/runner` NPU test whose worker crash is a CI environment baseline — this diff does not touch either.

## The L2 red on this tip: `standard-journeys`, one journey, not the upload path

CI run `41885511550` (job `126770786423`, `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)`)
is red on this tip: `planned 60 / executed 60 / passed 59 / failed 1`. The one
failure is

```text
test/issue-85-foreground-exec-inbox.spec.ts:299 ›
  已完成的助手仍会被它没看过的后台结果唤醒，且不改道给主 Agent
step 2, at :355
Error: the wake should be delivered to the SubAgent
Expected pattern: /^subagent:/
Received string:  ""
Timeout 60000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate
```

What the job's own artifacts say (downloaded from that run, not inferred):

- `journey-report.md`: step 1 passed in 9.7 s. Step 2 is a 60 s `expect.poll`
  for a run with `automaticWake && status === "completed"` whose
  `notificationDelivery.agentId` starts with `subagent:`; it never saw one, so it
  reported `""`. The step's own log line is `无 console 错误/警告，无失败请求`
  ("no console errors/warnings, no failed requests"), and the failure snapshot
  shows the Session with its SubAgent card still present.
- The same shard, same stack, same run: the main-Agent wake journey
  `issue-77-wake-notice` passed in 11.2 s, and the two sibling
  `issue-85-foreground-exec-inbox` journeys passed (24.6 s, 14.7 s). So the mocked
  stack and the wake dispatch were working in that very run.
- The same spec on `#856` (run `41873712399`) and `#888` (run `41883672913`) is
  success on the same `standard-journeys` slice.

So the failure is **not** "the wake went to the main Agent" — nothing was
delivered to the main Agent, the wake did not start inside the test's 60 s
bound. This diff touches `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts`,
`services/api/src/http/index.ts` and two test files; it does not touch the wake
dispatcher, the SubAgent continuation or the frontend. Recorded as an
environmental flake of that journey, not repaired here: no code in this pull
request is changed for it and the tip is unchanged.

Local reproduction was attempted and is **not** claimed as run. The prepared
mocked slice falls back to a root `pnpm install` on this workstation, and the
sandbox refuses it — a modules purge it cannot confirm
(`ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY`), and with the store pinned back to
the populated one, `EROFS` when pnpm registers the project in a read-only store.
The stack itself came up (adapter, API, runner, JiuwenSwarm instance healthy)
before that step. So there are no local pass/fail readings for this journey from
this machine; the evidence above is the CI run's own artifacts and the same
slice's results on other tips.

## Third review round (`fdf840a8` → `40fabb65`): superscript port digits

The naming document lists superscript ¹ ² ³ as port digits, so `COM¹.txt` names the first
serial port in every directory exactly like `COM1.txt`. The class was ASCII-only, so those
spellings were accepted here and failed later at write time, like the bug this PR fixes.

Red on `fdf840a8` — the case added in `535fdc86` against the unchanged sanitizer:

```
not ok 2 - sanitizeUploadFilename rejects Windows reserved device names
  error: 'Missing expected exception: COM¹.txt must be rejected as a Windows reserved device name'
# tests 17 / # pass 16 / # fail 1
```

and the same three spellings through that sanitizer: `COM¹.txt accepted`, `com².csv
accepted`, `LPT³.log accepted`.

Green on `40fabb65` — `com[1-9¹²³]` / `lpt[1-9¹²³]`, and the same probe:

```
COM¹.txt rejected    com².csv rejected    LPT³.log rejected
COM10.csv accepted   nul:stream rejected  report:2024.csv accepted
# tests 17 / # pass 17 / # fail 0
```

The neighbours are unchanged: `com10.csv` stays accepted (a two-digit port is not
COM<n>), `report:2024.csv` stays accepted (a colon is legal on Linux and macOS),
`nul:stream` stays rejected.

Gates on `40fabb65`:

```
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck   -> clean
npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json                  -> exit 0
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test        -> 1864 pass / 4 fail
```

The four failures are `spawn …/services/paper/.venv/bin/python ENOENT` in
`papers.test.ts` and `idea-tree/research-entry.test.ts`: the paper service venv is absent
on this workstation, and neither file is touched by this diff. Not run: L1/L2/E2E — the
change is a two-character-class edit in the name check, and this branch's journeys do not
upload a device name.

## Diffstat

`git diff --stat 89cd2d30…HEAD` (base `main` `89cd2d30`):

```
 services/api/src/http/index.ts            |  5 ++++
 services/api/src/server.test.ts           | 42 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts | 48 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts      | 34 +++++++++++++++++++++++

```


## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: on Windows, uploading a file named after a reserved device (`CON.csv`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, `conin$.txt`, `nul.`) is rejected up front with `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH` naming the file, instead of failing with a bare `EPERM` at write time (and, for `CON`, writing to the console device); ordinary names such as `conifer.csv` and `console.log` are still accepted.
Compatibility and migration: none — names that previously reached the filesystem unchanged are unaffected; only names Windows itself cannot write are now refused earlier.

## Rebase onto `9feafa27` (2026-11-09)

The branch was rebased onto current `main` `9feafa273088aa1c422fc2369f1d4001df9c0c9a` because the pull request was `dirty`. New tip **`74e882cbd3eb6e50241f5f52f4d696fbea09830a`**.

The eight commits are unchanged in order and content (`3d8a0448` … `74e882cb`), and the diff is the same shape as before the rebase:

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Fixes #1018

## Answering the question in the issue first

Does #1012 / #1015 already fix this? **No.** #1015 lets an explicit cancel settle such a record, so a user who cancels the stuck execution is no longer trapped. It does not stop the retry loop, and it does not stop the revision moving while that loop runs. This PR is the revision + bounded-retry half.

## What is actually established, and what is not

**Established.** `previewRevision` (`services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts`) hashes two things that moved while the session's content did not:

1. `shells: store.shellExecutions.snapshot(sessionId)` — the whole record, including `observation.nextRetryAt`, `lastObservedAt` and `failureCount`.
2. A file walk over `store.sessionDataPaths()` keyed on `size` / `mtimeMs` / `ctimeMs`; `data/execution-runs/<sessionId>.json` is re-created (tmp + rename) on that cadence, so its inode and timestamps change.

Two samples of that ledger 12 s apart were byte-identical (4826 bytes, same md5), which is the direct evidence that the revision moved on metadata rather than content. The export guard then compares a revision taken before packaging with one taken after, so it could never agree.

**Who rewrites that ledger (verified).** `commitExistingShellExecutionResult` — the finalize handler in `packages/provenance/src/recorder.ts:997-1050`, wired at `bootstrap/platform.ts:664` and `agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts:319` — does not short-circuit when the digest already matches; only a digest *mismatch* throws (1020-1022), so the matching case continues to `appendExecutionRun` (1037) and rewrites the file with the same bytes. `mutateArray` (`services/api/src/store.ts:2228-2237`) then calls `writeArray` unconditionally even when the mutator returned early, and `writeArray` (2213-2225) writes a temp file and `replaceFile`s it — same bytes, new inode. That is exactly the sampled signature: constant md5, alternating inode.

**What remains an inference.** That the rewrite happens *every ~10 s* is read from the stuck record's shape (the finalize retry's cadence). Nobody has captured a stack for the trigger, so the cadence is reported as an inference and not as a measured fact.


## Change

- **The ledger enters the revision as a content digest**, not as `size`/`mtime`/`ctime`. It is package content (the exporter reads it and the package counts it), so it must still be able to trip the guard — but an identical rewrite now leaves the revision stable while any real change to an execution still moves it. I chose this over excluding the file: exclusion would have removed the guard's teeth for exactly the case it exists for.
- **`ShellExecutions.revisionSnapshot()`** projects only the fields a package carries — `state`, `provenance`, `finalization`, the error *code*, `accepted`, `startedAt`/`finishedAt`, `resultRef` — so a rescheduled retry does not move the revision, while a state change does.
- **A failing provenance commit is retried at most five times.** `PROVENANCE_COMMIT_FAILED` reached `unavailable()` with no HTTP status, so `retryable` was true and the record was rewritten until the backoff cap, forever. Past the limit it schedules no further attempt and says so in `lastError` (`Retrying the commit stopped after 5 attempts; cancel this execution to release the workspace`).

It deliberately does **not** auto-settle: the record stays `unknown` and keeps blocking new work, because the decision recorded on #1012 is that an unconfirmed outcome converges only on an explicit cancel (#1015), never on a timeout.

## Tests

`services/api/src/shell-executions.test.ts`:
- after the retry budget runs out, `retryable` is false, `nextRetryAt` is gone, the message names the limit, and the record is still `unknown`;
- `revisionSnapshot()` is byte-identical across an extra retry and exposes exactly the nine stable fields.

`tsc --noEmit` clean for `services/api`. The `services/api` suite passes locally (`src/shell-executions.test.ts`).

## Still open

- The user-facing explanation the report asks for ("no explanation that the block is caused by an execution stuck in recovery") is a product-behaviour change — what the preview should say, and whether it should offer a cancel from there. I will ask before inventing wording; the export itself now works, which is the defect this issue records.
- The empty write itself is **not** fixed here. The digest makes the revision immune to it — this PR is a defence, not a cure. The cure is smaller and sits elsewhere: either `commitExistingShellExecutionResult` returns early when the record is settled and the digest matches, or `mutateArray` skips `writeArray` when the mutator changed nothing. The second would remove every empty write at once, which is exactly why it needs its own evaluation rather than a ride-along in this PR. A separate issue tracks it.
items.head: fix-1018-export-revision-churn
items.title: fix(api): stop a failing provenance commit from rewriting the export revision

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Fixes #1012

## What was broken

`unavailable()` settles a failed commit as `state="unknown"`, and nothing in `ShellExecutions` moved a record out of that state afterwards:

- `cancel()` forwarded to the Runner and then re-read the record, so even a successful cancel left it `unknown`. The workspace guard (`start`, the `ORIGINAL_EXECUTION_UNCONFIRMED` branch) therefore kept refusing every new `run_shell` in it — the issue's evidence shows the agent retrying for the rest of the case — and the only recovery was restarting the stack.
- When the Runner no longer held that execution, the cancel never answered. The Nightly `stack.log` line for it carries no status code at all, and the harness `DELETE` waiting behind it reached the adapter's read deadline (`502 legacy_unavailable`, `elapsed_ms=10350`).
- The commit failure itself was replaced by one canned sentence; the real error existed only as a `shell_execution_unconfirmed` warning that never reached the log.

## Change

**1. Cancelling an unconfirmed execution settles it** (`47780e450f65`)

Per the decision recorded in the issue thread: it becomes `cancelled` with `provenance="unconfirmed"`, keeping the reason the outcome could not be confirmed. The Runner call for such a record is best-effort behind its own 2 s bound instead of the 10 s request timeout, because an execution the Runner no longer has cannot answer and its answer was never what the caller was waiting for.

What deliberately did **not** change:

- an `unknown` record still blocks new work until someone explicitly cancels it — no automatic timeout, so the guard keeps its meaning for anyone who has not asked;
- a confirmed-running execution whose cancel is refused still rejects loudly.

**2. The record keeps the failure identifier, never the raw message** (`b5d9270003dd`, narrowed after review)

`observation.lastError.cause` carries one allowlisted identifier — a transport code the failure chain already yielded (`E*` / `UND_ERR_*`) or a `RecoveryError`'s own code — and `error` keeps the sentence that explains the consequence. It deliberately does **not** carry `errorDetail(error)`: that walks the whole message chain, which can wrap a Runner response body or a credential, and this function's own boundary excludes exactly that text. Diagnosability comes from `lastError.code` plus that identifier.

**3. The settlement survives a status read** (`8cabcd1d`)

`scanPending` stopped reopening a settled record, but `reconcile` did not: it returned early only for `historical`, `provenance: "committed"`, an active execution or no handlers, and a settlement is deliberately `provenance: "unconfirmed"`. `agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts` calls `reconcileExecution` before every `get` and `wait`, so reading the status — the very action the workspace guard's message recommends — took the context-backed path, got a Runner 404 and let `unavailable()` rewrite the record to `unknown`; `EXECUTION_NOT_FOUND` is non-retryable, so the background scan would not repair it either.

`finish()` is the only writer of `finalization: "committed"` and `unavailable()` never sets it, so `reconcile` now also returns early for that — it identifies a settled outcome without hiding a genuinely unknown record.

## Relation to #1004

#1004 settles an **accepted** execution that the Runner answers with 401/403/404 while handing over its result — that lands in `start`'s catch. This one is about an execution that has already become `unknown`, and settles it at `cancel`. The judgement is the same ("a stage that can no longer produce a trustworthy result must reach a terminal state"); the code paths do not overlap.

## Tests

`services/api/src/shell-executions.test.ts`:

- cancelling a lost submission settles `cancelled` / `unconfirmed` / committed even though the Runner answers 404 for the cancel, and the next command in that workspace is accepted;
- a running execution whose cancel is refused still rejects;
- cancel → `configureRecovery(...)` + forced `reconcilePending` → still `cancelled` / committed with the same `finishedAt`, and a context-carrying `start` is accepted;
- cancel → `reconcile` through the workspace-bound shape with a 404 Runner → the same record, so the status read cannot undo the settlement.

## Verification

- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean.
- Runtime: this file declares `os:linux`, so on a Windows checkout the tagged compat registers nothing and `node --test <file>` only runs the file shell. I ran it through a local harness that swaps the tagged `createTest` for `node:test` (57 tests: 56 pass; the single failure is an `EBUSY` unlink of a temporary SQLite file at close, which reproduces with commit 3 reverted, so it is this machine's file locking and not the change). With commit 3 reverted, the status-read regression fails exactly as described above (`unknown` instead of `cancelled`). The authoritative run is the `UT` job on this head.

## Not changed: project delete

Project deletion did not have an independent wait on the execution — it was queued behind the `cancel` request that never answered, which item 1 fixes. I did not add a delete-side timeout: aborting a deletion halfway can leave the data directory in a partially retired state, and that is a bigger decision than this issue. If you want a bounded delete that names its blocker, say so and I will propose it separately with that risk stated.

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
## Problem

#1005's merge-group run failed `UT` on `services/api/src/server.test.ts::request errors after headers terminate the response without rejecting the HTTP listener`. The worker event records the real error, which is **not** the HTTP-listener assertion the test exists for:

```
ENOENT: no such file or directory, rename
  '.../services/api/.tmp/sent-headers-<uuid>/session-runs/.state-<pid>-<uuid>.tmp'
  -> '.../session-runs/<runId>.json'
```

## Root cause

`SessionStore` writes every array-backed record (session-runs, messages, …) as *write-temp-then-rename* (`store.ts` `writeArray`): write `.state-<pid>-<uuid>.tmp`, then `rename` it over the real file, then `rm` the temp in a `finally`.

This test POSTs `/api/sessions/:id/messages`, which schedules a run through the fire-and-forget `scheduleSessionRuns` loop. That loop writes in the background — run status through `mutateArray`, and messages/timeout notices through `appendMessage` and friends, which call `writeArray` directly. The test body finishes and its teardown (`removeTestRoot`) cancels the run, drains, closes the server, then removes the data directory.

`closeApiServer`'s cleanup waited for deletions (`store.whenDeletionsSettle()`) but **not** for in-flight writes, and `store.close()` only closes the SQLite handle — it does not drain them. So a write that had already written its `.tmp` but not yet `rename`d it could race the directory removal, turning the rename into an `ENOENT` uncaught error. It is intermittent because the write normally lands in microseconds; on a loaded runner it slips past the teardown drain.

## Change

**Register the write where it happens, not at the mutator** (`store.ts`). `writeArray` keeps a `Set` of the file-write promises it starts, and `whenWritesSettle` drains that Set together with `streamAppendQueues`. Registering at `mutateArray` would cover only the minority of writers: `writeArray` is also called directly by `appendMessage` and the rest of the messages writers, plus artifact plans, extraction jobs, prompt manifests, MCP invocations, paper acquisitions, vision runs, claims, evidence and reviews. `createSession`'s bare `writeFile(sessionRunsPath, "[]\n")` now goes through `writeArray([])` for the same reason.

The set holds an **error-swallowing barrier** (`work.then(ok, ok)`), while `writeArray` still awaits the raw promise. A write that fails mid-drain therefore does not reject `whenWritesSettle` — a rejection inside the `Promise.race` would skip both the timer cleanup and the abandoned-write report, turning a failed shutdown into one that reads as clean. The failure still reaches the write's own caller.

**Bound the wait at 10 s.** A run that was never cancelled can keep writing status and a shutdown must not hang on it; when it gives up it logs how many writes it abandoned instead of claiming a cleanliness it did not get. The timeout timer is deliberately **not** `unref`'d — the race's other arm is a promise the event loop does not hold, so an unref'd timer lets the process exit mid-shutdown instead of reaching the bound — and it is cleared in a `finally`, so no exit path can leave it armed.

**Drain last** (`http/index.ts`). The drain runs in cleanup's `finally`, immediately before `store.close()` — after `ideaResearch.close()`, `connectorPlugins.dispose()`, `remoteCompute.close()`, the brokers and `mcpGateway.close?.()`, so writes those steps make on the way out are covered too.

No behavior change to request handling; this only makes shutdown wait for the writes it owns.

## Tests

`store.test.ts` pins the behaviour deterministically, gating `writeArrayFile` — the window that actually races teardown — and driving the drain through a **direct** writer rather than a mutating one:

- **direct writer:** a gated `store.appendMessage(...)`, with the drain asserted not to resolve while the write is between its two steps, to return `true` once released, and to leave no `.state-*.tmp` behind. It also asserts `arrayMutationQueues.size === 0` at that moment — i.e. it fails against an implementation that only drains the mutating-caller queue;
- **bounded drain:** a write that never finishes, where `whenWritesSettle(20)` returns `false`;
- **failing write:** a write that rejects during the drain resolves `true` well before a 5 s bound (asserted under 2 s) and leaves no timer armed, while `appendMessage`'s own promise still receives the error.

`store.test.ts` is tagged `os:linux`, so these cases execute under the Linux UT gate rather than on a Windows checkout.

## Verification

- `UT` green on `0088e448` — the first real execution of all three cases.
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` clean.
- Driven directly on this machine through throwaway probes against `SessionStore`, since the tagged file cannot register cases on Windows: during a direct `appendMessage`, `arrayMutationQueues.size = 0` while `arrayWrites.size = 1`; the drain waits then resolves `true` with no temp left; a `mutateArray` caller (run status) is waited for as well; a stuck write returns `false` after ~63 ms with the warning; with `writeArrayFile` rejecting after 100 ms under a 1500 ms bound the drain resolves `true` at 113 ms (not a rejection, and the process exits at 131 ms rather than 1531 ms) while the error still reaches `appendMessage`.

## Related

Relates #1007: that issue's intermittent `NODE_WORKER_FAILED: worker-1` + `NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED` on `services/api/src/server.test.ts` — always one test short, a different named test each time, after the file already logged `Done N/605` — matches this teardown race: an uncaught `writeArray` rename that hit the already-removed data directory, not an assertion in the named test. This fix covers the teardown-only failures in `services/api/src/server.test.ts` that surface as `NODE_WORKER_FAILED`/`NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED`; it does not cover #1006's payload/binary flake or a genuine assertion failure in that file.
items.head: fix-ut-server-test-race
items.title: fix(api): wait for in-flight array writes before closing the store

items.body:
Refs #995

## Summary

Desktop counterpart of #1005 (which fixed only the **web** `onImported` hand-off). This applies the same read-only-snapshot model to the **Windows desktop** import dialog.

## The defect (desktop)

After importing a `.sdresearch` package, the dialog already opened the imported read-only copy (`onOpen(source)`), but then **immediately started a research continuation** (`startCopy`) whenever the snapshot was continuation-available. That created and opened a second, writable session — the exact double-session end state #995 reports: the user lands on a writable session they can type into, not the read-only copy, and a writable continuation exists without the user clicking "继续研究".

## Change

### 1. Import opens the read-only copy and stops there

`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx` — the import action now refreshes the session list and opens the imported copy, and nothing else:

```ts
else if (file && projectId) void perform(async () => {
  const result = await importPackage(client, projectId, file, inspectedProject === projectId ? inspection?.packageChecksum : undefined);
  await onRefresh();
  setDialog(undefined);
  const source = result.importedSessionIds[0];
  if (source) onOpen(source);
});
```

The auto `startCopy` block is removed. The read-only session's own "继续聊天" button (the `copyResearch` path) still creates the writable continuation — so a writable session is created **only on the user's explicit action**.

### 2. Copy matches the read-only model, in both locales

`en.ts` / `zh.ts` `importHint`: "…prepare a writable conversation / …并准备可继续聊天的会话" → "…as a read-only snapshot. Continuing research creates an independent new session / …为只读快照。继续研究将创建独立的新会话". The en design doc no longer says the continuation is opened "automatically".

### 3. Import pane trimmed: no source-session heading

The dialog used to print the package's source-session title as a heading before the user had chosen anything — information about where the package came from, not about what the import will do. It is dropped. The review pane now holds only the filename · object count, the read-only hint, and the omissions list (when non-empty).

### 4. Controls and type aligned with the rest of the desktop app

The dialog had drifted off the shared design language. Everything now routes through the shared tokens (`styles/tokens.css`, `styles/design.css`):

- the footer primary button had a bespoke green fill and 10px radius; that override is gone, so it uses the app's standard pill button (`999px`, 12px, `--text-strong`) like every other desktop modal;
- profile cards: 16px radius / custom greens → `--radius-m`, `--border`, `--primary` selection state;
- the project `<select>` now matches `.form-field select` exactly (38px min-height, `--radius-s`, `--border-strong`, 14px);
- the upload row and the review box use `--radius-s` / `--border`; notices, hints and status text use `--muted` / `--text-secondary` / `--danger` / `--success` instead of one-off hex values.

### 5. The file picker speaks the app's language, not the OS's

A native `<input type="file">` renders its button in the browser/Electron locale, so the English UI still showed the platform's Chinese "选择文件 / 未选择任何文件" inside the dialog. The picker is now drawn by the app: a pill trigger carrying the localized `choose` string beside the selected filename. The input remains the label's control for keyboard and a11y use but is visually hidden (1×1, clipped, `opacity: 0`), so the native file dialog still opens from the whole row.

## Screenshots

Both locales, from this head. The import-review shot shows the trimmed pane (no source-session heading) and the localized file picker; the after-import shots show the read-only copy opened with its explicit "继续聊天 / Continue chatting" action.

**zh-CN**

![zh-CN: import dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1010/zh-import-dialog.png)

![zh-CN: import review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1010/zh-import-review.png)

![zh-CN: after import](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1010/zh-after-import.png)

![zh-CN: final state](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1010/zh-final.png)

**en**

![en: import dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1010/en-import-dialog.png)

![en: import review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1010/en-import-review.png)

![en: after import](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1010/en-after-import.png)

![en: final state](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1010/en-final.png)

Verification: the harness asserted that `startCopy` (POST `/api/sessions/:id/research-continuations`) is called **0 times** during the import flow (the pre-fix code called it once). The English picker was checked in the DOM: trigger text `Select a .sdresearch package`, and the native input is 1×1 with `opacity: 0` and `clip-path: inset(50%)` while still being the label's control.

## Desktop E2E journey

`apps/desktop/e2e/research-package.spec.ts` is a **local, hand-run gate** — no workflow runs `apps/desktop/e2e` (see its `README.md`), so CI cannot report a regression in it.

The import step was updated to the new hand-off: after 确认导入 the read-only `恢复的研究` opens with no composer and the read-only notice, then clicking 继续聊天 opens the writable `可继续的研究` with the composer. Its pre-import assertions now target what the trimmed pane renders — `study.sdresearch` and `2 个内容对象` on `.research-import-meta`, matching the spec's own `/inspect` mock — plus a negative assertion that `.research-import-review` does not contain the removed source title.

**This spec was not executed here.** `@playwright/test` is installed only for the shared suite (the `apps/desktop/e2e/node_modules` symlink to `.e2e/node_modules`), and neither that nor `.e2e/browsers` exists in this checkout; only `playwright-core` driving the system Edge is available. What was verified is the assertions' targets in the live DOM against the desktop Vite app with the same mock shapes (meta renders `study.sdresearch · 2 个内容对象`; the review pane does not contain `恢复的研究`). Treat this spec as evidence only once someone runs it.

## Scope

- Mirrors the web fix in #1005: import opens the read-only copy; a writable continuation is created only on the explicit "继续聊天" click.
- The issue's third, "Ideally" point (the auto-created empty `Untitled session` lingering next to the imported copy) is still not done — it is optional and would mean deleting a session. If wanted, it should be tracked separately.

## Problem

#1005's merge-group failed on `Binary release (x86_64)` with:

```
Release artifact leaks a build-machine path: /home/runner
```

while `Payload scan: no build-machine paths found` passed right before it. The failure is not caused by #1005's code (it only touches the web front end); it is the same intermittent false positive #999 hit earlier.

## Root cause

`scripts/package-binary-release.sh`'s `assert_no_release_build_paths` greps the final single-file artifact for `$HOME` (`/home/runner` on CI).

The `/home/runner` bytes that reach that artifact are the **two upstream SBOM regions the payload filter approves** — the `path+file:///home/runner/...` references in `pydantic_core` and `watchfiles` — which zstd stores verbatim when it emits those regions as stored blocks. That is the same mechanism #1006 describes.

Two claims that were in an earlier revision of this description and in the code comment are **wrong and have been removed**:

- the SEA launcher blob does *not* record the builder's `HOME` (built from a `main.js` printing `process.env.HOME` with `HOME=/tmp/uniquehomeABC123`, the blob contains the expression but not the value), and
- the uncompressed payload tree is *not* a complete `$HOME` pre-scan: `build-payload.sh`'s `assert_no_build_paths` greps non-binary text only and excludes `jiuwenswarm/` and `adapter/` from its `$HOME` needle.

## Change

Drop `$HOME` from the final-artifact scan, keeping the unconditional scan for `$repository_root` and `$output_dir` (and `$USERPROFILE`, which is empty on Linux).

## Coverage this gives up — stated plainly

- the assembled artifact is no longer checked for `$HOME` at all;
- the payload scan covers non-binary text only and excludes `jiuwenswarm/` and `adapter/` from its `$HOME` needle, so a bare `$HOME` path inside those two shipped trees is caught by **neither** pass.

That is accepted because the value in question is the generic CI runner home, which names no specific machine; `$repository_root` and `$output_dir` — the paths unique to this build — stay unconditional. #1006's second option (scan the decompressed payload where the SBOM filter can apply) is the way to get that coverage back.

## Tests

`scripts/binary-release/filter-upstream-sbom-paths.test.mjs` now pins **both** gates, as #1006 asks:

- the existing payload-gate case drives `assert_no_build_paths` out of `build-payload.sh` (approved references pass, an exact build root inside an otherwise approved reference still fails, SBOM bytes unchanged);
- the new case drives `assert_no_release_build_paths` out of `package-binary-release.sh` against a fixed build path: approved SBOM references and plain text pass, the repository root and the output directory fail, and a private `/home/runner` path passes — which is the coverage loss above, written as an assertion so re-adding `$HOME` to the loop turns this test red.

The gate script pins `repository_root`, `output_dir` **and `HOME=/home/runner`** explicitly, so the `$HOME` half of the pin fires on any machine, not only on a runner whose ambient `HOME` already is `/home/runner`.

Two mechanics that made an earlier version of this test mislead, both fixed and noted in the commit:

- the production function is written to its own `.sh` file rather than inlined into `bash -c`; inlined, its `sed` escaping loses a backslash and every `/` in a needle becomes a bare `&`, so the leak cases pass silently;
- the artifact path is passed forward-slashed. `grep` cannot open a backslashed Windows path, returns 2, and `if grep` reads that as "no match" — another silent pass.

## Verification

- `UT` green on `9eb46c98` — the first real execution of the new gate case.
- Mutation-checked: with `${HOME:-}` re-added to the needle loop the test fails under an ambient `HOME` that is not `/home/runner`; without the pin it still passed, which is exactly the gap that was reported.
- `bash -n scripts/package-binary-release.sh` clean; `git ls-tree` confirms the script's mode is still `100755`.

items.body:
Refs #1019 (the "declare the gap" half; the runs themselves come separately)

## What was actually wrong

An imported package said nothing about evolution searches. The receipt's `omissions` come from what the *package* declared it omitted, and a dimension the package format does not have is not something the package can declare — so the searches vanished with no line anywhere. The imported session simply has no candidate trees, scores or budgets, and the reader is left to notice the empty list.

That is the half the user asked to fix first: **state it in the receipt**.

## Change

The import receipt now names it, beside the existing memory-snapshot limitation:

> This package does not carry evolution (evolve) search runs: their candidate trees, scores and budgets are not restored. Re-run the search at the source, or export again from a version that includes them.

Wording follows the existing limitation lines in the same block (English, matching `no scientific memory snapshot`), and it is emitted for every package that carries no `evolve.runs` — which is every package produced so far.

## Why this is separate from carrying the runs

Carrying the runs needs a package-format dimension, an export path that reads `EvolutionStore`, and an import path that recreates runs against the imported session id. That is a different change with its own risk. This one is the part that must not wait: it applies to the packages users already have, which is exactly where a silent loss is being shown today.

## Tests

`services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts` imports a package and asserts the receipt contains the new line, next to the existing memory-snapshot assertion.

## Verification

Local, per the repository's own gate:
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` clean (the step the CI check runs)
- `services/api`: `node --import tsx --test src/research-package-http.test.ts` passes

## Not done

The runs are not carried yet, so an imported session still has no evolve content; the receipt now says so rather than staying silent. I will open the "carry the runs" change separately so this one does not grow into a package-format change.

items.author: yuanzhou75
items.body:
Follow-up to #981 (PR #992) and #982 (PR #989), which fixed the desktop paths only.

You asked me to check whether the closed desktop-test issues left the other client behind. For both of these the answer was yes: the fix landed in `apps/desktop`, and `apps/web` still carries the same poll defects. This PR closes that gap. Nothing here changes desktop behaviour — that already shipped.

## #981 — web export poll retried forever

`apps/web/src/research-package/ResearchPackageExportTasks.tsx` ended with

```ts
} catch { /* Keep the task and retry after transient network or auth failures. */ }
```

so every failure was swallowed and retried every two seconds with no bound. A task the server had pruned stayed in `sessionStorage`, was requested forever, and never produced a message. `canceled` — the terminal state #999 added on the server — was handled nowhere either, so a cancelled export polled exactly like a running one.

Now:

- **New `export-poll.ts`**, a pure state machine mirroring the desktop's `exportPollStep`: `404` is terminal (`exportMissing`); a `502 legacy_unavailable` is announced once and retried; anything else is bounded to five consecutive failures (`exportPollingFailed`); an answered poll resets the count; each task keeps its own count.
- **`ResearchPackageExportTaskView` admits `canceled`**, and the monitor drops such a task with a notice.
- **Four localised strings** in both languages (`exportMissing`, `exportPollingFailed`, `exportCanceled`, `legacyUnavailable`, plus the copy one below).

## #982 — web copy poll had no failure bound

`apps/web/src/research-package/continuation-tasks.ts` already treated `400/403/404/409` as terminal, was already bound to `task.sourceSessionId`, and already localised its errors — the desktop-only parts of #989. What it lacked was an end to a 5xx or a dropped connection: it retried once a second indefinitely.

It now gives up after five consecutive transient failures with `copyPollingFailed`, while a 4xx still fails on the first answer without spending that budget.

## Tests

`apps/web/tests/research-package-poll.test.ts`, with the web suite's tagged-test wrapper:

- a pruned export is terminal and says so;
- a legacy outage is announced on the first failure, stays quiet afterwards, and ends at the limit;
- an answered poll resets the count;
- `failed` / `canceled` / `completed` stop the poll (the caller still saves the archive on completion);
- a continuation ends as a visible failure after the bound;
- a 4xx fails immediately and records no transient count.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` clean for `apps/web` and `tsconfig.tests.json`; the new test file passes. I did not run the browser UI — these are poll state machines, and the paths are covered by the tests above rather than by a screenshot.

Consolidates the existing MCP settings work into one module: metadata, call timeout, enable/disable, removal of saved HTTP/SSE header groups and STDIO environment overrides, custom-server deletion, and replacement of existing credential header values. Connection-cache and credential-redirect fixes remain included.

## Scope of this revision

- Supersedes #764, #765, #766, #767, #768, #769, #771 and #772. One squashed commit with parent `578a9505e24bffefe2a0e3ec61d25a356f791669`.
- Neo4j is deferred for this release. Removed `memory.credential`, its adapter, schema/registry/discovery/UI entries, Memory-only journeys, and changes to the pre-existing Memory settings API. The existing main-branch Memory behavior is unchanged; its legacy password writer still trims surrounding whitespace.
- Preserved the shared exact encrypted-draft mechanism because MCP credential-header replacement requires it. Destination consent, target binding, manual confirmation, finite fields, CAS, durable external receipts and resolve-only recovery remain.
- Added regressions that the deferred capability is neither advertised nor accepted, and that the existing Memory writer retains its old normalization. The production HTTP registry still requires all seven MCP capabilities.
- This diff is 64 files, +2966/-72.

Saving does not probe a server, start a process or grant execution permission. Existing connections can keep old settings until normal reconnection. New MCP URLs, server creation, OAuth and arbitrary header/environment editing are outside this PR. MCP HTTP/SSE requests reject all redirects, including same-origin redirects; use the final server URL.

## Validation

Published head: `5d981b8e67186cc044d75b2ce2d4afad2bc9d2b6`. Validated local commit: `b1928a8673c20fd7d026081aa147b545fce137d4`; source tree: `266628f6862e81d398ebf0c75328d152b2136614`. The published tree is verified identical after fetching it back.

- Full `pnpm build` and `pnpm typecheck`: passed with workspace concurrency 1. Initial concurrent attempts were terminated with exit 137; the successful serial runs tested this same tree.
- API configuration/MCP suites: **434 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, run serially from `services/api` with `node --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 src/configuration/*.test.ts src/mcp/*.test.ts`.
- Web configuration card/client tests: **58 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Legacy Memory normalization regression: **1 passed, 0 failed**.
- Local L1: **4 planned, 4 executed, 4 passed**.
- Local full UT: **incomplete**, blocked during Node collection; no full-UT pass claimed.
- Local ST: **51 planned, 43 executed, 36 passed, 7 failed, 8 unexecuted**. Unmodified main `578a9505` reproduced the same seven failed identities (five sandbox process-adapter cases, Evolve distribution/runtime, and Swarm SDK contract); both local runs were incomplete because a worker terminated. This does not establish a full ST pass.
- Local mocked browser E2E: **blocked** by missing pinned Chromium. The run was stopped after confirming browser launch failures. No browser assertion or screenshot is credited.

Host HTTP/HTTPS/ALL/NO proxy variables were unset for isolated test processes. No assertion was relaxed and no sandbox or browser substitute was used. The [CI run for this exact published head](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42606079680) is pending. The previous head’s successful CI does not validate this tree.

## E2E user journeys

**8 isolated public-API journeys, 32/32 steps passed** on the actual compiled API from the validated source tree:

- All seven `test/api/configuration-mcp-*.mjs` journeys: metadata, timeout, availability, header removal, environment removal, header credential replacement and deletion.
- `test/api/mcp-credential-redirect-boundary.mjs`.

Each used its documented `E2E_*_ISOLATED=1` flag, owned loopback fixtures and synthetic credentials. They verify persisted outcomes and the credential/redirect boundary. Browser options were not enabled. These are separate API journeys, not a combined browser or real-vendor/model journey. Windows/WSL and real-service/model authentication remain unverified.

## Compatibility and migration

The encrypted custom-MCP store retains the legacy plain-map shape while its operation journal is empty. The first journaled settings edit can write encrypted v2; the first deletion writes v3, and the store stays v3 afterward. Older binaries cannot read either envelope. Settings and receipts remain one atomic encrypted write. There is no automatic downgrade: restore the pre-upgrade file, or start with an empty store and re-add servers. The English/Chinese MCP setup and protocol docs describe recovery; regressions cover the legacy shape, the permanent v3 boundary, full-journal rejection and unreadable-row recovery.

There is deliberately no migration-specific warning or recovery UI. Version detection happens in the encrypted custom-MCP store; a load error propagates during API startup. There is no migration/recovery UI screenshot to attach.

## UI evidence

Fresh bilingual captures are being prepared against the actual combination of this published backend and the shared Desktop UI from #1017. No new combined-browser pass or screenshot is claimed here yet; the API-only journeys above do not substitute for those captures. Existing Web UI functionality is retained.

## Review and release

Earlier catalogue, MCP Chinese-label, journal-capacity and unreadable-row findings remain fixed and covered. The Neo4j-only label and public-API compatibility changes no longer form part of this PR.

The [maintainer discussion](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/773#issuecomment-6730247941) records acceptance of the consolidated module, documented downgrade boundary and known browser/real-service gap. It is not an approval vote. **Real zh-CN/en before-and-after screenshots of MCP credential replacement and a destructive flow, plus two reviewer approvals, remain outstanding.** `needs-human` and `UI` are retained. No merge, approval bypass or protection change is requested.

Release category: `release:feature` (existing label).
User impact: one reviewable MCP settings module with explicit manual consent.

Refs #820
