items.author: HugoXK
items.body:
Fixes #910

Classification: **hygiene, not a product fix.** Test-only change to `source-health.test.ts`; product behaviour is unchanged. Excluded from sprint window scoring and today's KPI on the Lead's ruling.

The harm is real but indirect: the injected-fault wait timing out turns `UT` red for pull requests that do not touch `packages/data-source` at all. `#872` hit exactly this (`NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED: packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts`, `planned 6279 / failed 1`) although all four of its changed files are under `apps/web`. That is a false red, not a defect in the code under test.

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts` gave its injected fault a wall-clock budget of about 200 ms (200 polls × 1 ms). On a loaded runner — four UT worker processes (`UT_WORKERS = 4`, one Node file each) plus coverage instrumentation — the fault lands later than that, the helper falls through to `assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection")`, and the `UT` job turns the only required status check red on a pull request that does not touch this package. Two pull requests were blocked by exactly this identity on 2026-11-04.

## What was wrong

```ts
async function waitFor(predicate: () => boolean) {
  for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) { if (predicate()) return; await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1)); }
  assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection");
}
```

The budget is a fixed count of sleeps, so any event-loop delay counts against it. The product behaviour was never wrong; the wait was.

## What changed — the first proposal at `07c82091`

This is the shape the branch had before the rebase; the code on the current tip is in "Rebase and the review findings" below, which keeps the 10 s deadline but reads it with `performance.now()` and carries a diagnosis.

The helper now waits on a deadline instead of a fixed budget:

```ts
const FAULT_OBSERVATION_DEADLINE_MS = 10_000;
async function waitFor(predicate: () => boolean, timeoutMs = FAULT_OBSERVATION_DEADLINE_MS) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) { if (predicate()) return; await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1)); }
  assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection");
}
```

The poll interval stays 1 ms, so a healthy run is as fast as before; a loaded run waits for the observation up to 10 s; a genuinely missing fault still fails, and the new test pins that it fails quickly rather than hanging the layer. The failure message is unchanged, so a real regression keeps the same identity.

This touches only the test file — no product code, no other test. As first proposed the three existing `waitFor` call sites were unchanged; the rebase later gave each of them a diagnosis (see below).

## Red first

Commit `731bc426` adds the regression test only, on the old helper:

```ts
let observed = false;
const timer = setTimeout(() => { observed = true; }, 500);
try { await waitFor(() => observed); } finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
```

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/source-health.test.ts
ok 1 - 429 cooldown rejects later agent rounds without another upstream request or wait
not ok 2 - the fault wait tolerates a loaded runner instead of a 200 ms budget
  error: 'Timed out waiting for local fault injection'
ok 3 - parallel 429 callers share cooldown, drain their queue and do not retry inside one slot
...
# tests 17
# pass 16
# fail 1
```

A 500 ms observation is a stand-in for a busy runner: it is the same event-loop delay the ci hit, only deterministic, so the failure reproduces without needing a loaded machine.

## After the fix

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/source-health.test.ts
# tests 17
# pass 17
# fail 0
```

The new test also asserts the fail-fast path after the fix, so widening the deadline cannot hide a missing fault:

```ts
await assert.rejects(() => waitFor(() => false, 50), /Timed out waiting for local fault injection/);
```

Diffstat against `main` `2908e9e8`:

```
 packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts | 17 +++++++++++++++--
 1 file changed, 15 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
```

Commits: `731bc426` test (red), `07c82091` fix — the first proposal only. The four commits on the current tip are `21921b4f` test (red) → `58b85992` fix → `4c3535b7` test (red) → `7413208f` fix, listed under "Rebase and the review findings".

Ran:
- `cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/source-health.test.ts` — `# pass 16 # fail 1` on the red commit (`not ok 2`, `Timed out waiting for local fault injection`), `# pass 17 # fail 0` on the fix.
- `tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut` (the whole layer, 6 281 cases) was not run locally; CI runs it on this pull request, and the fix is confined to one UT file.
- `pnpm ci:st` / `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run: the change is a test helper, not product behaviour.

## Release

Release category: `release:test` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: none directly. A flaky UT identity that could turn the required check red on unrelated pull requests now waits for the observation it was already waiting for, so it stops blocking merges it has nothing to do with.

## Rebase and the review findings (`9feafa273088`, 2026-11-09)

The branch was cut from `2908e9e8` and the pull request showed `mergeable=false` / `dirty`. It is now rebased onto `9feafa27`; one conflict, in `waitFor` itself, resolved by taking this branch's deadline version.

Two review threads were still open on the previous tip and are answered here.

**F1 — the deadline is not a bound while `Date` is mocked.** Correct. One pre-existing call site (`cooldown admits one recovery probe…`) runs under `t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ["Date"] })`, where `Date.now()` stands still and only `t.mock.timers.tick()` moves it, while `setTimeout` stays real — so a `Date`-based deadline never arrives and a predicate that never becomes true spins instead of failing. The new guard test below adds a second such call site on purpose. Red evidence on the pre-fix helper: a never-true predicate under a mocked `Date` never returns —

```
$ timeout 20 node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "stays bounded while Date is mocked" src/source-health.test.ts
exit=124        # killed after 20 s: the wait never timed out
```

The helper now measures its bound with `performance.now()`, which the `Date` mock does not touch, so the deadline is real in all three call sites. The new test `the fault wait stays bounded while Date is mocked` pins it (red on the previous helper: `AssertionError ... Timed out waiting for local fault injection`, i.e. no elapsed report and no diagnostics).

**Timeout diagnostics.** A timeout now reports how long it waited and what it was waiting for; the three call sites pass the state a future red gate needs:

- `parallel 429 callers…` → `calls=N settled=[SOURCE_COOLDOWN, RATE_LIMIT_QUEUE_FULL, …]` (the errors that settled while waiting).
- `cooldown admits one recovery probe…` → `calls=N invocations=[…]`.
- `queue exhaustion, timeout and cancellation…` → `calls=N invocations=[…]`.

Example message: `Timed out waiting for local fault injection after 10012 ms: calls=1 settled=[RATE_LIMIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT, …]`.

**F2 — the worker count.** Correct: the `UT` slice runs four child processes (`UT_WORKERS = 4` in `test/support/tagged/scheduler.mjs`, one Node file per process), not sixteen; the 16 in the artifact is this file's test count. Both the comment and this body now say four.

## Validation on the rebased tip

- `node --import tsx --test packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts` → `# tests 18 / # pass 18 / # fail 0`, ten consecutive runs, every one identical (`run 1 … run 10: # tests 18 / # pass 18 / # fail 0`).
- `npx tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → exit 0.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` → exit 0.
- diffstat against `9feafa27`: 1 file, `+91/−13` (`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts`).

**F5 — the mocked-`Date` scope was overstated, and the snippet was stale.** Correct on both counts, and this is the wording fix rather than a behaviour change. An instrumented copy that recorded `Date.now !== realDateNow` at every `waitFor` entry printed `[false,false,true,false,true,false]`: the two `true` are `cooldown admits one recovery probe…` and the new guard test, not three call sites. The comment in the file and this body now say one pre-existing call site plus the guard, and the "What changed" snippet and commit list above are marked as the pre-rebase proposal, with the current four commits named.

Commit `43ccb4de` (`test(data-source): name the call sites the mocked Date actually covers`) carries the comment reword. It is pushed in the tip below, together with the determinisation that also settles the reason the reword was needed — see the next section.

## The CI red on `7413208f`: two L2 slices, neither reachable from this diff

Run `42581062474` is `failure` on two mocked E2E jobs, and the required `merge-gate` follows them:

- `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config)` (job `129041926772`, `planned 58 / executed 58 / passed 57 / failed 1`): `journey-prepare-environment.spec.ts:57` — `Error: BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: micromamba setup failed)`, failed in 231 ms, i.e. in environment provisioning, not in test logic.
- `L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys)` (job `129041926835`, `planned 87 / executed 87 / passed 86 / failed 1`): `journey-plugin-composition.spec.ts:36` — `getByLabel('artifact-json plugin')`: expected `"disabled"`, received `"inherit"`.

This diff is one test file, `packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts`; it cannot reach Python base provisioning or the plugin-composition settings UI. `L1`, `UT`, `ST`, `L2 research`, `L2 governed`, `L2 literature` and `Coverage` are all success in the same run.

## The determinisation at `f2fcfd44`, and why F5 no longer needs a comment

The deadline this pull request added in `58b85992` and `7413208f` bounds a wait; it does not remove it. Three observations still polled a clock for a moment this suite itself triggers: the 12 parallel callers and the recovery probe wait for their request to reach the transport, and a loaded runner can only make that late.

`nextCall(target)` makes the observation an event instead. The fixture's transport resolves every waiter whose call has arrived, so `await f.nextCall(1)` returns exactly when the first request enters it — no interval, no deadline, nothing a slow runner can turn into a failure:

- `parallel 429 callers share cooldown…` → `await f.nextCall(1)`, then release the fault.
- `cooldown admits one recovery probe…` → `await f.nextCall(2)`.
- `queue exhaustion, timeout and cancellation…` → `await f.nextCall(1)`.

F5's correction (one pre-existing mocked-`Date` call site plus the guard, not three) is in `43ccb4de`, and the paragraph that used to overstate the count is gone from the code.

**F6 then retired `waitFor` at `fd97a589`.** After the three observations moved, `waitFor` was reachable only from its own contract tests and `describeSettled` had no caller — and an unguarded rendezvous turns a regression into a stall, because `nextCall` returned a promise nothing settles and the tagged worker's 300 s test deadline would replace the 10 s failure with its diagnosis. The bound and the diagnosis moved into the rendezvous instead: `nextCall(target, wait)` keeps `FAULT_OBSERVATION_DEADLINE_MS` (10 s, `performance.now()` + `setTimeout`, so the mocked-`Date` cases are unaffected) and rejects with `Timed out waiting for local fault injection after N ms: <state>`; `describeSettled` and `describeInvocations` feed the three call sites, so `calls=… settled=[…]` and `invocations=[…]` can appear in a real failure again. `waitFor` and its two contract tests are gone; the rendezvous contract test covers both duties — it resolves only on the named call, and it fails with the observed state while `Date` is mocked.

Red first, kept as two commits: `5a1d2a7a` converts the three observations and adds `the call rendezvous names the call it waits for and resolves only on it` while the fixture has no `nextCall`, so the suite reads `# tests 19 / # pass 15 / # fail 4` with `error: 'f.nextCall is not a function'` on the four; `f2fcfd44` adds the rendezvous and the suite reads `# tests 19 / # pass 19 / # fail 0`.

The two L2 reds on the previous tip are unchanged by this and are recorded above: `standard-config` failed in 231 ms inside `micromamba` provisioning, and `standard-journeys` failed on a settings-select initial value in `journey-plugin-composition.spec.ts`. Neither slice runs this file; the same two slices are green on `#868` in the same window.

items.body:
Fixes #887

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What changed

`POST /api/sessions/:id/files` resolved `body.path` through `resolveWorkspaceFile` — which only refuses absolute paths and escapes — and wrote the result straight to disk. On a Windows workspace that makes `CON` target the console device and `nul.txt` fail with a raw `EPERM` the handler never classifies, so the client saw `500 Internal server error`. The reserved-device-name guard existed only in the upload path.

Chosen fix: **direction 2** — the predicate became a workspace invariant instead of an upload-only check.

- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` — new exported `isWindowsReservedDeviceName(name)`, sitting directly beside `assertWorkspacePath`. It matches the stems Windows resolves in every directory (`con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com1`–`com9`, `lpt1`–`lpt9`, `conin$`, `conout$`), strips trailing dots/spaces first (`nul.`, `CON `), and treats everything before the first dot as the stem, because the extension is irrelevant to a device. It is exported through the package index (`export * from "./workspace.js"`).
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts` — the write route walks **every segment** of `relative(workspaceRoot, target)` (the helper is a segment rule, so `CON/notes.txt` is refused before `mkdir("…/CON")`) and answers **400 naming the offending segment**. The route keeps accepting nested relative paths; the upload path's "plain basename only" rule is still not imposed here.

Why not direction 1 (call `sanitizeUploadFilename` in the handler): on this base that function has **no** reserved-name branch — it only rejects empty/NUL/absolute/traversal names, which `resolveWorkspaceFile` already enforces — so calling it today would be a no-op for the reported defect. Adding the rule inside it here would duplicate `#868`'s open hunk in the same function (and that PR exists to fix exactly that statement). Putting the predicate beside `assertWorkspacePath` gives both write paths one home once they meet.

### Relation to `#868` (open)

`#868` carries the identical rule inline in `sanitizeUploadFilename`. This diff deliberately does **not** touch `services/api/src/workspace-upload.ts`, so the two do not overlap: when `#868` lands, its guard should call `isWindowsReservedDeviceName` and drop the inline copy (one hunk), leaving main with a single implementation. Whichever merges second does that; if `#868` lands first I will rebase this branch and make that change here.

## Review fix — P2, a device name in a directory segment (review `5773758545`, reviewed at `93af68c8`)

The first version applied the predicate to `basename(target)`, i.e. only the last segment. The route accepts nested relative paths, so `body.path = "CON/notes.txt"` had basename `notes.txt` and passed the guard; the write then reached `mkdir(dirname(target), { recursive: true })`. On a Windows host `CreateDirectory("…/CON")` fails (Node surfaces `EPERM`/`ENOENT`), which is the same unclassified 500 this PR removes; on Linux it creates an unportable `CON/` directory. The helper was already documented as a segment rule, so the call site was the narrow part.

Fixed as asked: the route now splits `relative(workspaceRoot, target)` on the host separator and refuses the first reserved segment. That subsumes the old last-segment case, and the message names the segment the client must change (`"CON"` for `CON/notes.txt`, `"nul.dir"` for `nul.dir/x.csv`) instead of a basename it never sent.

The predicate's doc comment no longer claims to be called from every writer. It states the per-segment rule, names where it is applied today (this route), and says that the agent-side workspace tools, which write through `assertWorkspacePath`, are not wired to it yet.

`WSP-005` (`services/api/src/server.test.ts`) now covers, in addition to the top-level names (`CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, `CON .csv`, and the named-stream forms added below) and the look-alikes from the first version:

- `CON/notes.txt` → 400, the message names `CON`
- `nul.dir/x.csv` → 400, the message names `nul.dir` (stem before the first dot is `nul`, and Windows refuses the directory too)
- `notes/CON.txt` → 400 (control: clean directory, device-name file — refused before this change too)
- `conifer/notes.txt` → 201 (control: the walk must not start refusing legitimate nested paths)

## Review fix — F1, a device's named stream (`nul:stream`, `CON:$DATA`)

The predicate cut the stem at the first dot only, so Windows' named-stream spellings slipped through: `nul:stream` kept its colon, `/^(?:con|prn|aux|nul|com[1-9]|lpt[1-9]|conin\$|conout\$)$/i` never matched, `CON:$DATA` likewise, and the write route answered 201 and created a file a Windows host resolves to the device's stream rather than to a file. Windows takes everything before the colon as the device, so the stem is now cut at the first dot and then at the first colon:

- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` — `name.split(".")[0]?.split(":")[0]?.replace(/[. ]+$/, "")`. `con:$DATA` → `con`, `nul:stream` → `nul`, `NUL:stream` → `NUL`; `conin$`/`conout$` keep the `$` because no colon splits them; the trailing-dot/space strip still runs last, so `nul.` and `CON ` match exactly as before.
- The route needed no change: it already walks every segment through the predicate, so `{"path":"nul:stream"}` now answers 400 naming `nul:stream`.
- `#903` is re-scoped: F1 (named streams) is fixed here, so the follow-up keeps only D2, the POSIX segment split (`CON\notes.txt` when the host separator is `/`).

## Red first

Original case at base `89cd2d30` (test commit `1c3259df`, now the first half of `WSP-005`):

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
not ok 1 - WSP-005 a reserved device name in a session file write answers 400 and names the file
  error: CON must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

The two new directory cases are red at the previous tip `93af68c8` (`0a1ca4fc` is test only). The loop stops at the first failure, so each was run as the only new case:

```
$ node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
  error: CON/notes.txt must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
$ (same command, `nul.dir/x.csv` as the only new case)
  error: nul.dir/x.csv must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
```

`notes/CON.txt` and `conifer/notes.txt` are green at `93af68c8` by design: they are the controls, so they carry no red reading.

Named-stream case at `c4fb33d4` (test commit `ddd14462`):

```
$ cd packages/workspace && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern isWindowsReservedDeviceName src/workspace.test.ts
not ok 1 - isWindowsReservedDeviceName treats a named stream as its device
  error: nul:stream names a device stream
  false !== true
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1

$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts
not ok 1 - WSP-005 a reserved device name in a session file write answers 400 and names the file
  error: nul:stream must be refused as a bad request
  201 !== 400
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

The API route test reads `@sciencediscovery/workspace` from `dist`, so the package was rebuilt from `c4fb33d4` before this red run; an older local `dist` otherwise masks the defect.

## Review fix — F2/F3, the host separator and the superscript ports

- **F2** (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3815`): the segment walk split on `sep`, so on a POSIX host `CON\notes.txt` stayed one filename and passed (`relative(...)` → `"CON\\notes.txt"` in this shell, `segments ["CON\\notes.txt"]`, `reserved segment none`). The walk now splits on `/[\\/]+/`, which is what the predicate's "platform-independent" comment promises.
- **F3** (`packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts:464`): the class was ASCII-only, so `COM¹.txt` (`false` on the old tip) was accepted. It is now `com[1-9¹²³]|lpt[1-9¹²³]`, matching the copy in `#868`; `com⁴.csv`, `com⁰.csv` and `lpt¹⁰.log` stay ordinary names.

Red first — `fb2d5262` (tests only, source `fdb835fb`):

```
not ok 4 - isWindowsReservedDeviceName treats a named stream as its device
  error: |-
    COM¹.txt names a device

    false !== true
# tests 60
# pass 59
# fail 1

not ok 1 - WSP-005 a reserved device name in a session file write answers 400 and names the file
  error: |-
    COM¹.txt must be refused as a bad request

    201 !== 400
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

After (`484cab8f`, rebased onto `9feafa27`): `packages/workspace` `# tests 68 # pass 68 # fail 0`; WSP-005 `# tests 1 # pass 1 # fail 0`; the direct probe reports `reserved segment: CON` and `COM¹.txt: true`.

## Rebase — `9feafa273088` (2026-11-09)

The branch was cut at `89cd2d30`; main moved to `9feafa27` and the pull request showed `mergeable=false` / `dirty`. The same eight commits (four test, four fix, alternating — the red-first pairing is unchanged) were replayed onto `9feafa27`. Nothing was squashed or amended.

One conflict, on the `node:path` import line of `services/api/src/http/index.ts`: main added `join` (used eight times in the file), this branch needs `relative` and `sep` (one use each), and `basename` became unused once the last commit switched the split to `/[\\/]+/`. Resolution: `import { dirname, join, relative, resolve, sep } from "node:path";`. Both review fixes survive unchanged — `.split(/[\\/]+/)` in the write route and `com[1-9¹²³]|lpt[1-9¹²³]` in the predicate.

New tip `484cab8f8e5d26f7d1454380f9d7dcd2c9b34ea0`; the diffstat against the new base is identical to before the rebase (4 files, `+149/−6`). Re-read on the new tip: workspace unit `68/68/0`, WSP-005 `1/1/0`, `tsc` api/tests/workspace exit 0.

## Validation

The API tests load `@sciencediscovery/workspace` from its built `dist`, so the package is built first (CI does the same: the shared runner runs `pnpm build` before the heavy layers).

| gate | command | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| workspace build | `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/workspace/tsconfig.json` | exit 0 |
| typecheck (api) | `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| typecheck (workspace) | `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/workspace/tsconfig.json --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| tests typecheck | `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` | exit 0 |
| predicate case | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern isWindowsReservedDeviceName src/workspace.test.ts` (`packages/workspace`) | `1/1` pass |
| route case | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern WSP-005 src/server.test.ts` (`services/api`) | `1/1` pass |
| workspace route group | `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "WSP-00" src/server.test.ts` (`services/api`) | `3/3` pass |
| package UT | `npm test` (`packages/workspace`) | `101 tests / 101 pass / 0 fail` |
| api server suite | `node --import tsx --test src/server.test.ts` (`services/api`) | `109 tests / 108 pass / 1 fail`: `PDF upload extracts full text and tables into the session workspace` needs `reportlab` in `services/paper/.venv` (environment, not this diff) |
| api UT (full, earlier run at `c4fb33d4`) | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` | `1866 tests / 1860 pass / 6 fail`: 5 environment (`No module named uvicorn` in `services/evolve/.venv`; `No module named 'reportlab'` ×3; missing `@openai/codex-linux-x64`), 1 load flake in `evolution/orchestrator.test.ts` (`timed out waiting for the run to finish`) that passes on its own (`--test-name-pattern "settled"` → `3/3`). None touch this diff. |

Not run: a real Windows host — the guard is deliberately platform-independent, so the Linux route test exercises the same code path; there is no Windows-only branch in it.

`git diff --stat 9feafa27…HEAD`: 4 files, `+149/−6` (unchanged by the rebase) (`workspace.test.ts` `+29/−1`, `workspace.ts` `+31`, `http/index.ts` `+20/−5`, `server.test.ts` `+69`). No existing assertion is relaxed; the two edits to existing test lines are the look-alike loop gaining `conifer/notes.txt` and the top-level refusal loop gaining `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA`.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: writing a session file whose name or directory component is a Windows device (`CON`, `nul.txt`, `COM1.log`, `CON .csv`, `CON/notes.txt`, `CON\notes.txt`, `nul.dir/x.csv`, `COM¹.txt`, and the named-stream forms `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA`) now answers 400 naming the offending segment, on every platform, instead of returning 201 and creating a file a Windows host cannot open (or a write that silently goes to the console or fails as a 500). Ordinary names such as `conifer.csv`, `console.log`, `com10.csv` and `conifer/notes.txt` are unaffected.
Compatibility and migration: none — only names Windows itself cannot create are refused.

items.body:
Fixes #918

`GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests` gained two cases in `#915` that assert the walk stays *quiet*: a generated workspace file is not reported, and a file removed between the listing and the read is skipped. Both assert a negative, so nothing in the suite would fail if the walk stopped reporting anything at all — a future narrowing of `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` or `_files` could silence the boundary check while every test stayed green.

This adds the positive half: a file the walk *should* report is reported.

## Why

The two existing cases are `assertNotIn`, so they pass for any walk that returns an empty list. The only test that pins the positive direction is `ArchitectureBoundaryTests.test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names`, and it asserts the *absence* of findings on the real tree — it cannot go red when the walk is narrowed either, because the tree happens to be clean. A walk that silently ignores `services/api` would keep the entire module green, and vendor naming could escape the boundary unnoticed.

The new case reuses the mocking shape of the removed-after-listing case at `:162`: patch `_files` and let the patched listing hand the walk a path. It differs in what the listing returns — a file that still exists, with a vendor token in it.

## What changed

One test, `services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py` only. No product code.

```python
self.probe = self.positive_probe_path()   # apps/web/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts
self.addCleanup(self.probe.unlink, missing_ok=True)
self.probe.write_text("// deerflow vendor token\n", encoding="utf-8")
original = _files

def only_the_probe(root: Path):
    # Keep the real listing (so IGNORED_DIRECTORIES still governs) and drop
    # every other file, so the assertion cannot depend on the working tree.
    if root == self.API_ROOT:
        return (path for path in original(root) if path == self.probe)
    return original(root)

with mock.patch.object(sys.modules[__name__], "_files", only_the_probe):
    failures = _node_boundary_failures()
self.assertIn(f"content: {self.relative_probe()}", failures)
```

`only_the_probe` delegates to the real `_files`, so the ignore rules still decide what is listed; it only drops unrelated files so the assertion does not depend on whatever else is in the working tree. If `services/api` is ever added to `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES`, the real listing yields nothing and the case fails.

## Red first

Temporarily add `services/api` to the walk's ignore set — the equivalent of a future narrowing that the two negative cases cannot see:

```diff
-IGNORED_DIRECTORIES = {"__pycache__", ".tmp", "dist", "node_modules"}
+IGNORED_DIRECTORIES = {"__pycache__", ".tmp", "dist", "node_modules", "api"}
```

```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_architecture_boundaries.py'
....F.
======================================================================
FAIL: test_a_vendor_reference_outside_a_generated_workspace_is_still_reported
  (test_architecture_boundaries.GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests)
The cases above only prove the walk stays quiet; this proves it still speaks.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py", line 200,
  in test_a_vendor_reference_outside_a_generated_workspace_is_still_reported
    self.assertIn(f"content: {self.relative_probe()}", failures)
AssertionError: 'content: services/api/src/probe-boundary-5.ts' not found in []

----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 6 tests in 0.885s

FAILED (failures=1)
```

The other five tests stayed green under the same mutation, which is exactly the gap: only the new case noticed.

## After reverting the mutation

```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_architecture_boundaries.py'
......
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 6 tests in 1.271s

OK
```

Diffstat against `main` `2908e9e8`:

```
 services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py | 65 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 65 insertions(+)
```

## Rebase and F1 — the positive probe moves out of the egress scan

Rebased onto `9feafa273088` (2026-11-09); the branch was cut at an older main and the pull request showed `mergeable=false` / `dirty`. One commit, replayed unchanged.

F1 (thread `PRRT_kwDOT4OSoM60He32`): the positive case planted `services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts`, which `services/api/src/mcp/datasource-egress-contract.test.ts` reads — its `sourceFiles()` walks every `.ts` under `packages/` and `services/` skipping only `dist`, `node_modules` and `.tmp`, and `readFile`s each hit with no ENOENT tolerance. With `UT_WORKERS = 4`, a parallel worker could read the probe between creation and `addCleanup`, and a killed run would leave a vendor token in a tracked source directory.

Fixed with the reviewer's second option: the probe now lives at `apps/web/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts`. `NODE_ROOTS` includes `apps/web`, so `_node_boundary_failures()` still walks and reports it — the positive half of the contract is unchanged — while `sourceFiles()` never scans `apps/web`, so no other worker reads a file this case creates and removes. `only_the_probe` now filters on the walked root; see F4 below for why the first revision of that filter was wrong.

Red first (`2c41f812`): a test that mirrors the egress predicate —

```
EGRESS_SCANNED_ROOTS = ("packages", "services")
EGRESS_IGNORED_DIRECTORIES = {"dist", "node_modules", ".tmp"}
def _egress_scan_reads(path: Path) -> bool:
    ...
```

and asserts the probe path is not readable by it:

```
$ cd services/gateway && python3 -m pytest tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py -q
1 failed, 6 passed
AssertionError: ... services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.ts is read by the datasource egress worker while it exists; plant the probe under apps/web instead
```

After (`20318a36`): `7 passed`.

diffstat against `9feafa27`: 1 file, `+65/−0` (`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py`; three commits — the original positive case, the red egress test, and the move).

Ran:
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_architecture_boundaries.py'` — `Ran 6 tests ... OK` on the branch; `FAILED (failures=1)` with the assertion excerpt above under the temporary `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` narrowing, then `OK` again after reverting it.
- The probe file is created under `apps/web/` and removed by `addCleanup`, so the working tree is clean after the run (`git status --porcelain` empty).

Not run:
- `pnpm gateway:test` (the whole `services/gateway/tests` discovery) was not run locally; only this module was, and CI runs the full discovery.
- No UT/ST/E2E layers: the change is one gateway test, no product code.

## Release

Release category: `release:test` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: none. It makes the architecture boundary check able to fail when the walk is narrowed, instead of only when it is noisy.

## F2 — the probe moves back into `services/api`, with the four checks a killed run needs

At `20318a36` the positive half ran only over `apps/web`. The reviewer's mutation showed why that is not a narrowing guard: with `"api"` added to `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES`, or `services/api` dropped from `NODE_ROOTS`, the suite still printed `7 passed`. `Fixes #918` would have closed the issue without covering the tree it names first.

This tip takes the reviewer's first option and keeps the probe inside that tree: `PROBE_ROOT = services/api/src`, probe name `probe-boundary-<pid>.mdx`.

Two positive assertions, so a rename cannot pass for a fix:

- `test_the_positive_probe_lives_in_the_root_the_issue_names` — the path sits under `services/api/src` (`assertIn("services/api/src/", relative)`) and carries the probe suffix. Moving the probe back to `apps/web` fails it.
- `test_the_walk_enumerates_and_reads_the_positive_probe` — `_files(PROBE_ROOT)` enumerates the probe and `_node_boundary_failures()` reports `content: services/api/src/probe-boundary-<pid>.mdx`. That is the whole reason `.mdx` still counts: `.mdx` is in `TEXT_SUFFIXES` (`test_architecture_boundaries.py:48`), while `sourceFiles()` in `services/api/src/mcp/datasource-egress-contract.test.ts:394` collects only files whose `extname` is `.ts`, so the egress worker never opens it. A suffix outside `TEXT_SUFFIXES` fails this case.

The four checks a killed run needs, one line each:

1. **Location is pinned both ways** — the two positive assertions above; `apps/web` fails the first, `.bin` fails the second.
2. **`.gitignore` is exact** — `/services/api/src/probe-boundary-*.mdx` (comment plus one line). Not `*.mdx`, not `probe-boundary-*`, not the directory. `git check-ignore -v services/api/src/probe-boundary-12345.mdx` prints `.gitignore:100:/services/api/src/probe-boundary-*.mdx`, and `git ls-files services/api/src | grep -c '\.mdx'` is `0`.
3. **Every exit path cleans up** — `_guard_probe_against_signals()` runs in `setUp`, before any probe exists, so both probe-writing cases (and any added later) are covered rather than the one test that happened to install it. It installs `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` handlers that unlink the probe, restore the previous handler and re-raise the same signal, plus an `atexit` hook for a `sys.exit` or an interpreter that ends before unittest cleanups; both hooks read `self.probe` when they fire, so they unlink the probe the current test wrote. Verified in child processes: `SIGTERM` → probe gone, child exits `143` (the signal is never swallowed); `sys.exit(0)` → probe gone, exit `0`. `setUp` also sweeps probes a dead run left behind, keeping any file whose pid still answers `os.kill(pid, 0)`, so a parallel shard is never deleted (`SIGKILL` cannot be caught — that sweep is its fallback).
4. **No real values** — the probe content is the fixed marker `// deerflow vendor token`; the diff adds no `os.environ`/`getenv` read and no token, secret or path interpolation.

Readings on `75d5b7e2`:

- `cd services/gateway && python3 -m pytest tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py -q` → `16 passed, 1 warning` (was 7 before this round; the two new positive cases, the F4 filter case and the six sweep cases are the additions).
- Child-process checks: `SIGTERM` → probe gone, exit `143`; `sys.exit(0)` → probe gone, exit `0`.
- diffstat against `9feafa27`: 2 files, `+156/−0` (`.gitignore` +4, `services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py` +152).
- Mutation table, all on this tip: probe under `apps/web` → location case FAIL; `PROBE_SUFFIX = ".bin"` → walk-read case FAIL; `"api"` in `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` → positive case FAIL; `services/api` dropped from `NODE_ROOTS` → positive case FAIL; `apps/web` dropped from `NODE_ROOTS` → PASS (coverage no longer depends on it).
- Working tree clean after the suite: no `probe-boundary-*.mdx` left in `services/api/src`.

Not run: the rest of `services/gateway/tests` discovery (CI runs it), and no UT/ST/E2E layers — the change is two gateway test files' worth of test code plus one ignore line.

## F3 — the sweep runs before the walk, and it tells a dead run from a live shard

`ArchitectureBoundaryTests.test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` walks the real tree and is collected before the class that writes probes, so a probe a killed run left behind failed `:117` before `GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests.setUp` could delete it. `_remove_stale_probes(root, pattern)` is now a module function, called from `setUpModule()` — ahead of every case — and again from `setUp` as an idempotent second pass.

Its judgement, with the values actually in the file:

- **same pid**: skipped outright, never swept;
- **dead pid**: deleted;
- **live pid on a host with `/proc`**: deleted when the probe's mtime predates that process's own start by more than `PROBE_START_MARGIN_S = 3 s`. Start time is `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 over `os.sysconf('SC_CLK_TCK')` (measured **100** here, not hard-coded) plus `/proc/stat`'s `btime`. The margin absorbs `btime`'s one-second truncation and an NTP step: on this host `_process_started_at(getpid())` = `1794221689.93` against a wall clock of `1794221690.69`;
- **no usable `/proc`**: pid liveness plus `PROBE_STALE_AGE_S = 10 s`. The slowest probe-holding case measured `0.65 s` (`pytest --durations=0`), so 10 s is more than ten times a full probe life. The path is chosen by whether the `/proc` reads succeed, not by `sys.platform`: `test_process_start_time_is_none_when_proc_is_absent` mocks `open` to raise on `/proc/...`, and `test_without_proc_the_age_fallback_decides` mocks the start time to `None` and requires the age rule to delete an old probe.

Red and green, both residues: with either a `probe-boundary-999999.mdx` (dead pid) or a `probe-boundary-1.mdx` with a ten-minute-old mtime on disk, `python3 -m pytest services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py -q` was `1 failed, 8 passed` before the change and is `16 passed` after, with the residue gone. Collection order is deterministic: `services/gateway/pyproject.toml` depends on `pytest==9.0.2` only — no `pytest-randomly`, no `pytest-xdist`, no `pytest.ini`/`conftest.py` overriding it — so `setUpModule()` is guaranteed to precede `:117`.

What was deliberately **not** done, because it would be passing the gate by hiding the failure: no `probe-boundary-*` filter or `continue` in `_files()`, no probe pattern in `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES`, no extra ignore table, no `skipTest`/`skipIf`/early return in the real-tree case, no weakening of `assertEqual(failures, [])` to `assertNotIn`, and no vendor whitelist in `VENDOR_NAME`.

## F4 — the filter now keys on the root the walk visits

`only_the_probe` compared `root == self.PROBE_ROOT`, but `_node_boundary_failures()` only ever passes `NODE_ROOTS` entries, which contain `services/api`, not `services/api/src` — so the branch never matched and the positive case walked every root unfiltered. `_filtered_listing()` now filters on `self.API_ROOT`, and the positive case routes its patched listing through it.

The isolation is proved, not assumed: `test_the_positive_filter_drops_another_shards_probe` feeds the API-root listing this case's probe plus a sibling's same-pattern probe and an ordinary `neighbour.py`, and requires `[self.probe]` back; feeding the `PROBE_ROOT` listing returns all of them unchanged, pinning the distinction that was wrong. Checked on the tip: `PROBE_ROOT in NODE_ROOTS == False`, `API_ROOT in NODE_ROOTS == True`. `test_the_positive_probe_lives_in_the_root_the_issue_names` and `test_the_walk_enumerates_and_reads_the_positive_probe` both stay, and the red path is intact: with `"api"` added to `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` the positive case fails with `'content: services/api/src/probe-boundary-3.mdx' not found in []`.

## Known limitation: two shards sharing one checkout are not supported

`:117` deliberately walks the real tree and the sweep must not delete a live shard's file, so a sibling's in-flight probe can fail it. Forcing that overlap (one process holds its probe while another runs the module) gives `1 failed, 15 passed` with `AssertionError: Lists differ: ['content: services/api/src/probe-boundary-4.mdx'] != []`. Two shards run side by side on one checkout were green in three rounds (`16 passed` each) because the probe lives under a second inside a 2.4 s run, but the collision remains possible by construction. CI gives each job its own checkout, so this does not occur there; introducing xdist would need the probe moved or the walk redesigned, not a skip marker.

Readings on `75d5b7e2`: `16 passed`; dead-pid and live-pid-old residues both `16 passed` after starting from `1 failed, 8 passed`; `PROBE_ROOT in NODE_ROOTS == False` / `API_ROOT in NODE_ROOTS == True`; `SC_CLK_TCK = 100`, `PROBE_START_MARGIN_S = 3.0`, `PROBE_STALE_AGE_S = 10.0`; diffstat against `9feafa27`: 2 files, `+320/−0`.

items.body:
Related to #812

Partial. Keep #812 open.

A directed search can now run on the conversation's selected runner. A JSON the search had already measured was still spending a round, and a reply that was not a JSON object was spending one too. The NPU path handed the search library one task, which that library refuses to start on. A search that does not name editable fields stays the existing free program search.

## Directed edits

The chat agent starts the run and does not pick later steps. PUCT chooses which measured node to expand. The model then proposes one JSON object. Only the fields the user ticked may change. A proposal that matches an edit already measured, a reply that is not a JSON object, and an edit that leaves the declared fields are not sent to the runner. The model is asked again, inside the same slot, up to three extra times. If it is still not a runnable edit, that reply is rejected before the runner and has no score.

There is no task-specific update rule. The model sees the measured values and their scores and proposes the next JSON itself.

## NPU scoring

Each candidate is one fresh shell execution on the conversation's selected runner, in a sandbox with no network. The fixed program computes the score. The candidate is JSON bound as input, not the program that runs. Success is a completed execution whose result says the device is `npu` and includes a number. A job that is still queued or running is waited on and does not take another slot. A failure, a cancellation, or a missing result has no score and is not stored as 0.

The search library requires at least four tasks and a hold-out fraction strictly between 0 and 1. An NPU search supplies four task ids and holds one out. The domain caches the measurement, so those ids do not each use the card.

## Field table

The run shows the ticked fields. Each candidate row shows which field changed, the old value, the new value, and the score.

## Review follow-up

- Each submitted execution retains the runner that accepted it. Polling and cancellation no longer depend on the current runner order or NPU-card selection. A disconnected accepting runner produces an error rather than redirecting the execution. Execution IDs are isolated by run, cannot be resubmitted, and retain their route after an uncertain submit response.
- The field list now distinguishes loading and source-read failures, with localized retry in English and Chinese. Changing the run or source clears stale rows and ignores late responses.
- A repeated-edit prompt shows at most eight recent edits, with each preview capped at 200 characters. The full measured-edit set still prevents duplicate execution.
- `-inf` is an internal ranking sentinel, not a wire score. `events.seeded` and `events.expanded` normalize non-finite scores through `finite()` to JSON `null`. `encode_ndjson(..., allow_nan=False)` rejects a missed non-finite value before it can emit invalid JSON. A regression test covers both null conversion and fail-closed encoding.

## Validation

The checks in this section were recorded on the earlier head `eff542cc`. See the workbench follow-up for validation of the new head.

- Directed/NPU Python tests: 22 passed.
- Runner proxy, preflight, proposal and orchestrator tests: 79 passed, including 9 runner-proxy tests.
- FieldDirection React tests: 6 passed, covering both locales, failed load followed by retry, source/run replacement and stale responses.
- `pnpm typecheck`: passed. Local L1: 4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed.
- [Earlier-head CI](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42500907449) passed: L1, UT, ST, all five mocked L2 E2E shards, Coverage and merge-gate. Real L3/L4/L5 E2E were skipped; these results do not replace the required real-browser captures.
- [Previous head `7b6dcbf7` CI](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42497149247) passed: UT 6949/6949, ST 51/51, mocked E2E 136/136, and merge-gate.
- Full local layers cannot be claimed green on this cloud host. Its sandbox cannot create the required NETLINK_ROUTE socket, and inherited proxy settings also affected local tests. On the previous tree the full Evolve suite had 390 passes and the same 21 failures reproduced on unmodified main; the original ST failure set also matched main. The new focused checks above passed without weakening those assertions.

## E2E user journeys and captures

**Required visual evidence remains BLOCKED.** The requested before/after captures in `zh-CN` and `en` are not attached yet: the pinned Chromium download on this host returns an unavailable or invalid archive, so no browser or viewport verification is claimed for this update. The outstanding captures are the declared-field header, changed-value rows with a missing score, a long field table, and a free-program run with no editable fields.

The React tests establish state/retry behavior, not rendered layout. The passing prior mocked E2E suite does not replace these specific captures.

Earlier local NPU evidence recorded for this PR, not rerun for this follow-up: one selected card completed 10 requested rounds and stored 10 new measurements. Seven repeated proposals were re-asked within the same round without being sent to the card. That run did not exercise a non-JSON reply; the branch is covered by unit tests. The field table was not clicked through in that earlier run.

## Release

Release category: release:feature

User impact: a search can score candidates on the conversation's selected NPU runner, and can limit edits to named JSON fields. A reply that is not a runnable edit is asked again inside the same round.

Compatibility and migration: none for a search that does not ask for a runner or a field list. That path stays the existing program search.

## Workbench UI screenshots

The composer shows how many fields may change after the user confirms the scope. The scope card shows the task, the initial values, and the fields the user can select. It also offers a task-based draft, JSON upload, and row controls for adding, editing, or removing fields.

![Confirmed edit scope in the composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0761c1e5-df60-4c12-a247-952cb16561f9)

![Edit scope card with one editable field](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7bf2dca1-ee66-4b8e-9851-36d346de55bf)

### New desktop workbench UI (served in the browser)

These screenshots show the new desktop workbench served in the browser with `SCIENCE_AGENT_WEB_DIR=apps/desktop/dist`. The first shows the optional **Set edit scope** action beside the existing composer. The second shows the JSON draft and field selection card, using the task already entered in the composer.

![New desktop workbench composer with Set edit scope](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01930862-60be-43f4-b3a2-1c8ea6bbed0b)

![New desktop workbench edit scope card with a generated JSON draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dca69a40-5f72-4277-aed6-da7623f6d50d)

## Workbench follow-up

The existing Evolve setup still selects the algorithm and places the command in the conversation composer. The composer remains the only place to enter the task. **Set edit scope** is optional. It uses the composer text to generate a starting JSON draft or accepts a user-provided file. The user can edit, add, remove, and select fields before confirming. Confirming the scope saves it on the draft. Sending the task remains a separate action. The API binds the confirmed baseline and editable fields before creating the search.

The same workflow is available in the desktop workbench when it is served in a browser. Set `SCIENCE_AGENT_WEB_DIR=apps/desktop/dist` and restart the API to serve it at the root path.

### Follow-up validation

- WSL workspace build and both renderer type checks passed.
- 24 API proposal tests and 21 Python direction tests passed.
- The draft endpoint was exercised with a local model fixture. It returned a task-specific draft without starting Evolve.
- Chromium verified both workbenches. The original Web workbench was checked at desktop and narrow widths for draft generation, JSON upload, row edits, and scope confirmation. The browser-hosted desktop workbench was checked for the original composer flow, the disabled draft action before typing, draft generation from the composer text, and scope confirmation without sending the task.
- A full real Evolve search was not run. Full local UT, ST, and mocked E2E results are incomplete after a WSL interruption. The PR author requested that GitHub CI run the full checks on this revision.

### CI follow-up after rebasing

Rebased onto main at `9feafa27`. The platform conflict was limited to imports. The rebased code keeps main's stop-run and active-run guard and still passes the user-confirmed proposal to the orchestrator.

The WSL workspace build, both renderer type checks, all 35 focused API tests, and all 21 Python direction tests passed on `4e48ca3`. Full checks for the rebased head are tracked in [GitHub Actions run 42572726350](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42572726350).

items.body:
Fixes #995

## The defect

After a `.sdresearch` import, the dialog's `onImported` handler refreshed the session lists and then left the user on whatever session was open before. When the import creates a **separate** read-only research copy (the shape in the issue: target `dc455d7a…`, imported `119daad8…`), that produced the reported end state: the copy appears in the list, the previous writable session is still on screen, and since the copy rejects messages (`409 SESSION_EVIDENCE_LOCKED`) the writable one is the only place to type. One import looks like two open sessions, with the wrong one active.

## Change

`apps/web/src/App.tsx` — `onImported` now distinguishes the two outcomes instead of always leaving the view alone:

- **The import wrote into the session the user was already on** (the dialog imports into the current session when it can): keep that session and refresh it. Switching away would hide the history that was just restored into it.
- **A separate read-only copy was created** (the #995 shape): open it. The dialog has just told the user the package is a locked snapshot, so that is the session they asked for; the previous writable session — and the temptation to type into it — is no longer what they land on.
- Nothing is created here: a writable continuation still comes only from the explicit "创建新会话继续研究" action, which matches the read-only-snapshot model the dialog states.
- The imported id is adopted only when the refreshed list actually contains it, so a stale or rejected import keeps the previous behaviour.

The first attempt at this always opened the first imported id, and `test/journey-restore-research.spec.ts` caught it: in that journey the import targets the current session, so switching away from it left the imported transcript off screen after 「查看导入会话」 closed the dialog. The second commit fixes that by keeping the current session when it is one of the imported ids.

## Scope

- This is the web flow the issue reproduced. The Windows desktop import dialog has its own continuation hand-off (`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`, changed in #999) and is not touched here to avoid two PRs editing the same block.
- The issue's third point is marked "Ideally": *the project's auto-created empty `Untitled session` does not linger next to the imported copy when the project was created only to receive an import*. That one is not done: it means deleting a session, and the wording leaves it optional. If you want it, the shape is "delete the auto-created session when it is provably empty (no messages, runs or files) and it was created for this import" — say so and I will add it with that guard rather than delete anything that might hold work.

## Verification

`test/journey-restore-research.spec.ts` covers the import path end to end (import → close the dialog → act on the imported session), and its first run on the initial commit is exactly what proved the earlier version wrong. The corrected version is running on CI now.

## Screenshots

The two outcomes `onImported` now distinguishes, in zh-CN and en.

### Outcome 1 — import wrote into the session already open

The current session stays open and its restored history is reloaded; nothing switches.

**zh-CN**

![zh-CN: import into current session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1005/zh-current-after.png)

**en**

![en: import into current session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1005/en-current-after.png)

### Outcome 2 — a separate read-only copy was created

The imported read-only copy is opened; the previous writable session is left behind in the list rather than left on screen.

**zh-CN**

![zh-CN: read-only copy opened](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1005/zh-copy-after.png)

**en**

![en: read-only copy opened](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1005/en-copy-after.png)

The import-completion dialog for each is at `pr-1005/{zh,en}-{copy,current}-complete.png` on the same branch.

items.body:
Fixes #930

A caller-supplied string that is over its length limit answered `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}`, so a provider form could not tell the user which field to shorten. The store already produces the right message (`The LLM API token is too long`); the shared request classifier just never recognised the shape and fell through to the catch-all.

## What was wrong

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` listed eight legacy validation messages that stay `400` (`is required`, `must`, `cannot`, `invalid`, …). In `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, `POST /api/providers/preview-models` calls `normalizeApiToken(body.apiToken)` before any network call, and `services/api/src/store/secrets.ts` throws a plain `Error("The LLM API token is too long")` once the trimmed token passes 16 384 characters. That message matched none of the eight patterns, so it reached the `unclassified_request_error` branch and became a 500.

The same shape appears at seven throw sites, all rejecting a client-supplied string, so they all leaked the same way:

| site | message |
| --- | --- |
| `store/secrets.ts` | `The LLM API token is too long` |
| `store/settings.ts` | `The proxy URL is too long` |
| `store/settings.ts` | `neo4jHttp is too long` |
| `store/settings.ts` | `neo4jUser is too long` |
| `store.ts` | `The Neo4j password is too long` |
| `store.ts` | `Model ID is too long` |
| `store.ts` | `The stored ${kind} is too long` |

## What changed

One pattern in the classifier, nothing else:

```ts
/\bis too long\b/i,
```

No new error code, no change to `normalizeApiToken` or any limit, no change to a throw site, and `services/api/src/http/index.ts` is untouched (`#929` owns the dispatch line next to the chain and this change does not meet it). The message already produced by the store is passed through unchanged, so the client sees `{"error":"The LLM API token is too long"}`.

The test file extends the existing table with the seven length messages above and adds one negative case that mentions a length without the validation shape (`Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget`), which must stay a 500; the existing `Database invariant failed` assertion is unchanged.

## Red first

Commit `341a5007` is the test only, on the unfixed classifier:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts
not ok 1 - keeps known validation failures at 400 without hiding internal faults
  error: |-
    The LLM API token is too long

    false !== true
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

Per message, before the fix (`isKnownClientInputError(new Error(message))`):

```
false  The LLM API token is too long
false  The proxy URL is too long
false  neo4jHttp is too long
false  neo4jUser is too long
false  The Neo4j password is too long
false  Model ID is too long
false  The stored runnerToken is too long
false  Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget
false  Database invariant failed
```

Route level, against the same unfixed tree, with a temporary probe that started the real `createApiServer` (offline MCP transport, temp data dir) and sent the issue's requests (probe file not committed):

```
STATUS 500 TEXT {"error":"Internal server error"}          POST /api/providers/preview-models  apiToken "k"×20000
STATUS 400 TEXT {"error":"The LLM API token cannot be empty"}  same route, apiToken ""
STATUS 201 ...                                             POST /api/providers, apiToken 16384 chars
```

The empty-token and valid-token readings are the control: the validator was already healthy at both ends, only the length case escaped.

## After the fix

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts
# tests 1
# pass 1
# fail 0
```

Same probe, fixed tree:

```
STATUS 400 TEXT {"error":"The LLM API token is too long"}
STATUS 400 TEXT {"error":"The LLM API token cannot be empty"}
STATUS 201 ... POST /api/providers apiToken 16384 chars
```

Per message, after the fix: the seven length messages are all `true`, and both non-validation messages (`Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget`, `Database invariant failed`) are still `false`, so a genuine internal fault still answers 500.

Diffstat against `main` `2908e9e8`:

```
 services/api/src/http/error-classification.test.ts | 10 ++++++++++
 services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts      |  3 +++
 2 files changed, 13 insertions(+)
```

Commits: `341a5007` test (red), `8b4c124c` fix.

Ran:
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts` — `# pass 0 # fail 1` on the red commit, `# pass 1 # fail 0` on the fix.
- Temporary route probe as above (unfixed: 500; fixed: 400 with the store's message; empty token 400; valid token 201) — file deleted before the commit, so the diff stays at two files.
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `grep -rn "too long" services/api/src --include=*.test.ts` — no other test asserts one of these messages, so no existing expectation flips.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser journey: the changed surface is the request classifier, and the route-level probe above drives the real HTTP server rather than a browser.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: an over-long API token, proxy URL, Neo4j field, model id or stored credential now answers 400 with the validation message that names it instead of 500 "Internal server error". Genuinely internal failures still answer 500, and every accepted value behaves as before.

items.body:
Fixes #665

`web_fetch`'s public-URL guard lets several IPv6 families through even though each one carries an IPv4 address the guard already knows how to judge. A model-supplied URL such as `http://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/` or `http://[2002:a9fe:a9fe::]/` reaches loopback or the link-local metadata endpoint, while the equivalent `::ffff:127.0.0.1` is rejected. This closes those holes, pins that public addresses in the same forms keep working, and — after review — refuses the non-canonical suffixes of the local-use NAT64 prefix rather than guessing where their IPv4 address sits.

## What was wrong

`ipv6Blocked()` consulted `ipv4Blocked()` only for IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) and IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d`) forms, where the embedded IPv4 address sits in the last two hextets. Other families carry the same address elsewhere:

| family | prefix | where the IPv4 address sits | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NAT64 well-known | `64:ff9b::/96` | last 32 bits | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| NAT64 local-use | `64:ff9b:1::/48` | last 32 bits **only for the canonical `/96` sub-layout** | canonical `/96` decoded; every other suffix under the `/48` rejected |
| 6to4 | `2002::/16` | hextets 2–3 | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| IPv4-translated | `::ffff:0:0:0/96` | last 32 bits, after `ffff` and 16 zero bits | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| Teredo | `2001:0::/32` | last 32 bits, bitwise inverted | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| site-local (deprecated) | `fec0::/10` | no IPv4 — the range itself is non-public | reject |

No branch inspected those positions, so each form fell through to `return false`.

The local-use row is the review fix. `64:ff9b:1::/48` is wider than the `/96` an embedded address needs, and RFC 8215 allows deployments to use other suffix lengths — a deployment that puts the IPv4 address in bits 64–95 is not judged by hextets 6–7. Reading hextets 6–7 of *every* address in the `/48` therefore judged the wrong bits: `64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808` was interpreted as the public `128.8.8.8`.

## What changed

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts`: one helper, `dotted(high, low)`, and `ipv6Blocked()` extracts the embedded address for the rows above and hands it to the existing `ipv4Blocked()`. There is no second copy of the IPv4 block list, no blanket range ban, and no refactor of the existing mapped/compatible branches.

For the local-use prefix the rule is now explicit and fail-closed: decode the canonical `64:ff9b:1:0:0:0::/96` sub-layout, and **return blocked for every non-canonical suffix** under `64:ff9b:1::/48` (`return true`, never `return false` — an unknown suffix must not become the way around the guard). The well-known `64:ff9b::/96` prefix is untouched by that rule.

## Red first

The new test (`providers.test.ts`), run against the unfixed `url-guard.ts`:

```
not ok 11 - web_fetch judges NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local literals by their embedded IPv4
  error: |-
    64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808

    false !== true

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  expected: true
  actual: false
# tests 16
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

The assertion loop stops at its first failing literal, so every blocked literal was also probed one by one against the unfixed predicate, and every public one against the fixed predicate. Values are `blocked` / `allowed` from `isBlockedAddress`; the flipped rows are the review fix, all in the tightening direction:

| address | before `e9e7358c` review fix | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `64:ff9b::7f00:1` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b::808:808` | allowed | allowed |
| `64:ff9b:1::7f00:1` (canonical `/96`) | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1::a9fe:a9fe` (canonical `/96`) | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1::808:808` (canonical `/96`) | allowed | allowed |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:1:0:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:0:1:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:dead:beef:cafe:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:7f00:1` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:a9fe:a9fe` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |

Five flips in this probed set, all `allowed → blocked`; zero `blocked → allowed`.

## Only tighter

The same probe run before and after the review fix differs in exactly one line — the tightened address. Everything a legitimate client may reach still resolves as public:

```
ALLOW  literal 64:ff9b::808:808            (NAT64 well-known, public)
ALLOW  literal 64:ff9b:1::808:808          (NAT64 local-use canonical /96, public)
ALLOW  literal 2002:808:808::              (6to4 for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal ::ffff:0:808:808            (IPv4-translated for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal 2001:0:808:808::f7f7:f7f7   (Teredo for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal 2606:4700:4700::1111        (native IPv6)
ALLOW  resolver 64:ff9b::808:808 for http://example.com/
ALLOW  resolver 2606:4700:4700::1111 for http://example.com/
```

These are asserted in the test too (`assert.equal(isBlockedAddress(...), false)` and `assert.equal(await assertPublicUrl(...), url)`), so the guard cannot be "fixed" by blocking a prefix.

## After the fix

```
# tests 16
# pass 16
# fail 0
```

The test now has 17 blocked addresses and 6 public ones (23 assertions across the literal and resolver paths), including the canonical `/96` cases in both directions and the non-canonical suffixes.

Diffstat against `main` `f4dd1813`:

```
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts | 71 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts      | 35 +++++++++++-
 2 files changed, 106 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

This branch is `f4dd1813` + four commits, two files, nothing else:

1. `dd29d921` test: pin NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local fetch targets
2. `eb818998` fix: judge NAT64, 6to4 and IPv4-translated literals by their embedded IPv4
3. `e4bb3e67` test: judge the local-use NAT64 prefix by its canonical /96 only
4. `e9e7358c` fix: decode only the canonical /96 under the local-use NAT64 prefix

It does not contain any commit from #915; the three-file view was the reviewer's worktree.

Ran:
- `node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts` in `packages/data-source` — `# tests 16 # pass 16 # fail 0`; the same command on the unfixed source is the red above (`# pass 15 # fail 1`).
- `tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- Per-address probe of the 17 blocked and 6 public literals before and after the review fix — the before/after table and the only-tighter block above.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` (full layers) were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser/API/CLI journey was added: the change is a predicate inside the `web_fetch` URL guard, and the mocked E2E subset does not exercise NAT64/6to4 literals.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: a model-supplied `web_fetch` URL that encodes a private, loopback or link-local IPv4 address in NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated, Teredo or site-local form is rejected with `PublicUrlError` instead of being fetched; public addresses in the same forms keep working, and non-canonical suffixes of the local-use NAT64 prefix are rejected rather than guessed at.

Compatibility and migration: none. A deployment that puts the NAT64 IPv4 address in bits 64–95 of `64:ff9b:1::/48` is now rejected instead of silently misjudged; the canonical `/96` layout and `64:ff9b::/96` behave exactly as before.

items.author: qingkwl
items.body:
Follow-up to #969. That PR made A6 **count** the precompiled bytecode so an incomplete set fails the build; this one adds a gate for the bytecode's **invalidation mode**, and a step that converts the files A6 was already counting but could not judge.

## The defect

release7 shipped **37,324 `.pyc`, of which 971 were in timestamp invalidation mode**. Every gate was green and none of them was wrong: A1/A1b import fine (the bytecode *is* valid), A5 measures path length, and A6 counts `.pyc` against `.py` — 971 files that ship in the **wrong mode** still count as shipped. Coverage and mode are different properties, and A6 only ever checked the first.

The installed tree pays for the difference. NSIS extraction restamps every `.py` to the install instant, so a timestamp-mode `.pyc` is stale the moment it lands and CPython recompiles it. Measured on a field install (`D:\ProgramData\ScienceDiscovery`): **the first launch rewrote 1,048 `.pyc`**, inside the same busy two minutes as `jiuwenswarm-init` and `proactive_engine`.

## Why step 7c did not already fix it

7c already runs `compileall --invalidation-mode checked-hash`. But `compileall` only **rewrites a `.pyc` it judges invalid**, and all 971 were judged **valid** in the build tree — the copy chain preserved each `.py`'s original mtime, so the timestamp check passed and skipping them was *correct behaviour*, not a coverage hole. Measured, four arms (`logs/w28-evidence/w28c-compileall-mode-experiment.mjs`, run with the bundled interpreter): valid timestamp-mode `.pyc` + checked-hash `compileall` → **still timestamp-mode**.

Blocking the copy points is not an option either. Reading `co_filename` from **all** 971 (not a sample) shows three provenances: 619 from the dev venv, **350 from uv's CPython distribution stdlib** (copied by a different statement, `assemble-backend.mjs:689`), and 2 with relative paths. Any per-copy-point fix leaks one of them.

## What the change does

**A1c — convert, in place, after the import self-checks.** `py_compile(CHECKED_HASH)` over exactly the sources whose `.pyc` shipped timestamp-mode, overwriting the stale file.

**A6-mode — fail the build on any timestamp-mode `.pyc`.** This is the net for a cause nobody thought to blocklist: a conversion that skipped a target, an interpreter that declined a file, or a future copy step that pulls dev-tree bytecode in *after* A1c ran. The limit is **exact zero, not a ratio**: mode is binary per file and the conversion is deterministic, so a tolerance would be a budget for the regression this stops. An **unparseable header also fails** — a mode nobody could read is not a mode that is fine.

The driver is an exported string constant (`RECOMPILE_DRIVER`) rather than a separate `.py`, so `test/pyc-mode.test.ts` asserts the text the build *actually* pipes to python and executes it against a real interpreter. A hand-copied replica would prove the replica.

### Three constraints each finding added

1. **A1c must run *after* A1/A1b.** Both execute a payload python, and an implicit import that has to compile a source writes **timestamp-mode** bytecode by default. Converting before them would let a self-check silently undo the conversion. The test suite pins this ordering textually, and the mutation sentinel injects "A1c moved before the probe" as a defect that must be caught.
2. **`sourceOfPyc` must agree with CPython, not with my intuition.** It splits at the first dot to match `importlib.util.source_from_cache`. Diverging would map to a path CPython never uses. There is a test that checks it against the real interpreter.
3. **The A5 advisory got sharper.** A5 reports `maxRel=192` against a build budget of 176, and that overage is safe *only* while the shipped checked-hash set stays complete — first-run precompile must remain a no-op. A6-mode is now what keeps that promise true.

## Scope and cost — three shapes measured, not assumed

| shape | measured cost | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| delete the stale `.pyc`, let `compileall` recreate them | **~500 ms/file to delete × 971 ≈ 8 minutes** | rejected |
| **recompile in place, overwriting (shipped)** | **8.4 s for all 971**, `recompiled=971 failed=0` | **chosen** |
| global `compileall -f` | **280.2 s** — recompiles all 37,998 sources to fix 971 (**33×**) | rejected |

The deletion cost is not a property of the payload: `w28c-c2-unlink-cost.txt` measured unlink at **~500 ms/file in the workspace, in its parent, and on a different volume**, and only **0.92 ms in `%TEMP%`**. Defender real-time protection was off and the volume is a healthy local NTFS SSD, so that 500× spread is an artifact of this machine's filesystem stack. Measuring it only at the convenient location would have chosen a fix ~150× slower in the real build directory.

## Verification

- `test/pyc-mode.test.ts`: **25 tests, 0 skipped**. The behavioural ones run a real python and read the header of the `.pyc` the driver produced — conversion, idempotence, and loud failure on a source it cannot compile.
- **Mutation sentinel** (`w28c-mutation-sentinel.mjs`): 10 injected defects — A1c moved before the probe, the walk stops counting, the gate stops failing, an inlined driver, a 1000-file tolerance, `UNCHECKED_HASH`, a driver that swallows errors, an inverted mode bit, a short header read as fine, a zero-`.pyc` pass — **all 10 caught, 0 survived, 0 not-applied**. A green suite alone proves nothing; a gate that can never fail prints the same line.
- **Gate on the real tree** (`w28c-gate-on-real-tree.mjs`): extracts A1c / the walk / A6-mode **verbatim out of this file** and runs them on a copy of the release7 payload (37,998 `.py` + 37,324 `.pyc`). Negative arm (no A1c) → A6-mode reports **971 timestamp, exit=3**. Positive arm (A1c) → **recompiled 971, failed 0 → 37,324 checked-hash, 0 timestamp, exit=0**, coverage unchanged (`maxRel=192`). Text assertions prove the wiring; this proves the body runs.
- Full suite on this head: **247 win_desktop tests** (0 fail, 0 skipped), **architecture gate 347 files OK**, **44 root script tests**.

## Measured net benefit — a real installer, not a projection

Built **release8** end to end from this change (`assemble-backend` → `electron-builder`): `ScienceDiscovery-0.3.0-win-x64-setup.exe`, **614,944,658 B = 586.5 MiB**, blockmap and 3 locale paks. In the real build A1c reported `converting 971 timestamp-mode .pyc` → `recompiled 971, failed 0`, and A6-mode reported **`37324 checked-hash, 0 timestamp, 0 unparseable`**. An independent re-walk of the staged tree (not assemble's own counters) agrees: `pyc=37324 hash=37324 timestamp=0 unparseable=0`.

Then the first-launch cost, measured as a **pair** (`w28c-net-benefit.mjs`): the same 971 sources in the same location under the same bundled interpreter, differing only in the invalidation mode of their `.pyc`, with every `.py` restamped to one install instant exactly as NSIS does. The judgement goes through CPython's own `SourceFileLoader.get_code()`, so it classifies, validates, and writes back on a miss — the real import path, without executing module bodies.

| work tree location | control (release7 timestamp-mode) | treated (release8 checked-hash) | **saving** |
|---|---|---|---|
| `%TEMP%` (C:) | 971 recompiled / 7.01 s | 0 recompiled / 1.59 s | 5.43 s |
| **D: (the production install volume)** | **971 recompiled / 8.73 s** | **0 recompiled / 1.82 s** | **6.92 s (7.1 ms/file)** |

**The D: number is the one that counts.** Same harness, same files, different volume — `%TEMP%` on this host is a fast outlier (0.92 ms vs ~500 ms for unlink), so measuring there understated the saving by 22%. That is the same trap the cost table above avoided.

Two honest limits on **6.92 s**:

- It is a **lower bound**. It isolates the 971 mode-attributable files; the field install rewrote 1,048, and a real first launch also carries `jiuwenswarm-init` and `proactive_engine` I/O, which contention would inflate further.
- It is **not** an end-to-end installed cold-start timing. Both installers share `appId cn.sciencediscovery.desktop` with `perMachine: false`, so silently installing the second one rewrites the HKCU uninstall entry the first one owns and leaves the tester's existing install without an uninstaller. That is an irreversible change to a machine that is not mine to spend, so the paired measurement above stands in for it. A full installed cold-start timing needs a volunteer machine or a distinct appId.

One measurement defect worth recording, because it produced a confident wrong number before it was caught: the first revision of this harness enumerated files with `glob("**/*.pyc")`, which **skips path components starting with a dot** — and most of this payload lives under `backend\jw\.venv\`. It measured **711 of 971** files. The "both arms agree" sentinel passed, because the omission is symmetric. The harness now receives the file list explicitly and reports `listed`/`measured`/`missing`, with a coverage sentinel that fails unless all 971 were exercised.

## Regression

`assemble-backend.mjs` gains 112 lines; `lib/pyc-mode.mjs` (317) and `test/pyc-mode.test.ts` (433) are new. Nothing existing is removed or re-timed: A6's budget gate, A5's path gate, and steps A1–A4 keep their behaviour, and A1c is additive between A1b and A2. A build that already shipped all-checked-hash bytecode converts nothing and is unaffected (`recompileTimestampBytecode` does not spawn an interpreter for an empty list — tested).
